Thus, those devotees of the Abode of Weapons, together with the king and his subjects, celebrated that wonderful birth festival lasting twelve years throughout the night.
Then they performed the ritual circumambulation and slept thereafter;
on the morning of the ninth day, they had bathed and performed the auspicious rites.
They fed them exceedingly with the essence of milk,
the essence of food, the essence of savory juices, the essence of drinks, and the finest varieties of edibles and eatables.
The delighter of the cowherds gave him face-cleansing powders and cosmetics,
as well as Lomaśa, Agastya, and other preeminent sages.
Those skilled in weaponry worshipped Śambhu, the two sons of Aśvinī, and the tens of thousands of hosts of Gaṇas; they indeed bestowed wealth upon them.
They then offered various desirable substances, fruits, flowers, and garments; they avoided [disobedience] and respectfully accepted the king's command. (112)
Then, as they were requesting their own country for the sake of departure— that is, liberation— Hari said, "I shall effect your liberation at the time of the departure of your life-breaths."
Hemaśālāyana and the others were indeed those eleven sages;
from then on, they made their permanent residence on the shore of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake.
Then, O Rādhikā, the thousand daughters of the subjects of King Śatānīka,
being bewildered, gazed upon that Supreme Soul who was smiling.
The king gave those subjects to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
they were all protected by the Supreme Soul in the hermitage of Lomaśa.
Then, having received the command of Śrī Hari, they went to the abode of Uṣṭra in celestial chariots, while indeed worshipping Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Remembering the Imperishable One, praising the sacred field of Aśvatīrthaka,
and proclaiming his majesty, they reached their own country.
O Rādhikā, this narrative includes the protection of the kitten by the female cat,
the drinking of water by the female cakravāka bird, and Lakṣmī’s passage through her austerities.
Whoever hears, reads, causes others to hear, or remembers this [work] which wards off the oppression of the people in the great land of Uṣṭrālaya— 1.106.1–20.
For him, indeed, there shall be enjoyment and liberation according to his desire from Hari;
as well as the attainment of supernatural powers, sovereignty, and so forth, along with land, grain, sons, and other such things.
The expansion of one's lineage, health, and the state of being a householder—all this indeed comes about through the grace of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 122.

Thus, in the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the second section on the continuity of the Tretā Yuga, [is described]: the granting of boons to Hanumān; the fact that all holy places (*tīrthas*) were established by the Lord in the region of Uṣṭrālaya; the performance of a Viṣṇu-sacrifice by the local king Dakṣaja Vaṅgara; the arrival of the king along with his subjects at the sacred field of Aśvapaṭṭasara by means of a hundred celestial chariots; the offerings for worship during the festival of the Lord’s twelfth birthday; and the dedication of the king’s hundred daughters and the subjects’ thousand daughters to Bālakṛṣṇa, as well as the [devotion] of the king and others.
The one hundred and sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Return to One’s Own Country," etc. || 106 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, listen now to another marvel of Hari—
how Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa became the helper of his devotee.
Once, many daughters of Māna arrived by celestial chariot to behold the surface of the earth where his subjects resided.
The Brahmaputrī, the Lavahītā, the Candrāvatī, the Irāvatī, the Śālāvatī, the Mīnakaṅgū, the Lāṭiśā, and likewise the Kāniśā. || 3 ||
Māpīṅgā, Śīkyāṅgā, Aṅgasvāṅgā, Harāṅgahā, Mauktikā, Tārimā, Pannāmā, and likewise Tvāṅgahā. || 4 ||
The Mīnāmī, Tānasarimā, Sīnā, Gāndharvavedikā, Nṛtyagāyanakuśalā, Rāgarāgiṇī, and Abhijñikā—[these were the women]. || 5 ||
Beautiful, burdened with the fullness of youth, moon-faced, and radiant as the sun;
clad in garments of cloth purified by fire, adorned with divine ornaments, and endowed with splendor.
There were twenty maidens, with thousands of female attendants for each,
who could assume any form at will and were resplendent with the power and majesty of the Siddhas.
And goddesses bearing missiles and weapons, possessing invincible strength,
those women of auspicious limbs [arrived] from their own world in a divine celestial chariot.

Having offered salutations to the True One (Satya), as well as to Viṣṇu, Śambhu, and the Unborn (Aja), and having bowed to the gods seated in the assembly of Brahmā, they departed, having performed auspicious rites.
From the summit of Meru, they first proceeded to the Merudroṇī;
having circumambulated Meru, they beheld many celestial abodes.
He beheld palaces and great pleasure gardens equal to the abodes of the Brahma-world,
as well as the dwellings of the world-protectors, which were enriched with the splendor of heavens and even beyond heavens.
He saw the exceedingly brilliant palaces of the planets, lunar mansions, and stars,
as well as the abodes of the yogins, the sages, and the gandharvas.
The palaces of the Daityas and Dānavas, the dwellings of the Kinnaras, the abodes of the Kiṃpuruṣas, and likewise the hermitages of the ascetics; || 13 ||
Having beheld Ilāvṛta and the land of Jambū separated [from it] behind them,
they traveled through the sky over the earth toward the region of Kimpuruṣa.
[He saw] the Āpatāyin mountain, the Gopīraṇa mountain visible to the eye, the Kunalīnādri mountain, the Kārukora mountain, and the Tiyānaśa mountain. || 15 ||

Having seen the yellow ocean at the eastern part of Cipiṅga, as well as the river Śikṣāṅga, which has the limbs and sub-limbs [of the Vedas] for its streams, and likewise the river Śikṣāṅgikā; || 16 ||
Having seen the drinking places for water and the drinking places for wine, as well as the groups of islands for the women, they went to Sumātṛkā.
Then, turning back, they went toward the river Mīnakaṅkūna;
they reached Irāvatī, which has the moon for its fish and whose falling bodies are like mountains.
Meanwhile, the rākṣasas of the ocean— some stationed at the drinking-place of the waters and others traveling through the sky in celestial chariots— beheld the maiden’s aerial vehicle.
Tawny-colored and tall, resembling mountain peaks,
they arrived in the sky with weapons in hand to seize the jewels of maidens.
In this way, even the Dānavas born in the region of Phullipāna arrived by means of a vehicle traveling through the path of the sky to carry off the maiden.
Deceitful and terrifying, they assume forms at will;
bearing missiles and weapons, they roam through the sky and dwell within the ocean.
With bodies like mountains, wielding lightning as weapons, they are terrifying;
merciless, tawny-colored, with coarse bodies, they are burners of others. ||23||
In this way, other terrifying Daityas from the Vāraṇīya island were merciless, devourers of humans, and armed with fire, stones, and weapons. ||24||
Equipped with catapults, arrows, and other weapons,
those sky-travelers [approached] that beautiful and auspicious aerial chariot for the maidens, which was one krośa in length.
Having beheld Sūryaprabha, these arrived to carry off the maidens:
from the island of Ādama, as well as the black Nāgas and the Kaṣmalas. (26)
Having recognized that group of beautiful maidens, those five hundred and thousands of Rākṣasas came toward him. ||27||
Then the Daityas, the Dānavas, and thousands of black serpents—all numbering five thousand—approached from all sides. 28.
As the great mountain was falling upon his body, they obstructed the celestial chariot, saying:
"All of you must come for refuge; otherwise, you shall surely perish quickly. (29)
Having spoken thus, all the asuras, desiring to enter the celestial chariot,
rushed about in haste when they were about to enter.
The celestial chariot of the one whose essence is merit was untouched by sinners;
it was then in the sky, unassailable even by Rākṣasas, Dānavas, and Daityas.
And when they did not attain cessation, those asuras then once again employed the illusion of their own sins and, having assumed it, held fast to it at that very moment.
The forms of the principle of evil (pāpatattva), the weapons of the principle of evil, the missiles of the wicked, the arms of the sinful, and the nooses of evil; ||33||
[He saw] evil ministers, iron arrows, as well as bows, swords, and the like;
fires, stones, and shafts; maces, tomara-spears, and clubs.
Desiring to seize them, they indeed obstructed their celestial chariot with fire-sparks mixed with glowing embers and similar explosive projectiles.
With clouds whose essence was sin, they indeed obstructed his path;
they blocked the gates and entered the celestial chariot.
A great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose among the group of maidens in the celestial chariot;
though they were present in the chariot, there was no one at all to protect them.
Whether on the earth, in the sky, on a mountain, or even in the ocean,
the maidens fell into distress and remembered Aryaman.
Just then, Tvaṣṭṛ arrived with great haste along with his own attendants, [approaching] his father, his protector, his progenitor, and the dispeller of his sorrow. (39)
As soon as he was remembered, that one of a hundred splendors appeared in his celestial chariot;
with showers of thousands of arrows, he warded off the rākṣasas.
Then the Rākṣasas, Dānavas, Daityas, and Kṛṣṇa-nāgas tormented Āryaka from all sides with showers of arrows.
Aryaman, having produced the fire, dispatched it everywhere;
in order to burn up the Rākṣasas and others, it consumed all directions. ||42||
Having produced waters through their illusory power, the water-dwelling Rākṣasas extinguished the fire; then this Aryaman became their father.
Having created tens of millions of Aruṇas, he dispatched them everywhere;
those lords, with their sharp-flaming minute weapons, set everything ablaze.
Then those Asuras, assuming false forms through their own illusory power (māyā), became Rākṣasas, Dānavas, Daityas, and black serpents in every way. 45.
Concealing their original forms, they fought with the sons of Aruṇa;
the messengers of Aryaman, using weapons like the sharp and hot-rayed sun, [attacked them]. (46)
Seeking them out again and again, they caused the Daityas and other Asuras to be consumed by fire;
many who were burnt there were reborn from the ashes.
At that time, there were tens of millions of Rākṣasas;
and that entire battle took place in the sky, causing the destruction of everything. 48.
A great and profound deliberation arose among the Aruṇa Rākṣasas;
by means of the Aryaman and Sūrya mantras, millions of Aruṇas were produced.
Rākṣasas are produced by means of mantras from the Rākṣasas;
there is no end to the armies, and tens of millions of troops increase.
Weapons also increase, and heaps of arms multiply;
they are split apart, severed, killed, and they fall. (51)
The sky and the surface of the earth became red and filled with blood;
indeed, millions of bodily emanations fell there from every direction.
The bodies and trunks of the Aruṇa Rākṣasas, resembling mountain peaks, fell down in heaps and mounds as they were struck. ||53||
Having risen above the clouds in the sky like mountains,
they appeared upon the surface of the earth, which was a hundred yojanas in extent, with a height equal to that of mountains.
Those corpses of the naked ones indeed became mountains at that time;
with their bodies falling, those mountains became the Naked Mountains (Nagnaśaila).
Those tawny-colored ones who were skilled in battle perished;
for seven days a great war continued day and night,
and there was no cessation there, even though the noble Sun himself was present.
Pitṛkakṣa remembered the triad of Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the Unborn (Brahmā)—the lords of the gods of gods, who are the grandfathers in the form of the ancestors—for the sake of protection. (57)
"O lords of the gods, come quickly in an instant for the sake of protection!
May you protect all these maidens and destroy the asuras! ||58||
At that moment, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara arrived there, mounted upon three celestial chariots and accompanied by divine armies. ||59||
At that very time, however, the Daityas, Dānavas,
and Rākṣasas remembered the great Daitya, who was highly skilled in the art of illusion.
He was named Kālaprāleya, accompanied by an army of ten million;
equal to Mahākāla, born from Mahāmāyā, and resembling Mount Meru.
With a thousand heads and chewing a hundred lotuses in his mouth,
he indeed arrived instantly, making the worlds tremble.
By the mere sound of whose loud laughter the hosts of planets fell down,
all the oceans were agitated, and even the earth trembled.
The mountain peaks collapsed and living beings certainly perished;
the roars became equal to the falling of a great thunderbolt.
The peak of Mount Mandara was indeed held up with one hand,
while the banners were grasped with his other hand, which was like the frost of Time.
Such was that great-bodied asura whose mouth then became wide open and expanded to ten yojanas.
Thus, having seen Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śaṅkara,
he who possessed a thousand faces summoned them along with ten million gods into the sky by cracking his thighs.
Then, seeing him who resembled Vairāja, the massive-bodied Saṃkarṣaṇa, the destroyer of Time, the gods remembered him.
Then the god Saṃkarṣaṇa quickly arrived there in the sky;
the three gods praised the Lord, who held a mace, for the sake of protection.
Saṃkarṣaṇa forcefully brought his mace down upon his head;
however, Kālaprāleyaka quickly evaded that mace.
He struck Saṃkarṣaṇa on the head with his mace;
Saṃkarṣaṇa, with his own mace, pulverized that mace.
Then, with great force, he struck Kālaprāleyaka on the head;
the mace was shattered by the blow, but it did not break the Daitya's head.
At that moment, the Daitya took up his trident and rushed forward to kill;
Sankarshana pierced Kalaka in the chest with his own spear.
Then, struck by the spear in the throat and likewise by the thunderbolt in the belly, he fell into the eastern ocean with the height of a mountain.
Crushed by mountains and likewise torn apart by spears, he fell like the sun; having lost consciousness, he fell into a swoon in an instant.
Rising up for the sake of protecting his life, he fled;
having circumambulated Mount Meru, he ran outside when he reached it.
Saṃkarṣaṇa, however, went as far as the Lokāloka mountain,
following behind that demon who was the destroyer of Time itself.
Leaving behind the Lokāloka mountain, he went out into the light of the sky;
out of fear of Saṅkarṣaṇa, he too fled into the infinite, countless expanse of space.
The god Saṃkarṣaṇa also, having bestowed fearlessness upon Śambhu and the others through his subtle form, departed for the abode of Īśvara.
Then Śaṅkara and the others fought with the Daityas and Dānavas;
they struck down the Daityas on all sides, who were like the dark fortnight of the month of Kārtika.
With tridents, discuses, lightning-nooses, ordinary nooses, and javelins;
with swords, projectiles, rocks, scimitars, and likewise with spears.
With the wind-missile, mountain-missiles, cloud-missiles, and fire-missiles;
with the serpent-missile, garuḍa-missiles, lion-missiles, and śarabha-missiles. ||82||
With boar-missiles, lizard-missiles, crab-missiles, and scorpion-missiles;
with Yama-missiles, Rākṣasa-missiles, crocodile-missiles, and water-missiles. ||83||
With tiger-weapons, torch-weapons, madness-weapons, fainting-weapons,
hunger-weapons, thirst-weapons, and insanity-weapons, they struck one another.
And the armies of Brahmā and the others excessively tormented the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, and finally destroyed them.
Those asuras, numbering in the tens of millions, were slain in battle on all sides—both artificial and natural, as well as illusory and non-illusory. ||86||
And the armies of the Āruṇas, as well as the hosts of the Brāhmas, the Gaṇas of the Śāṅkaras, and the attendants of the Vaiṣṇavas. ||87||
Those three Asuras restored to life by means of Vedic mantras and the power of their perfected will all those asuras who had been slain by the millions in battle.
Brahmā and the others said to them, "We are here to grant boons as givers of desired things. They all requested supreme liberation, and they were all granted their lives. (89)
Then Brahmā and the others said, "Choose indeed something other than liberation";
but Aruṇa and the others, having been restored to life, did not choose anything other than liberation.
Then Viṣṇu said to them: "There are indeed many paths to liberation, such as the world of Nara-Nārāyaṇa and also Badarikāśrama."
"Shall I give you the ocean of milk, or shall I give you Śvetadvīpa?
They replied, "That abode is not eternal; therefore, we do not desire it. (92)
"We desire this, yet we also desire the supreme, eternal, and highest state.
Viṣṇu, however, spoke from Vaikuṇṭha, situated above the covering of the waters. 93.
"If that exists, I shall indeed grant it, or else the supreme abode of Vairāja.
They replied, "Neither Vaikuṇṭha nor even the eternal Vairāja [abode] exists. (94)
Therefore, we indeed desire another supreme abode called liberation;
Viṣṇu has declared it the immortal abode, and I shall grant it to you, who are abundant.
"Or else, I shall grant you Vaikuṇṭha, which is designated as 'unmanifest' (avyākṛta).
They replied, "We do not desire that abode at all; rather, we desire that which is beyond it. (96)
Viṣṇu said, "I shall indeed grant you Goloka, the supreme abode. They replied, "We do not desire that; we desire what is beyond even that. (97)
The eternal state of the imperishable Brahman, revealed by the Vedānta; the supreme abode of all abodes, auspicious and described in the Upaniṣads. 98.
That which is equal and beyond which there is nothing else—that is the supreme abode of Hari.
We desire it; grant us that abode which rests upon the Supreme Brahman. 99.
Viṣṇu said: "I do not have the power to deliver that;
[it belongs to] the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. (2.107.10)
The Supreme Self, the Supreme Brahman, the sustainer of all incarnations, is capable of granting that abode; He indeed shall grant that state.
Thus addressed, they immediately remembered that glorious Puruṣottama, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Svāmī, the Supreme Person. 102.
And at that very moment, they suddenly became absorbed in meditation;
having plunged their very selves into the Self, they forgot the one who descends in all avatars.

Thus ends the one hundred and seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Battle Fought by Brahmā and the Other Devas to End the Obstruction Caused by the Rākṣasas and Others in the Kimpuruṣa-khaṇḍa of the Pitṛkanyakās, the Restoration of Life to the Dead, and the Request for Liberation through Life—That the Bestower of Supreme Liberation is indeed the Beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā; when Nārāyaṇa is meditated upon by the gods and remembered, Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, [manifests] in the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā. || 1 ||
He spoke to his own supreme devotees, the ascetic sage Maṅkaṇaka,
as well as to the great sage Maṅki and the seer-worshipped Kūrmiṇa.
Prācīnabarhis, Trīta, the supreme ṛṣi Prabhūta, Ruśāyin, Khāsīna, and the sage Aṅgaśyāmalaka. || 3 ||
Ārakarṇa, Brahmadāsya, Anāmayarṣi,
Śyāmalarṣi, Malayarṣi, and the circle of the fourteen ṛṣis.
Having summoned those residing at Aśvapaṭṭasara, Hari said:
"Listen, O gentle sages, for you are great devotees of the Lord."
Ascetics and foremost Vaiṣṇavas, devoted to meditation on me,
[reside] from the Himalayas in the eastern region and in the southern region.
And as they were falling, the daughters of the Pitṛs were upon their celestial chariot;
but when they were assailed by the Daityas, Aryaman, their father, then [intervened].
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the great lord Saṃkarṣaṇa—
these Daityas fought and then slew the Daityas and Asuras.
They restored to life the deceased attendants of the Sun, Āruṇas,
as well as crores of Vaiṣṇavas, Śāṅkaras, and Vaiśvasṛjas.
To grant them a boon, the gods offered this word:
"Liberation, which is supreme and beyond the imperishable, has been requested by their attendants."
Then those [demons], Aruṇa and the others, were unable to give him liquor;
they were awakened by the hosts of gods to me, who bestow such liberation.
Therefore, being absorbed in meditation, they indeed remember me now;
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama).
And as you great sages have entered into my state of servitude,
I command you in every way, for you are all highly blessed devotees of the Lord.
"Go from here, in an instant, beyond the mountain Patatkāya;
having gone with due respect to Varṣa Kimpuruṣa and likewise to Prāgjyotiṣa," (14)
Even while wandering everywhere in the regions of the eastern mountains:
"Oṃ, salutation to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā! (15)
"By the command of the Great King, bestow this mantra upon all of them;
Śambhu and the others who guard the maiden are also waiting for me."
That region must be made into a domain dedicated to the Lord by you;
and having gathered together with Aruṇa and the others, worship must indeed be performed.
"I must bestow devotion upon them and grant their desired wish;
all of you go by means of celestial chariots—do not delay," he said indeed.
The Blessed One, the Supreme Person, granted him a divine celestial chariot;
and those fourteen sages departed from the sky in an instant.
As it was falling upon the mountain peak, they made that celestial chariot steady;
and they beheld the chariot of the daughter of the Pitṛs stationed in the sky.
Beholding that radiant celestial chariot, which possessed the splendor of ten million suns, the maidens saw Brahmā,
Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and others, as well as the attendants of Aruṇa.
Filled with enthusiasm, they raised shouts of "Victory! and cries of joy;
even the sages then cried out, "May Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa be victorious! (22)
Thus they raised shouts of victory across the expanse of the sky:
"Victory to Kṛṣṇa! Victory to Nārāyaṇa, O Śrī Puruṣottama!"
Victory indeed to the primordial God Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa;
victory to Kṛṣṇa, who transcends the Imperishable (Akṣara), the Supreme Brahman! 24.
Having heard this from the path of the sky,
they indeed paid their respects in the aerial chariots of the sages, which were ten yojanas in width.
Then they all went and repeatedly bowed to the supreme sages,
along with the daughters born of their fathers and the young maidens.
First, the cleaning of the sandals, then [the cleaning] of the feet;
then the service of the sages, the washing of their feet, and the offering of fruit. ||27||

The offering of water, the words of welcome and so forth, the respectful oblation (arghya) with sandalwood paste and other ingredients, the provision of a seat and the like, and the presentation of the honey-mixture (madhuparka) were all performed. ||28||
Then, in those regions, according to that custom, the daughters of noble families continuously offer hospitality to guests. (29)
Furthermore, in the regions of the Kimpuruṣas, auspicious rites must indeed be performed;
these are everywhere first set in motion by young maidens.
O Rādhikā, having performed the worship of the sages, Kanyakā and the others led those stainless sages to their own celestial chariot. Thus they departed. 31.
Having attained a state of supreme excellence through the majesty of the Supreme Brahman,
they performed worship to Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Brahmā, and Āryaman.
The disciples of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa spoke: "By the remembrance of the Illustrious Ones, we have been sent here by Him, and thus they speak. (33)
They also declared, "We have been sent here specifically for the purpose of bestowing the mantra;
indeed, a Vaiṣṇava must be made [the officiant] on all sides. (34)
Thus they spoke, saying, "This is the command of Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
Then the Blessed Lord Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself [spoke]. (35)
"He will come as the soul of all"—thus they spoke to them.
Upon hearing this, everyone rejoiced, and indeed two celestial chariots appeared.
On the beautiful bank of the river Candrāvatī, in the vicinity of a forest,
they eagerly brought [the image] down at the command of the sages.
Beholding that beautiful forest at Mīnasthāna, those people—
the sages and the Vaiṣṇavas— performed a sacrifice to the gods there.
Then, from the attendants of Aryaman, the ruddy ones, the great sages [uttered]:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Master; Svāhā! (39)
There they gave him this mantra and a garland of tulasī upon his neck;
thus, those thousands of Vaiṣṇavas became fathers and sons.
Then those sages, whose wealth was their austerity, in numbers reaching into the millions upon millions, took refuge there in Hari, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. 41.
They gave that very same mantra to the attendants born of Viṣṇu,
as well as to the hosts of Rudra and to the disciples of Brahmā.
From thousands of millions upon millions, they bestowed that very mantra;
all those Vaiṣṇavas there worshipped Puruṣottama.
Then the sages [bestowed] that Manu upon the daughters of the Pitṛs as well:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā. (44)
And having given those maidens away, they were united with Puruṣottama;
thus, after the initiation, there arose from him the tree of the creeper of desire.
Those twice-born ones gave to the Vaiṣṇavas and to the maidens delicious prepared food, such as meals and other delicacies, as an offering to the sages.
Having eaten, the Vaiṣṇavas and others bathed in the Candrāvatī river;
then the Vaiṣṇava sages deliberated there.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, Aryaman, and likewise the Kanyakās [should be worshipped];
indeed, the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice is to be performed on the bank of the Mīnakaṅgū river.
There, it is said, all the subjects of Prāgjyotiṣa will come from every direction, having been summoned from all sides as far as the ocean. 49.
Likewise, the subjects of the Kimpuruṣa region will arrive;
indeed, the Vaiṣṇava mantra must be offered to them at the sacrifice.
"In this way, the command of the illustrious Hari shall be fulfilled here;
Brahmā said that there will also be a battle at that sacrifice. (5.1)
Indeed, the subjects here are of the nature of darkness (tāmasa); the kings are mountain-dwellers born in the regions of Jalapāna, Philīpāna, and Vāraṇīya. ||52||
Furthermore, there will be men who are excessively tamasic and resemble Rākṣasas;
in those regions as well, there will be battle with them. (53)
"Therefore, let this ground indeed become Vaiṣṇavī, purifying and in the form of a sacred ford (tīrtha).
"So be it," the sages said; Viṣṇu replied, "So shall it be. (54)
Rudra said, "So be it," and Aryaman likewise said, "Om.
[This occurred] at the base of the river Mīnakaṅgūna, on the ground of the land of Melakāṅga.
"Let Makha be born upon the central ground of all lands," having thus resolved, they all departed from the Himalayas. (56)
In the northeastern region, in the auspicious direction of Īśāna,
in the Piṅga country among the Kiṃpuruṣas, those who were devoted to Viṣṇu gathered for the sake of sacrifice.
There, in the Menakāṅga forest on the bank of the Mīnakaṅgūna river,
in the Piṅgā forest, they performed the purification of the ground for the sake of the sacrifice.
To the west of Aṅgasvāṅga and to the east of Śālāvata,
there is a circular region, fifty yojanas in extent and adorned with forests.
To the west of Mīnakaṅgā, they prepared a sacrificial pavilion;
and to the east of Mīnakaṅgā, they constructed excellent dwellings.
Then, on both banks of the Mīnakaṅgū, they established hermitages for sages;
likewise, they established hermitages for the gods, abodes for the ancestors, and hermitages for the Siddhas.
Brahmā, Maheśa, and the other lords established hermitages on the banks of the Śālāvatī river, in the exceedingly beautiful eastern region.
To the west of Śālāvatya, they constructed beautiful and enchanting hermitages for the liberated Vaiṣṇavas who travel through the sky.
Having thus prepared the region of Triṇada, the vast Piṅgā forest,
for the sake of the sacrifice, he summoned everyone by means of messengers.

Likewise, [he should worship] all the liberated ones, the lords, the incarnations, the goddesses of the lunar days, the beloveds of Brahmā, the ancestors, the sages, the gods, and the lords of the directions. ||65||
[He saw] humans, divine beings, those dwelling in Pātāla— both virtuous women and virtuous men—
as well as Gandharvas, Kimpuruṣas, Vidyādharas, and hosts of Apsarases.
And also the goddesses and the yoginīs from Kailāsa in their entirety, and all those from Vaikuṇṭha, and all those from Satyaloka. ||67||
And all the hosts of ancestors, the lords of the gods, the deities,
as well as the guardians of the quarters, the protectors of the earth, and the guardians of progeny, [he addressed] from every side.
He also created beasts, flocks of birds, and numerous offspring of the earth,
as well as creepers, trees, clusters of grass, and groups of bulbous roots and medicinal herbs.
Rivers, riverbanks, ponds, lakes, and likewise oceans; mountains, excavated areas, and uncultivated forest lands. ||2.108.70||
He abandoned forests, groves, and the like, as well as ponds and long lakes;
he also left behind holy fords, houses, men, and women on all sides.
[He saw] the attendants of Gaṇeśa, Kārttikeya, and Hanumān; all the weapons, together with their personified forms, such as the Sudarśana discus and other armaments.
The mantras, the Vedas, all branches of knowledge, all arts, as well as the various flavors, all the principles (tattvas), and even the diverse shrines (caityas). ||73||
The seasons, months, years and so forth, the yugas, and the days; the moments, illusion, the qualities, and past actions; the followers of Yama, the pretas, and the dānavas. ||74||
Then Maheśa and the other gods summoned all the Daityas, those of Asura nature, the Rākṣasas, and those born of the lineage of Brahmā to the sacrifice.
Those great-souled ones, eager from all the worlds, arrived;
followed by the three classes of gods, they were offered hospitality during the festival.
In the place of Brahmā, he himself is Brahmā; in the place of Rudra, he himself is Hara;
in the place of Viṣṇu, he himself is Viṣṇu; and in the place of the Pitṛs, he himself is Aryaman. ||77||
Let the Mātṛkās be upon their seats, and the planets upon the seats of those planets; and let the sentient beings be in the places of the world-protectors and the sages. (78)
They sat down in the places of other gods and divine women;
those gods and goddesses sat down in embodied form, each according to their rank.
Then the Supreme Lord Himself, Anādi-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa,
was directly remembered by them, accompanied by their mother and father.
Accompanied by Lomaśa and others, and joined by Brahmapriyā,
the Blessed Lord Puruṣottama arrived swiftly by means of a celestial chariot.
Accompanied by the wish-fulfilling creeper, the wish-granting tree, the celestial cow, and other such treasures, the sacrificial priests offered him a welcome with great honor. (82)
The assembly, having attained joy from the sight of the Supreme Lord, performed their ablutions and took up residence; then Hari proceeded to the sacrificial ground.
There, by means of the wish-fulfilling creepers and other such things, there were long channels of clarified butter,
as well as similar channels of curd, honey, and milk.

The channels for juices were filled with juice-halls containing the nectar of sweet foods; the collections of sacrificial offerings were innumerable, and the varieties of edible provisions were infinite. (85)
Then, by the power of the Supreme Lord, there was manifested there Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the illustrious Puruṣottama. 86.
In the temple of the principal deity, upon a golden throne, the father, the patron of the sacrifice, shone resplendent together with his wife, the illustrious Kambharā. 87.
The illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa indeed shone upon his own throne, accompanied by the two divine attendants who were like the splendor of the gods. 88.

The self-luminous Lord shone resplendently in the beautiful pavilion; there followed the selection of the bridegroom, the purification of the body, the declaration of an auspicious day, and other such rites. (89)
Having performed the installation of the deities of the limbs and other rites, the sage Śrī Lomaśa then consecrated the fire within the sacrificial pit along with the appropriate mantras.
The fire sacrifice proceeded comfortably with Vedic mantras;
Gaṇeśa, the Bhūtas, Yakṣas, and others, as well as the gods and other deities, [partook] of their respective food. 91.
The Pitṛs and Devas received their respective portions from the mouth of the Fire, offered by Hari; they were satisfied, as were the liberated lords numbering in the tens of millions.
And the men of Prāgjyotiṣa were summoned from all sides,
as were the people of Jīvasumātṛka and the people of Malaya.
Those dwelling on the banks of the Irāvatī, those situated on the banks of the Mīnakaṅgu, those on the banks of the Śālāvatī, and those established on the banks of the Śikṣāṅgā; || 94 ||
Those dwelling on the banks of the Aṅgaśikṣāṅga, those residing on the shore of the Harāṅga, those living on the bank of the Tārimā, and those inhabiting the Mahatītaṭa; ||95||
Men dwelling on the banks of the Āmūrā river, those living in the regions of rivers, and those residing in that central region were invited to the sacrifice. 96.
This supreme Vaiṣṇava mantra is indeed the cause of auspiciousness in all places;
its presiding deity is the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī. (97)
"Everyone should proceed here for the sake of attaining auspiciousness"—having heard this invitation, the sattvic men likewise [prepared to go]. (98)
Brahmins and others characterized by passion (rājasa), as well as Kṣatriyas living the life of Vaiśyas, the best of Vaiśyas, and Śūdras—both women and men—went to the sacrifice. 99.
Beholding that sacrifice, they considered themselves to have accomplished their purpose by means of celestial chariots, sky-faring vehicles, and even Garuḍas and Jaṭāyus.
Having attained that which is pleasing and likewise having obtained the mantra of Kṛṣṇa:
*oṃ anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine svāhā*. (101)
Then, having performed the recitation of mantras and having directly beheld the glorious Puruṣottama, they partook of nectar, drank it, and attained a divine state.
Having worn a tulasī necklace around their necks, millions of human beings became supreme Vaiṣṇavas— devotees seeking liberation who were dear to Hari.
Then they performed the final purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) and the concluding rite of the sacrifice; meanwhile, those who were of a tamasic nature and were indeed haters of the sacrifice [remained].
Hundreds of thousands of those enemies of the gods, bearing weapons, were destroyers of sacrifices;
they were cruel beings born from water, who ruined meritorious deeds. 105.
They were extremely violent toward the inhabitants of Phoenicia, and they were arrogant toward the people of the West. (106)
But others, born from the frost of time, gathered together with one another;
and there were also his friends and companions, who were equal to him even in their virtues.
The Rājānas, the Bodhapāṭhīyas, those born of the Caityapāṭhaka lineage, the Cāṃkaśekas, the Siṃgaliṅgas, and likewise the Hāṃgacāudakas. || 108 ||
The Tūnakīnas, Hanoyas, Rāyagas, Baṅgakākinas, Lāśahas, those born of the Māṅga race, and others such as the Mañcarāyas. (109)
And all these kṣatriyas, like rākṣasas of a tamasic nature,
then arrived, taking with them armies numbering in the hundreds of thousands and tens of thousands.
War-drums were sounded and roars arose;
then, the weapons of the heroes flashed in the sky.
Thus, O Rādhikā, at the conclusion of that sacrifice, a battle broke out there between the Daityas and the creators of the cosmic egg.

Thus ends the one hundred and eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Dispatching of the Sages from Kuṅkumavāpī, the Journey of Hari by Vimāna along with His Parents and Others to Regions such as Prāgjyotiṣa, and the Occurrence of Battle at the Conclusion of the Sacrifice," in the second section (Tretā-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, to the roars of those demons;
they made the ends of the quarters resound and the sky, along with its planets, was thrown into agitation.
The king of the Jalapāneya regions was Makaraketumān,
and the king of the Philīpas was named Phalajaṅgama.
The king of Vāraṇīya-dvīpa was named Vārdhūṣaketana;
the king of Ārdramāna-dvīpa was named Kalmāṣakesarin.
And the king of the Kālaprāleyakas was Raṇamadāṅkana;
and the king of the eastern regions was Bodhavihaṃgama. || 4 ||
And likewise, Piṅgalaka was the king of the Cipiṅga countries;
the great king of the Maṅgūjas was named Samaramaṅgala.
Likewise, the king of the Mañcūrās was named Hārakīrti;
the great king of the Lāśahās was known as Kṣaṇātmavādana. || 6 ||
Likewise, there was a king named Kāruvarman born in the Karvarī region,
and the very powerful ruler of the Ilā country named Māṇḍalākṣi.
And there was a king named Pannāmadeśa, also known by the name Pādasaha;
he was the king of the eastern regions and was called Prācīnaśāyana.
King Śṛṅgaśekhara was the ruler of Aṅga, Śikhaṇḍa, and Deśa;
these and other principal kings, intoxicated by war,
[advanced] together with their own armies numbering in the tens of thousands and millions, which spread across the sky.
With electric balls, fire-engines, and dummies that explode instantly;
with the hurling of weapons, atom-bombs, and likewise with tunnels and missiles;
with aerial nets, *śataghnī* engines, illusion-nets, and poison-tears.
They fought with gods and humans who were like artificial noble ones through the winds of poison;
this battle took place within a circle of a hundred yojanas.
The god Śaṅkara and Bālakṛṣṇa himself protected the celestial chariot of Pitṛkanyā and the celestial chariot of Brahmapriyā.
And other hosts of Śaṅkara, Brahmā, Sūrya, and Viṣṇu, by the millions, then fought there against the asuras by his command. (14)
O Rādhikā, those [demons], who were like mountains, leaped up into the sky at a height of many yojanas; then, like planets, they all fought in the firmament.
Others, rising fifty yojanas high from a height of five yojanas,
go suddenly like the sun and fall upon the weapons of the army.
The warriors shone in the sky like circles of stars;
King Makaraketu was surrounded by those numbering one hundred thousand.
Accompanied by his warriors, he fought in the sky with the Cāruṇas;
Aryaman, however, [fought] that king along with his army over the ocean.
Having swiftly struck them in the sky with the discus granted by Viṣṇu as well as his own discs,
he dispatched them to the abode of Yama.
And his son, Sūryaketu, sought refuge in Hari;
he was protected there by Hari and subsequently made a Vaiṣṇava.
The great king of the Pahlavas fought with the hosts of Śaṅkara, accompanied by ten thousand warriors, against the Vahnigolas and the Hotis. 21.
The hosts, numbering hundreds of thousands, struck down tens of millions of warriors, including King Philemon, with lightning-weapons.
His son, who was born from the seed of Śrī Hari, sought refuge;
hundreds of other sons as well went for refuge to Śrī Hari. ||23||
All those, beginning with Bījajaṅga, were made Vaiṣṇavas by Hari.
Dvaipa was the king of Vāraṇīyabhū, whose banner bore the sign of a usurer.
Accompanied by five hundred thousand soldiers, he fought with the attendants of Viṣṇu using fire-engines,
swift weapons, and discuses in the sky.
At the confluence of the ocean, the attendants struck them down with their own discs;
four hundred thousand soldiers perished, and the king was slain by the Sudarśana discus.
His son, Sāraketu, accompanied by a hundred thousand warriors,
sought refuge in Śrī Hari and was made a Vaiṣṇava by Hari.
All his soldiers became Vaiṣṇavas, desiring to protect their lives;
the king of the island of Ārdramāna was the Daitya Kalmāṣakeśarin.

Traveling in his celestial chariot, he fought against ten thousand fierce soldiers of Kṛṣṇa with missiles and weapons such as the *vyomajāla* and others that discharged poisonous tears. The Vaiṣṇavas, accompanied by hundreds of thousands of Vaiṣṇava warriors born from the Kalpa-valli creeper, cut through the *vyomajāla* nets with multitudes of scissors.
They quickly struck all those soldiers with great effort using many *kalpavallī* creepers raised up in the sky, and they killed them along with their life-breaths using *sudarśana* discuses.
Then, he split the crown of Kalmāṣakeśa’s head into two with his discus;
and when Kalmāṣakeśa was slain, his five sons were named the Kalmaṣas.
Raktakeśa, Kṛśākeśa, Citrakeśa, Agnikeśaka, Dhūmrakeśa, and others likewise went for refuge to Śrī Hari. (33)
By the bestowing of mantras, even those terrifying Asuras born from the dissolution of time were made Vaiṣṇavas by Hari.
Those thirty lakhs of birds, bearing weapons and assuming many forms,
fought with ten lakhs of the Vaiṣṇava attendants.
With artificial puppets in the sky, with rapidly bursting balls,
with showers of arrows, with lightning-nooses, with showers of water-pots,
with serpent-nooses, with stones, and likewise with dense iron weapons; || 36 ||
The cruel attendants, arrogant with false pride and illusion, struck down the Vaiṣṇavas;
but the attendants, wearing the armor of the Lord, stood in their celestial chariots in the sky and fought with them using various weapons. ||37-38||
The eldest son of Kālakāleya, whose banner was the mark of battle-intoxication,
seized a mace and slew many Vaiṣṇavas, including the deluded Māra.
Others fell to the earth in a swoon, while some, their hopes shattered, fled.
The twice-born ones chanted the Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa-Varma for the sake of protection.
Of this Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa-Varma, Satī Ramā is the deity,
the Anuṣṭubh is the meter, and Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is the bestower of its fruits.
I bow to Śrī Hari Kṛṣṇa, the all-conquering Supreme Brahman, the destroyer of Daityas and Dānavas, the Lord of Lakṣmī, the beloved Sovereign. 42.
Bīja, Gopālabāla, and the great lord Bhaktapāla;
and the auspicious Vaiṣṇavī initiation, which is the Great Bhāgavatī. ||43||
The *kīlaka* is Śrī Kambharā, the son of Śrī Nanda, who increases devotion; having remembered the Lord of Rādhā and Pārvatī, he is employed in the recitation. 44.
Meditation [is the means] for all entries, for all powers, and for all splendors; it resides in the heart of Mañjuhaṃsahari, who is the source of excellence and endowed with virtues. 45.
May the Nyāsa be upon my head; here, the head of Śrī Hari [is placed]. May the eyes of the Lord be in my eyes, and the ears of Hari in my ears. (46)
May Kṛṣṇanāsa be in my nose, and Nārāyaṇānana in my mouth;
may Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇakaṇṭha, the protector of the Asuras, reside in my throat.
May the heart of the wielder of the discus be in my heart, and may the back of Hari, who dwells in the Kuṅkuma-vāpī pond, always be upon my back. (48)
May the belly of Him who resides at Aśvapaṭṭasaraḥ be within my belly;
may the world-sustaining navel of Bālakṛṣṇa be within my navel. 49.
May the hips of Lord Hari be mine, endowed with strength;
and may the two private parts of the Creator Hari be established within my protected loins.
May the two thighs of the destroyer of Daityas and Dānavas be my thighs;
and may the two knees of Lord Hari, the worshipper of Śakti, be my knees. (51)
May the legs of the Supreme Nārāyaṇa, who is the refuge of the universe, be in my two shanks;
may the feet of the Supporter of All be my two feet, protecting me from Bali.
May the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa be present here within me in embodied form.
And may he be the beloved lord of Brahmā within my body, senses, and so forth.
May the Lord, who has attained the abode of the supreme imperishable, protect me from above;
may Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Sovereign, protect me from the front. (54)
May Kṛṣṇa and Hari, my two excellent brothers, protect me on both sides;
and may Nara and Nārāyaṇa likewise protect me from behind and below. (55)
May the Lord of Lakṣmī protect me on earth; may the True Lord protect me in water; may the Beloved of Śrī protect me in fire; and may the Lord of Radiance protect me in the atmosphere. ||56||
May the Lord of Brahmapriyā protect me in the sky; may Māṇikīśa protect me in the wind; and may the Wielder of the Discus, the Lord of Rādhā, grant me protection in the forest. 57.
May Hari, the wielder of the mace, protect me from tens of millions of demons;
may Bālakṛṣṇa, the bearer of the spear, protect me in all directions and intermediate points. ||58||
May Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Goloka, protect me from the hosts of fire;
and may Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, protect me from the asuras.
May the Valiant One protect me from the destruction caused by missiles and weapons;

may He who dwells within my heart protect me from sudden fears. May He who bears the trident, the fish, the banner, the bow, and the svastika protect me from the fear of Time, Māyā, evil karma, enemies, and the wicked-hearted servants of Yama.
Thus, O Vaiṣṇavas, those divine beings who have transcended Māyā and possess spiritual bodies have indeed worn this armor of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. 62.
They were born with all-black strength and endowed with every power;
for they are indeed the very forms of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Employing their Sudarśana great discuses in every direction,
they swiftly cut down three million asuras born at the time of cosmic dissolution.
While you were still alive, all those others fell dead in battle into the great waters;
even Kālaprāleyaputra, the ornament of the battlefield, died.
A hundred of his sons were destroyed by Viṣṇu’s discus in the sky;
Bodhavihaṅgama was also a king among the Prācīnas in the sky.
Bearing a spear as bright as ten million suns, he indeed waged war upon the earth with the hosts of Aruṇa,
Vaiṣṇava, and Raudra, who had arisen from the Kalpa-creeper.
In battle, in various regions, and by means of weapons and missiles beyond calculation—in the sky, in water, on the earth, on mountains, and in forest lands—[he was struck]. (68)
From all sides, his armies fought him with fire-weapons,
lightning-balls, fire-engines, quick-explosives, and mechanical dummies.
With subtle whistles, projectiles, arrows, secret tunnels, spears, lightning-bright fire-nooses, celestial nets, and poisonous flames; || 2.109.70 ||
With *śataghnīs*, army-destroying *śakaṭīs*, and *vimānaka* machines,
as well as with water-sprays and earth-throwers, those fierce warriors struck down [the enemy].
The hosts led by Āruṇa donned the armor of the Lord and indeed struck down the armies of Bodha, which numbered ten million.
Indeed, beautiful puppets resembling gods,
produced from wish-fulfilling creepers and filled with fire-machines, struck the Dānavas in the sky.
Half of the great army was lost— consisting of puppets whose very essence was that of puppets—
whereas the conscious army thereafter numbered eighty lakhs.
Indeed, that [sin] was destroyed for the demons; ten lakhs fled, while ten lakhs there sought refuge in Śrī Hari. (75)
In that manner, King Piṅga, the bird of awakening, met his destruction, as did his hundred sons, including the birds of discernment and the rest. ||76||
Having attained refuge in Śrī Hari, they were indeed made Vaiṣṇavas;
even ten lakhs of soldiers were made Vaiṣṇavas by Hari. (77)
Three hundred thousand Cipiṅgas, warriors traveling by aerial chariots,
were commanded by Piṅgalaka and fought against the Vināyakas.
Then, in that forest and in the sky, by all those fierce Kalpavallīs born from the desire-granting trees,
hundreds of thousands of soldiers were destroyed.
They were all struck down in the water and in the sky by axes, iron balls, projectiles, mountains, serpents, nooses, thunderbolt-fanged creatures, and tridents.
Whether on the ground or in celestial chariots, wherever they were encountered, they were indeed slain;
Piṅgalaka was killed, as was his son Piṅgaśekhara.
Having taken refuge in Śrī Hari, he was indeed made a Vaiṣṇava by Hari;
he was Samaramaṅgala, the king of the Maṅgūjana regions. ||82||
The king Hārakirīṭa was the lord of the Mañcūraṇa regions, and King Kṣaṇātmavaktra was the ruler of the Lāśahāna regions. (83)
Likewise, King Kāruvarmā and also he who was born in the Karvarī region—these [two], with their own armies numbering five million, [set out]. ||84||
Together with the supreme Brahmā, they all fought;
then Brahmā, by means of Atharva-mantras, generated the Jāṭikas.
He swiftly urged the gods against the armies of the Daityas;
joined by lightning-nooses, they [traversed] the path of the sky in an instant. ||86||
Fifty lakhs of the Jāṭikas quickly took flight,
while thirty lakhs of the Dānavas were struck by lightning-weapons and those nooses.
They destroyed them with lightning-thunderbolts, while the remainder fled like clouds driven away by swarms of locusts arising from the Atharva-veda and by the currents of the celestial Ganges.
The remaining ten lakhs of Daityas who were bitten by those poisoned [arrows] all died;
thereafter, only ten lakhs of his soldiers remained.
And for the sake of their livelihood, they came there for refuge to Śrī Hari;
indeed, Bālakṛṣṇa made them all Vaiṣṇavas there.
Hārakirīṭa and Samaramaṅgala were killed,
as were all ten of Hārakirīṭa’s sons, who were all exceedingly powerful;
then, abandoning all hope for life, they all sought refuge in Śrī Hari.
The supreme Prabhāsakirīṭas were indeed made Vaiṣṇavas by Hari. ||92||
All the thousand sons of Samaramaṅgala, who were indeed devotees of Hari,
came to you for refuge and were made Vaiṣṇavas by Hari.
King Kṣaṇātmavadana fought with Śambhu once again;
accompanied by an army of one hundred thousand, he was slain by Śaṅkara.
Kāruvarmā, accompanied by an army of one hundred thousand, fought again with the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, Lord Hari; he too was struck down by the Sudarśana discus.
Their sons and grandsons, as well as their allies, were all slain in battle by Viṣṇu with his Sudarśana discus. (96)
The king of Ilādeśa was Maṇḍalākṣi, who possessed great strength;
likewise, King Pādasaha was the protector of the region of Pannāma. || 97 ||
Formerly, there was a king named Prācīnaśāyana;
accompanied by an army of one hundred lakhs, he fought with Śambhu. (98)
A king named Śṛṅgaśekhara, [ruling over] the regions of Aṅga, Śikhaṇḍa, and Deśa,
fought with Śambhu along with a hundred million soldiers.
Accompanied by two hundred lakhs of warriors, they were all struck down in battle; they were destroyed and killed in the fray by Hara along with his own attendants.
Not even one remained among those who had marched to the battle for Mount [Hara];
thus were these four crores of warriors destroyed.
O Rādhikā, at that time, the remaining subjects as well as the soldiers of the army were made Vaiṣṇavas by the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.

"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā! Hari gave this mantra to them, and the sages likewise [received it] by the command of Hari. (103) Thus ends the one hundred and ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Seeking of Refuge by the Twenty-five Lakhs of Survivors from the Battle with Śambhu and Others, after the Death of the Fifteen Kings beginning with Makaraketu and their Fourty-Million-Footed Armies," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. (109)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Thus, O Rādhikā, in ancient times, on the earth near the ocean in regions such as Prāgjyotiṣa, there occurred a battle that brought about the end of the dānavas.
Then, for the sake of their purification, he performed the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice once again at the foot of the Śālāvatī river,
on the bank of the Lāśahāsa lake.
On the northern side of the Brahmaputra, extending for a hundred yojanas,
Anādikṛṣṇanarāyaṇa created lakes all around.
All the subjects, who were intent on the field of battle,
were summoned by means of *sarvatobhadra* celestial chariots capable of traveling a thousand *krośas* in an instant.
All the gods, as well as the sages and the ancestors, assembled there;
the sacrifice lasted for seven days with most excellent oblations and other rites.
There is no number for oblations, nor even a calculation of their flavors;
there is no end to edible foods—what then can be said of drinks?
There, the Sāttvika kings, greater than those born of the lotus, were united;
as were the earthly men and women, who longed for the purification of battle.
There was no counting of the gods, the great seers, and the hosts of ancestors;
all the sacred fords, rivers, streams, and oceans were summoned there.
They went to the waters of the Lāṃśahāsa lake, to the waters of the Brahmaputra,
and likewise to the holy sites at the source of the Śālāvatī river.
The ground, extending for a hundred yojanas and serving as a refuge for the deities,
became like Goloka and was like Vaikuṇṭha.
For it was like the world of Brahmā, or indeed became the Imperishable (Akṣara),
where the primordial Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the glorious Supreme Lord, resides.
There, Brahmā himself shines resplendent, as do the Brahman-sages,
the Ṛṣis, the gods, and likewise the progenitors of the worlds.
In that place, O Rādhikā, what indeed could be lacking or devoid of prosperity,
where the beloveds of Brahmā reside and where there are truly wish-fulfilling trees?
What harm is there if Brahmā, Hara, Viṣṇu, and Aryaman are themselves present there,
where the unborn Agni, the seven-tongued bearer of the four Vedas, resides?
Since Rudra himself is there as the five-faced one, what deficiency could there possibly be? For there, the sattvic gods and lords bestow the welfare of the world. (15)
Where pure Vaiṣṇava great sages, bestowers of liberation, have gathered in the form of sacred fords (tīrthas) for the sake of purifying the world. || 16 ||
Where a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice is performed by the Vaiṣṇava gods, what ground for deficiency could possibly arise there in such an auspicious place? (17)
Likewise, the wish-fulfilling creepers, pearls, rivers, streams, and trees,
as well as the gods and the fundamental principles, brought forth the supreme materials for the sacrificial assembly.
The lords, those sages who were stationed in celestial chariots and remained together with Nārāyaṇa, indeed caused them all to drink the five products of the cow.

Then, out of enthusiasm, they caused the purification of the bodies of the subjects and those who had gone to battle according to the prescribed rites, and likewise performed the Vaiṣṇava mantra-ritual.
May Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa be my refuge in every way.
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā! ||21||
Out of fear of Time, Illusion, evil karma, enemies, Yama, and treacherous friends,
he was protected by the boat bearing the trident, fish, banner, bow, wheel, and svastika.
I am Brahmā, an eternal devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is my Lord and my Master.
First is the refuge-mantra, and second is the act of surrender;
the first consists of sixteen syllables, as does the second. (24)
The third is the protective mantra consisting of thirty-two syllables;
likewise, the fourth is the mantra of the nature of Brahman, which bestows half of Hari’s own body. (25)
Those fourteen sages—Maṅkaṇaka, Maṅki, Aya, Kūrma, and Prācīnabarhiṣa—bestowed the thirty-two syllables. (26)
Trīta, Prabhūtānaka, Ruśāyī, Khāsan, Aṅgaśyāma, Ārakarṇa, Brahmadāsa, and Anāmaya. || 27 ||
Then Śyāmalarṣi and Malayarṣi gave these to the Manus;
after the oblation, they indeed bestowed garlands of tulasī upon the subjects.
And by the command of Hari, they gave [the earth] to the subjects who were as vast as lotuses;
Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa Svāmī, the glorious Hari, is my refuge. 29.
At the sacrifice, they gave mantras to them, and Pāvanya created offspring;
Keśava bathed them all in the waters of the Lāśahāsa.
And likewise in the waters of the Śālāvatya and the Brahmāputrī; thus [he saw] all creatures—women, men, boys, and girls. (3.1)
The Blessed One caused all his kinsmen and men to purify themselves,
having gratified the gods with the essence of oblations and the ancestral deities with the fire.
Having satisfied both the attendants and the maidens who had protected him in battle,
the Blessed One fed the sons of the Lotus-born with sweet foods.
Having attained the grace of the sacrifice, they became fulfilled;
and having performed the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), Bālakṛṣṇa [entered] the assembly hall.
Having bowed to Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, the beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Brahmā commanded Aja for the sake of a reward.
He spoke openly to all the subjects, granting them freedom from fear:
"I am the Supreme Brahman, beyond the imperishable, the cause of all incarnations. (36)
From whom indeed the military arrays (vyūhas) beginning with Vāsudeva arise, whose powers are Time, the Great Puruṣa, and Māyā. (37)
He from whose form the incarnations and divine abodes are born is this very Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, the beloved of Svāmī Śrī Kṛṣṇavallabha. (38)
The illustrious Gopālabālaka Hari, son of Śrī Kambharāśrī, made his residence in the field of Aśvapaṭṭasara, the field of the Imperishable. 3.9.
The Lord, the husband of Prabhā, Pāravatī, Kṛṣṇā, Brahmapriyā, Rādhā, Ramā, and Lakṣmī, resides at Kuṅkumavāpikā.
He is the Lord of the virtues of Māṇikī, Lalitā, Haṃsā, Mañjulā, and Asagunā; he is the Lord of the golden arts of the goddesses Jayā, Śāntā, Dayā, and Muktā.
The Lord of the virtuous, the beloved of liberation, the Lord of creation, the Supreme Sovereign, the Lord of all abodes, the inner self of embodied beings, he himself is the bestower of fruits. 42.
That by relying upon which nothing remains to be known or attained;
that than which there is no higher, no equal, and no other whatsoever exists. (43)
This Lord, the Master, the beloved, the supreme Hari, is the giver of that eternal and supreme liberation which is to be sought after by the followers of Āruṇi. 44.
O people, supreme liberation is indeed to be sought from this Śrī Hari;
for our victory always exists through His majesty alone. (45)
He whom we, Nārāyaṇa and the others, constantly worship is indeed He Himself. Worship His form and revere Him alone. (46)
"Render him service and abide by his word;
his speech is the Great Veda, and his action is the Great Dharma."
His form should always be served, for he is to be meditated upon constantly by people; indeed, through his touch, both the insentient and sentient become purified. (48)
May all those gods who were slain in battle, as well as those on the side of the gods—may they all become alive here this very moment through his grace. (49)
"Whether they be on earth, in water, or in the sky— those who have died following the gods,
may they quickly become divine and come toward Hari."
Having spoken thus, Brahmā took water from the foot of Hari into his water-pot (kamaṇḍalu) and cast that water, resembling a cloud, into the sky.
Increasing and flowing swiftly through the earth, the sky, and the waters,
it then became nectar and indeed restored the dead to life.
All living beings on the side of the gods, as well as others who were artificial, became that very water itself when touched by the sleep-inducing power of the Dānavas. 53.
Nevertheless, the Dānavas did not remain alive at that time;
for such was the will of Śrī Śaśvata-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
When it was touched equally by both sides, the gods were restored to life, but the Dānavas were not;
then Brahmā bestowed upon them a fourfold mantra.
There, Hari bestowed rewards upon those who saved lives,
and likewise, he gave excellent rewards there to those who were victorious.
One of the two bodies was fit for liberation, while the other remained on earth;
he sent all those who were fit for liberation to the imperishable state (akṣara-pada). //57//
The Blessed One, with a mind full of grace, himself spoke to those worthy of the earth:
"The sacrificial offering, the favor, the drink, the sweet food, and the excellent meal. (58)
"Let them take it," he commanded; and by his order, they all ate, including the princes, the sages, and the armies as well. (59)
Having summoned all the subjects, Hari spoke thus:
"Indeed, the regions have been purified by me through you, who are yourselves like sacred pilgrimage sites."
Rivers, streams, lakes, and mountains have been made bestowers of liberation;
and here on the surface of the earth, the destruction of the Daityas and Dānavas has been thoroughly accomplished.
These princes are indeed Vaiṣṇavas who have taken refuge in me;
my sons shall be established by me upon the thrones of kings. (62)
Moreover, you ladies are my subjects and are entirely like young daughters to me;
let them proceed according to the king's command, for this is my eternal decree. (63)
"Let my venerable sages likewise practice devotion toward me,
and let them listen to how I shall divide and bestow that kingdom."
"This is Brahmā, the grandfather of all creatures and the self-existent Lord;
let him give a crown to this one whose name I shall utter. (65)
The land of Jalapāna-dvīpa is given to Sūryaketu;
the collection of lands of Pilīpa-dvīpa is given to Bījajaṅgin.
The island-land of Vāraṇīya is given to Sāraketu;
the island-land of Ārdramāna is given to Raktakeśa. ||67||
The ancient kingdom is bestowed upon the wise bird,
while the kingdom of Piṅga and Cipiṅga is given to the one with tawny hair.
The Maṅgū region is given for the auspiciousness of battle,
while the Mañcuraṇa district is offered to Prabhākirīṭa.
And the region known as Lāśahā is given to Tritarṣi;
let that kingdom become renowned by the name Trītāvitta.
"Let this become the kingdom of the sages; let those who are beautiful, whose forms consist of shadow-bodies, and who know the self-knowledge of Brahman, dwell there. (7.1)
And let the kingdom of Kāru be given to the great sage Kūrmi;
let that too be a kingdom of sages, always pure and devoted to Viṣṇu. (72)
May Brahmā himself rule over the kingdom of Ilādeśa;
may Brahmadeśa always remain a sacred site, with the river Airāvatī as its holy stream.
May Viṣṇu forever protect the land of Pannāmna-dikā;
may the region of Śyāma, situated to the east of Brahmapura, become the sacred ford (tīrtha) of Pannāmna.
May Śiva always be the protector of the ground known as Prākcayana, and may the Vināyakas be intent upon protecting that eastern region. (75)
May Śaṅkara himself, the king of the limbs, the sciences, and the regions, rule that kingdom of the east and south together with his own attendants. (76)
And may the Mothers always abide in the region of Sumātṛkā for the sake of protection, they who are devoted to Śiva and are the destroyers of the ocean-dwelling Daityas.
"May these kingdoms indeed become Vaiṣṇava," thus was it spoken by Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, O Rādhikā. (78)
And Brahmā gave him that crown of sovereignty;
and Hari himself also gave it to Viṣṇu, the unborn Śambhu.
Then Bālakṛṣṇa himself gave them a *tilaka* made of saffron, as well as a garland of *tulasī*, to those who were new [to him]. (2.110.80)
Then Hari spoke these beneficial words to those kings:
"Even my own gurus are being offered by me here for the sake of your devotion."
The preceptor of the Karvarī-jalapānas was indeed the sage Kūrmī;
Śambhu Maheśvara was the preceptor of the Prācīnas and the Philīpas;
and Prācīnabarhiṇa was the preceptor of those belonging to the eastern and northern regions.
The preceptor of the Śyāmalas and the Cipiṅgas was the sage Śyāmalaka. ||83||
From the Malayas came the Malaya-ṛṣi; from Ilā came Brahmadāsaka;
from the Lāśas came Gurutrīta; and likewise from the Lūśas came Lūśaya. (84)
The heavy mothers of the elephants should be known as the beloveds of the sages;
Brahmā, the creator of the universe, is the Guru of the Ārdramānas and of the Brāhmaṇas as well. 85.
Maṅkaṇaka was the preceptor of the Maṅgūjas who dwell in that region;
Maṅkiraya is considered the preceptor of the Mañcūras, the Prajās, and others. ||86||
The preceptor Cayanarṣi is considered the foremost among beings, abundant in power, free from disease, and the master of the regions for the piling of the altar prior to its construction. ||87||
Aṅgaśyāmalaka was the preceptor of the Aṅgas, Śikṣās, and Deśas;
Ārakarṇa was the preceptor of the Ārās; and Khāsana was the preceptor of the Khasīs. || 88 ||
"These great sages, the most excellent of great devotees of Viṣṇu, have been given by me as perpetual gurus to the kings and subjects of those lands.
Those kings, being Vaiṣṇavas themselves, accepted these Vaiṣṇava gurus. || 89 ||
And all those sages, kings, and subjects attained great joy.
Then the Blessed Lord, who knows the hearts of his devotees and dispels the suffering of living beings,
assumed the form of a lotus and mingled with all embodied creatures.
He placed his feet, adorned with all the auspicious marks, upon all their chests;
[the marks were] the eight-sided figure, the upward line, the svastika, the barley-corn, and the thunderbolt.
The rose-apple fruit, the banner, the goad, and the lotus appeared on the right foot;
likewise, the triangle, the jar, the cow’s footprint, and the bow. (93)
A fish, a half-moon, and the sky appeared on the left foot; likewise, a tortoise, Garuḍa, a mountain peak, an elephant, and a swan [appeared]. 94.
These two, Vimāna and Sūrya, were situated below the knot of the foot; they were located at the joint of the ankle and the direction of the big toe of Hari’s right foot.
In the hollow of the left knee, however, there appeared these five on the foot of Hari: Lakṣmī, a palace, a tree, a cow, and a throne. (96)
Then, the right hand— bearing a fish, a banner, a bow, a discus, a svastika, and a trident,
as well as a lotus, an arrow, and a staff— is the bestower of spiritual accomplishments.

Accompanied by the fearless discus, marked with the auspicious line, joined by the peacock, bearing the emblem of the flute, endowed with the wish-fulfilling creeper, and possessed of the horse and the bull. 98.
Then the Lord, having formed the auspicious añjali with both hands and his left hand, placed it upon the heads of the subjects, including the kings and others. || 99 ||
The Lord bestowed upon him a supreme image that grants the fruits of one's desires,
as well as his own *kalpamūrti* for the purpose of worship;
likewise, he granted blessings consisting of an abundance of food, clothing, and prosperity.
And He granted a divine vision, resplendent with His supreme abode.
Wherever the Supreme Lord is pleased out of grace toward Rādhikā, there the gain for all living beings of the three qualities from Hari shall be equal. || 101-102 ||

Thus ends the one hundred and tenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Establishment of Vaiṣṇava Kings in Regions such as Prāgjyotiṣa, the Establishment of Sages, the Showering of Grace, and the Divine Vision," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, to the supreme vision of the divine youth.
Mādhava revealed his form as it exists in the supreme abode.
With limbs proportioned to his form, a beautiful abode of the highest desires, consisting entirely of splendor, and bearing all bliss, peace, and compassion. || 2 ||
Endowed with boundless compassion, likewise a treasure-trove of affection, and filled with infinite, endless friendliness, tenderness, and love. (3)
It is endowed with all fragrances and flavors, possessed of all nourishment and strength, the source of all precious things, and the bestower of pleasure through every touch. || 4 ||
Adorned with ornaments such as a crown, it was enchanting; it was beautifully arrayed in divine garments and resplendent with all the [auspicious] emblems. || 5 ||
Accompanied by Rādhā and Lakṣmī at his sides, joined by Prabhā and Pāravatī,
together with Māṇikī, he is divine and saluted by the beloveds of Brahmā.
It was introduced by the innumerable liberated ones, the abodes, and so forth, as well as by the incarnations, all the male attendants, and the goddesses; likewise, it was bowed to by them all.
It is praised by the principles with attributes and those without attributes, by the guardians of creation,
by the seers, the ancestors, the gods, humans, and all things sentient and insentient.
The Lord was praised by the inhabitants of Pātāla and by the Śaktis;
in him all that is subtle is contained, and from him this entire universe has emerged.
Then [he saw] Bālakṛṣṇa, the son of Śrī Kambharā, who is the soul of all, subtle, filled with wonder, and the locus of all marvels.
The Lord indeed showed him the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, the Aśvapaṭṭa lake, and the supreme, divine-syllabled field.
There were twenty daughters of the Pitṛs, each with ten thousand female attendants;
all those daughters of the Pitṛs then became infatuated with Śrī Hari.
The ten million daughters of Prajāpati chose him as their beloved lord, the one dear to all beings; they chose him alone as their beloved.
They were entrusted to Aryaman, to the progeny, and to Bālakṛṣṇa;
and they were accepted by the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 14.
They had accomplished what was to be done, for that which was to be attained had indeed been attained;
then the Blessed One granted them residence in his own celestial palaces.
Then the Blessed One, being entreated, said on Mount Kārūka:
"For the welfare [of beings], you must always remain here at the source of the Indus with your physical form. (16)
And in the western region, for the protection of the Cāruṇas, O Aryaman, that kingdom shall be yours, bringing them happiness. (17)
Thus the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa gave Kurukarādri, situated on the shore of the Sindhu river, to Aryaman Bhāsvat.
Those women, ruddy-hued, clad in divine garments, and possessing celestial forms, having reached that beautiful place, rejoiced like deities. (19)
What is that bliss? It is the auspicious nourishment and the dwelling place of the stones.
What is the *kashmerā*, the mountain terrain, beautiful with its many peaks? (2.111.20)
There, Āryamā himself always made his residence together with Śrī;
and that purifying Śrībhūmi became forever known as Śrīnagarī. (21)
Having thus established everything, Hari,
desiring to perform a pilgrimage, caused holy fords, rivers, streams, and lakes to be prepared.
Then, having commanded the subjects to return to their respective regions and having directed the kings to depart, Kṛṣṇa set out by means of celestial chariots.
Together with the daughters of Brahmā, the maidens, the gods, the ancestors, and the ṛṣis,
he bathed in the waters of the lake named Lāṣāhā on the Brahmaputrī.
Then he bathed at the mouth of the Sindhu river, and then in the waters of the Terimā;
he bathed in the waters of the Āmūrā and then in the waters of the Homāṅgā.
Then he bathed in the water of Mahatī, then in the water of Aṅgaśikṣāṅgā,
then in the water of Śikṣāṅgā, and then in the water of Manikaṅkvā.
Having bathed in the waters of the Pannā, the Śālāvatī, and the Irāvatī, he arrived at the Sundara forest. ||27||
Hari said to the daughters of the Pitṛs: "O ladies, you shall be dear to me here;
become auspicious ones of dual form, consisting of both the root and its shadow. (28)
Let those whose essence is my root-dwelling reside with me in my field; let those whose essence is my shadow dwell in the form of rivers within the sacred bathing grounds. 29.
The Brahmaputrī, the Lavahītā, the Candrāvatī, the Irāvatī, the Śālāvatī, the Mīnakaṅgū, the Lāṭiśā, and likewise the Kāniśā. ||2.111.30||
Māpīṅgā, Sīkyāṅgā, Aṅgasvāṅgā, Harāṅgikā, Mauktikā, Tārimā, Pannāmā, and likewise Tvāṅgahā. ||3 1||
The one named Mannāmnī, Maṇivarṇā, Raṅgavarṇā, and Sundarī—all you, my beloveds, shall attain fame by these very names of yours. (32)
I have bestowed upon you all this power which destroys sin, grants liberation, bestows merit, confers prosperity, and provides sons and other blessings. || 3 3 ||
O my beloveds, I shall describe the greatness of you all,
for whom there is a direct union with Hari that bestows auspicious divine status.
For those women with whom Nārāyaṇa indeed bestows the yoga that grants liberation,
their divinity is eternal and their state of liberation is equal to that of Kamalā.
You are equal to Rādhikā, equal to Lakṣmī, and likewise equal to Śrī; you are divine, resembling Prabhā, and equal to Pārvatī. (36)
"You are indeed like rubies to me, as dear to me as my own life;
for those who have attained association with you, there is residence in my abode. (37)
Those birds, animals, humans, insects, moths, creatures, and so forth who have bathed in your waters shall go to the supreme state. (38)
Just as the Gaṅgā, the Yamunā, and the virtuous Sarasvatī are so, even so you all are divine saviors who bestow complete liberation. 39.
Just as the Gaṇḍakī, Gomatī, and Svarṇalekhikā are the most excellent [rivers],
so indeed you women are always worthy of being my dwelling place.
Just as the water from my own form is [holy], so too is this water of yours;
this auspicious water of yours is equal to the water from the water-pot of Brahmā. 41.
Just as the water of the Virajā river, like the water of the Brahma-lake, and just as the water from the source down to its confluence with the ocean is purifying for you; ||42||
May there always be for you cleansing in the water of those great sins and even greater evils, such as killing and slaughter, which arise from what ought not to be done. 43.
May even a mere drop of water—whether drunk, touched, seen, smelled, or used for ritual sipping—purify you through my yoga. (44)
Asuras, Rākṣasas, Daityas, Mlecchas, and sinful Dānavas shall attain purification from your waters in age after age. 45.
Pretas, bhūtas, rākṣasas, and others who have gone to evil destinies shall indeed attain liberation in an instant through bathing at any time whatsoever. ||46||
Furthermore, within the Śālāvatya and Aṅga branches of the Veda, I performed my first auspicious sacrifice on the bank of the Menakāṅga. ||47||
Likewise, here near the lake named Lāśahā, this second auspicious Vaiṣṇava great sacrifice was indeed performed. (48)
The first ground is like Vaikuṇṭha, while the supreme second ground is equal to Goloka;
by virtue of your yoga, this divine earth becomes like liberation itself.
And all the inhabitants there are in the form of my attendants;
they are women who are truthful and virtuous, equal to my Brahma-priyās.
The young are like my own children, and the old are like my elders;
those who are equal to me are of equal disposition, for they are purified through union with me.
O ladies, indeed, all embodied beings dwelling on your banks—those born from the womb, from eggs, from sweat, and from sprouts, these four types of living creatures—[attain liberation]. 52.
Those beings who dwell in the water of you all, endowed with devotion, are considered by me to be as pure as Viṣṇu himself. (53)
They shall dwell eternally in Vaikuṇṭha, of this there is no doubt;
for in whichever direction the winds carry even a particle of your remains, [they shall go there].
Those regions are indeed purifying for embodied beings, equal to the world of Viṣṇu,
even if a fragment of one's bones should fall into your waters.
Or rather, when even a small amount of ash from a corpse falls [upon them],
then those living beings, having become purified, shall indeed go to my abode.
By the recollection of you ladies in the morning, whatever beings may perform their ablutions in the waters of a step-well or elsewhere by means of your names, [they shall attain purification]. (57)
Whether at home, on a mountain, in a forest, by the sea, or in a vehicle, they shall obtain the fruit of the sacrifice simply by [reciting] the names beginning with "Daughter of Brahmā. (58)
Then the Gaṅgā is in Ajanābha, and Narāyaṇī in Abrikta;
Irāvatī is in Brahmadeśa, and Brahmaputrikā is in Trivitta. ||59||
In the region of Śyāma is Menakāṅgā, and in the eastern region is Aṅgaśivāṅgikā;
all of them are equal to the Gomatī and bestow residence in Goloka.
By bathing and even by merely remembering [you], a human being shall attain the fruit of all sacred fords (tīrtha);
moreover, someone will offer you a water-pot (ḍhabbuka) on your banks.
A person shall obtain the fruit of bestowing ten million mudrās:
either silver coins, gold coins, gems, or diamonds.
Those who give pearls, rubies, gems, copper,
or cowries as a gift on the bank [of the river] shall obtain a fruit ten million times greater.
Clothing, ornaments, collyrium and the like, cosmetics such as sandalwood paste, sandals, a vehicle, or likewise other articles of utility. ||64||
Whoever shall give with devotion a house, the household requisites, food, flavor, and nourishment, his merit shall be infinite.
He who gives an elephant, a horse, a goat, a milch cow, a maiden,
or a garden as a gift on its bank shall obtain infinite merit.
Furthermore, he will provide knowledge and assistance for those seeking learning, as well as a school on the shore of the Vastu river; for them, heaven shall follow immediately thereafter. (67)
"I am the Lord Nārāyaṇa; those who give gifts upon the bank when my four hands emerge from the water shall go to my abode. (68)
Service to women, children, the helpless, yogins, virtuous wives, and the righteous must be performed, for it bestows infinite merit. (69)
For those who are bodiless, penniless, homeless, and lifeless, service should be rendered on its bank; for that, the merit is infinite.
In the month of Māgha, on the fifth lunar day,
the first sacrifice was commenced on that very day upon the bank of the Menakāṅga river.
There he will perform a sacrifice dedicated to Viṣṇu or even to Rudra;
they shall likewise attain the kingdom of heaven, the kingdom of Brahmā, and liberation.
On that day, the eleventh, they shall complete it;
by providing him with food and other necessities, they will attain the supreme goal.
Then, by undertaking the complete recitation of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā,
they shall cause it to be performed and will attain my abode.
Those devotees who shall cause a festival to be held for me right there in my temple in my presence shall attain eternal liberation. ||75||
And having surely caused a firm temple to be built on that bank, it was endowed with Lakṣmī, Rādhā, Prabhā, Pāravatī, and Śrīmāṇikī. (76)
To those people who shall establish my form as the sevenfold embodiment (saptamūrti), I will grant my own supreme and beautiful abode.
Those people who, on the bank of your [river] at my temple, shall provide for you a continuous flow of worship, sustenance, livelihood, gifts, and food; ||78||
To them I shall grant celestial, delightful, and radiant abodes—divine and eternal, without a doubt. (79)
The offering of lamps in the temple and likewise in the water by you all—
those who shall perform this offering of lamps will indeed possess eternal vision.
I shall create that entire divine garden, filled with wisdom, auspicious, and bestowing liberation, complete with tulasī, campaka, and lotus trees, and endowed with fruit.
I shall lead those devotees who cause [this] to be performed to the imperishable abode;
indeed, [I shall grant this] for the sake of the worship, food, and sacrificial fees of my Vaiṣṇava devotees. (82)
