Those people who shall perform service at the feet or servitude, or who shall perform the service of the virtuous women or the attendants; ||83||
"By means of food, wealth, clothing, and other desired things, I shall lead them to the imperishable state;
and for you, [I shall provide] dwellings and such in a delightful village on the bank. (84)
I shall always wander in the form of a virtuous man as your beloved,
and my wives shall always wander in the form of virtuous women.
For their own welfare, people should perform worship for them with offerings of food and other gifts;
they shall bathe in your waters for the sake of the sacred site (tīrtha). 86.
And my incarnations as devotees, as well as my own incarnations, shall bathe repeatedly in your waters age after age.
Those embodied beings who bathe in these rivers during the month of Māgha,
their sins of ten million lifetimes shall go to destruction.
And those people who, having gone a long distance, bathe at the confluence of rivers or at the time of the Kumbha-lagna, shall go to the supreme state. ||89||
Out of compassion, I have always made the daughters of my father into sacred fords (tīrthas).
Therefore, you shall indeed become dear to me and equal to me; of this there is no doubt.
In the month of Māgha, the gods who dwell in heaven and the ancestors shall also come daily to your waters.
All holy places from all over the worlds will come to you;
your water shall become the essence of ten million sacred sites.
"Truly, everything—such as heaven and the like—will then exist for you within the water;
of this there is no doubt, and therefore you shall be most excellent. (93)
Indeed, virtuous men born in various lands shall dwell upon your banks; these holy ones will increase your great sanctity. (94)
It likewise bestows sons, grandsons, wives, and so forth, as well as wealth, grain, clothing, ornaments, fields, gardens, sovereignty, prosperity, and abundance. (95)
The auspicious bath in your waters, which bestows all desired happiness and grants both heaven and liberation, shall accomplish everything for you.
"For you who have made your dwelling on this bank, liberation will come;
those who cause the tonsure to be performed shall, in every way, be freed from their sins. (97)
They shall go to destruction and thereby attain purity for themselves;
moreover, men and women will receive initiation on your banks.
They are liberated and equal to those dwelling in my abode, even while still possessing bodies;
[they perform] bathing, charity, austerity, fire-offerings, Vedic study, and libations to the ancestors.
Those people who here on this bank shall provide protection for the helpless, protection for cattle, and assistance to the distressed, shall partake in liberation.
Those who bestow sons and those who perform the rite of giving daughters shall,
at the end, attain the state of Brahma’s abode, the eternal station.
But those people who bathe even once in your waters,
having remembered [you], shall bring about the liberation of a hundred generations.
On your banks, there shall be funeral rites for the deceased, meritorious ceremonies, the installation of deities, the planting of trees, the provision of drinking water, and likewise temples. (103)
Those people who provide shelter, a Dharma-hall, and assistance to those in distress here shall attain the supreme goal. (1.04)
Those people who shall cause temples to be built for you, and those who shall honor Kūlavāsā, the family deity, [shall attain success]. (105)
Those who worship with various kinds of new and sweet foods, as well as with water, flowers, fruits, and offerings (arghya), shall indeed attain eternal heaven. 106.
For those sages, my disciples, there shall indeed be no suffering from drought, excessive rain, or other calamities; for them, the worship of the image in the temple [shall be constant]. 107.
"People will honor them, and poverty shall never be seen among them.
Thus, O Rādhikā, did he bestow these words of blessing upon them.

Thus ends the one hundred and eleventh chapter, titled "The Description of Hari’s Bestowing of Divine Vision upon the Daughters of Brahmā and Others, the Gift of Twelve Thousand Maidens, the Granting of the Kingdom of Kashmir to Aryaman, the Transformation of the Daughters of Brahmā and Others into Rivers, Hari’s Bathing in Them, the Bestowal of Boons, and the Fruits of Pilgrimage and Charity," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. 111.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, to that which was requested by those rivers: "O Kṛṣṇa, by Your grace, You have made us all sacred pilgrimage sites. (1)
"And grant us dwellings for all the gods here upon our shores;
O Lord of Light, fulfill this noble resolve of ours. (2)
Having heard this, the great king, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
spoke to Brahmā, Śaṅkara, and Viṣṇu in order to summon all the gods.
The three gods remembered the thirty-three crores of deities;
they all arrived quickly at the place where Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa was.
Having come together in the forest named Sundara, they, desiring the command of Nārāyaṇa, paid homage to him.
Hari spoke to the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the twelve eminent Ādityas, and the two Aśvins for the sake of the world: || 6 ||
"Sirs, for the sake of the desire for liberation, remain in various forms within the waters of the Brahmaputrī and other rivers for the purpose of purifying the world. (7)
From that time forward, the Vasus took up residence at its root;
the foremost Ādityas stayed at the confluences, and the Rudras at the confluence of the ocean.
Then the Aśvins began to dwell in the crooked movements and other [regions],
and likewise the eight guardians of the directions, beginning with Indra, in their respective lakes.
The seven sages dwelt in the groves along the banks where the mountains stood,
while the nine planets made their abode in the vicinity of the city.
The Marut deities dwelt on the banks at the confluence of small rivers,
while the sixty-four Mahāyoginīs resided upon the high ground.
In all his incarnations, there is everywhere the circle of sixty-eight sacred fords (tīrthamaṇḍala),
as well as the Vālakhilyas, the Pitṛs, the Ṛṣis, and the Viśvedevas.
"And the Siddhas dwell upon their paths in the form of sacred fords (tīrtha).
Thus did Śrī Hari himself bestow the tīrthas upon them.
But when acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity are performed in their dwellings,
they produce eternal merit for the patron who performs them.
After the eleventh day of the dark fortnight of Māgha, there occurred once again a fierce battle;
there, for seven days, Mādhava indeed destroyed all the Daityas.
He performed the second sacrifice in the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha;
on the fifth day, that seven-day sacrifice was completed on the day of his vow.
On the eleventh day, he performed the concluding purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) for that [rite],
and thereafter he practiced bathing in the waters for all four days.
On the day of the full moon, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa arrived by celestial chariot at the forest named Sundara.
Therefore, all sacred fords (tīrthas) are truly present here for seven days in the waters of the lake named Lāśahā, which belongs to the Śālāvatyā, the daughter of Brahmā.
They dwell there and arrive, especially during the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha;
they also reside together on four specific days at other rivers.
In that regard, a gift of cows should be given, as well as elephants and horses; likewise, goats, camels, and bulls should also be given. (21)
The gift of woolen blankets, garments, and vehicles is supreme;
likewise, celestial palaces, houses, and fields are also to be given. (22)
The offering of various kinds of grains, of split pulses (dvidala), as well as of vegetables, vessels, and tubers, should also be given. (23)
One should also give grains, delicious things, sugar, feathers, leaves, stalks of sugarcane, and fruits. (24)
The gift of chests, caskets, and bowls is supreme; as is the gift of couches, utensils, gold, and silver. (25)
One should also perform the giving of seals and wealth;
likewise, the gift of knowledge should be bestowed, as well as the excellent gift of servants. (26)
The gift of a maidservant should be given; the gift of liberation is most excellent.
The gift of knowledge, the gift of stories, the gift of a son, and the gift of one's own self [should be given]. (27)
The gift of a maiden should be bestowed upon a worthy bridegroom;
likewise, the gift of a mansion, the gift of a bed, and the gift of a couch [should be given]. (28)
That which is to be performed through both divine and human means yields fruit when the divine element is true;
likewise, the gift of a divine image bestows heaven as well as liberation. (29)
One should perform the gift of the body, the gift of the waist for the Supreme Self;
the gift of everything should be bestowed upon Śrīśa, the Supreme Soul. (2.112.30)
One should always offer the gift of one's own self to the guru who bestows liberation; likewise, the gift of reciting the scriptures should always be performed for the reciter. (31)
In the month of Māgha, all types of gifts should certainly be given; indeed, by those with desires, they should be performed in all months, for the imperishable fruit is obtained.
The gift of blood, the gift of tears, the gift of one's own womb as well as that of a woman,
the gift of sexual pleasure, and the giving of medicines and so forth should be bestowed.
The Nārāyaṇabali śrāddha, which grants liberation to the deceased, should be performed; likewise, shelters, dwellings, dharma-śālās, and sacrificial halls should be established on its banks. (34)
Feasts of food should be provided, as well as shelters for the elderly; one should establish centers for the dissemination of knowledge, and likewise provide refuge for widowed daughters. (35)
The wealthy should establish shelters for widows and those bereft of husbands, providing them with means for their livelihood on the banks of rivers. (36)
The currents of service to the world must be set in motion everywhere; men and women alike should perform acts of assistance for others. (37)
Those very same acts performed at sacred fords (tīrtha) indeed yield ten million times the fruit;
likewise, the gift of a measure of time and the gift of a measure of lightning [yield great results]. (38)
The gift of armlets should be bestowed at sacred sites;
likewise, the gift of mechanical devices and the gift of images should be performed. (39)
The gift of instruments for hearing and seeing from afar is likewise excellent;
as is the gift of agricultural implements and the like, which is a great and supreme means of accomplishment.

Then, one should offer fragrant substances and the like, the essence of flowers, which is most excellent—the essence of fragrance, the essence of flavor, the essence of essences, higher than the highest. (41)
The Brahmaputrī should be installed, four-armed and exceedingly beautiful;
the Lavahītā should be installed, two-armed, charming, and virtuous. 42.
Candrāvatī, endowed with sixteen arms, should be installed;
Irāvatī, a beautiful maiden with eight hands, should be installed. (43)
Śālāvatī and Manoharā are to be established as four-armed; Menakā and Aṅgamanikā are to be established as four-armed. 44.
The Lāṭīśā and Kāniśā should be established as auspicious maidens with two arms;
furthermore, the Māpīṅgā and Sīkyāṅgā should be established as possessing eight hands.
When she is established with eighteen arms, her limbs and minor limbs are those of Hara;
when established with two arms, she is made of pearls and captivates the mind. (46)
One named after Prajñā, possessing limbs and beautiful in form, should be installed as two-armed;
and one named after me, with the color of a jewel, should be installed as auspicious ten-armed.
Likewise, the river Satī, possessing four arms and the colors of various pigments, should be installed;
such, O beloved, are the forms of the rivers who are the wives of Kṛṣṇa.
O Rādhikā, having manifested the state of blossoming youthfulness in every respect, their faces are endowed with beautiful smiles, gentleness, and affection. 49.
Having caused images of the color of white campaka flowers and endowed with the luster of gold to be made, as well as auspicious temples.
These beautiful places were established on earth by the eternal Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa together with Kiśora for the sake of human beings. 5.1.
For those rivers are indeed the mothers of the people living in their respective regions;
when constantly honored and saluted, they will provide protection to the subjects. (52)
Ornaments should be given to them by women desiring a husband;
for when honored, they always bestow good fortune upon women. (53)
They bestow freedom from widowhood and likewise increase longevity;
they grant sons and grandsons, as well as health, wealth, and grain. (54)
To them, girdles should be given, as well as bodices and tunics;
hair oil should be provided, along with combs for grooming the hair and other such items. (55)
Flower garlands, collyrium, oil, and the essence of fragrance;
small bells, armor, clothing, and likewise Matsaravāriṇī.
People should offer to the river a bed, an excellent soft bolster with its cord concealed, an upper garment, and a hair-braided girdle. (57)
A lion-throne should be fashioned, as well as a parasol made of gold and other precious materials;
likewise, a crown, a headband, a girdle, a waist-band, bracelets, and so forth.
Finger-rings, bracelets, chains, and anklets; necklaces made of gold, as well as svastikas and crescents.
Bindus, moon-shaped cloths, and nail-paints, as well as foods and drinks, should be offered by people in the temples of the rivers. (2.112.60)
There was also a *kaṅkati* and a *doraka*, as well as a silver *cipīṭaka*,
and a *caḍḍikā* on the feet adorned with a network of beautiful small bells.
Incense, lamps, food offerings, as well as the waving of lights (nīrājana) and so forth,
the water-pot, and other articles should be offered in the abode of the rivers.
Maidens should offer saffron, unbroken grains of rice, and sugar; and those with fragrant scents should present auspicious items such as ornaments, garments, and decorations.
Indeed, the most excellent [gifts] should be given to the rivers beloved by Hari;
swings, horses, and the like, as well as cradles and protection, should also be offered.
The wind-vehicle, the steam-vehicle, and likewise the auspicious fire-vehicle;
the heat-vehicle, the light-vehicle, and the most excellent atom-vehicle. ||65||
It should be given for the sake of a monastery, as well as for movement through the sky, water, and air;
and vehicles for water, vehicles for horses, and those for traveling upon the earth should be given. (66)
One should fully satisfy the daughter of the Pitṛs, who is both the form of water and the embodied form;
when those wives of the Lord are satisfied, the Lord himself is pleased. (67)
Great festivals for them should be held during both the dark and bright fortnights of the month of Māgha;
before them, dancing and the playing of musical instruments must be performed.

At that time, there was the chanting of the Lord's names, singing of His praises, and the recitation of Sāman Vedic hymns; and those [women] were adorned with millions of diamonds, gems, and other jewels. (69)

Adorned with flowers, fragrances, and beautiful ornaments, these beloveds of Hari should be worshipped at the time of dawn on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, accompanied by the beloveds of Brahmā.
The Lord Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, accompanied by the daughter of the Pitṛs, is to be worshipped with supreme devotion and adorned with the finest of objects. (7.1)
Then the Blessed One was made to appear as a lover, like a sovereign king of kings,
adorned with golden necklaces and the like, as well as garments of golden thread.
Furthermore, Kṛṣṇa is to be propitiated with one hundred and eight kinds of foods, both solid and soft, as well as with services and most excellent songs.
With charming crowds, well-mingled with men and women, in every city, in every village, in the forest, and even in dwellings; (74)
In the cowherd settlement, in the city, in the town, and especially in the royal capital,
Nārāyaṇa Hari dwelt together with those various noble wives.
With elephant-vehicles, horse-vehicles, and likewise with golden carts and silver carts,
accompanied by jars, banners, and attendants.
He must indeed be paraded with auspicious musical accompaniments, and the chariot must be steadied by attendants at every crossroads. (77)
At every market, at every street, at every shop, and at the city gate—as well as at every royal palace—he should be worshipped with bilva fruits and other offerings. (78)
A shower of flowers mixed with unbroken rice, parched grain, and other offerings should be made;
furthermore, sandalwood and scented water must indeed be used for the ritual sprinkling.
Sweet food and sweet drink must be given from the chariot to those who seek them;
and favor must always be bestowed upon devotees on the road. (2.112.80)
With musical instruments and silver trumpets to be sounded before him, this supreme festival of circumambulation is accompanied by incense and lamps. (8.1)
The great festival of Kṛṣṇa’s birth should be celebrated in the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika;
indeed, having thus paraded the Blessed One together with his beloved, [one should perform the rites].
At night, [the deity] should be installed upon an elephant-throne in a spacious pavilion;
thereafter, the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) should be performed with one hundred and eight wicks.
There, the *rāsa* dance should be performed with clapping, staffs, and other instruments; and various musical instruments should also be used while the story of Hari is narrated. (84)
Having performed the worship, one should then carry out the ritual dismissal;
the Blessed One, together with his consorts, should be led to that temple at night.
Then, the devotees should likewise perform a vigil, or else,
having gone to their own homes, they should sleep while remaining devoted to celibacy.
Having bathed in the morning, bowed to Hari, and performed the rites of viewing and worship,
one should then perform acts such as giving charity on the ninth day, even at dawn.
There is no end to that merit, for it bestows supreme liberation;
thus, during such a great festival, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is pleased.
The rivers become tranquil and bestow exceedingly great wealth;
they grant ever-new prosperities of riches, grain, and other such things. (89)
Health, sons, grandsons, and so forth, as well as cattle, buffaloes, and wealth; horses, elephants, camels, and vehicles; celestial chariots and royal splendors—[all these are obtained]. (2.112.90)
When satisfied along with the Lord of Śrī, these best of rivers surely bestow fame, gold, honor in the world, supreme renown, and stability. (91)
Thus the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself spoke:
"In every house, my image, along with the river, must be protected."
She is always to be worshipped—in the morning, at midday, and likewise in the evening.
I shall fulfill her mind and grant her her own desired object again and again. (92)
Thus spoke the Blessed One to those virtuous women there in the beautiful forest; afterwards, they indeed bathed at the ocean of the daughters of Brahmā.
And all those traveling in celestial chariots bathed at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean together with the Blessed Lord Svāmī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. 95.
Having meditated for a moment, they worshipped the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
they fixed the form of Nārāyaṇa firmly within their hearts. (96)
Thus, O Rādhikā, this account of Hari’s deeds has been told to you by me;
it is auspicious and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation through hearing or even reciting it. 97.
Bestowing both heaven and liberation, and destroying the torment of sin, it should indeed always be recited by devotees as well as by those seeking liberation. 98.

Thus ends the one hundred and twelfth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Installation and Worship of the Embodiments of the Second Sacrificial Ground, Upalāśa, Hāsa Lake, and the River," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Then, O Śrī Rādhikā, those beloved daughters of the Pitṛs asked Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa with great reverence.
O beloved, our greatness has been increased by you through your grace;
now we shall come to know the greatness of the Illustrious One as well. (2)
"O Soul of All, tell us how liberation may come to us at the end.
Thus addressed, the Lord, the Sovereign, who is devoid of birth, destruction, and the like, [spoke].
He said: "From them comes the knowledge of one's true nature, which is aided by devotion.
Indeed, there are realms of the lords beyond the world of living beings. (4)
Vāsudeva and others dwell there in crores of divine manifestations;
and I, Kṛṣṇa, reside in Goloka, served by Rādhā.
In Vaikuṇṭha, I indeed dwell as Nārāyaṇa, united with Śrī;
and in that supreme, imperishable abode, I exist as Puruṣottama.
I am known as the one who transcends the imperishable (akṣara), the two-armed Supreme Lord; I am beyond even that which is beyond the imperishable, in the supreme abode.
I am served by innumerable liberated souls and attended by the beloved of Brahmā;
from even a single pore of my hair, the divine splendor has emerged.
That [power] pervades all lords and arises as if full;
by a mere fragment of my single quality, they become lords through the excellence of their qualities.
Indeed, my incarnations occur by my mere volition;
and truly, countless creations come into being through the will of my Puruṣa.
Innumerable beings are born there, and I abide as their inner controller; I dwell within and without all creatures, each in its proper place.
O my beloveds, having become according to their purpose, according to their expectation, and according to their devoted service, I dwell among the multitudes of devotees.
In some places I exist among the lords (īśas), in others among the gods in heaven;
in some places among the most excellent sages who are devoted, and in some places among the human races.
In water, on land, in the forest, on a mountain, on the earth, and in a cave;
among beasts, birds, aquatic creatures, trees, creepers, and grasses—[he is present]. 14.
According to the task at hand, I indeed become a man, a woman, or another;
a king, a subject, or a pauper; a virtuous man, a virtuous woman, or a passionate lover. (15)
O beloved ones, whether it be in a kalpa, a yuga, a day, or at an auspicious moment, my descent as Gopāla, Gobāla, Gojāla, or the husband of Gopikā is certain.
Now I am Bālakṛṣṇa, the son of the virtuous Śrīkaṃbharā; I am the beloved of ten million lotus-eyed maidens, existing for the sake of fulfilling the desire of the maiden.
I am indeed the Supreme Soul, the human form of Śrīmad Gopāla Kṛṣṇa, known as Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa and Puruṣottama. || 18 ||
He who is the object of your attainment, whose compassion is feigned as a mere pretense,
resides in Saurāṣṭra at the sacred site of Kuṅkumavāpī, adorned with the Aśvapaṭṭa.
I dwell in the Akṣara-kṣetra near the hermitage of Lomaśa;
though immeasurable, I have assumed a state of being measured while performing the dance of Nara.
By her who bestows the fruits of the penance of the maidens of former kalpas, I have been granted the beauty of ten million Kandarpas and infinite valor. (21)
Endowed with the six fortunes, the eight powers, and the eight accomplishments, he is the locus of qualities of strength as numerous as the atoms in ten million lotuses. ||22||
For the sake of fulfilling the inner nature of maidens, I have been born here in person as Kāntaka;
and by the power of my ascetic penance, I now stand as your husband.
Service must be rendered to me by you for the attainment of happiness;
indeed, service to me with affection is considered by me to be true devotion. 24.
And by her alone shall I be pleased, not by any other means whatsoever, just as a virtuous and devoted wife always serves her own husband. (25)
With such exclusive devotion, one desiring liberation should always worship me;
that [devotion], which consists of supreme passion, must be directed toward me in every way. (26)
And the hearing of the account of my births and deeds must be performed by my devotee or my devotee’s wife; for that indeed bestows liberation.
Just as the hearing of my incarnations and deeds is for one seeking liberation, so too is the hearing of the wonders of my devotees auspicious. (28)
Those seeking liberation should listen to the accounts and narratives of noble conduct; likewise, the glorification of those who are virtuous like me is dear to me. (29)
Discourses and narratives concerning the births, deeds, and conduct [of the Lord] should be delivered from the mouths of the virtuous at appropriate times, repeatedly and with faith. (2.113.30)
The reading of my devotees as well as of my books, and likewise the teaching of the lives of my consorts, indeed bestows liberation. (31)
I shall always joyfully sing the songs of my own works—both those composed in verse according to the rules of prosody and those in prose, written in both Sanskrit and Prakrit. (32)
My kīrtana should be performed accompanied by musical instruments such as the lute (vīṇā), or with rhythmic clapping (tālikā), and with the sounds of singing and cymbals (cipīṭā). 33.
Accompanied by the sound of small bells tied to her anklets on her feet,
and by the jingling of the girdle-bands fastened around her waist.
Or it should be performed together with dance and accompanied by the chanting of my praises; likewise, there should be my hymn of praise, my prayer, and the recitation of my names. (36)
Out of affection for me, you should compose works in verse as well as delightful prose;
furthermore, you should keep me in mind and meditate upon me within the lotus of your heart.
O beloved ones, my form, together with its limbs and sub-limbs, should be meditated upon within your own hearts;
one should contemplate each individual limb, beginning from the hair down to the nails of the feet.
In the meditation on my form, my smile should be contemplated especially;
my names and deeds should be remembered at all times.
The miracles of my devotees and of myself are to be remembered;
one should practice the recollection of my qualities, and likewise, my mantra should be chanted.
Of the supreme abode, the abode of the Imperishable, Goloka, and the Immortal;
likewise of Vaikuṇṭha, the Unmanifest, and Śvetadvīpa.
Of my abode named Viśāla, of my [abode] named Sāketa, of that named Nityakailāsa, and likewise of my Kṣīroda; ||41||
And Śrīpura is dear to me as the abode of my Śaktis, my attendants, the wives of the Brahmas, my sovereign powers, my perfections, and my manifestations.
On festive occasions, one should remember me, the divine sages,
my temples, and my parents along with their families.
May there always be remembrance of my cattle, such as my vehicles and so forth, as well as of my attire, my weapons, and all things connected to me. (44)
"Indeed, liberation must be achieved by her, for she is divine and bestows liberation upon me. Now, O beloveds, you must perform a massage of my feet. (45)
"Here, you must repeatedly perform the massaging of the feet of my manifest form, Lord Hari, the true Master, who has been Kṛṣṇa here from time immemorial. (46)
Remaining there, I accept service such as massaging and so forth;
my image should be fashioned with all its limbs adorned with the auspicious marks. (47)
Whether made of stone, wood, or even clay, the image of Kiśorikā should always and in every way be served by men and women alike. (88)
One should perform acts of service filled with affection, as desired by the mind;
or, having fashioned a mental image of me, created through meditation. (49)
The touch of her feet and the touch of all her limbs should be performed with devotion, and one should take delight with her.
My mind should be cultivated in every way to serve me; you must especially provide for my food, honor me, and please me. (51)
"Though I, Kṛṣṇa, abide in your hearts, I shall accept your service;
indeed, having placed me upon your bed, you must sleep with me constantly. (52)
Even in legal proceedings, that [act] must indeed be performed with me placed at the forefront;
one must eat only after having first honored me, and never otherwise.
"I am always present in the body and likewise in all the senses;
having thus placed me within both the enjoyer and the objects of enjoyment, one should perform one's actions. (54)
All that shall be devoid of qualities (nirguṇa), bestowing liberation and bestowing merit;
one should proceed placing me at the forefront, and one should abide in me in every way. (55)
"In this manner, my service must be performed—the massaging of my body—through service to me, who am Vāsudeva’s younger sister and possess the form of the Vyūha. (56)
While she attains the power to create, sustain, nourish, and withdraw the universe,
the Gaṅgā, purified by my big toe, sanctifies the entire world.
Time, illusion, evil karma, enemies, treacherous hearts, fear, and so forth—these quickly perish for those who take refuge at my feet through service. (58)
Rādhā, Ramā, Prabhā, Pāravatī, Śrīmāṇikī, and Priyā—these, along with one hundred and twelve other wives of Brahmā, [are present]. (59)
Other women, numbering in the millions and billions, attend upon my feet—
indeed, even those who have attained liberation always attend upon those two feet.
Indeed, countless Devapriyas and countless Gopīs attained even greater fame through their service at my feet. ||6 1||
Those two feet of mine which the Vyāsas indeed praise by the hundreds of thousands—those two feet should be massaged and served by those who desire liberation. 62.
My feet are to be served by you, and likewise my arms;
my head is always to be served, as is my back through massage.
My limbs, as well as my secondary and tertiary limbs, are dear to me;
the devoted service of any one of these limbs of mine bestows liberation.
Then my worship must be performed by the Sāttvatīs and the Sāttvatas;
the external worship is performed with sixteen [articles], as well as with one hundred and eight.
One should perform the worship with heart-pleasing, excellent, and delightful offerings;
having invoked me into my mobile image, one should worship me there. 66.
One should bathe [the image] with ghee, milk, and other substances, and likewise sprinkle it with water;
thereafter, one should have excellent garments prepared and duly offered.
One should properly place various ornaments on their respective parts,
and apply an ointment to the body consisting of sandalwood and saffron from Kashmir.
According to the season, one should apply an unguent with oil as a forehead mark containing a central dot,
as well as fragrant necklaces, crests, and ear-ornaments.
One should offer me a lamp, excellent incense, and the finest food offering;
one should perform the great lustration ceremony accompanied by the sounding of songs and musical instruments.
One should perform circumambulation, praise, prayer, prostration, and so forth, and offer handfuls of flowers; thus, worship should be performed at the five appointed times.
One should perform it three times a day, or twice a day, or indeed only in the morning;
on my birthday, a great worship must be performed here.
On the day of breaking the fast, virtuous and truthful persons should be fed during the observances of Ekādaśī, preceded by songs and instrumental music.
"The wealthy should cause strong temples to be built for me;
there, a wealthy person should perform the consecration with great festivals. (74)

One should give a village, a field, wealth, or a house to those desiring the means for worship; one should establish a beautiful source of income for the sake of ensuring the continuity of worship. (79)
One should cause wells, ponds, flower gardens, and beautiful lakes to be made, as well as basins and cisterns, for my sake and for the benefit of the virtuous.
One should cause excellent Vaiṣṇava sacrifices to be performed with abundant sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā),
and one should also perform the recitation of mantras and the reading of hymns.
One should likewise perform the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) repeatedly for my names,
as well as for the mantras and even for the sacred texts, with devotion.
The ancestors are deities to be worshipped, as are the sages who possess aged bodies;
thus is external worship described, while that which is mental is internal.
Filled with an ocean of love, you should perform my worship within your heart using the one hundred and eight supreme mental offerings.
Then, my salutation should be performed with the eight limbs— the six limbs plus two more—
namely, with the two feet, the two hands, the two knees, the chest, the head, and the eyes.
"With speech and with mind"—thus [it is said] that men should always [bow] like a staff;
with feet, hands, mind, speech, head, and sight. (8.2)
Women must indeed prostrate themselves by sitting down together before me; they must roll about on the ground, which has been made sacred by contact with my feet. (83)
Those very dust particles should be placed upon the body and the head;
indeed, they are like water that has touched my limbs, and like sandalwood paste that has touched my limbs.
"The fragrant powder for the stage and the water should also be carried.
"Oh, what supreme good fortune! I have obtained this powder, this very dust! (85)
"Ah! How fortunate is he who has been touched by the lotus feet of the Blessed One!"—speaking thus, a person becomes eternally blissful and liberated from worldly existence. (86)
Therefore, I must always perform service in such a way that the sage Lomaśa remains ever present in the state of a servant,
just as Lakṣmī herself is ever-present.
One should certainly not harbor pride in that service, for it causes injury;
at all times, one should remain like a servant in the service required. (88)
Every kind of service, whether appropriate or inappropriate, must be performed by me in every way—as a female slave, as a servant, and even as a wife. (89)
I, the Supreme Lord, am always to be served with devotion by a person;
for the purpose of my bathing, one should personally fetch water.
One should also gather flowers and weave a garland oneself beforehand;
one should likewise grind tulasī and sandalwood into a paste.
Being devoted, one should cook the food oneself and feed me with morsels;
one should give water for drinking and so forth, and even cause me to take sips of water.
A devotee should personally offer me betel-leaf as an oral fragrance, and should fan me appropriately with palm-leaf fans and other such items. 93.
One should perform the sweeping of my temple and its anointing;
one should carry out restoration of what is decayed or construct a new temple and so forth. (94)
One should perform auspicious service for devotees with food, water, fruits, and so forth; having abandoned pride, one should indeed bow down to them with sincere devotion. (95)
"One should cause the offering of one's body, wife, children, wealth, and so forth, to be made into servitude.
To me who conducts myself in this manner, I grant equanimity. (96)
Therefore, all friendship must be established with me openly;
one should act exactly so here and in the hereafter, for he is equal to me.
You should direct greater affection toward me than toward your body, wife, husband, children, and so forth;
for while I am performing the drama of human life, you must not perceive faults in my actions. 98.
"O my beloveds, you must never entertain any doubt regarding my actions—whether I am the agent, the non-agent, or otherwise—insofar as I am dependent upon my devotees. (99)
Whether out of desire, anger, greed, delusion, self-interest, or the wish for happiness—in whatever way people surrender unto me, in that very same way do I reciprocate with them. (2.113.10)

No doubt should be entertained in this matter regarding this friendship and affection toward me; for whatever I do is for the sake of my devotees, for the purpose of the welfare of my devotees. || 10.1 ||
People do not understand that profound course of mine;
therefore, one must place full confidence in my actions in every way.
Now, indeed, the entire task is this: whether by a man or even by a woman, the body must be offered to me in every way as a surrender of the self.
In that same way, the senses are to be offered to Me, as well as the internal organs;
one's own natures are to be offered to Me, and indeed, even the family is to be offered to Me.
That which is to be offered should not indeed be dependent on the devotee;
I am the Lord, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 105.
He should always remain under my authority, performing all his actions for my sake;
with all his activities directed toward me, such a devotee is dear to me.
"In this way, you must always conduct yourselves toward me with affection;
for I am your beloved, and I shall indeed grant you eternal happiness."
Thus spoke Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself, the Supreme Lord:
"O Rādhikā, the various forms of devotion are especially manifold. (108)

Thus ends the one hundred and thirteenth chapter, titled "An Analysis of the Various Forms of Devotion that Bring About the Lord’s Complete Satisfaction," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. 113.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Thus did Śrī Narāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, speak in detail;
O Rādhikā, listen now to that which he spoke even further.
One should abandon even one's own kin who create obstacles to my devotion;
one should behold me with both eyes in my physical form, complete with its major and minor limbs.
One should constantly hear my stories and accounts of my deeds with one's two ears;
one should experience the touch of me upon all the limbs of the body with the skin.
One should perform the recitation of my qualities with the tongue as the muttering of mantras; one should consume the food of my grace with the mouth and drink the water [of devotion]. || 4 ||
May my nose accept the grace [of your presence], the leaf born of the Tulasī plant, the flower, the fragrance, and the sandalwood offered to me. || 5 ||
With both hands, one should perform a pleasant massage of my body;
with the head, one should offer salutation to me, and likewise, one should circumambulate me on foot.
May she cause my resolve to be formed by the mind, my supreme determination by the intellect,
and my contemplation of my beloved by the consciousness.
He should always maintain the conceit of being my servant toward himself;
indeed, he should perform all agricultural labors and virtuous deeds solely for my sake.
The daughters of the Pitṛs shall indeed exert effort for my sake;
whatever object may be dear to them, they should always offer that to me.
Having accepted this auspicious grace of mine— consisting of fragrance, flowers, ornaments, garments, and likewise unguents— one should thereafter wear them.
Whether it be a leaf, a flower, or even water, whatever is not offered to me must not be eaten, nor drunk, nor worn—even if it be a diamond or other such thing. (11)
One should perform austerity, one should perform sacrifice, one should give gifts, and likewise perform recitation;
indeed, for the sake of my gratification, one should perform everything for the sake of the Supreme.
O sinless ones, my devotees must indeed practice the service of the Sātvatas as well as the service of virtuous women, for the sake of my own gratification. (13)
I am indeed ever present within the devotee, the virtuous man, and likewise the virtuous woman;
my limbs and all my senses are always situated within their bodies. 14.
They truly abide there, of this there is no doubt; therefore, they should be served every day.
The virtuous should be served by those who have desires, for in my opinion, they are like wish-fulfilling trees.
Holy men fulfill desires and bestow heaven and liberation;
virtuous women are like wish-fulfilling trees to be served by a woman who possesses desire. (16)
From them, all desires are surely fulfilled; there is no doubt.
By their constant blessings, the desires of those [devotees] indeed bear fruit.
The aims of human life known as dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa bear fruit;
within them and in those [deities], I myself, the supreme Nārāyaṇa, truly dwell. || 18 ||
And according to their respective capacities, I fulfill the desires of my devotees;
and at the end of the body, I grant them the eternal abode of great bliss.
There they indeed obtain their desired pleasures, which are truly inexhaustible;
namely, residence in the same world (sālokya), sharing the same power (sārṣṭi), proximity (sāmīpya), similarity of form (sārūpya), and identity with that [divine essence] (tadātmatā). || 2.114.20 ||
"I shall indeed grant these very things to them, for I am pleased by their service;
yet there are others who are superior—those highly fortunate ones who are my supreme devotees. || 21 ||
Without my service, they desire nothing else—not the splendors of supernatural powers (siddhi), nor do they ever seek the fourfold liberation (mukti). || 22 ||
My devotees do not desire even the supreme and mighty sovereignty being granted or already given by me, just as Lakṣmī does not;
for perfections (siddhis) are indeed obstacles because they create impediments.
Even sovereign powers, though they appear as obstacles, do not affect you even in your heart. || 24 ||
My heart, that auspicious little chamber of the Self, is filled with bliss;
my beloveds indeed become permeated with the bliss of my form. || 25 ||
Those people who worship me with such a desireless disposition are declared by me to be the best of devotees, because my heart is completely filled by them.
For one who thus honors and serves me constantly, affection increases ever more, so that no obstacle arises therein.
Just as the waters of the Brahmaputrī, having broken through many Himalayan mountains, flow toward the Āsāma region and enter the beautiful ocean; || 28 ||
Likewise, for devotees, love indeed pierces through obstacles arising from place, time, and association, as well as others, and enters into Me, the Infinite. 29.
All the functions of both internal and external principles, as well as their inherent natures and mental impressions, truly find their rest in me alone.
While I am present before you, having arrived in person and standing in close proximity, there exists among my own kind—a class of beings called humans—who behave like those of my own genus. (31)
Having attained the fullness of affection, my devotees have found happiness in the ocean of my bliss;
they will not be attached to anything else, for they can never be apart from me.
Two kinds of objects are obtained by people, for they are indeed twofold: secluded and non-secluded;
the first is considered to be delightful, favorable to oneself, and bestowing happiness. (33)
The second [type of companion] is neither favorable nor pleasant, but brings suffering;
that indeed must be abandoned by its very nature—for what need is there to mention this for everyone? (34)
Indeed, although this [world] is always desired by all embodied beings, even then it appears to those possessed of discernment as the source of great suffering. (35)
Indeed, for yogins, only the mere maintenance of the body is to be forcibly undertaken;
yet even that appears to their intellect as something distinct and a source of suffering. (36)
This quality of loveliness never resides in things that are merely lovely;
rather, wherever I am, there alone does this loveliness exist for these great-souled ones. (37)
Without me, sandalwood—though delightful, cool, and filled with fragrance—quickly turns into poison when touched; yet when joined with me, it becomes like nectar. (38)
Without me, flower garlands as well as golden necklaces and the like become nooses when placed around one's neck; yet, when joined with me, they become the hands of a bride.
An ornament made of gold, pearls, and diamonds, when devoid of me, is indeed like a lizard; but when joined with me, it brings happiness like the moon.
Even a beautiful flower-bed, though delightful when shared with my beloved,
acts like the Raurava hell when devoid of me, even if it is fashioned from garments washed in fire.
The autumnal moonlight, devoid of me, flows with nectar; yet when united with me, it becomes like poison and heat. 42.
A palace worthy of Indra's residence becomes like a cave when deprived of me;
likewise, a dwelling for people becomes like a wilderness of wild beasts when deprived of me. (43)
The fragrant and cool breeze, when separated from me, acts like fire;
even the finest garment, when separated from me, acts like a piercing spear.
"Deprived of me, his kinsmen act like wolves in every way;
his gentle and charming form, bereft of me, acts like leprosy. (45)
Delicious food, when devoid of me, becomes like poison to a devotee;
even nectar-like drink, when lacking me, turns into vomit.
Even a gait full of sweetness, when deprived of me, acts like an arrow;
even a woman who is a goddess, when deprived of me, becomes as if burning with grief.
Everything that is pleasant becomes painful, and likewise, everything peaceful appears cruel; for one devoid of me, even the sweetest thing turns bitter. 48.
A festival devoid of me always becomes like a broken celebration;
likewise, even joy when deprived of me tastes bitter, as it were. (49)
Every pleasant occurrence, even when occurring without me, results in death for my devotee;
yet every pleasant thing, when occurring without me, turns into misfortune for the devotee alone. (2.114.50)
In this way, the boundless affection of the devotee for me should be understood;
indeed, I alone manifest both within and without the devotee. 51.
Whenever I am suddenly seen by my devotee within [his heart], then, beholding me, the devotee sometimes indeed laughs out of love. (52)
In some places, seeing me as if departing for afar, she weeps;
in others, through the attainment of bliss, she dances and sings. ||53||
In one place he converses with me, who possesses a divine form;
in another he performs the eight-limbed prostration, and in another he embraces me. (54)
In one place she kisses me, and in another she sleeps with devotion;
at times, rising suddenly, she then offers me water.
In some places he gives me baths, food, ornaments, and the like;
in other places, becoming intent on meditation, he delights within me.
Sometimes, maintaining silence, she summons me within her heart;
sometimes, drawing me toward her with affection, she leads me indeed into solitude.
Sometimes, having herself become a maidservant, she performs service for me;
at times she acts with friendliness, at times with superiority, and at times with equanimity. (58)
In some cases, having recognized one's own fault, one even says, "Forgive me";
in some cases, one requests an object; and in some cases, one becomes subject to another's will. (59)
Sometimes becoming unrestrained, he utters only the names:
"O Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Svāmī, Pati, Prabhu! (2.114.60)
O Supreme Brahman, O Supreme Self, my Lord, Beloved, Hari, All-pervading One;
O Nārāyaṇa, O Mahāviṣṇu, O Kṛṣṇa, O Glorious Nārāyaṇa! ||6 1||
"O Supreme Lord, ocean of compassion, where are you? Tell me that to me!
Having addressed him thus, he serves me according to his own desire. (62)
In this world, there shall be no shame for him that hinders my service—whether he be such a devotee of mine, or a female devotee, or a servant. (63)
He purifies the entire world and the cosmic egg with his waters that flow to the furthest shores;
indeed, by the dust of his feet, all wicked calamities are set ablaze.
Indeed, by the mere sight of him, people become purified instantly;
through the refuge of such a devotee, supreme liberation is attained.
Through service, service unto Me alone shall be accomplished here; of this there is no doubt.
There is no difference between him and Me; he is indeed My very body.
"I possess those very senses; of this there is no doubt.
With his two eyes I see, and with his skin I touch. (67)
I hear with his two ears and taste with his tongue;
I speak indeed with his speech and smell with his olfactory faculty.
Right there, with my nose I perceive various intensities of fragrance;
with my eyebrows I express [my intent], and I grasp it with his very hand.
I always go with his two feet to the fields of the gods,
and I bring delight to his very senses through the functioning of desire.
I indeed discharge excrement through that organ, the anus;
yet I contemplate it with my own mind by means of that very mind. (7.1)
And with that [mind], I always perform contemplation upon Him with my mind;
indeed, I maintain the sense of "I" everywhere with His heart as my own. (72)
O beloveds, I always determine for him by my own intellect:
sound, touch, taste, form, smell, and even bliss. (73)
Standing there, I accepted him as my husband, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa;
thus all his actions were divine, for they were indeed my own actions. (74)
Devotional states that take the form of liberation are not at all illusory; indeed, they are beneficial.
One should perform service to Him, for through that I obtain satisfaction.
By the offering of that [Self], there shall indeed be the offering of all for embodied beings;
for I am manifest, and I exist as the true nature of the virtuous.
In that way, I am indeed absent and separated from my virtuous ones;
yet those virtuous ones are truly present before me as divine forms.
One should perform service to those Blessed Ones through all ritual actions and so forth;
no doubt should be entertained in this regard, for they are indeed identical in essence to my own form. (78)
Neither the Brahmins, nor the sages, nor the great seers, nor the teachers, nor the gurus are as excellent as my virtuous friends. (79)
Among the social orders, the Brāhmaṇa is the best; among Brāhmaṇas, the Sāttvatas;
and among the Sāttvatas, my devotees who have offered their very selves are supreme. (2.114.80)
Among those who offer themselves, the virtuous who have received initiation are indeed the best;
among the virtuous, I alone am the best—there is no other equal to me, nor anyone superior to me. 8.1
The virtuous are equal to me and most excellent; indeed, I always chant their names and constantly behold the virtuous who dwell within me. (82)
I perform the remembrance of those great-souled ones who have offered everything to me, who grant liberation, and whose very selves are dedicated to me; [I perform] their service and friendship. 83.
I perform the chanting of the names and the salutation of those holy men;
I perform the massaging of the feet of the holy men who are my very selves. (84)
Out of my own secrecy, I shall even make this disclosure to you;
for I have no affection for the virtuous, due to my contemplation of ultimate reality.
Known by the name Parameśvara, they indeed grant liberation through my name; they are called Nārāyaṇas, for those virtuous ones are truly dear to me. (86)
Through their mouths I partake of food, and I am satisfied within them;
neither gods, nor gandharvas, nor cāraṇas, nor guhyakas and the like [are my enjoyers]. (87)
The ancestors, sages, and brahmins are indeed not superior to the virtuous man for me;
nor are the lords, the world-protectors, and the rest superior to the virtuous man for me. (88)
Even those who have attained liberation and reached emancipation are not superior to a saintly person in my eyes;
what then need be said of Lakṣmī herself, Rādhikā, Kamalā, and the others? (89)
Śrī, Līlā, Bhū, Vibhūti, Pārvatī, Māṇikī, Prabhā, and the others are not superior to me because of my saintly nature; what then can be said of anyone else?
"O daughters of the Pitṛs, worship me with such devotion;
I shall deliver you all and purify all embodied beings. (9.1)
Having spoken thus, O Rādhikā, Śrī Narāyaṇa then placed his two feet and even his own form within their hearts.
Having bathed, eaten, and fed [them], Hari himself gave the command for them to go to their respective places and to the purifying holy sites (tīrthas). ||93||
Always worship me, your lord and master, in the manner I have described; for I cause my devotees to practice devotion without any effort. 94.
Having attained cessation within me without effort,
such devotees as well as you shall go to my own abode.
Having attained divine bodies through my will, you people who possess devotion shall go with me to my abode. 96.
All that has been given by me is eternal and supreme;
indeed, it consists of infinite syllables and divine bliss at all times. //97//
Filled with devotion, you shall obtain my service, as shall those people and even those women who likewise practice such devotion. (98)
They, both male and female, shall go to my supreme state of liberation;
let them know me thus, let them approach me, and likewise serve me as their beloved. (99)
"Having bestowed my mantra upon them, let them indeed liberate embodied beings;
I shall go to my own eternal field, Kuṅkumasthalī."
Having spoken thus to the daughters of the Pitṛs and also to the rivers,
as well as to the sages and the gods— the beloveds of Brahmā— he then remained silent for a moment.
He reflected within himself on something to say to the venerable Śaṅkara;
meanwhile, the men and women stood ready to carry out his command.

Thus ends the one hundred and fourteenth chapter, titled "The Demonstration by the Blessed Lord of the Nature of Devotion to His Own Self, to His Devotees, and Others, through the Rivers Consisting of the Daughters of the Pitṛs," in the second section, the Tretā-saṃtāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. || 114 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, listen; having thus commanded the personified rivers to go to their respective regions, Hari [then addressed] Śrī Śaṅkara.
He said, "O Yogin, these warriors who are your devotees must be granted a kingdom; therefore, let the auspicious Pārvata region, which is suitable for them, be given. (2)
And here, on this Himalaya mountain in the vicinity of Kailāsa,
let the mountains be for all beings upon these upper levels.
"Let this great mountain kingdom indeed be Bhūtāsana!
Having spoken thus to Śambhu, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa gave that auspicious realm to him.
Then, under the name Bhūtanātha, he bestowed the kingdom upon him;
for the Lord, whose nature is Bhairava,
appeared in the form of Bhūtanātha to that great-souled sovereign of beings who was his own very self.
And there Śaṅkara also gave a crown to Bhairava.
Having obtained the kingdom, Bhairava bowed to the Lord Nārāyaṇa,
and having bowed to Hara, his own father, he took possession of the circle of spirits.
He went swiftly to the Himalaya mountain, which exceeds sixty lakhs [in yojanas];
by him, those mountains were then indeed made the abodes of living beings.
Having thus bestowed the kingdom upon him, the Lord, the Blessed One, spoke to Brahmā right there: "You shall go to the land of Airāvati."
May the Teacher protect the land known as Brahmadeśa at all times;
may Śaṅkara go to Piṅgā in the region of Prācīnarājya.
"Let Viṣṇu go to the dark kingdom, which shall become famous by your name.
Having thus commanded those gods and having dismissed them, he [departed] toward the rivers.
Then, having commanded the sages of those respective regions to depart,
he also instructed the subjects regarding their own permanent places of residence.
Then Hari spoke to all the various hosts of gods born as warriors: "Let these followers of mine dwell in the region called Sāmaveda."
Those who remain here, flowing eastward along the Brahmaputrī,
quickly reach as far as Patākā in the regions of Kāmarūpa.
In this southern region, as far as the Lūkaśāyina [mountain],
there are naked mountains extending toward the river Lukahītā.
Having thus settled all the hosts of warriors so that they might dwell as far as the region of Sāma, Hari himself [remained] in their midst.
There, he established a Śiva-liṅga as the lord of these Āsāmīyas;
then the Gaṇa named Śivaliṅgākhyaka, having led all the soldiers,
established a settlement on all sides in the region of the Āsāmīyas.
The goddess Śivā, born from the Śivaliṅga, who is the very embodiment of desire.
Taking with him Kāmākṣī, who could assume any form at will, the Gaṇa went to that auspicious and lofty palace on the mountain.
Having fashioned her, the Gaṇa established that virtuous woman as Kāmarūpā;
regarding her always as his mother, he worshipped her with reverence.
And he established an excellent city named after himself on the heights;
thus Nārāyaṇa, having bestowed the kingdom upon the Śiva-liṅga, [departed].
Having stationed all the soldiers and dismissed both the gods and the sages,
he then took ten million maidens presented by the subjects onto the celestial chariot.
Ten thousand maidens served as her attendants,
along with twenty Pitṛ-kanyās and other supreme Brahmapriyās.
Having taken them with him, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa Svāmī, together with Lomaśa and accompanied by his mother and father, arrived through the sky at Kāśī, the abode of Śrī.
In that palace of Śiva, his own daughter Lakṣmī indeed shines forth, waiting expectantly for Śrī Puruṣottama. 25.
There, in that garden on the bank of the Varaṇā, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa brought his own celestial chariot down to the earth and went to his home.
Having bowed to Śivarāja Hara, as well as Pārvatī, his father-in-law, and likewise to Bhakta, Jaya, Candra, Kṛṣṇa, and Dhenupa; ||27||
Then, having met his own beloved Satī, Lakṣmī, in a secluded place,
he [placed] her in the celestial chariot along with all the maidens and beheld them.
Having caused her to see her parents as well as Lomaśa,
and having comforted her, let her be settled once more in her father's house.
Having granted the blessing, the Blessed One, the Supreme Person, arrived by means of his celestial chariot at the sacred field known as Akṣara, the site of Kuṅkumavāpī.
On the second day of the dark fortnight of Phālguna,
the supreme Lord Hari himself arrived at the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpī in the evening.
Seeing you arrived at the end of the month, your brothers, kinsmen, and virtuous friends,
as well as Rudra, the gods, and the sacred fords, came to Aśvapaṭṭasara itself.
Millions of sages, partial incarnations of the Lord, and likewise his devotees arrived in his presence upon seeing that extraordinary splendor in the sky.
Having seen that divine celestial chariot, adorned with Śrī Nārāyaṇa, beautiful with the radiance of ten million suns and as cool as the splendor of the moon; (34)
Accompanied by ten million maidens, ten thousand maidens, and twenty thousand maidens, those inhabitants of Akṣarakṣetra uttered cries of "Victory! (jaya).
With parched grains, unbroken rice, and saffron from Kashmir,
they greatly increased the splendor of the supreme lord’s celestial chariot.
And then he descended from the Aśvasarovara lake into the garden of Anādikṛṣṇa, in the vicinity of the palace. ||37||
Śrī Svāmī Nārāyaṇa, Hari, descended from the celestial chariot,
along with the beloveds of Brahmā, the daughters of the Pitṛs, and the servant-maidens of Prajāpati.
Lomaśa, as well as other great sages, his father, and his mother Ramā and the others, all true ones, entered their own abodes. (39)
Hari rested for a moment, as did his mother and Lomaśa;
those maidens gazed upon Hari’s palace, which was most supreme.
The Great Abode (Mahālaya) is pervaded by a wealth of supreme beauty residing in the Imperishable (Akṣara);
it is endowed with divine prosperity and resplendent with the sovereignty of ten million powers. ||41||
It was auspicious, adorned with seven stories and with statues of the lords,
and further beautified by the Brahma-lake and the Brahma-pond.
Then, having seen that divine [palace] endowed with celestial qualities and resplendent with divine machines and other wonders, all those maidens attained a state of supreme amazement.
Then the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa said to his sister Santoṣā, "O sister, let food be given to these [women]."
Likewise, Mādhava said to the immortal goddess, the wife of his brother:
"Let a drink and auspicious mouth-fresheners and other such things be given to these women. (45)
When this was said, those two [trees] suddenly produced food of a hundred forms, as well as various kinds of drink, like wish-fulfilling gems that grant all desires for an eon.
They gave much honor and paid respect to the wives of Kṛṣṇa;
and they all embraced one another like sisters and the wives of brothers.
Likewise, other maidens as well as the wives of sages and women were [graced] by that most divine stream of vision offered by Kṛṣṇa. 48.
Then all those divine maidens beheld him, appearing in the form of creepers as well as taking on the forms of birds, deer, and other creatures. (49)
The dark-complexioned beloved, possessing many forms, appeared bringing wonder;
thereafter, the Blessed Lord Puruṣottama spoke to Śrī Lomaśa.
O Guru, these women must be led by you yourself to your own auspicious hermitage;
they must be protected with great effort along with Brahmapriyā and the others. (51)
And Lomaśa, having been honored, fed, and saluted, took the girl and departed for his own hermitage by his own command. ||52||
The Blessed One took rest, and the parents departed happily;
then indeed, O Rādhikā, the Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa himself [remained].
In the month of Phālguna, he indeed celebrated the great festival of the flower-swing,
having caused various divine arenas to be prepared, moistened with water.
Then, having prepared the necessary materials with Hemanta and Bhagavat as his two primary attendants and other attendants as well, he began the play.
Having worshipped Śrī Vasantaka with excellent golden mechanical dolls, as well as his own image and Kṛṣṇa Narāyaṇa, [he offered them]. (56)
Having personally taken in her hand a golden yantra adorned with colors, she likewise [honored] the syllable, the liberated ones, and the practitioners of Sāṃkhya and Yoga. (57)
He repeatedly cast [his gaze] upon the assembly standing within the boundaries of the arena, and indeed upon his own countless beloveds who were the most devoted of devotees. 58.
Thus, he cast that supreme splendor upon his devotees, the Sāttvatas, the great sages, the people, the cowherd women, and the cowherd devotees.
He scattered red powder and turned them all the color of blood;
he likewise turned himself red as well, along with all those who had taken refuge in him.
The sky became red, and the filaments likewise turned tawny;
the water of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake was mixed with various colors.
Just as the sky takes on a variegated appearance through a rainbow,
so too did the imperishable ground and the field become filled with a wondrous stage.
The clay from the Kuṅkumavāpī field, having assumed the form of sandalwood,
attained a tawny hue when well-mixed with colored water.
Then, having thus arranged for Puṣpadola’s play,
Hari bathed with all his subjects and sported together with them.
Then, wearing new garments, the people went into the groves among the trees and throughout the gardens permeated by fragrant breezes. 65.
There, having tied down flower-made swings upon the branches of the trees, each one distinct and variegated, on all sides; ||66||
Having created unsurpassed beauty there with fruits, flowers, and other offerings,
all the maidens as well as the Blessed One assumed new attire.
And indeed, all the subjects, during the great festival of the flower-swing,
performed auspicious swinging and rejoiced exceedingly.
All the young female friends swing to and fro with one another,
while the beloved of Brahmā swings her own lover with deep emotion.
They proclaim various wonders through their hymns of praise, and some then dance near the swaying of Lord Hari. (2.115.70)
Others play beautiful musical instruments in the presence of Kṛṣṇa,
while still others make Kṛṣṇa laugh with humorous words.
Other women gave cool water to that beloved one,
and yet other women gave him ripe fruits.
Then, having made her own beloved Kṛṣṇa the swing,
she repeatedly swings the swing herself with her feet along with him.
Then the beginningless Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Sovereign Lord of husbands, knowing the minds of all, assumed countless forms right there.
Toward every maiden, every woman, every lover, and every tree, the youth became delightful, removing the intoxication of ten million desires. (75)
Having accepted the service of all the virtuous women, his devotees, and the wives of Brahmā,
the Blessed One once again became one.
Thus, on the first day of the dark fortnight of Caitra, Lord Hari performed the excellent festival of the flower swing in Akṣarakṣetra.
Then he went home and again provided a meal;
in the evening, he held a festival with singing, dancing, and instrumental music.
Then they all fell asleep and quickly attained rest;
and while he was living in this manner, the month of Śrāvaṇa arrived.
The devotees fashioned various swings out of gold and silver,
richly adorned with many ornaments and beautified by rows of flower garlands.
Inlaid with divine diamonds, gems, and other jewels, they were fragrant;
they shone with divine, soft beds and auspicious seats. ||81||
There, having seated the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, who is the Lord Nārāyaṇa, those beloveds of Brahmā caused their own Lord to swing. 82.
Then a marvel occurred there: clouds indeed became human beings at that time, and having come from the sky, they arrived there for the purpose of swinging Hari.
And they gave to that Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul, a new swing—divine, radiant as lightning, without support, and resting upon the sky. ||84||
In each and every limb, there are seen liberated gopīs and attendants, as well as incarnations, divine abodes, and likewise lords. (85)
The seers, the sages, the gods, the ancestors, and even humans;
the oceans, the mountains, the planets, and the circle of constellations—[all these were present]. (86)
The guardians of the directions, the protectors of the worlds, as well as those dwelling in the netherworld;
Kṣīroda, Śvetadhāman, and the inhabitants of Viśālākṣa. ||87||
Likewise, the indeterminate (avyākṛta) is seen there, as well as the immortal abode (amṛta-dhāma), Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, Sāketa, and Kila-asaka. ||88||
Likewise, Brahmā has four faces, and Brahmā also has eight faces;
likewise, the Unborn (Ajā) has sixteen faces, and likewise thirty-two faces.
He is seen with fifty faces and even with a hundred faces;
he is seen with a thousand faces and even with a hundred thousand faces.
Likewise, Brahmā with ten million faces is seen within the circle of jewels;
such a divine palanquin was indeed given by the clouds to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
Then the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa took her;
having ascended the swing, he then questioned the clouds. 92.
Why has this divine, auspicious, and worthy celestial swing been brought here, which reveals the entire universe, for the sake of me, the Lord of All? (93)
The clouds said, "O Great King, we have assembled here in Kāśī in the month of Āṣāḍha for the purpose of a pilgrimage to the banks of the Varaṇā. (94)
In the beautiful Mahālaya, we beheld the daughter of Śivarāja; there, we engaged in pleasant conversation with one another. (95)
Having performed both bathing and the act of beholding [the deity] here,
one must indeed proceed to the Aśvapaṭṭasara tīrtha and the auspicious hermitage of Lomaśa.
The auspicious field known as Akṣara is the supreme, eternal bestower of liberation, wherein dwells the Supreme Person, the Lord Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (97)
He who maintains all incarnations, the cause of all causes, the Great King, the beginningless Śrī Puruṣottama, shines resplendent. ||98||
Bālakṛṣṇa himself is the manifest Supreme Self, higher than the highest;
he is the son of the illustrious Kambharā and Śrī Gopālakṛṣṇa. ||99||
"Let us indeed go this very day for the sake of seeing him.
Having heard that, the maiden said, "I do indeed have a swing in my house."
Indeed, she should be given to him if you must go;
for this Lakṣmī, the destroyer of suffering, has been brought here by her and offered to you, O Lord. (101)
"O Ocean of Compassion, accept her; the weight of maidenhood is her master.
Thus addressed, the Blessed One rejoiced greatly and accepted her.
He gave blessings to her and to them again and again;
then the clouds, having bowed, departed into the sky, and Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa himself [remained].
In the month of Śrāvaṇa, remembering the goddess Lakṣmī, the consort of Nārāyaṇa, he himself performed the swinging ritual on a swing; indeed, he regarded it as a great festival.
Thus has been narrated, O Rādhā, the auspicious and beautiful life-story of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, which bestows liberation and grants all prosperity. 105.
Through reading, hearing, causing others to hear, and even through teaching,
as well as through reflection, it bestows liberation and grants the divine body of Brahmā.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifteenth chapter, titled "The Description of how the Lord granted the kingdom of Bhūtāsana to Bhairava, the kingdoms of Nagna and Parvata and the kingdom of Sāma to distinguished warriors, and having commanded the rivers in the Sundara forest to go to their respective regions, performed the Phulladola festival and the Śrāvaṇa festival upon returning to the field of Kuṅkumavāpī," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, to the auspicious birth-month of Anādi Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa; it is indeed the month of Kārtika, consisting of the dark fortnight.
The thirteenth divine day, the eighth lunar tithi, has arrived;
therefore, the Vaiṣṇava people of Prāgjyotiṣa have come to perform that festival.
Those who are devoted to the eastern lands, those born in the regions of Śyāma-Brahma, those born in the land of Trivitta, and the inhabitants of Kāśmīra; || 3 ||
Likewise, other men, women, boys, and girls residing in snowy regions, born in the land of Śambhu, and those who serve their elders [were there]. || 4 ||
The great sages arrived at Aśvapaṭṭatīrtha by means of celestial chariots,
as did the virtuous and the truthful, bringing various offerings with them.
Eager indeed for the sake of worshipping Bālakṛṣṇa,
they arrived from the region of Uṣṭrālaya as well as from the region of Abrikta.
Likewise, there are those born from the region of Ārabīja and from the field of Kumārī;
others indeed are born from Ajanābha as well as from the land of Kaccha.
Eagerly, they arrived with offerings for the sake of worshipping Kṛṣṇa;
then, in the morning, Gopālakṛṣṇaka constructed a beautiful pavilion.
Having bathed and put on his garments while seated upon the elephant-throne, Bālakṛṣṇa adorned himself with ornaments and the like, and then entered the assembly hall.
Therein dwell the gods, the ancestors, and the sages who have attained liberation in the Imperishable,
as well as the lords residing in other abodes, the deities, and human beings.
They arrived at that assembly for the sake of worshipping the illustrious Hari;
excellent musical instruments were played, and shouts of "Victory! arose.
Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa shone resplendent as he was seated upon his own throne;
and in that assembly, the brahmin Lomaśa worshipped Acyuta.
He placed a crown upon him and then gave him two earrings;
thereafter, he made a forehead mark with unbroken rice grains and a crescent moon on the forehead of Hari.
He performed the nightly lamp-offering for him and placed flower garlands around his neck;
afterwards, he gave blessings, and the lords performed worship. || 14 ||
Then [the forms of] Rādhikā, then the Lakṣmīs, then the beloveds of Brahmā,
then the goddesses, the Gāndharvas, the Āryās, and after that the wives of the sages.
The gods and goddesses, as well as the Vaiṣṇava progeny of Prāgjyotiṣa,
and even those who had come from other lands and the lords of the earth, [honored] that Lord.
They worshipped him exceedingly with all divine articles of offering; they performed the *ārātrika* ceremony and presented great gifts before him.
Various garments, ornaments, and pearls;
necklaces made of gold and silver, diamonds, and girdles. || 18 ||
They gave vehicles, elephants, horses, and likewise excellent ornaments; they provided foods, drinks, fruits, and even nectar.
Having thus worshipped Bālakṛṣṇa in the beautiful pavilion,
they then likewise worshipped His mother Śrī, Gopāla, and His father Śrīhari.
Having bowed to the venerable Lomaśa and the sages, and having risen from his elephant-throne in the manner of common folk, he then indeed prostrated before the elders seated in the assembly hall.
Having fed the honored guests, the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, departed for his own abode with the approval of his father.
Then he dismissed the people, each to their own homes, as well as the virtuous women;
at that time, Lakṣmī and Śrī-Kambharā honored him with devotion.
And having fed them, he dismissed them to their own homes;
thus was celebrated the festival for the birth of Śrī Hari, numbering thirteen [days].
Having completed their great festival, they returned to their own regions.
O Rādhikā, listen to the wonder that occurred there on the second day. ||25||
Sent by his preceptor, the blessed Dattātreya, who is the Supreme Self,
a certain Śarabha was dispatched to the presence of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
He arrived there for the sake of liberation and then praised Śrī Hari;
having indeed attained a divine body, he went to the abode named Akṣara.
Śrī Rādhikā said:
O Kṛṣṇa, who was that Śarabha who was impelled by Dattātreya?
Tell me the entire story of it; I desire to hear it in its entirety. (28)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhā, I shall tell you the auspicious story of Śarabha.
There was a king named Samīraṇa, born of the Solar dynasty (Sūryavaṃśa). || 29 ||
He was the sovereign lord of the auspicious western region of Ājanābha-khaṇḍa,
as well as of the Gaurjaras, the Kacchas, and the Saurāṣṭras.
He was compassionate in protecting his subjects and devoted to Nārāyaṇa;
he was constantly intent on righteous deeds and dedicated to the practice of giving and fire-offerings.
He possessed unblemished fame and was likewise devoted to protecting the distressed;
he was a protector and a supreme guardian of cows, the earth, brahmins, and the virtuous. ||32||
In whose kingdom there was never any famine in the past, who provided protection to those seeking refuge, and likewise protected the country. (33)
The archer himself constantly performed service to the gods,
and his capital city was situated on the bank of the river Śatruñjitā.
The great divine city named Kuṇḍala is adorned by Brahmins and inhabited by gentle subjects consisting of Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and others. (35)
There, the brahmins were devoted to sacrifices and offerings, chanting the Vedas;
likewise, there were virtuous ascetics intent on meditation upon Kṛṣṇa.
Even forest-dwellers do not encounter such hardship anywhere in his kingdom;
both women and men have always lived happily under his protection. (37)
In the kingdom of Samīraṇa, this was always a particular custom:
every morning, a drum was constantly sounded by the king's men.
Whether one is wretched, blind, miserable, without support, without refuge, without food, or even a helpless child, an old man, or a beggar; (39)
A woman who is without support, aged, a widow, and without family; or one who is virtuous, chaste, a yoginī, or an ascetic, and destitute of wealth. ||2.116.40||
Whether he be poor or wealthy, a eunuch or a female eunuch, let him come to my door at dawn and receive food and sustenance. (41)
In my village, city, and town, and among the subjects—
wherever indeed there are houses belonging to me.
Coming together here and there, let them receive food and drink;
let them take up garments and vessels, and worship the Supreme Person.
Thus, at dawn, his drum resounds to awaken him;
penniless men eat his food at every place. (44)
Having eaten, they were constantly satisfied and offered words of blessing;
thus the meritorious king, on one occasion, [addressed] his circle of servants.
Having taken [it], he set out for the tiger-infested forest, eager for sport;
his servants, elephants, horses, and even the slaves went along with him. (46)
Then that king, having caused dwellings for elephants, horses, and other animals to be constructed among the trees on the bank of a pond in the middle of the forest; 47.
In accordance with the duty of a king, he entered the forest to hunt;
some servants also went along with the king, accompanied by their mounts.
Having merely caught sight of a gavaya, the king followed its tracks and entered the dense forest in vain. (49)
The bow-wielding King Paśupriya, mounted upon his horse,
reached with great speed a beautiful river there that was auspicious and filled with a flood of water.
On its bank stood a delightful and exceedingly beautiful hermitage,
indeed well-arranged with trees laden with fruits, flowers, and the like.
He inspires great confidence in sages; he is a source of beauty for beasts and birds; he brings peace to those of violent nature through his non-violent conduct; and he is exceedingly pure. (52)
Served by the disciples and grand-disciples of the Sage, it was like the abode of Brahman;
there, the emergence of the defects of desire, anger, and excessive greed did not occur.
Indeed, even among the animals there, defects such as illusion and falsehood did not exist;
even the birds sang sweet songs from among the trees and other plants.
And at that time, O Śuka, the parrots, peacocks, cuckoos, and royal swans gathered together and sang in their own tongues the words of the Vedas. ||55||
For even the gods and goddesses do not dwell in the sky from which they have come;
rather, having bowed to the sage, they depart indeed, considering themselves to have accomplished their purpose.
And in such a hermitage, the great sage Pārṣṇigraha performs extensive penance for the sake of the welfare of the world. (57)
In the summer, he sits continuously in the midst of five fires;
during the rainy season, he sits upon the bare ground amidst the downpours of rain.
Having made his dwelling in the cool water, he remains there entirely during the day;
at night, he stays beneath a tree in that open space.
In one place it takes fruit, in another flowers, and in yet another even the food of sages; in one place water, and in another drinking water—the cloud receives them all.
Remaining without food, he dwells somewhere, worshipping Śrī Narāyaṇa;
he worships the true Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, within his heart.
At that time, when the sage was staying beneath such a tree,
the gavaya approached him from the front out of extreme fear.
Having taken refuge with the sage, the king remained there very steadfast;
yet, from a distance, he did not see that hermitage nor the sage.
With his mind fixed on hunting, he forcibly struck a gavaya with a sharp-edged arrow that pierced deep into its belly.
Thereupon, the Gavaya, having cried out before the sage with his arrow still fixed,
fell down just like a son, solely for the sake of protection.
Seeing the sage fallen with his arrow still lodged in him, and beholding him with a piteous eye, the sage Pārṣṇigraha [was moved].
The compassionate one immediately touched that animal with his hand,
placed water in its mouth, and then saw an arrow lodged within it.
Likewise, seeing the deer fleeing in terror and the beasts running about on all sides, he experienced great distress. (68)
