Having bathed themselves and caused the people to bathe, and having then given them the *mantras*, they made the subjects of Hari-Kṛṣṇa hear [the teachings] most thoroughly.
All of them, traveling in celestial chariots, went to the confluence of the Yāneśī and the ocean;
having caused the people to hear [the teachings], they bathed there and performed the ritual ablution.
The sage Devāyatana, the king of devotees, gave the name-mantra to the gods;
he also gave the *manus* to the subjects of the region of Aikāgārika.
In the northern regions and the higher strata of the Śibi and Rājapradeśa territories, along the banks of the rivers Tuṅgā and Asiknī, he bestowed the Manus upon the subjects. (54)
The sage Devāyana, honored by all, went to the region of Tandrā;
there, he caused the people of the snowy land to hear the name of Hari. (55)
To them, the sage Devāyana gave the Mantras for the three-fold progeny;
having caused them to hear these, he then bestowed upon them the name-mantra.
The sage Rendīmeṣāyana honored those who were traveling in their celestial chariots;
he made his own abode pure by being covered with the dust of their feet.
Worshipped by the sage Meṣāyana, Pradyumna and the others went to the Anāvarā river while chanting the name of Hari.
Having caused the names to be heard and having bathed the subjects,
they themselves bathed at the confluence and bestowed the *mantras* upon those subjects.
In celestial chariots they went toward the river Ālanaukā;
at its confluence with the ocean, all the subjects also bathed.
Having heard the names of Hari— Kṛṣṇa, Bālakṛṣṇa, and Nārāyaṇa— King Śaktākṣi bathed at the confluence of the ocean together with his family.
Having received the worship offered by the king and the subjects, Pradyumna and the others received the name-mantras from the great seers who had come to the gods.
They proceeded along the Bīna river toward the previously established regions of Tandrā;
then, all those traveling in celestial chariots bathed at the confluence with the ocean where it meets the sea.
The subjects gathered there and chanted his name;
they then received the name-mantras from that temple of the deity.
Then the sage Vṛṣabha, who was from that region, honored them;
and having received that honor, they all departed by means of a celestial chariot.
There, together with the subjects, they bathed in the river Askānadī;
then the deity Devāyatana bestowed Manus upon the subjects.
Then, while causing the name of Viṣṇu to be heard, they went to the river Yānā;
having bathed at the confluence of the Yānā and the ocean, they performed the ritual ablution for the people.
Having caused them to hear the name of Hari, they gave the sacred mantras to them;
then they departed by celestial chariot to the river Kālindī.
Having bathed in the waters of the ocean of Kālī and having bathed the people,
they caused them to hear the name of Hari and then bestowed the Mantras upon them.
And the great seer Tulāyana led those who were traveling in their celestial chariots to his own abode and paid homage to Pradyumna, Devatā, and the others.
And King Kālimāśa also became a true Vaiṣṇava at that time;
with supreme devotion, he worshipped the lords of the gods seated in their celestial chariots.
The devotee of Viṣṇu, together with his family, indeed ascended the celestial chariot;
from there they went to the regions of the finest silken garments, and beyond that.
Having caused the proclamation of the names of the regions called Dviraṅga and the banks of the Anādī river to the people dwelling on that land, [he established] the recitation of those names. (73)
Then they gave those mantras to them and departed at will;
thereafter, they purified their progeny by means of the name of Hari.
Having bestowed the mantras upon them, they returned to Akṣauḍhābhū;
there, they caused all the inhabitants of the thieves' settlement to hear the mantra of Hari.
Having bestowed the mantras upon them and having caused the people dwelling on that land to hear the name of Hari, they went to Mount Prabhāsa.
Then the gods, led by Āyatanā, gave them the mantra;
thereafter, they all proceeded toward the western region of Vilīnāyupradeśa.
And all the people there, filled with longing, made this proclamation:
"Hare Kṛṣṇa! Hare Svāmin! Bālakṛṣṇa! Hare! Hare! (78)
They also gave them mantras, and having accepted the offerings made by them, they all departed for the regions of the sixfold wombs (yoni).
Having caused all the inhabitants there to hear the name of Hari,
they bestowed mantras upon them and thereafter performed worship for their sake.
Having taken [the Lord] with them, they all departed for the regions of Oṃ, traveling in celestial chariots;
having descended there, they caused all the subjects to hear the name of Hari.
They gave those auspicious Vaiṣṇava mantras to them;
thus, O Rādhikā, the sage Devāyana [traveled] through all the lands.
Likewise, he was accompanied by Pradyumna and the most eminent twelve sages,
as well as by kings from the regions of Rāśiyāna.
Having wandered through the eight divine realms of delusion, he indeed made living beings Vaiṣṇavas;
in every place, people were devoted to the chanting and recitation of Hari’s name.
Indeed, men and women—whether young, old, or middle-aged—were always and at all times engaged in the bathing and worship of Bālakṛṣṇa. (85)
At that time, the abode of the God of gods indeed came to be in every house;
then they truly began to pray for a temple for the god.
The sages beginning with Meṣāyana, and kings such as Ṛkūṭastha and others—we indeed, through our yoga with you, are devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa. (87)
Today all we subjects have been born anew, turned away from the path of evil;
having become devoted to the service of Kṛṣṇa, a great favor has been bestowed upon us. (88)
The fruitfulness of this human body has now been brought about by you;
for you alone are our Guru, the Supreme Brahman, and our savior. (89)
Through the Guru’s door, Hari is indeed met face-to-face; of this there is no doubt.
Act for us in such a way that our direct union with Hari may come to pass. (2.122.90)
"May we have a direct vision of Bālakṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, our own chosen deity; please, may you make such an arrangement. (91)
If even a mantra consisting of a mere name is capable of incinerating sins, why indeed would the direct vision of Him not bestow [liberation] upon embodied beings? 92.
Hearing of whom is auspicious, remembering whom repeatedly is auspicious, and praising whom is auspicious—what indeed would his very sight not bestow? (93)
Just as you have come here and performed this act of compassion, so may our chosen deity also arrive; grant us such grace.
For children, girls, men, and women alike, as well as for those who are incapable, the vision of Śrī Hari may indeed be attained through the sacred scripture. (95)
Those who, through the influence of a devotee, have by chance attained the desire for liberation—such wise Vaiṣṇavas worship Him here upon His arrival. (96)
By the grace of Hari, even regions shall attain divinity, as shall rivers, streams, lakes, and oceans;
and by his arrival, the very earths shall attain the status of sacred pilgrimage sites.
Then forests, mountains, villages, cities, and waters,
as well as excavated and natural pools, shall attain a divine state.
Furthermore, the battlefields and the lands of the continents, as well as the fortresses and difficult terrains, shall thereafter attain a divine nature. (99)
The hearts of human beings, which are indeed filled with impurity,
will become pure through the yoga of Hari by means of great merit.
Thus we pray here for the sake of the high-souled Pradyumna;
we also offer auspicious words of blessing to the deity of this temple.
Thus requested, O Rādhā, those two who have Pradyumna as their deity gave them a firm assurance of "Om" and comforted them.
Then the celestial chariot was brought down by everyone at Bālakṛṣṇa-sarovara,
on its northern shore, for the purpose of disembarking.
Having performed their meals and other duties, they all rested;
at night, they took refuge in Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa and remembered Him.

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-second chapter, titled "The Description of How the Great Sages and Kings, having traveled by celestial chariot through the regions of Rāśiyāna, proclaimed the name of Hari among the subjects, bestowed the mantras, and established temples for the gods and hermitages," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Now, O Rādhā, Queen of the Rāsa, at dawn, after bathing,
people should worship the form of Bāla-Kṛṣṇa and also Pradyumna.
The sages, beginning with Meṣāyana, as well as King Tharkūṭastha and others, conducted deliberations regarding the temples of the deities.
They were the foremost devotees of the regions where the zodiacal signs move, the most excellent among the Sātvatas.
Having heard this in the past, the Blessed Lord performed a sacrifice on the banks of the Lāśahā;
and on the banks of the Śālāvatī as well as in the Piṅga regions,
Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, purified his subjects out of compassion.
Having come in person together with the gods, including Brahmā’s beloved consort and others,
and accompanied by his two parents, he rendered that land a sacred pilgrimage site (tīrtha).
And thus, let them come together here; let these places become sacred sites—purifying, bestowing happiness, and possessing the power to destroy all sins.
May all rivers become worthy abodes for all the gods, objects of universal worship, bestowers of liberation, and purified by the feet of the Blessed One.
Therefore, we shall perform five auspicious Śrīvaiṣṇava sacrifices;
the first sacrifice shall take place in the kingdom of Śibi on the bank of Lake Bālakṛṣṇa.
In the kingdom of King Tharkūṭastha, he performed the second auspicious sacrifice;
in the kingdom of the great king Vīrajāra, the third sacrifice;
and in the kingdom of King Śaktyakṣi, the fourth auspicious sacrifice.
In the kingdom of King Kālimāśa, he performed the fifth sacrifice, which was most excellent.
We shall serve with offerings of wealth and all articles of adornment those who are liberated, as well as those who have crossed over, the Lords, and their attendants; likewise the Goddesses,
the wives of the God of gods, the ancestors, and the preeminent Siddhas and Ṛṣis.
Indeed, all embodied beings, including humans who are the locus of both insentience and consciousness. || 12 ||
We shall indeed summon the sacred fords and the guardians of the world,
and we shall perform the most excellent sacrifices for the gratification of Kṛṣṇa.
Therefore, let it be so ordained by the devotees that Nārāyaṇa Svāmī, Bālakṛṣṇa Janārdana, may come to our regions. || 14 ||
Thus addressed, the sage, who resembled a god and was a sanctuary for the deities,
then said "So be it, so be it" to those Vaiṣṇavas seeking liberation.
And the king of devotees gave the command to rest for a moment;
having gone to the shore of the lake named Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, he [dismissed] the kings and others.
The sages, the kings and others, and the sage Devāyatana proceeded by way of the celestial chariot path to Bālakṛṣṇasarovara.
And they all descended to the ground in their celestial chariots upon the northern bank—
the four kings as well as the twelve great sages.
Likewise, thousands of eminent people of noble birth, endowed with wealth,
who were Vaiṣṇavas, descended there, having resolved to perform the sacrifice.
And Pradyumna said to the sages: "Let a proclamation be made throughout the earth that a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice must indeed be performed on the bank of Bālakṛṣṇa-saras."
To the north is the first [shrine], and to the west is the second, the best of sacrifices;
furthermore, on the shore of the lake known as Dvikalā, by Mount Tharkūṭa.
And the third sacrifice was to be performed by King Vīrajāra at the confluence of the rivers Obīrā and Trīśan on the expanse of the earth.
Furthermore, the auspicious fourth sacrifice should be performed by the King, who possesses power and vision, upon the vast surface of the earth where the ocean meets the shore. (23)
The fifth sacrifice must be performed by King Kālimāśa;
indeed, let the Vaiṣṇavas come to them at the conjunction of Kālimā and the ocean.
Therein dwells the beginningless Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, the Lord of Akṣara, the illustrious Supreme Self, the Supreme Lord. (25)
For the Blessed Lord Bālakṛṣṇa is our chosen deity;
he himself will come from the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā.
One must certainly come for the purpose of seeing [the deity] and for the purpose of service;
initiation has been granted at various locations up until the full moon.
Now, on the eleventh day of the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, the commencement of the first sacrifice will duly take place. (28)
Kṛṣṇa will perform the rites of the seven-day sacrifice on the fifth day of the second sacrifice's course. (29)
The commencement and the conclusion of the eleventh sacrifice took place on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight;
likewise, the commencement of the third sacrifice occurred on the third lunar day.
The conclusion will take place on the ninth day of the dark fortnight of Pauṣa,
while the commencement of the fourth sacrifice will occur on the eleventh day.
On the second day of the bright fortnight, the conclusion will take place;
indeed, the commencement of the fifth sacrifice shall be on the fifth day.
"It is certain that the conclusion will take place on the eleventh day"; let them proclaim this in every way throughout all the regions. (33)
Thus addressed, the groups of kings as well as those great sages quickly made proclamations throughout their respective lands.
Then, by means of a celestial vehicle, the king and the others thoroughly prepared various auspicious requisites. (35)
There, gathered from all directions, they indeed caused pavilions,
halls, dwellings, and camps to be constructed.
And on the ground extending ten yojanas, they eagerly had it constructed;
Pradyumna, acting as supervisor, had it built according to what was appropriate.
And those twelve sages, having reached the temple of the deity, departed in a celestial chariot toward the glorious Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. 38.
They prayed to Kṛṣṇa-Narāyaṇa, the Lord of the lords of lords;
and Hari, being pleased and urged by his father, said, "So be it. || 39 ||
Thus instructed by Lomaśa, the sage Devatāyatana took thousands of ṛṣis and departed for the sacrifice by means of a celestial chariot.
They all caused various sacrificial pits (kuṇḍas), altars (vedīs), and platforms for the installation ceremony to be constructed on the bank of the Bālakṛṣṇa lake. ||41||
He built sacrificial halls, dwelling-halls for the great ones, as well as beautiful abodes for the liberated souls and temples for the incarnations. ||42||
He likewise [beheld] the abodes of the Īśvaras, the abodes of the Īśvarīs,
as well as those of the Pitṛs, the Ṛṣis, and the beloved abodes of Brahmā.
He likewise saw the abodes of the Brahmasaras apsarases,
as well as the various dwellings of many kinds of gods.
He also [saw] the abodes of the Dāsas, as well as the dwellings of those inhabitants of Bhuvarloka, of human beings, of sacred fords (tīrthas), and likewise of stationary beings.
Then they constructed many-storied abodes for those dwelling in the Atala and other nether regions,
both upon the vast surface of the earth and in the sky.
By the command of Pradyumna, the Viśvakarmas constructed a vast seven-storied pavilion extending ten yojanas.
At intervals of fifty yojanas, they established dwellings supported by pillars; and at each dwelling, there were lamps produced from the natural radiance of jewels.
Likewise, there were natural channels for waters that were cold, warm, and so forth, as well as natural channels for milk, curd, and clarified butter. (49)
There are natural streams of honey and sugar-juice, and lakes known as "Nectar" containing cool waters fit for drinking. (2.123.50)
Likewise, the Brahma-lakes, the Gopa-lakes, the Nārāyaṇa-lakes, the Satya-lakes, and the Deva-lakes are established as eternal. ||51||
Just as the fire-pits were made blunt and small according to requirement, so too the natural curds,
the cooked milk, and the essence of milk are produced by nature.
There were herds of wish-fulfilling cows (kāmadhenu), groves of trees with sap-filled creepers,
and auspicious laboratories of nectar that provide all manner of food and drink for every creation.
Caskets containing garments, ornaments, cosmetics, articles of enjoyment, and the like; as well as camphor, various powders, collyrium, lac, and perfumes. ||54||
They display musical instruments, singing, dancing, and the like;
they employ nets for enchanting the mind and so forth, as well as sparks, fire, and wind. (55)
Vehicles, mounts, palanquins, garuḍas, swans, cows, and bulls; couches, thrones, canopies, hangings, cloths, and wall-coverings. (56)
There were diverse gardens with rows of every kind of medicinal herb, and heaps of food, drink, and other articles that resembled mountains. (57)
Likewise, there were heaps of sacrificial offerings, grains, and fruits;
and likewise, piles of leaves, juices, and fuel sticks.
There were heaps of rice and barley, especially of the grains of sages, as well as piles of sesame seeds, portions of ghee, and cooked foods. (59)
Of those instruments for hearing from afar, those that enable seeing from afar, those moons for piercing through distance, and those that bring about the perception of touch; ||2.123.60||
And at every station, he indeed established those who announce the seasons, those who provide news from within the *golaka* (enclosures), couriers, and houses for travelers;
as well as female slaves, servants, and natural scribes.
There, on that sacrificial ground, it was prepared by the appointed ones at every spot.
Royal highways, divine paths, and roads for elephants, horses, swans,
and garuḍas were likewise constructed at that time, upon which they travel with ease.
A storehouse for materials intended for sacrificial fees, a temple for the purpose of sacrifice, clothing halls for the purpose of charity, and shrines worthy of divine worship; ||64||
And all the halls for services were constructed by the Viśvakarman artisans; in every place there were wish-fulfilling creepers (kalpalatā), and in every corner was the luster of jewels.
The dwellings, preeminent with wish-fulfilling gems (cintāmaṇi), bestowed every happiness.
Of the liberated ones in the white sky, and of the celestial beings in the intermediate space.
Dwellings that grant happiness were constructed for the terrestrial beings upon the ground, and for other embodied beings upon the trees, during the festival of Bālakṛṣṇa’s sacrifice.
Thus, in every way, the earth was adorned with great pavilions.
At the top of the pavilion, a banner eight hundred cubits long was raised;
a thousand golden jars were set up,
and Vedic mantras were inscribed upon the cymbals and the archways.
The splendors of the colored decorations were made like the gardens of heaven;
thus indeed did the dwellings shine all around the sacrifice.
Then the great lords, invited by letters, arrived;
this sacrifice is being personally conducted by Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa himself.
Everyone must go with reverence through King Śibi-deva,
now indeed on the eleventh day of the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.
Behold the commencement of the sacrifice on the shore of Lake Bālakṛṣṇa;
the great drum of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa resounds. (73)
Commanded by Hari, the auspicious one resounded throughout all the worlds;
hearing of the sacrifice on the tenth day, those residing in all the worlds arrived.
Indeed, all those liberated from the world of the Imperishable Brahman arrived, as did all the abodes inhabited by the Blessed Ones. (75)
The female deities assembled, as did innumerable others who were liberated;
likewise the lords, the goddesses, the ancestors, and the sages. ||76||
The Siddhas, those devoted to the practice of Brahman, the gods and goddesses, the Apsarases of the Brahma-lake, and the preeminent guardians of the quarters [were there]. (77)
Even the Sāṃkhya-yoginīs, as well as the gods of the Bhuvarloka, human beings, sages, brahmins, and the people of Kuṅkumavāpikā.

Those born in the open air, those born from lotuses, those dwelling in the chest, the back, and other parts of the body, as well as those living in water and those inhabiting the cavities of the earth, all arrived. (79)
Rivers, streams, and oceans; trees and even creepers; sacred fords, animals, winged creatures, and all species born from the womb—[all these are likewise]. (2.123.80)
Embodied beings consisting of earth, water, fire, and air arrived there, having resolved to participate in the sacrifice for its sake. ||81||
The gods, dānavas, and daityas, as well as the Rudras and Vasus, the Viśvedevas, the Sādhyas, the Manus, and the sons of Brahmā; ||82||
The virtuous Sanaka and others, the great sages Nārada and others, and the sons, grandsons, and descendants of Brahmā all arrived at the sacrifice of Hari. (83)
All the directions resounded with the gathering of celestial chariots;
kings and groups of ministers respectfully presented garments.
Meanwhile, the sage Devāyana was in a beautiful celestial chariot that moves at will,
magnificent and filled with every prosperity, in the great Śātabhauma heaven.
[He meditated upon] the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Śrī Puruṣottama, all the beloveds of Brahmā, and likewise his entire family. (86)
To Lomaśa and the other seven ṛṣis, to the brahmins, to men and women, to his mother and father, to the gods and others, to the sacred fords, and to Śaṅkara and the rest. ||87||
Having taken the guardians of the fields, the serving goddesses, the deities beginning with Īśvara,
and those possessing divine bodies belonging to that place, he returned through the sky.
Excellent musical instruments were played and shouts of victory then arose;
everyone indeed celebrated that event with parched grain, flowers, and unbroken rice.
And they all gazed around at the auspicious celestial chariot of the Supreme Lord, which was as radiant as ten million suns, immensely brilliant, and equal to the Imperishable.
Richly adorned with the beautiful splendor of divine weapons, graced by divine swans,
and shining with divine banners and auspicious jars, it moves at will and is full of bliss.
Beside which thousands of excellent celestial palaces move about,
and from which a soundless [light] has emerged from the cloud at a height of fifteen yojanas.
Having attained stability in the sky, the Blessed One himself then suddenly descended, adorned by a multitude of ten million lotuses.
The sounds of electrical machines and other such devices resounded as omens;
and the sky, having taken on a physical form, sang the song of Kṛṣṇa. (94)
Passionate women and impassioned ones, Sarasvatīs and Śāradās, and all the sciences, then sang with eagerness for the sake of Kṛṣṇa. (95)
Lakṣmī, Gaṅgā, Virajā, Sulalitā, Vijayā, and Jayā. ||96||
Then Suśīlā and the others sang a captivating song;
the Gandharvas likewise performed a chant for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa.
The sages produced the resonant sounds of the Vedas with deep roars and other such noises, while the deities, beginning with Agni, likewise uttered cries of "Victory! (jaya).
The disciples and other sages all performed respectful obeisances prostrate before him like a staff and cried out, "Victory to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa! ||99||
Meanwhile, Hari indeed arrived at the assembly pavilion on earth;
they gave him flower garlands, crest-jewels, and clusters of blossoms.
With heaps of flowers, they all offered salutations to Acyuta, as well as to their mother, their father, and the venerable Śuka. || 101 ||
[He saw] Santuṣṭa, Amṛta, the sage Devāyatanaka,
the blessed Hemanta, Lomaśa, and Śambhu and Viṣṇu’s unborn [son].
O Rādhā, the offspring of Kuṅkumavāpikā, headed by Brahmapriyā,
repeatedly caused the progeny of Rāśiyāna to increase exceedingly.

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Construction of the Sacrificial Pavilion and Other Structures on the Banks of Bālakṛṣṇa Lake, the Arrival of the Mahīmānas, and the Arrival of Bālakṛṣṇa and Others," in the second section (Tretā-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhikā, thus spoke Kṛṣṇa, the great lord Bālakṛṣṇa.
Having descended from the celestial chariot, he proceeded to the sacrificial pavilion.
And having observed that, he quickly performed his ablutions in a small pond.
The sacrificer himself, together with the twice-born who observes the vow of his wife, [should perform it]. || 2 ||
The Lord was likewise accompanied by Lomaśa and Devāyatana.
Accompanied by his mother, father, and others, he sat down upon an auspicious seat.
Meanwhile, the Brahmins, eager for the recitation of benedictions, spoke the words of auspiciousness.
Then, having caused him to perform the ceremonial sipping of water (ācamana), the sage Lomaśa [proceeded].
Having recited the purification mantras and having offered the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), |||
Having sprinkled with water, he should take the thread in his hand.
And he bound Bālakṛṣṇa, the patron of the sacrifice, in the inner apartment.
Likewise, [he addressed] the king, the sacrificer, who was accompanied by his wife, using figurative designations.
The sage Lomaśa performed the naming ceremony for Śibi-deva;
the blessed Lord Bālakṛṣṇa also honored Lomaśa, the knower of sacrifice.
And there he bound the primary vow, as well as the secondary vow of the wife.
Having appointed a pair of preceptors, he then [appointed] twelve Brahmins.
He bound the fierce ones, who were of the very nature of Rudra, in the presence of Rudra;
and near Brahmā, he bound others numbering ten thousand.
And there he bound the sages who were engaged in muttering prayers and performing oblations.
By the command of Kṛṣṇa, Brahmā himself came to stand upon the altar of the Veda. ||10||
At that time, the Vedas, as well as the Upavedas, became the singers.
And at that time, there were also Udgātṛ priests who were embodiments of the Vedic branches.
Then there were the Hotṛ priests and the Upahotṛ priests, beginning with Sanaka and the others.
Likewise, the masters of yoga, the perfected ones (siddhas), and men such as Kapila and others, are all Nārāyaṇas. ||12||
Likewise, the Āhartṛs and Pratihartṛs are auspicious lords.
The Bhūman and others likewise came into being, endowed with the Vairāja and other qualities.
And there, the great sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha became the officiating priests (ṛtvij),
and the Vālakhilyas then became the reciters of the Vedas.
Vyāsa and others who were knowers of the Vedas, as well as Bṛhaspati and others, became reciters of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā. ||15||
Then all those carriers of oblations among the fires were indeed Nārāyaṇas.
And then, at the sacrifice, there were incarnations with faces like fire.
And there in that assembly, the fires of divine form shone forth;
there were wish-fulfilling trees accompanied by wish-granting creepers, bestowing sacrificial offerings. ||17||
At that time, they indeed gathered the materials that had been prepared;
thus were the assistants for the sacrifice appointed there at the ritual. (18)
There is also the worship of the Earth, as well as the worship of Vārāha;
the worship of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), and also the worship of the altars (vedikās). ||19||
Then Śrī Lomaśa and the others performed the worship of Gaṇeśa.
Then the twice-born performed the worship of Gaṇeśa, who was present before their eyes. ||20||
There is also the worship of the conch and likewise the worship of the discus;
the adoration of the pitcher and likewise the excellent worship of Lakṣmī. (21)
Furthermore, there is the worship of Rudra and likewise the worship of Durgā;
also the installation of the water-pot (kalaśa) and likewise the worship of the Mothers (mātṛkā). ||22||
The worship of the guardians of the directions and likewise the adoration of the planets;
the worship of the lords and likewise the worship of the powers (śaktis). ||23||
And likewise, there is the worship of the attendants and the worship of the Vasus.
And the worship of the Ādityas, as well as the worship of the gods. ||24||
Also, the worship of the world-protectors, as well as the honoring of virtuous women;
the worship of the gods, the worship of the ancestors, and the worship of the sages. (25)
And also the worship of the elements, which makes known what is desired and undesired.
And also the worship of the directions and the worship of the Viśvedevas. ||26||
Likewise, there is also the worship of the two sons of Aśvinī and of the Rākṣasas.
Likewise, there is the worship of the fields, the guardians of the fields, and the yogins. ||27||
And the worship of the Yoginīs, as well as the worship of the Kalās.
There is also the worship of the Manus, as well as the worship of the Tattvas. ||28||
Furthermore, there is the worship of the Maruts, as well as the worship of the sacred fords (tīrthas).
Likewise, there is the worship of gods who are characterized by passion (rājasa) and darkness (tāmasa). ||29||
Likewise, there is the worship of the Vighnas, the Vighnarājas, and the Brāhmīs;
as well as the worship of the Vidyās, the wives of Brahmā, and the women of the Dhāmas. (30)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa performed the worship of all those who were embodied there, for their complete satisfaction. (31)
Then Harikṛṣṇa Svāmī himself, the venerable Puruṣottama, [arrived].
Bālakṛṣṇa resides in the primary abode of the Supreme Brahman. ||32||
Śibi-deva indeed performed his worship, a great worship;
and when the principal deity was worshipped, ten million musical instruments were sounded. ||33||
Then Nārāyaṇa himself spoke to the Fire-god, who was present in embodied form:
"Stay within my sacrificial pit, O embodied one, for the satisfaction of the gods in this sacrifice. (34)
Having spoken thus, the Fire-god, being worshipped, became gracious and took his place in the sacrificial pit;
there, the bearer of oblations appeared in the form of a flame amidst the fuel.
And then the sages, having performed the worship of the sacrificial vessels and other implements, [proceeded].
Having worshipped the Kuṇḍadevas, the Samiddevas, and the other deities, || 36 ||
Having offered them worship according to the rites, he proceeded with the fire-sacrifice (homakārya).
There, the goddesses beginning with Svāhā were indeed his companions, possessing divine forms.
And taking the sacrificial offerings in their hands, they offered them into the mouths of the fires and other such receptacles.
The deities, the lords, and even those liberated ones who are Nārāyaṇas [are also there]. ||38||
And there were Brahmapriyās, Muktānīs, Īśvarīs, and Devikās.
And there were also divine and human sages, beloved by the seers. ||39||
The gods are indeed of the nature of sattva, rajas, and tamas as well.
Furthermore, the bodies of Hari are composed of sattva, rajas, and tamas.
Manifest and embodied, they took their portions at the sacrifice—
those who belong to the creation of the individual soul, the creation of Īśa, and the creation of Brahmā.
Residing upon the leaves of the body's Veda, they all consume [the offerings] in the fire.
In the sacrifice, Hari becomes fully satisfied by the oblations offered. ||42||
In this manner, the sacrifice proceeded according to the prescribed rites for exactly seven days.
The Vaiṣṇava sacrifice is the supreme oblation, a rite that bestows satisfaction upon all. ||43||
Śrī Rādhikā said:
I wish to hear everything regarding those deities whom one must remember so that the fire-oblation (homa) may be properly performed during that Vaiṣṇava sacrifice. 44.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhā, to how the fire-offering (homa) is indeed performed there:
"To the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord, svāhā! ||45||
Svāhā to the imperishable Brahman, and also svāhā to those who are liberated.
Svāhā to those dear to Brahmā, and svāhā also to those who are liberated. ||46||
Svāhā to Kṛṣṇa, the beloved; svāhā to the multitude of gopīs as well.
To Rādhā, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, Svāhā! And to the multitude of cowherds! || 47 ||
Svāhā to the abode of Goloka, and svāhā also to the cows.
Svāhā to Nārāyaṇa, and likewise svāhā to Lakṣmī and Śrī. ||48||
Svāhā to the illustrious female companions, and likewise Svāhā to Vaikuṇṭha;
Svāhā to the host of attendants, and Svāhā to the multitude of maidservants. ||49||
Svāhā indeed to Vāsudeva, and svāhā to Saṃkarṣaṇa;
likewise svāhā to Pradyumna, and svāhā to the one known as Aniruddha.
Svāhā indeed to Mahākāla, who is known as the Great Puruṣa.
And likewise, Svāhā to Māyā, and Svāhā to Tatpuruṣa. ||51||
To the Pradhāna and the Puruṣa, Svāhā! To the bestower of the unmanifested state, Svāhā!
Svāhā to the dweller in immortality, svāhā to the vast one, svāhā to the one of excellent intellect! ||52||
And to Ahaṃkāra, to Mahāviṣṇu, and likewise to Manas; Svāhā! To Viṣṇu in the form of Vairāja, and likewise to Śambhu. ||53||
And likewise, *svāhā* to Brahmā, and *svāhā* to Sadāśiva;
likewise, *svāhā* to the Īśvaras, and also to the Īśvarīs. Likewise, *svāhā* to the Tanmātras, and also *svāhā* to the Indriyas.
And likewise, "Svāhā to the vital breaths" and also "Svāhā to the beings. (55)
Svāhā to the dwellers of the eight enclosures and to Īśeśvara;
svāhā to the Fish-form and to the Tortoise-form, and to the one in the form of the Boar. ||56||
Svāhā to Kapila and Hari, and likewise to Śrīpṛthu;
svāhā to Dattātreya, the Swan, who possesses the form of Nṛsiṃha. ||57||
Svāhā to Ṛṣabha and Vāmana, to the wielder of the axe;
svāhā to Yajña and Kumāra, and to Rāma the archer.
Svāhā indeed to Hayaśīrṣa, svāhā to Nāradanāmī;
svāhā indeed to Rājarāja, svāhā to Vyāsa Kalki. (59)
Svāhā to Mohinikā, and likewise svāhā to Antaryāmin.
Svāhā to those who dwell in truth; svāhā to the illustrious Parameṣṭhin. ||60||
To Sarasvatī, Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, and the consort of Brahmā;
to Asiknī and Paliknī, and to Svadhā, the consort of Vīriṇa. 61.
And likewise for Sṛṣṭi, Sandhyā, Mohinī, and Svāhikā.
And one should also offer the *vaṣaṭ* call to Dakṣa and the others, and likewise to the Prajāpatis. ||62||
"Vaṣaṭ to Manu, to the Vālakhilyas, and also to the Ṛṣis!"
And "Svadhā to the ancestors," and also "Svāhā to the clouds. ||63||
Svāhā to the host belonging to the lineage of Dharma and Adharma, who has desire as his form!
"Obeisance to the seasons, beginning with the year; obeisance also to the ages. (64)
Svāhā to the directions, and svāhā to the qualities; likewise to the substances, and also to the actions, to the classes, and also to the yogas. ||65||
Svāhā to Indra and the other lords of the directions, and also to the inhabitants of the worlds;
svāhā to Truth, to Austerity, to the People, and also to the Great One.
"Oblation to heaven! Oblation to the inhabitants of heaven! To the gods! Oblation also to the hosts of Apsarases! Oblation also to the goddesses! ||67||
Svāhā to the Siddhis and to the Vasus, and also to the Nidhis;
svāhā to all the Grahas, to the Sūryas, and to the Tithis! (68)
And likewise, "Svāhā to the Kalās," and also "to the Nakṣatras";
likewise, "Svāhā to the Tārakās," and also "Svāhā to the Maruts. (69)
Svāhā to the Rudras and the wives of the Rudras, and to Śrī Śaṅkara.
"Obeisance and Svāhā to the Kalās and the Yoginīs, and also to the Khanis;
obeisance and Svāhā to Nara-Nārāyaṇa, and indeed to the one who reclines upon Śeṣa."
Svāhā to the one whose nature is the descent [into the world], and likewise to the one who is the self of the manifested forms.
Likewise, [he offers] "Svāhā to Gaṅgā and the others," and also "Svāhā to the sacred fords (tīrthas)," as well as to Kailāsagaṇakeśa, to Gaṇeśa, and to Śiva. ||72||
Svāhā to the Mother, to the circle of Yoginīs, and to Hanumān;
to Kārtika, to Haṃsa, to Garuḍa, and to Aruṇa. ||73||
" Svāhā to the circle of Agni! Svadhā also to the one belonging to Yama!
Svadhā also to the Śrāvaṇas, and indeed svadhā also to the departed spirits (pretas)! ||74||
Svadhā likewise to the bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and kūṣmāṇḍas;
svāhā and svadhā likewise to the vināyakas and vetālas. ||75||
"To the ḍākinīs and śākinīs, svadhā indeed; to the wives of the ancestors, svadhā; to the bards, genealogists, and female singers, vaṣaṭ; and likewise to the sacred fords. (76)
Likewise, "vaṣaṭ" to human beings, and likewise "vaṣaṭ" to trees and shrubs.
Vaṣaṭ to the creepers, and vaṣaṭ likewise to the grasses and climbing plants. ||77||
Vaṣaṭ likewise to the animals, the beasts, and the birds;
and vaṣaṭ likewise to the reptiles, the insects, and the small creatures. ||78||
Svāhā to the deities of the house, the village, and the field, and to the Earth.
And from the forests, wilds, and rivers, Vauṣaṭ; and likewise from the oceans. ||79||
Vauṣaṭ to the hermitages, to the social classes, and also to the mountains;
Svadhā to the father, the grandfather, and the great-grandfather.
Svadhā to Mātrādyā and also śrauṣaṭ to Viśvādhivāsin;
śrauṣaṭ to the Gandharvas, the Kinnaras, and the Kiṃpuruṣas. ||81||
And also to the Viśvedevas who are to be propitiated, Svāhā! Also to the Maruts;
Vaṣaṭ and Vauṣaṭ to the Cāraṇas; and Ā to the women and the courtesans. 82.
And likewise, "Śrauṣaṭ" is for virtuous women, and "Tyāginībhyaḥ" is for those who have renounced everything in every way.
And *vaṣaṭ* to the aquatic creatures, and likewise *vaṣaṭ* to the *nāgas* and serpents. ||83||
Vaṣaṭ likewise to the Daityas, the Dānavas, and the Rākṣasas;
and vaṣaṭ also to the Yakṣas, and to the descendants of Kaśyapa according to their respective order.
Svāhā to all the gods who preside over creation, and likewise to the Inner Controller;
svāhā to Śrī Harikṛṣṇa, who is dark as a rain cloud. ||85||
And to Bālakṛṣṇa, Svāhā! And to Śrīkṛṣṇavallabha, Svāhā!
"To Gopālabālakāya, and to the son of Kambharāśrī. ||86||
Svāhā to Śrī Hari, and likewise to the illustrious Lord of Māṇikī.
"To Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, Svāhā! And to Him who consists of love! ||87||
Svāhā to the Lord of Pārvatī; svāhā to the Lord of Rāseśvarī;
svāhā to the Supreme Self, the husband of Lakṣmī, who destroys the suffering of Śrī. 88.
Svāhā to the victorious Lalitādhipati, the Haṃsa-yogin;
svāhā to the one whose nature is the inner controller, and to the Lord of All. ||89||
They offered the oblation to the Blessed One with the mantras: "Svāhā to Yajñanārāyaṇa," likewise "Svāhā to Śrī Vahni," and "Oṃ Svāhā to the Supreme Brahman. ||90||
Then all living beings were satisfied with the charming offerings to the gods (havya) and the ancestors (kavya).
Having thus performed the oblation, they respectfully fed [the guests]. 11.
Likewise, [he described] the greatnesses, the dwellings in various lands, and [numbers] in the tens of millions and billions.
And [he gratified] humans, sentient beings, and insentient things with edible objects. ||9||
At that time, indeed, millions of men arrived there at the sacrifice.
And the remaining ones likewise received the Śrī-Vaiṣṇava mantras.
In this manner, even though they are eternal, the oblations and other rites are constantly being performed.
And even millions of human beings are born as Vaiṣṇavas. ||94||
The auspicious sacrifice, which was easily accomplished in seven days, came to an end;
then they all performed the ritual ablution (*avabhṛtha*) in the Bālakṛṣṇa lake.
Indeed, all embodied beings—both divine and non-divine—who had gathered there [performed it].
And they became purified through the power of Bālakṛṣṇa. ||96||
Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa bestowed exceedingly abundant sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās).
Then King Śibi Deva also gave away his entire possession in sacrifice.
He indeed gave his own hundred daughters to Bālakṛṣṇa,
as well as elephants, horses, chariots, golden vehicles, and celestial chariots (vimānas).
At that sacrifice, the king then gave gold, silver, diamonds, and so forth, as well as houses and gardens; he also gave many male and female servants.
The king gave gifts of food, clothing, and cattle numbering in the tens of millions.
Then, O Rādhikā, he indeed gave all his own possessions to Hari. ||100||
Then he made his defense, and everyone rested for the night.
Śibi, however, had a beautiful palace constructed there. ||101||
And where Bālakṛṣṇa shines resplendent together with his six wives.
Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Māṇikī, Kamalā, Śrī, and likewise Ramā. ||102||
They always serve their beloved in the celestial palace;
by reading or hearing this, one shall partake in the fruit of sacrifice. (103)

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Arrangements for the Sacrificial Rites, the Conclusion of the Sacrificial Works, and the King’s Gift of One Hundred Maidens to Śrī Hari, during the Great Sacrifice on the Banks of the Bālakṛṣṇa Lake in the Kingdom of Śibi, within the Second Section (Tretā-santāna) of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. || 124 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Having thus performed a sacrifice on the bank of the Bālakṛṣṇa lake, Hari,
who is Bālakṛṣṇa, created that lake by his own name as Bālakṛṣṇasara.
Having bestowed the mantra and his own vision upon those who had assumed countless bodies,
and having subsequently purified them and fed the people as well,
the Lord himself personally instructed the people on the evening of the third lunar day.

The great king Śibideva conducts himself on earth like one who is liberated. By the power of my grace, the kingdom of Śibi became Vaiṣṇava; and the subjects of Śibi were provided with an abundance of fortune, wealth, and objects of enjoyment.
May they become vessels of happiness; may there be no depression for them. May there never be suffering anywhere, but rather constant prosperity.
May it always be so for you, for your subjects, and for the king as well. || 5 ||
"May there always be devotion toward the royal lineage and toward me on the part of the subjects.
Now, let the subjects, the servants, the sages, and the kings such as Tharkūṭastha go forth to perform the second sacrifice. || 6-7 ||
And let them go forth for the sake of assistance to the kingdom of King Tharkūṭastha;
your own duty must be fulfilled by you with devotion. (8)
The virtues of the wise should be acquired; they bestow happiness and grant divine peace.
One must always remain established in one's own true nature, which is the nature of Brahman.
Truth—speaking according to reality—must be maintained, for it grants welfare.
Purity consists in the constant purification of one's own self through the cleansing of the internal faculties.
It must always be observed by the devoted, but never by those who are defiled by sin.
Compassion should be shown toward living beings to remove their suffering;
patience, which is forbearance even toward those who have committed offenses, must be maintained.
It consists of the restraint of the mind and is always characterized by freedom from agitation.
Generosity is to be constantly guarded, for giving arises from the state of having all desires fulfilled;
indeed, disregard for illusory enjoyments bestows tranquility. (12–13)
Open-handedness toward those in need, lack of greed even when wealth is obtained,
contentment as the state of being filled with one's own innate bliss, and the absence of longing as the lack of desire for whatever has been acquired— these too [are its characteristics]. (1.4)
Even the state of being free from afflictions must always be guarded by people. || 15 ||
Straightforwardness (*ārjava*) and simplicity (*sāralya*) are the uniformity of the three—the mind, speech, and body—and the uniformity of one's inner dispositions (*bhāva*). (16)
Peace—the eternal tranquility consisting of withdrawal from sense objects—must always be protected with effort by devotees of the Lord. (17)
For the sake of one's ultimate welfare, self-restraint—the constant discipline of the senses—must always be practiced toward those things known as excessively vulgar which cause suffering. (18)
People should always exert effort for the sake of attaining knowledge through austerity;
they should observe vows and fasts, and serve their elders. (1.9)
Equanimity must be maintained toward the virtuous; one should always disregard the deceitful when they are wicked.
Forbearance and endurance must be maintained when one is situated in the suffering known as the pairs of opposites.
One should indeed abide in the form of the Self with a state of non-resistance;
cessation must always be protected through the avoidance of futile activity. (21)
The knowledge of the scriptures, which is to be attained from the true teacher and the deity, must be understood both by oneself and especially by others as well. (22)
Dispassion toward all objects, constant freedom from longing, and the state of having an unattracted mind must be especially guarded. (23)
Sovereignty is attained through union with the Blessed One, reaching equality of power before Hari; valor is victory by one's own nature—this must be practiced by people in every way. (24)
His splendor is to be protected by his devotees; he is devoid of being assailable by others;
and his strength is always self-strength, due to his union with the Controller of all. (25)
Indeed, my compassion for Bālakṛṣṇa must protect his power; I must maintain mindfulness regarding what is to be done and constant reflection upon the auspicious refuge.
One must strive with great effort to protect [this state] through devotion to the Supreme Lord;
for the Sātvatas, autonomy and independence from others are what must be guarded. 27.
Skill in all undertakings and supreme proficiency must be protected;
likewise, the beautiful luster born of the power of celibacy must be preserved. (28)
Fortitude is the avoidance of agitation even in adverse circumstances;
gentleness must always be maintained by abandoning harshness and rigidity. (29)
Boldness and inspired intuition, which grant insight into the investigation of liberation, must be preserved; humility and discipline must be maintained, for they produce virtuous conduct. (2.125.30)
One must practice forbearance with the mind; even when all things are being struck down, one should remain unstruck.
One’s vital energy (*ojas*) must be protected in every way from the eyes and other organs of perception (*jñānendriya*). (31)
Likewise, majesty and strength must be protected within the organs of action;
and sovereignty, which is my own lordship consisting of the state of being pre-eminent over all and so forth, must be protected. (32)
One's profound depth must be protected, as must the inner counsel that is difficult to grasp; steadfastness should always be preserved by devotees, free from all fickleness. (33)
Faith (*āstikya*) is a firm mind directed toward me, Hari, regarding dharma, liberation, and the like;
it is conviction in the meaning declared by the scriptures and trust in the Supreme Self. (34)
Pure fame, devotion, renown, and the granting of light are to be attained by people;
silence must always be maintained and idle talk avoided by the followers of the Sāttvata path. (39)

The absence of pride must always be guarded against, as it is the lack of self-reproach regarding one's virtues and so forth; likewise, the absence of conceit must be guarded against, as it is the loss of one's true nature through vanity.
Likewise, the absence of hypocrisy must be guarded against, as well as freedom from deceit;
one should consume suitable food that yields the fruit of liberation. (37)
Skillfulness, the protection [of others], and the teaching of beneficial words—not anything else—must be maintained;
likewise, friendliness must be preserved as the foundation of trust for all embodied beings. (38)
One should perform service for all beings with great longing,
and one must always protect against agitation, whether by force or even by thirst.
Those devoted practitioners of yoga who abide in goodness must never be agitated by sense objects;
likewise, Vaiṣṇavas must never, under any circumstances, inflict suffering upon living beings.
One should practice showing respect to all in every way, and one must also ensure that there is no attainment of what is undesirable or any humiliation. //41//
One should dwell together with those who possess knowledge of Brahman and with the virtuous;
one must preserve goodness and protect those who have come for refuge. 42.
Free from desire for fruits, devoid of possessiveness, one should preserve [this state] within me, the Supreme Self, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 43.
And devotion consisting of the surrender of all one's possessions must be practiced toward me by my Sāttvatas;
just as devotion is to be performed toward me, so too must it be performed toward my virtuous devotees. 44.
Likewise, serving the guru with a spirit of sincere love—service to the guru is service to me, which always bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (45)
My worship must be performed, as well as the adoration of me by the virtuous;
for this bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and destroys all sins. ||46||
A wife should always be protected for her happiness and never oppressed at any time;
a husband should always be honored by his wife and never oppressed at any time. 47.

Those in the middle stages of life, such as sons and others, must indeed always serve the elderly; likewise, cows and virtuous people must always be protected, for they are the ones who inspire devotion and awakening. 48.
The deities, who are the very embodiment of the divine form and whose sight purifies, must be protected within the home;
and the gurus, who deliver one from the cycle of worldly existence, must always be protected in the home. 49.
One should always perform devotion to me, Nārāyaṇa;
and one should take refuge in me, Puruṣottama, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
The command of the guru—whether auspicious or bestowing liberation—is always to be observed;
the words of the guru must always be honored by his younger brothers as the bringer of peace for themselves. 5.1.
Worship of me, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, must always be performed here by the foremost of my devotees within this image, which is indeed the Supreme Brahman. (52)
A bath should be taken here in the lake at Bālakṛṣṇaka on the eleventh day of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, or on the second day of the new moon.
This rite, which destroys all sins, should be performed during the seven days;
herein, one should practice charity, which bestows liberation, through the gift of cows.
The gift of my image shall be the accomplisher of all goals;
likewise, the gift of an elephant, the gift of a horse, and the gift of a bull [shall do so]. (55)
The gift of a buffalo-cow and the gift of a reṇḍī-bull, as well as the giving away of a cart, a vehicle, and a celestial chariot (vimāna). ||56||
The gift of palanquins and the gift of vehicles;
the gift of garments, woolen blankets, and fine cloths. ||57||
The chamberlains should perform the gift of gold, silver, and copper, which yields ten millionfold merit and bestows prosperity. (58)
The gift of a vessel should be performed, as well as the most excellent gift of food;
the gift of water, the gift of sweets, and the gift of desired objects bring auspiciousness. (59)
One should perform the gift of vegetables, the gift of a maiden which is the station of heaven, as well as the gift of knowledge and the bestowing of the sacred thread. (2.125.60)
Likewise, the gift of a house, as well as gifts arising from household utensils and the like, the gift of a garden, and the gift of a field should be performed. (61)
Whatever may be dear to oneself, that indeed should be given as a gift here;
food should be given to the virtuous, and honor should be rendered to the great seers.
One who desires their own welfare should provide food, bark garments, and other such items;
and for the satisfaction of the ancestors, the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍas) and other rites must be performed.
It shall provide eternal satisfaction, just like the Bālakṛṣṇa lake;
the worship of the gods should be performed on the bank of the Bālakṛṣṇa lake. (64)
Temples for the gods should be constructed on its banks,
as well as abodes for the liberated ones, the incarnations, and the lords.
One should also cause to be built auspicious palaces for the sages and the ancestors that bestow liberation, as well as dharma-halls and halls of devotion that bring about welfare. (66)
Gardens, groves, and the like should be constructed for the sake of Hari;
having built a temple here together with my image, [one should install] the gods. (67)
To those devotees who shall establish [this], I grant a dwelling, as well as a livelihood, a means of subsistence, and a continuous stream of offerings for worship. (68)
For those devotees who cause [this] to be made, their merit shall be infinite;
I myself, as Puruṣottama, shall bestow everything upon them in my abode.
All the gods, as well as the liberated ones, the lords, and the Nārāyaṇas; the incarnations, the goddesses, the liberated women, and the foremost of the gods. || 2.125.70 ||
"May the goddesses, the gods, the sages, and the sacred fords dwell here;
for I myself, Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, shall indeed reside here. (71)
On the eleventh day of the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa,
every year, all the holy fords, the gods, and the virtuous remain there incessantly.
Likewise, the liberated ones and the lords must come here for the sake of the world,
for seven days, in order to attain all forms of purification through the sacred power of this holy site.
Indeed, millions of people shall bathe here in this lake;
for them, there shall be the destruction of sin and merit that is truly infinite. (74)
This is the most excellent of sacred fords, the highest among all the best of tīrthas;
having made my residence here permanently, I shall establish myself in this place.
Here, the diseases of those who establish holy fords shall indeed go to their destruction;
poverty shall come to an end, and misfortune shall meet its ruin. (76)
Prosperity shall dwell in their homes, and likewise they shall increase their good fortune;
moreover, the lineage of sons, grandsons, and so forth shall flourish here for those who visit sacred pilgrimage sites.
For those who perform rites at sacred fords, even in months other than Mārgaśīrṣa, the attainment of whatever they desire among the four aims of human life shall be theirs.
Sins are destroyed and merit becomes the bestower of heaven, even for those who die here in the water or whose ashes and bones are cast into it. (79)
Even the destruction of all sins and eternal liberation shall accrue to that person who drinks even a single drop of the water from this lake. (2.125.80)
Even for one who has reached the state of death, there is eternal liberation;
and I, the Supreme Lord, have arisen as his master, full of aesthetic essence (rasa). ||8 1 ||
Through union with Śrī Bālakṛṣṇaka, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, my own yoga shall become eternal by means of this lotus-like connection. 82.
Through bathing in it, drinking from it, beholding it, sipping its water, touching it, and even by remembering this sacrifice, there is liberation from the lake. (83)
"It shall certainly come to pass, there is no doubt; I, the Supreme Person, will grant it.
Penance, pilgrimage, vows, and fire-offerings must be performed here by those seeking liberation. (84)
And the dedication of all actions to me, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, must be performed;
for that which is offered to me will certainly result in eternal merit. (85)
Therein are Muktatīrtha, Brahmatīrtha, the Tīrthas beginning with Brahmapriyā,
the Tīrthas beginning with the Avatāras, and likewise Bhūmatīrtha.
The holy site named Vāsudeva, the Prādyumna holy site, the Devāyatana holy site, and also the Vairāja holy site. ||87||
Likewise, there is Kṛṣṇatīrtha, Rādhātīrtha, and Śrītīrtha;
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme tīrtha, and Lakṣmītīrtha is the most auspicious. (88)
The Brahmatīrtha, Viṣṇutīrtha, Śivatīrtha accompanied by Satī, Rudratīrtha, Rāśitīrtha, and likewise the excellent Ṛṣitīrtha. ||89||
The sacred ford of the ancestors, the sacred ford of the gods, and the sacred ford of the guardians of the directions;
the sacred ford of Indra, the sacred ford of Agni, and the most auspicious sacred ford of Dharma.
The Vāyu-tīrtha, the Yama-tīrtha, the excellent Kubera-tīrtha, the preeminent Īśāna-tīrtha, and the Bṛhaspati-pratīrtha. ||9 1||
The auspicious holy site named Lomaśa, the most excellent and auspicious Yajñatīrtha, as well as Kambharātīrtha and also Santoṣātīrtha. || 92 ||
And there is the illustrious Gopālatīrtha, as well as Māṇikītīrtha;
likewise Sabhātīrtha and the auspicious and beloved Pāravaśantīrtha. (93)
The Vedatīrtha, the Gāyatrītīrtha called Sāvitrikā, the Kuṅkumavāpikātīrtha, and the Bālakṛṣṇapratīrthaka. ||94||
The great holy site of Kalpavallī is auspicious and bestows all desired objects;
there is also the Graha-tīrtha, the Sūrya-tīrtha, and the Devāyatana-tīrtha. ||95||
Vasutīrtha, Sādhyatīrtha, Viśvetīrtha, the auspicious Śubhāspada, as well as Sāmudratīrtha and Kailāsatīrtha. ||96||
There is also Vaikuṇṭha-tīrtha, as well as Gaṇeśa-tīrtha;
Gaṇa-tīrtha, Satī-tīrtha, and the most excellent of all excellent Sādhvī-tīrtha. (97)
The Vratatīrtha, the tīrtha called Vimāna, the Śibitīrtha, the Avabhṛtha, and the Mahātīrtha, which is the abode of all holy fords (tīrthas). ||98||
Indeed, all these and other embodied forms dwell here; by my command, from this day forward, they shall be purifiers for embodied beings. 99.
Therefore, human beings must always perform religious duties here;
then they all surely proceed to the kingdom of Tharkūṭastha.
"Wherever fame is to be established, there let them establish their presence;
I shall come there either tomorrow or the day after.
Having spoken thus, the deities of the holy sites assumed a second form.
For they always abide there in the form of sacred fords, O Rādhikā.
Then they all went there, to the lake named Dvikalā,
in the kingdom of the great king Tharkūṭastha, specifically for the purpose of performing a sacrifice.

Indeed, all the lords, gods, and humans— numbering in the millions, billions, and hundreds of millions— along with virtuous and chaste women who are dear to Hari, traveled by celestial chariot. Bālakṛṣṇa resided for a day in the royal palace of Śibi.
"Indeed, for the sake of rest as well as for the acceptance of service by the King.

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Instructions and Blessings bestowed by Śrī Hari in the form of Bālakṛṣṇa, the Command for the Second Sacrifice, and the Holy Tīrthas of the Bālakṛṣṇa Lake," in the second section, the Tretā Cycle, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, a great marvel occurred there in the presence of the assembly;
thousands of those with emaciated limbs were gathered there.
Men and women of coarse complexion, dark, and bereft of luster arrived like wretched people—suffering, destitute, and forlorn. || 2 ||

Seeking their own liberation from the bondage of the ocean of suffering, the people saw them, and then a great wonder arose. "Who are these? From where have they come?"—thus the people made an inquiry.
Having understood their inner intention, Hari asked them, "Who are you here?"
Weeping, they then spoke while men and women listened:
"We were formerly deceased ancestors, ghosts dwelling in the realm of the departed. (5)
Having all gone to an evil state, by the thousands we dwell here on the shore of the lake in this great forest, hungry and likewise distressed.
"In this matter, they consider us to be the fathers of these subjects, yet they do not think so of us.
O Blessed One, please grant us our share here by means of the offering of water. (7)
To them who had spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, having made his own water auspicious, gave it to them for the purpose of drinking.
Having given them sweet divine food and having repeatedly satisfied them,
he granted them the most excellent liberation that leads to the world of Brahmā.
All of them indeed became auspicious, liberated beings with divine bodies;
equal to the liberated, they departed in celestial chariots to the eternal Brahman.
Thus, on the shore of the lake, Hari granted liberation to them;
having witnessed this supreme wonder, the people performed śrāddha rites.
By that, liberation and satisfaction were produced for the ancestors;
thus, O Rādhikā, did that Pitṛtīrtha come into being.
In the garden of King Śibi,
the beginningless and glorious Bālakṛṣṇa, surrounded by his army and retinue, was worshipped while wearing the guise of a king.
Richly adorned with the splendor of royal attire and accompanied by Ambālikā, the Supreme Lord was seated upon a white four-tusked elephant. || 14 ||
Having traveled by means of a celestial chariot to his own capital city named Svāmipālāśā, he [seated himself] upon a four-tusked elephant.
Furthermore, Kṛṣṇa was led along the royal highway and other streets; there, Acyuta was honored by the subjects with flowers, parched grain, and fried rice.
Kṛṣṇa was honored, saluted, and entreated with great devotion by King Bhūpāla, together with Queen Bhūprabhā, for a long time in the royal palace. || 17 ||
Then, having traveled by way of the celestial chariot to Tāmrakaśā,
the Lord granted his vision to the queen and was honored by her parents.
Mādhava traveled by means of a celestial chariot together with King Śibi to the bank of the lake named Dvikalā in the kingdom of King Ṭharkūṭastha.
On the western land, as far as the river Bīnā,
they saw the pavilions that had been constructed and the new encampments.
Having caused the aerial chariot to circle the lake,
he brought it down on the western shore of the lake, near the pavilion.
Then indeed auspicious musical instruments were played; there were shouts of victory and likewise cries of "Well done! (22).
With flowers, sandalwood paste, parched grain, unbroken rice, saffron, and other offerings, the people offered worship to Lord Hari, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. 23.
There, on the shore of the Dvīkala ocean, there were millions of men, eager for a vision of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (24)
Desiring purity, ten million men and women—human beings from the young to the old—also gathered there to witness the sacrifice. (25)
To that Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, who was shining like the sun,
as well as to his mother, father, two brothers, sister, and daughter-in-law.
Seeing Śibi, the foremost of devotees, they rejoiced with eager anticipation; so too did Lomaśa, who was accompanied by his wife and devoted to his vows, upon seeing the temple of the deity.
The sages, beginning with Vasiṣṭha, gave necklaces to Śrī Hari;
so too did King Tharkūṭastha and his four queens. (28)
The sages, beginning with Meṣa and others, offered necklaces to Viṣṇu around his neck;
there, at a distance of fifty yojanas, a great pavilion exists.
In the midst of that, Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa went and bathed in the lake;
he sat upon a golden central throne and shone resplendently.
On the morning of the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, Hari himself appointed a circle of sages, each according to his fitness, for the performance of the sacrifice.

The gods, the lords of the gods, the liberated ones, those who have not yet descended [into incarnation], the twice-born and others, virtuous wives, saintly women, and male and female servants, just as they were indeed in the first sacrifice.
Then the great king Tharkūṭastha, the sacrificer accompanied by his beloved,
chose Brahmā and the other officiating priests by grasping their forearms.
Lomaśa bound the king and Bālakṛṣṇa, the sacrificer, to his forearm; and Kṛṣṇa also bound Lomaśa to his forearm.
He bound even his teacher, who was merely secondary, as well as his wife, his vows, Hari, and the twice-born;
indeed, he bound others by the thousands and even beyond a hundred thousand.
Purification, the recitation of auspicious prayers, the installation of the deities, worship, the fire sacrifice, and the giving of gifts were performed just as they had been in previous rites. (36)
Worship, feeding, giving, sacrificial fees, the welcoming reception, and so forth—all this was accomplished in its entirety, just as it had been performed in previous rites. (37)
This Vaiṣṇava sacrifice itself has reached completion in seven days; the sacrificial fees consist of gifts of food, clothing, gold, silver, and other such items. (38)
Everything here was indeed performed by Tharkūṭaka as before,
and the ritual bath (avabhṛtha) for the path took place on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight.
At that western lake during the second watch of the day, the eager liberated ones, the lords, the incarnations, the gods, and the ancestors and humans performed [their rites]. (2.126.40)
Likewise, others dwelling in the netherworld (pātāla), as well as other embodied beings, both insentient and sentient, along with the people joined by Kṛṣṇa, bathed at the root of the seed. 41.
And thus, at the time of the two watches, Kṛṣṇa bathed in the waters of the Bīnā river,
visited the sacred fords, and fed those who were honored.
Devoted to that purpose, he fed the wretched, the helpless, the poor, and others;
thereafter, he fed all his subjects with various kinds of sweet foods.
Afterwards, Hari fed those who served the meal,
and he gratified the groups of both sentient and insentient beings with food and water.
There, the sage Lomaśa gave the mantras to all those who had arrived seeking liberation; Śrī Hari himself also bestowed his own mantras.
When the sacrifice had been thus completed by King Tharkūṭastha,
Hari placed his own lotus feet within the heart of that king.
May your kingdom be unshakable, may your subjects be joyful, may you be laden with all prosperity, and may you be the sustainer of your lineage. (47)
Just as there are sacred fords in the waters of Lake Bālakṛṣṇa, so may all sacred fords likewise dwell within this lake. 48.
The liberated lords and incarnations, such as Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and Ramā;
as well as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and others, along with the ancestors and the sages. (49)
In that interval, wherever the gods, goddesses, and humans bathed,
may they all dwell there in divine form, possessing celestial bodies.
Thus commanded by Hari, they dwelt there continuously;
all those sacred fords were established by the Supreme Soul.
He said, "Bathing, giving gifts, chanting, sacrificing, and offering oblations performed here shall yield infinite rewards, equal to ten million times their merit. (52)
A śrāddha ceremony should be performed here at this auspicious holy site of the seven-day sacrifice;
for here, the abode of all sacred fords, it shall grant liberation and fulfill one's desires.
In the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, during the moments of the fifth and eleventh lunar days,
an assembly should be held there on the auspicious bank of the Sarasvatī.
And here a temple should be constructed, containing my auspicious golden image,
which bestows the gift of fearlessness and is likewise accompanied by a garland.
The excellent [image] should be installed here in this temple together with six maidservants, accompanied by Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Brahmavidyā, Ramā, Śrī, and Māṇikī. (56)
Sacrifices such as the Sarvamedha and others dedicated to Viṣṇu should be performed right here,
just as this Vaiṣṇava sacrifice, which is an adoration of all the gods, has been performed.
Likewise, devotees should perform auspicious sacrifices according to their means;
indeed, through this libation, there shall be liberation from evil destinies.
One should perform ancestral rites, such as *śrāddha* offerings, here at this sacred site (*tīrtha*) by reciting the names of one's ancestors;
furthermore, for the sake of completely destroying all sins, one must certainly bathe here in every way. (59)
Those whose death is imminent should take up residence on the shore of this lake;
I, Lord Nārāyaṇasvāmī, shall give you the mantra that grants liberation.
The divine discourses of the *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā*, which awaken my own spiritual capacity, should be recited by those who know the ultimate truth. 6.1.
In this matter, she who bestows liberation and grants the primordial awakening must be recited;
my scripture is indeed the Veda itself, and it was heard by Lakṣmī and Rādhā.
It was likewise heard by Māṇikyā, Ramā, Vidyā, Mañjulā, Haṃsā, and Sadguṇā. (63)
Thus it was heard by Jayā, Lalitā, Bhūlīlā, and others who were liberated;
likewise, it was heard by the sages, the ancestors, the gods, Nārāyaṇa, and the inhabitants of the earth.
For those situated in the lower realms and elsewhere have not heard the deeds performed by me in body after body, one after another, throughout the past.
That is worth hearing, worthy of being proclaimed, and should be heard again and again:
"I am Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman, the Puruṣottama. (66)
He alone is to be worshipped, and I am that very one, the inner self, higher than the highest;
such is my firm conviction, which must be maintained as constant and free from doubt. 67.
Devotion to me must always be practiced, preceded by the offering of all one's possessions;
my devotees should always be honored for their divine nature, just as I am.
One must not commit treachery against a devotee; treachery is the destruction of one's own true nature. However, one should always cultivate association with my devotees. ||69||
I must always be seen by you after bathing in the morning at my temple;
likewise, the devotion of a servant and the devotion of a slave must be shown toward me, who am the virtuous ones.
One should dwell in my abode for the cessation of suffering and its defects;
one must not commit violence against anyone, nor should one enjoy another's wife. (7.1)
One must not eat meat, nor drink liquor and the like; one must never commit a breach of moral conduct toward an unworthy person. (72)
One should not even commit suicide, nor should one ever practice theft;
furthermore, one must never cast false accusations or stains upon another. (73)
Neither the gods nor goddesses, nor even embodied beings, are truly objects of censure;
for censure gives rise to evil and consequently destroys merit. (74)
That which is inedible must never be eaten, and that which is undrinkable must never be drunk;
for it is considered inedible and undrinkable when it is devoid of the grace of the deity. (75)
One must not entertain the company of atheists, for it obstructs liberation; one should always serve the virtuous, for the virtuous are indeed my own forms. (76)
Whether a man or a woman, one is indeed liberated from evil through service;
those who are my virtuous ones are the bestowers of liberation. ||77||
That body is in every way meritorious, a bestower of merit, supremely purifying;
there is no exclusion of anyone’s share therein, just as it is with me when I am present.
Service to one's mother and father must be performed in every way on this earth;
for those who shall obey my command, their accomplishments (siddhis) are certain.
The currents of lightning from the cosmic eon, the atomic essences of the eon,
and the juices of the eon-creeper shall always be present in their homes.
Possessing halls for the fulfillment of desires, with the expansion of the lineage of their volitions,
all these collections of reality are wish-fulfilling and universal in scope.
In the homes of those who carry out my command,
I shall always be a granter of whatever they desire, just as I am in the Imperishable.

One should enjoy pleasures, but not excessively; one should practice devotion, but in a superlative manner. One should sleep, but not excessively; one should practice service, but in a superlative manner. ||83||
The mind should not be drawn toward base activities; one should practice the art of deluding [the senses] through illusion.
One should not harbor excessive thirst, nor should one entertain desires that exceed what is mine.
One should not harbor attachment here; rather, one should practice that which bestows liberation in the hereafter.
Agitation must be abandoned in every way, and eternal peace must be attained. (85)
One should not exert effort in many ways regarding worldly knowledge; rather, one should strive for the highest goal.
One must not remain dependent on others, but should instead abide in the reality of the Self.
One should certainly not conduct oneself as if identifying with the body; rather, one should act through one's own true self.
One should not maintain attachment to the household, but should remain steadfastly devoted to the true Master.
For I am indeed the supreme master, known as the Supreme Lord, who exists in every way as the ultimate master of all devotees whatsoever. (88)
Water is a sacred place, land is a sacred place, and the self is always the most excellent sacred place; virtuous people are always a sacred place, and my own Lord Hari is the sacred place. (89)
"Wherever I am and my image is, that is a sacred ford (tīrtha) granting divine liberation. Thus, O people of Tharkūṭa, you should understand this in every respect. ||2.126.90||
"Perform devotion to me with daily respect;
receive my mantras from me alone, for they grant excellent liberation."
Thus instructed, those devotees went by the millions to obtain the *manus*; they approached the presence of Śrī Hari, and Hari bestowed the *manus* upon them. (92)
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā!
May Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa be my refuge at all times. 93.
Out of fear of Time, Māyā, evil karma, enemies, Yama, and treacherous friends,
one should wear the trident, fish, banner, bow, wheel, and svastika.
I am Brahmā, an eternal devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is my master and my husband. (95)
Bālakṛṣṇa is the Supreme Brahman; he is indeed my eternal Lord.
May he be my father, kinsman, well-wisher, friend, protector, and guardian. (96)
"Śrī Kṛṣṇavallabhasvāmī, Śrī Hari, is my refuge"—in this very way, O Rādhikā, Kṛṣṇa indeed bestowed the mantras upon them. 97.
Then, having made his defense, he went home for the sake of rest;
likewise did the great king Tharkūṭastha, as well as the queens, the sons, and the daughters. (98)
Then they all massaged the feet of Bālakṛṣṇa;
honored by the king and fed, they rested.
And on the second day in the capital, the subjects, filled with longing, joyfully beheld Bālakṛṣṇa mounted upon an elephant as he was being paraded about.
They increased [his joy] exceedingly and, being eager, likewise offered worship;
having arrived at the royal palace, Keśava spoke in the assembly hall.
Tomorrow, let them depart after having enjoyed the union with the Lord of the Night;
for in the kingdom of the great king Vīrajāra, the third sacrifice shall take place.
The commencement of the sacrifice shall take place from the third day of the dark fortnight of Pauṣa;
it must be performed for seven days, until the ninth lunar day.
"I shall come there on the very morning of the second day," having been thus addressed, all those lords of gods and sages departed by means of celestial vehicles.
All the great sages of creation went to the bank of the river Auvinadī;
and Śrī Hari, having attained composure, dwelt there at Arkutasthaka.
O Rādhikā, Hari— who grants liberation, who is the treasury of all desires, the Lord, and the fulfiller of every aspiration— resides happily in that house for the time being.

By reading this, by hearing it, by causing others to hear it, and even by reflecting upon it, a person shall obtain the merit of bathing at the two sacred times (dvikāla) as well as the merit of fame. || 107 ||

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Performance of the Second Viṣṇu Sacrifice in the Dvikalasarovara Lake during the Reign of the Great King Tharkūṭastha, as well as the Bestowing of Mantras and Instruction upon the Subjects," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, to that wonder which indeed occurred there;
formerly, by means of an earthquake, those who had died attained the state of the gods. || 1 ||
More than a hundred thousand pretas, residing on Mount Samāna,
came to the Dvikala Tīrtha in the presence of Kṛṣṇa for the sake of liberation.
Some indeed had crooked faces, some had withered bodies;
others had broken waists, and still others had bellies pressed against their backs.
Others were covered in hair and swarming with flies, while others were entangled in webs of mosquitoes; some suffered from the pains of hunger and thirst, and others were blind, lame, or maimed.
Those afflicted with leprosy, those with impaired limbs and so forth, those suffering from asthma, cough, and other diseases,
as well as others with hanging bellies or dropsy, and those who are blind or devoid of ears— (5).
With their feet turned backward and their faces turned toward their backs, hideous and impoverished,
thousands of those suffering beings arrived before Hari.
For the sake of destroying suffering alone, they prayed to Acyuta—
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama.
For in the past, during earthquakes, we were destroyed by the collapse of houses and the crushing of trees; we even fell when the earth split open.
Sunk in water-filled cavities, we were then lost and dead;
indeed, we are miserable ghosts through these sudden deaths.
In this matter, you alone are capable of delivering us, and no others;
therefore, deliver us from this most sinful womb and show us compassion.
Thus entreated, the Blessed Lord indeed cast water upon them with his joined palms; it was auspicious, and they received it at that time.
Their sins having been burnt away, they again requested water for the purpose of drinking;
Kṛṣṇa then gave them the water from the lake.
The Lord caused them to drink what had been brought for his own purpose;
having drunk again and again until they were fully satiated, they then requested food.
The Blessed One gave to them auspicious sweet food mixed with sugar,
along with milk-rice (pāyasa) prepared with ghee, produced from the wish-fulfilling cow.
Having eaten and become satisfied, they were born anew and requested freedom from disease;
Hari granted them beautiful health and a gentle physique.
Then they requested liberation and service with divine bodies; Hari granted them liberation, and they departed with divine bodies.
They reached the supreme world of Vaikuṇṭha by means of celestial chariots resembling the sun;
there, the men became attendants (pārṣadas), four-armed and brilliantly radiant.
The women and the female attendants, possessing four arms and great fortune, indeed became liberated in form and dwellers in the abode of liberation. || 18 ||
Thus, out of compassion for them, Bālakṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śrī,
by means of his own yoga, truly bestowed Vaikuṇṭha itself upon them this very day in an instant.
In this matter, neither merit nor even devotion is the cause; rather, the state of being a protector of those who have sought refuge, imbued with compassion, is the cause. (2.127.20)
Then Kṛṣṇa, the great king and lord of Ramā, who is beloved by Māṇikī and the lord of lords, spoke to her as she stood upon the mountain peak. ||21||
O great king Tharkūṭastha, listen to that which is to be known here:
dharma, knowledge, detachment, and devotion—this is the fourfold [path]. (22)
For you must always protect four objectives on this earth;
they grant happiness in this world and bestow bliss in the hereafter. (23)
