"To the Viśvedevas known as Satya and Vasu, and to the Nāndīmukhas: Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, this comfortable seat. (76)
"May there be *svadhā* for you; let the *nāndī-śrāddha* be performed, and let it be so, Om!
May you both accept it and attain it, endowed with happiness. (77)
May the comfortable seat for your mother, paternal grandmother, and great-grandmother be established; may we establish for you this seat which brings happiness, svāhā!
May this comfortable seat for your fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers be provided; we offer it with the cry of Svāhā, bringing you happiness. (79)
O maternal grandfather, great-grandfather, and great-great-grandfather, this seat is for you; Svadhā! May it bring happiness, O Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ!
Fragrance and flowers are offered to Satyavasu and to the Viśvedevas who are Nāndīmukhas; this is the worship consisting of fragrance and other offerings. (81)
May there be prosperity here; may the *svadhā* offerings reach you all, as well as my mother, paternal grandmother, and paternal great-grandmother.
And may this offering of fragrance and so forth, accompanied by the word "svāhā," result in prosperity for the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather. (83)

And let this worship with perfumes and so forth, along with the *svadhā* and the *vṛddhi*, be complete for the maternal grandfather, the great maternal grandfather, and the great-great maternal grandfather. (84)
"May this offering of fragrance and worship be for the women; svadhā! Prosperity!"—having thus given the offering, [one gives] the price for the meal. (85)
O Satyavasu, one should give wealth to the Viśvedevas;
and food sufficient for the meal of an even number of persons is offered as nectar (amṛta).
May there be *svadhā*; may this auspicious prosperity bestow long life and splendor upon [my] mother, paternal grandmother, and paternal great-grandmother. (87)
Food sufficient for a couple has been offered as nectar;
may it result in *svadhā* and prosperity, accompanied by the gift of gold. (88)
And indeed, to the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers, food sufficient for a pair of diners was offered as nectar. (89)
"May there be prosperity; may there be growth, accompanied by the sacrificial fee of gold.
[Salutation to] the maternal grandfather, the great-grandfather, and the great-great-grandfather. (2.145.90)
This food, sufficient and like nectar, has been offered by you along with your wives;
may it become *svadhā* for the increase [of our merit], accompanied by the gift of gold.
I give this sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) consisting of the price of grapes, myrobalans, and barley.
And for the sake of the fruits of the Nāndī-śrāddha, and for the sake of the grain and wealth [of the ancestors]. ||92||
And likewise, for the sake of fulfilling the fruit of the Nāndī-śrāddha, I give this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to my mother, paternal grandmother, and paternal great-grandmother.
And likewise, for the sake of fulfilling the fruit of the Nāndī-śrāddha, I give this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to my father, grandfather, and great-grandfather.
To you—my maternal grandfather, great-grandfather, and great-great-grandfather, together with their wives—I here give this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) as a means of ransom. 95.

For the fulfillment of the fruits of the *nāndī-śrāddha*, may they accept the grapes, *āmalaka* fruits, and ginger; and for the successful completion of the consecration of the fruit-offering, I now relinquish them.
Having recited the *nāndīśrāddha* as fully accomplished and offered the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the dismissal of the gods is performed with:
"May the Viśvedevas be pleased; Om! (97).
May the Nāndīmukha mothers be pleased at their dismissal;
may the Nāndīmukha fathers be pleased at their dismissal. ||98||
"May the maternal grandfathers, whose faces are joyful, be pleased"; with these words, he performs their dismissal.
Having followed the Brahmins for some distance, he completes the rite according to their instruction. (99)
"May this rite of the *śrāddha*, made complete by the favor of the *nāndīmukha* ancestors, indeed be fully accomplished in accordance with the words of the Brahmins. (2.145.10)
Thus, O Rādhikā, the supreme Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa has spoken to you this instruction regarding the body of the temple deity, as I have related it to you.

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Installation of the Vessel, the Recitation of the Auspicious Day, the Invocation of the Mothers, the Nāndī-śrāddha, the Worship of the Seat, the Offering of Food, the Giving of Dakṣiṇā, the Dismissal, and so forth," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā, to what the Blessed Lord told His devotee after the Nāndī-śrāddha, regarding the selection of the preceptor and others.
Since this foundation must be established through ritual acts, I choose you, O Brahmin, as my preceptor by means of perfumes, unbroken grains, and other offerings. (2)
I am honored with flowers, betel, seals, and garments;
having worshipped him thus, one should then perform the formal selection of the Brahman priest. || 3 ||
While this installation is to be performed during the ritual acts, I choose you for the station of Brahmā, since you examine whether the rites have been performed or left undone. || 4 ||
With perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice, betel, seals, garments, and other offerings, [I declare]:
"I have been chosen for the office of Brahman; indeed, I am the Brahman in your sacrifice. (5)
Having honored him, one should choose eight or four officiating priests (ṛtvij) who are knowers of the Vedas for the installation of this deity.
"I choose you, so-and-so, for the office of officiating priest (ṛtvij) here with perfumes and other offerings.
To them, he should say, "Om, we are chosen," and honor them with perfumes, unbroken rice grains (akṣata), and other such items.
The sacrificer should appoint eight or four door-keepers;
he should appoint two reciters for each of the Vedas.
In this manner, there are twenty-five officiating priests (ṛtvij);
or, if one is unable, one may instead appoint eight Hotṛs.
The four chanters, the four door-keepers, and the Guru—
thus indeed there are seventeen officiating priests (ṛtvij).
Alternatively, there are thirteen: four *hotṛ*s, four *jāpaka*s, four gatekeepers, and the preceptor.
Or rather, the performer of the sacrifice should choose both the Ācārya and the Brahmā;
by these two alone, the entire sacrificial rite is accomplished, without a doubt.
The king, however, should choose a hundred thousand [brāhmaṇas] according to his strength;
thereafter, he should honor the preceptor and the others according to the prescribed rule and in the order of their selection.
One should indeed honor [the guest] with madhuparka, such as sweet milk-rice (pāyasa) and the like;
for madhuparka is of many kinds, consisting of sweet, sour, and other flavors, including milk-rice and so forth.
Then the sacrificer, rising with palms joined in reverence, should entreat the Brahmins:
"May the Brahmins be peaceful for me, warding off all evils. (15)
Through acts of charity, sacrifice, recitation, and fire-offerings, these officiating priests grant satisfaction to both the ancestors and the gods; they are indeed the very embodiments of the Vedas.
May the reciters protect me and grant me both supernatural power and prosperity;
may the Brahmins selected for the sacrifice perform rites of pacification so that the ritual may reach completion.
"And let the twice-born, established in their observances, perform the rite for prosperity.
Having thus properly entreated the Brahmins, the sacrificer should entreat the preceptor. (18)
"You abide as the embodiment of the mantra; bring about the advancement of my dharma.
By your grace, let this sacrifice indeed be completed without obstacles. (19)
Having thus offered this prayer, the sacrificer himself then rose up,
took the appropriate ritual materials, and placed the married women in front of him.
Having placed the Brahmins at the forefront and set the sound of musical instruments in motion,
the patron of the sacrifice, accompanied by a full water-pot, [enters] the pavilion.
Having performed a circumambulation and reached the western gate itself,
he should stand holding the vessel of *argha* with both hands.

Having meditated on the Earth situated upon a tortoise at the entrance, white in color and possessing four arms equipped with a lotus, a conch, a discus, and a trident—this is the Sārgha [mudrā]. (23)
O Earth, come here assuming the form of a cow with her calf;
accept these fruits and flowers, and accept this worship performed by me.
For the sake of the sacrifice, I choose you here, the consort of the Lord and a devotee of Viṣṇu;
grant me good fortune and sons, and bestow upon me wealth and beauty. (25)
"O Goddess, accept this *arghya* from me and grant me great good fortune.
Having thus offered the eight-limbed great *arghya* and bowed down, the sacrificer then [proceeded]. (26)
The patron of the sacrifice should enter by way of the western gate;
however, the entry of the sacrificial materials is prescribed to be through the eastern gate.

The entry of the materials for the gift is indeed considered to be through the southern gate—those things intended for giving, for sacrificial fees, for consecrations, and which are most purifying. (28)
The officiant should cause [the disciple] to enter by means of the gateway of the unsurpassed accumulations;
then the preceptor should indeed place white mustard seeds in the left hand.
And having taken them mixed with parched grain (lājā), one should indeed perform the protection of the directions:
"Oṃ, I scatter the demon-slayer and the secret spell on all sides. (2.146.30)
I dig up all that is undesirable and scatter you, O Valaga;
I sprinkle the Rakshasa-slaying Valagas, the powers belonging to Vishnu.
I place grass here and pile it up on all sides;
the portion belonging to the Rākṣasas has been cast out, so there shall indeed be no harm from the Rākṣasas.
The slayer of demons, the observer of all people, has approached his dwelling;
he has settled upon the secure, well-nourished ground within the wooden vat. 33.
May the spirits who have become the ground and those in the form of obstacles not crawl from this place; may the bhūtas and piśācas depart from all directions. (34)
A spirit that obstructs the sacrificial rite is indeed present here on this ground;
let it depart from this place to another location and grant us peace. (35)
"May the pretas and other such beings depart; I take possession of this ground.
I shall perform the rite of pacification here, scattering [the materials] starting from the northeast (Īśāna) in due order. (36)
"Let the gods come here, and let the Yātudhānas and others depart! O Viṣṇu, standing between them, protect this field, the sacrificial ground of the gods. (37)
Having thus performed the protection rite with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) and sacred kuśa grass,
one should sprinkle the ground of the pavilion as well as the sacrificial materials.
Golden-hued, pure, purifying, purifiers of the world—those waters who have held Agni within their womb, may they purify us. 39.
May those waters, which belong to Varuṇa, flow with sweetness, and which are worthy of praise;
may they purify us so that whatever we have touched shall indeed become fit food for the gods. 2.146.40.
May those waters, which are the white essence arising from the atmosphere and the earth, providing nourishment for all the gods, purify us here. 41.
Behold me with a gracious eye, and let your waters touch me;
likewise, sustain me with your auspicious form, endowed as I am with strength and splendor.
May Pavamāna, accompanied by water, purify the sacrificial materials;
may the Manus, the gods, and all living beings purify them. ||43||
O Agni, through your power of the waters, we purify this sacred prayer (brahman);
may Vaiśvānara purify me with his rays, and Vāta with his breath and splendor. 44.
May Heaven and Earth with their moisture, and Savitṛ with his rays, purify me here; may they purify the ritual materials, and we purify this sacred knowledge (brahman). 45.
The deities indeed consume that which is the purifier consisting of the *pāvamānī* verses;
moreover, the ritual materials (*saṃbhāra*) are always considered by the wise to be accompanied by the *pāvamānīs* and the excellent juices.
From her, who yields the essence-filled [milk], the deities consume everything:
milk whose essence has been gathered by the seers, as well as clarified butter and the finest honey. (47)
The immortal nectar is placed within the Brahmins and is contained in those substances; the gods consume it with devotion through the purifying filter of the *pavamānī* verses.
May Indra, Soma, Varuṇa, and King Yama purify this;
we purify the Brahman-born collection of entities, the purified Brahman. 49.
And having thus consecrated him with these verses beginning with "āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ," [he says:
"Give us those waters for strength, so that we may behold great joy. (2.146.50)
Whatever most excellent and sweet essence you possess, we are the recipients of that;
water is the vessel for all of that—O Waters, produce that essence!
Having thus sprinkled all the sacrificial materials, the Brahmin sacrificer should stand with palms joined in reverence and say: "May the Aśvins grant you well-being. (52)
May Aditi grant you well-being; may Pūṣan bestow well-being upon you.
May Heaven and Earth grant you well-being, and may Aryaman likewise ordain well-being for you. (53)
May Vāyu grant you well-being; may Guru grant you well-being; may Agni grant you well-being.
May the goddesses as well as the gods always grant you well-being. (54)
May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the knower of all things, grant us well-being;
may Tārkṣya with his unbroken wheel grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us. 55.
Having thus established [the deity] within himself, he should perform the worship of the pavilion as well,
and having sat down in the presence of Vāstu, he should indeed perform the Vāstu-pūjā.
In the southwest corner of the pavilion, the sacrificer, facing east, having sat down, performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), and restrained his breaths, remained composed in mind. ||57||
Having proclaimed the place and the time, the sacrificer should perform the worship of Vāstu;
he should plant four stakes in the four corners of the Vāstu site.
Oṃ! May the Nāgas and the guardians of the world enter this ground;
may they always remain here in this pavilion, bestowing strength and long life. (59)
I offer the bali-oblation with black-gram rice and curd-rice;
may the Śaṅkus accept what has been offered at your side.
I also offer a beautiful oblation to the Rudras and the serpents;
may those who dwell in the region of Īśāna and others who depend upon it accept it. (61)
Om! To the fires and to the serpents, and to those others who depend upon them—may you accept this bali-offering in the southeastern quarter; I present this cooked rice to you. (62)
To the lord of the Nairṛta region and to those Rākṣasas who dwell in the southwest, I offer this oblation; may they accept this consecrated offering. (63)
To the lord of the Vāyavya region and to those Rākṣasas who dwell in the Vāyavya direction, I offer this oblation; may they accept this meritorious cooked rice that has been presented.
On the site-altar (vāstupīṭha), one should likewise [draw] with saffron and other substances, or with a golden stylus,
or even with a gem, silver, fruit, or flower.
Nine lines should be drawn there; [one should recite] "Oṃ, obeisance to Lakṣmī," "Obeisance to Yaśovatī," and likewise "Oṃ, obeisance to Kāntā. (66)
"Oṃ, salutation to Supriyā; salutation to Vimalā;
Oṃ, salutation to Śrī; and salutation to Subhagā—Oṃ. (67)
"Oṃ, obeisance to Sumati; Oṃ, obeisance to Iḍā; Oṃ.
Having thus established [the deities] and having drawn nine lines once again, [one should proceed]. 68.
Oṃ, salutation to Dhānyā there; likewise, Oṃ, salutation to Prāṇā;
also salutation to Viśālā, and likewise, Oṃ, salutation to Sthirā. ||69||
"Oṃ, salutation to Bhadrā; likewise, Oṃ, salutation to Jayā;
Oṃ, salutation to Niśā; and Oṃ, salutation to Virajā."
Having established [the deity] with the mantra "Vibhavāyai namaḥ," one should worship;
and in the northeast quarter, one should worship the god Īśāna, the crested Hara.
Having meditated, I invoke [the deity] here: salutations again and again to Śambhu;
salutations again and again to Bhava, to Śambhu, and to the most auspicious Śivatara. ||72||
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śikhin, come here and stay; salutations to you!
Having meditated upon Parjanya to the south of him, I invoke him. (73)
May Parjanya rain down; salutations, repeated salutations to Parjanya!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Parjanya, come here and stay! ||74||
Then, having meditated upon Jayanta on the right, I invoke him:
"O Jayanta, covered by armor and bathed in nectar! (75)
May the gods here crush you with their chest, O you who have attained strength!
Om bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Jayanta, come here and stay! ||76||
"Salutations to Jayanta; may he grant victory in every way.
Then, having meditated upon Mahendra in the south, I invoke him.
Oṃ! May Indra come; may he dwell here, praised as the hero and the increaser.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Mahendra, come here and remain! ||78||
"Salutation to Mahendra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, who radiates celestial light.
Then, having meditated upon the Sun-god in the south, I invoke him. (79)
Salutations to you, Savitṛ, whose form is Brahman, the treasury of splendor!
Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Sūrya, come here and remain here.
Then, having meditated upon Truth in the south, I invoke it:
"Through Truth initiation bears fruit; it is characterized by faith and consists of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). (81)
All that has Satyakā as its support; salutations again and again to you, O Truth!
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Satya, come here and remain! ||82||
Then, having meditated intensely upon the right [side], I invoke you with devotion:
"I have drawn you within; remain firm and immovable. (83)
May all the subjects desire you; may your kingdom not fall away. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Bhṛśa, come here, stay, and salutations to you! ||84||
Then, having meditated upon the great space in the right [hand], I invoke it;
[therein are] vowels, sounds, and resonances, as well as truthful speech and sweet honeyed words. (85)
O Great Space, you are present; salutations indeed to you, the divine!
*Au*, *bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*! O Ākāśa, come here and remain! ||86||
Then, in the southern corner, I invoke Agni;
likewise, having meditated upon Vāyu, the friend of wind, I invoke him as well.
O Agni, you who possess seven thousand tongues, salutations, salutations unto you!
O Vāyu, like one with a thousand chariots, and O Vahni-mitra, salutations to you as well. ||88||
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Agni and Vāyu, come hither and remain! Thereafter, having meditated upon Pūṣan, I invoke him as well. (89)
O Pūṣan, under your protection may we never suffer harm.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Pūṣan, come here and remain here. 2.146.90.
"O Pūṣan, salutations to you; we are your worshippers, so grant us happiness. Then, having meditated upon him as being present, I invoke him. (91)
O Vitatha, O son of Sūrya, salutations to you again and again!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vitatha, come here and stay! || 92 ||
Then, having meditated upon Gṛhakṣata in the southwest, I invoke him:
"Om! They have eaten and rejoiced; they have shaken off what was dear. (93)
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, Gṛhakṣata, salutations! Come and stay.
Then, having meditated upon Yama to the south, [I invoke him]: "Salutations to you; I invoke you. 9.4.
To Yama, who possesses the ancestors, be *svadhā*; to Dharma, to you, be homage!
*Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, O Yama, come here and stay! || 95 ||
Then, having meditated upon the Gandharva in the west, I invoke him:
"O Gandharva Viśvāvasu, may you entrust yourself to me for my prosperity. (96)
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Gandharva, salutations; come and stay!
After that, having meditated upon Bhṛṅgarāja, I invoke him. || 97 ||
Salutation to Bhṛṅgarāja and to the wise one endowed with feathers.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Bhṛṅgarāja, come here and stay! || 98 ||
Then, having meditated upon the deer, I invoke you; salutations to you!
O King of Beasts, make me free from enemies and be my companion even in times of distress. (99)
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Mṛgātra, come hither and stay!
To the south-west of that, I invoke the ancestors. || 2.146.10 ||
Salutation to the ancestors; we meditate upon all the ancestors.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O ancestors, come here, be present. || 101 ||
To the north of that, I invoke the gatekeeper Nandin;
O Nandin, who possesses great protective power, salutations to you—please protect us well.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Nandin, come here and stay here!
Having meditated upon Sugrīvaka to the north of him, I invoke him as well. 103.
Salutation to Sugrīva, to you, the host who is resorted to by Rudra.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Sugrīva, come here and remain here. 104.
Having meditated upon Puṣpadanta to the north of that [deity], I invoke him:
"Obeisance indeed to you, Puṣpadanta, the ordainer of the Sāman hymns of Śambhu. (105)
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Puṣpadanta, come here and stay! And having meditated upon Varuṇa to the north of him, I invoke him. 106.
Salutation to the Lord of Tastes, the radiant one whose abode is the sweet oblation.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Varuṇa, come here and remain here. 107.
Having meditated upon the Asura to the north of that, I invoke you; salutations!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Asura, come here and stay! 1.08.
To the north of that, I invoke Śeṣa; salutations, salutations to you!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O you named Śeṣa, come here and remain here! 1.09.
And thereafter, I meditate upon and invoke the sin:
"O Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, O Sin, salutations to you; come and remain. (2.146.11)
To the north of that, in the northwest corner, I invoke Disease:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Disease, salutations to you; come and remain. || 11 1 ||
May there be no evil diseases among living beings; I bow to both of them.
I also bow to the one named Nāga who preceded them, and to Ahirbudhnya.
"I invoke you; come, stay here—Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ!
Having meditated upon the one named Mukhya to the east of that, I invoke him. (11.3)
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Mukhya, come here and stay; salutations to you!
And to the east of that, salutations to Bhallāṭa; I invoke him. 1.14.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Bhallāṭa, come here and stay here! To the east of that, I invoke Kubera with obeisance. 1.15.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, come, O Soma, stay; salutation to you!
To the east of that, I invoke Śaila with salutation. 1.16.
To the Serpent: Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, come, stay; obeisance to you! To the East of that: obeisance to Aditi; come here and stay! 1.17
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Aditi, be the bestower of my desire;
having meditated upon Diti to the east of her, I invoke you—salutations to you! 1.18.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Diti, come here and remain here;
having meditated upon the waters at the throat of Vāstu, I indeed invoke you—salutations! (11.9)
O Waters, you are indeed the source of our life; grant us strength.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Waters, come here and remain. 2.146.120
Having meditated upon the shoulder, I invoke Āpavatsa; salutations to you!
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, Āpavatsa, come here and remain here! || 121 ||
On the right side, I bow to and invoke Aryaman:
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Aryaman, come here and stay here! || 122 ||
Then, I invoke Sāvitra upon the right hand:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Sāvitra, come hither; stay here, salutation to you. (123)
I invoke Savitṛ at Sāvitrapārśvaka;
I bow to and remember him in the vicinity of Kaphoṇikā. || 124 ||
Oṃ, O divine Savitṛ, drive away all misfortunes.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Savitṛ, come here and remain here. || 125 ||
To the south of that, I remember Vivasvat at the right thigh;
I invoke him and say: "Salutations to you, O Vivasvat, make me pure. (126)
"O couple, eat here; come, stay, and homage be unto you!
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, may we meditate upon the god Vivasvat. (127)
I invoke Indra in that [place] and in the region of the penis:
"O Vasu, become present; come hither; salutations to you; stay, O Lord of Heaven! (128)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Salutation to you, Indra, the lord of the gods;
and below that, in the region of the anus, I remember Jayanta.
I invoke: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, come and stay!
Homage to Jayanta, homage to Aṣāḍha, homage to you, Jaya!
To the north of that, on the left thigh, I invoke Mitra:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Mitra, come hither, stay, salutations to you! (13.1)
And in the left hand above that, I invoke Rājayakṣman;
salutations to you, O Yakṣman, who causes separation. (132)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Rājayakṣman, come here and stay!
At the elbow, or on the left hand, I remember Rudra. 133.
I invoke you, O Rudra; I bow to you for the sake of well-being, O Bhava.
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Rudra, come here and be present.
Then, on the eastern left side, I remember Pṛthvīdhara;
I invoke Pṛthivīdhṛk for the sake of welfare, and I bow to him. (135)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Earth-Sustainer, come and remain here;
within the womb of the site, I remember and invoke Brahmā. || 136 ||
O you whose form is Brahman, salutations to you; grant us the source of existence.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain here.
In the outer northeastern corner, I remember Carakī;
I invoke Carakī, the destroyer of bonds, and I bow to her. 1.38.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Carakī, come here and stay here! I invoke Vidārī in the outer south-eastern corner of the fire. || 139 ||
O Yoginī Vidārikā, who destroys death, I bow to you!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, Vidārikā, come here and remain! 2.146.140
In the southwest corner, I invoke and bow to Pūtanā:
O Pūtanā, destroyer of fetters, you who remove the misfortunes of Nirṛti! 141.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Pūtana, come here and stay here!
I invoke the sinful one in the northwestern corner and I bow to her. || 142 ||
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Sin, come here and stay here!
In the east, I bow to Skanda, I invoke him, and I remember him. (143)
O General, protect us from arrows; may the Destroyer of Evil grant us refuge.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Skanda, come here and remain present. || 144 ||
I bow to Aryaman as he is being invoked; I invoke him and I remember him.
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Aryaman, come hither and remain! 145.
In the west, I bow to Jṛmbhaka, I invoke him, and I remember him;
[I offer] svāhā to him who neighs, snorts, lies down, and leaps. 146.
To him who sleeps and to him who is awake, svāhā! To him who yawns and to him who utters cries—Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Jṛmbhaka, come hither and stay! 147.
In the north, I bow to Pilipiccha; I invoke her and meditate upon her.
To Pilippilākī and Piśāṅginī, svāhā! Homage be to you here.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! Pilipiccha, come hither and remain! In the east, I remember Indra; I invoke him and I bow to him. || 149 ||
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Indra, come hither and stay here!
I remember Agni within Agni; I invoke him and I bow to him. || 2.146.150 ||
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Agni, come hither and stay here.
In the southern quarter, I remember Yama, I invoke him, and I bow to him. || 151 ||
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Yama, come hither and stay here!
In the southwest, I remember Nirṛti; I invoke him and I bow to him. || 152 ||
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Nirṛti, come here and stay here!
In the west, I remember Varuṇa; I invoke him and I bow to him. || 153 ||
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Varuṇa, come here and stay here!
I remember Vāyu; I bow to him in the northwest and invoke him. || 154 ||
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vāyu, come here and stay here!
I remember, invoke, and bow to Kubera in the north. || 155 ||
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Kubera, come here and stay here!
In the northeast, I invoke the god Īśāna and I bow to him.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Īśāna, come here and stay here!
Indeed, in the middle between the northeast and the east, I remember Brahmā.
I invoke and bow to him; may the gods protect me on all sides!
O Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, O Brahmā, come here and remain here! 158.
Between Varuṇa and Nirṛti, I meditate upon and bow to Ananta;
I invoke Ananta, the Hari who provides protection against poison.
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Ananta, come here and remain here!
Having thus invoked [the deities] and having prostrated before the deities of the Vāstu-pīṭha, O Rādhikā...
Then, during the sacrifice, one should indeed perform the installation of the deity along with all its primary and secondary limbs;
may Bṛhaspati establish him, and may the Viśvedevas be established.
Thus indeed did the divine Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa speak;
that very meditation on the sacred site (vāstu) has been proclaimed by me here for you. || 162 ||

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Selection of the Preceptor, Priests, and Others; the Sprinkling of Materials; the Utterance of Auspicious Verses; the Worship of the Pavilion; and the Invocation of the Deities of the Vāstu-pīṭha," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā; the all-pervading Lord Anādi-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa spoke concerning the abode of the gods, and I shall now relate that to you.
Since the worship of the deities of the site must be performed immediately after the consecration, a new copper pitcher, which is the very soul of that [ritual], should be installed. (2)
Oṃ, smell the jar; may the Soma drops enter you, the great one.
May those with a thousand streams, full of milk, enter you; remain firm! 3.
Having thus established the water-pot (kalaśa), one should fill it with water:
"Varuṇa’s pleasant abode and the supporting water are within you. (4)
"O you who are the seat of Truth, bestow indeed the purifying water.
Having thus filled [the vessel] with water, one should wrap a cloth around the neck.
"Thou art the purifier of wealth, possessing a hundred streams and a thousand streams"—
having thus wrapped the cloth, one should place the betel nut into the jar.
Oṃ! May you be fruitful and flowering; even if you are fruitless and flowerless, may you belong to me. O Pūgī, abide in this jar and become the bestower of fruits for embodied beings.
Having thus offered a betel nut, one should present the five jewels:
gold, silver, diamond, ruby, and likewise pearl. (8)
"Agni, the lord of wandering mendicants and the seer, has accepted the oblations. Having thus spoken, one should place jewels and gold into the jar. (9)
In ancient times, the offspring of Agni was held by the god upon his head;
that gold was carried away by Hari, and I now bestow it within this vessel.
Having thus offered gold, one should place fragrance into the jar:
"I offer you saffron, kesara, and sandalwood fragrance. (1.1)
Having offered this fragrance, one should then present the medicinal herbs;
they were born of old upon the body of Hari, overflowing with essence and dripping with honey.
"I shall indeed cast those seven hundred and seven Rudhghanas as well.
Having thus offered all the medicinal herbs, one should present the seven types of earth. || 13 ||
One should offer [the clay] produced from elephant, horse, or cow pens, from anthills or crossroads, obtained from royal crossroads, or that which has grown at the root of a *tulasī* plant.
"O Earth, you who possess all forms, be the bestower of protection and a dwelling place.
Having spoken thus, he should offer the seven types of earth and then present *dūrvā* grass into the water-pot.
Growing from joint to joint, and from every stalk, O Durvā grass, may you spread for us with a hundredfold and a thousandfold increase.
Having thus placed *dūrvā* grass in the jar, one should indeed offer five types of sprouts [with the mantra]:
"O Aśvattha tree, you are our seat; on the Parṇa tree, your dwelling has been made. (17)
Indeed, he who shares in the cattle and who now possesses the man—Oṃ, salutations to the one in the jar, at the mouth of the Aśvattha and the Vaṭa tree. 18.
"I shall indeed place fresh leaves here from the mango, the udumbara, and the plakṣa tree; thus your kingdom shall be like a field of ripening grain. (19)
Oṃ! May that which is pure, known as the purifier, sanctify [this] like the rays of the sun.
O Lord of the Purifier, I offer this purifier here into the water-pot.
Oṃ, salutations to you, the purifier, born of kuśa grass, the creator;
I place you in the jar—make those waters pure. (21)
Having thus offered the purifier (pavitra), one should place upon the pitcher a new vessel filled with unbroken rice (akṣata), containing sugar and other ingredients, and made of fine gold.
O ladle, fly away full; fly back again well-filled.
Like two merchants trading wares, let us exchange food and strength, O Śatakratu! 23.
Having thus bowed to the vessel of rice, one should offer a bilva fruit [with the mantra]:
"Śrī, Lakṣmī, Ramā, Rādhā, Brahmavidyā, Satī, and Rati. (24)
Suguṇā, Mañjulā, Haṃsā, Lalitā, Kambharā, Satī, Santoṣā, Māṇikī, Durgā, Amṛtāmbā, and Śāradā—these [are the goddesses]. ||25||
"May they dwell here in this *śrīphala* (bilva fruit) and may they grant us prosperity.
Having thus established the *śrīphala*, the officiant should bow to that bestower of fortune (*śrīda*). (26)
Oṃ! May the mind-impelling Bṛhaspati enjoy the clarified butter;
may he extend this sacrifice unimpaired and establish it.
May all the gods rejoice here in this jar. Oṃ! Be established. 27.
Having thus consecrated the jar, one should then invoke Varuṇa;
for water is indeed rich in all flavors, purifying, and beneficial for the sacrifice.
I approach that reality, worshipping with a sacred prayer; the sacrificer seeks it with oblations.
O Varuṇa, be mindful here without anger; do not steal away the long life of one who praises you. 29.
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, Varuṇa, come here and stay here!
Having thus invoked Varuṇa, one should worship him with the sixteen articles.
May all the oceans, rivers, sacred fords,
and lakes come for the sake of destroying the sins of those who perform the sacrifice.
The mouth of the jar is Kṛṣṇa, the neck is remembered as Sadāśiva;
the base is Brahmā himself to be understood, and the belly is remembered as the Mothers. (32)
The oceans are his bellies, the earth is the form of the pitcher,
and the Vedas along with their auxiliary limbs are the very components of the pitcher.
I invoke the sacred fords (tīrthas); come hither and remain!
Born at the churning for the nectar of immortality, this jar was held in the hand of Viṣṇu. (34)
You are the dwelling place for the holy fords, living beings, and the gods; you are the bestower of fruits.
The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvedevas, along with the Pitṛs, [reside within you].
"May the Aśvins abide in you; be present for the sake of the sacrifice.
Having thus prayed to the water-pot, one should [place] a golden [image] upon it. (36)
One should place there the image of Vāstu in the form of a lizard;
one should perform the rite of fire-transference and cover it with cloths and fabrics.
Then, having proclaimed the place and time for the rite of raising the fire, one should meditate upon the person as lying supine upon the site, with his head toward the northeast. 38.

And for the very purpose of avoiding defects such as those arising from threshing and so forth, one should perform the rite of transferring the fire (agnyuttāraṇa) and the consecration of life-force (prāṇapratiṣṭhā). ||39||
Having placed the image in the vessel, one should cause a stream of milk to flow;
then one should offer a stream of water and recite the hymn again and again.
Oṃ! With the reed-grass of the ocean, O Agni, we encircle you;
as the purifier who delivers us from all [sins], be auspicious to us. 41.
Oṃ! We envelop you with the membrane of the snow, O Agni;
as the purifier who delivers us from all [sins], be auspicious to us. 42.
This is the path leading to the ocean, the dwelling place of the waters;
may those missiles of yours, as well as others in the form of obstacles, consume us. 43.
O Purifier, who delivers all the gods, be auspicious to us!
Homage to you for your heat and your flame; homage be to you for your radiance! 44.
May those missiles of yours burn up the forms of obstacles as well as others;
O Purifier, who delivers all the gods, be auspicious unto us. (45)
O you who bestow life-breath, inhalation, exhalation, vigor, and the highest excellence—may your weapons burn up those who take the form of obstacles and others as well. 46.
"O Purifier, who delivers all the gods, be auspicious unto us!
Having thus performed the rite of crossing over the fire, [one should sprinkle] with the five nectars.
Having bathed the Vāstupuruṣa, one should place him upon the water-pot (kalaśa);
one should meditate upon the nature of Vāstu as having originated in the past from the Supreme Brahman. 48.
Then, from the body of Śambhu, there was born a great and powerful son;
he was this very one who obstructed the sacrifice and was defeated by the gods in battle.
Having been cast down face-down and bound on all sides by hosts of deities,
his head was placed toward the northeast and the pair of his feet toward the southwest.
Having placed the knees and the pair of arms in that same manner,
one should then place the knee toward the northwest and the southeast, and likewise join the palms at the heart.
Having placed him at the top, all the gods and the Rohitas [should do so];
I invoke that Vāstuka who is the abode of all happiness.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! I invoke Vāstunara and I bow to him;
I honor him—come, O you of great strength and prowess! (53)
O son of Brahmā, whose body is the refuge of all the gods, homage be to you!
You are the sustainer of the entire cosmic egg; come here, O Blessed One! (54)
Come, O Lord Vāstu, accompanied by all the gods;
stay here, bestow auspiciousness, and be present at this sacrifice. (55)
Oṃ, O Lord of the Dwelling, acknowledge us; be a gracious refuge and free from disease for us.
Whatever we entreat of you, grant that to us; be auspicious to our bipeds and our quadrupeds. (56)
Having thus invoked [the deity] and worshipped with unbroken rice, flowers, sandalwood, garments, and ornaments, one should pray for protection: "Protect me from calamity and distress. (57)
One should offer the food offering (naivedya), incense, lamps, the waving of lights (nīrājana), and so forth;
then, having uttered "svāhā," the physician should worship according to the prescribed rite.
Oṃ, salutation to Śikhin, the Lord Īśāna: water for the feet, as well as the arghya offering, water for sipping, bathing water, clothing, fragrance, and likewise unbroken grains (akṣata).
I offer flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, water, fruit, betel leaf, a bed, and a sacrificial fee; please accept them for my peace.
Salutations to Parjanya; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant prosperity.
Salutations to Jayanta; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant prosperity. ||6 1||
Oṃ, salutations to Indra; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness.
Oṃ, salutations to Sūrya; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness. (62)

Oṃ, obeisance to Satya; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness. Oṃ, obeisance to Bhṛśa; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness. (63)
Oṃ, homage to Ākāśa; and Oṃ, repeated homage to Vāyu.
Oṃ, homage to Pūṣan; and Oṃ, repeated homage to Vitatha as well. ||64||
Salutation to Gṛhakṣata; Oṃ Oṃ, salutation, salutation to Yama;
Oṃ, salutation to Gandharva and to Bhṛṅgarāja, Oṃ, salutation. ||65||
Oṃ, salutations to the deer; Oṃ, and salutations again and again to the ancestors.
May they accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and may they grant well-being; salutations, salutations.
Oṃ, obeisance to Nandin; Oṃ, repeated obeisance to Sugrīva.
Oṃ, obeisance to Puṣpadanta and to Varuṇa; Oṃ, obeisance! (67)
Salutations to Omasura and salutations again and again to Śeṣa;
salutations to Pāpa, to Roga, and salutations to the one named Oṃ-Ahi. ||68||
Oṃ, salutation to Mukhya; Oṃ, salutation to Bhallāṭa.
Oṃ, salutation to Soma, to Nāga, to Aditi, and to Diti. ||69||
Salutations to those who are full and to those who are empty; salutations, salutations!
May they accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and may they bestow peace; salutations, salutations!
Om, salutation to Uṣarbudh; Om, salutation to Sāvitra and salutation to Om.
Om, salutation to Savitṛ, to Vivasvat, and to Indra—Om, salutation! ||7.1||
Oṃ, obeisance to Jayanta; Oṃ, obeisance to Mitra; Oṃ, obeisance!
Obeisance to Rājayakṣman; Oṃ Oṃ, obeisance, obeisance to Rudra. ||72||
Oṃ, obeisance to Pṛthivīdhara; Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā.
May they accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and may they grant well-being; obeisance, obeisance. ||73||
Oṃ, obeisance to Carakī; Oṃ, and obeisance to Vidārī; Oṃ. Obeisance to Pūtanā; Oṃ, and obeisance to Pāpā; Oṃ. ||74||
Oṃ, homage to Skanda; homage to Aryaman; Oṃ, homage to Jṛmbhaka. Oṃ, homage to Pilipiccha; and Oṃ, homage to Indra. ||75||
Oṃ, salutation to Agni; Oṃ, salutation to Yama; salutation, Oṃ, to Nirṛti; and salutation, Oṃ, to Varuṇa; salutation, Oṃ, to Vāyu. ||76||
Oṃ, salutation to Kubera; Oṃ, salutation to Īśāna;
Oṃ, salutation! Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā, and salutation again and again to Ananta. ||77||
May they accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant peace; salutations, salutations!
And may you, Aṅgadeva and the others, accept the perfumes and unbroken grains of rice. (78)

Thus did Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa speak to the abode of the gods;

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Installation of the Vessel, the Installation and Worship of Vāstu, the Worship of the Vāstu Deities, the Offering of Food, the Balis, the Encircling of the Pavilion with the Triple Thread, and the Mantras," in the second section on the Tretā Age of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.

come here and enter into the fourteenth pillar.
Oṃ! We, maintaining our minds within our bodies under your lunar vow, O Soma, may we be endowed with progeny;
may we be possessed of splendor.
Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Giver of Wealth, come here and remain here. 111.
Accept this offering produced from the sixteen substances; homage to you!
[I bow] to the preceptor Bṛhaspati, who resides upon the pillar situated in the intermediate space between Vāyu and the North. || 112 ||
I invoke, I establish, I bow to the treasure-house of speech.
O Bṛhaspati, come hither; enter the fifteenth pillar.
Om! O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the enemy, which is worthy, radiant, and possessed of wisdom, shines among the people.
O you who have shone forth by your own power, born of the Eternal Law (Ṛta), bestow upon us that wonderful wealth.
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Bṛhaspati, come here and remain;
accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles, and salutations to you. 11.4–5.
In the pillar situated between the north and the northeast, I invoke, establish, and bow down to Viśvakarman of great splendor. || 116 ||
O Viśvakarman, white, rich in artistic skill, omniscient, and eternal—come here; enter into this sixteen-pillared pillar.
Oṃ, O Viśvakarman, through the increasing oblation, you made Indra the protector and strengthened him.
To him the ancient subjects bowed down, so that he might be formidable and worthy of invocation.
O Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ, Viśvakarman, come here and stay;
accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles, and salutations to you! || 118-119 ||
"O Rādhikā, one should thus worship these sixteen pillars of the earth;
whatever the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa has said, that has been declared by me here.

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Invocation and Worship of the Deities of the Sixteen Pillars in the Pavilion of the Sixty-four Yoginīs and Fifty Kṣetrapālas," within the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā; afterwards I shall tell you what the Blessed Puruṣottama spoke to the devotee Devāyatana. 1.
One should worship the sacrificial wood with the mantra: *Oṃ nāgamātre namaḥ*.
One should offer sandalwood, flowers, incense, a lamp, and food offerings (*naivedya*).
With the mantra *Oṃ sarvebhyo namaḥ*, one should worship the binding of the branches.
One should offer sandalwood paste, flowers, incense, a lamp, and food offerings.
Having exited through the western door, one should worship the archway of the eastern door, auspiciously located outside the pavilion at a distance of one cubit to the east. 3–4.
One should worship the Aśvattha archway, known as Sudṛḍha, which is vermilion in color,
joined with Mount Mahendra, and marked with conch shells.
Oṃ, protect this sacrifice and guard it well, O Aśvattha archway!
Warding off all obstacles, I bow to you who stand firm here. 6.
Oṃ, I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the divine ministrant of the sacrifice, the invoker, the bestower of jewels; protect the purpose of the pavilion. 7.
Oṃ, salutations to the one presided over by the Ṛgveda and to the firm archway;
salutations to you, O firm archway, I invoke you, salutations!
[8] Fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, and water.
"Accept the betel and the sacrificial fee; salutations to you, O Torana!
Om, salutations again and again to the Kṛta Yuga who dwells here;
I invoke the Kṛta Yuga into the archway—salutations to you! (2.149.10)
Accept the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, water, betel leaf, and the priestly fee; O Satyayuga, salutations to you! 11.
Right there, salutations to Rāhu; I invoke Rāhuka.
O Lord Rāhu, accept the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, water, betel leaf, and the priestly fee; salutations to you.
Salutations to Bṛhaspati; I invoke Bṛhaspati.
O Bṛhaspati, accept this perfume, flower, incense, lamp, food offering, fruit, water, betel leaf, and sacrificial fee; salutations to you.
There, holding one water-pot and touching the ground, one should recite the mantra:
"Oṃ! May Heaven and Earth sprinkle this sacrifice for us. || 15 ||
"Fill us with provisions; make us prosperous with juices and other essentials.
In that regard, medicinal herbs should be sown, and barley should be sown, scattered by hand. (16)
Oṃ! The plants hold consultation together with Soma, their king:
"O King, we shall bring to safety that man for whom a Brāhmaṇa performs [this rite]. 17.
Then, having placed the *kalaśa* upon the ground, one should recite the mantra:
"Oṃ, smell the *kalaśa*; may the drops enter you through the earth.
Return again with vigor; grant us a thousandfold milk. (18)
May wealth, flowing in broad streams and rich in milk, enter me again. || 19 ||
Having filled the jar with water and remembered the sacred ford (tīrtha), one should recite the mantra:
"Oṃ, you are the support of Varuṇa; you are the pillars that sustain Varuṇa. (2.149.20)
You are the seat of Varuṇa’s Truth; you are the dwelling-place of Varuṇa’s Truth. Sit upon the seat of Varuṇa’s Truth; become the Truth of all sacred fords. || 21 ||
Then one should cast perfume into the jar and into the waters of the sacred fords, reciting:
"Oṃ, [I worship] her who has the door of fragrance, who is invincible, eternally nourishing, and bestowing prosperity. (22)
I invoke here Śrī, the sovereign lady of all beings.
Then, reciting the mantras of those [plants], one should scatter all the herbs there:
"Oṃ! Those herbs which went forth for the gods in the three ages of old..."
The greatness of the tawny ones is a hundred and seven abodes.
Then, reciting the mantra of the dūrvā grass, one should scatter dūrvā blades there:
"Oṃ, from joint to joint it grows, from node to node it rises. (RV 10.97.16)
"O Durvā grass, spread out for us with a thousand and a hundred [shoots].
Then, reciting that mantra, he should cast five sprouts there.
Oṃ! The holy fig tree is your seat, the leaf is your dwelling made for you.
You shall indeed be sharers of cattle when you win back the man. 27.
Then, reciting the mantra for them, he should offer seven types of clay:
"Oṃ, may the earth be pleasant to us, thornless, and a peaceful dwelling. (28)
"Grant us that protection which is far-reaching and bestows nourishment here on earth.
Then, while reciting its mantra, one should offer a betel nut. (29)
Oṃ! Those plants which bear fruit, those which are unfruitful, those which are without flowers, and those which are flowering—impelled by Bṛhaspati, may they release us from sin. 2.149.30.
Then, reciting their respective mantras, he should place exactly five jewels:
"Oṃ, Agni, the lord of spoils and the sage, has stepped forth toward the oblations. (31)
Bestowing jewels upon the donor, bring all kinds of gems;
then, reciting the hymn to Hiraṇyagarbha, one should cast gold [into the fire].
Oṃ. In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists.
He supported this earth and this heaven. To which god shall we offer worship with our oblation? 33.
Then, reciting the Yuvāsu mantra, he should wrap [the image] in clothing:
"Grant me radiant and beautiful garments; wear these golden ones. (34)
Oṃ! The youth, well-robed and girt with the sacrificial cord, has come; he becomes even more excellent as he is born.
The wise sages lead him forward.
Wise, seeking the gods with their minds. 3.5.
Then, having placed a vessel filled with grain and other offerings upon his head: Oṃ, O full ladle, fly away; well-filled, fly back again! (36)
"O Śatakratu, let us sell food and vigor as if for a price"—with this mantra, having consecrated [the vessel], one should invoke Dhruva into the pitcher. || 37 ||
I invoke Dhruva and establish him; salutations to you!
I offer you fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings. || 38 ||
"I worship here at this sacrifice; may you be firm, even more firmly established.
Then, having gone to the south, [he worships] the Audumbara archway.
I invoke and worship the smoke-colored archway named Vikaṭa, which bears the mark of a wheel and is joined with the mountain called Vindhya.
Come, O Vikaṭa archway; protect and thoroughly guard this sacrifice!
Ward off obstacles from here and bestow the prosperity of the essences. 4.1.
Oṃ! For sap, thee; for strength, thee. You are the winds. May the divine Savitṛ impel you toward the most excellent work.
Swell, O inviolable ones, as a portion for Indra—prolific, free from disease, and free from affliction. 42.
Let not the thief nor the malevolent one have power over them; may you remain firm here for this master of cattle. Protect the many livestock of the sacrificer;
protect the cows, the buffaloes, the elephants, the horses, the gayals, and the bulls. 43.
Oṃ, salutations to you who are presided over by the Yajurveda and possess a formidable archway;
I invoke you, I establish you, and salutations to you!
[I offer] perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, and water.
Accept this betel and the sacrificial fee; O Vikaṭatoraṇa, salutations to you! ||45||
Oṃ, salutations again and again to the one who abides in the Dvāpara age and to the Tretā Yuga;
I invoke the Tretā Yuga at the archway, and salutations to you. ||46||
Accept the fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, water, betel leaf, and the sacrificial fee; salutations to you, the Tretā Yuga. ||47||
In that very place, I invoke Sūryaka with "Obeisance to Sūrya," and I summon Aṅgāraka with "Obeisance to Aṅgāraka. ||48||
Accept the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, water, betel, and the priestly fee; salutations again and again to you both! ||49||
There, a single water-pot should be placed according to the previously mentioned rites;
it is to be worshipped there, and I invoke the Earth—salutations to you!
Accepting the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruits, water, betel, and the priestly fee (dakṣiṇā), O Earth, become the bearer of prosperity.
Then, having sipped water and gone to the west, he reached the Plakṣa archway named Subhīma,
which was golden in appearance and adorned with Mount Gandhamādana.
Having placed the mace-marked [archway] and reciting its mantra, one should worship it:
"Come, come, O most formidable archway! Protect the sacrifice and guard it well!
Ward off all obstacles and summon all the flavors! || 5.3 ||
Oṃ! O Agni, come for the feast, being praised for the giving of the oblation. ||54||
Sit as the Hotṛ priest upon the sacrificial grass and bestow the bliss of the Sāman upon us;
Oṃ, to you who are presided over by the Sāmaveda and who possess a most formidable archway! 55.
Homage! I invoke you; homage and homage to you!
Therefore, I invoke the Dvāpara Yuga here; let there be homage.
Accept the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, water, betel leaf, and the priestly fee; salutations to you, Dvāpara.
There, "Salutation to Śukra; I invoke Śukra," and there, "Salutation to Budha; I invoke Budha.
[I offer] perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, and water.
Accept this betel and the sacrificial fee; salutations, salutations to you both! ||59||
There, one water-pot should be placed according to the previously mentioned rites;
there he is to be worshipped, and I invoke Vākpati—homage to you!
O Lord of Speech, accept this perfume, flower, incense, lamp, food offering, fruit, water, betel leaf, and sacrificial fee; be the bestower of eloquence.
Then, having sipped water and gone to the north, he reached the auspicious Vaṭātma-gate,
known as Suprabha, which was white in color and adorned with the Himālaya mountain.
Having placed the lotus-marked [archway], one should worship it while reciting its mantra:
"Come, come, O beautiful radiant archway; protect the sacrifice and guard it well! (63)
Ward off all obstacles; bring together all splendors.
Oṃ, may the divine waters be for our well-being and for our pleasure. 64.
May auspiciousness flow toward us; may our splendors increase.
Obeisance to you, the gateway of the beautiful dawn, presided over by the Atharvaveda. 65.
I invoke you; salutations to you, and repeated salutations to that [Lord].
And here I invoke the Kali Age; let there be salutation to it as well.
Accepting incense, flowers, incense-sticks, lamps, food offerings, fruit, water, betel-leaf, and the priestly fee—homage to you, the Kali Age! (67)
There, "Salutation to Soma," and I invoke Soma;
and there, "Salutation to Ketu," and I invoke Ketu. [68] "Salutation to Śanaiścara," and I invoke Śani.

"Accept the fragrance, the flower, the incense, the lamp, the food offering, the fruit, the water, the betel leaf, and the priestly fee; salutations again and again to these! There, one water-pot should be placed according to the previously mentioned rites. (2.149.70)
He is to be worshipped there; I invoke Vighneśa and offer salutations to you.
Accept the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, water, betel leaf, and the priestly fee (dakṣiṇā). O Vighneśa, be the bestower of success!
Then, having gone to the east while reciting "mahī dyauḥ," he should place two water-pots upon each of the door-posts;
those mantras, which are proclaimed for the pots of each respective direction, are to be repeated.
At the eastern gate, upon both pitchers, I invoke the world-elephant named Airāvata; salutations to you, O Airāvata!
I offer worship, beginning with perfumes and ending with betel.
A very beautiful ghee lamp should be placed upon the water-pot (kalaśa).
There, two officiating priests (ṛtvij) presiding over Brahmā as the deity should be requested according to the Ṛgveda ritual:
"The Ṛgveda has lotus-leaf eyes, is associated with the Gāyatrī meter, and has Soma as its presiding deity."
"O best of Brahmins, you belong to the Atri lineage; please become my officiating priest (*ṛtvij*).
Om! I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the divine minister of the sacrifice, the invoker, and the greatest bestower of jewels. And I worship him with perfumes and other offerings. (77)
One should recite the Śrīsūkta, the Pāvamāna, the auspicious Somasūkta,
the Puruṣasūkta, the Rudrasūkta, and the Vāmadevya hymn;
[and one should meditate on Viṣṇu] as the thousand-eyed one, seated upon an elephant, wearing a yellow crown and earrings.
One should meditate upon Mahendra, who holds a vajra and an utpala lotus in his right and left hands;
having been praised with the words "Come, O you who are extolled by the immortals! Protect the sacrifice! Salutations to you! [one should say]:
"O Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! Indra, come here and stay!"
I invoke and worship Indra, together with his limbs, his retinue, his weapons, and likewise his powers, at the door-pitcher;
and one should hoist two yellow-colored banners and two standards. ||81-82||
Oṃ, Indra the protector, Indra the savior, the hero Indra who is easily invoked in every call—I invoke Śakra, Indra who is invoked by many; may the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us.
(83) Homage to Dhātṛ on the southern branch and to Vidhātṛ on the northern.
Salutation to Dvāraśrī above, and salutation to Gaṇādhipati.
Above that, salutation to Vāstupuruṣa of radiant splendor;
salutation to Dehalī below, and repeated salutations to Kṣamāśakti.
Salutations indeed to Gaṇeśa on the left pillar and to Skanda on the right;
and salutations again and again to Gaṅgā and Yamunā at the two water-jars.
To Indra and the other gods, and to Surabhi, [I offer] fragrance, flowers, water, and fruit.
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and a sacrificial fee.
To you, Indra, together with your limbs [retinue], with your attendants, with your weapons, and with your power, I offer this oblation of black gram; salutations to you! (88)
Having thus offered the bali-oblation and sipped water (ācamana), he should then go toward the south-eastern direction and,
as before, place the vessel containing all the deities.
And there, I invoke him by the name Puṇḍarīka;
then, with the words "Salutation to Amṛta," I indeed invoke Amṛta.
Having worshipped him thoroughly with perfumes and other offerings, a lamp should be presented.
And then [he saw] the Fire-god, red in color, with that [Fire-god] as his tongue, seated upon the back of a goat. 91.
The sacrificer should meditate upon and invoke [the deity] holding a spear in the right hand, a water-pot in the left, and wearing a topknot on the head and a sacred thread.
Oṃ! Come, come, O bearer of the oblations for all the immortals, you who are honored on all sides by the most eminent sages;
together with the radiant host of worlds, protect my sacrifice, O Sage—salutations to you! (93)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Agni, come here and stay here;
come together into this water-pot and remain; indeed, I invoke you. || 94 ||
Oṃ! O Agni, worthy of praise, protect our wealthy patrons and our own bodies with your divine guardians;
you are the protector of our children and grandchildren and of our cattle, guarding them even for the blink of an eye within your sacred law. 95.
Having thus worshipped with perfumes and other offerings ending with the food oblation, [one recites]:
"Oṃ, I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I invoke the bearer of the sacrificial offering. (96)
Having said, "May you cause the gods to sit here," one should likewise hoist a red banner and a red flag,
and then offer prayers for prosperity.

The person [of fire] is red, composed of all the gods, and imperishable; he has smoke as his banner, is the presiding lord of the quality of passion (rajas), and therefore I seek forgiveness from him. 98.
I offer an oblation of black-gram and rice to Agni, together with his limbs, accompanied by his retinue and weapons, and endowed with his power.
Having thus offered the bali-oblation, one should sip water (ācamana) and give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā);
there, having placed two water-pots (kalaśa) at each door-jamb.
Then, one should likewise invoke the world-elephant named Vāmana at that very spot;
one should worship the excellent lamp, offer oblations, and likewise prostrate.
One should indeed choose two door-keepers who recite the Yajurveda while chanting the *manu*;
the Yajurveda has timid eyes, is in the *traiṣṭubha* meter, and has Viṣṇu as its presiding deity. (102)
"O best of Brahmins, you are a descendant of Kāśyapa; please become my officiating priest (ṛtvij) at this sacrifice.
Having thus chosen him, he should worship each one individually with perfumes and other offerings.
One should recite the *Ā no bhadrā* hymn, the *Anuvāka*, as well as the *Āśuḥ śiśānaka*;
then one should recite "Yad devā" three times, and thereafter the eight verses beginning with "Punantu māṃ. (104)

Having meditated upon Yama, who is seated upon a buffalo, holding a staff and a noose in his right and left hands respectively, who is dark-complexioned and has three eyes like fire, one should utter the mantra beginning with "Namaḥ. (1.05)
Come, come, O Vaivasvata, King of Dharma, embodiment of the Law worshipped by all the immortals!
Lord of auspiciousness, inauspiciousness, joy, and sorrow, protect our sacrifice for our welfare; homage to you!
(106) Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! Yama, come here and stay!
Then, having invoked Yama along with his limbs (attendants) and his family into the water-pot:
Oṃ, svāhā to you, Yama, who possess speech and the ancestors!
Svāhā to the Gharma, svāhā to the Gharma, and obeisance to Yama, the father! (107–108)
Having worshipped him with perfumes and other offerings, the performer of the sacrifice should hoist a black banner and a flag while reciting the mantra: "Obeisance indeed to Yama!
Om! The bull has come hither; he has stepped forth and sat before his mother. (109)
And having offered [the oblation] to his father and to the heavenly realm, the sacrificer should then pray:
"O Vaivasvata, O Great God, salutations to you, the witness of dharma!
O God, protected by the command of Śiva, guard this direction here."
Salutations indeed to Balā and Sabalā at the two door-posts;
salutations to Śrī above, and salutations, salutations to Gaṇapati.
Salutations below to the Dehalī, and salutations, salutations to Vāstupuruṣa.
To Puṣpadanta and Kapardin at the two pillars, salutations again and again.
To Godāvarī and Kṛṣṇā at the two jars, let there be salutations.
To Yama together with his family, I offer this bali-offering of black-gram and boiled rice.
Having sipped water (ācamana), one should then proceed to the southwest and place a water-pot there, saying:
"I invoke Kumuda and Durjaya; salutations, salutations to you both!
Having offered a lamp, [one should visualize] Nairṛti, who stands upon a man, is blue in color, and holds a sword.
Having meditated upon him as being joined by the Rakṣas and adorned with yellow ornaments, one should invoke him:
"O Rakṣas, accompanied by Piśācas and Vetālas, come indeed to protect this sacrifice!
Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, O Nirṛti, come here and remain! || 116-117 ||
"Oṃ! Seek out the one who does not press the soma and does not sacrifice, the thief, the path of the robber;
seek another than us for your pursuit. O divine Nirṛti, let there be homage to you!
(118). Having thus bowed and worshipped Nairṛta in the pitcher, [he should proceed].
Oṃ! May Nirṛti, the evil-minded one, strike down those who are near and far.
May she be struck by thirst; let her raise up blue banners and standards. Standing upon a corpse, protect the sacrifice and likewise guard it from the Rākṣasas.
Having bowed and offered a bali of black gram and rice to Nirṛti along with his limbs and retinue,
one should then go to the west and place two jars on each branch as before.
Thereafter, I invoke the world-elephant named Añjana;
then I worship the two door-keepers who are masters of the Sāmaveda.
Sāmaveda is tawny-eyed, ever-watchful, and has Śakra as his presiding deity.
"O best of Brahmins, Bhāradvāja, you must become my officiating priest (*ṛtvij*) at this sacrifice.
Having thus chosen him, [the king recited]: "Om! Agni, being praised, come for the feast, for the giving of the oblation. (1.24)

Then, having worshipped with perfumes and other offerings while reciting, "Sit down as the Hotṛ-priest upon the sacrificial grass," two [priests] should chant the Sāman for Indra with beautiful singing. || 1.25 ||
"I am the first-born; may I spread the bridge with the most pleasant oblation.
Those who sing the Gāyatrī verses shall sing [this]; let there be the recitation of the gatekeepers. 1.26.

Having meditated upon the white Varuṇa, seated upon a sea-monster (makara) and holding a noose in his hand, [one should recite]: "Come! O you who are surrounded by aquatic creatures, Apsaras, clouds, and Vidyādharas; protect me! Homage to you! (1.27).
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Varuṇa, come here and remain here! I invoke you with all your limbs into these two jars; I bow to you. || 1.28 ||
I approach the truths, worshipping with a prayer; the sacrificer desires this through his oblations.
O Varuṇa, be mindful here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not steal away our life. 1.29.129.
Salutations to Varuṇa; I worship him with fragrant substances.
"O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation today and be gracious unto me. (2.149.130)
Seeking protection, he should invoke you; he should raise up white banners and flags, and having bowed to Varuṇa, he should place Jaya and Vijaya upon the two door-posts.
I bow to Śrī and Gaṇapati above, and likewise to Dehalī below;
I also bow to Vāstupuṃsa at the two pillars, and to Nandin and Candra.
I bow to Revā and Narmadā in the two water-pots;
I worship Varuṇa along with his family, offering a bali-oblation of two black gram beans.
Having gone there, I then offer [the oblation] and take up the water-pot from the northwest;
I invoke and bow down to Puṣpadanta and Siddhārtha.
I worship the lamp and offer it; I meditate upon the Wind-god, seated upon a deer, smoke-colored, clad in variegated garments, and flickering.
Then, [one should worship] the bearer of the excellent banner with the right and left hands:
"Come for the protection of the sacrifice; accept this worship; salutations to you. (1.36)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vāyu, come here and remain here!
I bow to the friend of Agni; reciting the mantra, I worship you. (137)
Oṃ! Come to our sacrifice with your teams of horses, by the hundreds and by the thousands;
O Vāyu, rejoice at this libation.
May you always protect us with blessings. || 138 ||
Oṃ Vāyu! With those thousand chariots of yours, come hither, drawn by your teams of horses, for the drinking of Soma; one should raise aloft the smoke-bannered standard. 1.39.
I bow to Vāyu together with his limbs; I offer a bali-oblation of two black gram beans.
Having gone to the northern branch, I place two water-pots there.
There, I invoke you by the names Sārvabhauma and Diggaja; salutations to you!
And I offer a lamp to the two door-keepers who are masters of the Atharvaveda. 141.
The Atharvaveda has Bṛhannetra as its seer, the Anuṣṭubh as its meter, and Rudra as its deity;
O best of brahmins, descendant of Vaṃśa, be you my officiating priest at this sacrifice.
Having recited "śanno devīr abhiṣṭaye" [and] "āpo bhavantu pītaye," [and] "śaṃyor abhisravantu naḥ," I worship with perfumes and other offerings.
Likewise, [I worship] the Atharvāngirasas and the Atharvaśiras.
By reciting "The Chapter on Peace" and so forth, there shall be victory over the gatekeepers. || 1.44 ||
I meditate upon and worship Kubera, who has a greenish hue, is adorned with ornaments, holds a garment and a mace in his two hands, and is seated upon a human vehicle.
Come, perform our protection along with the constellations, the medicinal herbs, and the ancestors.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Kubera, come here and stay! 1.46.
Oṃ vayarṭha! O Moon, while bearing your vow within our bodies, may we, possessing progeny, abide together; I bow to you and I worship you.
(147) Oṃ! May you swell; let virility come to you from every side, O Soma.
One should raise two green banners and flags at the gathering of the prize.
To Kubera and Soma, I bow at the two door-posts;
to Pracaṇḍa and Caṇḍa, and to the Goddess of the Door, I bow.
Salutations to Gaṇeśa, and salutations again and again to the threshold below;
salutations to Vāstupuruṣa at the two pillars, and to Mahākāla accompanied by Bhṛṅgin;
salutations to Vāruṇī and Veṇī at the two water-jars, and salutations again and again.
Salutation to the illustrious Kalaśa; Oṃ, salutation to the gods residing therein.
(151) I offer a bali-oblation of two māsas to Kubera, who has the form of Soma, together with his limbs; I depart toward the northeast and I install the Kalaśa. (152)
And there, I offer salutation and worship to Supratīka Maṅgala;
I present a lamp to the one who rides upon a bull and holds a trident,
the radiant three-eyed deity who bears [the trident] in his right and left hands.
I meditate upon the Lord Īśāna, I invoke him, and I bow to him.
Come for the sake of the success of the sacrifice; accept this worship, salutations be unto you!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Īśāna, come here and be seated! 154–155.
Oṃ! We invoke for protection that Īśāna, the Lord of all that moves and stands, who quickens our intellect;
may Pūṣan, as the guardian of our wealth, be our undeceivable protector for our well-being and increase. 156.
Having thus worshipped and bowed to the three-eyed wielder of the trident,
one should raise five-colored banners and flags with the mantra "O Īśāna.
One should offer this oblation of two black gram beans along with its limbs to the body of Īśāna.
Having placed a water-pot directed upwards in the space between the northeast and the east,
one should worship Brahmā there with fragrant substances;
he is depicted holding a rosary and a handful of kuśa grass in his right hands.
Holding a sacrificial ladle and a water-pot in his left hands, four-faced,
bearded, and with matted hair, I meditate upon and worship the goat.
O Father of all, come to this sacrifice and grant us auspiciousness in the rite!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain here. || 161 ||
Oṃ. Brahma, through his wisdom, first revealed from the front the shining, wide-extending light; he, the Seer, disclosed its highest and most excellent stations.
The source of the existent and the separator of the non-existent. || 162 ||
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, and raise red banners and flags;
having bowed to him, I offer an oblation of black-gram and rice to Brahmā.
Then, having placed the jar in the space between Nirṛti and Varuṇa,
one should visualize there [Viṣṇu] seated upon the bed of Ananta, adorned with hoods.
Having meditated upon the blue Anantaka, whose two right hands hold a lotus and a conch, one above and one below, one should then invoke him with the word "Ehi" (Come!).
O Lord who supports the earth, protect our sacrifice with your feet that are worshipped by the Nāgas!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Ananta, come here and remain here! 166.
I invoke [the deity], together with his limbs, his retinue, and his powers.
Om! The radiant bull has stepped forward; he has settled before his mother. (RV 1.164.1)
And one should say, "Homage, homage to the beloved father, to the heavenly one, to the infinite.
With the mantra "Āyaṃ gauḥ," one should raise two smoke-colored banners and flags.
And one should offer a bali-oblation of two māsas to Ananta along with his retinue;
thereafter, in the center of the pavilion, [there should be] a seat provided with chowries and small bells.
The staff shall be sixteen cubits long, or even ten cubits;
it should be provided with a five-colored banner hanging down three cubits.
He should be held aloft with the mantra "O Indra, of the bull," and thereafter he should worship Brahmā with the mantra "Brahma jajñānam. || 171 ||
Having meditated again and again upon the deities stationed on the sixteen pillars,
one should offer salutations to the Kinnaras in the rafters and to the Pannagas on the roof-ridge.
Having worshipped them and having smeared the ground in the eastern direction, the sacrificer,
sitting outside the pavilion upon this [ground], should speak.
May the fourteen classes of beings, both insentient and sentient,
pervaded by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Hara, protect our sacrifice.
The Siddhas, the Ṛṣis, the Pitṛs, the Devas, the Asuras and Rākṣasas, the Dānavas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, and so forth. || 175 ||
May humans, beasts, birds, and species of trees,
as well as those with subtle bodies and the hosts of serpents, likewise protect our sacrifice.

May all the gods, the male lords and the female goddesses, the protectors of the earth, the guardians of the fields, and the guardians of the worlds—may they all protect the sacrificial rite and the pavilion. (177)
May they destroy the obstacles, misfortunes, and adversaries in this sacrifice;
I invoke and worship both the stationary and the moving [deities]. || 178 ||
I bow to and ever remember Brahmā; salutations to Viṣṇu! Salutations again and again to the gods, the dānavas, and the gandharvas. || 179 ||
Salutations again and again to the Siddhas, the Ṛṣis, and the Pitṛs; salutations again and again to the Āsurīs, the Rākṣasas, the Yakṣas, and the Bhūtas.
Salutations again and again to the Piśācas, to human beings, and even to the beasts and birds; salutations to the trees, to those with subtle bodies, and to the serpents. || 181 ||
Salutations again and again to the Īśas and the Īśvarīs, to the lords of the earth; salutations to the Kṣetrapas and the Lokapas, and to all that is moving and unmoving.
I invoke those Mothers who are the wives of Brahmā;
I worship them, I remember them, and I offer them their appropriate vessel. 183.

Having thus performed the worship with an offering of black gram (māṣa), milk-rice (pāyasa) and the like, as well as fruits, nectar, and so forth, one should indeed say: "Salutations, salutations to all! (184).
The sacrificer, the preceptor, and the officiating priests, having washed their feet and hands and performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana),
should enter the pavilion by the eastern gate.

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Worship with the Sixteen Services (Ṣoḍaśopacāra) of the Arches, Vases, Door-frames, Thresholds, and Their Deities," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā; I shall tell you what must be done hereafter.
I, the beginningless Śrī Hari, declare all of that to you, my devotee. (1)
Then the pure patron and the twice-born priest, seated facing north near the southern gate in its western portion, [should remain there]. (2)
"Perform the rites of the sacrifice with devotion, exactly as prescribed.
Having thus requested, he should then [invite] two twice-born priests learned in the Rigveda to the eastern sacrificial pit.
The two Hotṛ priests should sit down; the Brahmā priest, however, faces west.
The performer of the fire-oblation (Homa) sits to the north facing east, and then [the other] to the south.
In the [southern] pit, two followers of the Yajurveda [should be present], and the Brahmā priest there indeed faces north;
the performer of the oblation faces east, and then [the officiant] at the western pit [faces west].
Two twice-born ones learned in the Sāmaveda [should sit] at the northern pit, and two Atharvavedins likewise; furthermore, there should be two reciters (jāpakas) and even more Brahmins.
Then the two experts in the respective Vedas should sit according to their seats;
thereafter, the preceptor [should sit] in his own sacrificial pit between Indra and Īśāna.
Then the Brahmā priest should sit facing east,
and likewise the Guru, having arrived at his own fire-pit (kuṇḍa), should sit facing north according to the procedure prescribed in his own Gṛhya-sūtra.
One should establish the fire in five sacrificial pits (kuṇḍas), and others may do so likewise;
however, they should perform the installation of the fire in a single pit according to the specific requirements of each case.
The preceptor should sit facing the east, and the Brahman priest facing the north;
then the patron of the sacrifice should first perform the worship of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa).
Then, having himself sat down to the south of the fire’s location,
the preceptor likewise sat down to the west of the sacrificial pit.
Having sipped water (ācamana) and likewise performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), he should then say:
"May those beings depart who are present here, and those beings who dwell upon the earth. (12)
"May those beings who create obstacles depart far from the site of the sacrifice.
Having scattered mustard seeds and sprinkled the pavilion with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), [he should perform the ritual]. 13.
One should pay homage to the sacrificial pit, the ritual implements, and the gurus;
having also prostrated before Gaṇeśa, one should take the unbroken rice grains (akṣata) and other materials in the hand.

Having offered perfumes, flowers, water, and so forth, and having proclaimed the place and time, [one should offer this] with devotion during the rite of the dedication of the temple of the deity. (15)
I shall perform the installation of the fire and its ancillary rites, such as the purification of the site,
as well as the placement and worship of the deities of the girdle and the womb.
Then, having swept the site of the fire and sprinkled the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) with water mixed with kuśa grass,
one should take flowers in both hands and touch the pit.
I invoke that sacrificial pit fashioned by Viśvakarman,
as well as your own divine and wonderful bodily seat of fire.
May all those deities who reside in the sacrificial pit, as well as those deities who stand before the pit,
being composed, grant prosperity and the successful completion of the sacrifice.
"May Kuṇḍa grant us the desired success of the sacrifice, which is beneficial to us";
having prayed thus, one should worship Viśvakarman within the center of the sacrificial pit.
Oṃ! O Viśvakarman, by means of the strengthening oblation, you made Indra a protector who cannot be harmed;
to him the ancient peoples bowed down, so that he became formidable and worthy of invocation as he truly is. 21.
You are taken with a support; for Indra Viśvakarman, you!
This is your womb; for Indra Viśvakarman, you! Om, obeisance! 22.
Having worshipped with sandalwood paste and other offerings, one should pray for the purification of the excavation:
"Obeisance to you; destroy all defects of the excavation, whether known or unknown. (23)
Then, one should invoke Śrī Viṣṇu upon a white girdle:
"Oṃ Viṣṇu, for the sake of protecting the sacrifice, be present in the sacrificial pit. (24)
Oṃ. Viṣṇu strode across this; in three ways he planted his step.
His stride is gathered in the white [lotus]; svāhā, I worship the Wielder of the Discus. 25.
Having worshipped Śrī Hari Viṣṇu, [one should say] "Obeisance, obeisance to Mekhalā. Then, having worshipped the white girdle and others, one should worship the red one in the middle.
There, reciting the mantra, one should invoke Mekhalā and Brahmā:
"Seated upon a swan, for the sake of protecting the sacrifice, be present in this sacrificial pit. (27)
Oṃ. Brahmā first revealed the knowledge from the east; from the boundless, the radiant Vena brought it forth.
His highest stations are the foundations of the world.
The source of both the existent and the non-existent, the separator of the two. 28.
