Having thus worshipped Brahmā, the sacrificer should worship the girdle with the mantra "Salutation, salutation to the girdle," and he should worship the red girdle presided over by Brahmā. (29)
Then, upon the black girdle below that,
I invoke Rudra himself— the bull-mounted, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, the wielder of the Pināka bow.
Come, O Lord Rudra, be present in this sacrificial pit.
Om, salutations to you, O Rudra, who possesses the mind; and likewise, salutations to your arrow. (3.1)
"Salutation to your two arms, salutation to the girdle, salutation, salutation!
The sacrificer should worship the dark-colored girdle, which has Rudra as its deity. (32)
In a triangular, circular, hexagonal, lotus-shaped, or eight-cornered sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), the yoni should be joined in the west;
it should be foremost and likewise face the east.
In a corner pit or a yoni-pit, a [separate] yoni should not be made in any case;
it should have a height equal to half the area of the field and a length equal to one part of the field.
The upper part [of the *mekhalā*] shall be one twenty-fourth [of the total height], and it shall be level with the edge of the *mekhalā*;
it enters the pit to the extent of half the fire-altar and is likewise joined by two globes (*golaka*).

With broad roots, a symmetrical central stalk, and the form of an *aśvattha* leaf, she whose nature is the foundation of Brahman should indeed be worshipped within the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍaka*). 36.
Homage to you, the cause of the world, and homage to you, the sustainer of Brahmā!
Oṃ, you are the source of all, and you are also the navel of all. (37)
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings, and I pray for the attainment of my desired goals;
embodied beings serve you, who bestows upon them the aims of human existence. (38)
"The Brahma-yoni grants happiness; salutations to you who are within the womb of Brahman.
Having thus worshipped the yoni, one should then perform the worship of the throat.
And I invoke Sragdhara, the support of the head;
the blue-necked, dark-throated Rudras have taken refuge in heaven.
Having worshipped them with perfumes and other offerings while reciting, "We bow to those whose bows extend for a thousand yojanas," one should pray to the radiant throat. (41)
Standing at the neck of the *kuṇḍa*, you are the auspicious girdle encircling it;
thereafter, one should worship the navel, which resembles the *kuṇḍa* or the lotus. 42.
I invoke the Navel, the foundation of all sacrificial pits;
may my navel be consciousness of the mind, and may my anus be the honor of the ashes.
May my anus be the seat of bliss; may my vulva be the source of good fortune.
Through my thighs and feet you are Dharma; as King, you are established in the entire world.
Having thus worshipped her at the navel, and having prayed, "O Goddess,
remain present in this sacrificial pit," he then bowed down once more.
One should worship Vāstupuruṣa in the southwest corner of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), saying:
"Taking flowers, I invoke Vāstu; I worship Vāstu. (46)
Oṃ, Lord of the Dwelling, acknowledge us; be one who brings us well-being and freedom from disease.
Whatever we entreat of you, accept that from us with favor.
Be auspicious to us who have two feet, and be auspicious to us who have four feet. ||47||
I offer perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings;
and I present a sacrificial oblation (bali) to the one who has the form of Vāstupuruṣa. ||48||
Having bowed to Vāstu— the son of Brahmā, the son of Rudra, the refuge of all the gods, and the Supreme Person—
the performer of the sacrifice should then duly install the sacred fire.
Or likewise in a vessel free from husks, hair, bones, and the like;
or on a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), having swept the ground into a square shape with excellent kuśa grass.
Having scattered *kuśa* grass in the northeast and smeared [the ground] with cow-dung water,
one should mark a space of about one forefinger-breadth toward the east using either a wooden sword (*sphya*) or the base of a sacrificial ladle (*sruva*).
Having traced [the lines] three times in successive order from top to bottom, and then likewise,
one should [wipe them] by the same tracing sequence using the pressure of the ring finger and the thumb.
Having taken up earth and sprinkled it with water, one should place the fire in a bell-metal vessel,
covered by another bell-metal vessel, facing westward.
Having established [the fire] and worshipped it with the Gāyatrī mantra:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ; may we meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ. (54)
May he who impels our intellects inspire us; I also worship the Fire-god. Oṃ, we know Nārāyaṇa, we meditate upon Vāsudeva. (55)
"May that Viṣṇu impel us; I bow to and meditate upon Agni.
Then, one should establish the fire within the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) by means of the path of the womb (yonimārga).
Reciting, "Oṃ, Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters," one should cause [the fire] to be placed down. ||57||
Having offered some fuel sticks for the sake of maintaining the fire's life, one should then pour water and other substances into the vessel of the fire; thus it becomes auspicious. 58.
One should perform the ritual of lifting the teacher from the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍaka) and transferring him into other pits;
then one should establish the fire and offer worship to the nine planets.
In the northeast, upon the household pedestal, one should perform the invocation of the nine planets;
in the center, within a circular area, one should place the Sun with red flowers and unbroken rice grains.
Facing the east, one should invoke and establish [the deity] while reciting the mantra:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Sūrya, come here and stay! (61)
Oṃ! Moving through the dark space, establishing both the immortal and the mortal, the divine Savitṛ comes on his golden chariot, beholding all worlds. 62.
I pay homage to Sūrya and worship him with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings;
and in the southeast, upon a wheel shining like a half-moon, [I worship] with white flowers and unbroken grains of rice.
One should invoke, meditate upon, and worship the Moon with sandalwood and other offerings:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Moon, come here and remain here! (64)
Oṃ! O gods, consecrate this man as one without rivals for great sovereignty, for great preeminence, for great lordship over the people, and for the full power of his senses. (65)
"This one is the son of so-and-so, the son of so-and-so; he belongs to this people. Yonder is King Soma; he is the king of us Brāhmaṇas. Om, obeisance! ||66||
In the southern triangle, facing south, one should invoke and worship Mars with red flowers, unbroken rice grains (akṣata), and other offerings.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Bhauma, come here and remain here!
Oṃ, Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth. (68)
He quickens the seeds of the waters; Om, salutation, salutation to Bhauma.
In the northeast, within a circle resembling an arrow, facing north— || 69 ||
Having invoked Budha with beautiful yellow flowers and unbroken grains of rice, one should worship him with:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Budha, come here and remain here! (2.150.70)
Oṃ! Awaken! Wake up from your sleep!
Having performed sacrifices and works of public utility, you have been created along with health;
dwell in this higher assembly-place, O All-Gods.
O gods and sacrificer, sit down! 7.1
In the northern square mandala, facing north,
one should invoke Bṛhaspati with yellow flowers and unbroken rice grains and pay him homage.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! Bṛhaspati, come here and remain here!
Reciting the mantra, I worship the Guru with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings. (73)

O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the enemy, which is worthy of honor, which shines brilliantly and possesses wisdom among men—that splendor born of truth which has shone forth, bestow upon us that wonderful wealth. 74.
In the eastern pentagonal section of the mandala,
one should invoke and worship Śukra, facing east, with white flowers and parched grain.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śukra, come here and remain here!
Accept the fragrance, flowers, incense, and so forth; I bow to you. (76)
Oṃ! From the essence flowing from food, Prajāpati drank the milk, the Soma, and the power of sovereignty with the aid of the Brahman;
by means of the Cosmic Order (Ṛta), he drank the truth, the sensory power, the pure essence of the plant-juice.
This milk is the sensory power of Indra; it is nectar, it is honey. ||77||
In the western mandala, which is equal in size to a bow, one should face westward;
there, one should invoke and worship Saturn with black flowers and unbroken rice grains (akṣata).
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śani, come here and remain here!
Oṃ! May the divine waters be auspicious for our aid and for our drinking. ||79||
May peace and well-being flow toward us; I honor and bow down to [the deity] in the southwest, who faces south within a winnowing-basket-shaped mandala.
One should invoke and worship Rāhu with black flowers and unbroken grains (akṣata), saying:
"Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Rāhu, come here and remain here! ||81||
Oṃ! With what aid has he, the wonderful, ever-increasing friend, come to us?
With what most powerful means do I honor and bow down to him? 82.
And in the northwest, within a banner-shaped maṇḍala,
one should invoke and worship Ketu, who faces south, with incense, flowers, and unbroken grains of rice.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Ketu, come here and remain here!
Oṃ: Making light for that which was without light, and form for those without form, O men... [RV 10.3.2]
You were born from the sacrificial hearths; I honor you and bow to you.
Now I invoke and establish the presiding deities. ||85||
The deities should be established facing the sun, with the Sun in the center;
one should invoke Rudra on the right side with white flowers and unbroken rice grains (akṣata).
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Rudra, come hither and stay here!
Oṃ! We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant one who increases prosperity. ||87||
"May I be released from death as a cucumber from its stalk, but not from immortality.
[With these words], one should worship Umā in the southeast and in the presence of the Moon with red flowers and unbroken rice grains (akṣata). 88.
One should invoke her, establish her, and worship her with sandalwood and other offerings:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Umā, come here and stay! (89)
Oṃ! Śrī and Lakṣmī are your two wives; day and night are your two sides; the constellations are your form; the Aśvins are your open jaws.
Bestowing [wealth], bestow it upon us; impelling, impel it upon us.
Salutation to Umā, who desires the welfare of the entire world. ||2.150.90||
To the south, on the right side of Bhauma, one should invoke, worship, honor, and meditate upon Skanda with yellow flowers, unbroken rice grains (akṣata), and other offerings. ||9 1||
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Skanda, come here and stay here!
Accept the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and so forth. ||92||
Oṃ! When you first cried out at birth, whether rising from the ocean or from the primordial waters,
with the wings of a hawk and the forelegs of a deer.
O steed, great and high-born, you are worthy of praise. 93.
To the northeast, to the right of Budha, one should invoke Viṣṇu with yellow flowers and unbroken rice grains, saying:
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Viṣṇu, come hither and remain! (94)
Oṃ, Viṣṇu strode across this; in three places he planted his foot.
It is gathered in his dust. Svāhā! And obeisance to Viṣṇu. ||95||
To the north, on the right side of the preceptor, one should invoke the goat with white flowers and unbroken rice grains, saying:
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come and stay! (96)
Oṃ. Brahman first revealed the knowledge from the east; from the boundless expanse, he disclosed the radiant light.
He, the foundation, has disclosed its highest forms, the womb of both the existent and the non-existent. 97.
In the east, on the right of Śukra, one should invoke Hari with yellow flowers and unhusked grain, saying:
"Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Indra, come and stay! (98)
Oṃ! Indra, the protector; Indra, the helper;
Indra, the hero who is easily invoked at every call—I invoke Śakra, Indra, who is invoked by many.
May the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us. ||99||
In the west, and with black flowers and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), one should invoke Yama with the mantra:
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Yama, come and stay! (2.150.1).
Oṃ! For Yama thee, for Makha thee, for the heat of the Sun thee!
May the divine Savitṛ protect thee from the touch of the earth’s moisture. 101.
"O Arcci, you are light; O Śoci, you are heat; O Tapas, homage to you!
[One should worship] Kāla in the south and southwest of Rāhu with brown flowers and unbroken grains."
One should invoke [the water]: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Kāla, come and stay!
"Oṃ! You are the furrow; I draw you up from the earth of the ocean. 1.03.
"May waters unite with waters, and herbs with herbs; O Kāla, homage to you!
In the north-western direction, one should worship the Banner (Ketuda) with red flowers, unbroken rice grains (akṣata), and other offerings. || 104 ||
One should invoke Citragupta: "Come here and stay! Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, O Citrāvasu, may you have well-being; may I reach the further shore. (1.05)
"O Rādhā, 'I worship'—this indeed is the worship of the presiding deities;
that which Śrī Hari spoke to His devotee has been related by me to you. (1.06)

Thus ends the one hundred and fiftieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Installation of the Fire, the Pit, the Deity, the Girdle, the Womb of the Deity, the Worship of the Fire, the Worship of the Nine Planets, and the Worship of the Presiding Deities," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, to that which Hari spoke to Devayātā;
I shall now describe to you the invocation of the presiding deities and other rites.
In the center, indeed to the left of the sun, with red flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings, [one should recite]: "Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Agni; come and stay! || 2 ||
Oṃ. I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I invoke the bearer of oblations. Bring the gods here to this sacrifice. O Agni, I honor you with praise; homage to you! || 3 ||
In the southeast and to the left of the moon, [one should offer] water with white flowers and unbroken grains [of rice], [reciting]:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! I invoke the water; come here and remain! (4).
Oṃ! O Agni, you have taken your seat within the waters; you take hold of the plants.
Being in the womb, you are born again. I honor you with water; salutations to you! 5.
On the right side, at the flank of Bhauma, [one should worship] the Earth with red flowers and unbroken rice grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Earth, I invoke you; come here and remain! (6)
Oṃ! Be gracious to us, O Earth, thornless, providing a dwelling;
grant us wide-spreading protection, O Bhūmi; I worship you with reverence. || 7 ||
In the northeast and to the left of Budha, one should worship Viṣṇu with yellow flowers and unbroken rice grains, saying:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Viṣṇu, I summon you; come and stay here! (8)
Oṃ. Viṣṇu strode across this; in three places he planted his step. It is gathered in his footstep-dust. O Viṣṇu, I worship you; homage to you! || 9 ||
In the north and on the left of the preceptor, one should invoke Indra with yellow *sumanā* flowers and unbroken rice grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Indra, I summon you; come and stay here! (2.151.10)
Oṃ! With joyful accord, O Indra, together with the host of Maruts, drink the Soma, O wise hero, slayer of Vṛtra!
Slay the enemies, drive away the adversaries, and then grant us fearlessness.
Make [it] for us on every side. || 11 ||
To the east and to the left of Śukra, one should invoke Śacī with yellow flowers and unbroken rice grains:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Indrāṇī, I summon you; come hither and be established here. || 12 ||
Oṃ! You are the girdle of Aditi, the turban of Indrāṇī.
You are Pūṣan; shine for the sake of the Gharma offering. O Indrāṇī, I honor you; salutations to you! || 13 ||
To the west, on the left, one should worship Prajāpati with white flowers and unbroken rice grains for Śani, [reciting]:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Prajāpati, I invoke you; come here and stay. || 14 ||
O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these forms.
Whatever desire we have in offering this oblation to you, may that be ours; may we be masters of riches. 15.
And to the left of Rāhu, in the southwest, [one should worship] Nāga with black flowers and unbroken rice grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Nāga, I invoke you; come here and stay! || 16 ||
Oṃ, homage be to the serpents, whoever they may be, who dwell upon the earth, those in the intermediate space, and those in heaven; I worship you all, and to you I offer salutations. || 17 ||
And to the left of the lamp, in the northwest, [one should place] a goat with white flowers and unbroken rice grains, [reciting]:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, I invoke you; come and stay here! || 18 ||

Oṃ. Brahma, through his wisdom, first revealed from the front that which was beyond the horizon, the radiant Vena; he disclosed its highest and lowest stations, the womb of both the existent and the non-existent. 1.9.
Then one should invoke the five world-protectors as excellent guardians:
Nairṛta in the southwest and Rāhu in the north, with yellow flowers, unbroken rice grains, and other offerings.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Gaṇeśa, I summon you; come and remain here!
Having worshipped you with perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice grains, and food offerings, I bow down to you. (21)
Oṃ! We invoke you as the Lord of hosts among hosts;
we invoke you as the Lord of the beloved among the beloved; we invoke you as the Lord of treasures among treasures.
I bow to Gaṇeśa, my protector. ||22||
I have been born from the womb; you too are born from the womb.
To the north and west of Śanī, one should worship Durgā with red flowers and unbroken grains of rice. 23.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Durgā, I summon you; come here and remain. I worship you, I bow to you; grant happiness to the people; salutations! (24)
Oṃ! Let us press the Soma for Jātavedas; he drives away the wealth of the one who acts as an enemy.
May he carry us across all difficulties.
Like a boat across a river, Agni carries us beyond all difficulties. ||25||
In the center [he worships] Sūrya, and in the north Vāyu with yellow flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vāyu, come here and stay! (26)
Oṃ! Come to our sacrifice with your teams of horses, by the hundreds and by the thousands;
O Vāyu, rejoice at this libation. Do you all protect us always with your blessings. 27.
To the east, in the eastern part of the Śukra [mandala], [one worships] Ākāśa with blue flowers:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Ākāśa, come here and remain here! (28)
Oṃ! O drinkers of ghee, drink the ghee; O drinkers of fat, drink the fat. You are the oblation of the atmosphere; svāhā!
The quarters, the intermediate quarters, the primary quarters, the secondary quarters, and the upward quarters.
To the quarters, svāhā! I worship and I bow. ||29||
To the south and southwest of Rāhu, with white flowers, unbroken grains of rice, and other offerings, [one should say]:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Aśvins, come here; stay here! (2.151.30)
Oṃ! O Aśvins, with that whip of yours which is honeyed and full of truth, sprinkle the sacrifice; and I worship the two Aśvins. 31.
Having offered incense, lamps, and food offerings to the gods, I bow down;
then the sacrificer shall invoke Indra and the other deities in the directions beginning with the east.
To the east: Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Indra, come here and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you. ||33||
In the southeast: Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Agni, come hither and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you. ||34||
To the south: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Yama, come here and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you. (35)
In the southwest: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Nirṛti, come here and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow to you. ||36||
In the west: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, Varuṇa, come and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you. (37)
Oṃ Vāyavyāṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vāyu, come hither and remain!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you. ||38||
In the north: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, Kubera, come and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you. (39)
In the northeast: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Īśāna, come and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you. (2.151.40)
Between the northeast and the east, I invoke Brahmā:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and stay! ||41||
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember, and I bow down;
in the space between Nirṛti and Varuṇa, I invoke and praise Ananta.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Ananta, come here and remain here!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you. 43.
Then, one should invoke Brahmā and the other deities stationed in the center of the maṇḍala:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain here! (44)
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [you], and I bow down.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śiva, come here and remain here. (45)
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember You, and I bow down to You.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Viṣṇu, come here and be present! ||46||
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow down to you:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Gaṇapati, come here and stay! ||47||
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow to you.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Lakṣmī, come here and remain here. ||48||
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember, and I bow down:
"Oṃ! The five rivers, with their flowing currents, flow into the Sarasvatī. (49)
The Sarasvatī indeed became a river that flowed in five ways in that region:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Sarasvatī, come here and stay here! (2.151.50)
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow down to you:
"Oṃ! O Ambā, O Ambikā, O Ambālikā—may no one lead me astray. (51)
Sasastyaśvaka [invoked] Śubhadrikā, the resident of Kāmpīla:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Durgā, come here and stay! (52)
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow down to you:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Kṣetrapāla, come here and remain here. (53)
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [you], and I bow down.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O beings, come here and stay! ||54||
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow to you:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Viśvakarman, come here and remain! ||55||
Having proclaimed the place and time, I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [the deity], and I bow down for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of the sacrifice. (56)
I perform worship for all the gods with sandalwood and other offerings.
Oṃ, obeisance to the nine planets beginning with the Sun; may you grant us peace. (57)
Oṃ, homage to the deities beginning with Rudra; may you indeed grant us protection. Oṃ, homage to the deities beginning with Agni; may you indeed grant us splendor. ||58||

Oṃ, salutations to Gaṇeśa and the other guardians of the worlds; may you grant our desires! Oṃ, salutations to Indra and the other guardians of the directions; may you indeed bestow nourishment upon us! 59.
"Salutation to those who bestow prosperity, beginning with Brahmā and ending with Viśvakarman.
Having thus worshipped them, the sacrificer [should proceed] near the sacrificial altar for the planets.
And one should offer bali on the ground with the respective name-mantras as follows:
jaggery-rice to Sūrya, and ghee-porridge to Soma.
Masūra rice for Maṅgala, milk-rice for Budha,
curd-rice for Guru, and ghee-rice for Śukra.
One should offer sesame flour to Śani, milk-rice (pāyasa) to Rāhu,
rice mixed with various colors (citraudana) to Ketu, and milk-rice as an oblation (bali) to the others.
Having given that, the sacrificer should then place a water-pot in the northeast corner;
he should perform the touching of the ground with the mantra "oṃ bhūrasi. (64)
With the mantra "oṃ dhānyam asi," the performer of the sacrifice should scatter grain upon the ground;
with the mantra "oṃ ājighra," he should place the water-pot upon the grain.
With the mantra "Oṃ varuṇasya... one should fill the water-vessel with water;
and with the mantra "Oṃ vasoḥ pavitre... one should wrap a cloth around its neck.
One should offer a betel nut with the mantra "oṃ yāḥ phalinī" and cast five gems with the mantra "oṃ parivājake". ||67||
One should offer gold with the mantra "oṃ hiraṇyagarbha," and one should offer perfume and other articles with the mantra "oṃ gandhadvārā. ||68||
With the mantra "Oṃ yā oṣadhīḥ," one should scatter all medicinal herbs taken from a horse stable, an elephant stable, an anthill, a confluence of rivers, and a lake. (69)
Having brought earth from the king’s gate and from a cow-pen, one should deposit it;
and one should place *dūrvā* grass into the water-jar while reciting "oṃ kāṇḍāt kāṇḍāt... (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.2.1).
One should cast five sprouts with the mantra "oṃ aśvatthe," and one should deposit the purifiers with the mantra "oṃ pavitreṇa stha."
With the mantra "oṃ pūrṇā darvī," one should place a vessel of rice into the pitcher;
with the mantra "oṃ śrīśca te," one should place a bilva fruit into the pitcher. ||72||
Having thus established the jar, one should invoke Varuṇa in the water;
one should summon Varuṇa with the mantra "oṃ tattvā yāmi" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.4.45). ||73||
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Varuṇa, come here and remain here!
I worship you and pay homage to you with the sixteen auspicious offerings. ||74||
May all the oceans, rivers, sacred fords, and lakes, as well as the clouds that destroy all evils, come together. ||75||
"All the purifying gods reside within the jar;
and [they are] at the mouth of the jar"—with these words, one should consecrate the jar.
Then one should pray to the water-jar with the mantra of the gods and demons;
thereafter follows the worship of the Sarvatobhadra mandala.
One should draw nineteen lines extending toward the northeast;
in the corner, there is a crescent moon consisting of three squares, and a chain consisting of five squares.
The *vallī* consists of eleven squares, while the *bhadra* consists of nine squares;
the *vāpī* consists of twenty-four squares, and the *paridhi* consists of twenty squares. (79)
In the center, with sixteen squares, an eight-petaled lotus is prescribed;
one should fill the white crescent moon and the chain with black, and the creepers with blue.
The pond is auspicious, reddish-brown, or white; the perimeter is yellow in color.
The outer and inner petals are white, and the pericarp is yellow in color. 8–1.
Outside the lotus encircled by the boundary-line (paridhi) are the qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas;
in its center, one should place the gods, the lords of the suras, beginning with Brahmā.
Having proclaimed the place and time for the rites of installing the deity, one should invoke the fifty-six deities in the Sarvatobhadra [mandala]. ||83||
Having taken unbroken grains (akṣata), one should then invoke Brahmā in the center:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain! ||84||
I worship, I remember, and I bow down; accept this offering!
To the north: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Soma. ||85||
I worship, I remember, and I bow; come and remain!
In the northeast, Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Īśāna.
I worship, I remember, and I bow; come and remain!
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Indra from the eastern direction. ||87||
I worship, I remember, I bow; come and remain!
In the southeast, Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Agni.
I worship, I remember, and I bow down; come and remain!
To the south: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Yama. ||89||
I worship, I remember, and I bow down; come and remain!
In the southwest, Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Nirṛti.
I worship, I remember, and I bow; come and remain!
In the west: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Varuṇa. (9.1)
I worship, I remember, and I bow; come and remain!
In the northwest: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Vāyu. ||92||
I worship, I remember, and I bow; come and remain!
To the north: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Kubera. (93)
I worship, I remember, and I bow; come and remain!
O Īśāna, *oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ*, I invoke Īśāna. || 94 ||
I worship, I remember, I bow down; come and remain!
And I invoke Brahmā between the northeast and the east. 95.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain;
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you—be the bestower of happiness. (96)
And I invoke the eight Vasus in the space between Vāyu and Soma:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vasus, come here, be present! ||97||
I worship, I remember, and I bow to you, for you are indeed the bestowers of happiness upon us;
and within the space between Soma and Īśāna, I invoke the Rudras.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Rudras, come here, stay here!
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; may you indeed grant us happiness. 99.
Between Īśāna and the East, I invoke the Ādityas:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Ādityas, come here, stay here! (2.151.10)
And I invoke the two Aśvin-kumāras in the space between Indra and Agni:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Aśvins, come here, stay here! 10.1.
I worship, remember, and bow to the Viśvedevas together with the Pitṛs, who reside between Agni and Yama and grant us happiness—Oṃ. 102.
I invoke you, O Pitṛs of the realms Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ; remain here!
I worship you, I remember you, and I bow to you, for you are indeed the bestowers of happiness upon us. 103.
And I invoke the Yakṣas between Yama and Nairṛta:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Yakṣas, come hither and stay! 104.
I worship, remember, and bow down to her who indeed bestows happiness upon us;
and I summon the spirits and nāgas dwelling within the southern and western quarters.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O beings, come here, stay here!
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; may you indeed grant us happiness. 106.
Right there, I invoke the serpents of the earth, the atmosphere, and the heavens: "Stay!
I honor you, I remember you, and I bow to you; may you indeed grant us happiness. (1.07)
Between Varuṇa and Vāyu, as well as the Gandharvas and Apsarases, and the worlds Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ—I worship, remember, and bow down to them. 108.
Right there abide Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and the Apsarases as well;
I worship them, I remember them, and I bow to them, for they are indeed the bestowers of happiness upon us. 109.
Oṃ! Puñjikasthalī and Kratusthalī are two Apsarases;
biting creatures are their weapon; cattle are their missile; human slaughter is their hurling weapon—homage be to them! 2.151.110.
Between Brahmā and Soma, I invoke, remember, and bow down to Skanda, Śūla, and Nandin; I call upon Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ. || 111 ||
I worship you here in this place; come and remain!
Homage to you, Nandīśvara, Śaṅkara, and Mahākāla! 1.12
And between Brahmā and Īśāna, [he should worship] the seven auspicious Prajāpatis:
"O Lords of Creatures of the worlds Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, come here and remain! (11.3).
I worship you, I remember you, and I bow to you, for you are the bestower of happiness upon us;
O Durgā, come and remain here in the space between Brahmā and Indra.
"Bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! I invoke Durgā; I bow to her and I worship her.
To the east of Durgā, Bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! I invoke Viṣṇu."
I worship, I remember, I bow; come and remain! Between Brahmā and Agni, I invoke the ancestors; remain! 1.16
"O Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and O Pitṛs, come hither; I worship you.
And between Brahmā and Yama, I invoke Death and Diseases. (1.17)
O Death, go away along the other path, which is yours and distinct from that traveled by the gods; I speak this to you who have eyes and hear: do not harm us.
Do not harm our offspring, nor our heroes. || 1.18 ||
I worship, I remember, I bow to you; come, stay!
And I invoke Gaṇeśa in the region between Brahmā and Nirṛti.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Gaṇeśa, come here and remain;
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you—be the bestower of happiness.
Between Brahmā and Varuṇa, I invoke the Waters:
"Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Waters, come here, stay here! (121)
I worship, remember, and bow down to them, for they grant us happiness;
and in the space between the directions of Brahmā and Vāyu, I invoke the Maruts.
I invoke and bow to the Earth at the foot of Brahmā:
Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Earth, come here and remain here. || 123 ||
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; be the bestower of happiness.
And there, the seven rivers as well—come here, stay here! 1.24.
I worship and bow down to Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and the Gaṅgā and other rivers.
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śatadrū, and Āpikā;
O Uṣṇā and Ikṣu—O seven rivers, I remember you and offer salutations again and again.
Right there, I invoke and bow down to the seven oceans.
O Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and you oceans, come together and remain!
I honor and remember you, for you are indeed the givers of satisfaction and happiness to us. 127.
Above that, I invoke Meru: come here and remain!
O Meru, you who are Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, I bow to you; be the bestower of happiness upon me. (128)
Now, indeed, outside the mandala, in the vicinity of Soma and the others, in due order, I invoke and establish the mace in the north. (129)
O Gada, Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, come here and stay!
In the northeast, I invoke and establish the trident.
O Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, and you, O Trident, come here and remain! In the east, I invoke the Vajra, I establish it, and I bow to it. || 131 ||
"O Vajra, you who are Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, come here and remain! I invoke Śakti in the southeast and establish her. (1.32)
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Come here, come to this place, stay; I bow to you.
I invoke and establish the staff in the southern direction. || 133 ||
In the southwest, I invoke Khaṇḍaheti and I bow to him;
in the west, I invoke Pāśa and I establish him there.
I invoke and establish the goad in the northwest.
O Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Daṇḍa, and the others, come here and remain! 1.35.
I worship, remember, and bow to him who indeed bestows happiness upon us;
and outside that, to the north, I invoke and praise Gautama.
I invoke and bow to Bhāradvāja in the northeast;
I invoke and bow to Viśvāmitra in the east. (137)
I invoke Kaśyapa in the southeast and I bow to him; I invoke Jamadagni in the south and I bow to him. (138)
In the southwest, I invoke and bow down to Vasiṣṭha;
in the west, I invoke, worship, and bow down to Atri. || 139 ||
In the northwest, I invoke and bow down to Arundhatī;
in the east, salutations to Indrāṇī, and in the southeast, repeated salutations to Kumārī.
Salutations to Brāhmī in the south; salutations, salutations to Vārāhī in the southwest;
to Cāmuṇḍā in the west; and salutations to Vaiṣṇavī in the northwest. || 141 ||
To Māheśvarī in the north and Īśānī in the northeast, and to Vaināyakī and Śrī, I pay homage, I worship, and I remember them, for they are indeed the givers of happiness to us. || 142 ||
"Having invoked the fifty-six classes of deities, one should worship them"; thus spoke Śrī Hari to the devotee Devāyatana. (143)
O Rādhā, I have explained to you the mantras pertaining to those deities;
one should satisfy the hosts of deities with incense, lamps, and excellent food offerings.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-first chapter, titled "The Demonstration of the Invocation of the Pratyadhidevatās, the Invocation of the Lokapālas, the Three Deities and Goddesses, and the Planets, as well as the Installation of the Vessel, the Worship of the Sarvatobhadra Mandala, and the Worship of the Fifty-six Deities," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhā, I shall tell you what the Blessed One then said to his devotee:
"One should place a copper pitcher upon a lotus in the center of the altar."
Having touched the ground with the mantra "oṃ bhūr asi," having scattered rice grains or barley, and having placed medicinal herbs there with the mantra "sam it," || 2 ||
With "oṃ ājighra," one should place the water-pot (kalaśa) on that spot;
then, having poured water with "oṃ varuṇasya," one should wrap it with a cloth.
Oṃ! With the mantra "yāḥ phalini," one should cast betel nut, the five jewels, gold, perfume, and likewise all medicinal herbs.
One should also cast seven types of earth, dūrvā grass, and the five sprouts;
one should cast purifying substances and cause a vessel of rice to be placed there.
Having placed a bilva fruit nearby and having installed the deity:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Varuṇa, come here and stay here. (6)
I bow to you and worship you with sixteen substances; salutations to you! Having offered this prayer, one should place the golden image of Nārāyaṇī within its mouth.

Having first performed the rite of transferring the fire (agnyuttāraṇa) and having clothed [the image] in silk garments and the like, [he says]: "Come, come, O Blessed Viṣṇu, you who bestow grace upon the worlds! (8)
Accept this sacrificial portion, O Vāsudeva; salutations be unto you!
Om, salutations to Viṣṇu, salutations again and again to Madhusūdana.
Oṃ, obeisance to Trivikrama and to Vāmana; Oṃ, obeisance!
Obeisance to Śrīdhara; Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī-Hṛṣīkeśa; Oṃ, obeisance! || 2.152.10 ||
Salutations to Padmanābha and to Dāmodara; Oṃ, salutations! Salutations again and again to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa; Oṃ, salutations! || 11 ||
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa; Oṃ, salutations to Nārāyaṇa;
Oṃ, salutations indeed to Nara-Nārāyaṇa and to Hari. 12.

Having worshipped Kṛṣṇa with these names, one should prostrate once more; then the preceptor, having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), should worship the door-keepers with fragrant scents.
Recite the prayers and perform the sacrifices, and likewise urge the Brahmins forward;
the preceptor and the officiating priests, having meditated upon the fire within the sacrificial pit, should carry out the ritual according to the prescribed rules.
And the sacrificer, having sat down to the right of each pit and holding kuśa grass, barley, and water, [should perform the rites] today at an auspicious time and so forth.
In this sacrificial rite for the purpose of installing the deity,
this oblation is indeed offered to all the planets as well as to their presiding deities.
And also to the individual presiding deities, as well as to the world-protectors (lokapālas),
to the guardians of the directions (dikpālas), to the triad of gods, and likewise to Gaṇeśa.
To Ambikā, to the hosts of spirits (bhūta-yūthas), and likewise to Viśvakarman;
and also to Varuṇa, Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, and Prajāpati. || 18 ||
Having uttered "Sviṣṭakṛt and all other deities, obeisance to you!
Om," one should perform the renunciation of the materials for each sacrificial pit.
While the recitation of the *jāpaka*s is taking place, one should perform the fire-oblation (*homa*);
having proclaimed the place and the time, one should indeed carry out the formal selection (*varaṇa*) with the appropriate rite.
"I choose you, such-and-such a Brahmin, for the office of the Brahman priest.
"I am chosen," he replies; then let him perform the prescribed rites. (2.1)
Then, according to my knowledge, I shall perform [the rite] to the south of the fire;
having vacated the ground intended for the strewing of grass and having offered it to Brahmā.

Having spread out a seat made of wood from an elephant or similar source, and having strewn kuśa grass upon that seat with its tips pointing eastward, one should proceed by circumambulating the fire from left to right.
Having personally invited a Brahmin for the rite of consecration,
one should address him as "Be the Brahmā" and seat him upon the throne.
In the absence of that, however, one should prepare two seats consisting of fifty kuśa grass blades; these should be placed to the north of the fire with the tips of the kuśa pointing eastward.
Having fashioned an elephant twelve finger-breadths long, four finger-breadths wide, and with a hollow four finger-breadths deep; ||26||
Having placed the *camasa* in front, having filled with water the vessel held in the right hand, and having covered the face of the *brahman* priest with *kuśa* grass; ||27||

Having looked [at the fire], one should place [the materials] on the western seat upon kusha grass to the north of the fire; then, the ritual strewing (paristaraṇa) should be performed in the following manner.

Having taken one-fourth of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), [he should strew] with four *kuśa* blades each, having their tips pointing eastward, starting from the southeast and ending at the northeast. (29)
From Brahmā down to Agni, and from Nairṛti up to Vāyu;
from Agni to Praṇītaka, this is prescribed as the ritual strewing (paristaraṇa).
Having done that, one should then take three blades of *kuśa* grass for the purpose of cutting the *pavitra* from the north-western side of the fire. (3.1)
And for the purpose of purification, one should bring two bunches of *kuśa* grass;
[one] for warding off [impurity], and a *prokṣaṇī* vessel twelve finger-breadths in length.
The vessel for clarified butter (ājyasthālī) should be made of metal, twelve finger-breadths wide and one span high;
likewise the vessel for the sacrificial porridge (carusthālī), as well as the three blades of *darbha* grass for wiping.
The three types of fuel sticks, such as those of the *upavīta*, *kuśa*, and *aśvattha* trees;
the *pālāśa* ladle (*sruk*) measuring a span (*prādeśa*) in length; and the *khādira* dipping-spoon (*sruva*) held in the hand. || 34 ||
The clarified butter should be from a cow; the materials are rice grains and gold.
There are fifty-six as well as two hundred handfuls of rice. (35)
A vessel filled with rice should also be kept for protection in the pavilion;
furthermore, the placement of the *pavitra* grass-cuts and *darbha* blades should be to the east. (36)
Then, having set aside three blades of kuśa grass at the front, leaving a space of one span (prādeśa),
and having cut off two young kuśa shoots, the preparation of the *pavitra* [is performed].
Then, with the pavitra held in his hand, he should sprinkle the water from the praṇītā vessel into the prokṣaṇī vessel using the space between the ring finger and the thumb.
Having taken up the two strainers with their tips pointing north, and having likewise moistened them three times,
one should then place them in the left hand upon the *prokṣaṇī* vessel.
Then, having obtained two blades of *pavitra* grass with the ring finger and the thumb,
one should perform the sprinkling three times, and thereafter [sprinkle] with the water from the *praṇītā* vessel.

Then follows the sprinkling of the *prokṣaṇī* vessel; thereafter, with the water from that *prokṣaṇī*, one sprinkles everything from the *ājyasthālī* (the clarified butter pot) up to the *pūrṇapātra* (the full vessel). ||41||
Then, having sprinkled [the materials] one by one in sequence, he should place the *prokṣaṇī* vessel in a place free from passage, between the *praṇītā* water and the fire.
Having placed the clarified butter (ājya) into the butter-pot (ājyasthālī) over the five fires,
and having poured it out [into the fire], he should thereafter place it into the pot for the sacrificial porridge (carusthālī).
Having poured out excellent water and set down the prepared rice grains,
he places the clarified butter on the fire, and he himself places it to the north of that.
Having thus simultaneously placed the sacrificial porridge (caru) upon the fire, one should then,
once the porridge has slightly boiled, circumambulate a flaming torch clockwise.
Then, one should again cause the clarified butter and the parched grain to be whirled around on all sides; then, taking the *sruva* ladle with the right hand, one should hold it facing forward.

Having likewise heated it with its face downward over the fire, and holding it in the left hand, one should cleanse it from the base to the tip using the tips of the *saṃmārjana* grass held in the right hand alone.
Then, having scrubbed from the top down to the base with the roots, and from the base up to the top with excellent water; 48.
Having consecrated [the vessel] again as before and heated it from the south,
one should then place the clarified butter (ājya) there, having lifted it up from the east of the sacrificial pap (caru).
Having led [the vessel] to the north of the fire and placed the *caru* there,
he should then lift it up, lead it behind the clarified butter (*ājya*), and then lead it to the north of the clarified butter.
Having set aside the clarified butter and brought the sacrificial pap (caru) behind the fire,
and having brought it and placed it to the north of the clarified butter, one should then proceed as before.
Having purified the clarified butter with the two strainers and inspected it,
one should then remove any impurities and purify the *prokṣiṇī* water once more.
Then, taking the marriage-thread from the ring-finger with his right hand and placing it upon his left hand,
he should rise while meditating on Prajāpati within his heart.
The sacrificer, having sat down, should silently cast three fuel-sticks smeared with clarified butter into the fire,
using water from the *prokṣaṇī* vessel joined with the *pavitra* strainers.
Then, having sprinkled [the fire] with water held in the right palm, starting from the northeast (Īśāna) and ending in the north, he should indeed circumambulate the fire itself.
Then, with the tips of kuśa grass held by the Brahman priest, and likewise touched by the hand of the sacrificer placed upon his right knee, [the fire] is indeed consecrated.
When the fire is kindled, the sacrificer should offer oblations of clarified butter with the *sruva* ladle,
beginning from the *āghāra* and continuing through the twelve oblations.
The residue of each respective oblation, as well as the ghee clinging to the *sruva* ladle, must be poured into the *prokṣaṇī* vessel; such is the procedure.
If a desired fire-oblation (homa) is to be performed there, it should be done as appropriate:
"Oṃ, svāhā to Prajāpati; this is for Prajāpati, [may it be] mine. ||59||
Om, svāhā to Indra; this [offering] is for Indra, salutation to the two Āghāra libations.
Om, svāhā to Agni; this [offering] is for Agni. Om, om, salutation. ||2.152.60||
Oṃ somāya svāhā—this [is for] Soma; the two ājyabhāgas are mine.
Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā—this [is for] bhūḥ; mine. Bhuvaḥ svāhā—this [is for] bhuvaḥ. ||61||
Oṃ svaḥ svāhā—this is Svaḥ; these are the Great Utterances (Mahāvyāhṛtis).
Oṃ tvanno agne—to Agni and Varuṇa, salutations, Om. ||62||
Oṃ satvano’gne idam agnivarūṇābhyāṃ namaśca oṃ; oṃ ayāścāgne iti ca idam agnaye namaśca oṃ. ||63||
Oṃ, "Those hundred of yours," svāhā! This is for Savitṛ and Viṣṇu.
And this is for the Viśvedevas, the Maruts, and the Arkas; Oṃ, this is for them.
Oṃ uduttama iti ca svāhā; this is for Varuṇa, salutation to him.
Like armor, it is said to be the warding off of divine obstacles and a source of peace. ||65||
"Oṃ! May the waters, auspicious, most auspicious, peaceful, and most peaceful, provide healing for you.
In this manner, the priests should perform the sprinkling (prokṣaṇa) in all the sacrificial pits (kuṇḍas), concluding the ritual with the sprinkling of the fire.
Then the preceptor, having worshipped the fire, should perform the oblation for the planets.
[The sacrificial wood should be] Arka, Palāśa, Khadira, Apāmārga, and Pippala.
Audumbara wood, Śamī, Dūrvā grass, and Kuśa grass are to be known as the fuel sticks for the nine planets respectively, smeared with curd, milk, and ghee.
Chanting the *manus*, one should indeed offer oblations of fuel-sticks (*samidh*) joined with *śākalya* formulas—either one hundred and eight, or twenty-eight, or eight times over. (69)
Oṃ *ākṛṣṇena* iti vai svāhā; this is for Sūrya, salutations!
O *imaṃ deva* iti vai svāhā; this is for Candramas, salutations! ||2.152.70||
Oṃ *agnir* iti vai svāhā—this indeed is for Bhauma; I bow to him. O *udbudhyasva* iti svāhā—this indeed is for Budha; I bow to him. (7.1)
Oṃ *bṛhaspate* iti svāhā; this is for Bṛhaspati, [may it be] mine.
Oṃ *annāt* iti vai svāhā; this is indeed for Śukra, [may it be] mine. ||72||
Oṃ *śanno* indeed, Svāhā! This is for Śanaiścara; obeisance to him. Oṃ *kayā na* indeed, Svāhā! This is for Rāhu; obeisance to him. ||73||
Oṃ *ketum* iti vai svāhā; this indeed is for Ketu, salutation to him.
Then, holding water in the hand, [one should worship] the planetary deities with the oblation (*homa*). 74.
And saying, "May they be pleased; obeisance," he should pour water upon the ground.
Thereafter, he should perform the fire-oblation (homa) for the presiding deities of the nine planets.

Eight or four auspicious fuel-sticks (samidh) of Palāśa wood, measuring one span in length and originating from trees such as the Īśvara-tree, should be offered with clarified butter for each [deity]. ||76||
Sesame seeds mixed with ghee and barley should be offered according to the prescribed rule:
"Oṃ, we worship Tryambaka, svāhā; this is for Īśvara, may it be mine. (77)
Oṃ śrīśca te lakṣmīśca svāhā; this is for Umā, obeisance to her. Oṃ yadakrandaḥ prathamam svāhā; this is for Skanda, obeisance to him. ||78||
Oṃ, you are the wide expanse of Viṣṇu; svāhā! This is for Viṣṇu, salutation to him.
Oṃ, Brahman is the first knowledge; svāhā! This is for Brahman, salutation to him. ||79||
Oṃ, svāhā! To Indra, the protector; this [offering] is for Indra, salutation! Oṃ, svāhā! To you, Yama, the sacrificer; this [offering] is for Yama, salutation! 2.152.80.
Oṃ, you are the black one, svāhā; this [offering] is for Kāla, Oṃ, salutation to me.
Oṃ, O Citrāvasu, svāhā; this [offering] is for Citragupta, salutation to me. ||81||
"May the presiding deities be pleased by this oblation of material substances.
Having uttered "namas," the sacrificer should pour out water.
Then, after that, follows the oblation for the secondary deities (pratyadhidevatās) in sequence:
"Oṃ agniṃ dūtam iti svāhā; this indeed is for Agni, [I offer] salutation. (83)
Oṃ *apsv agne* svāhā; this [is for] the waters, Oṃ, salutation. Oṃ *syonā pṛthivī* svāhā; this [is for] the Earth, Oṃ, salutation. ||84||
Oṃ *viṣṇorarāṭam*—svāhā! This is for Viṣṇu; Oṃ, salutation to me. Oṃ *sajoṣāḥ*—svāhā! This is for Indra; Oṃ, salutation to me. ||85||
Oṃ ādityair eti svāhā; this [is for] Indrāṇī, oṃ namas.
Oṃ brahma yajñānam iti svāhā; this [is for] Brahmā, oṃ namas. ||86||
Oṃ, obeisance! Svāhā! This is for the serpents; Oṃ, obeisance!
Oṃ, Prajāpati! Svāhā! This is for Prajāpati; obeisance! ||87||
"May the presiding deities of each [element] be pleased by this oblation of substances.
Having uttered "Namaḥ," the sacrificer should pour out water. 88.
Then follows the fire-oblation (homa) for the five world-protectors according to the prescribed rite:
"Oṃ gaṇānām... svāhā; this [offering] is for Gaṇeśa, Oṃ, salutation to me. (89)
Oṃ ambe ambālike svāhā—this is for Ambikā; obeisance to her. Oṃ vāto vāmana svāhā—this is for Vāyu; obeisance to him. 2.152.90.
Oṃ ghṛtaṃ ghṛteti svāhā—this [is for] Ākāśa; Oṃ namama. Oṃ yāvāṃ kaśeti svāhā—this [is for] the two Aśvins; Oṃ namama. ||91||
"May the guardians of the world be pleased by this oblation of substances.
Having uttered "namas," the sacrificer should cast forth water.
Then, according to the ritual procedure for the guardians of the ten directions, one performs the fire-oblation: "Oṃ, svāhā to Indra the protector; this is for Indra, obeisance! Oṃ. (93)
Oṃ agnidūtam iti svāhā; this is for Agni, [and] mine.
Oṃ yamāya tvā iti svāhā; this is indeed for Yama, [and] mine. ||94||
Oṃ asunvanta iti svāhā; this is for Nirṛti, [I offer] salutation. Oṃ varuṇasya iti svāhā; this is for Varuṇa, [I offer] salutation. ||95||
Oṃ vāyo ye te svāhā; this is for Vāyu, may it be mine. Oṃ kuvidaṅga ceti svāhā; this is for Kubera, may it be mine. ||96||
Oṃ *tam īśānam* iti svāhā—this is for Īśāna; it is mine.
Oṃ *asme rudrā* iti svāhā—this is indeed for Brahmā; it is mine. (97)
Oṃ, "May the earth be pleasant," svāhā! This is for Ananta; may it be mine. By this oblation of substances, may the guardians of the directions be pleased. (98)
Having uttered "namama," the sacrificer should offer water,
as well as fragrance, flowers, water, food offerings, a lamp, and incense.
"And I offer betel-leaf; may the Supreme Lords be pleased.
O Rādhikā, one should perform the worship in this manner according to the prescribed rule.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa spoke according to the prescribed rule;
that which was spoken to the devotee of the divine abode has likewise been told by me to you.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Worship of the Pitcher and its Guardian Deities, the Invitation, the Prokṣaṇī Vessel and other items, the Caru, the Ghee Oblation, the Warding Off, the Planetary Homa, the Homa for the Adhidevas and Pratyadhidevas, and the Homa for the Guardians of the Quarters and Directions," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. || 152 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:

O Rādhā, I shall now describe to you the fire-offering (homa) for the deities residing in the site according to the prescribed rite, as well as other rituals which Hari has taught to His devotee. || 1 ||
For those beginning with Śikhin and the others, first [one should offer oblations] ending in "svāhā" and preceded by the Praṇava;
each [deity] should be worshipped one hundred and eight times with their names and Vedic mantras.
Twenty-eight or eight oblations should be offered with sesame seeds, clarified butter, and milk-rice,
as well as with fuel-sticks made specifically of udumbara wood.
In its absence, sacrificial fuel-sticks of the Aśvattha tree, mixed with honey, clarified butter, and milk,
as well as black sesame seeds, should be offered according to the prescribed rite and preceded by the recitation of mantras.
Oṃ, svāhā to Śikhin; this is for Śikhin, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Parjanya; this is for Parjanya. || 5 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Jayanta; this is for Jayanta.
Oṃ, svāhā indeed to Indra; this is my salutation to Indra. || 6 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Sūrya; this is for Sūrya, salutation to him. Oṃ, svāhā to Satya; here is for Satya, salutation to him. || 7 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Bhṛśa; this is for Bhṛśa, salutation to him. Oṃ, svāhā to Ākāśa; this is for Ākāśaka. || 8 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Vāyu; this is for Vāyu, [I offer] salutation. Oṃ, svāhā and salutation to Pūṣan; this is for Pūṣan, [I offer] salutation. || 9 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Vitatha; this is for Vitatha. Oṃ, svāhā to Gṛhakṣata; this is for Gṛhakṣata. || 2.153.10 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Yama; this is for Yama, [I offer] salutation. Oṃ, svāhā to the Gandharva; this is for the Gandharva, [I offer] salutation. || 1 1 ||

Oṃ, svāhā to Bhṛṅgarāja; this is for Bhaga, [I offer] my salutation. Oṃ, svāhā indeed to the Deer; this is for the Deer, [I offer] my salutation. Oṃ, svadhā indeed to the Ancestors; this is for the Ancestors, [I offer] my salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to the Doorkeeper; this is for the Doorkeeper. || 13 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Sugrīva; this is for Sugrīva. Oṃ, svāhā to Puṣpadanta; this is an offering to Puṣpa. 14.
Oṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa; this is for Varuṇa, [I offer] my salutation. Svāhā to the Asura; this is for the Asura, [I offer] my salutation. || 15 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Śeṣa; this is for Śeṣa, salutation to him. Oṃ, svāhā to Pāpayakṣman; this is for Pāpayakṣman, salutation to him. || 16 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Disease indeed; this is for Disease, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to the Serpent indeed; this is for the Serpent, [I offer] salutation. || 17 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Mukhya; this is for Mukhya. Oṃ, svāhā to Bhallāṭa; this is for Bhallāṭaka. || 18 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Soma; this is for Soma, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to the Serpents; this is for the Serpents, [I offer] salutation. || 19 ||
Om aditaye ca svāhā; this is for Aditi, my salutation.
Om ditaye ca vai svāhā; this is for Diti, my salutation. ||2.153.20||
Oṃ, svāhā to the *madbhyaḥ* [those who eat]; this is for the *madbhyaḥ*, obeisance. Oṃ, svāhā to Sāvitra; this is for Sāvitra, obeisance. ||2 1||
Oṃ, svāhā to Jaya; this is for Jaya, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Rudra; this is for Rudra, [I offer] salutation. ||22||
Om, indeed, Svadhā to Aryaman; this is for Aryaman, obeisance. Om, indeed, Svāhā to Savitṛ; this is for Savitṛ, obeisance. ||23||
Oṃ, svāhā to Vivasvat; this is for Vivasvat, let it be mine. Oṃ, svāhā to Vibudheśa; this is for Vibudheśa, let it be mine. ||24||
Oṃ, svāhā to Mitra; this is for Mitra, salutation to him. Oṃ, svāhā to Rājayakṣman; this is for Rājayakṣman, salutation to him. ||25||
Oṃ pṛthvīdhṛke svāhā; this is for Pṛthvīdhṛk, salutation to him. Oṃ āpavatsāya svāhā; this is for Āpavatsa, salutation to him. ||26||
Oṃ, svāhā to Brahmā; this is for Brahmā, may it be mine. Oṃ, svāhā to Carakī; this is for Carakī, may it be mine. ||27||
Oṃ, svāhā to Vidārī; this is for Vidārī, salutation to her. Oṃ, svāhā to Pūtanā; this is for Pūtanā, salutation to her. || 28 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to the evil Rākṣasī; this is for the evil Rākṣasī, not mine. Oṃ, svāhā to Skanda; this is for Skanda, not mine. ||29||
Oṃ, to Aryaman, Svadhā! This is for Aryaman; obeisance to him.
Oṃ, to Jṛmbhaka, Svāhā! This is for Jṛmbha; obeisance to him. ||2.153.30||
Oṃ, svāhā to Pilipicchā; this is for Pilipicchā, [I offer] salutation. Oṃ, and indeed svāhā to Indra; this is for Indra, [I offer] salutation. ||3 1||
Om, svāhā to Agni; this is for Agni, my salutation. Om, svāhā to Yama; this is for Yama, my salutation. ||32||
Oṃ, svāhā to Nirṛti; this is for Nirṛti, [I offer] salutation. Oṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa; this is for Varuṇa, [I offer] salutation. ||33||
Oṃ, svāhā to Vāyu; this is for Vāyu, may it be mine. Oṃ, svāhā to Kubera; this is indeed for Kubera, may it be mine. ||34||
Oṃ, svāhā to Īśāna; this indeed is for Īśāna, salutation to him. Oṃ, svāhā to Brahmā; this indeed is for Brahmā, salutation to him. ||35||
Oṃ anantāya svāhā; this is for Ananta, [I offer] my salutation. Oṃ ugrasenāya svāhā; this is for Ugrasena, [I offer] my salutation. || 36 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Ḍāmara; this is for Ḍāmara, [I offer] salutation. Oṃ, vaṣaṭ to Mahākāla; this is for Mahākāla, [I offer] salutation. ||37||
Om, Svāhā to the two Aśvins; this is for the two Aśvins, [I offer] my salutation.
Om, Svāhā to Durgā; this is for Durgā, [I offer] my salutation. ||38||
With this oblation, may Śikhin and the others be pleased; one should pour out water.
Then, for Vāstoṣpati, one should likewise offer one hundred and eight oblations.
One should offer oblations of sesame, sugar-cane juice, milk-rice, and clarified butter, joined with the mantras;
indeed, each of those [oblations] should be performed twenty-seven times with each individual mantra.
Oṃ! O Lord of the Dwelling, acknowledge us; be one who grants easy access and freedom from disease for us.
Whatever we implore you for, favor that with your acceptance. Be a source of well-being for our bipeds and a source of well-being for our quadrupeds. Svāhā! 41.
To Vāstoṣpati, Svāhā! To Vāstoṣpati, obeisance!
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and water. ||42||
Oṃ! O Lord of the Dwelling, be our furtherer; O Indu, increase our household with cattle and horses. May we remain unaging in your friendship, like a father toward his sons.
Be pleased with that; be near to us; bring well-being to our bipeds and well-being to our quadrupeds. Svāhā! ||43||
To Vāstoṣpati, svāhā; to Vāstoṣpati, obeisance.
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and water. ||44||
Oṃ! O Lord of the Dwelling, may we ever be united with you through your auspicious, golden, and path-providing [grace]. Protect us in peace and in exertion; grant us your favor.
Do you protect us always with blessings; Svāhā! ||45||
To Vāstoṣpati, svāhā; to Vāstoṣpati, obeisance.
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and water. ||46||
Oṃ! O Vāstoṣpati, dispeller of disease, entering into all forms, be a most gracious friend to us; Svāhā! Increase us with prosperity. 47.
To Vāstoṣpati, Svāhā! To Vāstoṣpati, obeisance!
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and water. ||48||
Then, indeed, there are six oblations with the cooked rice (sthālīpāka), as follows:
Om! I invoke Agni, Indra, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods. ||49||
To Sarasvatī and to Vājin, grant me a dwelling-place, O Vājins! Svāhā!
This [is for] Agni, Indra, Bṛhaspati, the Viśvedevas, Sarasvatī, and Vājin. 2.153.50.
Oṃ! [I bow] to all the serpents and gods, to Himavat and Sudarśana, to the Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas, and Īśāna, together with the guardians of the world. ||51||
I take refuge in all these; may the Vājins grant me a dwelling, svāhā!
This [is offered] to the Sarpadevajanas, to Himavat, to Sudarśana, to the Vasus, to the Rudras, to the Ādityas, to Īśāna, and to the Jagadbhis, svāhā! Namama! (52)
Oṃ! The forenoon, the afternoon, along with midday, the evening, midnight, the dawn, the Goddess, and the Great Path. 53.
I take refuge in all these; may the sacrificial horse grant me a dwelling, svāhā!
Homage to this [deity] of the forenoon, the afternoon, the evening, the midnight, the dawn, the goddess, and the great path. 54.
Oṃ! To the creator and the transformer, to Viśvakarman, to the plants and the lords of the forest—unto all these I take refuge; grant me a dwelling-place, O vigorous ones! Svāhā! ||55||
Salutation to this Viśvakarman, the creator and the transformer; salutation to the plants and the trees.
Om, [salutation] to Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, and the Lord of the treasures together. 56.
I take refuge in all these; may the horses grant me a dwelling, svāhā!
This [obeisance] is to Dhātṛ, to Vidhātṛ, and to the Lord of Treasures, namas. ||57||
Oṃ, this site is pleasant and auspicious; it is given by Brahmā and Prajāpati and all the deities, svāhā!
This is for Brahmā, for Prajāpati, and for all the deities; obeisance! (58)
Furthermore, one should offer oblations of bilva fruit accompanied by ghee and seeds, either with the mantra beginning "vāstoṣpate" or with the single mantra that is about to be described. (59)
Holding a bilva fruit combined with clarified butter as the fifth,
one should offer oblations one hundred and eight times for each, reciting the mantra according to the prescribed rule.
Oṃ! O Lord of the Dwelling, you are the firm pillar; you have approached this sacrificial session as the radiant drop, the breaker of eternal fortresses.
Indra, the friend of the sages, be auspicious to us bipeds and to our home.
Svāhā to the four-footed; this is for Vāstoṣpati. ||6 1 ||

To those who are not terrible, to those who are terrible, and to those more terrible than the most terrible—to all of them, to all the lords, let there be salutation to you in your forms as Rudras. ||62||
For the purpose of joining the vital points (*marmans*) of the site, one should offer more than a hundred oblations;
having offered again to Śikhin and the others, one should worship them with the fivefold offerings (*pañcopacāra*).

Likewise, one should worship the image of Vāstu situated upon its pedestal with curd, a sacrificial ladle (darvī), and so forth, as well as with śaivala grass, the seven types of grain, perfumes, unbroken rice (akṣata), flowers, and other offerings.
When the vessel made of unburnt clay has been prepared and covered,
it should be placed either in the southeast corner of the palace or in the northern part of that corner.
Having filled the hollow at the knee with water in the space designated as "ākāśa," and having scattered perfumes and flowers there, one should place an earthen vessel.
Reciting "Obeisance to Varuṇa," one should gently fill [the vessel] with soft earth;
having thus offered oblations to the deities of the site (vāstudevas), one should then present them to the Yoginīs.
Oṃ divyayoginyai svāhā; this is for the divine Yoginī, [offered] to me. Likewise, everything should be joined with the formula "namo yoginyai. ||68||
Oṃ, to Mahāśabdā, to Siddhi, to Gaṇeśvarī, svāhā! To Pretākṣī, to Ḍākinī, to Kāmī, to Kālarātri, svāhā! To me, obeisance! ||69||
To Niśācarī, to Huṃkārī, to Siddhivaitālī, svāhā! Adoration!
To Hrīṃkārī, to Bhūtaḍāmara, to Ūrdhvakeśī, svāhā! Adoration! ||2.153.70||
To Virūpākṣī, to Śuṣkāṅgī, to Narabhojinī, svāhā! Adoration to me! To Phutakārī, to Vīrabhadrā, and to Dhūmrākṣī, svāhā! Adoration to me! ||71||
To Kālapriyā, the Rākṣasī, the terrible Rākṣasī, Svāhā! Adoration, let there be mine! To Virūpākṣī, the terrifying one, the large-eyed one, Svāhā! Adoration, let there be mine! ||72||
To Kaumāryā, Caṇḍikā, Vārāhī, and Muṇḍamātā, Svāhā! Adoration!
To Bhairavī, Cakriṇī, Krodhā, and Durmukhī, Svāhā! Adoration! ||73||
Svāhā! Adoration to Kuraṅgī, who carries away the hungry ghosts, the long-lipped one;
Svāhā! Adoration to Mālinī, the Mantra-Yoginī, the slayer of Time. ||74||
To Mohinī, to Vakrā, to Kuṇḍalinī, to Bālakī—svāhā! Adoration!
To Kaumārī, to Yamadūtī, to Karālī, to Kauśikī—svāhā! Adoration! (75)
To the Yakṣiṇī, the devourer, the maiden, svāhā! To me, obeisance! To the wielder of the machine, the large-eyed one, the lustful woman, svāhā! To me, obeisance! ||76||
To the tigress, to the ogress, to the devourer of the deceased, Svāhā! Adoration to me! To Dhūrjaṭī, to Vikaṭā, to Ghorā, to Kapālī, Svāhā! Adoration to me! ||77||
To Vikalā, Mālā, and Sarvasiddhi, svāhā! Homage!
May the sixty-four Yoginīs indeed be pleased by this oblation.
The performer of the sacrifice should indeed perform the oblation to the Kṣetrapāla according to the prescribed rite:
"Oṃ, svāhā to the Undecaying One; this is for the Undecaying One, salutation to him. (79)
To Pāvaka, to Caura, to Dakṣa, to Indramūrti, to Kuṣmāṇḍa, to Varuṇa, and to Bāhuka—svāhā! Salutation! 2.153.80.
To Nimukta, to Liptaka, to Tilalopa, svāhā!
To Ekadaṃṣṭra, to Airāvata, to Auṣadhighna, svāhā! Homage to them! ||81||
To Kambala, who is pervaded by Bandhana and the others, svāhā! To me, obeisance!
To the Blessed One Kṣobhaṇa, who is Dharāyāla, svāhā! To me, obeisance! ||82||
To Aṇava, to Candravāraṇa, to Karāṭopa, svāhā! Adoration to me! To Uroṭopa, to Jaṭila, to Ṛtu, svāhā! Adoration to me! ||83||
To Maheśvara, to Vikāra, to Maṇimā—svāhā! Adoration and obeisance! To Guṇabandha, to Ḍāmara, to Dṛḍhakiraṇa—svāhā! Adoration and obeisance! ||84||
To the one with a staff, the one with protruding teeth, the giver of wealth, svāhā! Adoration!
To the maker of the nāgas and the producer of foam, svāhā! Adoration! ||85||
Svāhā! Adoration to Mahādala, Cirakāya, and Siṃha;
svāhā! Adoration to Mṛga, Pakṣin, and Siṃhavāhana. ||86||
To Tīkṣṇauṣṭha, to Alābha, to Sruktuṇḍa—svāhā! Adoration! To Yudhāmanyu, to Alīla, to Vavraka—svāhā! Adoration! ||87||
To Pāvana, svāhā! Obeisance! May the Kṣetrapālakas be pleased.
Then follows the Mātṛkā-homa: To Gaurī, svāhā! And om, obeisance! (88)
To Padmā, Śacī, Medhā, and Sāvitrī, Svāhā! Adoration!
To Vijayā, Jayā, and Devasenā, Svāhā! Adoration! ||89||
To Svadhā, to Svāhā, to the Mothers, Svāhā! Om, salutation!
Om! To the Mothers of the World, to Hṛṣṭi, to Puṣṭi, to Tuṣṭi, Svāhā! Salutation! ||2.153.90||
Salutation to the family deity, Svāhā; thereafter follows the Vasu-homa:
to Dhruva, to Dharā, to Soma, to the Waters, and to Anila. (91)
To Nala, to Pratyūṣa, and to Prabhāsa, Svāhā! Adoration! And now, the oblation to Āditya; to Dhātṛ and Aryaman, Svāhā! Adoration! (92)
Svāhā! Adoration and obeisance to Mitra, Varuṇa, and also to Āśā. Svāhā! Adoration and obeisance to Indra, the radiant one who possesses outstretched arms. 93.
To Pūṣan, to Parjanya, and also to Viṣṇu and the Jaghanas, [I offer] Svāhā! Namas! Then follows the oblation to the Rudras as prescribed.
Oṃ, svāhā and obeisance to Vīrabhadra, and likewise to Śambhu, to Girīśa, Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, and Pinākin. 95.
To Aparājita, the sovereign lord of the world, svāhā! Adoration!
To Kapālin, Sthāṇu, and Bhaga, svāhā! Adoration! ||96||
And the offering to the Seven Mothers: Svāhā to Brāhmī, obeisance;
to Vaiṣṇavī, Māheśvarī, and Kumārī, Svāhā, obeisance. ||97||
To Kuberā, to Vārāhī, to Indrāṇī, svāhā, obeisance!
Now follows the oblation to the six Vināyakas: to Modā, svāhā, obeisance! (98)
To Pramoda, to Sanmukha, to Durmukha, svāhā! Adoration and obeisance! To Avighna, to Vighnahartṛ, svāhā! Adoration and obeisance! Oṃ namaḥ! ||99||
And the oblation to the Grandfather (Brahmā) and others: "To Brahmā, svāhā; this is mine. To Viṣṇu, svāhā; this is mine. To Rudra, svāhā; this is mine. || 2.153.10 ||
To Gaṇeśa, Svāhā! This is mine; to Lakṣmī, Svāhā! This is mine; to Jātavedas Viśvakarman, Svāhā! This is mine. || 10.1 ||
And [the mantra] "bhūtagrāmāya ca svāhā idaṃ na mama ca oṃ namaḥ.
Then, one-tenth of the recitations should be performed as the Gāyatrī fire-oblation, numbering ten thousand.

The Lakṣmī-homa, which consists of the primary oblations to the deity, is performed with sacrificial fuel (samidh), clarified butter (ājya), cooked rice (caru), barley, sesame seeds, milk, and sugar, accompanied by the Śrīsūkta and other hymns. 103.
"O Rādhā, Hari said to that devotee who was building a temple for the deity, 'This must be done,' and I too have told you exactly as it was spoken."

Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Oblation to the Vāstu Deities, the Yoginīs, the Kṣetrapālas, the Mātṛkās, and the Oblations to the Vasus, Ādityas, Rudras, the Hosts of Mothers, Gaṇapati, Pitāmaha, Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī, Sūrya, and Others," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Thereafter, Śrī Hari spoke to Yama, whose body was a temple of the gods;
O Rādhā, I shall tell you that very homa which is dear to Brahmā.
One should invoke and worship the four hundred and forty forms of Brahmapriyās, who are the embodiments of the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa in the form of Brahmā. || 2 ||
Having visualized a vast golden lion-throne, she should summon them;
then, she should worship them with liquid offerings upon either rice grains or betel nuts.
Oṃ! Śrī and Lakṣmī are your two wives; day and night are your two flanks; the constellations are your form; the Aśvins are your gaping mouth.
Bestow [blessings], bestow [blessings], bestow [blessings] upon me; bestow [blessings] upon all the worlds. 4.
First, the sacrificer should invoke the six Great Brāhmīs and their consorts:
"Oṃ śrīrādhikāyai svāhā; this is for Rādhikā, [may it be] mine. (5)
I invoke her, I establish her, I worship her, and I bow to her;
[I offer] incense, lamps, sandalwood and the like, food offerings, and even water. (6)
I offer betel leaf as well as the lustration rite (nīrājana).
Om, Svāhā to Śrī Lakṣmī; this is for Lakṣmī, salutation to her. Om. 7.
I invoke you, I establish you, I worship you, and I bow to you;
[I offer] incense, lamps, sandalwood and the like, food offerings, and even water. (8)
I offer betel-leaf and likewise the lustration rite (nīrājana).
Oṃ, svāhā to the illustrious Māṇikyā; this is for Māṇikyā, may it be mine. || 9 ||
Oṃ śrībrahmavidyāyai svāhā; this is for Brahmavidyā, [I offer] salutation.
O śrīramāyai ca svāhā; this is for Ramā as well, [I offer] salutation. || 2.154.10 ||
Oṃ, and likewise to Śrī, Svāhā! This is indeed my salutation to Śrī. I invoke her, I establish her, I worship her, and I bow to her. || 1 ||
I offer incense, lamps, sandalwood paste and the like, food offerings, and water; likewise, I present betel leaf and the ritual waving of lights (nīrājana).
I invoke the Supreme Knowledge (Paravidyā), I worship it, and I bow to it;
I offer incense, lamps, and excellent food offerings—Oṃ, salutations! 13.
Likewise, I call upon the *Brahmapriyās*, the *Gītās*, and the *Upaniṣads*, as well as the *Jayaṇtīs*, the *Ekādaśīs*, and the *Ārādhanās*.
[He gave] Mahālakṣmī, as well as Bhakti, Rādhā, Ramā, the devoted wife (Pativratā), Gaṅgā, Rohiṇī, Kāmadughā, and likewise Pṛthivī. || 15 ||
I invoke you, I establish you, I worship you, and I bow to you;
[I offer] incense, lamps, sandalwood and the like, food offerings, and even water. (16)
I likewise offer betel-leaf and the lustration rite (nīrājana),
as well as Saṃjñā, Vibhūti, Duḥkhahā, Lakṣmī, and Kamalā.
Siddhi, Mohinī, Urvaśī, Muktā, Buddhi, Pārvatī, Dīkṣā, Līlā, Virajā, Vṛndā, and likewise Nārāyaṇī; || 18 ||
[Sarasvatī, Svarṇarekhā, Sitā, Devikā, Vibhāvarī, Tulasī, Mūrti, Jayā, and Gomatī. (19)
I invoke you, I establish you, I worship you, and I bow to you;
[I offer] incense, lamps, sandalwood and other perfumes, food offerings, and even water.
I likewise offer betel-leaf and the lustration ceremony (nīrājana),
as well as my dear friends Rukmiṇī, Godāvarī, and Mañjulā.
Haṃsā, Suguṇā, Lalitā, Dhātrī, Rambhā, Kumudvatī, Campā, Śītalā, Svarṇagaurī, Nandā, Dayā, and Kalā. ||22||
Durgā, Nandinī, Sādhyā, Vijayā, Vañjulī, Dhanyā, Dolā, Sāvitrī, Puṇyā, Kokilā, and Manu. (23)
I invoke you, I establish you, I worship you, and I bow to you;
[I offer] incense, a lamp, food offerings, sandalwood and other perfumes, as well as water. (24)
I likewise offer betel-leaf and the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) to Citralekhā,
Pūrṇimā, Śāradā, Māṃ, and Mañjarī.
Devikā, Preyasī, Śreyasī, Vikuṇṭhā, as well as Aruṇā, Jyoṣṭrī, Śabarī, Pampā, Gālavī, and Sudughā. ||26||
Yājñasenī, Vasumatī, Padmāvatī the daughter of Bhṛgu,
Padminī, Śrīmatī, Jaratkārvī, and likewise Līlāvatī.
And [he saw] Kalāvatī, Kadalī, Revā, Kāntimatī,
as well as Kālindī, Vardhinī, Puṇyanadī, and Sumitrikā.
I invoke you, I establish you, I worship you, and I bow to you;
likewise, I offer incense, lamps, sandalwood and other perfumes, food offerings, and water. (29)
I likewise offer betel-leaf and the lustration ceremony (nīrājana),
as well as Bandulā, Suśīlā, Mānasā, and Mādhavī.
Śarmavatī, Dīrghikā, Karṇotpalā, Akṣamālikā,
Udumbarī, Badarī, Kubjikā, Haimī, and Ṛtambharā.
O beloveds of Hari, I invoke, establish, worship, and bow down to Maṅgalā, Amṛtā, Mahāvedī, Kṛṣṇā, and Haripriyā. ||32||
I offer incense, lamps, sandalwood and other perfumes, food offerings, water, as well as betel leaf and the waving of lights (nīrājana). ||33||
I invoke and bow down to the goddess Kaṃbharā Lakṣmī, the embodiment of contentment;
I establish her and worship her with incense, lamps, water, and other offerings. ||34||
I offer the sacrificial food, sandalwood paste, and betel leaf.
Oṃ, svāhā to the group of six Rādhās; this is for the group of six Rādhās, may it be mine. || 35 ||
I offer milk-rice, fried cakes, sweetmeats and other delicacies along with excellent side dishes, as well as foods to be chewed, eaten, licked, and sucked. (36)
Oṃ, to the four hundred and forty [deities] beginning with Parāvidyā, svāhā! This is for Parāvidyā and the others; Oṃ, obeisance to them! ||37||
I offer milk-rice, fried cakes, sweetmeats and other delicacies along with excellent side dishes; I present various foods to be chewed, eaten, licked, and sucked. (38)
Oṃ, svāhā to Kaṃbharā Lakṣmī, who is accompanied by the goddesses of contentment; salutations to them both.
[I offer] milk-rice, fried cakes, sweet foods, and excellent side dishes. (39)
"I offer foods to be chewed, swallowed, licked, and sucked.
Having thus worshipped the forms of Brahmā, one should indeed worship the incarnations.
Matsya, Kūrma, Vārāha, Kapila, and Hari; likewise Vāsudeva, Pṛthu, Dattātreya, Haṃsa, and Nṛsiṃhaka. ||41||
Ṛṣabha, Vāmana, Paraśurāma, Yajña, the Kumārakas, Rāma, the god Hayagrīva, Nārada, and the king of kings. 42.
Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa, Gopāla, Buddha, Kali, and Mohinī;
Dhanvantari, Bālakṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, and likewise Nara. ||43||
One should establish the Sahasrahasta array within golden images;
one may also place it within rice grains, betel nuts, or even jewels.
I invoke you, I establish you, I worship you, and I bow to you;
[I offer] incense, lamps, sandalwood and the like, food offerings, and even water. (45)
I offer betel-leaf and the lustration rite; Oṃ, obeisance!
Oṃ, svāhā to the Fish-form and the others; this is for the Fish-form and the others, obeisance. ||46||
I offer milk-rice, fried cakes, sweetmeats with excellent side dishes, as well as foods to be chewed, swallowed, licked, and sucked. (47)
Accompanied by their powers, weapons, ornaments, and attendants, let them accept eight hundred and sixty-four portions of food offered at the sacrifice. 48.
Oṃ. By means of sacrifice the gods performed the sacrifice; those were the first ordinances.
Those great ones attained the heavenly world.
Wherein dwell the ancient Sādhyas, the gods. ||49||
Thus, the performer of the sacrifice should perform one hundred and eight oblations for each of the incarnations,
or he may do so for each individually according to his capacity.
Then, upon a golden throne, one should worship the fourfold group of qualities:
Vāsudeva, Aniruddha, Pradyumna, and Saṃkarṣaṇa.
I invoke you, I establish you, I worship you, and I bow to you;
I honor you, together with your Śakti, with one hundred and eight substances.
"Vāsudevādibhyaḥ svāhā; this [offering] for the fourfold group is mine. [I offer] milk-rice, cakes, vegetables, savory juices, and sweets. (53)
Then, upon a golden throne, he [saw] the fourfold form that is devoid of attributes:
Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
One should invoke Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa and Nara-Nārāyaṇa;
I invoke you, I establish you, I worship you, and I bow to you. (55)
I worship Him along with His Śakti with one hundred and eight substances;
Svāhā to Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa and the others! ||56||
I offer this salutation to them; indeed, I perform the *nīrājana* rite with obeisance.
I offer milk-rice (*pāyasa*), fried cakes (*polikā*), vegetables, savory juices, and sweets. (57)
Having thus worshipped the Supreme Lords, one should perform the oblation;
one should offer eight oblations with milk-rice and clarified butter, using their respective names.
There is an oblation of māṣa beans for Viṣṇu and an auspicious oblation of milk;
reciting "idaṃ viṣṇuḥ" with the twelve-syllable mantra, one should offer it. (59)
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; Svāhā! [Recite] this sixteen-syllable mantra one thousand and eight hundred times. 2.154.60.
One should offer the sacrificial oblation (caru) with the mantra: "Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya svāhā.
Likewise, one should offer oblations with fuel-sticks, clarified butter, barley, sesame seeds, and fruits.
Oṃ, Viṣṇu strode across this; he planted his foot in three places.
It is gathered in his dust—svāhā! This [is offered] to Viṣṇu.
And with this [mantra], one should also offer one thousand one hundred and eight oblations: "Oṃ agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā; this is for Agni, may it be mine. (6.3)
Then: *Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā; this [is] for Agni, salutation to him; grant welfare at the sacrifice!
Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā; this [is] for Vāyu, salutation to him; grant welfare at the sacrifice!* (64)

Having performed the *vyāhṛti-homa* with the mantra: "Oṃ svaḥ svāhā! This [oblation] is for Sūrya; I bow to him. Grant me peace in the sacrifice," he should then [offer to] those situated within the pavilion.
Having performed worship, one should offer oblations (bali) to all the gods;
then, having gone outside, one should present them to the guardians of the world (lokapālas).
O Indra, come from the east; protect the sacrifice, homage be unto you!
Guard the quarter, consume the offering, and bring prosperity to the sacrificer. ||67||
