A stalk of sugarcane, vegetables, leaves, and so forth are given to the guest;
likewise, fruit, roots, leaves, tubers, and even clothing are provided in the house of the gleaner.
Or perhaps some virtuous devotee of the Blessed One might come to the garden;
he, along with his wife and son, serves him by massaging his feet and other such attentions.
At night, beneath a tree in a sacred field on the ground by a pure fire-pit,
having kindled a fire, he finds rest in its light.
He offers food, water, fruits, roots, tubers, grains, leaves, and whatever else to the mental image of the Lord. (1.3)
At night, having recollected the god Nārāyaṇa, he goes to sleep;
then, having risen in the morning, he performs the bodily purification consisting of purity.
Having taken food, he engages in agricultural work in the field;
for one who lives in this manner, there is never any sin in his house. || 15 ||
Knowing that the circle of devotees had arrived at the holy site of Aśvapaṭṭasara at the beginning of the night to perform [the rite], he went to that place of refuge.
Filled with heartfelt devotion, he also provided shelter in his arrow-hall;
to his devotees, he gave water, milk, flat cakes, and other such provisions.
He provided them with grass mats and rest right there at the city gate;
eager, they performed worship and engaged in kīrtana throughout the night.
In this glorification, Kṛṣṇa, Śrīpati, Nārāyaṇa, Hari, the Lord who is the son of Kaṃbhā and the delighter of the cowherds, has been praised. 19.
He who exists in the supreme imperishable abode is of the nature of non-dual essential form;
He is the Lord of Śrī, the beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, possessing a divine form. ||2.163.20||
Mādhava is the sustainer of all incarnations and the inner controller of all; Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, is the self of the entire collection of insentient and sentient beings. ||21||
He who is the Lord of lords, the deity even of the gods, and who exists as the very life-breath of all living beings—he is indeed that Bālakṛṣṇa. (22)
He who is the Indra of the senses, the real strength of all things, and the bestower of the fruit of actions—he alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa. (23)
The purifying dharma of the Brahmins, the invincibility of the Kṣatriyas, and the abundance of crops for the Vaiśyas—he alone is that very Bālakṛṣṇa. (24)
The abundance of sap in trees, the flowering and fruiting of creepers, and the serviceful conduct of servants—all that is indeed Bālakṛṣṇa himself. 25.
For those in the stages of life, it is celibacy; for householders, it is having sons; and for ascetics, it is the Supreme Brahman—he alone is that very Bālakṛṣṇa. (26)
He alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa, who is the statesmanship of kings, the service of subjects, benevolence toward others, and the grace of the gods.
O Bālakṛṣṇa, that very same light which belongs to the planets, constellations, and stars, as well as to fire, lightning, and even gems, is He alone who is seen by the eye. 28.

That satisfaction which embodied beings find in food, that satisfaction which is considered to come from enjoyment, and that peace which exists upon obtaining what was sought—that is indeed Bālakṛṣṇa himself. (29)
Whatever fruitfulness is found in trust, whatever faith is held in giving, and whatever inner awakening exists in the sacred narrative—that indeed is Bālakṛṣṇa himself. (2.163.30)
That which is declared as the offering in sacrifice, the cultivation of goodness within the brahmins, and the mode of livelihood for the sacrificer—he is indeed that very Bālakṛṣṇa. (3.1)
He in whose hand lies the thread of the embryo, who brings about the longing of pregnancy,
and who provides nourishment for the stalk [of the fetus], he alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa.
He who, being stainless, made the non-inert sky out of the sky of consciousness—he alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa, who fashioned the cosmic eggs. 33.
He who is Bālakṛṣṇa himself made the potters known as Brahmā, the farmers known as Viṣṇu, and the weavers known as Rudra.
He alone who is Bālakṛṣṇa created animals consisting of milk-machines, trees consisting of juice-machines, and men consisting of knowledge-machines. 35.
He who, by his very nature, impels the wheel of the world and its seasons,
and has attained the state of the universal architect (Viśvakarman)— he alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa.
Even though trees consume food from a single layer of earth, they possess distinct natures due to the difference in their seeds; such is Bālakṛṣṇa, who possesses the seed.
Food, though of a single kind, is placed within the belly and assumes diverse forms;
because it possesses diverse qualities within the body, that Bālakṛṣṇa is the one residing in the belly. 38.
From the invisible state, visible beings indeed arise from those of their own kind;
through such immersion, he is truly that very Bālakṛṣṇa himself.
The gods are dependent on mantras; the intellect that perceives meaning is dependent on speech;
even the insentient self is dependent on him—He alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa. (2.163.40)
If Śukadeva was dependent on his own merit, and likewise the world is dependent on karma, then he who is dependent upon whom liberation is attained—that indeed is Bālakṛṣṇa. (41)
He who serves guests, to him Bālakṛṣṇa—who bestows the fruit of service—gives a hundredfold, like a seed; he alone is that very one. 42.
He who bestows all happiness, he who provides all protection, and he who fulfills every desire—that indeed is Bālakṛṣṇa. 43.
He by whom night was made to grant rest and day was made to provide activity, and by whom sleep was ordained to remove fatigue—he indeed is that very Bālakṛṣṇa. 44.
He by whom the form of a virtuous man was assumed, and likewise the form of Vairāja;
he by whom even a paramāṇu was made [into a child]—he alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa.
He who created softness in divine garments and the like, and hardness in stones and the like,
and who established both qualities within his own body— he alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa.
He by whom Mahākāla was created, he upon whom Mahāmāyā depends, and he by whom Puruṣa was joined with Bālakṛṣṇa—he indeed is that very one. 47.
He by whom dissolution is brought about and by whom creation is repeatedly performed—
he who remains therein untainted, he alone is that Bālakṛṣṇa.
Even while manifesting desire, anger, great greed, delusion, pride, and envy, Bālakṛṣṇa remains unattached; he is indeed that very same one.
He who, even among seeds that are identical, bestows diverse potencies and grants various ripenings—he alone is Bālakṛṣṇa. (2.163.50)
Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu, Vāsudeva, the Lord of the Imperishable,
and He who is the Inner Self and the Supreme Lord— that very one is Bālakṛṣṇa.
He is the Blessed One, the Supreme Self, Hari, the glorious Puruṣottama;
he who is the Lord of Rādhā and Lakṣmī is indeed that very Bālakṛṣṇa. ||52||
In the field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, at the abode of the Thousand Vases, that very same Bālakṛṣṇa is served by countless beloveds of Brahmā. 53.
He alone is Bālakṛṣṇa, who is to be revered, worshipped, and meditated upon within the heart; he is the one to be attained through service. ||54||
Thus all the devotees performed the kīrtana during the night festival;
having heard it, Dyuviśrāma and Karṣuka attained great bliss.
He made an inquiry regarding the reception of mantras from the circle of guests;
there, a brahmin guest known as Ṣaḍguṇa spoke to him.
Receive from me the mantra of the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa:
*oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine svāhā*. (57)
The six-armed one gave this mantra to that farmer, and he also gave him a beautiful-necked Tulasī plant and the name Nārāyaṇa.
He gave him a rosary for the purpose of recitation, as well as an image for the purpose of beholding Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (59)
For the purpose of chanting upon the rosary, he then gave them the name "Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa"; thereafter, they all set out in the morning.
They arrived at the sacred site of Kuṅkumavāpī, the hermitage of Śrī Lomaśa,
as well as Aśvapaṭṭasara and the temple of Sahasraghaṭa.
Then all the holy places of pilgrimage created a garden for Nārāyaṇa;
they all went to Bālakṛṣṇa, who was shining within the house.
Having duly honored the holy ford and made it their own place, they departed;
meanwhile, the farmer Dyuviśrāma, together with his family, was filled with joy.
Having reflected thus, he set out from the city of Kāmyaka for the purpose of a pilgrimage to the sacred ford,
accompanied by cows and bulls, toward the Aśvapaṭṭa lake.
Chanting the praises of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, he arrived full of eagerness;
tending the cows and bulls in the forest, he reached that place at evening.
At night, he took rest on the eastern bank of the lake;
having given water to the cows and the bulls, he settled them under the shelter of trees.
Those animals released him and stood near him out of affection;
at night, both those animals and those men fell under the power of sleep.
Their fatigue from the journey was dispelled by a deep sleep;
free from fear, they slept on the bank of the lake in that sacred place.
When midnight had passed, when the movement of people had ceased,
when the sound of the village was hushed, and when the beasts and birds were overcome by sleep.
From Vyāghrajaṅgala, he brought a circle of seven lions;
then, most terrifyingly, he suddenly seized bulls from Govṛṣa.
The cows and bulls also let out loud cries of distress;
hearing these lamentations, the people quickly came to their senses. ||7.1||
And they remembered the Blessed One, the Supreme Lord, for the sake of protection;
indeed, the devotee remembered Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa within his heart. (72)
Come, O Blessed One, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme beyond the supreme!
You who dwell within all living beings, protect us, save us, and preserve us! 73.
"The wealth of cattle is my strength when I am weak, as it is for a farmer;
if they are destroyed by lions, I shall become a miserable slave. (74)
Act quickly, O Great King, before they are attacked;
for if they are assaulted, neither your cows nor your bulls will survive.
"These animals have been entrusted to your protection; they are truly no longer mine.
You alone must protect them, O Blessed One; drink the milk as you see fit. (76)
"I shall give you cows, O Great King; quickly protect and guard them!
Having spoken thus, he [offered] a large piece of wood, burnt by fire and still glowing with flames. (77)
Having forcibly lifted him up, the devotee stood in the presence of the lions;
the lions, however, let out terrifying roars with repeated sounds. (78)
The entire lake and its surrounding fields were filled with that sound consisting of thundering; and all embodied beings, deprived of sleep by the roar and other such noises, trembled with fear.
Afflicted by fear upon seeing that great log with fire, the lions fled here and there, both outside and inside, overcome with terror.
The cows, indeed, did not come into his presence; filled with fear, they abandoned the embankment of the lake and fled far away.
Lions ran after them, and having gone a great distance, they seized them;
the best of devotees wept, for the animals were devoid of knowledge.
"Overpowered by the lion and the thunderbolt, what shall I do here? he wept;
for Bālakṛṣṇa, the storehouse of compassion, is the protector of his devotees. (83)
In an instant, the divine Lord became the cowherd boy Cakradhārī;
shouting with a roar of joy, Kṛṣṇa released his formidable discus.
The wheel, moving with speed, struck the circle of lions;
wherever the touch of the animals' claws occurred at that time, [the wheel followed]. (85)
There was tearing of the skin and breaking caused by the lion;
here and there on the animal's body, he touched it with his own hand. (86)
The compassionate Lord Hari quickly dispelled the pain in an instant;
by the mere touch [of his hand], he restored the joining of the skin as it was before.
He acted in such a way that no scratching of the nails was perceived, nor was there any flow of blood at those various places. ||88||
Due to the touch of Śrī Hari’s hand, not even a drop of blood flowed;
indeed, his limbs became entirely free from pain, just like the body of a god.
Indeed, he fashioned the bodies of cows and bulls, and thus protected the wealth of cattle; thereafter, he sounded his flute.
Having gone into the presence of the devotee, he graced the devotee with his attention;
then, suddenly hearing the sound of the flute of the Child-Hari, [he was filled with joy]. 91.
He quickly arrived at the shore of the lake in the vicinity of Dyuviśrāma;
like the Blessed Lord who wields the discus, he sat down upon the seat offered to him.
And the bulls, having gathered together, licked the lotus feet of Hari;
the cows, emitting streams of milk, indeed made a lowing sound.
The devotee, having had the cows milked at that very moment, repeatedly caused the Lord Hari to drink the beautiful, sweet, and excellent milk. 94.
Praising it, the Blessed One drank the milk offered by his devotee;
he held the conch, discus, mace, and lotus in his four hands. (95)
He revealed his own form in the likeness of the incarnation of Hari;
he granted liberation from the lions and sent them indeed to Vaikuṇṭha.
After showing his wife, sons, daughters,
and family members a divine form that provided rest for their eyes, Hari quickly vanished.
On the eleventh day of the dark fortnight of Phālguna, in the middle of the night,
Bālakṛṣṇa protected the cows from lions.
On the twelfth day, the devotee gave various kinds of gifts and worshipped Śrīpati, the Supreme Person, with sincere devotion. 99.
Then Dyuviśrāma gave the wealth of cattle to Bālakṛṣṇa;
Hari returned it, and even though he was his devotee, he rejoiced exceedingly.
Having obtained the cows by Indra’s command, he went to his own city of Kāmyaka;
that sacred ford became known as Haritīrtha, and it was also celebrated as Gotīrtha.
Thus, a temple for Hari was constructed there by the farmers,
and they installed the four-armed Hari, the Supreme Lord.
And full of eagerness, they stationed Bālakṛṣṇa and the cows there;
by hearing and reciting this, both worldly enjoyment and liberation shall be attained. 103.
There, in the southeast corner, a gift of cows should be given;
may the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa attain satisfaction. 104.
O Rādhikā, Bālakṛṣṇa, the ocean of mercy, indeed provides protection from the messengers of Yama for the pilgrim, as well as for the giver of cows and the giver of bulls. 105.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Protection of the Cow-herd Dyuviśrāma by the Lord in the Form of Hari when his Cattle were Attacked by Lions, and the Narration of Haritīrtha and Gotīrtha," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhikā, listen now to another marvel of Hari that occurred in the city called Bakasrāva, situated within a tiger-infested forest.
It was crowded with many trees, inhabited by ascetics and holy men,
filled with people of the four castes, and situated on the bank of the river Vṛkaśāvī.
A man named Nīlakarṇa, together with his family, lived in a sacrificial enclosure (cātvāla) in a vast forest; however, due to excessive rain, the river overflowed and reached the city.
O men, great calamity has arisen on all sides; likewise, cattle have died, food has perished, and no edible thing can be found anywhere. (4)
Due to seven days of rain, the ground appears like the ocean;
the roads are blocked for travel, and one cannot go from village to village. || 5 ||
This Cātvāla, together with his family, hangs from the branches of trees;
having bound pieces of wood with creepers, he lives upon swings made from branches.
The family also lived upon the branches and swings;
it became hungry, and death drew near.
And the great seer Vṛkāyana, established in meditative absorption, was carried by the waves and arrived in the vicinity of the tree. || 8 ||
Then, having been enclosed by a long rope and a branch at the sacrificial pit (cātvāla),
he was confined there beneath the tree, obstructed by the trunk of the tree.
Having slowly descended from the tree by way of the sacrificial pit, Vṛkāyana was seized by his matted hair and hoisted up onto a branch.
With his body exceedingly weak, he remained utterly absorbed in meditative concentration; he was not even aware of the rain, the flooding, or the obstruction by the tree.
Touched repeatedly by the sacrificial pit (cātvāla), shaken on his head,
and awakened by many cries, the sage indeed attained consciousness.
Then he understood that all was water from excessive rain;
he quickly took refuge in the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. (13)
O beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, son of the cowherd, Lord of Lakṣmī, and son of Śrī Kaṃbharā! 14.
O Keśava, who manifested yourself at the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā;
O Lord of Brahmapriyā, O Lord of Ramā, Māṇikī, and Padmaja! 15.
O Lord of the virtuous, O All-pervading One, O Sovereign of the Imperishable Abode, O Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, protect, protect these people who are deeply distressed by the excessive rain! 16.
"Oṃ, obeisances to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Master; svāhā!
Thus did Vṛkāyana perform worship and offer prayers. (17)
At that moment, the supreme lord Bālakṛṣṇa, out of great affection for him,
arrived by way of the sky mounted upon a white elephant.
Holding a conch, a discus, a mace, and a lotus in his hands, with a crown upon his head, the Vaijayantī garland around his neck, and the Sudarśana as his ring; || 19 ||
With a face of gentle smiles and beautiful eyes raining forth love,
he was accompanied by chests filled with food and caskets containing woolen garments and other fine things.
Served by two attendants resplendent with parasols and chowries,
Kṛṣṇa arrived through the path of the sky and came to the midst of the trees.
And the boy himself, sitting on a branch, immediately gave food from two baskets to that Vṛkāyana.
The Blessed Lord himself gave food and full garments to Nīlakaṇṇa and to the family of Nīlakaṇṇa.
Then Nīlakarṇa, having seen Hari and seeing that his family was without refuge,
beheld Nārāyaṇa directly through the power of virtuous yoga.
He indeed became one who had accomplished his purpose and enjoyed the food produced by that grace;
he wore garments, and the cold was then driven far away.
Vṛkāyana, the great sage, repeatedly bowed down to Kṛṣṇa, Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord,
and indeed offered a hymn of praise to Hari.
Then he performed worship with the leaves of the Śāla tree;
with the waters of the rain and his own mental dispositions, he worshipped the Supreme Lord.
By him who provided protection at the beginning for Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, by him you have provided protection for me here; salutations, repeated salutations to you! ||28||
By him who formerly provided protection for Satyavrata in the ocean, by him you have provided protection for me here; salutations again and again to you! (29)
By whom, in the past, protection was indeed afforded to many during the churning of the ocean;
by whom the gods were protected and the Daityas were struck down.
By whom the earth was milked and living beings were protected in the past;
by whom the earth situated at the bottom of the ocean was indeed protected in the past.
By you, with the water from your big toe, this entire universe was made pure;
by that same power, protection has been afforded to me here. Salutations to you!
By whom Dhruva and Prahlāda were protected as children in the past, and by whom the demon Sāṇa was slain here—by that Supreme Self. (33)
By that Supreme Soul, Talājā was protected and released when she had come for refuge;
by him, the Daitya Damanaka was liberated. (34)
By him who liberated the Kaṅkatālas and likewise the denizens of hell, and by whom Sālamāla was destroyed—I am protected by him. (35)
By him the children were liberated, the kingdom was released, the creeper was deprived [of its support], and the cowrie shell was destroyed. ||36||
By him the Vanaspati and others were liberated from their state as Rākṣasas, and the rescue of Devāyana from his birth as a Caṇḍāla was accomplished. (37)
By that son Raṇaṅgama, who bore a patched garment (kaṃthā), even Cirañjīva was indeed rescued by that wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
Māñjāmbikā and Rakṣitā were protected, and likewise the Mlecchas were destroyed;
since he also caused the destruction of Raktabīja, I have been protected by him.
Salutations to you, by whom the king named Udaya was protected while submerged in water, and Vasumedha was likewise saved from the waters.
Salutations to you by whom Jyāmagha was delivered from thieves, Sudhana was protected, and Tryaṣṭakāru was liberated. (41)
By him indeed the disciples of Hiraṇyakeśin were restored to life, Vṛhadvarcas was rescued, and even Baleśvara was liberated. ||42||
Salutations to you by whom Jayadhvaja was liberated, Ailavilā was rescued, and the one whose life is unrighteousness was destroyed. (43)
By him the great pestilence was destroyed and the dead were restored to life; by him the people of Uṣṇālaya, who had perished in the waters, were brought back to life. ||44||
By whom water was offered to the female ruddy geese upon the mountain peak, and by whom the kittens of a female cat were protected from the fire-heater. ||45||
Salutations again and again to you, by whom the regions of Kiṃpuruṣa and the territories of Prāgjyotiṣa were purified through sacrifices and other rites. 46.
Salutations again and again to you, by whom Samīraṇa was protected and Pavamāna was also guarded, and by whom Santāraṇa was protected. ||47||
By the Supreme Self, he protected the abodes of the gods;
by the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, the deliverance of the hungry ghosts was accomplished in the cremation grounds. (48)
Homage again and again to him by whom Śūrajāra was liberated, as were the Piśācīs, and Dhanameda was set free. (49)
Salutations again and again to Bālakṛṣṇa, by whom the driver was made wise and the cows were likewise protected; may there be salutations to him a hundred thousand times for me. (2.164.50)
O Blessed One, by my yoga this sacrificial pit has been excavated;
salutations again and again, ten million times, to that compassionate God. ||51||
O Lord, restrain the excessive rain and cause the clouds to disperse;
bring back the waters of the floods and protect the embodied beings who are submerged.
Having spoken thus, they cast *sarja* leaves upon the head of Hari;
then he blew his conch, and the clouds quickly resounded with its roar.
The waters were rent asunder and their raining ceased;
the waters and the floods vanished through that roar.
Through the influence of Vṛkāyana, living beings became happy;
and the great seer Vṛkāyana departed for Mount Kṛtasmara.
Bālakṛṣṇa vanished and went to Aśvasarovara;
Nīlakarṇa, along with Cātvāla, [worshipped] the Supreme Lord from that day forward.
He propitiated that Lord Hari, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa,
and constantly performed the worship of that very Hari who was ever present before his eyes.
Dwelling in a tree, subsisting on fruits, wearing garlands, and chanting prayers, he was a man of dispassion;
a man of knowledge who possessed sublime devotion for Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa within his own heart. (58)
He constantly worshipped Hari, praising Him with hand-claps and other gestures, saying:
"O Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, protect me! (59)
Bālakṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Victory to Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare!
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Beloved of Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Hari, victory to You!
Thus he made his offering together with his wife, sons, and others,
being content with whatever food was obtained and satisfied with even a small amount of clothing and such.
He worshipped the illustrious Bhagavān, the great lord Kāṃbhareya;
indeed, he established a circle of his own kinsmen who were devoted to him.
Always meeting at night, they remain in the maṇḍala and worship;
they proclaim Hari-Kṛṣṇa, praise him, and bow down to him. ||63||
They worship with Tulasī and other offerings, feed them fruits and such, perform the waving of lights (ārātrika), and consume the sacred remains (prasāda).
Then they go to their own homes and sleep with their minds fixed on Hari;
having risen, they meditate upon Hari and thereafter attend to their worldly affairs.
Proceeding in this manner, those Cātvālas,
who were well-versed in the divisions of the sacred texts, once reached a decision for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kuṃkumasthalī.
To see the hermitage of Lomaśa, to behold Bālakṛṣṇa, to visit Aśvapaṭṭasara, and to perform holy rites at the sacred fords there. (67)
Taking provisions for their journey, those more than a hundred people— including men and women, children and the elderly— departed together with their families.
Singing songs rich in instrumental accompaniment dedicated to Nārāyaṇa,
they proceed slowly along the path and then arrive at Kuṅkumavāpikā.
Some bent down toward the trees, some carried up dust,
and some, remembering Nārāyaṇa, rolled upon the surface of the earth.
Some then prostrate themselves like a staff with the eight limbs,
while others dance with devotion accompanied by circles of musicians.
Some, being full of devotion, sing the virtues of Hari-Kṛṣṇa; others sing those very same virtues back to them in response. (72)
Remembering the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa, they indeed drink and eat on the road;
then, as they proceed along the path, they perform service for the virtuous.
Thus all the devotees, their minds fixed on Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
arrived at the hermitage of Lomaśa with the sounding of musical instruments, hymns of praise, and the roar of chanting.
Then all the sages, as well as Brahmapriya and the others, went out to see them on the side of the path; and upon seeing them, the devotees [also followed].
And they all prostrated like a staff and placed the dust upon their heads;
having washed the feet of the sages and their beloved ones with water, [they honored them]. (76)
They drank the water of grace and placed it upon their bodies and heads;
having beheld Lomaśa according to the rite and worshipped him, those beloved of Hari [departed].
Having burned away one's own sins and having received the mantra from Lomaśa: *oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya pataye svāhā*. (78)
Chanting while wearing a garland of tulasī on their own chests,
they cried out for Bālakṛṣṇa, the eternal Supreme Brahman.
Having seen the divine temple of Hari with its thousand pitchers,
they bowed to those divine jars and to the banner situated atop the mango tree.
In the past, they went quickly to bathe on the shore of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake;
having bathed, drunk the water of the sacred site, and rested under the shade of mango trees. (81)
Indeed, in order to behold the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, they all went with offerings into the interior of that divine palace. (82)
The Blessed Lord Śrī Hari quickly summoned his own disciple, the great yogi Svayaṃprakāśa, and bestowed upon him the nectar of his own feet.
He gave it to them, and they all drank it in an instant;
thereafter Kṛṣṇa bestowed his grace upon them, and they then partook of the meal.
As soon as they were all gazed upon by Hari with a mere glance, they assumed divine forms and were entirely freed from their elemental bodies. ||85||
The gods, possessing divine forms, became equal to the body of the sun; they were freed from dullness and began to travel through the path of the sky. ||86||
Free from the obstruction of walls, their vision is unobstructed;
all of them bear divine knowledge, are white in color, and possess beautiful forms. (87)
With limbs corresponding in beauty to their forms, as if pearls had come here, or perhaps they have arrived from the world of the Imperishable Brahman or from Vaikuṇṭha. (88)
Or else, they have come from the abode of Goloka or the abode of Śveta;
they are of such a white complexion, with a splendor like that of the lunar orb. (89)
Having attained the grace of Hari, they reached divine state through devotion;
their childhood was dissolved, and likewise their dullness vanished.
Impurity was destroyed and human nature dissolved;
divinity arose and mastery of the scriptures was acquired. (91)
Having attained divine vision, Nīlakaṇṭha and all the others then worshipped the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa with the utmost reverence.
At that moment, a divine celestial chariot descended from the sky there;
then, for the sake of liberation, those devotees of Hari offered their prayers.
And we carry out your command here; for that alone is considered by you to be liberation.
Neither a celestial chariot nor anything pertaining to the next world is sought after here.
"O Great King, we shall remain right here and perform service for you.
To those who were thus entreating him, Hari then gave his command.
"O devotees, remaining in divine vehicles, proceed toward the northern direction—to the great land of Ketumāla, which lies to the west of Mālyavat. (96)
"This Mālya, known as Urala, is the eastern neighbor of Ketumāla;
let him also grant the bestowal of counsel upon the subjects in those regions. (97)
Having been addressed thus, they bowed to Śrī Hari and ascended the celestial chariot;
at that moment, the most excellent sage Vṛkāyana was remembered by Kṛṣṇa.
Having arrived by way of the celestial path, that very Śrī Hari gave him the command to go to Ketumāla for the sake of engaging in devotion. 99.
He too, having ascended his celestial chariot, went into the sky together with more than a hundred great sages who had assumed divine forms during the month of Śrāvaṇa.
Having beheld Kaccha, Sindhu, Indukuśa, Kaśyapa, and the ocean, he swiftly directed his celestial chariot toward Ketumāla.
Having crossed over Kukkeśāsana, he went swiftly to Ketumāla, where the Kaśyapa progeny dwell with white bodies due to the coolness [of the land]. 10.2.
All the people of Kāśyapa’s realm were indeed equal in their religious duties; and on the bank of the river Nīparā was his own celestial mansion.
Then Nīlakarṇa, the king of devotees, by the command of Vṛkāyana,
brought him down from the sky so that he might find rest for a moment.
O Rādhikā, Nīlakaṇṭha and others bathed at the Aśvapaṭṭa-sarovara;
because they bathed there, that sacred ford indeed became known by the name Nīlakaṇṭha.
For that indeed brings about divinity for embodied beings merely by bathing;
moreover, divinity is attained by people through reciting it or even hearing it.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Protection Granted by the Lord to the Family of Nīlakaṇṭha Cāṭvāla through the Sage Vṛkāyana during a Severe Drought, the Divine Transformation of Nīlakaṇṭha and his Hundred Attendants upon Reaching Kuṅkumavāpī, and His Dispatch by the Lord to the Region of Ketumāla," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Rādhikā said:
O beloved, O Lord of my life, O Kṛṣṇa, O lover, O you who enchant all!
Nīlakaṇṭha, Vṛkarṣi, and likewise other preeminent devotees— || 1 ||
What did they do then on the bank of the Nīparā in the region called Ketumāla?
Since that place is unknown to me, you should tell me all of that.
Having heard again from the mouth of my beloved Prāṇa this story concerning the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, I do not attain satiety.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhā, on the bank of the Nīparā, which is crowded with many trees,
a dwelling place for many birds, and enchanting with its cool breeze— || 4 ||
Then they all descended from their celestial chariots onto the earth near the edge of the water;
having gone there, they bathed and performed worship to Ādinātha and Hara.
Having likewise offered an oblation of fruits, roots, and other cooked foods,
and having consumed provisions for the journey and the like, one should drink the water born of grace.
Having rested for just a ghaṭikā, they performed the chanting of the Name:
"Hare Kṛṣṇa, Bālakṛṣṇa, Supreme Brahman, Hare Hare! (7)
"O Maheśāna! O Pareśāna! O Sarveśāna! O Hare Hare!
Thus they joyfully performed the kīrtana along with musical instruments.
Then they ascended their celestial chariot to behold Khaṇḍa,
proceeding with skill and in due order along the path of the sky.
From the sky, they beheld the region of Yavakrīta,
where the stars had vanished from the river, the banks of which were parched and its soil was scorched by heat.
Having beheld the mountain Kṛpāsthala, the river Dinapā, and the servant Sevikā,
as well as the regions of Yugaśāva and the districts of Valgurāya.
Having observed the regions of the Lord of Mountains (Śiva) and those small, desired portions of land, and having likewise observed Āpyāyanādri and then Alpādri thereafter; || 1-2 ||
Having seen the degrees of their own desired longitudes, as well as the degrees of the nodes (pheru-nasa), and having observed the rivers and the surrounding mountains of the Rāhus; || 13 ||
Having seen the river Indirā, the river Gavādakavitānadī, the river Gavādayānā, and the regions of Pūrta and Gaṇḍa; 14.
Then, having observed the Trigrasā river, the Dūra river, the Mitrā river, as well as the Supāna region, and the river of the Gurus; || 15 ||
Then, having observed the regions where fruits were eaten, as well as the river Lavavārā, the Senānadī, and the river Cāpagā which remained there, [he departed].
He beheld the regions of Vallī and Jīvana, the lands of Jarā and Mauna, as well as the river Ālpāpā and likewise the river Audarī.
Then, having observed the river Prapīṭhā among the protected regions, as well as the river Viṣatulā and the rivers of the Niyamās; || 18 ||
Then, having seen the Lātavāya regions and the Dūnā river,
he beheld the Pāyupaśya lake and indeed the Leṇḍuga lake.
And having seen the lake situated within the womb, as well as the regions of the phalanges, the regions of the sweet-smelling mouth, and the regions of the sounds of men.
Having observed the river Trinayā and the regions suitable for smearing, having closely examined Koladvīpa, and having beheld the White Ocean; || 21 ||
Then, having observed the low-lying river Pācaurā as well as the Sarit,
and beholding the beautiful confluence of the Kāmā and the Vastunā, [he remained there].
Then, beholding the river Donā at its confluence with the ocean of Ājā,
those devotees slowly brought down their own celestial chariot.
They stayed there in that delightful place among the trees and other features, and they performed worship of Śrī Hari with instrumental music, singing, and dancing. ||24||
Having obtained rest at night, on the second day they again performed the six duties, proclaiming [the praises] accompanied by musical instruments.
And in that very same order, these beings, traveling in celestial chariots,
wandered about after hearing the lamentation of the subjects and the kings regarding the Supreme Lord.
Attaining supreme bliss, they raised shouts of victory and uttered words of welcome, saying, "Welcome! Welcome! and thus offered words of honor.
They increased [the offerings] with flowers and other items in every region and at every site;
having thus wandered through the lands, they arrived at the Donā river.
Satiated by food and drink, they rested;
and likewise on the third day, they passed the night with recitations.
Having performed their morning rites and seated themselves in the celestial chariot,
they traveled through the air in that very same order, moving as passengers of the vimānas.
And having then touched that wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi) which was worn upon the neck of the form of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, positioned in the midst of His garland; ||3 1||
And the great seer Vṛkāyana, having reflected upon sugar,
produced it again and again, sweet as if it were nectar.
Wherever people were seen in any land,
there he rained down in many ways for the sake of obtaining the grace of Hari.
The people, with cries of joy, seized those sugar-candies;
being exceedingly delighted, they ate them and raised shouts of victory.
"Welcome! Welcome! they cried out with eager anticipation;
and having offered him their favor, they presented that very celestial chariot at evening.
And at the onset of night, they arrived together at the confluence of the Donā and Javā rivers; during the night, they indeed performed worship, chanting "Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa."
Just then, twenty-eight maidens arrived there;
they were all young girls possessing divine forms, radiant with white splendor. ||37||
Wearing divine garlands, garments, and ornaments, possessing the luster of the moon,
they were most beautiful and charming, adorned with Vaiṣṇava garlands of Tulasī.
Uttering "Nārāyaṇa," "Hare," "Kṛṣṇa," and "Bālakṛṣṇa"—calling upon Hari with a gentle disposition, their minds fixed on the Blessed Lord. (39)
With flowers, jewels, and unbroken grains (akṣata) in their hands, and anointed with musk and sandalwood paste, they,
equipped with the materials for worship, bowed down to that celestial chariot (vimāna).
There were five divine maidens, adorned with celestial ornaments,
dressed in divine Vaiṣṇava attire, and equipped with the implements for worship.
One is white and another is black; the third is swift;
the fourth has three eyes, and the fifth is blue in color. ||42||
Having bowed down, those youths remained for a moment gazing at the celestial chariot;
meanwhile, the other three arrived, all of them exceedingly beautiful. (43)
Free from the states of being male or female, white in color, and enchanting—the celestial chariot (vimāna) bowed down and then quickly came to rest for a moment at the Trika. ||44||
Just then, there arrived a divine Vaiṣṇava ascetic belonging to the twentieth maṇḍala, who wore matted hair and was radiant with Brahmanic splendor.
"Nārāyaṇa, Hare, Kṛṣṇa, Bālakṛṣṇa, obeisances unto You!
As they spoke thus in a single voice, that celestial chariot did not descend. ||46||
Then four noble beings arrived there,
auspicious, adorned with divine ornaments, and endowed with divine splendor.
Having bowed to that divine chariot, the ascetics and the perfected ones, who were indeed like celibate students, stood for a moment and rested.
Then those sixty men and women of divine form assembled together,
and having bowed down to Vṛkāyana as well as all the sages of Aṭvāla, [they spoke].
Beholding him facing their celestial chariot, they then offered praise with devotion,
closing their eyes and speaking in a single voice, filled with joy.
Salutations to You, Kṛṣṇa, who are the all-pervading Supreme Brahman, the primordial Śrī Puruṣottama, served by the hosts of liberated female souls. ||51||
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, in whom the imperishable Brahman resides—that divine abode higher than the highest—whom he always serves there. ||52||
Salutation to that Kṛṣṇa, from whose form the beautiful Śakti Rādhā was born, and who assumed the form of Kṛṣṇa for the sake of Rādhā. ||53||
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, the bestower of happiness, whom the cows, gopīs, and cowherds serve eternally in Goloka during the rāsa dance. ||54||
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, for whose sake Nārāyaṇa became a beautiful-formed embodiment, born as the personified Lakṣmī from his own form. ||55||
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, whom the male attendants, female attendants, and their consorts in Vaikuṇṭha, as well as millions of companions, serve.
Salutations to You, Kṛṣṇa, the Protector who assumes the fourfold manifestation beginning with Vāsudeva for the sake of the continuous flow of creation that is without beginning. ||57||
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa who was formerly the great deity Mahābhūma and Vairāja, and who has attained the state of the three deities. ||58||
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa who bears within his own form Māṇikī, Ramā, Padmāvatī, Satī, Lakṣmī, and Nārāyaṇī. ||59||
Salutations to You, Kṛṣṇa, who bears upon Your own form the swan-like Suguṇā, Mañjulikā, Dayā, Jayā, and Lalitā.
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, who bears Rādhā, Yamunā, Gaṅgā, Virajā, Sarasvatī, Śāradā, and Kamalā.
Salutations to You, O Kṛṣṇa, who holds millions of cosmic eggs within the cavities of Your own form, and who remains pervading those cosmic eggs.
Salutations to You, Kṛṣṇa, who dwells as Nārāyaṇa in the indeterminate, immortal abode of Śvetadvīpa, served by the auspicious Ramā.
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa who shines as the golden one within the orb of the sun, and who exists in the fire in the form of sacrifice. ||64||
Salutations to you, Kṛṣṇa, who in the cosmic egg is Viṣṇu, who in heaven assumes the form of Vāmana, and who as Hari dwells in Badarī.
Salutations to You, Kṛṣṇa, who in Your remaining aspect is the form of Nārāyaṇa, the inner controller within the self, and the witness of all beings. ||66||
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, who dwells as this Bālakṛṣṇa, the joy of the illustrious cowherds, in the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā. ||67||
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, by whom the divine Gaṅgā was truly made our mother with his big toe when we were sixty children. 68.
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, the Blessed Lord Hari, who dwells here in this celestial chariot in embodied form, raining down the grace of Gaṅgāpati.
Salutations to that Kṛṣṇa, who is for the sake of the ritual section, for yoga, for knowledge, and for discernment; for moral conduct and for inquiry. 2.165.70.
Salutation to that Kṛṣṇa-soul, who is Jīva and Jīvakāya, Prāṇa and Kośin, Kha and Kāya, and Satya. ||71||

Salutation to Him whose nature is Kṛṣṇa, who is the holy ford, who possesses a virtuous form, who is omniscient, who dwells [in all beings], who is liberation itself, and who bestows liberation. ||72||
Salutations to You, whose form consists of all consciousness and matter, who abide in Your celestial chariot, the embodied one, the child, Bālakṛṣṇa, the lovely Kṛṣṇa. ||73||
Salutations again and again to you, the beloved lord of Brahmā, the master of ten million powers, who is cherished by forty-one maidens above.
Salutations to You, Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Māyā, Time, and the Puruṣas; the Lord of the abodes and their inhabitants; the Sovereign of the Īśvara and the individual souls (jīvas). ||75||
We have come for refuge to you, whose form is both accessible and inaccessible, who is worthy of sixty-fold veneration; salutations to you, the one worthy of refuge. ||76||
Having thus offered praise, O Rādhikā, those [sages], desiring to go to Vṛkāyana,
bound their hands with handfuls of flowers and ascended to the level of the celestial chariot.
Those sixty boys, the sons of Gaṅgā, entered the celestial chariot where Bālakṛṣṇa himself, Hari in embodied form, was residing.
Upon seeing him, they respectfully offered handfuls of flowers and prostrated like a staff; at that moment, Bālakṛṣṇa appeared before their very eyes from within the image.
The Lord possessed a form of fourteen years, beautiful with divine limbs; he was more handsome than ten million Cupids, with a face gentle and smiling.
Accompanied by Brahmapriyā and his six wives, he himself,
together with the Gaṅgā and other sacred fords, became visible within a celestial chariot.
Upon seeing their mother Gaṅgā as well as Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the sixty children rejoiced; then Gaṅgā’s breast milk flowed forth.
They quickly fell at the feet of Śrī Hari and his mother;
with their minds absorbed, they all washed them and drank [the water] with joined palms. (83)
They worshipped him exceedingly with flowers, pearls, and diamonds;
with divine jewels, golden garments, ornaments, fruits, and other offerings.
And with divine honeys, fragrant sandalwood and the like, with the essence of perfumes, all flavors, and indeed with meditative visualizations performed with the heart-mantra. 85.
Then they performed the lustration ceremony for both Hari and his mother;
they circumambulated them and offered prayers as well. (86)
O Lord Nārāyaṇa, you who forgive the offenses of ten million births, please come to our lands and indeed make them pure. (87)
We await your arrival for the purification of all beings;
having come here, O Hari, purify us who have remained for a long time.
When our return from the world of the truthful (Satyaloka) occurred along with my mother through the effort of Bhagīratha, it was indeed brought about by Hara.
At that time, our mother was not seized by her own matted locks;
we were separated from the Himavat and the sky, having abandoned the realm of the Kimpuruṣas.
Having seen that Ketumāla is uninhabited and free from affliction,
we have come here by the will of Nārāyaṇa and dwell here in supreme peace.
"Among us are these twenty-eight maidens; we are all daughters of Gaṅgā, and these five are likewise our sons. (92)
"These three children, as well as these twenty youths and these four boys—all of us are born from the Gaṅgā. (93)
Having performed sacrificial festivals here and having summoned the assembly of gods,
purify Ketumāla and Kṛṣṇa on all sides.
Having heard this, Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, laughed and rejoiced, and he accepted what was requested.
Having granted them his favor, he vanished within the image;
indeed, his entire retinue also disappeared in an instant.
The great sage Vṛkāyana, Nīlakaṇa, and the others likewise, having heard the account and seen it, embraced him with joy in their hearts. (97)
They welcomed him with hospitality, food, and water; and all those descendants of Gaṅgā, who were recipients of Bālakṛṣṇa’s grace, likewise honored him. (98)
Having gathered together in their celestial chariots, they performed the glorification of Śrī Hari and then shared their personal accounts with one another. 99.
And they addressed the sons of Gaṅgā who were traveling in their celestial chariots,
inviting them to purify their own lands and to visit them again and again.
Then Vṛkāyanā and the others again accepted the invitation;
they spoke of staying together in their own celestial chariot for sixty years.
And those sixty divine girls accepted everything exactly as it was spoken.
Thus, O Rādhikā, the union indeed took place by the will of Kṛṣṇa. 102.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Journey by Vimāna of the Great Sages Vṛkāyana, Nīlakaṇṭha, and Others toward Ketumāla, the Surveying of the Land, and the Meeting with the Sixty Descendants of Gāṅgeya," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Rādhikā said: How and when were these young girls born from the Gaṅgā?
O Kṛṣṇa, tell me all of that in truth; I desire to hear it as it really is. || 1 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Questioned by Vṛkāyana and the others, they all likewise related the account exactly as it had occurred; I shall tell it to you.
Once, indeed, in Goloka, I, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, was requested by you through Rādhā for the sake of offspring; at that time, I was conceived by her.
Then, having produced your daughter named Vikuṇṭhā and the seven oceans as your sons, you gave them away and became satisfied in mind.
Seeing you possessed of offspring while she herself was childless, Gaṅgā became desirous of offspring and requested me for children.
I gave her auspicious daughters, as many as she desired;
numbering twenty-eight, she then attained satisfaction.
Then she desired that the princes also be given to me by her; yet, even so, she was not satisfied, and therefore four more were offered.
Even then, the twenty boys did not attain satisfaction;
although they were given by me, she still desired to obtain satisfaction.
At that moment, three offspring were then entrusted by me to her;
likewise, sixty boys were given by me to Gaṅgā in Goloka.
Then she, having been granted [the boon] born of the power of her resolve, attained great satisfaction;
and when she descended into the world, she was accompanied by her offspring.
Having arrived together with her affectionate children,
she first descended from Goloka into Vaikuṇṭha.
Then, upon the second covering of water, Vaikuṇṭha,
she descended from there into Satyaloka, which had arisen from the foot of Viṣṇu.
Protected by Brahmā in the world of truth with a desire for consecration,
she was constantly held within his water-pot and remained embodied even in her own home.
In the abode of Brahman, she shines forth in the very form of cause and effect;
through the effort of Bhagīratha, she manifests in the form of cause and effect.
Entrusted by the Creator to Bhagīratha for the sake of liberation from the ocean,
she purifies the great seers, the ancestors, and the gods born of Vāyu.
By way of Meru, that goddess fell upon the head of Rudra;
held there by Śambhu within his own matted locks, she attained dissolution.
Then, as instructed by their mother, the sixty girls abandoned the abode of Śambhu in the Himalayas and fled far away in haste out of fear.
Having abandoned Indukuśa, Kaśyapābdhi, and likewise Kiṃpuruṣa,
they went to another region where they remained indeed free from fear.
Having established their dwellings in Ketumāla, those sons of Gaṅgā—the Kumāras and the sixty Kumāris—resided there according to their desire. (19)
Remaining in a state of ease, they awaited the lotus feet of the Blessed One;
they propitiated Hari and constantly remembered their mother.
To fulfill their heart's desire, the Supreme Lord sent Śataka under the mere pretext of being a devotee. ||21||
Under that pretext, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself became visible in the celestial chariot in the form of Rādhikā. 22.
Desiring to perform a sacrifice for the sake of fulfilling their resolve,
he spoke those words there and then vanished once more.
Listen to the names of the maidens and the names of the youths;
they abide in embodied forms, and they abide as created beings. (24)
The eldest daughter was named Valgu; the second was Niṣṭhāparā;
and there were also Nistārā, Pṛthā, Dinapā, and Sevikā. ||25||
The seventh is considered Indirā; the eighth is Gavadakavitā;
the ninth is Rāhūnā; and likewise, the tenth is Gavādayānā. ||26||
The *trigrāsā*, the *dūrikā*, the *mitrā*, the *gurūṇā lavavārikā*, the *sthāyinī*, and the *senā*—these are considered the eighteen minor offenses (*alpāpā*). || 27 ||
Audarī, Viṣatulyā, Prapīṭhā, Niyamānikā, Dūnā, Trinayā, Hīnā, Pācaurā, and likewise Kāmikā. ||28||
The twenty-eighth maiden is said to be Donā;
likewise [the others are] Bālatrika, Śveta, Kṛṣṇa, and the one named Kaśyapa. (29)
Ājava was the fifth; these were indeed the elder brothers.
Thereafter, there were only four brothers; I shall speak of them to you. (2.166.30)
Parīja, Alpa, Āpyāyana, and Kṛpāsthala as the fourth;
from that, twenty [others] were born—listen, I shall tell them to you by name. ||3 1||
Yavakrīta, Romāyana, Yugaśāvaka, Valgu, Āya, Girīśa, and the sixth is considered to be Iṣṭalava. ||32||
Sveṣṭajara, Pherunasa, Pūrtagaṇḍa, Supānaka, Phalāśana, Vallijīva, and Jarāmauna as the thirteenth—these are the thirteen [ascetics]. ||33||
Pālanāda, Lātavāya, Phālanāda as the sixteenth, Svādvadana, Nārarava, and Lepanāda, who is Kolaka. ||34||
These twenty in number were indeed equal to Kṛṣṇa in prowess;
from them, moreover, three lineages were born by name.
The anus, the rectum, and the vulva—these constitute the neuter [organ].
Thus, O Rādhikā, there are sixty [channels] of innate origin, possessing divine majesty. (36)
The ritual of offering to Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, which belongs to Viṣṇu, is indeed practiced;
and wherever anyone resides, that place and so forth shall be designated by his name. (37)
From that, each attained its own established status as its presiding deity.
These sixty Bālas indeed [followed] the Gāṅgeyas and Vṛkāyana. (38)
They all, numbering exactly one hundred, prayed most fervently to wander through their own lands; then, they all once again ascended the celestial chariot.
Then, together with the sixty [sages], they set out in their celestial chariot to wander through the sky,
proceeding by way of circumambulation and according to the previous order.
Descending to those various places with the desire for the sons of Gaṅgā, they indeed performed purifications while offering worship to Hari. 41.
Having visited the sixty sacred sites and held festivals there,
he caused the name of Hari to be heard again and again among the kings and the people.
Once again, they all went there to the confluence of the Drona and the Arjuna rivers;
they all dwelt there happily, recounting the stories of Hari.
Gāṅgeya spoke again to these, beginning with Vṛkāyana:
"When will Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself, Hari manifest, appear? (44)
"When will he come for the sake of the sacrifice, and when shall we behold him?
All the people in these lands await this festival. (45)
O great sage Vṛkāyana, proceed toward Śrī Hari;
you ought to entreat him so that the sacrifice may take place quickly. 46.
Thus addressed, the divine Vṛkāyana, possessed of perfection, quickly restrained his vital breaths through meditative absorption and ascended to the aperture of Brahmā.
He departed by means of yoga itself and arrived at Āśvasārasa;
having bowed to Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, he requested that which was in his heart.
Having heard this, the Blessed One said: "In the bright fortnight of the month of Śrāvaṇa, the sacrifice should be commenced on the fifth day and brought to completion on the eleventh. (49)
Then, one should indeed travel through all regions and from place to place among kings during the month of Bhādrapada and during the dark fortnight of Āśvina.
Go to those various regions and make it known in such a way that the people and subjects may know the time for the sacrifice. ||51||
O descendant of Gaṅgā, having gathered the necessary materials, prepare them;
take this Sudarśana discus with you and proceed toward me. (52)
Dispatch them by way of the sky in all directions to those regions;
having wandered there repeatedly, let them rest upon whatever spot of ground they may find.
A sacrifice must be performed there; therefore, prepare that site.
And that place shall be illuminated again by day by means of a celestial chariot. (54)
Having circled through the path of the sky, cause it to be manifested;
I shall [do so] by way of the celestial chariot on the third day of the month of Śrāvaṇa.
On the bright lunar day, having taken [the image] together with the gods, the family members, the great sages, and the Śaktis, I shall indeed arrive after midday.
Thus commanded by Sudarśana, the illustrious great sage,
through his yogic power, suddenly reached the confluence of the Drona and the ocean.
In the morning, he went and related the auspicious news to everyone;
those sixty boys became joyful upon hearing of the arrival of Acyuta.
Having performed their morning rites with all kinds of musical instruments and hymns of praise,
they all ascended the celestial chariot as an auspicious omen.
Accompanied by Sudarśana according to the previously mentioned sequence, they went forth through the sky, proclaiming [the truth] for the purpose of determining the sacrificial ground.
Having once caused the great wheel to revolve and surveyed the stages of existence,
he displayed his own orb of splendor, resembling the sun.
The thousand-spoked [wheel], extremely difficult to perceive yet slightly visible to those possessing spiritual luster, produced a great wonder within the hearts of the people. (62)
He aroused curiosity and established a divine appearance;
thus, when this wandering had occurred, the subjects became greatly distressed.
And again, in order to see that wheel, he [ascended] the celestial chariot (vimāna) which possessed the brilliance of the sun;
then the wheel, by means of that same chariot, returned to the earth.
He spread forth swiftly to determine [the truth], producing a clear happiness;
he descended into the tranquility at the union of the seat of the supreme goal.
In the northern land, beautifully adorned with forests of elixir (rāsāyana),
on a level ground situated in the very center of all regions.
Beholding the descent of Śrī Hari’s Sudarśana upon the earth,
the great sages brought their celestial chariot down there at the confluence.
Vṛkāyana, Nīlakaṇa, Yavakrīta, and others likewise,
having rested and beheld that divine, delightful ground worthy of sacrifice, [proceeded].
Gāṅgeya and the others praised him and became filled with joy;
then they proceeded to proclaim the venue, the date, and the sacrifice.
In the celestial chariot in the sky, there arose songs of praise accompanied by musical instruments,
performed in the order of circumambulation preceded by the sounding of conch shells.
Sounding drums and singing hymns of praise:
"Hare Kṛṣṇa! Bāla Kṛṣṇa! Ramā Kṛṣṇa! Hare Hare! (7.1)
"O Padmajā-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Hari!"—
thus they cried out repeatedly at various places along the way.
They proclaim the sacrifice, as well as the auspicious place and the day;
this seven-day Vaiṣṇava sacrifice is Vedic and dedicated to all the deities.
In the vast expanse where the Niṣṭhā and Parā rivers meet,
at the site established by the sages who had performed their austerities, situated between two rivers.
The Blessed One, Śrīpati, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), will arrive here;
and Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa himself will also come.
On the third day of the bright fortnight of the month of Śrāvaṇa, at the time following midday, the Lord [revealed] Śrī Hari from the region of His navel.
From the field known as Kuṅkumavāpī, he will come by means of a celestial chariot,
accompanied by gods, sages, and ancestors, and joined by the beloved wife of Brahmā.
On the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Śrāvaṇa, at the very dawn,
he will commence the sacrifice that purifies all embodied beings.
The conclusion of the sacrifice will take place there on the eleventh day;
all the subjects, as well as the kings and householders, are invited. (79)
"Let men and women of all castes come together to this great sacrifice;
let them behold the Lord of the Gods of gods and make their birth fruitful."
May they accept the offerings of the sacrifice, may they worship the Lord, may they listen to the divine, auspicious stories, and may they purify their lineages. 8.1.
Let them all worship that Blessed One, Kṛṣṇa by name, who is directly manifest;
let everyone partake of the sacrificial food during the seven-day festival. (82)
May they in every way bring to fruition this divine opportunity that has been attained;
indeed, may they receive the Vaiṣṇava mantras from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa himself. 83.
May they wear purifying garlands born of tulasī;
may they chant the name of Śrī Hari and become divine in form. (84)
"Let the illustrious ones come to the sacrifice dedicated to Nārāyaṇa; indeed, no sacrifice such as this has ever existed before, nor will there ever be another like it. (85)
And at the sacrifice, those dwelling in every abode will arrive:
millions of liberated souls, millions of lords, millions of gods, and human beings. (86)
The sages, the ancestors, the yakṣas, the gandharvas, and likewise the rākṣasas;
the trees, the sacred fords, the principles, the mountains, and likewise the earths. ||87||
All the hosts of embodied and disembodied beings will assemble at the sacrifice,
as well as the wish-fulfilling creepers, the cows that grant all desires, the supernatural powers, and the ascetics.
The yogins, the perfected beings (siddhapuruṣas), and likewise the powers (śaktis) who are women—all these shall come here; let them behold that great sacrifice. 89.
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Svāmī Kṛṣṇa, Bāla Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare! Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Svāmin, Hare Hare! (2.166.90)
O Lord of Rādhā and Lakṣmī! O Lord of Haṃsā, Ramā, and Padmāvatī!
O Lord of Māṇikī, Śrī, Mañjulā, and Sadguṇā! O Lord of Śrī! 91.
O Lord of the beloved of Brahmā, O Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare! O Hari-Kṛṣṇa, O Svāmī-Kṛṣṇa, O Bālaka-Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare! (92)
May there be victory for Hari here, and may there be victory for all living beings;
may there be an increase in happiness alone, and may there be prosperity that is forever imperishable.
May there be health for all lands, and may there be devotion to the Supreme Lord;
may they meditate upon the Supreme Lord and attain the supreme goal. 94.
May they attain both worldly enjoyment and liberation through the grace of Nārāyaṇa;
indeed, having surely assembled at this sacrifice, may they be fully satisfied. (95)
May the devotees there be purifiers, fit for liberation, and auspicious refuges; may they be intent on giving and fire-offerings, and partakers of the sacrificial portions. (96)
May kings and royal circles, guilds of merchants and the common people, children and women, and the elderly, all receive the benefit of the sacrificial rite. (97)
Thus, O Rādhikā, having circled seven times over Ketumāla, the celestial chariot repeatedly proclaimed this in the sky.
In the western region beyond the Urals, reaching as far as the shores of the ocean, the proclamation of Kṛṣṇa has indeed been set forth in all lands. (99)
Then the celestial chariot descended in a peaceful place where people had gathered,
to the east of Prapīṭhā and to the west of Nīpara.
"May the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa be victorious forever!
As they were thus uttering these words, they descended, accompanied by Sudarśana.
Those great sages rested in the vast forest during that godless night;
then, those descendants of Gaṅgā, beginning with Bāla and Bālādi, attained supreme peace.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Origin of the Gāṅgeyas and Their Names, Vṛkāyana’s Arrival at the Kuṅkumavāpikā Field, the Invitation of Hari, Vṛkāyana’s Journey to Ketumāla with Sudarśana, the Determination of Kratusthalī as shown by Sudarśana’s Steadfastness, and the Proclamation of the Sacrifice," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā, to what happened afterwards; I shall tell you:
the Lord of Lords, the Master Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who is without beginning. || 1 ||
He dispatched Lomaśa and other great sages skilled in sacrifice,
as well as the eternal great sage Śvetavyāsa, who was devoted to his wife.
And likewise Sanatkumāra, Gaṇeśa, Jātavedas, Satrāyaṇa, Gālava, and also Svīyaprakāśa. (3)
Śatānanda, Nārada, Bṛhaspati the preceptor of the gods, Īśāna Mahādeva, and the venerable sage Kapila. || 4 ||
Śuka, Vallabhamuni, Vāmana, Suratāyana,
Hemanta, Devaprakāśa, and also the sacrificial implements.
On the day of the first lunar tithi, after midday, he sent all those sages together to the celestial chariot.
They had reached the further shore of perfection, where Vṛkāyana and others reside;
Yavakrīta and the rest then offered them a welcome.
They honored Lomaśa and the other great sages who had arrived with cries of victory and with offerings such as the madhuparka.
Having caused his celestial chariot to descend to the earth along with [the other] chariot,
Gāṅgeya, Yavakrīta, and the others honored him with great reverence.
Then Viśvakarman and Devāyatana, the two preeminent artisans, met there on that very day at the command of Hari. 2.167.10.
Having rested and taken their meal, they then prepared the clearing of the ground,
the pavilions, the assembly halls for dharma, and the kitchens.
They constructed a sacrificial hall, a dwelling hall, and fire-offering halls;
they also built water-jar halls, storehouses, and auspicious pavilions for the great assembly.
He saw halls for the liberated, dwellings for those who have descended [to earth], temples of the deities,
halls for the sages, halls for the ancestors, and the excellent abodes of the yakṣas and rākṣasas.
And they established dwellings for both the insentient and the sentient beings all around,
within a region measuring one hundred krośas between the two rivers.
They constructed beautiful pavilions, furnished with all the honors appropriate for their respective guests;
meanwhile, Yavakrīta and the others also departed quickly for their own countries.
They brought the kings of those various lands, as well as the subjects, merchants, excellent devotees, men, women, and householders. (16)
All of them quickly brought the sacrificial ground by means of their celestial chariots;
listen, O Rādhikā, to the principal names of those who desired the sacrifice. (17)
The sovereign of the eastern regions, known by the name Uralaketu,
together with the sage Yavakrīta, was accompanied by sixty lakhs of subjects.
Accompanied by his family, along with wealth, grain, and prosperity,
and with the abundance of vehicles and mounts, he arrived for the sake of the sacrifice.
King Krathaka, together with his family and accompanied by a hundred thousand subjects, arrived along with the sage Romāyana and the Ruma people. (2.167.20)
King Pṛthu, accompanied by his family and ten thousand followers, arrived together with the sage Kṛpāsthala for the purpose of performing a sacrifice.
Likewise, King Uṣṭrāla together with Yugaśāvarṣin, as well as the king named Haṃkāra and the lord of the earth Jayakoṣṭhala. ||22||
Those three brothers, the kings, together with their families and accompanied by hundreds of thousands of subjects, arrived there for the sake of the sacrifice. ||23||
Then King Tīrāṇa, together with the sage Valgurāya and ten thousand men accompanied by their families, arrived for the sacrifice.
King Alvinara, accompanied by his family and ten thousand followers, came together with Girīśa for the sake of the sacrifice. ||25||
Then King Jinavardhana, together with his beloved wife Varṣiṇī and his household of five thousand subjects, went to perform a sacrifice.
Then King Alpaketu, together with the seer Āpyāyana and his family,
set out accompanied by ten thousand men.
King Jayakṛṣṇa Vabhūpati set out together with his own chosen preceptor,
accompanied by ten thousand men and his family.
In that sacrifice, King Pariśāna, accompanied by his family and ten lakhs of subjects, arrived together with the sage Pherunara. (29)
In that sacrifice, King Indurāya arrived together with the sage Parīja,
accompanied by his family and three thousand subjects.
Then King Gaṇḍaka, together with his family and five hundred subjects, arrived at the sacrifice along with the Ṛṣi Pūrtagaṇḍa. ||3 1||
Then King Nudrāṇḍa, accompanied by five hundred thousand subjects, approached Supāṇamuni like a householder. (32)
Accompanied by the fruit-eating sage, King Urṇa,
together with his family and two hundred thousand subjects, arrived at the sacrifice.
King Bṛhacchara, accompanied by Vallījīvana Muni and a thousand followers, came to the sacrifice like a householder.
Accompanied by the sage Jarāmauna, King Balalīna,
together with his family and ten lakhs of subjects, arrived at the sacrifice.
King Varasiṃha, together with his family and accompanied by a hundred thousand subjects, arrived at the sacrifice along with King Pālanādṛśin. (36)
Together with the sage Lāṭavāya, the king of Rājagṛha,
accompanied by his family and a thousand followers, came to the sacrifice.
At the sacrifice, King Phenatantu arrived together with Phālanādarśin;
accompanied by a thousand men, he came as a householder.
At the sacrifice, King Stokahoma, accompanied by his family and joined by a thousand men, arrived together with the sage Svādvadana.
At the sacrifice, King Kāṣṭhāyana, together with Nārada who was raining down arrows,
arrived accompanied by his family and five hundred subjects.
Together with the seer Lepanādarśin, King Kolaka,
accompanied by his family and a hundred attendants, arrived at the sacrifice.

And from the regions where the gifts were distributed, the King of Aṅga arrived, accompanied by his assembly of ministers, joined by a hundred thousand subjects, and bringing his entire household. 42.
And from the region of Śakunta, King Śākuntaka, accompanied by a hundred thousand subjects and his family, arrived there at the sacrifice. ||43||
Indeed, the subjects gathered for the sacrifice from the region of Āyasa,
and likewise, the subjects gathered from the regions of the northern continents.
They were endowed with celestial chariots, elephants, horses, carts, and palanquins,
as well as camels and bulls, and possessed gold, jewels, and wealth.
Accompanied by many articles of food and gifts, they arrived together with male and female servants, surrounded by their sons, daughters, and other kin.
And groups of couples all assembled there; they arrived with offerings suitable for sacrifice and with all necessary materials. ||47||
Those twenty-six kings, endowed with innumerable riches,
brought the collection of materials for the sake of the sacrifice, filled with great enthusiasm for the ritual.
Then they all arrived and presented various kinds of provisions to the sage Gālava, who was the presiding lord over them all.
Īśāna, the illustrious Mahādeva, the Vaiṣṇava Supreme Lord,
became at that time the presiding overseer of all sacrificial rites and the overseer of the universe.
For he indeed became the regulator of the arrangement of the pavilions and other structures;
and when the kings arrived there, they offered everything to Īśāna.
For each member of the royal class is capable of providing the expenditure for a sacrifice when acting as a patron; therefore, sacrifices are sought after by kings. (52)
"And let there be twenty-six in number, beautified by sacrificial pits.
Having heard these words of the assembly of kings, Vṛkāyana likewise [acted].
Likewise Lomaśa, Īśāna, Nīlākarṇa and others; Svayaṃprakāśa, Kapila, Devaprakāśaka, and others [are there]. (54)
The foremost ones took up their words; there, Viśvakarman, the divine architect, having received the command of the sages, constructed the sacrificial pits accordingly.
The twenty-seventh was the great Kuṇḍamūrdhnya, performed for the sake of the Blessed One; it was established as the foremost of all fire-sacrifices for the purpose of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. ||56||
There, nine types of sacrificial pits (kuṇḍas) were indeed fashioned by Viśvakarman,
all according to the rules of the Vedas and Ṛṣis, as well as the regulations for the various directions.
The sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) is lotus-shaped and called the Sarvatobhadra-altar;
likewise, the Sarvatobhadrikā altar is made square.
A vulva-shaped pit was also made, and a crescent-shaped pit was made;
there was also a triangular pit, as well as a circular pit. ||59||
There is also a hexagonal sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), as well as a six-petaled sacrificial pit;
likewise, there is an eight-cornered sacrificial pit and an eight-petaled sacrificial pit.
The pit for the teacher was prepared, as was the pit for the Rigvedic priest;
likewise, the pit for the Yajurvedic priest and the excellent pit for the Atharvavedic priest were prepared. ||61||
The Sāmavedi-altar and other altars were constructed;
likewise, the central altar and the side altars were built according to the prescribed rite.
Thus, having consecrated the ground accordingly within the pavilion,
one should prepare suitable and auspicious sacrificial pits and most beautiful altars.
And Viśvakarman also constructed divine temples and beautiful pavilions, splendidly adorned with lovely pillars and banners. (64)
Adorned with excellent archways and other features marked by the cardinal directions,
those two caused divine structures of magnificent splendor to be built for a distance of a hundred krośas.
Natural splendors, natural waters, cool and fragrant breezes, and natural garden lands; 66.
There were small celestial chariots, millions of lightning-chariots,
various swings, and likewise natural songs.
There are lakes and pools of cool and warm water, naturally fragrant with the essence of scents;
likewise, there are beds, vehicles, objects of enjoyment, as well as garlands and flowers.
The essence of oil is natural; everything is made by nature.
Is that heaven, or Satyaloka, or even Vaikuṇṭha itself? ||69||
There the suns are born of nature, and the moons are naturally radiant;
there the lakes and rivers flow, all born of nature.
Thus indeed is everything pertaining to the body— whether divine or innate—
ordained for kings, subjects, merchants, and ascetics alike.
For poor men, for women, and for eunuchs,
enjoyments, as well as garments, foods, drinks, and dwellings, are likewise objects to be enjoyed.
At that time, the divine realm is equal [to the Lord], born of eternal glory (nityavibhūti), fashioned as existence-consciousness-bliss (saccidānanda), and devoid of laughter and destruction. ||73||
And for the sake of milk, the wish-fulfilling cows (kāmadhenus) arrived there from Goloka;
there were streams of milk, streams of curd, streams of clarified butter, and streams of milk-rice porridge (pāyasa).
At that time, the milk, the essences of milk,
and the butters became divine and inexhaustible, as did the sacrificial offerings from the Infinite One.
The trees and creepers, as well as the wish-fulfilling vines (kalpalatās), brought forth honey;
they also produced countless essences of sugarcane, molasses, candied sugar, and refined sugar.
They led away from the endless wildernesses, forests, and gardens *gundra* plants, *gundrapāka* plants, fruits, and leaves. (77)
Then the divine medicinal herbs,
eager and excited, brought grains of rice, juices, sesame seeds, barley, excellent grains, and sacrificial fuel.
The clouds, the oceans, the sweet rivers, the streams, and the lakes carried forth, as their ultimate purpose, pleasant drinks that were naturally cool.
Śrī and Lakṣmī, the two wives of Śrī Hari, along with Bhū, Līlā, Abjā, and Vibhūti—
namely Ramā, Annapūrṇā, and Kamalā— brought mountains of sweet food.
Stems, clusters, bunches, thickets, stalks, and trunks, as well as creepers, grasses, and leaves, eventually brought forth flowers. (8.1)
Caverns, mines, mountains,
and chasms brought forth red chalk and variegated powders that served as the colors for saffron.
At the great festival of the sacrifice, Meru took all the vessels, Indra the coverings, and the deities the celestial chariots.
Vasava and Kubera gave various articles for the sacrifice; Himālaya, Arala, and others indeed gave precious gems and jewels.
The oceans and the regions of the islands gave pearls at the sacrifice;
the clouds then cast their shade, and the seasons became favorable.
All the Gandharvas, who were musicians, gave autumnal musical instruments;
and the kings gave male and female slaves and servants skilled in their duties.
At that time, during the sacrifice, parasols, chowries, and vehicles were present;
furthermore, multitudes of wish-fulfilling gems were accumulated in every house.
Whatever object they desire,
that very thing the divine drum of Śrī Hari gives them all, even as it dances and resounds repeatedly.
This [mantra] is like a drum at the end of an aeon, possessing the nature of the imperishable Brahman;
resembling a treasure-store for all who look to it, it even grants what is desired.
Whatever ornaments of garments, jewelry, and flowing materials were required for the sacrifice, the divine artisans indeed presented them immediately.
Thus, indeed, the infinity of all things is found therein, where the Goddess of Water herself was born in the form of essence (rasa). 91.
The Earth-goddess is of the nature of food; O Rādhikā, what is lacking there?
Indeed, this is by the will of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (92)
By the command of Him who dwells within, that [universe] quickly became a unified whole, including the sun, the moon, night, twilight, day, wind, and likewise the sky. (93)
Mādhava commanded Anala, Śravaṇa, the gods, the earth, the waters, the mountains, the clouds, Time, Vṛṣa, Māyā, and Ājñā. ||94||
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, [is present] everywhere and indeed instantly throughout all fourteen worlds. 95.
Let the people announce that the sacrifice is indeed being prepared;
let those eager for the rite go forth, taking the oblations with them to Ketumāla. (96)
Thus commanded, the residents of the site and the forest-dwellers were informed;
they brought there sacrificial offerings and gifts, excluding those belonging to the border regions.
Thus, O Rādhikā, in this sacrifice, countless multitudes of ritual materials had already been prepared beforehand by the great sages, who are indeed inconceivable.
The twenty-six rulers of the earth were struck with great wonder: "Oh, the majesty of the Lord cannot be measured! (99)
They became free from pride and understood their own resources to be meager;
by reading and hearing this, O Rādhā, one obtains the fruit of sacrifice.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Arrival of the Sages headed by Lomaśa, as well as Viśvakarman, the Devas, the Kings of Ketumāla, and the Subjects, at the Sacrificial Ground, and the Presentation of the Pavilions, Fire-pits, Oblation Materials, and Other Requisites," in the second section (Tretā-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā; I am myself the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa.
I immediately called to mind my own attendant named Akṣara.
The Imperishable Lord arrived there at the site of Kuṅkumavāpikā;
having bowed down, Hari stood before him and gave him the auspicious command of the sacred revelation.
"A great sacrifice will take place in Ketumāla"— thus [he wrote] a letter,
rich with saffron, which bestowed wealth for the purpose of inviting all created beings.
"Dispatch me quickly with divine attendants; do not delay!
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One gave him that letter accordingly.
May the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa be ever victorious! At the meeting of the supreme Niṣṭhā, she is present in Ketumāla along with her great-grandsons.
On the fifth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Śrāvaṇa, he will perform a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice, a rite desired by all;
therefore, those residing in the three worlds must come there with reverence.
May we receive the arrival of guests and may they recognize our attainment;
on the eleventh day, there shall be a full oblation accompanied by joyful festivals.
The incarnations, the lords, the ancestors, the seers and deities, all humans, the descendants of Kaśyapa, and those dwelling in the netherworlds and elsewhere—[all these were present]. (8)
May the immobile and mobile beings also come happily to the sacrifice;
as well as Lomaśa, Yavakrīta, Kapila, and Bṛhaspati. (9)
The venerable Sanatkumāra, King Uralaketu,
and Īśāna— these we respectfully announce.
"Those who dwell in the world of living beings, in the world of Īśa, and in the world of Brahmā—all of them must come; I say this even of Nārāyaṇa. (11)
Having made a vow three times upon the leaf, Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa spoke again: "Let everyone indeed come to the sacrifice."
On the third day of the sacrifice, I shall go from the Kuṅkumavāpikā field to the sacrificial arena; you all must also attend that sacrifice at that time.
May the attendants residing in all abodes and the female attendants who are Śaktis come on the previous day for the purpose of service to Mahāmānasī.
In this manner, the Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself dispatched millions of such letters to all the worlds.
And through the space of consciousness, the elemental space, as well as Māyā, Mahākāla, and Dharma, indeed by these gateways in all creations. || 16 ||
O Rādhikā, at the beginning of creation, there was a union, a connection, a meeting, and a communion among all principles and all worlds and their inhabitants, like that of a family.
In this matter, there is no cause for wonder that these [gates] take the form of doorways;
for I too have come from Goloka along with you.
Seeing the letters, all the Nārāyaṇas went there,
and all the people of the created world arrived there, filled with affection.
Then, the multitudes of people’s celestial chariots were seen in the sky from all directions as they approached the sacrificial ground.
From every direction and from afar, there arrived ten million billion trillion beings;
as many were the liberated ones, so many were the attendants and others.
