"May he be our father, kinsman, well-wisher, friend, protector, and guardian"—
with these words, they then accepted this mantra of self-surrender.
Then those sages, O Rādhā, having bowed to the venerable sage Lomaśa, inquired about the duties of protection; thereupon Lomaśa spoke.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama,
will himself proclaim all the duties worthy of the virtuous.
Then, thereafter, the queen, the consort of the king, [shall receive] the initiation of the virtuous woman (sādhvī-dīkṣā).
There, on the bank of the lake, he indeed took hold of the auspicious Rādhikā.
Then many virtuous women undertook initiation;
indeed, that became the Tīrtha of Initiation, the Tīrtha of the Virtuous, and the Tīrtha of the Chaste Women.
Then, five hundred male ascetics and five hundred female ascetics likewise went with Lomaśa to the auspicious and glorious abode of Bālakṛṣṇa.
Having all gone there, both men and women, they sat down after honoring the virtuous teachings from the mouth of Hari, and indeed listened to what was being questioned.
The subtle body resides within the gross body, while latent impressions reside within the subtle body;
life resides within the latent impressions, and the state of being a witness resides within life.
In the state of being a witness lies freedom from the qualities (nirguṇya); in freedom from the qualities lies the absence of taint;
in the absence of taint lies steadfastness in Brahman; and in the state of Brahman lies liberation.
Upon liberation, there shall be supreme bliss produced by the Supreme Brahman;
thus, having ascended the tenfold altar, one enjoys bliss.
The virtuous should always practice tenfold concentration;
they should bring the body under control through austerity and restraint.
Through endurance, forgiveness, virtuous conduct, and constant service, one must achieve mastery over the subtle senses by means of cultivating fortitude. (2.1)
Through the non-engagement with sense objects, through the mind’s non-grasping, as well as through discernment, investigation, and constant tranquility of mental activity; ||22||
Therefore, the destruction of latent impressions (vāsanā) must always be accomplished through lack of desire, by means of non-recollection, by the final recollection, and over a long duration. (23)
Life is the movement of the vital breaths, arising from the non-separation from the fruits of action;
[it is sustained] by the offering of the fruits to Kṛṣṇa and by the restraint of the vital breaths.

By taking only what is necessary for sustenance, one should repeatedly perform the restraint of the vital breaths (prāṇāyāma) through methods such as the "bad pot" (kumbhaka) and thereby abandon the defects of the vital breaths. || 25 ||

One who is endowed with selflessness (nirmamatā) should abandon the sense of being a witness to pleasure and pain, as well as one's own pride regarding what is "one's own"; thus, one is also said to be without ego (nirahaṃkāra). //26//
For witnesshood exists when there is no concern for one's own interest; how could there be witnesshood when acting for the sake of another?
Thus, by abandoning the sense of "I" and "mine," the ascetic should conquer the state of being a witness.
Then, through contact with his qualities (guṇas), there arise states that cause pleasure, pain, and delusion;
likewise, there are illumination, activity, and restraint, as well as cold, heat, and the intermediate state. (28)
Since they are not born, he alone has attained freedom from the modes;
for the offering of the modes to Kṛṣṇa results in freedom from the modes even while remaining within them.

That reflection which is performed with the mind when offered to Kṛṣṇa does not create attachment; likewise, that contemplation performed with the consciousness when offered to Kṛṣṇa certainly does not create attachment. (2.273.30)
O Kṛṣṇa, awakening through the intellect when offered unto You does not cause bondage; likewise, the identification with the ego-sense when offered unto You does not cause bondage. (3.1)
Therefore, mere observation does not at all cause defilement;
rather, it is meditation, latent impression, or even mental refinement that is directed toward Hari. (32)
One who applies ointment attains divinity all the more, yet he is not devoid of qualities;
likewise, when everything is offered, everything becomes devoid of qualities through union with Hari.
This must certainly be performed here by virtuous men and virtuous women in every way,
provided that no lapse has occurred through the qualities of *māyā* and that [the ritual] is not deprived of its fruits and other benefits.
The state of Brahman, steadfastness in Brahman, conduct like that of Brahman, and abiding therein—these arise in every way for the virtuous one, who is at all times equal to the Imperishable. (35)
Indeed, creations arise and dissolve within the syllables;
in Brahman, there is neither contact with creation nor even contact with māyā.
Therefore, for him there is no bondage at all; for contact with illusion is indeed bondage.
And for the virtuous one who is free from illusion, there is the constant absence of dualities. (37)
Direct realization and immediate perception arise only within the conscious Self;
and through that immediate experience, all that is false is dissolved. (38)
By that, there is the destruction of defects, the cessation of activity, the destruction of the connection with fruits, and the destruction of all suffering and so forth. ||39||
When a virtuous person here becomes one whose sole delight is in the Self alone, he is indeed liberated and is called such even while living. (2.273.40)
For one who practices in such a manner, the bliss of Brahman arises, for that person who has always attained their own self as being of the nature of Brahman in this very world. 41.
Indeed, identity with Brahman is fully attained by the mind;
a supreme identity, as it were, arises [between them]. (42)
Just as the tongue, though distinct from honey, perceives the taste of honey, and just as the eye, situated within its orb, perceives the form of an object; ||42||
Just as the mind perceives what is situated within and what is distant,
so too does the intellect, directed toward the Self, arise as the knower of the supreme Self.
Furthermore, the knower of itself arises with a range that exceeds its own self;
likewise, the Self is self-luminous, it is the knower of itself, and it illuminates itself. 45.
Endowed with its own self-luminosity, the Self makes Kṛṣṇa—who is conjoined with it—manifest;
Kṛṣṇa makes this [Self] manifest; thus they manifest one another. 46.
When two manifestations are unified, a kind of identity arises;
through the identity with the commonality of their qualities, the possessors of those qualities attain such a nature. (47)
In this manner, through the process of the descent of the divine being, the state of identity with the Supreme Brahman arises for both the virtuous practitioner and the Supreme Self. 48.
Through the state of being the self of the Supreme Brahman, one partakes in the bliss of Brahman;
this indeed is the yoga of ten limbs, the truly virtuous and eternally supreme dharma. (49)
This state, which is to be served by the most virtuous and which dwells within the Supreme Brahman, has been described;
it consists of both self-luminosity and other-luminosity, provided there exists no further state beyond it.
Excluding intrinsic nature, that which is other-natured is the supreme state to be realized;
such a practitioner is one known as "without cognitive awareness" (asamprajñāta). ||51||
He is celebrated in the Vedas and scriptures as being the very nature of Nārāyaṇa;
likewise as Sanatkumāra, Śambhu, and Śeṣanārāyaṇa. ||52||
This great sage Lomaśa and these others are considered Nārāyaṇas;
likewise, all those such as Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and Ramā are beloved of Brahmā.
Garuḍa and the others are my vehicles; all these are Nārāyaṇas.
The entire city of Kuṅkumavāpī is my Nārāyaṇī. 54.
But here, liberated, virtuous, and equanimous holy men and women abide;
they dwell as my playful manifestations, whose very nature is the Supreme Brahman. 55.
Indeed, some of my thousands of qualities exist right here;
indeed, some of my sovereign powers and spiritual accomplishments exist right here.
Some among these are indeed my divine ornaments; some among these are indeed my powers (śaktis) born from my own form.
Some things here are indeed my splendors, my lusters, and my radiances; some things here are indeed the various objects of enjoyment that belong to me.
This entire Kuṅkumavāpī is my very instrument;
it exists as my entire form—untainted, beyond qualities, and supreme.
This earth is indeed of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, dwelling in the abode of Brahman;
it is the abode of Brahman, O holy ones, and my own body.
Thus, by always contemplating and meditating upon your own true nature as being identical with the Supreme Brahman, you shall attain the highest bliss. 61.
Thus have I here declared to you these sublime and subtle dharmas, which are accessible through wisdom; for such are the virtuous ones considered to be. (62)
The virtuous ones said:
"O Blessed One, the subtle dharmas have indeed been understood by us from you here;
but what are the gross dharmas like, and how are they to be protected? Tell us, O Lord. (63)
The Supreme Brahman said:
Whether it be a man or a woman, when one is established in the state of goodness, then indeed the defects of the body must be abandoned and its virtues alone should be embraced in this world. (64)
Always at dawn, having abandoned laziness, negligence, and sloth, one should become alert and,
acting with haste, perform the bath during the Brāhma-muhūrta.
One should indeed perform the purification of the body with water, ashes, wind, or by sweeping, as well as by anointing with oil and other substances.
One should always practice internal meditation on the Blessed One as the highest form of purity;
thereafter, one should indeed perform the worship of Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who is Hari. (67)
Likewise, one should perform the worship of Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Gaṇeśa, Lakṣmī, and Sūrya,
as well as the honoring of holy men, the waving of lights (ārārtika), and the offering of food (naivedya).
One should perform hymns of praise, the chanting of the Lord's names, and the turning of garlands;
how indeed could one perform [worldly] discourse for Hari? One should indeed practice begging for alms and the cooking of food.
One should perform the sacrifice to beings, the sacrifice to the gods, and the sacrifice to the ancestors;
having performed the sacrifice to Brahman and the sacrifice to men, one should then partake of food.
In the evening, one should perform the auspicious ninefold worship of Śrī Hari;
with faith and as is appropriate, one should practice all that leads to well-being.
One who follows the dharma of the virtuous should subsist with contentment, gentleness, and non-possessiveness; such a person should practice neither excessive eating nor extreme austerity.
One should not practice improper conduct, nor should one do what ought not to be done; one should indeed avoid affliction, violence, falsehood, censure, and speaking ill of others. (73)
One should perform service to others through body, mind, and speech;
for the sake of the happiness of others, one should practice what is beneficial and conducive to well-being. (74)
One should especially establish the path of the waters and the path of liberation;
for the sake of destroying the sins of others, one should always be a source of refuge. (75)
He should bestow my mantras upon him and grant me initiation;
he should perform the study of the scriptures and impart the liberating knowledge, and likewise he himself should listen to it. (76)
One may also wander to sacred fords (tīrthas) and take pure food;
one should drink pure water and strained milk and other such liquids. (77)
One who contemplates Brahman should never at any time give way to passion, craving, pride, or greed; indeed, he should not show contempt toward anyone.
One should certainly not practice deception, nor should one ever harbor hatred;
one should give gifts according to one's ability, including the gift of liberation and the gift of fearlessness.
One should cultivate affection and devotion toward those who have taken refuge [in the Lord], which leads to liberation;
for the virtuous are purifiers, and association with the good is also purifying. (2.273.80)
Always, during my own assembly, having invited embodied beings, one should purify them with supreme devotion and send them to my abode. 8.1.
One should withdraw the senses, the internal organs, and so forth into the heart;
one should constantly perform meditation upon me and accumulate the bliss of Brahman. ||82||
One should effect the state of being dissolved into my form, which is the highest duty;
and one should perform daily worship consisting of meditation upon me. ||83||
Thus should you virtuous men abide and act according to my instruction;
likewise, the virtuous women here must also practice service toward the holy ones. (84)
For women, the constant granting of liberation, the imparting of knowledge, instruction, and the initiation of virtuous men and women shall lead to emancipation. (85)
One should not engage in vices or those actions that obstruct liberation;
for I am Nārāyaṇa, the eternal husband of virtuous women and the righteous. 86.
I am to be served through the dharma of devotion to one's husband;
by offering yourself to me, eternal happiness shall be attained.
"But you must enjoy [the fruits] together with me, for our union is divine;
I am never to be abandoned by you at any time or in any activity. (88)
Thus, O virtuous ones who are the refuge of auspiciousness, this living liberation has been described by me as consisting of divine dharma and as bestowing supreme liberation. 89.
The bodily functions must indeed be maintained by the virtuous as is appropriate;
they should not be pursued in excess, for they are of the nature of obstacles to my service.
"May there be well-being for you, O virtuous men; may there also be well-being for you, O virtuous women.
Having spoken thus, O Rādhikā, the Lord Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa [departed]. (9.1)
Then the virtuous ones ceased [speaking] and performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) with offerings;
they sang together, saying, "May you be protected and liberated. (92)
Having taken the blessings, they went from the shore of the lake to their own abodes;
meanwhile, Nārada, who had gone to Kāśī, arrived before Hari.
Then, together with his teacher who held an auspicious letter, he eagerly performed the *daṇḍavat* prostration to Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa.
Having bowed to his father and mother, he uttered a blessing;
Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods, having offered salutations and received honor, did the same. (95)
Having offered a welcome with the honey-mixture (madhuparka) and other honors, and having inquired after his welfare,
he paid homage for the sake of the happiness of Śiveśvara and his daughter Lakṣmī.
Having given Rādhikā a leaf encircled with saffron thread and adorned with jewels, he reported the auspicious news. 97.
He always offered auspiciousness and the moment of the union with Lakṣmī on the fourth day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa. (98)
Having increased that leaf-offering and having worshipped Bṛhaspati,
Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa there also worshipped Nārada.

Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-third chapter, titled "The Description of how the Beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa bestowed mantra-initiation, spiritual knowledge, and instruction upon the saintly men and women in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*; and how Bṛhaspati, accompanied by Nārada and carrying an auspicious letter sent from Kāśī by Śiveśvara, arrived at Kuṅkumavāpī and presented that letter. || 273 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, having seen the letter, Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa rejoiced; He bowed to Bṛhaspati and placed a jeweled necklace around his neck.
Bṛhaspati observed the birth-day of that Hari on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the lunar month of Kārtika.
The birth of Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa from the womb of Satī Śrī Kambharā occurred; his age was fourteen years, one month, and six days.
The appointed time has passed; today is the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, the day designated for the acceptance of the marriage proposal.
And from here, on the fifth day, on the fourth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, during an exceedingly auspicious moment, the festival shall take place in Kāśī. || 5 ||
Likewise, the letter conveys most auspicious news:
"I have been sent by the Lord Śiveśvara along with this letter."
Everything shall become auspicious and fortunate, and Gopālakṛṣṇa shall be supreme.
Gopālakṛṣṇa, having beheld the divine sage Lomaśa, the muni... || 7 ||
He summoned him quickly, and that sage arrived there; having been shown respect and having performed worship of the gods and his gurus, he sat upon an auspicious seat.
He sat down and inquired after the welfare of Bṛhaspati;
he then examined the letter given by Gopāla Kṛṣṇa.
Lomaśa caused her, who had offered praise to Nārada, to recite [the auspicious verses]; he also made me hear the auspicious words and increased [her merit].
Bālakṛṣṇa rejoiced, and Kaṃbhārā rejoiced greatly;
the members of the household were filled with joy upon hearing that letter concerning the yoga. || 11 ||
And all those who were dear to Brahmā, having heard this, attained supreme joy; Pārvatī, Hārītī, Śakti, Amā, and the others likewise experienced great delight.
Then Gopālakṛṣṇa played musical instruments and gave auspicious sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) as a reward to his preceptor.
He fed him milk-rice that was very sweet according to the prescribed rite,
and thereafter he gradually honored him with sandalwood paste and other offerings.
The Lord Gopālakṛṣṇa questioned the sage Nārada regarding the qualities and characteristics of a maiden; Nārada then spoke concerning the maiden.
The god Śaṅkara, a portion of Brahmā, shines as the Lord of Śivā;
and Mahālakṣmī is indeed Pārvatī, the great devotee of the Lord.
For both are portions of Nārāyaṇa, most venerable and most excellent;
they are honored by all the worlds, most weighty, and supreme lords.
Their daughter was Lakṣmī herself, the destroyer of suffering and poverty;
she was the most excellent among maidens and women, and exceedingly beautiful. (18)
What praise can I possibly offer, especially for the daughter of Śambhu? She is delightful and exceedingly beautiful, and among beautiful women, she is honored as the very embodiment of Ramā.
Her youth has now blossomed; she is indeed a treasure-house of all prosperity, the supreme sovereign lady adorned with thousands of marks of Lakṣmī.
She has the luster of the color of a yellow campaka flower, adorned with jewel ornaments;
like a flash of lightning, she is graced with the playful charm of a smiling glance. ||21||
Possessing the luster of molten gold, blazing with splendor,
she is divine in limb and divine in essence, always endowed with pure being.
Truthful, compassionate, and virtuous, she was an ascetic devoted to the vow of Hari;
she was peaceful, self-controlled, auspicious, and a treasury of infinite generosity. (23)
Her forehead was adorned with svastikas and hidden golden lines;
it was enchanting with curved, long lashes that were golden at the tips and black at the edges.
She was resplendent with shimmering hair upon her head that possessed a radiant luster,
and she bore a broad, beautiful tilaka mark as lovely as a streak of gold.
Bearing the natural moon upon her forehead, she truly shines;
is she Rādhā, or Kamalā, or Māṇikī, or perhaps Arkajā? 26.
She is Pārvatī, Sāramā, or Sarasvatī Śāradā;
she is Vairājī, Vāsudevī, Nārāyaṇī, or Sadāśivā. ||27||
Whether she be Padmā, or Virajā, or Sāvitrī, or Vaiṣṇavī;
or Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, Candrāṇī, or Rohiṇī. ||28||
Is she Kubera’s wife, the consort of the Sun, Svāhā, or Vāhalyikā?
Is she the Sky itself, or perhaps the power of Brahmā, or even Śīlikā herself? (29)
Or rather, whatever other charming and excellent women there may be, they all do not equal even a sixteenth part of Śiva’s daughter.
Rich with the splendor of the autumnal full moon, with eyes like autumnal lotuses—your form is identical to that of your son; has he entered into her body? (3.1)
She is a young woman fit for marriage, exceedingly beautiful;
she possesses a divine body and is devoid of any material elements. (32)
She is indeed Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇī, whose very nature is that of Bālakṛṣṇa;
I consider this Supreme Brahman to shine forth, having manifested in two forms. ||33||
What indeed is there to be described here? For she is Hari herself in visible form; O Gopālakṛṣṇa, your son is the fortunate Lord himself.
She who is celebrated under the name Puruṣottama in all creations—she is this very Śrī Lakṣmī, the Puruṣottamī, whose every limb is a portion of Him. (35)
Manifested here in this world by Bālakṛṣṇa, she bestows liberation upon men;
she is the Mother of the Universe and the Mother of All—how then can I possibly describe her here? (36)
Listen to all the signs by which she may be recognized as being such, or what kind she is, or who she is herself; for that which is beyond [these] must not be determined. (37)
Having heard which, people undoubtedly attain liberation;
I describe those divine states of the Guru as they were perceived by me through divine vision. (38)
In the heart of Śivakanyā resides the auspicious form of Bālakṛṣṇa;
on her two feet, there are beautiful and auspicious lotus-marks and upward-pointing lines. (39)
On her hips there is a line like an arrow; on her forehead is the shape of a crown;
and on the right side of her cheek, a crimson dot shines beautifully.
On the chest is the Viṣṇurekhā, on the left arm the auspicious mace,
on the left thigh the sandal, and the Vaijayantī garland is situated upon the heart.
In her hand there is a lotus, and likewise another mark of an elephant;
on her right foot there is the mark of a conch, a boat, and a celestial chariot;
as well as a mace, a fish, a temple pinnacle, a large fish, and a betel vine.
On the left foot, there are lines of barley, a temple, and an umbrella;
also vertical lines, a lotus, a banner, a goad, and a jar;
as well as a water-lily, a bilva fruit, a land-lotus, and the moon. (43)
The ten fingers were adorned with full circles and golden lines;
on his forehead was a golden necklace and dots of golden lines. (44)
The *bindu* is on the chin; the lines of the hand are above the right breast;
the *cakra* is on the left breast; the necklace is on the throat; and the golden ornament is on the chest. 45.
A banner, a fish, and a flute, as well as a svastika, are on the right hand;
a bow, a fish, and a jar are also present on the right hand. (46)
On the right side, there are a wall, a gateway, and a lotus;
likewise, a horse with the extent of a foot and a serpent's hood, as well as a plow and an elephant.
There is a tree, a sacrificial post, and likewise an arrow and a javelin on the feet;
on the hand there is a garland-line, a lamp-line, and a fly-whisk. (48)
Indeed, she possesses auspicious marks such as the Śoḷa, the Kuṇḍala, the Vedī, and the Cakra;
she also has other beautiful and pure signs.
No other woman like her has been seen in the three worlds except for Kamalā;
indeed, no such marks as these exist anywhere except in Śrī.
This son of Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Lord himself;
he knows all that has occurred regarding you, and he constantly goes there to offer worship. (51)
He accepts what is done by her, and likewise what is done by his parents;
yet Hari himself remains here like one ignorant, even while manifesting his divine power (māyā).
The king of sages named Hemaśālāyana knows this;
and Hanumān also knows the penance of Lakṣmī for the sake of Hari.
Then Bālakṛṣṇa granted a boon for his own yogic purpose;
all this is auspicious, as everything has been offered to Nārāyaṇa through Lakṣmī.
O Gopālarāja, behold this preceptor of the gods, Bṛhaspati,
who has brought a letter to your house for this auspicious and momentous task.
Since the lords of the gods worship the lotus-feet of one who has come here, your house—blessed, meritorious, and glorious—is purified by that very fact. (56)
"Oh, I consider my fortune to be great, for I am steadfastly engaged in milking the cows and possess the good fortune of witnessing this festival of the union of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa. (57)
I shall exist and dwell forever on the banks of the Aśvapaṭṭa;
I shall serve the illustrious Puruṣottama, the lord of innumerable consorts.
With pure devotion, I shall cause that Bālakṛṣṇa to hear these songs;
and during festivals, I shall always wander together with the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
This indeed is the fulfillment of birth: that one may attain union with Hari in this world;
by whatever disposition one may be, the Supreme Lord is to be worshipped.
O Gopālakṛṣṇa, you are blessed; blessed is Śiva, the benefactor;
blessed is Kambharā-Lakṣmī; and blessed is the goddess Pārvatī.
Blessed is the Kuṅkumavāpī pond, and blessed is the land of Vārāṇasī;
blessed also is Bṛhaspati, and blessed is the celestial sage Nārada.
For those in whose heart and eyes Śrī Narāyaṇa dwells,
that fourth day shall be blessed and worthy of worship by all.
Future incarnations will also celebrate a festival here;
on that day, a maiden offered as a gift shall become equal to Lakṣmī.
Having spoken thus, Nārada observed silence, and Bṛhaspati likewise;
thereafter, they both took rest in the abode of peace.
Then the venerable sage Nārada went to the abode of Bālakṛṣṇa in order to inform Kṛṣṇa of that divine secret which had been spoken by Lakṣmī.
The Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, too, being anxious to understand what Lakṣmī had said, waited, thinking, "When will Nārada speak that which is dear to my heart? (67)
At that moment, the illustrious Nārada arrived there at Kṛṣṇa’s palace;
having bowed to the glorious Bālakṛṣṇa, he said with a smile, "Obeisance to the Blessed One! (68)
Having uttered this and rejoiced, he indeed sat down upon the ground;
at that moment, the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa quickly raised him up.
He seated that celestial sage upon his own golden couch;
placing the great muni upon his chest, he embraced him with joy.
He inquired after Lakṣmī’s welfare: "Tell me, Nārada, what is in her heart? What happiness does she dwell in, and how much has she been filled with joy on my account? (7.1)
What did the daughter of Śiva say while reflecting upon me?
Or what secret did she reveal to me? (72)
"O Nārada, tell me quickly that which I desire to know and which brings happiness.
Thus addressed, O Rādhā, Nārada, desiring to speak, was filled with great joy. (73)
He spoke everything according to the rules, exactly as told by the daughter of Śiva:
"Listen, O Hari-Kṛṣṇa; she who seeks you is dwelling in happiness. (74)
When I went to Kāśī, to the auspicious bank of the Varaṇā, in a delightful garden area near the temple of Śiveśvara. (75)
Then, in that beautiful temple of Viṣṇu filled with golden jars,
she was joined by her mother, her sister, and Kṛṣṇā.
She had come for the purpose of seeing you, and having bowed to Viṣṇu,
she was moving swiftly in circumambulation, beautiful in her graceful movement.
I beheld you with Lakṣmī as your half-body, distinguished by bodily marks;
at that time, I was indeed a boy of wondrous form. ||78||
He who was his equal in age, with whom he had remained engaged in childhood play, [was led] by her to the palace under the pretext of circumambulation. (79)
And Bālakṛṣṇa repeatedly spoke with speed, saying, "Abhrama!
as well as "Aśvapaṭṭasara" and "Śiveśvarasuta. At that time, she indeed heard these words from my mouth.
He questioned me: "Salutations to you, O youth; from where have you come here? (8.1)
"You have arrived; tell me, do you know Bālakṛṣṇaka?
Quickly report the truth regarding his residence at Aśvapaṭṭasara. (82)
Then I assumed there a form approved by Nārada;
she, recognizing me as a being, laughed and bowed down to me. (83)
Then I became a child once again, and she too was there, at a spot in the open square adorned with a kadamba tree. (84)
Having summoned him under the pretext of playing games and other such diversions, he spoke privately:
"O Great Sage, tell me here—how and why did that happen, if indeed it occurred? (85)
"O virtuous lady, I have been sent by Bālakṛṣṇa;
I have come at his command to inquire about the welfare regarding the marriage. (86)
Speak quickly what is in your heart, so that Satī may not know;
speak without delay under the pretext of playing with five stones and such. (87)
O Kṛṣṇa, upon merely seeing me, she was filled with joy and great delight, and said, "Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa is my lord of life. (88)
When will you come quickly? When will you accept me?
Indeed, I am not able to endure even a moment's separation. (89)
"O Kṛṣṇa, speak quickly and come with all haste;
O Guru, tell me, for this is the time appointed for my giving."
He gave me this word: "The Blessed One himself will come and take my hand, when he is fourteen years older than I. (9.1)
If Kṛṣṇa does not accept me this year, I shall certainly give up my life and come there in a divine form. 92.
Speak to my father and inform my mother as well;
O wise one, do not make my words public in their presence. (93)
"Arrange matters so that he may quickly become mine," she said, and at that moment her limbs were covered in horripilation as she was overwhelmed with love. (94)
With eyes filled with tears of affection, as if absorbed in meditative concentration, she spoke again briefly: "Please announce that she has been surrendered."
"O Nārada, do not say anything further in the presence of Śrī Hari;
go instead and tell my mother and father that you have arrived at their home. (96)
Having spoken thus and having playfully prostrated at my feet,
she rose up, intent on her sports, and quickly performed a circumambulation.
Having seen Hari again there in the temple along with her mother, she went to her own home, O Kṛṣṇa; after that, I became Nārada.
Having bathed at the confluence of the Varaṇā and the Gaṅgā, I went there, addressing Nārada in his true form as "Nārāyaṇa. (99)
Upon seeing me wearing matted locks, Satī performed a prostration;
and when she saw me, I bestowed a blessing upon her, whereupon she indeed attained great joy.
He inquired after my complete well-being as I stood upon the seat offered to me, accepting the honey-mixture and other honors, having arrived there unexpectedly. || 10.1 ||
"O Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu, Bālakṛṣṇa, Hari, Lord!
Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa!"—thus I proclaimed at that time.
All your names, O Kṛṣṇa, are purifying and auspicious; they serve as reminders of you, and therefore I drank a little water.
Then, having attained peace, whenever I shall desire to speak, may the goddess Lakṣmī, the bestower of happiness, listen with eager ears before me in the assembly.
Jyeṣṭhā, Kṛṣṇā, and likewise other friends possessed of divine vision, though they were virtuous women,
did not bow to me, but sat down all around me.

Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Auspicious Letter Given by Bṛhaspati, the Ritual Worship and Recitation Performed by Lomaśa, Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa and Others Feeding [the Guests] Following the Welcome and Madhuparka, and Nārada’s Explanation to Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa of the Maiden’s Sovereignty, Qualities, and Divine Marks, as well as His Explanation of the Secret Meaning of the Maiden’s Words," in the second section, the Tretā-Santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, I shall relate to you in its entirety that which Nārada indeed told them; listen with a one-pointed mind.
Nārada said:
I have come from Satyaloka to the Aśvapaṭṭa lake,
located in western Saurāṣṭra on earth, where Puruṣottama resides.
Together with him, I wandered upon the earth for the sake of performing sacrifices,
where those liberated from their abodes as well as the attendants of other realms had arrived.
Likewise, there were female attendants, truthful goddesses, and divine beings;
human women, Naga maidens, virtuous wives, and excellent Siddha women.
All the incarnations, as well as the lords and the virtuous, the perfected ones, those who observe the vow of Brahman, the ancestors, and likewise the seers; || 5 ||
The Ṛṣis, all the gods, and those others who had assembled,
as well as humans, the guardians of heaven, the world-protectors, and the great lords.
The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, the two Aśvins, as well as their wives;
the Vahnis, Maruts, Nidhis, and likewise the Grahas. || 7 ||
The directions, Kāma, the months, the lunar days, and likewise the digits;
the principles (tattvas), all sacred fords, rivers, lakes, and oceans.
The mountains, the Vālakhilyas, Vāyu, Deha, Asura, and others,
as well as the Daityas, Dānavas, Pakṣas, and likewise the Rākṣasas, were his devotees.
Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, and likewise Kinnaras;
Uragas, Kiṃpuruṣas, trees, grasses, and creepers.
Those beginning with Dharma and those devoted to Yama; the Śaivas who dwell on Kailāsa;
those who dwell in Vaikuṇṭha, the White Ocean of Milk, and Badarī. ||11||
Dwellers of Meru, dwellers of Āvaraṇa, and inhabitants of Pātāla—
countless crores of deities indeed flocked to every sacrifice.
Everyone praises Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord Bālakṛṣṇa;
they bow to him, honor him, and offer hymns of praise to the son of Kaṃbhārī.
Then those guardians of the worlds, guardians of the abodes, guardians of creation, and Nārāyaṇas drink His grace—that nectar of His feet. (14)
Those who are Nārāyaṇas and those who carry out his command—all this was witnessed by me there directly. || 15 ||
Śaṅkara himself has made his residence in the sacred field of Akṣara;
indeed, he dwells as the guardian of the field (Kṣetrapāla) all around the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Lord Śrī Rāma, Nara, and likewise Nārāyaṇa;
the manifestations (vyūhas) such as Vāsudeva and others, and Sanatkumāra, the king of yogis.
Likewise, there are other supreme lords such as Saṃkarṣaṇa and others, as well as Mahāviṣṇu, Bhūman, Vairāja, and Sadāśiva. || 18 ||
He whose command even the lords of Time, Illusion, and the Yamas carry out;
from whom all beings arise, by whom they are nourished, and into whom they pass away.
But that which is called the inner self is the Lord himself, the witness; he who is called the supreme Brahman, by whom all this is pervaded. ||2.275.20||
The flashes of lightning, the sun, the moon, fire, and likewise Dhruva—all these luminous bodies that radiate light are made manifest by his splendor. (21)
By entering into which all beings become possessed of knowledge, and by which there is indeed illumination for the world of living beings within their own self. 22.
The Blessed One, who is indeed beyond the imperishable, shines forth at the site of Kuṅkumavāpikā as the bestower of all illumination. (23)
"In his own human form, he is the cowherd boy Kṛṣṇa"—
thus indeed did those who were proud of their greatness praise him at the sacrifice.
That Bālakṛṣṇa, Janārdana, who assumes ten million forms,
indeed brings millions of devotees together at once upon his chest.
Indeed, I have seen that directly; I have heard it all and praised it;
and I have heard the voices of women at every place during the great festival. (26)
Blessed are we that today we behold the vision of Surūpa, the Lord of All and a yogi, for whom there is no limit to his merit. (27)
"Ah! From the sight of him, eternal peace has arisen;
today, indeed, the length of our eyes has attained its fulfillment. (28)
Even from afar, great joy arises upon seeing him;
it is a bliss exceeding all bliss, rich with an uninterrupted and surging momentum. (29)
And we experience great happiness for all our senses, such that by merely looking from afar at this [place], there is such supreme bliss. (2.275.30)
Then, what would it be like for the daughter of Śiveśvara, the divine Lakṣmī, who was lying by the side of her husband in person? ||31||
She who is indeed the sovereign mistress, the half-body of the Lord, Nārāyaṇī, the supreme sovereign;
her two cheeks and temples are like the sun and the moon.
Her body is like gold, resembling the campaka flower;
likewise, the palms of her hands and the soles of her feet resemble red lac.
Her lips, which are the abode of love, resemble ripe bimba fruits; her two beautiful thighs are like the trunks of plantain trees. (34)
She whose eyes are like the petals of a lotus, whose form is indeed unsurpassed, and who dwells upon the chest of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa—that one is the Supreme Goddess. (35)
And she who dwells upon her own breast with her beloved Kṛṣṇa—being united with him in every limb, how happy she must be! (36)
"Oh, blessed is the daughter of Śiva who enjoys happiness from Kṛṣṇa!
Blessed is that goddess Pārvatī, by whose happiness Śivā herself is made happy. (37)
That bliss belongs to Ramā, or Kamalā, or Śrī, the consort of Kṛṣṇa; or to Vṛndā, or Tulasī, or Bhārgavī. (38)
That which was written on our foreheads by Kṛṣṇa and always inscribed by Lakṣmī—oh, there is no greater fortune than this for us, that it is not being diminished! 39.
And this Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa is our husband;
for a woman in this world, birth is in vain without the bliss of union with Kṛṣṇa.
All devotion to one's husband is in vain if the husband is not Kṛṣṇa;
oh, how great indeed is the fruitfulness and dignity of the daughter of Śiva! 41.
She enjoys all tastes, all fragrances, and all touches filled with bliss;
she enjoys all sounds, all sights, and all joys. (42)
Having obtained Kṛṣṇa—the abode of all bliss, the beloved, the master of all, whose senses are conquered and whose prowess is unbroken—that daughter of Śiva enjoys him. (43)
Even while residing in Kāśī, she remains eternally attached to Kṛṣṇa, yet she stays unmanifest;
only those with divine vision—truthful and virtuous women—behold her day and night.
Thus indeed have I repeatedly heard such reports from groups of women;
therefore, I was desirous of seeing him and sought to know more about him again and again. (45)
Having inquired again and again, I slowly arrived here at your house;
indeed, I repeatedly heard even the name "Lakṣmī," the destroyer of sorrow. (46)
"What is she like? Whose daughter is she? What kind of qualities must she possess?
If that goddess were here, she ought to be seen by me. (47)
Where does she dwell? What is her true nature? What is her condition? What are her garments? What is her innate disposition? What is her physical form, and what is her configuration? (48)

Of what form was she, of what radiance, and how many years of age was that beautiful woman? What was her face like, what was her speed, what was her disposition, and what were her auspicious marks? (49)

What are her arts? What is her voice? What is her complexion? How radiant are her feet? What is her forehead like? What are her beautiful hair-locks? What is her nature? What is her perfection? What is her power? What is she rich in happiness? What is her splendor? And what is she who brings true awakening?
What is her duty, what is her devotion, what is her divinity, and what is her inner nature?
What is her knowledge, what is the splendor of her signs, what is her height, and what is her gait?
What is her dress, what is her companion, what is her ornament, and what is the array of her vessels? (51–52)
What is her strength, what is her courage, what is her food, and what is her asceticism?
What is her contentment, what is her purity, what is her study of the scriptures, and what is her virtue? (53)
What is her heart? What is the object of her love? What is her skill? And what is her intellect? What are her limbs? What is her wealth? What is she fickle at? And indeed, what is her writing? (54)
What is its taste, what its discourse, what its conduct, and what its activity?
What are its three periods, and likewise, what are its initial, middle, and final fruits? (55)
What is its activity? What is its particularity? What is its generality? What is its middle state?
What is its trust? What is its yoga? What is its awakening? What is its worship? (56)
Is she one who seeks propitiation? Is she one who seeks adornment? Is she one who seeks passion? Or is she contented? Is she greedy? Is she full of hope? Or is she full of desire? ||57||

What is its reasoning? What is its certainty? What is its debate? What is its means of valid cognition? What is its object of cognition? What is its application? What is its tenet? What is its point of defeat? (58)

What are her Vedas, what are her means of accomplishment, what is she fond of, and what does she reject? What is her self-restraint, what is her discipline, what is her meditation, and what is her posture? (59)
"What is her life-breath, what is her delight, and what is her desire?
Such a curiosity has arisen in me to see this, and for that reason I have come here. (2.275.60)
"O Blessed One, this celestial sage Nārada has arrived;
he is the mind-born son of Brahmā, the illustrious brother of Rudra, and a renowned divine seer."
If those who are devotees of Viṣṇu—though lacking in steadfastness and always fond of quarreling—honor me when I go to their homes; ||62||
Indeed, these words have been spoken by me; I am the one who brings happiness through them.
If people do not heed these words, they will find no satisfaction.
Then, having created an unbearable quarrel in their house,
I shall go forth to another home where I might receive honor.
The young girls show me their hands to examine their fortune;
having seen everything, I shall tell them what brings happiness. (65)
If there should be any suffering whatsoever, I shall destroy it;
yet by treating me with disrespect, people do not obtain happiness. (66)
Those who follow my words receive great honor;
indeed, for them, a residence arises in one place lasting as long as it takes to milk a cow.
Nevertheless, observing your devotion, I shall dwell here day and night;
from that, my special residence shall bestow prosperity and heaven upon you.
Even more excellent than that is my dwelling which bestows the attainment of Nārāyaṇa; even more excellent than that is my dwelling which bestows the Supreme Brahman.
I grant liberation by my word; I grant liberation by being glorified;
I grant affliction by a mere fraction [of my power]; and I grant happiness by being propitiated.
I administer poison to that news in which I am not satisfied;
and I cause even nectar to be drunk in that which I have favored.
"Wherever my desire for knowledge is fulfilled, there I grant the highest heavenly bliss and depart elsewhere; let this be known as my vow. (72)
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Bāla Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare!
O Lord of Śrī, son of Kaṃbhārā, Lord of Lakṣmī, Hare Hare! (73)
O beloved of the daughter of Śiveśvara, O Hare, O delighter of the cowherds!
O Lord of the beloved of Brahmā, O Kṛṣṇa, O Bālakṛṣṇa, O Hare, O Hare! (74)
O beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Lord of Brahmā, O Hari!
O Lord of all beloved women, Beloved Kṛṣṇa, Hari, Hari! (75)
O Śrī Kṛṣṇavallabha Svāmin, who possesses the form of Prince Kṛṣṇa;
O Teacher, O Vedic scholar, O Self of all, O Soul of all, O refuge of Śeṣa! 76.
Having thus performed this worship toward Nārada with her mind, speech, and actions, Lakṣmī indeed ceased; so did Nārada. (77)
"The activity of my other senses has ceased, for they have become absorbed in that;
O divine sage, Śivā says, 'O Ṛṣi, blessed is my fortune! (78)
Since you, who are the very embodiment of Kṛṣṇa, have come to my home, it is a great fortune for my daughter that she has obtained a vision of you, the virtuous one. (79)
I am Nārada; I know whatever merit has been accumulated through a hundred births, by which one indeed attains a human birth. ||2.275.80||
Furthermore, if one were to perform a hundred sacrifices there, one would indeed attain heaven for a duration equal to that of Indra; thereafter, he returns here to this earth.
By the power of the remaining merit, one shall attain the status of the most excellent among men; therein, through the majesty of the Brahmins and also by the blessings of the virtuous. (82)
One shall obtain a kingdom that is excellent, full of devotion, auspicious, and bestowing happiness;
therein, service is rendered to the gods and to guest-attendants. 83.
Indeed, through the satisfaction of the father, one attains virtuous intellect, prosperity, and the creeper-like continuity of the lineage; therein, sons and daughters are truly born as sons. (84)
Through the power of serving the virtuous, people become happy;
service to the virtuous bestows wealth, grants land, and provides happiness. (85)
And that [attainment] is indeed met through righteousness, devotion, austerity, and likewise through vows; otherwise it is not at all, for the service of the virtuous is difficult to obtain. (86)
Through favor and compassion, service to the virtuous is undertaken;
through the dharma of devotion to one’s husband, service to the virtuous is undertaken.
For virtuous people who are habituated to helping others, who provide food as alms, and who are constantly devoted to giving, gain is produced. (88)
For those devotees who possess a gentle disposition, who offer everything [to the Lord], who are virtuous, and who perform acts of hospitality toward the good, true gain is produced. (89)
For the virtuous who are always of the nature of sacred fords, who always listen well to the sacred narratives,
and who are always inclined toward salutation, spiritual gain is produced.
For those who constantly offer worship to the gods, who always perform acts of hospitality, and who always possess the mindfulness of the virtuous, prosperity arises. (91)
For those who desire their own welfare, for those engaged in the occupation of service, and for virtuous seekers who serve, gain is produced. (92)
For those who are mindful, who seek [the truth], and who are endowed with virtuous qualities, gain arises for the virtuous in the house of the virtuous and through the yoga of the virtuous. ||93||
In the dwellings of true gurus, at the great festivals of the virtuous, and through constant association with the good, the attainment of the virtuous arises. (94)
And for those established in the vow of truth, who perform sacrifices to the supreme Brahman, there arises the attainment of the virtuous ones who are in union with the attendants of Hari. (95)
In the home of those devoted to Hari, in the house of female devotees, and among assemblies of dispassionate saints, spiritual gain arises. (96)
Through association with good friends, by dwelling in a holy land, and through union with the right time, service to the virtuous arises. (97)
Service to the virtuous arises through association with the initiation of the virtuous, through the reception of mantras from the virtuous, and even by the power of affection for the virtuous. (98)
Through faith, through respectful address, through fame, through noble lineage, and through connection with the great, service to the virtuous arises. (99)
Either by the grace of Śrī Hari, or by taking refuge in the consort of Hari, or by the constant residence of Hari, the service of the virtuous is attained. (2.275.100)
O Nārada, today my dwelling in the cremation ground, the abode of Śaṅkara,
has been purified by you, O virtuous one, a holy man devoted to Hari.
By the grace of your feet, the entire world has been purified;
it surely proceeds upon the path to liberation, and even my own home has been sanctified.
You have caused to be heard all that which bestows auspiciousness and brings happiness arising from the connection with Kṛṣṇa;
the purifying glory of Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa has been proclaimed by you.
O Nārada, my heart has been purified here by your presence, as has that of my daughter, who stands before you, golden-hued like Lakṣmī; therefore, live long!
"Oh, what great fortune for my daughter, that her name is renowned among all beings throughout the three worlds! Blessed am I, who have such a daughter."
"Daughter Lakṣmī, pay obeisance indeed to Śrī Nārada;
perform the massaging of his feet and the anointing of his body with oil."
"Give me water and food—sweet, desirable, and most excellent—without delay;
give me a couch, the honey-mixture (madhuparka), drink, and likewise my heart."
"O best among the virtuous, grant him your full consent so that this Nārada may perform an examination of him, just as Hari himself desires."
"O daughter who causes me grief, you are indeed the daughter of Śambhu, the brother of Brahmā;
this son belongs to Brahmā, and as my son, he is your elder brother."
By virtue of our relationship, he is indeed my guru and a great rishi;
this Nārada is a portion (aṃśa) of Hari, and he is worthy of worship for you and for me as well.
"O daughter, serve [him] in such a way that he may become well-pleased. Having been addressed thus, Lakṣmī, the mother of Ajā, bowed down to Nārada. || 111 ||
He gave him water to drink, as well as sweet food and a beautiful seat;
he also gave him a golden-colored couch and flower garlands and other such offerings.
Lakṣmī massaged the feet of the illustrious Nārada,
and after resting, O Rādhikā, Nārada brought about the removal of her fatigue.
Nārada also scrutinized the characteristics as they had been described; indeed, he saw there once again all those very same features that he had previously observed.
And the virtuous Jānakī joyfully called upon her own husband, Śiveśvara, the Lord of the Universe, who was present in the great garden nearby. 1.15

Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-fifth chapter, titled "The Narration of Events such as the Glory of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa as Spoken by Nārada to Pārvatī and Satī, the Glory of Lakṣmī, the Causes for Attaining the Company of the Virtuous, and the Honoring of Nārada," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, Nārada then spoke thus to the Lord of Śrī,
Bāla Kṛṣṇa, regarding everything that had occurred at the house of Śiva.
Nārada said: O Hari, I have rested for a while; now the creator of Śrī Śiva, the hero of the universe with a divine body and three eyes, has arrived at my home.
"I am blessed, I have fulfilled my purpose; today a Vaiṣṇava has indeed come to my home, and even more so, today my affectionate nephew has arrived. (3)
"Oh Nārada, my son, from where have you indeed come? Is all well and auspicious with you and likewise with my brother? (4)
"Is Viṣṇu well, and are his family members happy?
Having said this, Śiva suddenly embraced me with his chest.
I have indeed announced my welfare to Satyaloka, as well as to my father Brahmā,
and also to my mother Sāvitrī.

Then indeed, the account of Sanaka and the others was proclaimed, and that of Rudra as well; thereafter, the welfare of Dakṣa and the others was also fully recounted. Then, the entire narrative of Viṣṇu and Mahālakṣmī was told.

That which is situated in Vaikuṇṭha is proclaimed to be both blissful and auspicious. Then, at the time of Śiva’s Tandava dance, the events that had previously occurred regarding Lakṣmī’s curse and so forth were once again brought to mind within that realm of Vaikuṇṭha.
The birth of Śiva upon the earth so that you might become Śiveśvara, and also that which was done by Nārāyaṇa regarding the abandonment of Lakṣmī—[these were the purposes]. (2.276.10)
Indeed, for the sake of His devotees, Nārāyaṇa descended upon the earth;
through that pretext, the Supreme Lord, the beginningless Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa, appeared. ||1||
Having arrived at the Aśvapaṭṭa lake, I indeed proclaimed that Supreme Brahman, and Lakṣmī also arrived there.
"This daughter was born in the house of Śivasvāmin;
she has been proclaimed as Śivā, the goddess Pārvatī—all that has been related by me. (13)
Remembering her again and again, the Lord of Śivā shed tears; embracing me firmly, he cried out, "O son! O son! and embraced me.
Having bowed to Śaṅkara, I indeed made known what was in my heart;
and the Blessed One [Śiva] remembered this maiden and that medicine.
Indeed, the time for her giving away in marriage has truly arrived;
one should act appropriately and according to the facts, for by that, happiness will be attained.
O Śambhu, you perform worship of Kṛṣṇa constantly;
indeed, that very divine and beautiful one has been seen by you again and again as the best of suitors. (17)
Janārdana is indeed determined to be the Supreme Brahman himself;
he was seen by me and has also been seen by you in human form.
He is to be seen in the form of the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla); nothing remains [elsewhere].
Nevertheless, if you have the desire, then come. 19.
Thus addressed by me, Śambhu indeed remembered Bṛhaspati;
and Hara quickly arrived, [offering] the madhuparka and other honors.
He offered everything to his preceptor, reporting all that had been told by me;
Bṛhaspati declared it all to be auspicious and indeed most excellent. (21)
Then, having made his decision, Śambhu indeed spoke repeatedly in my presence and also before the Guru regarding the oral betrothal of the girl.
Having observed an auspicious moment, I indeed bestowed ornaments, garments,
a bilva fruit, and a sectarian mark upon the maiden.
Born from you, she became radiant; having put on garments and various excellent ornaments, she was then addressed by her preceptor. (24)
Filled with joy and considering herself the most beautiful among her friends regarding the prize, she was delighted;
then Hara said to Bṛhaspati, "When will this great festival take place? (25)
On the fourth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, Bṛhaspati indeed spoke that [instruction];
having heard it, all attained joy and remained steadfast in the words of Bṛhaspati. ||26||
Then, having deliberated with me and having ascertained the mind of the maiden, Vācaspati quickly took up the marriage contract.
Having observed Pārvatī’s mind, having worshipped the Lord of the Gaṇas, and having made him wet with saffron paste, he waited for an auspicious moment. ||28||
They even wrote a document with Nārada himself as witness;
and by the command of Hara, the people there played musical instruments.
Likewise, auspicious women and celestial goddesses sang hymns,
while the illustrious Nārada and Bṛhaspati performed the *gūḍhadhānā* and other rites.
Likewise, Śaṅkara and all the others partook of that which brings auspiciousness;
then this king of the preceptors of the gods was joined by Śiva with the yoga-leaf.
"Sent by me along with [you] to the abode of Kuṅkumavāpikā, this very deity, the preceptor of the gods, has certainly arrived. (32)
"O Kṛṣṇa, having taken her who was promised by word, bring your beloved here;
she remains waiting for your path like one distraught. (33)
When will Kṛṣṇa come? When will he take me as his own?
And when, having previously abandoned him, shall I regain this life of my life? (34)
When will that Kambharā-lakṣmī look upon me with love—she who, having come twice, looked at me and then departed again and again? (35)
When Hari came from the sacrifices by means of a celestial chariot, she was honored again; why does he not come back, and why does he not even remember me? (36)
Previously she saw me, and at that time I was but a young girl; thinking, "She is worthy of my son," she placed me upon her lap. (37)
I believe that queen remains ever firm in her resolve;
she is content, gracious, and satisfied, for she does not forbid me at all. (38)
O Nārada, you have arrived; at that time, what did that Kaṃbharā, who is Ramā, say to me or to my mother? Tell me the truth. 39.
In this manner, she repeatedly asked me about that secret;
O Kambharā, all of that must be told by me to you.
"O ocean of mercy, act quickly; everything will bear fruit according to your heart's desire.
Thus was Bālakṛṣṇa addressed there by the celestial sage, O Rādhikā.
Having risen, he went quickly toward his mother Kambharā;
having prostrated before his mother, Nārada said, "To my home. (42)
Eager to make her known the secret,
he called out to my satisfied sister and likewise to his virtuous brother’s wife.
"Taking Amṛtā along with Śrī, come to my abode. Thus addressed by Bālakṛṣṇa, the mother, accompanied by her sister, [departed]. (44)
O Rādhā, that virtuous woman, closely joined with her brothers' wives and united with Bālakṛṣṇa, arrived at the abode of Bālakṛṣṇa full of eagerness. 45.
Upon seeing her, Nārada smiled gently and bowed to Satī;
rising with his neck bent low, he welcomed her with words.
With his hands joined in añjali, he then stood up as soon as his mother had sat down upon the golden throne.
Then, as his sister and his brother's wife sat down, the sage Nārada was honored, worshipped, and saluted. (48)
Having paid homage in accordance with the truth in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, he said:
"O Mother, I bow at your feet; I shall declare the secret which the Śaiva goddess told me again and again as a matter for privacy."
Śrī Kaṃbharā Lakṣmī said:
"O great sage, was that girl Nārāyaṇī, the Supreme Goddess, speaking on my behalf? Tell me everything that she said here."
Is that young woman beautiful, indeed free from physical defects and endowed with all auspicious marks?
What indeed is her health, and what is that stainless mind of hers? (51)
"What does she desire for my son? What indeed does that heart-born woman feel here? Does she still possess affection for me, or has her mind now turned toward my son? (52)
With a serene heart, she remains there, surely mindful of me;
for when the sacrifice took place in the Piṅgā forest, then Satī [was present].
Seeing her arrived, I indeed became exceedingly joyful;
and having manifested my status as a daughter-in-law, she took me onto her own lap. (54)
Again, having gone to my own country, and then during the interval between sacrifices, I went to the regions of Rāśiyāna and returned there once more. (55)
Having seen her together with my own son, I was indeed filled with joy;
she remained in private, having made a request for the sake of her own son.
Having then spoken of everything connected with that very subject,
she departed as if having reached a final decision, and did not return to her again.
"Is that girl suitable for my son?
Tell me everything regarding her—what virtues she possesses and what training she has received. (58)
"What kind of wisdom and what kind of skill does she possess that she is so [accomplished]?
Tell me everything here regarding what must be understood for the sake of my daughter-in-law. (59)
Nārada said:
O Mother, upon hearing that name Kambharā-Lakṣmī, she became filled with great reverence;
out of a state of love, she was thrilled and likewise moved to tears.
Having become composed for a moment, she smiled at me and said:
"Is all well with me, who am worthy of such honor? Does he even remember me?"
What is her news? What is my venerable lady's disposition toward me?
Is she intent on making efforts for my sake, and is she well-disposed toward me? (62)
O Great Sage, tell me about the states of the qualities as they truly exist;
or, if there is anything else that ought to be known, please explain it to me.
Then I spoke to the maiden, whose mind was fixed on Śravaṇa:
"O Lakṣmī, Queen Kambharā never forgets you at any time. (64)
Constantly remembering you at every meal, she even causes you, Kṛṣṇa, to be remembered; and here and there, she remains immersed in news of you and the description of your virtues. (65)
With eyes filled with tears of affection, she is indeed born; what more can I say to you?
Your mother-in-law always remains happy, awaiting you who are so full of joy.
Accompanied by a body, a home, and children, and enriched with every prosperity, she—possessing all auspicious circumstances—waits for you, O Lakṣmī. (67)
Just as Kambharā was always satisfied with her daughter,
so too does the virtuous Kambharā feel even greater affection toward you.
For your sake, she, my beloved daughter, is always striving;
indeed, the Sovereign Kaṃbhārā remains forever well-disposed toward you.
In some places she says, "My auspicious daughter-in-law—what vow must she have undertaken?
Without her, my beloved and worthy Kṛṣṇa does not shine at all. (2.276.70)
"O Mother, in this very manner I reported everything to her; and I offered the blessings that you had instructed me to give. (71)
"She remains serene, affectionate, and endowed with excellent virtues"—when I had spoken thus to her, she replied to me again, "Salutations! (72)
And offer my salutations at her feet;
likewise, inform the Noble Lady that your life-breaths reside in your son. (73)
"My self has indeed come there; announce this to the one worthy of worship.
And let her know: 'The ignoble acts of my childish nature must be forgiven. (74)
"Tell them that I am exactly as I am, the daughter of those who dwell in the mountains and forests; I am composed of dullness, and I must be forgiven. (75)
"O Noble Lady, I am not possessed of learning, nor am I a repository of the arts;
I am not endowed with discernment, nor am I beautiful through cleverness. (76)
I am neither a sorceress nor one who employs harsh means;
I am not Kṛṣṇā, nor am I worthy of Kṛṣṇa; nevertheless, you should not forget me.
"I am the daughter of one worthy of worship and the wife of the son of one worthy of worship;
I am a maiden, so quickly make me your daughter-in-law; enough with such talk! (78)
"The words spoken by the maiden are true, for the time for giving has indeed arrived";
having said this, she gave me sweet fruits that were like nectar. (79)
"Gifts should be given to Kambharālakṣmī and to her son Viṣṇu.
Having said this, he prostrated before me; thus has the secret been told to you.
That virtuous woman never passes even a single moment without Kṛṣṇa;
she is equal to Lakṣmī, but Lakṣmī is never equal to her.
Indeed, all splendors abide as condensed masses within her very nature; she stands radiant, like the sprout of the blossoming of youth. 82.
The state of the virtuous woman always abides as the supreme garment of the sky of consciousness;
she is of eternal nature and the condensed mass of existence, consciousness, and bliss. 83.
Established in the state of Brahman, she possesses the form of a liberated soul and the luster of Hari;
twelve excellent years have passed since she has considered herself the Supreme Person.
The currents of her affection for Hari shine forth as her devotion to her husband;
Hari dwells within the center of her heart, marked by the characteristics of Kṛṣṇa. (85)
O Mother, how could I possibly describe her who is perfected in all the arts?
She knows the science of cooking, and she knows the techniques of weaving. (86)
She understands household duties and those pertaining to calculation;
she is well-versed in the sciences for children and even in the arts born of love. 87.
She understands all the arrangements of the dressing room and the arts of beautification; she knows all the duties of servants and even those tasks performed by maidservants. (88)
All acts of service and all that provides mental delight, as well as all theatrical performances and whatever dance productions there may be. ||89||
All musical performances, all singing activities in every respect, whatever festivals there may be, and all matters pertaining to assemblies in every way. ||2.276.90||
All the commentaries and likewise all the logical statements, as well as the complete teachings on self-realization and the arts arising from yoga; || 91 ||
He knows all spiritual accomplishments (siddhis), the knowledge of reality (tattvajñāna), and medicine;
he understands Āyurveda and all sacrificial rites in their entirety.
He understands all the Vedas, as well as all forms of exchange; he knows all causes, all seasons, and all transformations and evolutions. ||93||
He understands all arts of craftsmanship, he speaks all maxims of policy, he knows all Vedic meters, the lineages [of teachers], and the domestic rituals. (94)

He understands the hospitality due to guests, the offerings to the ancestors, and the worship due to the gods; he also understands the proper reception, the welcome, and the honoring [of others]. (95)
He understands the origin of helping others and giving charity; he knows affection, joy, devotion to his master, fidelity to his wife, and his own virtue. 96.
He discerns all blended flavors and sweet foods in their entirety, as well as the preparation of buttermilk and the cooking of milk and other such things. (97)
She understands weaving, purification, and religious observances directly; she is endowed with wisdom, remains equanimous, and is seen to be deeply learned. (98)
Is it Śāradā who resides there, or is it Rādhā, the one who delights all?
For she understands the arts of performance and knows how to serve the cows and so forth. (99)
He knows the work of agriculture, the nourishment of crops, and the forests;
he knows all medicinal herbs, sacrificial fuel, and even health itself. (2.276.10)
He understands the science of water, he knows the science of fire, and he thoroughly understands all the sciences of mantras as well as the various regions. || 101 ||
He well understands gain and loss, as well as the four aims of human life; he also discerns the means of conciliation, bribery, and the rest.
She understands all forms of discourse as well as the arts of the great gardens;
with a throat of sweet sweetness, she possesses an exceedingly melodious voice. (103)
Golden-hued, with the luster of Brahman, her hands and palms are red;
the brilliant autumnal moonlight dwells eternally within her body.
Her forehead has the splendor of the broad and lofty moon; she is as beautiful as the moon and other celestial bodies;
she possesses black hair, her very soul is black, and she is the one who bestows the perfections of black sovereignty and other powers.
She possesses the power of all prosperity and is endowed with the bliss of Brahman;
she is the radiance of the Supreme Brahman and the awakener of the Supreme Brahman.
Muktānikā was always devoted to Hari and intent on her spiritual welfare;
within her heart, Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, the bestower of liberation, shone resplendently.
And she resides in Kambharā, established in the fourteen branches of knowledge,
endowed with the conch, discus, mace, lotus, bow, and trident.
She was endowed with the previously mentioned marks and adorned with the emblem of Kamalā;
her entire body was beautified by thousands of the signs of Lakṣmī.
There were indeed seventy-two principal leaders there,
and Bālakṛṣṇa shone with a height reaching up to his neck.
She possesses the gait of an elephant and a swan, and she always has the gait of a supreme swan;
she is clothed in gold, fragrant, and likewise accompanied by ten million lotuses.
Rādhā, Ramā, Satī, Padmā, Māṇikī, Padmajā, Śrī, Śāradā, and others are her companions; they are all wives of Kṛṣṇa.
Adorned with all ornaments and resting upon every structural connection, she is endowed with a flash of wonder and possesses the dark strength of her vows. 113.
The divine Brāhmī, composed of pure being, is eternally beyond the bliss of Brahmā;
she is the virtuous Satī who consumes milk-rice and other offerings, and who restrains Kṛṣṇa for his own sake.

She is devoted to meditation on Kṛṣṇa and ascetic penance; she is satisfied by the purpose of Bālakṛṣṇa; she is content through the destruction of all cravings; she is free from deceit and beautiful in her purity.
She is one who has thoroughly studied the Vedic sciences, a great being of virtuous conduct, firm in her resolve for liberation, and whose heart is devoted to self-surrender. || 1.16 ||
She was a vessel for the love of Nirvana, devoted solely to the love of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
skilled in the means of spiritual practice, and possessed of the noble intelligence that leads to future awakening.
Her limbs are dark, her wealth is Acyuta; she is always fickle toward the non-devotee, possessed of the fickleness of Kṛṣṇa, and likewise sports for the sake of Kṛṣṇa.
A taste for liberation, a discourse on the stories of Kṛṣṇa, a stable disposition, and engagement with the Supreme Brahman—this is endowed with the three aims of human life. || 11.9 ||
She is the ordainer of the three worlds, whose fruit is the abandonment of effort and enjoyment;
she yields the fruits of sacrifice, heaven, and liberation, and possesses the activity that fulfills all desires.
She is the excellence of attaining Brahman, equal to the bliss of creation;
she is the essence of the bliss of the subtle self, and she is the yoginī who breathes with Mādhava.
She is united with Kṛṣṇa, possessing all-encompassing awakening, and endowed with the worship of the Omniscient One;
she is eternally devoted to honoring her elders and is resplendent with the amorous adornment of Kṛṣṇa.
She was detached from anything other than Kṛṣṇa, fully satisfied in Nārāyaṇa,
liberated, longing for the company of the virtuous, desiring Kṛṣṇa’s grace, and wishing for the welfare of others.
"When shall I indeed behold the home of Kambharā-lakṣmī, if she so desires?
If I am not for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, then whence is my life? (1.24)
Since my life exists for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, this is my reasoned conviction;
and since the two broad thighs of the Supreme Brahman are my home, this is my firm resolve.
At every step, there are proclamations of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
the directly manifest Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa is the divine and eternal authority. 1.26.
O Mother, that indeed proceeds, and other things rooted in it as well;
for its sake, every object of knowledge remains eternally distinguished.
The Supreme Brahman is the Great Reality, to which nothing is equal or superior;
the well-practiced yoga of that [Brahman] is the means for attaining the perfection of the Kṛṣṇa-siddhānta. 1.28.
She is the well-established ultimate doctrine of the Kṛṣṇa-tantra, devoid of all possessions;
she is the one who binds the planets of Bāla-Kṛṣṇa, and she is filled with the Vedas of the sacrificial command of Kṛṣi.
Nārāyaṇa is her goal, and her means of attainment is not tranquility or the like;
she is the beloved of Bālakṛṣṇa, the dear one who bestows everything other than that which is contrary to the Beloved.
She is the embodiment of the great dharma of the devotees of the Lord, joined with the discipline of Kṛṣṇa;
she is restrained for the sake of Kṛṣṇa, observing the vows of Kṛṣṇa, and does not rely on anything else.
With her mind absorbed in meditation on the face of Bālakṛṣṇa, seated upon the Kuṅkumavāpikā throne,
she possesses life-breath in your son and is intent on amorous play with Kṛṣṇa.
She is the one who fulfills the desires of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
she is the beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, exceedingly dear to him, and as dear to him as he is to her. 1.33.
That Mahālakṣmī resides in Kambharā, endowed with all virtues;
her mental affliction is the disease of separation from Kṛṣṇa, by which she is defiled.
Your heart shines here with a desire for a hundred million sons;
you possess all affection for Kaṃbharā, and love and tenderness for your son.
Your mind is constantly intent on his marriage, and your heart remains ever serene.
"O Mother, he constantly remembers you, his son, again and again.
With great urgency, she said to me once more, "Listen, O Kambharā! (136)
When the sacrifice took place in the Piṅgā forest, my mother-in-law arrived there;
having displayed herself as my daughter-in-law, she took me onto her own lap. (1.37)
Having gone to the regions of Rāśiyāna and returned again,
she stood in private and made a request to me on behalf of her own son.
Having hidden the moon-ornament along with the parched grain, she departed;
even now our mother, the venerable noble lady Pārameśvarī, has not yet returned. (139)
"O Nārada, tell me quickly when the illustrious Lord will arrive;
you must convey my salutations to Him," he said again and again. (2.276.140)
O Mother, she who is endowed with all virtues, trained in all duties, and skilled in household tasks, is manifest as worthy of being given in marriage. 141.
Therefore, having departed quickly and being informed by the festival leaf,
consider it the fourth day and perform the auspicious rites for those two.
Having spoken thus to Rādhikā and having bowed down to her, the brahmin Nārada returned to his own seat and once again attained rest.
Then Kambharā attained peace and rejoiced in contentment;
even Amṛtā then gave her joy and approval.
Having heard the news, Bālakṛṣṇa became pleased;
then everyone slept happily on the night of the fourteenth day.

Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of how Nārada told Bālakṛṣṇa the account of Lakṣmī’s secret speech as related in the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, within the second section on the Tretā lineage, and how he subsequently told it to Kaṃbharādevī."
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā; this morning, the cowherd girls, the daughters of brahmins, and young maidens sang auspicious songs indeed.
Likewise, the married women, the elderly, and the young girls, having heard the arrival of the yogic leaf—a source of auspiciousness—indeed sang auspicious songs. || 2 ||
In the field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, through the auspicious arrival of Bṛhaspati.
Having heard of Hari's auspiciousness, they sang songs in every house.
All those dear to Brahmā, as well as all the young maidens dear to Kṛṣṇa, sang songs that bring auspiciousness to their beloved.
All the gopīs gathered together and went to the house of Śrī Kambharā;
virtuous women and celibate maidens indeed sang auspicious songs.
The wives of the Kṣatriyas, the noble women of the Vaiśyas, and other attendants wearing pale-red garments,
arrived at the house singing songs filled with great enthusiasm.
The goddesses, who dwell there eternally and are ever eager for the imperishable field,
having heard the news of Hari’s wedding, came to the house singing.
Capable of assuming any form at will, the friends born from the four oceans,
as well as the Kāmavallīs, arrived at Kṛṣṇa’s palace while singing.
And the Mātṛkās residing at the holy site of Aśvapaṭṭasara, as well as the divine goddesses, having heard that the Guru had been chosen and knowing it to be highly auspicious, [rejoiced].
Singing and dressed in divine attire, they entered the palace of Kṛṣṇa; all the princesses, queens worthy of worship, and maidens followed. (2.277.10)

The women of Kuṅkumavāpikā arrived there singing; all the young women of every caste and all the ladies arrived as well. They [prepared] Satī, Śrī, Kaṃbharā, and Lakṣmī, who had already performed their baths and worship.
Having bowed down and seated themselves in a golden palace,
they sang auspicious hymns consisting of the glories of Kṛṣṇa, the Black One, who is Bālakṛṣṇa.

Acyuta had performed his bath and worship; his mother had applied auspicious *candraka* marks, his forehead was adorned with saffron and unbroken grains (*akṣata*), and he was fully arrayed in ornaments.
All the women, full of longing, sang praises and honored the beloved Lord, the Supreme Master, who had been dressed by his brother’s wife. || 14 ||
They placed a crescent moon made of unbroken grains and flowers upon his forehead;
and singing songs, they manifested their inner joy.
Having offered blessings, bowed to his preceptor Bṛhaspati, and performed his daily rites,
he drank the milk provided by his mother, sweetened with sugar and containing saffron filaments.
Having taken the desired betel and spoken auspicious words, they went home;
throughout every house here in Saurāṣṭra, there was talk of the festival of Kṛṣṇa.
The arrival of Bṛhaspati and Nārada spread rapidly;
hearing this, all the subjects attained joy and great festivity. (18)
Immersed in bliss, they gathered for the sake of the sight;
auspicious musical instruments were sounded within the palace—every kind of divine instrument and all those that are the royal instruments. (19)
Whatever musical instruments there are for domestic use, and whatever musical instruments there are for regional use; ||2.277.20||
And instruments played by hand, those played by breath, those that are purifying, all those played with a staff, and whatever instruments are played with lightning; 21.
And musical instruments for the limbs, those for accompanying ensembles, and those for various regional styles were played on all sides. ||22||
Indeed, the sounds of conch shells were sweet, as were the sounds of water-machines;
the loud-sounding flutes arose in every house. (23)
Singers sang and women equal to apsarases danced;
at that time, having heard of the festival for Bālakṛṣṇa, the women were exceedingly joyful. (24)
Peacocks dance and cuckoos warble;
birds sing forth, as do parrots, peahens, and cranes. (25)
The planets shone forth, and the fires blazed with brilliance;
the virtuous, pervaded by the splendor of their affection, sang his praises.
The Bhaṭṭas, Bhūsuras, and Vidyādharas are scholars who know the Vedas.
Then the bards sang songs in unison and recited their poetic compositions.
Others cried out "Victory! Victory to you, O Śrī Kṛṣṇa! toward the Lord;
indeed, O Rādhikā, such words of joy arose from person to person.
Having heard that the festival letter of Bālakṛṣṇa had arrived, and having heard that the preceptor Nārada was there, others came to see him. ||29||
Uttering blessings and saying, "May you live long," even the frogs,
resembling frogs, made the water-lifting machines resound.
Then they played the lip-instrument and the *tammarikā* lute; clapping their hands, they uttered cries of victory.
What is the use of saying much more before you, O Rādhikā?
For the sake of establishing righteousness, he will adopt the duties of a householder.
That supreme reality which is distinguished will always remain distinguished;
in order to make it known to the world, he will practice the dharma of a householder.
Having reflected thus, and having celebrated the occasion with the signing of a formal agreement, they joyfully performed the Rāsa festival, desiring to make it manifest to the world. (34)
Men and women, men and women—consisting of nothing but delusion—they wandered about and sang the virtues of Bālakṛṣṇa. ||35||
Having seen that [vision] in the past at Kuṅkumavāpī and in other cities with his divine vision,
the Guru was filled with wonder even while he was the sovereign ruler of Saurāṣṭra.

Oh, how wonderful is this devotion to the Lord on earth, consisting of abundant affection! Through the opportunity provided by this great festival, it has been witnessed by me among these people here. (37)
Such devotees in this world are liberated, there is no doubt,
because within their hearts exists the divine, most divine state of being toward Hari.
Oh, blessed is that Lakṣmī, the daughter of Śiva, who is Nārāyaṇī; for she shall indeed obtain the Lord of the Abode, his renowned, beloved, and eternal husband. (39)
I know that even beyond Rādhā there exists a higher step for Her, since He who is her supreme Lord stands upon it; therefore, She is one who ascends the upper steps.
Even if a maiden is called the mother of the world because she is the wife of Kṛṣṇa, even an old woman who is a hunchback is praised in the world through her union with Kṛṣṇa. ||41||
Vṛndā and Tulasī were indeed the two wives of the demon Jalandhara, as well as of Śaṅkhacūḍa; they were equal to Lakṣmī and united with Viṣṇu.
O you who are worthy of worship, adored by the world, and the givers of liberation, may you both always be so!
Oh, how great is the majesty of Kṛṣṇa, that the beloveds of Brahmā are innumerable! 43.
Indeed, while these [other women] exist, they do not attain the dignity of this Lakṣmī;
