The saintly ones went to their own hermitages, and the servants returned to their respective homes; Śrī Gopālakṛṣṇa, for his part, having partaken of pure, sattvic food, [remained there].
Having fed his household members, Bālakṛṣṇa, and the others,
he then changed out of his priceless attire and put on ordinary clothing.
For the sake of rest, he went to his own abode and fell asleep;
the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa also attained the yogic sleep.
The musicians also ceased their playing and, having taken their meals, went to their own dwellings, even as they were falling asleep. (96)
Having partaken [of the offerings], the guardians of the fields beginning with Śaṅkara, as well as the hosts of deities,
returned to their respective abodes and found rest during the night.
The vendors of meat, the servants, the tax-exempt officials, and the laborers, having finished their meal, were sleeping in their respective places. (98)
Then, O Rādhikā, those people who were guards and protectors, wandering at night, remained awake and performed an inspection of the sacred field. ||99||
Armed with weapons and mounted on vehicles and other conveyances, they wander all around;
remaining vigilant, they protect the dwellings of those who are asleep.
Thus, O Rādhikā, that radiant night passed away;
then, in the morning, everything became filled once more with all manner of divine auspiciousness.

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-first chapter, titled "The Description of Sending the Saffron Letter to All Creations after Writing It, the Great Festival of Betel Leaves, Areca Nuts, and Other Items; and the Festivities of the Night, including Singing, Dancing, Instrumental Music, Dramatic Performances, Martial Arts, Poetic Recitals, Rewards, and Feasting, as well as Leisure and Sleep," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the second section, the *Tretā-santāna*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Then, O Rādhikā, the great honors were awakened by the auspicious musical instruments at dawn and by the songs of the Sūtas and Māgadhas.
At dawn, the people were awakened by the recitations of bards, by the natural sounds of musical instruments, and by melodious songs of praise.
At dawn, the people remained awake to the sound of musical instruments played for four hours that invoked the memory of Brahmā, and to the resonant chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s praises.
The people stayed awake until dawn with songs sung by fortunate women, hymns performed by maidens, and the singing of professional singers.
On the shore of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake, the people kept vigil at dawn amidst the songs of the Maṇḍalīs and the resonant chanting of hymns from the sacrificial altars.
With enthusiasm, reflections, dispositions, acts of faith, virtuous conduct, and gentle activities, the people remained awake at dawn.
Due to the impelling of the Inner Controller, the weight of their intense love,
and the thundering of the celestial chariots, the people woke at dawn.
At dawn, the people were awakened by the sweet warbling of birds, by the sight of the festival for Kṛṣṇa in their dreams, and by the songs of the housewives.
At dawn, the people kept vigil with milch cows and their calves, with the sounds of musical instruments and singing, and with the resonant proclamations of the arrival of the great festival.
Driven by their merits, as well as by restless impulses and the force of their desire for knowledge, the people woke at dawn.
Having bathed in the waters of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake and performed the twilight prayers and other rites,
they adorned themselves with ornaments and offered blessings and auspicious invocations at the gates.
Having cleansed them with curd and powders, they fashioned decorative creepers,
and likewise placed multi-colored arches in the courtyards.
With eyes adorned with applied collyrium, their hair dressed in braided tresses, and wearing bright garments and ornaments, the women sang auspicious songs. (13)
O brahmins, they performed the worship of Gaṇeśa and the worship of the pavilion;
they performed the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the worship of Bālakṛṣṇa.
They performed the worship of their family deity, Puruṣottama,
as well as the worship of Śrī Śaṅkara and of the Sun.
Then they performed the worship of the deities of the Sarvatobhadra [mandala],
as well as the worship of cows and the worship of young maidens.
Then they performed the worship of the Mātṛkās and the worship of Viṣṇu;
they offered the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), excellent food offerings (naivedya), and gave sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) and other gifts.
They performed the worship of the Brahmins as well as the worship of turmeric;
the women, having ground it, prepared balls of turmeric paste with knotted centers.
Eagerly, they mixed together sandalwood paste, sesame paste, musk, saffron, and excellent fragrant oil.
Then, for the purpose of bathing Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa,
women adorned with the splendor of good fortune brought warm water and water from sacred pilgrimage sites.
The maidens brought auspicious water in golden jars;
indeed, they carried the water accompanied by the sounds of musical instruments and songs. 21.
Having placed [the deity] upon a golden throne and worshipped the water-deity,
one should likewise cast in the five jewels as well as fragrant substances.
Having invoked the gods, the oceans, and the sacred fords there, and having invoked the nectar of immortality,
they bathed Acyuta with that essence upon the cloth.
Then the women massage his entire radiant body, which possesses the luster of ten million suns and a face as auspicious as ten million moons. (24)
His limbs are like ten million flashes of lightning; he dwells in ten million fragrances;
he bears ten million forms; and he is distinguished by ten million flavors.
A treasury of all excellent virtues, filled with all loveliness, a vessel of all beauty, and the abode of all desirable qualities. ||26||
They, who remove the impurities of the stainless one, excessively crushed Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord who bestows all nourishment.
With oils possessing fragrant flavors, with perfumed substances that remove impurities, with *āmalaka* fruits, with sesame pastes, and with brightly shining alkaline substances. (28)
Eagerly, they bathed [the image] with soft substances such as fresh butter and nourishing pastes, as well as with fragrant sandalwood and other perfumes.
Then the barber performed the shaving as was appropriate;
thereafter he bathed with honey and then with water mixed with sugar.
The Lord himself bathed with milk, ghee, and curd;
and thereafter, he bathed again with honey and sugar as well.
Then he bathed with alkaline substances and with fragrant pastes;
then with oils, musk, sandalwood, and saffron.
By rubbing himself with flour paste, Campakabhū took his bath;
having thus performed the flour-bath, he put on his garments.
Having put on all his ornaments, garments, forehead marks, and so forth, as well as the moon-crest,
the Lord himself then sat down upon the golden throne.
Then, people came for the purpose of applying the tilaka mark and for the worship of Hari;
likewise, women, local dignitaries, and others arrived as well. (35)
Thus was the glorious Bālakṛṣṇa worshipped along with Piṣṭika;
indeed, a fragrant scent issued forth from his body in every direction. (36)
Indeed, Saurāṣṭra became fragrant from afar;
at that time, those of great honor arrived by means of aerial chariots.
From all directions and from all the worlds, Śaṅkara, Kṣetrapāla, and the great sage Nārada arrived. ||38||
The Blessed One, as well as Śuka who follows him, are self-luminous; likewise are the Blessed One and those beginning with Santuṣṭi. (39)
All those dear to Brahmā, being eager, offered a warm welcome;
indeed, meals and drinks of milk were served.
All kinds of foods, both solid and soft, are served from the kitchen, and rows of seats are indeed prepared for all the inhabitants of the world. (41)
They partake of many sweet foods with feelings of love, and they lick all kinds of things to be licked and sucked, as well as various flavors. ||42||
They drink milk-porridges and the like, they eat foods roasted with alkaline salts, and they relish curds as well as butter and clarified butter. (583)
The female bees consume balls of food and even fried cakes;
they drink nectars that are as sweet as ambrosia with deep devotion.
They secretly eat vegetables, various kinds of meat, fragrant boiled rice, and blossoming cakes, as well as their favorite polikās. ||41||
At that time, people were eating cakes, sweetmeats, laddūs, khājās, mohanasthalīs, and many other delicious and auspicious foods. 46.
Rivers of clarified butter, rivers of curd, and rivers of honey flow forth;
those capable of digestion drink them, and the enjoyers eat them. (47)
In this place, the attendants such as Lakṣmī and others provide in every way all those things appropriate for the inhabitants of each respective abode. (48)
Chewing-sticks (tāmbūla) are offered from inexhaustible vessels and similar containers, as well as from kalpa-vessels and the like, to be used for cleansing the mouth after eating.
Then the honored guests partake of water for drinking and auspicious powder that cleanses the mouth; thereafter, they proceed to their respective quarters.
Thus, O Rādhikā, a magnificent festival then takes place;
indeed, millions of great souls arrive there from all directions. (51)
Those who had gone to the abode of Brahmā and were liberated, as well as those residing in other abodes and all those dwelling in every realm who were liberated, gathered there.
Others who were liberated through Sāṃkhya and Yoga, as well as the beloved consorts of Brahmā, arrived;
and the Īśvaras and Īśvarīs also came together, full of eager anticipation.
There, the incarnations and those who bring about incarnations arrived with eager anticipation;
the lords of lords and the goddesses of lords likewise arrived.

Those who had gone to the world of Māyā were liberated, and others who were liberated arrived; those who were liberated from the eight coverings were liberated, and others who were liberated from them arrived. ||55||
The liberated ones who have reached the world of truth (satyaloka), the virtuous great seers, those devoted to celibacy, the holy ones, and the perfected beings (siddhas) all assembled there. ||56||
The ancestors, sages, elders, and perfected beings (siddhas) arrived; truthful, virtuous, and dispassionate goddesses also gathered there.
The Mātṛkās, the noble Yoginīs, and the Yogins arrived;
the gods, the lords of the gods, and the deities also arrived. ||58||

Also those dwelling in the fixed stars, those residing in the world of the lunar mansions, those who inhabit the planets, and those situated in the intermediate space who dwell within the circles of the sages. ||59||
The gods who dwell with the sun and the moon arrived there;
the daughters of Brahmā, the daughters of the gods, and the daughters of the Pitṛs also arrived.
Clad in lightning, clad in clouds, and dwelling on Mount Meru, they arrived;
the guardians of the directions, the guardians of the worlds, and the lords of the eight cities arrived as well.
And those dwelling in the Bhuvarloka, whose bodies are composed of air, arrived;
as did the Gandharvas, the Cāraṇas, the Siddheśvaras, and even the ascetics.
Aquatic creatures, land-dwellers, and sky-goers arrived,
as did yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas who were his devotees.
The Vaināyakas, the Kūṣmāṇḍas, and the Vaiṣṇavas arrived there;
the household deities, the village deities, and the forest deities also assembled.
Likewise, the forest-dwelling gods, sages, and even humans, as well as all the Gandharvas and others, and the ascetics, arrived there. (65)
The Siddhas, Vasus, Sādhyas, Kinnaras, and Kiñjanas, as well as the Vidyādharas, Kāmadeva, and others, along with their wives, all arrived. (66)
Dharma, the lineage of Dharma, and the wives of Dharma arrived;
likewise did the animals, the lower creatures, and the birds, all of whom possessed the memory of their former births.
Insects, moths, trees, creepers, and grasses arrived;
wish-fulfilling cows, kalpa-creepers, and kalpa-vessels also arrived.
The aesthetic sentiments, the varieties of the erotic sentiment, the goddess Śāradā, as well as the musical notes, the qualities, and the types of weapons arrived there in embodied form. (69)
The Vedic injunctions, the sacrificial Puruṣas, and the Vaiṣṇava fires likewise arrived there,
and the articles for ritual service came in embodied forms.
Rivers, streams, oceans, ponds, wells, and lakes, as well as sacred fords, mountains, and forests, all came there. (7.1)
People belonging to all four castes, both men and women, also arrived;
they came from the southern and eastern regions, as well as from Prāgjyotiṣa.
They arrived from the hot region of Uṣṭrabhāga and from Brahmadeśa;
they arrived from Piṅga in the eastern land and from Jalapāna. ||73||
They arrived from Rāśiyāna and from Trivitta; they also came from Śāmbhava, from the snowy regions, from Kashmir, and from the land of Orala. ||74||
They came from Kiṃpuruṣa and Ketumāla, from the islands and oceans,
from Ārakta and Abrikta, and likewise from Sāmudradvīpa.
They arrived there at that great festival from the northern regions of Tarka;
they also came from the vicinity of the Ārārtrika and from within the earth.
And how did they come from Uttarakuru, as well as from Kenāraka, from the region of Brāhmīla, and from the region of Hārītaka? (77)
And they arrived there for the great festival from the region of Amarīka,
from the region of Varāsana, and from the region known as Mākṣika.
And all those dwelling on the islands of the ocean, traveling by means of celestial chariots, arrived full of eager anticipation from regions free of dust.
The kings, the groups of servants, the fathers of the maidens, Bālakṛṣṇa’s father-in-law and others, and the members of their families all arrived. || 2.282.80 ||
The ṛṣis, the zodiac signs, the male rivers, the female rivers, the maidens, the prosperities, and the supernatural attainments also arrived from all sides. ||81||
The gods dwelling in Atala and the other regions, as well as the Daityas, Dānavas, and Āsuras who were possessed of devotion, arrived there as devotees. ||82||
The Nāgas, serpents, and elephants of the quarters, as well as the Śaktis who protect the creation, all the Vedas, all the sciences, and all the arts arrived together. (83)

Those on the mother’s side, those on the father’s side, as well as those belonging to the daughter’s side; those on the sister’s side, those on the wife’s side, and likewise their respective kinsmen. ||84||
Relatives connected through lineages arrived;
those belonging to the side of disciples, the side of devotees, and the side of sages all assembled. ||85||

Those belonging to the side of the mantras, those belonging to the side of the regions, and those belonging to the side of the subjects arrived; as did those on the side of the family members and those who followed the sides of their own partisans. (86)
Men and women, gods and goddesses, arrived there for that festival, accompanied by their servants, friends, allies, and followers. (87)
Those who were in union with Him, engaged in worldly affairs, and dwelling together arrived;
[there was] the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the beloved of Śrī, Mādhava.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa bears Lakṣmī, who is Kṛṣṇā, born from Śiva, upon the earth;
she is the daughter of Śiveśvara, the illustrious Lakṣmī herself, who is Nārāyaṇī. 89.
Lakṣmī is offered unto the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who is without beginning;
she shall indeed be eternally attained by Him, the Supreme Person, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Lakṣmī has half of her body as Kṛṣṇa; she is indeed Kṛṣṇa and her very self is Kṛṣṇa.
Kṛṣṇa has half of his body as Lakṣmī; he is indeed Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
On this earth, the identity of Kṛṣṇā with Kṛṣṇa arises;
oh, even though they must depart, the union of the two Kṛṣṇas is indeed perfect! || 92 ||
Likewise, the lords of the celestial realms and even humans, having been liberated from their abodes,
come with eager hearts, thinking, "A great union of the two Kṛṣṇas is occurring."
Children, the elderly, and the young, as well as those of the third gender—men and women alike—come together, for this is the auspicious union of the two Kṛṣṇas. (94)
At the bridge over the lake, Nārada heard the words of the ants:
"We shall obtain excellent food and shelter; there will be a great meeting between the two Kṛṣṇas. (95)
Indeed, the messengers of Dharmarāja hear these words in hell:
"We shall quickly attain liberation; there is a perfect union of Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī."
Having heard only the words regarding imprisonment, the onlookers thought, "We shall suffer confinement; there will be a great union of the two Krishnas. || 97 ||
"The virtuous and learned ones, even upon hearing the words of the mendicants, will consider giving [us] to the two Kṛṣṇas as the best course, for it would be a most auspicious union. (98)
Even the words of the poor and those burdened by debt were heard:
"We shall attain freedom from debt; it is a great fortune for the two Kṛṣṇas. (99)
Even the words of the servants were heard to be full of enthusiasm:
"We shall receive a reward when the two Krishnas are united in marriage."
Among the caravans that have set out upon the road, this word is heard in their conversation:
"One must proceed very quickly, as soon as the auspicious conjunction of the two Kṛṣṇas occurs. (101)
"Families of maidens are coming to Lake Aśvapaṭṭa; we shall go there together with the army at an auspicious conjunction of the two Kṛṣṇas. || 102 ||
At the time of bathing, the great sages indeed heard these words from the aquatic creatures:
"We shall obtain food during the excellent conjunction of the two Krishnas. (103)
The words of the ancestors, born of joy, were heard:
"We shall attain satisfaction at the śrāddha during the excellent conjunction of the two Kṛṣṇas."
In the forest, the voices of the predators were heard observing their restraint:
"No one should be harmed for seven days; this is an auspicious conjunction of the two dark fortnights."
Even the gods heard the words of dharma for eight days: "The period of celibacy must be observed by the two Krishnas during this auspicious conjunction. (1.06)
The words of the wise were indeed heard with great eagerness:
"We shall sing the *Sāman* right there at the auspicious union of the two Kṛṣṇas."
We have heard the words of those devoted to action: "We shall go to behold them, and we shall learn the path well during the excellent conjunction of the two Krishnas."
The principles regarding inauspiciousness dispute with one another;
however, inauspiciousness must be abandoned in favor of the auspiciousness of the two Kṛṣṇas. (109)
Having gathered together, they quickly departed from their own place, saying, "An evil omen has arisen;
the wicked nature of the two dark ones must be thwarted through ritual action. (2.282.110)
The planets also contend that cruelty must be abandoned during the eight days;
thus, no fruit [of such acts] should be given on the auspicious days of the two dark fortnights.
A certain old man, with withered limbs and a crooked waist, walking with a staff, breathing heavily and speaking quickly, says: "The marriage of the two dark ones has taken place. (1.12)
Upon seeing the saffron leaf-messenger, all the inhabitants of the world prepared for the arrival, thinking, "The wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas is at hand. (113)
And cows that grant all desires, accompanied by their calves, approached slowly and eagerly to the beautiful Aśvasara lake, thinking it to be an auspicious omen for the two Kṛṣṇas. || 1.14 ||
Even those engaged in their own occupations, having set aside their work, go to the field of Aśvapaṭṭasara, saying, "It is auspicious for Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī. (11.5)
And the farmers, abandoning their cultivation and bringing even the fruits from the gardens, went joyfully to Aśvasaras, exclaiming, "It is an auspicious omen for the two Kṛṣṇas! || 116 ||
Having shaken off the impurity of birth and the observance of vows with great difficulty, those who follow the auspicious conjunction of the two Krishnas go joyfully to Lake Ashva. || 1.17 ||
"Those dwelling in all the worlds perform the preparatory rites;
indeed, gifts should be given according to one's ability during the auspicious conjunction of the two Krishnas. (118)
"Even after accomplishing the impossible, one must go quickly to the pavilion," so say the spirits, "for the wedding of the two Krishnas is at hand. (119)
Thus, words devoted to the Blessed One were heard concerning Rādhikā;
by reading or hearing these, one shall attain both heaven and liberation.

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Morning Auspicious Visions, Divine Worship, Bālakṛṣṇa’s kneading of the flour, his bath, adornment, the arrival of the three worlds, the meals of the great ones, and the attainment of enthusiasm by Kṛṣṇa and [Rādhā] born of their auspicious union," in the second section on the Tretā Age of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Just as it was at midday, so too at night there were excellent foods suitable for everyone; having eaten and drunk water and other refreshments, [they rested]. || 1 ||
Taking betel leaves and night-ointments,
they all went to the arena to watch, and there they beheld ever-new wonders.
Then, having avoided the visible objects of perception and the various arts and crafts, they took up sleep and tranquility; thus the morning of the third day arrived.
During the Brāhma-muhūrta, embodied beings constantly remained awake amidst auspicious sounds of musical instruments, songs, and the recitations of bards.
Whatever musical instruments exist in the universe were indeed played there;
and the great sages, having bathed, being joyful, and having performed their twilight prayers, [were present].
They came indeed to Bālakṛṣṇa to bestow their blessings;
he had performed his ablutions, was dressed in his attire, and was seated upon a supreme throne.
Having bestowed their blessings, the Brahmins applied the *tilaka* and *candraka* marks;
they performed the worship of Gaṇeśa and the consecration of the water-pot (*kalaśa*).

They performed the Nāndī-śrāddha and other rites, and they carried out the worship of their preceptor; they performed the propitiation of the family deities and likewise conducted the chanting of the Vedas.
They performed the worship of the Sarvatobhadra deities and of Viṣṇu; the dignitaries on all sides partook of milk and other refreshments.
Then, beginning from morning, embodied beings prepared meals for populations numbering ten million, a hundred billion, a trillion, a quadrillion, and even a parārdha.
Having made preparations on all sides during the third watch,
at an auspicious moment, all the people became ready from every direction.
At that time, there were thousands upon thousands of celestial chariots belonging to those who followed the path of yoga in order to proceed toward Kāśī.
All the mounts were adorned and made ready;
indeed, all of them were capable of traveling through the sky, being suitable for a yogic expedition.
The excellent father proclaimed: "Let all those whose nature is devoted to the yoga-journey come to the purifying Kāśī; Śiveśvara desires this."
Śaṅkara, accompanied by his Gaṇas, shall protect this sacred field in every way;
he shall also protect the city, the hermitages, the pavilions, and so forth.
Upon hearing this, all the great dignitaries became ready—foremost among the subjects of Surāṣṭra, the preeminent of created beings, and those worthy of honor. || 16 ||
All of them were dear to Brahmā and devoted to every effort for Kṛṣṇa;
their fathers and all other relatives resided throughout the entire earth.
Listen, O Rādhā, to that wonder which was produced, bestowing amazement;
a celestial voice was heard clearly from all sides. (18)
In all three worlds, those by whom their own daughters were given to the Supreme Self, Bālakṛṣṇa, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, within the span of fifteen years—[to them I bow]. (1.9)
Since all of them, including the father and others, must certainly come there,
they will indeed become bound by the union with the Fortune of Śambhu.
According to the ritual prescribed by the Vedas, according to the Mānava rite,
and also according to the Vāhnaya rite, through the formal procedure for the giving away of a maiden.
"In order to avoid deficiency and in accordance with local custom, the ritual procedure shall be performed after circumambulating the fire from left to right. (22)
And indeed, by all the maidens who dwell in the hermitage of Lomaśa,
who are the beloved consorts of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
One must indeed come along with the army of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, together with one's father, family, and kinsmen; there shall be no obstruction.
Having heard this, all the people and their families, eager and accompanied by women, prepared themselves with all necessary materials and suitable implements;
and all the maidens likewise became fully prepared in every respect.
Lomaśa, other sages, and virtuous great seers [were there]. || 26 ||
The virtuous and noble guests became ready from all sides,
accompanied by ornaments, garments, celestial chariots, and other such things, numbering in the tens of millions.
O Rādhā, at that time, the joy of the maidens could not be contained within their bodies;
they were surrounded on all sides by chests filled with every kind of erotic ornament and decoration. || 28 ||
They quickly became ready and went to the abode of Kṛṣṇa;
at that time, the fathers and mothers of the maidens also arrived there swiftly. Having reached the abode of Kṛṣṇa, they [reported] the arrival of the maidens as well.

And by means of the Vāhinī [divination], they reached a firm conclusion and became joyful in heart. At that time, for all of them, auspicious omens repeatedly occurred; indeed, all the omens present were entirely favorable for everyone.
The auspicious omens that appeared were indeed bestowers of the highest yoga, bringers of fame and renown, and ensured the fruit of one’s undertakings would be free from obstacles;
they were accompanied by cows with their calves, whose faces were bright and filled with joy.
The wish-fulfilling cows gathered together, discharging streams of milk. || 33 ||
Abounding in all kinds of elegant ornaments and overflowing with every joy,
the maidens gathered together, and the courtesans also assembled.
Grains of grain with ripe and fresh ears, curd, well-adorned elephants, and the queen of kings accompanied by her mother-in-law arrived there;
as did swans, royal swans, and maidens carrying water. || 35 ||
The Gandharva women, beautifully adorned, also gathered together and sang.
The vision of the gods also became manifest in the sky,
and at that time, there were sightings of Lakṣmīs and lotuses.
The sounds of musical instruments, bringing auspiciousness, were heard;
and the Vedic mantras of sacrificial oblations, bringing welfare, were heard. (38)
The appearance of white objects occurred spontaneously, and the sacrificial fees, the fires, and the winds became favorable. (39)
And there were most auspicious words of the guru’s blessings;
all the men and women,
having gathered their belongings and finished their meals and drinks, remained stationed at Kuṅkumavāpikā.
Having presented their offerings, the people, filled with devotion and accompanied by their families—belonging to all classes, including their servants, friends, and kinsmen—became ready;
and ten million prepared celestial chariots quickly stood at the ready. || 41-42 ||
Then, at the commencement of the expedition, there arose the sound of the auspicious conch Pāñcajanya for the sake of performing a rite of blessing.
Then Gopālakṛṣṇa indeed gave gifts by the millions—
especially to maidens, brahmins, and children—
including sweet foods, sugar, and various kinds of fruits.
At that time, he gave garments, ornaments, vessels, jewels, and wealth;
he bestowed gifts of cows and donations of gold and silver.
At the commencement of the pilgrimage, he performed the worship of Gaṇeśa. || 45-46 ||
There is the Sarvatobhadra worship, the honoring of the elders, and salutations to one's family deity as well as to Puruṣottama, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow. || 47 ||
There he beheld Lord Viṣṇu and likewise performed the worship of Śrī; he made offerings and gave away countless gifts as well.
Having paid homage to the deities of the sacred sites, he worshipped the deities of the gateway.
Having worshipped the cows, Bālakṛṣṇa then fully honored the celestial chariot; he also worshipped the Vedic deities at that time,
bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, and adorned with a crown.
He was adorned with earrings in his hands, he held a golden sword,
and he quickly assumed a magnificent attire, beautified by necklaces of diamonds and other jewels.
Clad in all kinds of silk and golden attire, he was the most excellent of men;
his forehead was marked with saffron tilaka, and he was fragrant with exquisite perfumes.
Adorned with ornaments on his forearms, upper arms, waist, limbs, and fingers, he shone resplendent.
Endowed with splendor, he shone like the moon marked by the lunar spots. ||53||
His mother, Śrīkaṃbharā-Lakṣmī, applied the tilaka upon him;
his sister, named Santuṣṭā, placed a crescent moon on his forehead and gave him a garland for his neck; and Ujjayinī-Śukapatnī presented him with necklaces of jewels and pearls. || 54 ||
Amṛtā placed [an ornament] upon the neck of Hari and applied collyrium to his eyes; Śaṃvatī dressed his hair with oil,
and Ramā likewise applied red lac to the palms of his hands.
Then Māṇikī applied lac-dye to the soles of her feet,
while Lakṣmī offered garlands of lotuses and golden necklaces.
Hāsā gave a cluster of flowers; Mañjulā gave an armlet; Ambā fashioned a jewel of light; and Sugandhā cast a rosary of beads. || 58 ||
Having thus adorned themselves, the beloved wives of Brahmā and others, as well as the maidens who had dressed themselves in their finery, stood ready. Likewise,
the other brothers, headed by Gopāla and Kṛṣṇa, also arrived.
There were also other brothers born of Bālakṛṣṇa’s father,
as well as hundreds of daughters, boys, and girls,
along with thousands of sons, grandsons, sisters, and kinsmen.
Then those kings who were the fathers of the maidens, as well as the other rulers of the earth, quickly became ready, having indeed partaken of food and drink.
|| 61 || They too certainly became ready, having partaken of food and drink. || 62 ||
At that moment, there arose the sound of kettledrums and likewise the blast of conchs,
along with a deep rumbling that signaled their ascent into the celestial chariots.

Then Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa and the virtuous Lakṣmī Śrī-Kambharā ascended a magnificent celestial chariot together with their family and belongings; indeed, all the beloved wives of Brahmā also ascended that celestial chariot.
The sages, headed by Lomaśa, ascended a magnificent celestial chariot;
the virtuous ones, wearing horse-hair garments, also ascended a celestial chariot.
The people of Kuṃkumavāpikā ascended the celestial chariot;
King Svarṇāṅgada also ascended, together with the full extent of his lineage.
Raṇaṅgama also ascended, and Lakṣmaṇa indeed ascended;
the deities of the sacred fords ascended, and the common people ascended as well.
And millions of magnificent celestial chariots ascended;
O Rādhā, listen now to the names of those foremost among them, even if only briefly.
And fourteen thousand Meghanādas have been made ready;
and there is Ṣaṣṭhī, the goddess Manasādevī, who is always the protector of children. (69)

Her forms indeed became millions of maidens for the Dīpāvalī festivals; having adorned themselves with festive attire, they joyfully ascended the celestial chariot from Lomaśa’s hermitage by the command of Acyuta.
Talajā, the daughter of Tala, who had become a divine Rākṣasī, also ascended a celestial chariot here by the command of Mādhava. (71)
Then, by the command of Bālakṛṣṇa, ten million maidens who were like wish-fulfilling cows quickly ascended the celestial chariot there.
Then, by the command of Bālakṛṣṇa, the hundred daughters of the Rākṣasa Arjuna, together with Vasumatī, ascended the celestial chariot.
At the command of Mādhava, the wrathful daughter of Hara ascended,
along with ten thousand crores of daughters of the Earth accompanied by the Earth itself.
Then, ten million divine beings known as Gahvaras, adorned with all kinds of ornaments and garments and emboldened, ascended the celestial chariot. (75)
Sūcī, the daughter of Vedhas, ascended a celestial chariot,
and a hundred thousand daughters of forest deities also boarded the aerial vehicle.
The maiden named Oṣadhī was with her mother, the forest goddess;
and there were also a hundred thousand maidens known as Damanā and others, who were protectors of the Rākṣasas. ||77||
Adorned with ornaments, garments, and the like, they ascended the celestial chariot; six young maidens, as beautiful as fresh *kaṅkatālī* flowers, also ascended.
And noble women such as Kaṅkatālā, along with ten thousand divine maidens,
all adorned with every kind of ornament, ascended the celestial chariot.
The divine hundred thousand maidens of the ancestors, beginning with Aryaman,
sat together with their fathers in a celestial chariot, beautifully adorned.
By the command of Kṛṣṇa, five thousand well-adorned maidens of the Daityas dwelling in the netherworld ascended a celestial chariot. 8.1.
Then, sixteen springtime maidens, beautifully adorned,
ascended the celestial chariot by the command of Bālakṛṣṇa.
Five hundred daughters of the Daitya Tālamāla, well-adorned, ascended the celestial chariot at the word of Kṛṣṇa;
likewise, twenty thousand Nāga maidens did so as well.
Well-adorned, they ascended the celestial chariot by the command of Mādhava.
Then, a thousand daughters of Śāvadīna, beautifully decorated,
also ascended the chariot by the command of Bālakṛṣṇa.
Then, by the command of Kṛṣṇa, a thousand daughters of illusionists, adorned with ornaments, ascended the celestial chariot;
likewise did Sarasvatī and the maidens known as the fourteen branches of learning.
Likewise, sixty other maidens of beautiful form ascended the celestial chariot.
Then King Lakṣmaṇa emerged there from within the earth;
he too swiftly ascended his own most excellent celestial chariot along with two thousand of his own maidens.
Seventy-two thousand maidens known as Nāḍikās,
the daughters of Brahmā, ascended their own celestial chariot;
Viśvāvasu, with three hundred of his own daughters, likewise ascended a celestial chariot.
Then, full of longing, he ascended the celestial chariot of King Jumādagni, which was accompanied by a thousand maidens who had adorned themselves with beautiful ornaments; they too,
having been made radiant by the adornments prepared by their own fathers, ascended the vehicle.
A hundred maidens, virtuous and well-adorned, together with their Brahmin fathers, ascended the celestial chariot;
likewise, the three daughters of Mahābāleśvara then ascended along with their father. || 92-93 ||
And King Dakṣajaṅgharo, the sovereign of Uṣṇālaya, ascended a celestial chariot that was well-adorned and decorated,
together with his hundred beautiful daughters and a thousand daughters of his subjects. || 94 ||
Having taken [them], she ascended the well-adorned celestial chariot.
Twenty daughters of Aryaman and another ten thousand—
all of them together with Aryaman— ascended that celestial chariot.
Ten million daughters of Prajāpati,
adorned and accompanied by their respective fathers, ascended a divine celestial chariot. Of the brahmin Santāraṇa, two daughters were likewise adorned.
And the two daughters, together with their father, ascended the celestial chariot.
Thus, O Rādhikā, the maidens remained at the hermitage of Lomaśa, accompanied by their fathers and others, as well as by the sage Lomaśa and their mothers and others. || 98–99 ||
By the command of Kṛṣṇakāntā, they quickly sat down in the celestial vehicle—

adorned with finery and filled with longing, thinking, "This is the wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas," while regarding their own Kṛṣṇā as [the other] Kṛṣṇa and acting out of piteous devotion for Kṛṣṇa’s sake. (2.283.100)
"Bound by an inseparable connection with Kṛṣṇa, this is the wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas!"—
thus did all the women, filled with enthusiasm and making every effort, sing with the joy of their own festival that "this is the wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas. (101-102)
Then other maidens also ascended the celestial chariot;
O Rādhikā, I shall describe to you those beloveds of Kṛṣṇa who were adorned with ornaments.

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Morning Duties on the Third Day of the Bright Fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa in the Second Tretā Cycle of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā; the Midday Meals and other rites; thereafter, the preparations for the auspicious journey toward Kāśī; the adornment of Śrī Hari; the performance of auspicious ceremonies; and the boarding of the celestial chariots by the Brahmapriyās and Dākinyas. || 283 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhā; even those maidens born in regions such as Rāśiyāna who were beloved of Kṛṣṇa ascended the celestial chariot. || 1 ||
Then King Śibideva, together with his hundred daughters and accompanied by his family and attendants, ascended his own celestial chariot.
The great king Tharkūṭastha, accompanied by fifty maidens,
ascended his own celestial chariot, eager for the bridegroom’s procession.
The great king Vīrajāra, accompanied by his hundred daughters,
ascended his own celestial chariot, eager for the bridegroom procession.
Śaktākṣa, the lord of the earth, was also accompanied by sixty maidens,
as well as one hundred and one Piśācī maidens.
Eager for the bridal procession, he ascended his own celestial chariot;
two hundred maidens from the royal house of Kāliṅga also ascended the chariot.
Together with their parents, all of them, beautifully adorned, ascended;
and then Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa [ascended] with Rādhikā.
On the ruby [throne] are Śrīṃ, Ramā, Lakṣmī, and Padmajā;
and on the celestial chariot are Ambā, Hāsā, Sadguṇā, and Mañjulā as well.
He likewise seated Parāvidyā and the others— forty in number—
in the celestial chariot, adorned with every kind of ornament.
King Uralaketu, accompanied by thirty maidens,
ascended a beautiful celestial chariot for the sake of his supreme journey.
King Kratha, accompanied by five maidens, likewise ascended an excellent celestial chariot for the sake of a pilgrimage to Kāśī; he was as gentle as the moon.
Then King Pṛthu,
that best of travelers, ascended his own celestial chariot accompanied by twenty maidens.
Ten maidens of Uṣṭrāla ascended the celestial chariot;
King Haṃkāra, accompanied by five maidens,
also ascended the chariot for the very purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī.
Then King Jayakāṣṭhala, accompanied by five maidens,
ascended a celestial chariot for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī.
King Tīrāṇa, accompanied by six maidens,
ascended a celestial chariot for the very purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī.
Accompanied by five maidens and his family, Ālvīnara likewise ascended an excellent celestial chariot for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī.
King Jīnavardhana, eager for that purpose, ascended a celestial chariot accompanied by his seven daughters in order to perform a pilgrimage to Kāśī. || 17 ||
Then Anāthavipra, together with that one daughter alone,
ascended the celestial chariot for the sake of the chariot procession.
The scattered maidens who had been liberated from the Rākṣasas ascended two hundred and one thousand celestial chariots.
King Alpaketu with seven maidens,
and the royal sage Jayakṛṣṇa likewise accompanied by one maiden, [ascended] the celestial chariot.
And King Parīśāna, accompanied by twenty-one maidens, ascended a single magnificent celestial chariot.
And King Indurāya, accompanied by his two daughters, ascended the celestial chariot (vimāna) which was filled with every kind of ornament.
Extremely delighted, King Mudrāṇḍa, accompanied by fifteen maidens, ascended [the chariot] which was adorned with every kind of ornament. (23)
Then Gaṇḍarāja, accompanied by the nine maidens, ascended that excellent celestial chariot for the purpose of his yogic journey.
And King Līnorṇa, accompanied by his four daughters, ascended [the ship] for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī. ||25||
And King Bṛhacchara, eager for the journey of Kṛṣṇa, ascended the celestial chariot accompanied by his eleven sons. (26)
Then King Balalīna, accompanied by forty maidens, ascended the celestial chariot for the purpose of his yogic journey.
King Varasiṃha, accompanied by his five daughters, ascended his own opulent and adorned celestial chariot.
Then, for the sake of the pilgrimage to Kāśī,
King Rāyagāma ascended the celestial chariot accompanied by five thousand maidens.
He ascended the celestial chariot accompanied by three other maidens,
and the two queens also ascended the chariot, which was richly adorned.

Then King Phenatantu, accompanied by his two daughters, ascended a magnificent celestial chariot for the very purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī. And King Stokahoma, accompanied by his one daughter, [ascended] a celestial chariot.
Then, for the sake of the pilgrimage to Kāśī, he ascended a magnificent [palanquin].
A certain daughter of King Kāṣṭhāyana, accompanied by her father,
also ascended a splendid celestial chariot (vimāna) intended for a spiritual journey.
Then the daughter of King Kolaka also ascended a magnificent celestial chariot for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī.
Thus, O Rādhikā, those Gaurīs [departed] solely for the sake of the beloved of Kṛṣṇa.
Eager, having performed their adornments and being beautifully decorated, they attained great joy.
King Arka, the measurer of days, accompanied by his two daughters,
ascended his own celestial chariot for the sake of a successful journey through yoga.
And King Rāyakinnararāja, resplendent with prosperity, ascended the celestial palace Sarvasmṛddhi accompanied by fifty-one maidens;
likewise, King Rāyarokīśvara [ascended] with twenty-one maidens.
Then, taking his own celestial chariot, he indeed ascended it;
and King Rāvaṇajit, accompanied by twenty maidens,
ascended his own magnificent chariot for the sake of the supreme journey.
King Rāyavākakṣaka, accompanied by his three daughters,
ascended his own celestial chariot for the sake of a divine journey.
King Rāyamārīśa also, accompanied by his three daughters, [ascended his].
King Rāyabaleśvara,
accompanied by his three daughters,
ascended his own magnificent celestial chariot, eager for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī. || 41-42 ||
Then King Rāyalambāra, accompanied by six maidens,
ascended a magnificent celestial chariot for the sake of his journey.
And King Rāyanavārka, accompanied by seven maidens, likewise ascended.
Then King Rāyahuṇḍeśa, accompanied by the nine maidens, ascended his own magnificent aerial chariot (vimāna) for the sake of the journey;
he then mounted that chariot which was endowed with every prosperity.
Then King Rāyakūpeśa, accompanied by his only daughter,
ascended a celestial chariot for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī; likewise,
King Kālīmaṇḍalī, joined by four daughters, [ascended].
And he ascended a magnificent, supreme celestial chariot for the purpose of his journey.
Then King Vanajaleśa himself, accompanied by the five maidens,
likewise ascended that beautiful celestial chariot.
Then the lord of Pārāvārapiba, accompanied by his three daughters, ascended a celestial chariot endowed with all prosperity. Thereafter, King Koṭīśvara, accompanied by his two daughters, [ascended].
And then he ascended that auspicious celestial chariot, endowed with every prosperity.
Then the three daughters of King Śrī Satīśa, together with their father,
ascended a magnificent and auspicious celestial chariot intended for their journey.
And King Tretākarkaśa, accompanied by seven maidens,
then ascended a magnificent celestial chariot for the purpose of his journey.
King Āṇḍaja, accompanied by his four daughters,
also ascended his own chariot for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī.
Then King Bālyaraja, accompanied by his only daughter, ascended a magnificent and auspicious celestial chariot for the sake of the pilgrimage to Kṛṣṇa. 54.
Then King Rāyasomanabhūpa, accompanied by his three daughters,
ascended a celestial chariot for the purpose of the pilgrimage to Kṛṣṇa.
Then King Urugavākṣa, accompanied by his two daughters,
ascended his own magnificent celestial chariot for the sake of the journey.
Then King Parāṅmukhavratas, accompanied by his two daughters,
ascended a celestial chariot for the purpose of a pilgrimage to Kāśī.
And King Īśānapāna, accompanied by forty-one maidens, ascended his own opulent celestial chariot. ||58||
The king, the lord of wealth and sovereign, ascended his own magnificent palanquin for the journey,
accompanied by his thirty-three daughters.
The maiden, the sister of King Rājārāya and the wife of Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, ascended her own celestial chariot. (2.284.60)
Maṅgalā, Lalitā, Revā, Bhārgavī, Sarasvatī, Ramā, Gaṅgā, Dayā, Bhakti, Muktī, Ekādaśī, and Rati. ||6 1||
Kāmadughā, Tulasī, Kamalā, Virajā, Satī, Mūrti, Gomatī, Svarṇarekhā, Jayā, and Nandinī. (62)
Vanitā, Mohinī, Dolā, Puṣpā, Prīti, Kalāvatī, Mādhavī, Badarī, Campā, Kuśalā, Manu, and Maṇi. (63)
Śānti, Śāntā, Ramā, Haimī, and Ūrjā were seated in celestial chariots;
the others, adorned with ornaments, were also accompanied by Lomaśa.
And all those who have been mentioned, O friends, are indeed in their billions;
they are adorned as the daughters of Kubera, Indra, and Yama.
The Vāyavya, Vaiśvakarmya, Vārkṣya, Raudrya, and Vahnijā; the Śrāvaṇya, Khānijya, Sāṃvatsarya, and Gopikā [offerings]. 66.
The Prācīnyas, the Piśaṅginyas, the Rāśīyanyas, the Samuṣṭrikās, the Romāyanyas, the Pāraśvas, the Dhaivaryas, and the hosts of Kinnarīs. ||67||
And likewise the immortal ones, the Gaurīs, the Paryas, the Hāritikas,
the Ābriktyas, the Pātālyas, and the celestial Apsarases.
The two daughters of Brahmā, the Gandharva maidens, and the adorned daughters of Arbuda,
together with Lomaśa and each of their own fathers, were in their respective celestial chariots.
They each ascended their own precious, opulent, and fully equipped vehicles;
thus, O Rādhikā, the beloveds of Kṛṣṇa then became ready. (2.284.70)
Then other great sages who had come for Kṛṣṇa’s procession,
such as Hemaśālāyana and others, sat down upon the palanquin.
Cakravākī and Urvaśī, Hanumān along with Agastya, the sages headed by Maṅkaṇaka, and Devāyatana as well. ||72||
The Ṛṣis beginning with Meṣāyana, the sage Lālāsana, Pradhī, the five thousand Sāntas, as well as those beginning with Vṛkāyana; ||73||
Yavakrīta and others, as well as Śvetavyāsa and his peers,
and Sanatkumāra and the rest, also ascended the celestial chariot.
Tuṣita, Hārita, Divimāna, Āyana, and the others; Kuśala, Yoginī, and also Sāṃkhya-yogin;
Śāvadīnā, Mahākālī, Vārinara, and Kṣetrapa. ||75||

Then, for the sake of Kṛṣṇa’s journey, the sages beginning with Āryāyana, the doorkeeper Brahmanādaka, the sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha, and those such as the Vālakhilyas, all ascended celestial chariots. (76)
O Rādhikā, at that time, the letters were liberated, as were all other [entities] on every side; likewise, all the male incarnations and female incarnations were liberated.
Adorned with all kinds of ornaments, all the attendants who dwell in the abode, as well as the residents of Vaikuṇṭha, ascended their celestial chariots.
Vāsudeva and others, as well as the vast Viṣṇu, the radiant one;
and likewise the sattvic sages, the Siddhas, and the virtuous ones.
Adorned and highly prosperous, the Pitṛs, as well as Aryamā and the other world-protectors who guard the quarters of the sky, ascended their celestial chariots.
Then the Ādityas, the Vasus, the two Kumāras, and likewise the Aśvins,
ascended their celestial chariots for the sake of Kṛṣṇa’s journey.
The Maruts, the Siddhas, the Nidhis, and the auspicious planets;
the Sun and Moon, the Seven Sages, Dhruva, the Mothers, and the Directions. (82)
Kāmadeva, the Manus, the Kalās, and likewise the Tithis; the Tattvas, the lunar mansions, the Guṇas, the sacred fords, the rivers, and the streams. ||83||

The celibate students, those who have renounced worldly ties, the trees known as divine deities, the wish-fulfilling creepers, the wish-granting stones, and likewise the household deities and so forth—[all these are present here]. (84)
The temples and the sacred shrines likewise ascended the celestial chariot,
as did the nāgas, serpents, daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas.
Charioteers, bards, panegyrists, and wandering singers, as well as Brahmins, learned scholars, Kiṃpuruṣas, and Kinnaras—[all gathered there]. (86)
Gandharvas, storytellers, and millions of male and female servants,
all adorned with every kind of ornament, ascended celestial chariots that were beautiful to behold.
Artisans, goldsmiths, wealthy men, and likewise performers of sacrifices, as well as the gurus mentioned by Lomaśa—all these reside at Kuṅkumavāpikā. 88.
They ascended their celestial chariots, thinking, "The wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas has taken place";
the Earth herself, remembered there as Medinī, arrived at that spot.
The seasons arrived, and Dharmadeva himself was remembered;
then Nara also arrived from the Badarī forest.
And the goddess Akṣaravāsinī arrived with her pedestal; they mounted upon the well-formed seats and the flowing substances. 91.
Then the one known as Maṇḍapa, being liberated, arrived;
likewise, Māṇikya, who was indeed a pillar, also came before Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (92)
Likewise, Hara, the protector of the sacred field, having bowed down in the presence of Śrī Hari and taken his seat upon an auspicious throne, [held] the Sudarśana discus. 93.
Then their illustrious father, Gopālakṛṣṇa, forbade them and said to these nine for the purpose of protecting the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpī: || 94 ||
"Protect this field indeed; we shall go to Varāṇasī.
Having said this, [he gave them] the necessary equipment, weapons, and rewards. (95)
Having given [these], he prepared a ready celestial chariot as radiant as the sun's orb,
and adorned Bālakṛṣṇa, his brothers, the Lord, and the others.
Likewise, the wives of his brothers, the groups of his paternal kinsmen, from children to the elderly, the members of his household, and all his relatives were placed upon the celestial chariot. 97.
He seated the groups of men and women related to him, who had come down through generations,
upon celestial chariots and caused them to raise shouts of victory.
Kettledrums were also sounded, signaling the commencement of the procession; they produced auspicious sounds from their two-fold resonance, reaching the ears of all. 99.
And at that time, during the commencement of the journey, there arose the sounds of the musical instruments of the Gandharvas,
and the noise of the trumpets became like the roar of clouds.
"May the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa be ever victorious!"—
thus spoke the divine voice then, moving through the sky.
The celestial chariot of Bālakṛṣṇa, augmented by auspicious offerings such as flowers and unbroken rice grains presented by Devikā and others, proceeded toward the eastern direction.
Then, celestial chariots resounded with songs in the sky,
accompanied by the splendor of joyful people, following after him as he proceeded on his way.
Thus, O Rādhikā, the celestial chariot carrying them moved forward;
filled with the procession of Kṛṣṇa, it shone brilliantly as if swiftly ascending to heaven.
Joy could not fit within the heart of every single embodied being; a great exultation arose at the thought, "The wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas has taken place! || 105 ||
Having crossed the Maru country, the Kośalas, and the Madhyadeśa,
and having passed beyond Prayāga, the army proceeded toward Kāśī.
Seeing Kṛṣṇayānī roaring, resembling a thousand moons and having the form of a celestial chariot, Śiveśvara was exceedingly delighted.
The inhabitants of Kāśī, filled with eager anticipation, also went forth, saying, "O Rādhikā, let us go; the wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas is at hand!"

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Ascension of the Great Kings, Maidens, and Sages into Celestial Chariots, and the Departure of Kṛṣṇā and Others for Kāśī," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, having beheld in the sky the army in the form of celestial chariots, as well as the glories of Śaṅkara and King Śiveśvara; || 1 ||
Having paid homage to Kṛṣṇayānī, he then quickly commanded all those skilled in musical instruments, as well as the cowherds and others, to come for the purpose of welcoming her. || 2 ||
And those skilled in the science of musical instruments played the finest of musical instruments;
and then, pleasant sounds of music arose, filling the expanse of the sky.
Auspicious sounds produced by brass, beautiful sounds produced by kettledrums, those produced by instruments such as the *vyaṅgula*, and those produced by conch shells that travel far; || 4 ||
Likewise, sounds arising from peacocks, the resonance of flutes and lutes, those produced by water-machines and the like, and those born of the throat, bring about auspiciousness. (5)
There arose sounds produced by clay drums, hand-claps, and the like, as well as those generated by fire-machines;
there were sounds made by the wind and songs sung in the sky.
There were the throat-sounds of the apsarases and the songs of the yoginīs;
sweet were the resonances of Sarasvatī from the women of the Vedas and other [scriptures].
There, the beloved sounds of those traveling to the ends of the sky reached far; and those auspicious sounds were heard from the celestial chariots in the atmosphere.
Having heard those sounds, the inhabitants of the celestial chariots, overcome with wonder,
beheld that vast and beautiful land of Vārāṇasī.
Then all those traveling in celestial chariots beheld the city named Gaṅgāvaraṇa,
ten yojanas in extent, which was like Vaikuṇṭha itself.
And on the following day, they beheld the vast,
newly constructed city of Śiva, twenty yojanas in extent, situated on the bank of the Varaṇā.
And we, having summoned Viśvakarman, had another Kailāsa constructed, or perhaps another Goloka. || 12 ||

Those traveling in the celestial chariot perceived that divine object— which was established like Mount Kailāsa, fashioned with ten million moons, possessing the radiance of ten million suns, situated upon many terraces in the sky, or perhaps fixed upon a trident— to be indeed Kailāsa itself. (13)
Indeed, that city was constructed by Śiveśvara for the sake of celebrating the auspicious festival of his daughter and for her residence of honor;
it was resplendent with golden ramparts and adorned with ten million palaces.
It had beautiful golden halls, was adorned with golden domes,
was distinguished by a golden banner, and possessed a hundred stories on all sides.
Wherever the city of Kubera is, there likewise is the city of Īśāna;
the city of Indra is in the corner, and the city of Agni is in the intermediate corner.
The city of Varuṇa is where Dharmapurī is at its corner;
the city of the Maruts is at one corner, and Brahmapurī is at the other corner. || 17 ||
Likewise, Sūryapurī and Viṣṇupurī shine in the corners;
in the center are the abodes of the gods, palaces with a hundred stories.
With their sides covered by gardens and water-stations, and filled with exquisite fragrances,
they were white like the snowy mountains and resembled the moon.
All the new palaces have been constructed, resting upon every kind of prosperity;
the moon-chambers shine resplendently like those situated in the path of the planets.
For there, upon the walls, were jewels emitting natural radiance, and indeed, within the crystal lattices,
there was natural light.
Upon the archways there are wish-creepers dripping with nectar;
upon the pillars, in their upper regions, there are wish-trees.
And in the gables there exist rivers of milk produced by the power of desire;
and there is heat according to one's wish, arising from the wish-fulfilling trees.
And throughout Śivapurī, in every palace as well as on the grounds of every palace, there dwell wish-fulfilling cows (kāmadhenus). ||24||
Divine maidens, capable of assuming any form at will, moving through the sky, and bestowing happiness, exist as Kalpa-maidens established upon each respective level. ||251||
Male and female servants of divine complexion were present, as well as attendants;
all of them, divine and born of his mere resolve, were then stationed there for the purpose of service.
There were also body-massagers, singers, and dancing women;
all of them born of his mental resolve were established there by Śaṅkara.
All tastes, all fragrances, and all beautiful forms; palaces, all sounds, and all tactile sensations come to be. || 28 ||
There were altars where there existed the splendor of golden seats, lion-thrones, and elephant-seats, as well as beds that were soft and delicate. (29)
There are various kinds of grass mats and comfortable couches; there are divine coverings made of silk on every side.
There were woolen cloths, soft and delightful, variegated and auspicious; they were dyed in many colors, shimmering with various forms, and served as coverings for the seats. ||3.1||
There were balls, side-pillows, and soft cushions; hidden armlets of priceless value, and golden bracelets. (32)
And indeed, Śambhu has placed within those very palaces swings and hammocks,
along with creepers and provided with soft beds.
There, celestial chariots— even those of small size— hang from creepers for the purpose of beautiful swinging, as if they were moving upon the earth.
And by way of the air-courses, there are moving beings in every house; and through which [openings], people on the upper floors [reach] their respective dwellings. (35)
They enter and emerge from the path of the sky in celestial chariots;
even the stairways there are fashioned with ladders and adorned with jewels.
All the vessels there are made of gold and are like celestial kalpa-vessels; there are inexhaustible bowls and kalpa-jars abound.
In every house there were floors entirely made of jewels;
in every house, mirrors of transparent nature shone forth. (38)
And the doors of the gods consist of the vision of creation;
likewise, chests, caskets, and so forth, are indeed inexhaustible and meaningful.
All kinds of beautiful garments are found in every house,
as well as vessels for fragrant substances, oils, and saffron.
In every house there are indeed vessels of musk and camphor;
there are streams of liquid, streams of curd, streams of honey, and granulated sugar.
In every house there are stalks of sugarcane, streams of clarified butter, pools of nectar, jars of cream, and likewise lakes of ambrosia. (42)
There were also collections of fruits, flowers, and lotuses from the ponds,
as well as stores of bulbs— both fresh and dried— and seeds.
In every house there were implements for weapons, for beautiful stages, and for gambling; as well as instruments for hearing and for sight.
There are statues of Caityaputrikā, as well as factories for perfumes, kitchens, schools of learning, and underground chambers in every house. (45)
In every house there were mountain caves, bath-halls, and kitchens;
in every house there were halls for drinks, halls for peace, and halls for pleasure.
In every house there were secret sleeping chambers and balconies;
there were various pleasure rooms and diverse bridal chambers. (47)
The old-age homes are easily accessible and provided with all necessary articles;
likewise, purification halls and cleansing rooms exist in every house. (48)
In every house there were diverse halls for enjoyment, fully equipped with all necessary means, as well as assembly halls and pleasure pavilions. 49.
All vehicles— those born on land, those born in the ocean,
and even those born from the wind, including animals— were stationed at every door.
Great lions are at the gate-towers, elephants are stationed at the crossroads, Garuḍas are above the temples, and tigers are atop the gate-towers.
The Paryas, the Apsarases, the Gaṇyas, and the hosts of Yoginīs—
these sentient beings dwell there, devoted to the service of Mahīmāna.
O Rādhikā, a special distinction was established there by Śaṅkara,
such that wherever his house exists, it is for the very purpose of his dwelling.
He alone, like a reflected image, shines together with his own family,
appearing as if endowed with activity— whether he be a king, a god, a Daitya, or even an Asura.
Likewise, that reality is hidden within the secret walls of palaces;
whoever dwells in such a palace becomes double-formed.
Delusion arises for all; who here is real and who is other?
Those who do not know the original image wander after its reflection. (56)
Having turned away from the fruitless, they indeed search for the reflection; deprived of the knowledge of reality, they mistake the delusion for valid cognition. //57//
Seeing land in water and water on land, and fire in water, those who pride themselves on their greatness wander about, perceiving the sky upon the earth. (58)
And Śaṅkara is also seen everywhere in a subtle form; this is the Māyā of Śaṅkara manifested there within the palaces. (59)
And the god Anila (the Wind) attends upon him in service with fans, maintaining the highest honor according to his requirements, delighting the minds of all.
Aditi and Annadātrī exist in the form of maidens;
having appeared through the power of resolve, they depart into invisibility after giving. ||61||
By Śaṅkara, medicinal herbs were placed in every palace and every house; there were golden trees with fresh clusters of *vijayā* flowers.
The skins of lions, tigers, and other beasts, as if still possessing life, were displayed in the center of beautiful palaces in every house.
Ornaments for women, as well as beautiful garments, and vessels filled with the liquid essence of passion were placed in every house. (64)
All kinds of foods—those to be chewed, those to be eaten, those to be licked, those to be sucked, those to be tasted, and those to be drunk—are stored in every house. (65)
In every house, Śaṅkara has established a single, full vessel of moonlight that bestows nectar like a cloud and grants happiness. (66)
And Vāsanta was summoned and established in Śivapattana;
such is the city of Śiva, the dwelling place of the bridegroom's party. (67)
All those traveling through the sky beheld that wonderful creation of Viśvakarman;
they saw a second, beautiful, and excellent city belonging to Pārvatī.
That which was constructed for the purpose of providing a residence for the dignitaries on the bride's side is not deficient in any respect,
nor even in the slightest degree regarding its materials.
On the ground of the Varaṇā plateau, twenty yojanas in extent,
it stands situated between two divine and newly built cities.
The palace of the Lord of Pārvatī shines forth, possessing ten thousand peaks;
it was fashioned by Viśvakarman and embellished by Maya.
O Rādhā, in the city of Pārvatī, it truly shone like the peak of Mount Meru situated between the moon and the sun, belonging indeed to Śiva. 72.
And those who belonged to the side of Kanyā, O beautiful one, stayed there overnight;
indeed, Śaṅkara, the Lord of Beings, was accompanied by ten million attendants.
Piṅgarāja, Śaṅkara, and Īśāna, who resides on Ketumāla; Kāmarūpā, Satī, and Kāmākṣiṇī—they all dwelt there.
The king of the nine islands of living beings, named Kāmanāyaka—
all these Śaṅkaras dwelt in the city of Pārvatī.
The Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is indeed the manifest father of Śaṅkara;
he dwelt there together with millions of cowherd women and cowherds.
The Lord Saṃkarṣaṇa, whose form is the cosmic manifestation (vyūha) and who has ten million attendants,
dwelt in the city of Pārvatī accompanied by ten million Kṛṣṇas.
Mahāmāyā, the power of Kṛṣṇa, also resided there;
and Mahākāla, the sustainer of the world, accompanied by old age and death, was present.
And there dwelt the Lord Sadāśiva, who possesses sovereignty equal to ten million Śaktis; for he is indeed the father of Vairāja. (79)
He too, accompanied by Śiva, dwelt there in the city of Pārvatī;
likewise did all the Rudras, the Rudrīs, and the hosts created by Rudra.
The Mahimās lived happily in the city of Pārvatī,
while Śiva resided on Kailāsa accompanied by ten million Gaṇas.
Yamarāja dwelt in that city accompanied by ten million messengers,
and Agni and all the various deities also resided in that city.
Kubera, Nirṛti, and the circle of Yoginīs, as well as Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Pretas, and Piśācas; ||83||
The Vaināyakas, the Kūṣmāṇḍas, the Vetālakas, and likewise the Gaṇas;
the Vetālīs, the Śākinīs, the Ḍākinīs, Caṇḍikā, and the others. ||84||
The Mothers who practice celibacy, the Durgās, and those who are Śaktis;
likewise the Kālīs, Mahākālīs, Bhairavas, and the Bhadrakās. ||85||
They have entered the city of the mountain-dwelling Saudhama, where they sleep in comfort;
they are lords residing in Vaikuṇṭha, and likewise beyond the unmanifest (avyākṛta).
There indeed resided those who abide in immortality, as well as the followers of the Sun and the Moon, the Nyūṣus;
likewise the sages, the perfected ones (siddhas), the yogins, the ascetics (avadhūtas), and those who bear sectarian marks (liṅgins).
The yogins and the ṛṣis, as well as the ancestors, have also dwelt here;
so too the planets, the stars, the lunar mansions, and the comets. ||88||
At that time, the Daityas and Dānavas dwelt in that city, as did the celestial guardians of the worlds (Lokapālas) and the guardians of the sacred fields (Kṣetrapālas), among others. 89.
The inhabitants of Bhuvarloka, the purifiers, the family deity Hanumān, the human beings, the kings, and the lords of serpents dwelling in Pātāla; ||2.285.90||
Likewise, Hāṭakeśa, the Praśaktis who are of the nature of light, the Gāndharvas, the Gaṇikās, and the Sūtas, Māgadhas, and others. ||9 1 ||
The Vidyādharas and Kinnaras, as well as the Himālaya and other mountains, the sages, the fevers, the obstacles, and those who practice with poisons; ||92||
Trees and creepers, as well as cruel beings who were the very forms of Time, and scorpions and other creatures capable of assuming any form at will, dwelt in the city of Pārvatī. (93)
These and other great beings, the attendants and followers of Śaṅkara, all residing in the city of Pārvatī, looked up at the sky. (94)
And perceiving that Kṛṣṇa’s army was approaching through the sky, they quickly became alert at the temple of Śiva with the sounds of their two-fingered whistles. 95.

Accompanied by their families and others, taking refuge in auspicious sounds such as musical instruments, and adorned with the splendor of ornaments and attire, they arrived for the sake of a welcome.
Then all the people of Vārāṇasī also gathered together,
considering their own fortune and merit to be blessed because of the wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas.
Possessing fruits, as well as flowers and garlands of wreaths, they quickly followed after the temple of the Lord of Pārvatī. 98.
Śiveśvara quickly [returned] to his own Kailāsa, as well as to the divine Puruṣa Himādri, who was likewise divine and very extensive. ||99||
And in the region of the sky, he spoke of the spot supporting the celestial chariot,
so that it might become most divine there for a moment as a welcome offering.
O Rādhikā, these Kailāsa and Himālaya have immediately become a divine,
firm foundation in the form of earth, serving as a carpet in the intermediate space.
There, they fashioned another new abode, Kailāsa;
then Śiva and his followers quickly ascended into the sky.
In the new and beautiful palace, for the sake of welcoming the army,
the people following [the king] who were situated in celestial chariots beheld a wonder in the sky.
Beholding the great sovereignty of Śiveśvara, they were then struck with wonder;
they then praised Hara, who is of the nature of Brahman and whose self is Brahman.
Seeing the abundant wealth of Mahālakṣmī’s father, the Lord of Pārvatī, Śrīmad Gopākṛṣṇa and the others were filled with joy.
Upon seeing Kṛṣṇayānī, Śaṅkara and the others were indeed filled with joy;
and beholding her supreme majesty, they then became utterly enchanted.
O Rādhikā, Lakṣmī, who removes the pride of the two [Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī], is a young maiden;
and Bālakṛṣṇa himself, who removes their pride, is a young boy.
When there is a suitable meeting here between portions of two Blessed Lords, their portions indeed blossom; this is the "marriage" of the two Kṛṣṇas.
Wherein I am your beloved—Kṛṣṇa, Saṃkarṣaṇa, and Śiva;
wherein Viṣṇu, Mahāviṣṇu, Bālakṛṣṇa, and the Supreme Lord reside.
All the creators of the universe are present there; what wonder could there possibly be, O Rādhā, since the marriage of Kṛṣṇa and [you] is being brought about? 2.285.110.

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Sounding of Musical Instruments Caused by Śiveśvara for the Purpose of Honoring the River of Kāśī; the Vision from the Sky of Kāśikā, Śivapura, and Pārvatīpura; the Description of the City; and the Construction of Kailāsa in the Sky for One Ghaṭikā, wherein Śiveśvara, accompanied by the Earth and the Mind of the Maidens of Pārvatīpattana, Welcomes the River," in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, within the second section, the Tretā-Santāna.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, there on that vast Mount Kailāsa situated in the sky,
fifty yojanas in extent and endowed with all-surpassing opulence— || 1 ||
Within a beautiful and great garden, in a splendid golden pavilion fit for entry upon the royal road, Śrī Śaṅkara and the others took their stand.
And they showed him these celestial beings situated in their aerial chariots nearby,
as they were slowly descending from the sky toward that divine realm.
It was entirely golden in color, possessing the form of Mount Kailāsa,
beautified by a city of gold and filled with wish-fulfilling trees.
At that time, it was filled with trees bearing fruit in all seasons, produced by supernatural power,
and adorned with auspicious great groves containing millions of resting pavilions.
It was endowed with trees beautiful with blossoms and fragrant with scent,
and it was surrounded on all sides by landing-places for celestial chariots.
Then that vast city was shown to him,
along with the level grounds suitable for dwelling on all sides.
O Rādhikā, Bālakṛṣṇa and the others, as well as the great sages, kings, maidens, saintly persons, deities, and so forth, [all boarded] their own celestial chariots. || 8 ||
The liberated Īśas, as well as the Īśvarīs, the Pitṛs, the Mānavas, and others,
indeed possess their own aerial chariots (vimānas) which take the form of their respective retinues.
Then, full of eagerness, they brought them down upon the grounds of Kailāsa,
while hundreds of thousands of auspicious musical instruments were indeed sounded.
They played instruments that were both fierce and sweet, providing great delight—
those belonging to Goloka, to the nectar, and even to the unmanifest.
Of Kailāsa, of Kubera, of the Earth, and of the inhabitants of the asura realm;
of the Daityas, of the species of beings, and likewise of the Gaṇas and the Yogins;
of the Yoginīs, the Gaṇikās, and the women of the Gandharvas. || 12 ||
On all sides, musical instruments were sounded for Caṇḍī and the others;
and atop the walls of the golden city, which were lined with trees,
as well as upon the pinnacle of the great palace, stood the celestial chariot of Bālakṛṣṇa.
And it descended slowly and came to rest steadily within the circle of trees;
likewise, other celestial chariots also descended individually into separate groves of trees.
Having descended, they each attained stability upon their own respective palace-tops.
O Rādhikā, I beheld that wonder of Śaṅkara:
he assumed as many forms as there were celestial chariots, and Bṛhaspati likewise assumed as many forms there. || 16-17 ||
I, however, stood before the aerial chariot of Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa together with Śaṅkara, my preceptor, Vāmadeva and others,
as well as Vyāsas, Brahmins, and sages who held vessels worthy of worship.
[The worship was performed] with flowers, unbroken grains of rice, liquid offerings, parched grain, saffron, and bilva fruits;
accompanied by fragrant flower garlands and the like, with the chanting of the Vedas,
with words of auspicious benediction, and with jars filled with water for worship.
For the sake of sweet food and drinking water, he was accompanied by numerous attendants bearing golden vessels and other utensils,
as well as by countless female servants carrying trays of sweets and similar delicacies.
[He was accompanied] by female attendants and others bearing water-vessels and the like, adorned with such forms, and provided with fly-whisks, fans, and so forth;
as well as by groups of divine servants equipped with parasols, vessels, and other [regalia]. || 22-23 ||
Together with groups of cane-bearers, weapon-bearers, and those who obeyed his commands— all of whom were skilled in the offering of perfumes and honors, provided with fruits and betel,
full of mental respect and courtesy, and endowed with all pleasant speech— [he entered].

[He was served] by groups of attendants who provided excellent and superior seats and knew how to wash his feet; who were cognizant of his gestures, diligent in their duties, and ready to grant whatever was required;
as well as by young male and female attendants skilled in ritual preparations. || 25–26 ||
There, joined by the wicks of our volitions, I was Śaṅkara, as well as Bṛhaspati and others; we were there seeking to welcome [the guest].
Just as everything occurred with me, so did all of that happen.
In every place, there appeared a celestial chariot for the purpose of welcoming them.
Listen, O Rādhā, to another wonder born of Bāla-Kṛṣṇa:
then the Lord, beholding Śrī Śaṅkara assuming many forms, [acted]. || 28-29 ||
The Lord Bālakṛṣṇa also, accompanied by his family and joined by Lomaśa,
assumed those respective forms and suddenly descended from the celestial chariots, each separately.
Śaṅkara, too, was filled with great wonder upon beholding Mādhava.
Indeed, Śaṅkara then assumed various forms along with all those embodied beings situated in their celestial chariots, for the sake of honoring them.
However, because those who travel in celestial chariots have indeed surrendered their very selves,
they do not take even a leaf or anything else without first offering it to Bālakṛṣṇa.
If they then accept offerings made without devotion, there will be a loss of the food offered by the self; Śaṅkara would become a partaker in the fault. (34)
To avoid that fault, the Lord, the Master Bālakṛṣṇa, having understood [the situation], accepted the worship individually for each. (35)
Then Śaṅkara, the foremost of all, descended from all the celestial chariots, accompanied by all his divine manifestations and all his various forms. (36)
He indeed offered worship to Kṛṣṇa, who is the Supreme Brahman itself; meanwhile, Hari, having received that honor, bowed down to the venerable ones, beginning with Hara.
Having inquired after his welfare and announced his own well-being, and having received words of blessing, he vanished from that spot to another place. (38)
Then the Lord Śambhu became steady in his own principal celestial chariot, while Bṛhaspati and the others performed the worship of the great ones.
Then they performed auspicious rites according to the prescribed rules with Vedic mantras;
they inquired after each other's well-being and freedom from ailment.
The father and mother of the excellent maiden, as well as all their kinsmen and relatives, inquired after his welfare and then embraced him with their chests. 41.
"Welcome! they exclaimed with beautiful words, and being filled with eagerness, they quickly offered him honor by washing his feet and other such services. ||42||
With seats, offerings of honey-mixture (madhuparka), gifts of fragrant water, flower garlands, sandalwood paste and the like, and the presentation of floral wreaths and other ornaments; ||43||
The lords honored them with parched grain and unbroken rice,
as well as by offering handfuls of flowers and by touching their chests.
On suitable grounds, Niṣādas [served him] with golden lion-thrones and the like, in groves and golden palaces, by offering handfuls of water. ||45||
Then they performed auspicious hospitality, offering sweet foods, drinks such as milk, and gifts of betel leaves.
With fans, chowries, and the display of the royal staff, as well as by massaging their feet and other such services, they offered various forms of welcome. (47)
Then the magnificent palanquin of the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa was indeed adorned with abundant parched grain, unbroken rice, flowers, and other offerings. 48.
Thus, amidst shouts of "Victory!", the Lord of Śrī descended from his celestial chariot,
accompanied by welcomes, flower garlands, and handfuls of flowers.
He was nourished with barley sprouts and sandalwood;
and Śambhu inquired after the welfare of Gopāla Kṛṣṇa.
The followers of Kṛṣṇa were questioned by the devotees of Śaṅkara regarding their welfare and health;
then likewise, the goddesses and maidens, such as Kātyāyanī and others, [were questioned].
Durgā and the others, as well as Satī, Kambharā and other women,
and even the young maidens, inquired after his welfare and freedom from ailment.
They welcomed him with honey-mixtures and other offerings, with the gift of water and delicious food,
and they honored him with betel leaves and the like, as well as with garlands and other ornaments.
Then, by means of various seats and likewise through attentive service, the women indeed brought about the increase of the honor of the ladies of the earth.
Also by joining the palms in supplication due to suffering, by pressing the chest [in prostration], by offering all that is appropriate, by sweet words, and by services; ||55||
Jayaścaṇḍa, Dhenupāla, and other devotees of Śiva offered honor and a warm welcome to the families of Bālakṛṣṇa. (56)
Then Queen Aśokasundarī and her female friends welcomed Santuṣā and the other maidens, as well as the young girls who were their companions.
Then millions of maidens and Śāṅkarīs also performed a welcome for the girls with offerings, food, and service. ||58||
They also inquired after the welfare of the subjects,
and the kings likewise inquired after the welfare of the other monarchs at that time.
Then the gods among the deities, millions upon millions of liberated souls,
and even the sages among the seers, inquired after his welfare.
The lords of lords performed the rites of welcome and so forth,
and at that time, groups of women offered honor to the ladies.
Śaṅkara said: "I am blessed that the Blessed One himself has come to my house as a mendicant, a worthy recipient of merit for the sake of my daughter."
Blessed is this delightful city of Kāśī and its people as well;
blessed indeed is Satī and Lakṣmī, in whose very home the Blessed One resides in person. (63)
I am blessed, since today in my home there are indeed those liberated from worldly existence;
for here dwell Vāsudeva, the Lord himself, and the Viṣṇus.
Since virtuous men equal to Nārāyaṇa dwell in his house, and since sacred fords reside in his house today, I am truly blessed and fortunate. (65)
