Blessed are the trees and likewise the creepers; blessed are the insects and the winged creatures;
blessed are those who honor the earth, for here they have union with the Wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
In whosever home there are Sāttvatas, for they are indeed virtuous Bhāgavatas, and in whosever home there are even sages who purify the three worlds; ||67||
Today my Kailāsa has become supremely Vaiṣṇava,
since the abode of my Lord of Life now exists there in the sky.
Today all my attendants have become supreme Vaiṣṇavas;
today my name "Śiva" has truly become meaningful for me forever.
Having spoken thus, she shed tears of love from her own eyes;
and with joy, she made the turbid third eye clear once more.
Then the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa said to Rādhikā and Śaṅkara:
"We are truly blessed, for today we have obtained the sight of you. (71)
He who is the very form of the Supreme Brahman, the self-effulgent Lord Saṃkarṣaṇa,
and whose nature is that of Mahākāla— our meeting shall take place in his abode.
"We are blessed, O Great Yogin, O Destroyer of the World! By a mere fraction of your grace, this son of mine has today become worthy of receiving gifts. (73)
Blessed is my young Kṛṣṇa, for he shall obtain your daughter,
the virtuous Satī, who is the mother of all the worlds, the divine Brāhmī, and Nārāyaṇī.
Today Hari-Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Goloka, together with Rādhā, the Gopīs, and others, is present here, as is Śiveśvara, your father. (75)
Having obtained the vision of this Supreme Person of infinite nature, we are truly blessed; what other supreme fortune could there be beyond this? (76)
Having spoken thus, Śrī Kambharā bowed down to Śaṅkara and also to Kṛṣṇa; she then spoke likewise to Satī, expressing the greatness of her good fortune.
And Satī spoke of the auspicious greatness of her own fortune:
"Oh, blessed is my daughter, since the virtuous Kambharā is to be served by her! (78)
Today my home has become sanctified by the arrival of Mahālakṣmī, and my family has become sanctified by the arrival of the entire creation. (79)
The field of Kāśikā shall become a purifier and a bestower of liberation for the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Brahman.
Likewise, from the assembly of lords who bestow liberation, as well as from the assembly of virtuous men, chaste women, maidens, and goddesses. ||81||
From the arrival of the Mothers, the Apsarases, and the Brahmasaras;
from the arrival of the Īśvarīs, and from the union of Rādhā and Ramā. ||82||
From the *Kamalā*, *Tulasī*, *Lakṣmī*, *Māṇikī*, and *Śāradā* Āgamas;
from the *Ramā*, *Padmāvatī*, *Śrībhū*, *Līlā*, and *Vibhūti* Āgamas.
Indeed, through the arrival of the Muktānīs and especially the Vaiṣṇavīs, as well as the arrival of the devoted queens, this place has become blessed here. (84)
Today my birth has become fruitful, today my actions have become fruitful, and today my prosperity has become fruitful through union with the glorious Kambharā. (85)
Today my knowledge has become fruitful, my sovereignty has become fruitful, and my male and female servants have become fruitful through the union with Śrī Kambharā. (86)
Indeed, I am Pārvatī, married in the house of Śiveśvara;
together with my family, I have attained fulfillment, and I am the beautiful mother of Lakṣmī. (87)
Today Pārvatī realizes her own supreme good fortune, since the Lord himself will take as his daughter the young girl Kambharā. (88)
Having spoken thus, Kaṃbharāśrī and the others prostrated themselves;
then Kaṃbharāśrī said, "Today our [efforts] have also borne fruit."
"In whosever house we come and behold the virtuous Satī, Girijā,
in my house Satī’s daughter and Lakṣmī shall also arrive."
She is the nourisher of all the world; indeed, she is my supreme fortune here.
This virtuous Brāhmī shall become worthy of being honored as my daughter-in-law.
He by whose mere glance the three worlds are dissolved—he is to be worshipped today by my son, and my son is to be worshipped by him. (92)
"Aha! My fortune in the three worlds is peerless; no other possesses its equal.
Having spoken thus, the virtuous Kambharāśrī then bowed down before Satī.
The Goddess of the Mountain honored all the women who had arrived for a moment,
repeatedly offering them a welcome with honey-mixture (madhuparka) and other offerings.
By providing drinks of nectar and establishing sweet-water stalls, the two brothers, the Jayacandras, then took their rest with joy. (95)
Reflecting upon their own good fortune, the two rejoiced intensely;
the party of the bridegroom ceased, and a great sound of "Brahman" arose. (96)
Then, indeed, as they were about to depart toward the city of Śiva, Nandīśvara repeatedly uttered the Brahma-sound (Brahmanāda). 97.
Having fully worshipped Hari, Bṛhaspati then rose up; and after resting, the men and women likewise arose at that time. 98.
O Rādhā, listen to how it became a source of great wonder, full of marvelous and extraordinary events, for returning to our dwellings. ||99||
Everyone says that one must go toward the city of Śiveśvara;
by what method can one leave Kailāsa and travel through the sky?
Then, indeed, Śambhu swiftly brought down the entire Mount Kailāsa there gradually by means of his power of yoga. || 101 ||
Then, all of Śiva’s created cities— toward the earth, toward the city of Śiveśvara as was appropriate, and toward the city of Kailāsa— [were established].
Having descended, they entered within the interior; those who were in the gardens went into the gardens, and those in the groves went into the groves, as their bodies were perfectly equalized.
Then, in the palaces, the palace-dwellers likewise vanished;
and at that time, celestial chariots appeared in the places where the chariots had been.
Indeed, those very ones for whose sake the dwellings were previously ordained there are the Mahimānas who reside in those dwellings there.
The maidens sat in the maidens' quarters, endowed with happiness;
the kings sat in the royal palaces, and the virtuous men sat in the dwellings of the holy.
In the dwellings of sages there are sages; in the dwellings of gods there are deities;
in the dwellings of lords there are lords; and in the dwellings of the liberated there are the liberated.
O Rādhikā, Hari resides in the abode of Kṛṣṇa, while other deities reside in other abodes, according to their respective fitness within the dwellings of the three worlds.
At that time, his natural abode in the three worlds indeed vanished;
Kailāsa was seen to have dissolved away, leaving only the city of Śiva visible.
Having quickly reached their dwellings, they performed the purification of their baths;
thereafter, they indeed took their meals in magnificent mansions.
They took betel nut and then took their rest;
having gazed upon sights that delighted the mind, they then fell asleep.
Then the male and female servants performed tasks such as massaging the body;
Śiveśvara and the others returned to their own homes at night.
The honored elders on the bride's side, having partaken of the excellent feast, obtained rest and sleep; O Rādhikā, they became happy.

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Welcome, Prosperity, Worship, and Honor accorded by Śaṅkara through his many forms with musical instruments to Kṛṣṇavāhinī on the ethereal Kailāsa; the mutual inquiries regarding welfare and health among men and women, the disappearance of Kailāsa, the descent into Śivapura, the taking of food and so forth, and the rest for the night," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣ�ṇa said: O Rādhikā, having attained happiness through their services,
those great souls then became enjoyers of unprecedented bliss in the city of Śiva.
On the morning of the fourth lunar day, people [should go] to that divine city of Śiva, where everything follows one's intention and is present.
Awakened by musical instruments, auspicious sounds, and songs proclaiming his glory,
those who honored the earth abandoned their sleep and bathed according to the rites of purification.
They worshipped Hari, performed their Vedic study, and recited prayers;
and auspicious songs of maidens arose there.
In every house and in every courtyard, colorful patterns were created using curd, barley sprouts, saffron filaments,
and saffron pigments.
Svastikan and lotuses were fashioned here and there in front;
archways were set up and banners were fastened.
The sounds of musical instruments resounded in the pavilion and in every house.
And in the morning, rituals were also performed with warm water and other such means.
In the morning, however, everyone received milk to drink along with sweet food from Śivasvāmin according to their desire;
and the honoring of the elders was likewise performed there appropriately.
Then the daughter of Śiva, having bathed, adorned, and decorated herself,
bowed repeatedly to her father and likewise to her mother along with her female companions.
With a face like ten million moons, beautiful and adorned with every ornament,
she was accompanied by all the necessary materials on foot for the purpose of worshipping the family deity.
The virtuous Durgā set out to worship Hanumān,
accompanied by ten million maidens and attended by women blessed with good fortune.
Accompanied by female singers, delighted by the sound of musical instruments,
and surrounded by women whose heads were adorned with golden jars, she remained there.
Indeed, she is beautiful when surrounded by virgins equipped with the five products of the cow and other substances,
together with those who possess the materials and vessels for worship.
Adorned with garments as radiant as fire and endowed with all auspicious charms,
she first went to Durgā and worshipped the Supreme Goddess.
With the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), sandalwood and other [unguents], waters from sacred fords, and substances such as saffron, unbroken rice, musk, and the juice of filaments. || 16 ||
With fragrant flowers, garlands, and the like; with food offerings such as milk-rice (pāyasa) and other sweets; with drinks such as water, betel leaves, and gold ornaments. || 16 ||
With sacrificial fees and vessels, with lustration rites and hymns of praise, with circumambulations and prostrations, and with requests for forgiveness for one's offenses. || 17 ||
Then he worshipped Durgā, and likewise offered her a sari and a bodice; having presented her with a waist-belt, a night-gown, anklets, and rings.
He also gave him a chain, a girdle, golden necklaces, auspicious gems,
bracelets, bangles, rings, and a lotus.
She wore a string of pearls, golden earrings, leaf-shaped ornaments,
crescent-moon pendants on her forearms, bracelets, and other such decorations.
He gave everything to the goddess Durgā and then spoke:
"O Mother, may there be no obstacle to my union with the Blessed One in this marriage."
"O Durgā, you should always look for me wherever I go," [said Rādhikā].
Durgā also replied with a smile, "So be it. (22)
Having thus worshipped Durgā and obtained the fruit of her grace,
she went to Śrī Hanumān, who provides refuge for the sake of penance.
Having gone and bowed to the son of Vāyu, the divine brother of Śaṅkara,
he offered him the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), water, sandalwood paste, and a garland of arka flowers.
Saffron, unbroken grains of rice, a golden garland, vermilion, as well as oil, the essence of sugar-cane, and indeed ornaments and garments. (25)
Having given sugar, cakes, and auspicious sweet foods, and having offered water for drinking, mouth-cleansing materials, fruit, and a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), [he should proceed]. ||26||
Then, having performed the lustration rite (nīrājana), as well as hymns of praise and circumambulation,
Lakṣmī begged for forgiveness from him who is the companion to the perfection of asceticism.
"O brother, you who practice the yoga of the Blessed One, always protect me!
May my excellent yoga be free from obstacles through Bālakṛṣṇa, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow. (28)
"O sister, act in such a way that I may be happy with Jagannātha as my lord";
thus entreated, Hanumān indeed spoke to her.
"So be it; may you always be possessed of good fortune, O source of sorrow!
Then, having bowed down and received his favor, she departed accompanied by her own friends.
He approached his father, the Lord of the Universe, who was seated in the temple,
and honored Viśveśvara in many ways with milk as well as honey.
Having bathed [the deity] with curd, ghee, sugar, and water from a sacred ford,
one should worship with sandalwood paste and offer the food oblation.
Then, having performed the *ārārtrika* rite, he asked for forgiveness and entreated him for freedom from obstacles in his auspicious undertaking; [the deity] likewise replied, "So be it. (3.3)
The Lord of the Universe, his father, spoke; then he went to Annapūrṇikā, having likewise worshipped his mother and presented her with an ornamental gift.
He presented the offering and then performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana);
he then placed a crescent moon-mark with unbroken grains of rice upon the forehead of Annapūrṇā.
"May you possess unbroken good fortune and enjoy eternal life!
Thus she gave her blessing, and then the maiden bowed to Gaṇeśa.
Having worshipped Sarasvatī with offerings of dūrvā grass, vermilion, and sweetmeats,
he went to the Gaṅgā at Pañcagaṅgā and worshipped the god Dharma.
Having bowed down and having given gifts consisting indeed of gold and silver, as well as necklaces of gems and rubies, and precious stones and pearls; (38)
Then, having received the blessings of the subjects,
the virtuous lady bowed to Śivapura and departed for her own home.
Then at midday, she gave food to all her friends;
Lakṣmī, eager, performed the serving for her companions.
Then, millions of women from the Himalayas, the mountains, and the cities sat in rows on all sides and enjoyed sweet foods. ||41||
Indeed, the women, from children to the elderly, became satiated with the foods; likewise, the women who were honored on the earth attained the city of Śiva. 42.
All the maidens and others partook of the food, and thereafter the men dwelling in both parts of the city also ate. 43.
The inhabitants of Śivarājagṛha and the people of Kāśī—lords, gods, and humans alike—enjoyed [the fruits of their merit] by the millions, billions, and trillions. ||44||
He offered unwholesome, deluding foods such as black-gram *laḍḍūs*, fine pearls, powdered *laḍḍūs*, milk-preparations, *pāyasa* porridge, and milk-filled *polikās*. ||45||
Sweet polīs, pūrikās, sūtrapheṇī, barphikā, dugdhasārā, biranja, śaṣkulī, khājaka, and baṭīs. ||46||
Cakes, flour-cakes mixed with curds, *bindu-laddūs*, *prabharjikās*, *śrīkhaṇḍas*, *śatachidras*, *jāmbūkas*, and likewise *ghēvaras*. ||47||
Also balls of dough, knotted sweets, *kalikās*, *ghurghurās*,
as well as *vaṭas*, *phullavaṭīs*, and almonds coated in sugar.
Chickpeas and rice, both roasted and boiled, as well as soup with rice, thick gruels, and various kinds of vegetables. ||49||
There were various vessels as well as sudhā and amṛtakas; there were buttermilk, drinks, foods to be chewed, and excellent fruits.
Savors, linctuses, edible grains, and sour gruels; also parched rice, fried snacks, and seasoned condiments, all well-prepared. (5.1)
Likewise, sweet fruits and those with moist seeds,
as well as pods, mung beans, and gundrāpāka and similar vegetables.
Various bulbous roots, diverse ripened fruits, the finest tubers, even those produced from black mustard seeds, and whatever fruit-powders there may be— (53)
Wild tubers and cultivated tubers, medicinal herbs that ripen without cultivation,
and various excellent foods and delicacies produced by the wish-fulfilling trees (kalpavṛkṣa).
They ate and drank, especially nectars; Hara gave them the various foods characteristic of each respective world.
Hara gave to each of them drinks appropriate to their respective classes,
as well as beautiful betel rolls for cleansing the mouth, which were sweet to eat.
The illustrious Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world, also gave garden-enclosures;
then the dignitaries and even the guests partook of them. (57)
Beggars and wretched people, protectorless men and women, laborers as well as servants, male and female slaves, and even their followers; || 58 ||
The attendants, the gatekeepers, as well as the servers, the guards, and the spectators also ate with delighted minds. ||59||
Inert things and conscious beings alike, lords, gods, and humans,
as well as those who dwell within the three worlds and all the great beings here on earth— [all these were created].
All those great ones indeed became fully satisfied by the finest foods, and then for a moment they all attained rest. 61.
Then, in order to ascertain Śiva’s firmness of resolve, that illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa,
assuming the form of Śrīkṛṣṇa, the Lord of Śivā, went forth swiftly.
Having gone to Lord Śiva in secret, he said: "Listen, my dear;
I shall tell you here whether your son is worthy or unworthy; listen to me."
"May you know that whoever I know, I speak of him:
this Brahmin is indeed the son of Pativratā, and he is a mendicant. (64)
There is indeed one named Bālakṛṣṇa, who is like a child and of humble birth;
the king must by no means give his daughter to such a beggar. (65)
It should never be given to one residing abroad;
rather, the giving of a daughter in marriage to a man of equal birth is auspicious and brings happiness.
In this world, however, there would be suffering through one of a different species; of this there is no doubt.
Furthermore, this Kṛṣṇa is seen to be weak in body. (67)
O Dhavalā, your sons do not shine even in their pair;
I shall tell you something else: this Purāṇa is being observed. (68)
O Indra among kings, how can this delicate girl, so very young, as well as another maiden, be given to the prince? (69)
If you desire eternal happiness for your daughter, then you must give her away;
for Bālakṛṣṇa has indeed arrived here together with ten million brides.
In that regard, how insignificant will this young girl be in the calculation? But the quarreling of co-wives is more unbearable than poison or fire. (71)
Listen further: he indeed possesses the nature of devouring everything;
he consumes whatever is offered by all, for he has not even a single dharma.
Moreover, he is always free from deceit and devoid of the [three] guṇas;
furthermore, he constantly devotes himself to the conduct of a sage. (73)
He does not even know how to enjoy, for he is devoid of desire;
this is a mere illusion, and he does not know how to create an illusion.
Behold, his father is a cowherd who resembles a cowherd;
he bears the name Kṛṣṇa the Cowherd, yet relies upon a different occupation. (75)
"A daughter must not be given by a Kṣatriya to a Brāhmaṇa who performs forbidden acts;
having understood this in every respect, do as you wish. (76)
Having spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the child Kṛṣṇa, became silent;
but Viśveśva, having bowed to his father and reflected, spoke indeed.
O Father, the lines on my daughter's forehead indicate that she was previously destined to be given away in marriage there, along with one in the form of a Brahmin. (78)
Mahāviṣṇu himself, devoted to his wife, indeed dwells upon the earth;
through the vision of yoga alone, I know him to be his son, Puruṣottama. (79)
This [child] is always a beggar for those devotees who are full of affection;
yet he himself is the Supreme Brahman—how could his daughter not be given away? (2.287.80)
Hari, the bestower of welfare upon the ignorant, remains for the sake of the wretched;
he brings about both worldly prosperity and liberation for those who are pure yet possessed of an ignorant nature. (81)
Bālakṛṣṇa, Hari, the Lord and Sovereign of the Imperishable Abode,
was [offered] by me, the king, to the great queen as a mendicant bearing the Śārṅga bow.
A daughter should indeed be given away there, for therein lies the rise of fame and gain;
since the foreign land is the imperishable Brahman, why indeed should she not be given to him? (83)
By birth my daughter is equal to this Brahmin woman;
for caste is never born of the body, but always arises from one's qualities. (84)
My daughter Brahmī Lakṣmī is united with Brahmā;
and this Kṛṣṇa is truly meaningful because he likewise draws away (saṃkarṣaṇa) evil.
Furthermore, because he leads [beings] to their own abode, this Kṛṣṇa is just like you;
he is indeed the ancient Puruṣa, known by the name Puruṣottama.
My ancient maiden is Nārāyaṇī, the supreme among persons;
all progeny are considered to be the bodies of him who is designated as Puruṣottama. (87)
All those wives of Hari are capable; there is no fault in them.
But today this daughter of Bali is seen to be easily capturable by that wielder of the Śārṅga bow. (88)
That enumeration is foremost among all and most excellent;
there is no rivalry before Kṛṣṇa, for he is the remover of passion and hatred. (89)
Indeed, it is fitting that this Supreme Self should be the consumer of all;
for it is the ornament of the Lord who upholds dharma, whose very nature consists of all dharmas.
Indeed, where illusion—which bestows bondage—does not exist, its qualities do not exist either;
he alone who conducts himself with integrity bestows the fruits of all actions. (9.1)
He conducts himself solely according to the path of justice and remains non-violent;
he always abides as a silent sage (muni), and the Vedas are indeed his very breath. 92.
They constantly sing his excellent qualities, and silence itself is his ornament;
for a father who is incomplete, desire indeed arises again and again.
For Kṛṣṇa, who is filled with every perfection, who bears all bliss, and who is the self of all, his freedom from desire is indeed a great quality. (94)
He who is supreme does not know that delight arising from sense objects;
likewise, my daughter remains thus, devoted to Māyā and consisting of the nature of Ramā.
This Supreme Lord is the giver of bondage to Prakṛti and yet He is its destroyer;
He never practices deception, for He is indeed beyond Māyā.
"You are a cowherd, and your father is a cowherd; he too was a cowherd.
Yet, by sheer good fortune, the meeting of two Vaiśyas has occurred here."
The root *viś* means "to enter"; therefore, He is the pervader and the inner controller, for He is the Lord.
Lakṣmī is the internal regulator who has entered into all things within the three worlds. (98)
The union of those two is always considered appropriate and is ever praised; for the Kṣatriya is the perpetual protector of those who dwell seeking refuge. 99.
How indeed could the Blessed Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa not be a Kṣatriya?
My daughter is a Kṣatriya, and the Blessed One is also a Kṣatriya.
"Indeed, by good fortune, there is a union of two Kṛṣṇas; this marriage appears auspicious to me, therefore, O father, doubt does not please me. (101)
Upon hearing him speak thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, his heart gladdened within, said to his son, "So be it," and then departed from that place.
Then, O Rādhikā, the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa himself, as well as Śāmbhavī, went to the house in the form of women in order to find out [the truth]. (103)

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Auspicious Rites Performed at Dawn on the Fourth Day in the Second Tretā Cycle of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā," including the worship of the family deity performed by the girls, the feeding of the honored guests, and the dialogue between Bālakṛṣṇa (in the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa) and Śiveśvara regarding whether or not the girl should be given away.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, thereafter the glorious Bālakṛṣṇa,
having himself assumed the form of Rādhā, went to the house of Śrī Pārvatī.
Seeing you, her daughter-in-law Pārvatī rose and offered a seat;
then, in private, Rādhikā said to her, "Listen to what is for your benefit."
She is called a mother; she should always be one who acts for the welfare of her daughter.
One should not look merely at the gift itself, but likewise consider her future prospects.
It is the considered opinion that a daughter born in the northern [quarter] shall always be happy;
yet among women, if there is the suffering of co-wifery, it is greater than anything else. (4)
Today I have heard that the one to whom this daughter is to be given is indeed a husband who,
since his childhood, has been the lord of ten million women upon the earth.
All those women who have indeed come here together with their fathers and others—this is clearly visible; among them, the daughter would be the one suffering.
I have a doubt in this matter; therefore, O Pārvatī, she should not be given.
For in the company of many women, enjoyments indeed become divided.
Even if there were divisions of wealth sufficient for them, they would not be satisfied;
for women do not reach satiety with a man who possesses many wives.
Indeed, everything pertaining to the sovereignty of the earth belongs to kings;
yet this brahmin exists as a son-in-law who performs the duties of a vaiśya.
"He has no village, nor a garden, nor a field, nor a shop or the like;
his livelihood is indeed alms—how then can my daughter be happy? (2.288.10)

Indeed, he possesses no wealth within his house, yet he displays great abundance outwardly; moreover, though betrothed according to the words of Nārada, she is separated from him even at the time of the formal giving of the bride.

Therefore, Lakṣmī should certainly not be given away; she who is so very happy might become miserable. "Speak, daughter-in-law, what is your opinion in this matter? I spoke thus with a heart burning with grief.
A daughter should be given to a handsome youth who is healthy, virtuous, well-disciplined, wealthy, and possesses two wives.

To one who has a family, who is of equal status, who possesses wealth in cattle, who is esteemed by the earth, who is endowed with prosperity acquired by his own arms, and who is distinguished by virtue.
To him who is renowned, capable, and the fulfiller of desires;
to the illustrious one who bestows happiness, regarding his wife as a deity. (15)
A daughter should be given to Rāma, who is endowed with righteousness and well-versed in the Vedas;
other qualities should then be examined, foremost among them being his freedom from having a co-wife.

Rivalry between co-wives is the foremost corruption in a household and leads eternally to hell; furthermore, the respect due to one's children will certainly not exist, or perhaps it will not exist at all.
And may my partiality for Rohiṇī be like that of the moon, yet my devotion to Virajā and Rādhā remain as it was in the past, O Kali. (18)
"Even in Goloka, she experienced the very suffering of co-wives because of him.
O daughter-in-law, do what is appropriate regarding that which was spoken by me and which has occurred to my mind. (1.9)
Having thus heard these words of Rādhā, O Rādhikā, Pārvatī—
the beloved of Śiva and Īśvara, the worshipful one— spoke this supreme conclusion.
This Bālakṛṣṇa is meritorious; he is the eternal Supreme Brahman, the Lord of perfect bliss, like the ocean is to the rivers.
Perfectly prosperous, perfectly powerful, and perfect in qualities, he shines resplendent;
from him alone has this entire circle of creation arisen.
Neither disease nor anxiety exists for that Lord whose desires are fulfilled;
this yogi remains forever in a state of youth, never falling from his perfection.
And his vow, known as ethical conduct (śīla), is proclaimed in the Upanishads;
he is a yogi, a knower of yoga, and is always possessed of restraint. (24)
He by whom all wealth was created is indeed this most excellent merchant;
by him the earth was made, and by him the Vasus were fashioned.
And because he was fashioned as Kubera by him, he became the wealthiest of all;
furthermore, he possessed as many bodies as there were wives for him.
He enjoys each wife separately and always conducts himself separately; therefore, since he has two wives, there is no fault on his part, just as in the case of the moon. ||27||
This handsome one became a counterpart to every form;
he possesses an innumerable family within the imperishable abode. (28)
Of whom alone there exist reflections in the form of millions of incarnations—lords, Manus, Rudras, world-protectors, and Viṣṇus. (29)
The Ādityas and the stainless sages are indeed his incarnations;
moreover, I have heard that he possesses a universal sovereignty as his family estate.
This Supreme Person abides with equanimity toward all, yet he bestows even greater affection until satisfaction is produced. || 3.1 ||
Whether situated in prosperity or adversity, he is the bestower of happiness upon his wife; furthermore, the wealth of cattle is considered by you and by me to be the most excellent in Goloka. (32)
It is well known that cows granting all desires are always present for his service;
moreover, the entire earth belongs to him, since kings are his fathers-in-law. (33)
The wealth acquired by his own arms is seen here visibly;
indeed, his pilgrimage to Kāśī is accompanied by ten million creations.
His mother is Mahālakṣmī herself who shines forth;
and his father is Mahāviṣṇu Gopāla, the creator of the universe.
Furthermore, eight great qualities, revealed by the Śruti, exist here in the Supreme Lord; they are eternal, beginning with the quality of being free from sin (apahatapāpmatva). //36//
Truth, purity, and likewise the other thirty-nine qualities, as well as innumerable other virtues, exist eternally in the one who is constantly united [with the Self]. (37)
His fame exists in the Vedas, in the celestial abodes, and even among the lords;
it is present among the gods, in the world of men, and in all the netherworlds as well. (38)
He is capable and he is the giver of liberation; for the sake of liberation, a maiden has been given by me, and she is even now being given—what cause for lamentation is there in that? (39)
This Supreme Lord exists as the fulfiller of desires;
He is the one who fulfills the wishes of His devotees and the fulfiller of all desires. || 2.288.40 ||
That true lord considers his own wife to be equal to a deity;
he is the giver of happiness, endowed with glory—Rāma is indeed the one who brings delight. 41.
The bearer of the burden of all phenomena exists, and the ancient Knower exists;
moreover, there is always freedom from rivalry even when one is joined with many wives.
In this realm, there is no deficiency in qualities or sovereignty such that one might become like Dhruva, or like the Moon, or even like Goloka; indeed, such a thing cannot occur here. (43)
In his hand are the marks of the Supreme Lord: the fish, the banner, the bow, the arrow, the trident, the svastika, the discus, the staff, and so forth. 44.
Even the marks of a universal monarch (sāmudralakṣaṇa) are indeed present upon his body;
I heard all of that from the mouth of Nārada. (45)
The daughter has been given to the Supreme Lord, who is the worthy recipient for bestowal in every respect;
therefore, O Mother, my virtuous daughter is happy and endowed with good fortune.
Having obtained the most excellent boon, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, she formerly performed severe penance in her childhood on the Himalayas. 47.
There, at Hanumān’s hermitage, he, assuming a divine form,
granted a boon to Lakṣmī for her husbandhood and then vanished from sight.
Then my daughter went home and told me that news;
from that time on, she has waited for twelve years.
Her own year with Kṛṣṇa was completed, and thus the fourteenth year has been declared.
Indeed, this most excellent occasion has arrived;
the Blessed One, the Supreme Person, has come to my home.
Today my purpose is fulfilled, for Puruṣottama is worthy of my worship;
Mahālakṣmī, the fortunate one who is the creator of this world, exists [for him].
"And my daughter, your granddaughter, O noble lady, has accomplished her purpose.
Having been addressed thus, Rādhikā observed silence and [bestowed] a blessing.
Having united with him, she departed for her own abode and vanished;
Bālakṛṣṇa, however, firmly understood the devotion of his two elders toward himself.
Delighted and exceedingly thrilled, Bālakṛṣṇa, in the form of a brāhmaṇa, approached Lakṣmī in private and spoke the heart-entrancing [teaching]. 54.
Listen, daughter; I have heard that the ceremony for your giving away is being prepared. A Brahmin has also arrived to marry you, O princess. (55)
"I have heard that he is a beggar, deprived of his kingdom, living on the shore of the ocean;
indeed, like a fisherman, so too does this cowherd live. (56)
In his house there is indeed no abundance, yet he observes the vow of a bridegroom;
however, even though he is a youth, he is not the husband of ten million women.
"I have heard that women of such a kind have also come here;
for indeed, there exist those who, sharing the same purpose as you, are staying here with you. (58)
They will come to the pavilion and circumambulate it clockwise;
having established the fire here as witness, those two daughters of yours shall indeed be co-wives. (59)
"What is this that pleases you? Your co-wives are in the pavilion. O princess, do not choose that brahmin who has many wives. (2.288.60)
O Indra among kings, choose as your king Nārāyaṇa himself,
who is most righteous, most venerable, and the bestower of all prosperity.
And you remain there, O beautiful and lovely one, the most honored among beautiful women,
endowed with fresh youth and radiant with splendor, a virtuous lady.
She possessed the luster of molten gold, was the very embodiment of pure being,
devoted to her husband, truthful in character, tranquil, and endowed with the most excellent virtues.
You are known as Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, Rohiṇī, Kalāvatī,
Svāhā, Saṃjñā, Sāvitrī, and Kuberāṇī.
Among other excellent beauties, you shine as the most excellent one;
you are rich with the splendor of the full autumn moon, with eyes like autumn lotuses.
"O Indra among kings, do not choose a Brahmin, a mendicant living far away.
Upon hearing this, the maiden spoke to her husband, who was in the form of a Brahmin: (66)
"You are a Brahmin; you are worthy of my worship. Do not speak such words again.
Otherwise, you shall become a fit recipient for punishment, since you have come here from that place. (67)
"Whatever kind of mendicant he may be, even if he is such a one, he was first examined by me and subsequently accepted by me. (68)
He whose sovereignty indeed encompasses the entire earth and consists of the three worlds— this omniscient Lord, the fisherman, now dwells upon the shore of the Ocean of Milk.
He shines as the protector of both cows and splendors;
for he possesses all prosperity, since this world belongs to the Lord (Īśa).
For he always abides in devotion and firm vows, ever intent on his beloved's practice;
even as the lord of ten million women, he is eternally possessed of supreme being.
The youth always remains [here]; I know him from a previous birth;
thus he is known indeed as one whose vital energy is unbroken and upward-directed, and who is skilled in ritual application.
If millions of Brahmin women were to circumambulate my back here in this pavilion, I would feel great honor in that. ||73||
Since I am indeed the foremost object of honor among all my co-wives, let ten million women bear witness before the sacred fire to my equality with them. ||74||
May they be even greater than this for me, and may there be reverence here;
when the Lord meets in person, what wish indeed could he not grant? (76)
Just as he is a dweller in a distant land, so am I a dweller in a distant land;
a meeting between us two is indeed fitting, so do not harbor anxiety, O Brahmin.

Indra and the others abide under his control, and Brahmā and the others likewise abide under his control; the Vairāja and other classes of beings abide under his control, and even his own emanations (vyūhas) abide under his control.
And when he is under the influence of his incarnations, what maiden would not choose him?
You surely already know the ancient narrative declared in the Vedas; you need not hear it from me again. (78)
Out of compassion, the Blessed One, the Lord of Śrī himself, the Supreme Person, has appeared for the sake of uplifting the worlds and his devotees in every way. || 79 ||
This very Bālakṛṣṇa, the most perfect Lord,
resides here in the noble home of Gopālakṛṣṇa, indeed by the side of Śrī Kambharā.
He has been born as the Supreme Lord, the husband of the virtuous Rādhā and Ramā;
he is the ordainer of even the Creator, and is worshipped by Brahmā, Śiva, and Śeṣa.
The Blessed One is the very nature of light, the Supreme Self, higher than the highest.
Untainted, desireless, and the witness of all actions;
dwelling in the heart and present in all things—for his sake have I come here. Of the two [suitors] previously mentioned, I choose him alone here and no other. || 82-83 ||
I have surrendered my very self right there into the Supreme Self;
O Brahmin, the line was drawn for me by the Creator for that purpose alone.
Behold that Supreme Self, whose form consists of grace toward His devotees.

O best of Brahmins, by the mere sight of him—who is the cause for compliance with meditation and who possesses an eternally divine and beautiful form—perform the destruction of the karma of your own birth;
he whom the four Vedas and even the virtuous deities do not know. || 85-86 ||
Neither the lords of the senses, nor the lords of sages, nor even the gods such as Brahmā and others, nor even yogins absorbed in meditation, can reach him who is lost in contemplation. (87)
Sarasvatī becomes rendered speechless in his description;
even Śeṣa with his thousand mouths, and Sadāśiva with his five faces, [are likewise silenced]. (88)
The four-faced creator of the world, Kumāra, and likewise Kārtika, as well as the sages and seers, were devoted and supreme Vaiṣṇavas. ||89||
O best of Brahmins, I am but a young girl; what can I say of his attendants, who are incapable of praising him and who are unattainable even through meditation by yogis? (2.288.90)
O Brahmin, I have always been devoted to him, and for his sake I am a passionate woman;
as a maiden, I too am dedicated to him, being the daughter of the Lord of the Universe.
Born here on earth as the daughter of Bhakta, she was a seeker of the Blessed One;
for even in her maidenhood, that which was called devotion to her husband remained fixed in her heart. (92)
The Lord is held in the mind, and He alone is always one's life;
indeed, the offering of the heart is accomplished through the heart itself. (93)
The bestowal of the gross body occurs subsequently through the gross [body];
the gross [body] is imagined for the sake of the continuous flow of worldly activity in this world. (94)
Therefore, understand this now: go and behold him, until you have seen the Great Lord who is the beloved of all. (95)
"O Brahmin, you have spoken here of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the beloved of Śrī Prāṇa; forgive me for having heard what should not have been told. (96)
Thus addressed, the Blessed One said: "If you possess such firmness, then what I have spoken must be forgiven; I am departing, so behold me again. (97)
Having spoken thus, he gave him a golden ring inscribed with his own name,
and he granted him a vision of his divine form as a means of identification.
Resplendent with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, earrings, and other ornaments;
beautified by the conch, discus, mace, lotus, yellow garments, and so forth. ||99||
Seeing her lord, the son of a brahmin, as he truly appeared before her eyes,
Lakṣmī quickly fell at his feet and embraced him for a moment.
Having spoken these sweet and pleasing words, "Dear one, I shall return in the evening," she, overflowing with joy, quickly vanished from sight. || 10.1 ||
With her mind entirely absorbed in him, she did not perceive even a moment there;
gradually regaining her composure, her body was filled with joy.
O Rādhikā, that most excellent of women considered herself blessed and fortunate;
yet, maintaining her composure, she did not speak this aloud.
Thus, the Blessed One, who assumes various forms while knowing all states of being, indeed became subject to the devotion of those devotees who offer themselves to him. 104.

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Dialogue between Bālakṛṣṇa in the form of Rādhā and Pārvatī regarding 'A Daughter Must Not Be Given,' the Dialogue between [Bālakṛṣṇa] in the form of a Brahmin and Lakṣmī regarding 'Do Not Choose a Brahmin Beggar,' their Subsequent Responses, and the Demonstration of Firm Resolve," in the second section (Tretā-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Now indeed, O Rādhikā, during the third watch there, the illustrious Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa, having partaken of milk and water, [remained]. (1)
Then, indeed, [he was honored] by those of great majesty, by the most excellent people, by the deities and others,
and together with kings along with their fortunate wives.
In spacious vessels made of gold and silver,
he prepared divine garments and ornaments for the sake of the maiden.
All ornaments as well as various necklaces,
all jewels of good fortune, and those things that contribute to auspiciousness.
Indeed, there were hundreds of new auspicious substances and perfumes,
as well as all kinds of sweet foods, betel leaves, and other such items.
He also had auspicious objects of supreme excellence, which were the very pinnacle of wonder, placed within golden vessels.
There were beautiful golden bells with a hundred different colors,
as well as garments purified by fire and hundreds of golden ornaments.
Others were of variegated colors and diverse patterns, made of silk;
they were adorned with rows of golden stars, had golden borders, and were set with diamonds.
There were golden-colored and red-colored silk garments, set with jewels,
made of fine muslin, and beautified by arrangements of silver necklaces and knots.
And likewise, there were delightful *colikās*, shining with a hundred strings of pearls; and priceless *keśalīs* and *kucalīs* of inestimable value.
There were also priceless small garments and golden coverings;
furthermore, there were golden tubes and golden waist-bands for binding the body.
Garlands with their stalks, armlets, necklaces, priceless hair-bands, breast-cloths, waist-bands, and whatever else is to be worn between the garments; || 12 ||
Then the father had fine silken garments, prepared in hundreds of folds, placed within golden plates.
He had two golden garlands fashioned and also two soft sandals;
dyed with the color of land-lotuses, he had them placed [upon the body] in a hundredfold manner.
All these preparations for the hair are indeed beautiful,
as are the various Viṣṇu- oils and likewise the fragrant essences.
Mud-pastes such as those made from musk and others, sandalwood pastes and the like,
various types of collyriums, and whatever red substances there may be— || 16 ||
And auspicious saffron powders, as well as beautiful streaks of vermilion paste,
shimmering soft powders, and liquid butter.
Likewise, substances for massage, liquids fit for bathing, pills suitable for bathing, principles for coloring the nails, and liquids for the soles of the feet; || 18 ||
Lac-dye and other such variegated substances, liquid pigments for painting, shimmering diamonds and moonstones, and whatever glittering powders there may be— || 19 ||
Then the father had all the cooked foods, such as land-lotuses and other delicacies, as well as fragrant waters, placed in golden platters.
Likewise, there were hundreds of beautiful golden rings set with emeralds, rubies, pearls, and other precious gems. (21)
Whirligigs, waist-bands, auspicious finger-rings,
bracelets for the forearms, and likewise golden vyaṃgiḍīs.
He also gave armlets set with beautiful diamonds,
excellent bracelets, golden arm-bands, and very splendid chains.
There were leaf-patterns joined by chains, dyed and adorned with blossoming leaves;
there were lion-faced ornaments, beautiful bracelets, and many rings.
Also the Natthikas, Cibukīs, Ṭibakīs, and likewise the Bindukīs;
and the Satārās, Sucandra, and the beautiful Bahuragas. (25)
Golden ear-crests, earrings, and ear-chains; golden vardhaka ornaments, as well as troṭikas and phullagranthikas. ||26||
There were also golden clusters of *śiṅghoṭaka* and *kadamba* flowers,
as well as *ārāyaka* and *subuṭṭika* blossoms set with gold and diamonds.
Also [the lutes] Vālikā, Stārikā, Kuñcikā, Rūpyakā, Ānakī, Tantī, Bhāgyamayī, Cāndrī, and the long Candrapattrī. (28)
He also gave a golden lotus, a most beautiful golden garland,
and a splendid golden sun-disk resting upon his forehead.
And she gave hair-pins and needles made of gold as well as silver,
along with golden chains for binding the hair into braids.
The crescent moons at the sides of the hair-tuft, the grains of sand concealed by the garments, the powder for coloring the lips, and the cosmetic paste for the cheeks. ||3.1||
Eager for the sake of the maiden, he indeed placed in the bowls necklaces, leafy garlands, and fruits tied with knots. (32)
Also [offer] chains and necklaces, a leaf of the Plakṣa tree made of gold,
a golden auspicious vessel, and likewise a golden Mādalī.
The svastika is golden, and likewise the wheel is indeed golden;
the lotus on the hand, the lotus on the throat, and the lotus on the forehead are all golden.
Also for the sake of necklaces, golden bracelets with lion faces, pearl necklaces made of sesame seeds, those made of mung beans, those made of black gram, and beautiful beads. (35)
They carried delicate leaf-shaped arrows, beautiful pearl necklaces, golden breast-plates, and locks of hair adorned with spears. ||36||
A golden image of Sūryamukhī, as well as golden jars, golden bands, golden garlands, and excellent necklaces of pearls; 37.
And golden waist-bands, as well as chains, girdles, and beautiful golden three-stranded belts. ||38||
Anklets joined with small bells, golden jhaṃjharī cymbals, plantain trees, flutes, as well as śṛṅgalās and ghurghuras. ||39||
All kinds of auspicious ornaments, new ones as well, betel-boxes for offering betel, small stools, and combs; 2.289.40.
Mirrors, masks, hand-warmers, and turbans; cloaks, helmets, and beautifully adorned horse-ropes—[he gave these]. 41.
The flower-ornaments, the buds, the golden fillets, the back-leaf, the hip-band, and the beautiful ivory-leaf [should be fashioned]. ||42||
Pearl necklaces, beautiful garlands of rubies,
strings of emeralds, and also rosaries of lapis lazuli gems.
There were also garlands of sapphire with leaves made of emerald and other gems;
wreaths fashioned from karketana stone, and strings of coral and crystal.
He also had placed upon platters beautiful *gālīcaka* fruits and *hārītaka* fruits, their leaves adorned with coral.
And likewise woolen and silken coverlets, red vermilion powders, and auspicious saffron pastes. ||46||
Unbroken grains, very sharp [implements], auspicious garlands of barley, flower wreaths, vessels, and golden incense burners; 47.
Thus, O Rādhikā, her father first had a jeweled ornament worth millions upon millions of billions of lotuses set,
and thereafter he had another ornament set that was worth a single lotus.
Having placed [the offerings] in vessels equal to the sun, the Lord of Kaṃbhārā, accompanied by the sounds of musical instruments as well as the songs of maidens, [proceeded]. 49.
Then he went indeed to the maiden’s residence, the abode of Śivasvāmī;
for the sake of the maiden, everything had been obtained from Kṛṣṇa by Śiva.
Then Hara, having with great affection offered them a welcome, honor, and acceptance, provided them with water to drink.
He caused a meal of sweet food to be served and performed a small auspicious rite; he gave betel-leaf as well and spoke many times, "Much! Much! (52).
Delighted, Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa gave everything to Śiva;
having received his permission, he then quickly returned to his own abode.
There, during the fourth watch of the day, he prepared the ornaments for the maiden.
All her friends, having gathered together in great excitement, spoke what was appropriate. ||54||
Kṛṣṇa’s father also had a beautiful elephant made for the occasion—a splendid, four-tusked mount for Sāmba, adorned with ornaments. 55.
The father adorned Dhavala, making him superior in every respect,
with a golden crescent-motif on his forehead and a golden garland of jasmine flowers.
On the trunk, there is a variegated trident; on the skull, the Sudarśana discus;
likewise, on the two ears and the two cheeks, there are fly-whisks and suns.
On their teeth were golden rings; on their necks were golden bells;
at their feet were attendants of variegated forms; and upon their bellies was the mace.
Then his father adorned the elephant with golden garlands on its tail and likewise provided a ladder on its side. Thus did he decorate the elephant at that time.
Then, with joy, his father decorated the elephants with ornaments that touched the ground and adorned with small pinnacles for the sake of the procession. (2.289.60)
Then, excellent elephants and Garuḍas belonging to those who were liberated also appeared;
as soon as they were remembered, they arrived, adorned and beautifully decorated.
Horses, camels, as well as swans, cranes, and cātakas;
bulls, gayals, and also deer, as well as crocodiles. ||62||
Likewise, geṇḍūka deer, lions, tigers,
and śarabhas were their vehicles, as they are traditionally described in the Kalpa tree.
Wish-fulfilling celestial chariots, created by supernatural power, quickly arrived there— both beautiful aerial vehicles and a few that travel upon the ground.
All were adorned with ornaments, as were the chariots and the chariot-warriors; likewise, the palanquins, the foot-soldiers, and the men serving as mounts were well-decorated.
The banners, standards, spears, and the canes and umbrellas—all of them were quickly adorned and made ready. (66)
Then the men and women stationed in the army were adorned with the grace of love;
they wore fresh and shimmering garments and were resplendent with ornaments and the like.
Then, with all their ornaments complete and without omission, the musicians, dancers, actors, and drummers were filled with joy. (68)
All the gods and goddesses dwelling in the three worlds, skilled in all musical instruments and adorned with various costumes, [were present]. (69)
Then the four crores of maidens, who were suitable for the bridegroom's procession, became adorned with ornaments appropriate for the wedding ceremony. (2.289.70)
Likewise, there were also other millions and tens of millions of women, numbering as many as the petals of a lotus,
who were then adorned by their fathers and female companions.
All were adorned with garlands of skulls and decorated with every ornament;
by the will of Hari, they all circumambulated the fire while dancing.
By the instruction of Lomaśa, we were adorned with all ornaments and became worthy of being given away as gifts, just like the maiden Lakṣmī.
At the end of the fourth watch, having performed a wonderful adornment, Kṛṣṇa departed from Śivapura at an auspicious moment. (74)
Accompanied by hundreds of millions of billions of beings, he was honored and increased by the people, and was worshipped and saluted with offerings of fruits, flowers, and wealth. || 75 ||
Having wandered through Vārāṇasī along the great royal highway,
having beheld the deity and bowed down to Viśveśvara, he,
who possessed ten thousand chariots, drank the auspicious water of the Gaṅgā. ||76||
Accompanied by a hundred thousand celestial chariots and surrounded by all the men and women,
he arrives at the Yoga-maṇḍapa, attended by as many honors as the earth can measure.
On the delightful bank of the Varaṇā, at the site of Kāpiladhārikā, in that vast and essential field adorned with gardens; 78.
And in front of Śivasvāmin’s temple, there was a pavilion consisting of Kailāsa itself,
shaped like Mount Kailāsa and measuring one hundred yojanas in extent.
He who indeed appeared in the form of Kailāsa in the sky as a welcome guest—
he himself shines here as this eternal Kailāsa pavilion.
O Rādhā, what deficiency could there be in that pavilion where the entire city of Śiva and likewise the city of Pārvatī are situated on all sides? (8.1)
And the city of Kāśī also attained an inner splendor;
such was the beauty created there by Śambhu within that pavilion.
On the ground where the Gaṅgā flows like a cow, a pavilion was indeed spread out, extending for a hundred yojanas and beautifully adorned with sacrificial pits and altars. ||8 2 ||
It was one yojana in height, endowed with divine splendor,
and filled with all the requisites belonging to Goloka.
He was seated upon a lion-throne and other such seats, resplendent with the brilliance of jewels,
and surrounded on all sides by his attendants and hosts intent on service.
It is surrounded by all the wish-fulfilling cows and the trees of paradise; it is enriched with the splendor of the rāsa-dance circle and resplendent with cowherds and cowherdesses. ||86||
It was adorned with effigies representing all the inhabitants of the world,
and it was graced by channels of clarified butter, channels of curds, and channels of honey.
And it was furnished with all kinds of soft seats, such as grass mats, strips of cloth, and the like, as well as woolen coverlets and silken rugs spread upon the floor.
He was captivated by songs endowed with enchanting melodies,
and he was graced by those skilled in the arts of dance and drama, as well as those who knew the art of humor.
It was fashioned with things visible from afar, audible from afar, and touchable from afar;
it was attended moment by moment by vehicles such as aerial chariots that move according to one's will.
It was illuminated in every way by cool currents of lightning and surrounded on all sides by stars that showered down nectar and ambrosia.
Upon the pillars and the upper portions of the archways,
there were representations of the marriage ceremony of the bridegroom and the bride, complete with their seats.
As many stars as there are in heaven,
so many jewels shine here in that pavilion on Kailāsa, within the pavilion of Yoga.
Indeed, Viśvakarman constructed as many assembly halls in that pavilion as there were for the creators of the worlds.
And Viśvakarman placed seats for the maidens worthy of receiving gifts upon the central sphere, along with necklaces, in their immediate vicinity. (95)
There, Mount Kailāsa shines forth in embodied form as a person;
indeed, he was present there at that great festival for the purpose of bestowing all worthy objects.
Neither has such a pavilion ever existed in the past, nor will it ever exist in the future;
yet, visible to those who perceive both the near and the far, it stands established like a celestial abode.
It was presided over by the consecration of the sacrificial post and the water-pot, by the deities, by auspicious signs such as the svastika,
and by the people of Pārvatīnagarī during the great festivals.
The city of Kāśī was crowded with its inhabitants and those dwelling in the three worlds, all speaking of the wedding of the two Kṛṣṇas. ||99||
In the most excellent and auspicious main gate of the pavilion,
Vīrabhadra spoke from the sky these words of blessing for the two Kṛṣṇas.
They said, "Let aerial vehicles come for this great festival;
let them behold the Supreme Soul and the gift of the two Krishnas. (101)
The Sāmaveda, having taken embodied form and remaining in the sky, offers salutation;
may that Śrīśarāja Hari, who is arriving, be most victorious! 102.
And the Ṛgveda, stationed at the front of the gateway, beheld the approaching army and signaled its arrival to Śiva and the others, appearing exceedingly long.
Then the virtuous goddess Śrī Pārvatī went to the upper realm to see how large and of what nature that army was as it entered.
Having brought [the image] from Śivapura to the vicinity of the pavilion in Kāśī,
and seeing it stretched out to an extreme length, she stood motionless for a moment.

Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Sending of Ornaments, Garments, and Utensils for the Sake of the Maidens; the Honor of the Female Attendants, the Adornment of Kṛṣṇa, the Departure of Śrī Kṛṣṇa toward the Pavilion, and the Splendor of the Pavilion," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Then, seeing Pārvatī ascending upwards, millions of women climbed from their own dwellings so that Kṛṣṇā might look upon them.
Standing in the upper chambers of the pavilion and eager for a sight of him,
Girijā spoke the Rigveda in the presence of Bṛhaspati.
But what is that which is seen before me? Tell me, for it is peaceful; who indeed are those great-souled ones today for the sake of my daughter? (3)
Who are they, and what are they like? And what is my own son like?
He is the greatest of all; I desire to know all that—tell me everything.
Thus questioned, the omniscient Ṛgveda attained great joy and then began to speak of the virtuous Śrī Girijā in due order.
Behold, O Mother, first indeed is the attendant named Maṅgala;
he has four arms, bears a sectarian mark on his forehead, and is adorned with all ornaments.
Accompanied by Maṅgalādevikā and endowed with all auspicious things,
he approaches bringing good fortune while chanting the Sāman mantras.
Mounted upon a very small swan and endowed with every splendor,
likewise Maṅgalā and Sarasvatī are mounted upon swans.
And Śāradā arrives, adorned with all ornaments;
this vision is indeed the most auspicious of all auspicious things. (9)
Then, indeed, the musical instruments of Vaikuṇṭha were played by the musicians;
their sounds resounded throughout the three worlds as they arrived.
Behold, from there approaches a magnificent elephant adorned with a banner;
freed from its driver, it shines like a great mountain.
Behold, then, these thousands of *snātakas* approaching, intent on celibacy and proclaiming shouts of victory. (12)
Behold, from there comes the auspicious Ḍaṅkāniśānavān, with dark ears and white horses; for he is indeed unrestrained.
Behold behind him a chariot drawn by bulls, carrying a drum,
made of gold, and adorned with a golden jar as its banner and a beautiful fender.
Behold, O Mother, then the horsemen by the thousands with their weapons; behold also the Nirṛti-rākṣasas stationed upon camels.
O Mother, behold all these Vaiṣṇavas, servants of Viṣṇu, rich in the splendor of their adornments;
and then behold the Yakṣas, who give gifts on foot.
And [he saw] thousands of those who were richly endowed with wealth, wearing golden ornaments and crowns, even as they brought down showers of gold, silver, and other treasures.
Behold, O Mother, those Vaiṣṇava people there who have performed the rāsa dance by the thousands, along with their musical instruments, chanting the virtues of Hari.
"Behold, O Mother, those thousands of Vaiṣṇava women there, adorned and intent on singing songs and chanting the praises of Kṛṣṇa. (19)
Then behold thousands of venerable great sages seated in palanquins and human-carriages, entirely devoted to the meditation upon Brahman.
Behold, O Mother, the ancestors and the gods together with Aryaman, seated upon golden celestial chariots, accompanied by hundreds of thousands of maidens.
Then behold the thousands of perfected beings and holy men mounted upon chariots and other vehicles— divine, purifying, and sanctifiers of the world.
Behold, O Mother, those youthful companions adorned in divine attire, playing tender melodies upon their flutes. (23)
Behold, O Mother, the thousands of Daityas mounted upon Sharabhas, who are devoted to Vishnu, adorned with ornaments, and uttering cries of victory. 24.
"Behold, O Mother, those fierce hosts there, riding upon bulls, belonging to Viṣṇu, wearing many kinds of dress, yet possessing forms similar to Śiva. (25)
Behold the spirits, the departed, and the piśācas who are servants of Viṣṇu;
behold then, O Mother, the divine gandharvas, the instrumentalists and singers. 26.

"Behold, O Mother, those who possess the luster of the color of the golden campaka flower and are endowed with the height of a palm tree; then behold all the sacred fords (tīrthas) there in embodied form. (27)
"Purifying and divine forms arrive by the hundreds of thousands;
behold them, O Mother, and then the goddesses by the millions, accompanied by songs. (28)
"O Mother, look at those auspicious men from Saurāṣṭra, adorned with divine attire, seated in human vehicles, and appearing beautiful; and then look at the aged men. (29)
Behold the gods seated upon their vehicles, adorned with umbrellas and chowries,
numbering in the hundreds of thousands, radiant as the sun, and accompanied by male and female servants.
He likewise saw gods situated in celestial palaces of very small kalpas, as well as those dwelling on land or moving through the sky,
possessing the luster of the moon, the sun, or fire.
Behold, O Mother, those hooded serpents residing in Pātāla who have come here by the millions, possessing many forms and able to assume any shape at will.
Behold, O Mother, the worlds of the Sūtas, the Māgadhas, and then the Kinnaras;
behold the Kiṃpuruṣas and the Vidyādharas who sound the musical instruments of the gods. ||33||
Behold, O Mother, the Brahmins there, those twice-born who utter the resonance of the Vedas;
behold then the kings seated upon elephants, the sovereigns of the earth.
Behold King Jummasemla seated upon an elephant, and likewise around him,
a thousand maidens beloved by Hari traveling in their vehicles.
Behold, O Mother, King Dakṣa’s younger brother on his elephant, as well as the more than one thousand maidens seated in their vehicles. (36)
"Behold, O Mother, King Śibi, the splendid monarch, mounted upon an elephant;
behold also the hundred adorned maidens traveling in human-carriages. (37)
O Great King, behold the immovable Tharkūṭa, accompanied by fifty maidens, seated upon a golden throne and supported upon the shoulders of the Viṣṭi spirits. 38.
Then behold King Vīrajāra, accompanied by a hundred thousand maidens, seated upon a human vehicle and adorned with every ornament. (39)
Behold King Śaktākṣi, beautifully adorned, together with sixty maidens and accompanied by a hundred Piśācinī girls.
Behold King Kālimāśa, accompanied by two hundred maidens, seated upon a golden vehicle and adorned with every ornament. (41)
These kings from Rāśiyāna, of the Kimpuruṣa lineage, who are equal to gods, have arrived and are present in your house. (42)
Now, listen to the sounds of musical instruments and behold these nine excellent ones—beautifully adorned with rows of banners and played by mechanical means. (43)
Behold King Uralaketu, traveling in a small vehicle together with thirty maidens, proceeding toward the region of Venumālaprakhaṇḍa. (44)
Behold King Krathaka, auspicious and accompanied by five thousand maidens; and behold the broad-chested Pṛthu, seated in a small vehicle and accompanied by twenty thousand maidens.
Behold the Uṣṭrāla-rājaka accompanied by ten maidens; behold the Haṃkāra joined with five maidens in the vehicle. ||46||
O Mother, behold King Jayakāṣṭhalabha accompanied by five maidens, and the King of Tīrāṇa joined by six maidens. 47.
Behold King Alvīnara accompanied by seven maidens;
behold King Jīnavardhin seated in a vehicle with a single maiden. (48)
Then behold, O Great Goddess, on the back of the kings a mandala, beautifully adorned by two hundred thousand maidens. (49)
The entire great celestial chariot, adorned with every kind of ornament and beautifully graced by wish-fulfilling creepers, traveled upon the surface of the earth.
"Behold King Alpaketu accompanied by seven daughters;
and behold, O Mother, King Jayakṛṣṇa with only one daughter. (51)
Behold King Pariśāna, accompanied by twenty-one maidens, traveling in a small celestial chariot and adorned with every kind of splendor and ornament. (52)
Then behold King Dvikanya, and this auspicious King Indu;
then King Mudrāṇḍa, accompanied by fifteen maidens.
Behold King Gaṇḍa, adorned with all ornaments, traveling in a small celestial chariot; behold him, accompanied by nine young maidens, seated within his aerial vehicle. (54)
Behold King Līnorṇa traveling in a celestial chariot with four maidens,
and King Bṛhacchara accompanied by eleven maidens.
Then behold the auspicious Balalīna, accompanied by forty beautiful maidens, traveling in a small celestial chariot and adorned with every excellence. (56)
Behold indeed King Varasiṃha with five daughters;
and behold the auspicious Rāyagāma king with eight daughters. (57)
Behold the king of the foam-thread accompanied by two maidens;
likewise behold the king of the small oblation and the auspicious maiden traveling in a vehicle. Behold the king of the wooden vehicle with one maiden, and the king of the peg.
And Kanyaika—these are the kings belonging to Ketumāla. ||59||
Understand from me that all these great masters are in your house;
now behold those skilled in musical instruments who are born in the region of Garima.
O Mother, behold the auspicious Hārītakas in their divine attire in due order;
then behold the king seated in his celestial chariot, accompanied by his two daughters.
"O Mother, behold the independent King Arka, adorned with great splendor, as he goes forth from there to meet the King of the Rāya-kiṃnaras. (62)
Accompanied by fifty-one thousand maidens, traveling in a golden celestial chariot,
he was the king of the Kinnāṭaka regions, attended by female chowrie-bearers.
Then behold the auspicious kings of Uttarakuru, born in the land of the immortals, traveling in great celestial chariots that touch the surface of the earth with a sense of agitation. 64.
King Rāyarokīśvara, who had twenty-one daughters,
and King Rāya-raṇajit, who was accompanied by twenty daughters.
Behold Rāyavākakṣaka, who possesses three daughters and dwells in a magnificent celestial chariot; and behold Rāyamārīśabhūpa, who also possesses three daughters and travels in a celestial chariot.
King Rāyabāleśvara, who went to the celestial chariot with three daughters;
and King Rāyalambāra, who indeed went to the celestial chariot with six daughters. || 67 ||
And King Rāyanavārka, with seven daughters, traveling in a celestial chariot; and King Rāyahūṇeśa, with nine daughters, traveling in a celestial chariot. ||68||
Behold King Rāyakūpeśa and his daughter, traveling in their own celestial chariot, accompanied by male and female servants and adorned with the splendor of royal parasols. (69)
"Behold, O Mother, those musicians dressed in black attire;
behold, O Mother, those kings born in the region of Dakṣiṇakuru."
Behold King Kālamaṇḍalin, accompanied by his four daughters,
mounted upon an elephant and endowed with every splendor.
And behold King Vanajeśa, accompanied by five maidens, seated upon an elephant, O Mother, and adorned with an umbrella and other ornaments. (72)
Behold King Pārāvārapiba, accompanied by his three daughters, mounted upon an elephant, and surrounded by all his servants and attendants. (73)
"Behold, O Mother, King Koṭīśvara, accompanied by his two daughters, mounted upon an elephant, and surrounded by all his servants. (74)
[He saw] King Śrī Satīśa accompanied by three daughters, and likewise King Tretākarkaśa joined by seven daughters. (75)
Behold the king born from an egg, accompanied by four daughters;
behold the king of the dust of youth, mounted upon an elephant with a single daughter. (76)
Behold the auspicious King Rāyasoman, accompanied by three daughters, and King Urugavākṣa, accompanied by two daughters. (77)
Then behold King Parāṅavratu accompanied by his two daughters, and also King Īśānapāna at the four great elephants. (78)
Behold him seated in the vehicle, accompanied by forty-one maidens, and well-served by female and male attendants with chowries, parasols, and other honors. (79)
Behold the lord of kings and kings, accompanied by thirty-three beautiful maidens,
seated upon a great vehicle drawn by four elephants, and adorned with parasols and other ornaments.
O Mother, behold also the subjects of the eastern region traveling in celestial chariots—
all ten million maidens and adorned by ten million youths.
Behold this vast army that has arrived at your courtyard, in which no one's gaze—whether of child or old man—fails to find its full satisfaction. (8.2)
Behold Mahābāleśvara and behold the Suratīyas;
behold the Sāntapanī offspring, the five thousand maidens.
All were traveling in celestial chariots, adorned and decked with ornaments;
and there was also the aerial chariot of King Bhūgarbha Lakṣmaṇa.
Behold, O Mother, Viśālaka accompanied by two thousand maidens, and Śāvadīna with his thousand daughters, all traveling in celestial chariots. (85)
Behold the celestial chariots of the Naga maidens mounted upon Nagas;
behold them by the thousands upon thousands here in your courtyard. (86)
Behold, O Mother, the gods there, adorned with parasols and chowries, mounted upon human vehicles, and accompanied by their own musicians and bearers of whisks. (87)
This Kubera, a devotee of Viṣṇu belonging to a former kalpa,
is approaching together with his own family, endowed with every splendor.
"Behold, this Mahendra approaches, accompanied by the gods;
he is seated upon a great lion-throne, the king of heaven, possessing the radiance of the sun. (89)
"Behold, O Mother, the wind-god approaching there accompanied by the gods;
and behold Rudra, resplendent as the king of kings, accompanied by his hosts."
Behold Agni as he goes forth from there; behold the Sun traveling in his celestial chariot;
behold the Moon, Mercury, and Venus, frequented by tens of millions of gods.
And behold, O Mother, the Lord of Sages, Ṛbhu, and Sanatkumāra, seated within a great celestial mansion and accompanied by ten million virtuous beings.
Furthermore, hear the sounds of musical instruments situated in Satyaloka; and behold, O Mother, the ancestors residing among the people, numbering ten million maidens.
Then behold Viśvāvasu, stationed with his army of celestial chariots, accompanied by three hundred maidens and attended by hosts of Gandharvas. (94)
Behold the Daityas of the netherworld who have come as devotees,
as well as Prahlāda and other kings here, along with five thousand maidens.
And behold, O Mother, Saṃvaraṇa on the earth, accompanied by ten million maidens, adorned and seated upon an excellent celestial chariot.
Behold the families of the wish-fulfilling cow, whose souls are liberated;
ten million such families come to your home, which is a refuge of happiness. (97)
Behold, O Mother, Viṣṇu there, accompanied by ten million attendants and preceded by people richly adorned with the splendor of Vaikuṇṭha musical instruments as they march forward. || 98 ||
It was augmented by the sounds of victory, endowed with rows of ten million lamps, joined by hundreds of Ārjantīs, and accompanied by ten million Ramās. || 99 ||
"Behold, O Mother, Brahmā Parameṣṭhin departing from there,
augmented by millions of world-protectors who guard the directions."
Accompanied by Sarasvatī and others, joined by the lakes of Brahmā,
and attended by seventy-two thousand maidens, he traveled in a celestial chariot.
Behold, O Mother, Lomaśa, who is resplendent even with a thousand illusionist maidens, and who is served by ten million great sages.
And behold, O Mother, the Guru of the Lord, the Master of Lakṣmī, seated upon a great celestial chariot; indeed, on his back are millions of groups of maidens.

Behold the inhabitants with stationary bodies: the hosts of hundreds of thousands of forest goddesses' daughters dwelling in celestial palaces, the trees, the flower clusters, and the wish-fulfilling creepers. 104.
O Mother, behold those of great majesty, beautiful and with forms like the gods; then behold that supreme circle of one hundred thousand maidens.
O Mother, behold that supreme multitude of lightning flashes situated in the celestial chariots of the Dāmanīs; beyond them are tens of thousands of Kaṅkatālīya maidens.
Seated in celestial chariots, adorned and intent upon singing were the maidens of Sālamālī and the maidens of Vāsantika.
"Behold, O Mother, thousands of others likewise stationed in celestial chariots;
behold, O Mother, those born of Yama, and then the maidens born of Vāyu. (108)
There were fourteen thousand Meghanādas, as well as others:
the Vārkṣyas, the Raudryas, the Khānijyas, the Sāṃvatsaryas, and the Gopikas.
The Śrāvaṇīs, Vaiśvakarmyas, Prācīnyas, Piśaṅgikās,
Rāśiyānyas, Romāṇyas, Pāraśyas, and hosts of Kinnarīs.
The Dhaivaryas, Pārthas, Āmaryas, and Gauryas were adorned;
the Hārityas, Svargyas, and Pātālyas were born from the waters. 111.
O Mother, behold that there are here crores, billions, and hundreds of millions of terrestrial and celestial damsels for the sake of honoring your daughter. || 11.2 ||
"See, Mother, all the women are coming in great excitement, saying, 'The wedding of the two Krishnas is at hand! And then they depart for the place provided with a thousand jars. (113)
In that great celestial palace, he beheld the supreme person Vairāja,
endowed with many lords and adorned with a thousand arms.
"Behold, O Mother, the unborn one with a thousand faces proceeding from there,
as well as thousands of auspicious Viṣṇus and Brahmās."
Behold, O Mother, all the lords; behold Mahāviṣṇu.
Behold, O Mother, the Infinite One, the Supreme Lord, traveling in his celestial chariot.
Behold Pradyumna and Aniruddha, joined by ten million lords;
and behold, O Mother, Vāsudeva likewise accompanied by his family.
Then behold Prakṛti and Puruṣa, endowed with all the principles;
thereafter, O Mother, behold the players of musical instruments among the lords.
Behold, O Mother, the circles of the goddesses beyond that;
they are situated in celestial chariots, mounted upon Garuḍas, and seated on elephants.
"O Mother, behold the adorned female attendants standing upon the chariot;
oh Mother, look then at the eternal Blessed One! (2.290.120)
Then behold the form of the Fish and the form of the Tortoise; next behold the Man-Lion (Nṛsiṃha), and then behold the Boar (Vārāha); finally, look upon the Swan-Hari.
Then behold Kapila, and after that behold Pṛthu;
then behold Dattātreya, and behold Ṛṣabha and Vāmana. || 122 ||
Then behold Paraśurāma; behold the sacrifice thereafter.
Behold Rāma, O Mother, and then look upon Hayagrīva. (123)
"O Mother, behold Nārada; behold the king of kings.
O Mother, behold Vyāsa Śveta; behold Buddha, the son of Aśvinī."
Then behold Dhanvantari; behold the many Nārāyaṇas;
behold those who ride in ten million celestial chariots, as well as his attendants and beloved ones.
"Behold, O Mother, those liberated ones who dwell in the abodes of light;
behold, O Mother, likewise the women liberated through the practice of Sāṃkhya and Yoga. (126)
Behold, O Mother, the friends of Brahmā and likewise the beloveds of Brahmā;
behold these one hundred and forty-six women. (127)
"Behold these daughters of Kṛṣṇa, O Mother: Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Ramā, Padmāvatī, Śrī, and likewise Māṇikī; they have all come together to your house. (128)
Mādhavī, Suguṇā, Hāsā, Dayā, Śāntā, Sumāmbikā, Campā, Haimī, Muktikā, Devikā, Lalantikā, and Jayā. (1.29)
And behold, O Mother, hundreds of others have come to your house—those whose lives are drawn by Kṛṣṇa, who perceive your daughters as sisters. (2.290.130)
"O Mother, behold this great celestial chariot drawn by elephants, wherein are my father, mother, brothers, and the entire family. (131)
Indeed, the seat of Śrī Hari is equal to ten million suns in brilliance;
behold it, O Mother, divine and borne by a thousand elephants. (13.2)
The celestial chariot was indeed enriched with jars and possessed a thousand peaks;
it was surrounded on all sides by thousands and tens of thousands of vehicles.
Behold the beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who possesses divine splendor, who has been increased by and served by millions of women of supreme fortune, and who gazes back upon them. 134.
I bow to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, to Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa,
to Śrī Kṛṣṇa the Beloved, and to all who are the very form of Svāmī Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
He is nourished by his brothers' wives, sisters, and others;
he is indeed Puruṣottama, the cause of the manifestation of all things.
Oh mother, your good fortune has never existed before, nor will it ever exist again; indeed, such a Kṛṣṇā as you have never been before, nor will there ever be another like her.
O Mother, behold then the great mountains situated along the Yamunā;
and behold also the horsemen, born of all the worlds, by the tens of millions.
"Behold, O Mother, those excellent women there who are singing; behold all the women of the earth adorned with ornaments, and then behold the spectators. (139)
Śrī Girijā said:
"Oh, what supreme fortune is mine! My eyes are fixed upon Bālakṛṣṇa; I do not see anything else. Speak no more of other things here."
"Blessed is the daughter born to me, for whose sake the lords have come here.
I shall go quickly to welcome her; please come near the pavilion. || 141 ||
Having spoken thus to Rādhikā, Himajā immediately descended from above into the house for the sake of honoring and welcoming her.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninetieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Presentation of the Greatness and Introduction of Śrī Kṛṣṇa by means of the Ṛgveda to the Goddess Śrī Śāṅkarī," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, having seen Hari— the youthful Supreme Lord— by the millions upon the Kṛṣṇavāhinī river, the throngs of women were utterly enchanted.
Filled with millions of splendors, beautiful with millions of charms,
nourished by a weight of millions of blisses, and adorned with millions of ornaments.
Beholding again and again the Lord, who was the abode of millions of virtues and the sustainer of millions of desires, the young women remained absorbed in him with steady gazes.
As many maidens as there were also became absorbed in meditative concentration;
even men, worlds, and lords attained a state of dissolution.
All the gods were bewildered; what then can be said of women?
Even the saintly, the yogis, the liberated ones, and even the personal attendants [were affected].
Even the ascetics were bewildered; what need is there to speak of those who are liberated?
Mahāmāyā, Pradhāna, Prakṛti, Dhāma, and Yoṣit—[these are her names].
Even the enchanting women were bewildered; what then need be said of ordinary worldly women?
From their very birth, young maidens went forth accompanied by their families.
Eager indeed for the sight of the two Kṛṣṇas, they spoke thus;
they too became bewildered there before the Supreme Lord, the Paramātman.
Ten thousand kings and princesses,
having arrived with Kṛṣṇā, also recognized him as their own lord.
Likewise, ten thousand princesses there,
being utterly infatuated, chose the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa as their own lord.
And they were indeed intent upon that, holding garlands of *kaṇṭha* flowers, saying: "In the presence of fire as witness, we shall become the handmaidens of Kṛṣṇa, surrendered to him.
In this way, crores and billions of maidens were then devoted to him.
Having prepared all their attire, they awaited the auspicious moment.
Millions of Vidyādharīs were transfixed upon beholding Mādhava;
millions of Apsarases were transfixed upon beholding Keśava.
Even millions of Gandharva women were bewildered upon beholding Acyuta, and even millions of Kinnara women swooned upon seeing him, the granter of all desires.
Even millions of female dancers were bewildered upon seeing the Master of Illusions;
