likewise, the artisans were bewildered, and the musicians were bewildered as well.
Even millions of female ascetics who had reached their menses were bewildered, and likewise millions of virtuous women and female renunciants were also bewildered. || 16 ||
The Brahmin women who were celibate students were bewildered, and likewise they were stupefied;
O Rādhā, upon beholding Bālakṛṣṇa, the entire world was struck with delusion.
Some, upon merely beholding Hari, were drawn toward Keśava;
another, seeing his steady golden-colored garment, [was likewise captivated].
Pervaded by tawny rays, they remained fixed right there;
and the golden crown, the abode of Lakṣmī, set with ten million diamonds, [remained as well].
Seeing that auspicious place, radiant like the sun and filled with various jewels and gems, some women became attached to it, while others remained steady and were as if submerged within it.
Some [brought] jeweled necklaces and fine flower-garlands resting upon their crowns, as well as rows of flowers, buds, crests, and floral fillets. || 21 ||
Beholding there those who indicated the act of giving, they stood firm and were struck with wonder;
some [beheld] beautiful locks of hair, endowed with a shimmering radiance.
Black, curved, rich in joints, delicate, captivating to the eye, and auspicious;
filled with fragrant oil and reaching as far as the tips of the ears like ornamental arches.
In the rear section, having observed the coverings situated scattered about, which were refined by ivory workers and made level at their edges; |||24||
Seeing those [beings] with reddish-brown extremities, the steady ones there were bewildered; some, moreover, seeing a great and blazing halo of light, were likewise struck with wonder.
It was a thousand yojanas across its inner circumference, filled with the luster of millions of rays, multicolored, and auspicious, bearing the wonder of sweet attraction. ||26||
Beholding that divine [form] right there, they were bewildered and became motionless;
some, merely beholding his broad forehead, which was like a half-moon, [were transfixed]. (27)
It is considered brilliant, enriched with a single line, bearing the luster of the moon at its two edges, radiant like the sun in the middle, intensely bright, and elevated. (28)
Then, seeing that which was nourished, delightful, and captivating, some innocent women became steadfast;
others beheld the moon and the beautiful saffron mark situated in the center.
Seeing him resembling the rising sun, the innocent women became steadfast;
some, seeing his beautiful *tilaka* and his golden vertical sectarian mark (*ūrdhvapuṇḍra*), were likewise fixed in their gaze.
There, the slender, charming women, anointed with a thin mixture of golden-hued sandalwood and saffron, became filled with steady bliss. ||3.1||
Some, however, having seen two leaf-shaped marks made of sandalwood at the two ends,
[beheld] in the middle small, sparse dots of saffron that were highly beautiful.

In those very [limbs], the women were infatuated; they were steadfast in their devotion to the husband, yet some were captivated by the beautiful pair of eyebrows, which are composed of the threads of desire and action.

Upon that [surface], which was adorned with a delicate, dark, and exceedingly shimmering line of hair, the tips of the slender petals at the edge were so fine that the bewildered bees became motionless there.
Some, fixed there, were enchanted by the union of her eyebrows, which shone with white light and possessed a beauty equal to a mass of moonlight. (35)
Some, being very steady, became enchanted by the depth of her eyebrows, the charming base of her nose, and the radiant space between her eyes. (36)
Some, beholding the noses of those radiant women, which possessed the luster of sesame flowers and were charming,
beautiful, and slightly curved, remained there thus, both bewildered and steadfast.
Some had cheeks like those of a cow, beautifully colored and radiant; their breasts were elevated in the center, well-rounded, worthy of a kiss, and adorned with jewels. (38)
Seeing them possessed of smiles, elevated, possessing a luster like that of the sun and moon, well-nourished, and carrying intoxication, the charming women likewise became steady.
Some [women] cast glances from eyes that were elongated as far as the ears, perfumed by passion, with sharp corners, flowing with love, and revealing their inner intentions through their expressions.
With red lines rich with collyrium, with white pupils that are tremulous, with beautiful black irises, she knows the inner state and awakens one to the true nature of reality. 41.

And [it is] that which brings about absolute awakening, which is at rest, filled with the means of valid cognition, which attracts, which possesses delusion, and which shines with the opening and closing of the eyes. ||42||
It was joined with a protective *chajjikā* (veil) shimmering with a line of fine hair,
and it was auspicious, serving as the substratum for the reflections of all the creations of the worlds.
And there, they stood motionless, utterly bewildered by the two oceans— the repositories of the rivers of love and of all splendors, the abodes of every measure and form.
And some, at that time, [adorned] their ears— which were shaped like conch-shells—
with golden earrings, golden flower-ornaments, and golden pendants.
And there, those who remained steadfast were utterly bewildered by the two horses, which were equipped with golden chains and jeweled saddle-pads, and possessed the brilliance of the moon.
But some women, beholding a small hillock resplendent with golden ground, fell into a state of infatuation right there and remained fixed in that place. ||47||
Some, beholding the back of his upturned mouth, which was radiant with gold and possessed a line of hairs so fine as to be exceedingly subtle, experienced an awakening of desire. ||48||
There, those who were otherwise steady became bewildered by her tawny-colored beard-line;
some [were captivated] by her lips, which were well-proportioned, long, and as they should be. 49.
Filled with blood, resembling a ripe bimba fruit, and brimming with essence; it was worthy of being kissed, its flavor fit for savoring, situated in the center like the middle of a bow.
Just as the two ends of a bow are well-jointed at their extremities,
so too did he possess the form of all bows, being a treasury of love.
It was a temple of laughter, revealing a state of love slightly curved with emotion;
it was a beautiful abode of serenity, resplendent with the juice of betel.
In some places with her teeth, in some places with her tongue, and likewise in some places with her lips and mouth, she caused him to perform beautiful kisses. (53)
Seeing her lower face centered at the middle point, with a nose formed like a slender rod and an upturned lip, the lovers there were transfixed and remained motionless.
Other women beheld his breath, filled with fragrance, as he sighed;
it spread in all directions, perfuming the lords of the quarters.
Having smelled him, who was intoxicating and calming, the bewildered women became steady;
[they beheld] his lower lip, red in color and imbued with the juice of betel.
Beholding his chin—which was the companion of his lower lip, firm, and adorned with golden-yellow spots—those charming women became steady [in their gaze]. (57)
It is beautiful with its symmetrical proportions, lovely with its suitable depressions,
and made exquisite by the splendor of its well-formed jaw and chin.
Beholding that divine form, which had the luster of fresh butter and the radiance of a land-lotus, the women were enchanted; they became motionless, holding it within their hearts.
Seeing his conch-like neck, his melodious voice, the well-developed muscles beneath his jaw, and his firm, pitcher-like throat, they stood motionless, struck with wonder. (2.291.60)
Beholding Hari’s lion-like shoulders, so well-nourished and capable of bearing strength,
some women were bewildered, while others remained steadfast there at that time.
Some gazed upon his excellent chest, which was elevated, well-developed, and broad;
it was auspicious, filled with the luster of milk and campaka flowers, and the refuge of all strength.
It reveals his humanity, momentarily agitates the mind of the Hero, is desired by women, and is manifested through the embrace of Rādhā, the embodiment of divine splendor. (63)
Adorned with a golden line and endowed with hair curling to the right,
he is filled with affection for his devotees and shines with breasts resplendent like the sun and moon.
It was indeed broad and long, resplendent with firm joints;
it possessed a softness of belly and was pleasant to the touch due to its supple sides. (65)
With its backbone firmly established and the base of its arms exceedingly beautiful,
such is the chest of Hari, the supreme abode of bliss.
Seeing him thus enriched by his desire for the happiness of prosperity, the groups of beautiful women were utterly enchanted;
they became deeply immersed right there, established in bliss.
A golden neck-ornament set with gems upon his neck,
as well as a golden leaf-patterned chain and a golden fetter.
A golden garland of *plakṣa* leaves, a golden five-stranded necklace,
a golden rosary of *badarī* berries, and likewise a wreath of *gokṣura* flowers.
A golden garland with fine petals, a garland of mung beans, a garland of barley, a golden garland, and a golden garland of kidney beans.
A golden vessel, a brass one, a necklace of eight-cornered gems,
a garland of *tulasī*, and a necklace of fine gold and jewels.
She also wore golden garlands and fragrant flower necklaces,
which rested upon her golden bodice and silken tunic.
Indeed, seeing the necklaces worn by them, resplendent with gems, jewels, diamonds, and the like, as well as the pearl necklaces and the Kaustubha gems they wore, the women [were struck with wonder].
Seeing the auspicious moonstones, sunstones, and firestones worn there around his neck, the celestial women were truly enchanted.
All the others rejoiced for a moment and remained steady there;
her two arms and back were beautiful, radiant, and resembled the interior of a plantain tree. || 75 ||
The two auspicious ones were adorned with ornaments made of precious materials, enriched with bracelets, resplendent with chains, and graced by the decoration of lion-faced armlets. (76)
Upon seeing them, the women were indeed bewildered and remained motionless for a moment;
[he saw] their forearms, which were like the fruit of desire, adorned with golden chains.
Seeing it endowed with auspicious ornaments rich in gems, pearls, and jewels,
and abounding in the splendor of floral decorations, the charming women became steadfast.
Beholding the palms of his hands with the luster of lac, the nails filled with blood, the fingers resembling small moons, and the rows of rings upon them; ||79||
Likewise, the women were adorned with golden rings set with gems and jewels, and their soft, reddish fingertips were graced with finger-stalls.
Beholding them to be richly jointed, pleasant to the touch, charming, and likewise steady, [he saw] two beautiful hands marked with five lines and endowed with dark spots. (81)
Beholding this, the women were bewildered and became motionless there,
seeing upon the palm of the right hand a fish, a banner, and a trident.
A bow and arrow, a svastika, a thunderbolt, a staff, a discus, a mace, a lotus, a conch, a sword, and a scimitar adorned with gold. ||83||
All the women indeed fainted, yet they remained steady there;
likewise, the sword-strikes and the shield, bound with jewels, were of that same nature.

Even upon seeing it, all the celestial women were bewildered; the charming goddesses were further struck with wonder upon seeing the auspicious thread around his neck and the auspicious cord on his arm. (85)
The women possess tongues that are red, fit for tasting, bearing every flavor, broad, the foremost cause of delusion, and as beautiful as land-lotuses. (86)
And seeing their teeth, which were like jasmine buds, resembling pomegranate seeds, endowed with white luster, and shimmering with radiance, they were utterly enchanted. (87)
They indeed felt longing for the sake of obtaining [it], and they remained steadfast therein;
their belly was beautiful, radiant, auspicious, and possessed of the three folds.
Beholding her coolness, her deep navel, and her waist adorned with a slender creeper, they were then enchanted and became motionless right there. (89)
Seeing the golden cloth held around her neck with a half-fold and its trailing edge hanging from her shoulder, the simple-minded women then stood still.
Some, having meditated upon the protected vulva and the two dark hips,
became infatuated there at the waist where the garment was fastened.
And upon a costly footstool joined with gold and silver, possessing excellent legs, worthy of a king, and fashioned from the finest silk; ||92||
It rests upon ten million jewels, is adorned with golden finials and pearls, and is entered by pipes provided with blooming *phummakikā* ornaments. ||93||
When the beautiful bow was held, the young women were enchanted;
when that desirable object, the refuge of all desires, was within their grasp, all the women were utterly captivated.
Deluded by the basis of all their ignorance, they did not perceive anything else for even a moment,
as they stood before the tips of the feet on the lovely, jewel-studded pavement.
The two feet, marked with the sign of the five-spoked wheel, were adorned with fine hair;
they were well-fitted with soft sandals and graced by the beauty of golden ornaments. ||96||

Upon seeing them thus colored, the innocent women—both those who were steady and those who were not—became utterly bewildered by that non-corporeal [sensation] between the thighs and the middle of the root of the thighs. (97)
Seeing the finger-rings with their golden ornaments, as well as the women,
and seeing the golden foot-ornaments equipped with tiny bells, the steady [ascetics] were bewildered by the bracelets and the armlets adorned with tinkling rings. (98)
Beholding the women’s hands reaching down to their knees, their hips like the trunks of elephants, and their forearms like the trunks of elephants; 99.
They became motionless there, absorbed in meditative concentration,
upon a soft surface on a golden lion-throne within the elephant-palace.
Seeing the excellent lord, the king of the kings of the lords of kings, seated as he approached the city gate, all the women were bewildered.
Beholding the illustrious Supreme Lord, who was enriched by drops of saffron and unbroken grains of rice,
the people indeed beheld him and sang shouts of "Victory!
Thus, O Rādhikā, they reached the great gateway.
And the sound of musical instruments was pleasing to the minds of the people as they set out on their journey toward yoga.
O Rādhikā, listen: there, on his own seat during that journey, the Lord, who knows the hearts of all, granted a vision that was distinct [from his usual form]. 1.04.
In the form of Puruṣottama, he gave his vision to those who were liberated;
in the form of Kṛṣṇa, he gave his vision to the cowherds and the cowherd-women.
To his attendants, he gave a vision as the self of Nārāyaṇa;
to the lords, he gave a vision in the form of Vāsudeva.
To the hosts of Siddhas and Sādhus, He gave that [vision] in the form of Viṣṇu;
then, as Brahmā, He gave His own vision to the great ṛṣis.
To the ancestors, he gave his own vision in the form of Aryaman;
and to the gods, he also gave his own vision in the form of the Lord of Milk (Kṣīranātha).
He bestowed that [power] upon human beings in the form of Nara and Nārāyaṇa,
and he bestowed it upon the inhabitants of the world of Pātāla in the form of Śvetaprabhu.
To the women, he gave a vision of himself in the form of Kāmadeva;
to the maidens, he gave a vision of Mālādhara in the form of their own husband.
To those worthy of worship, he gave a vision in the form of a child;
to his devotees, he gave a vision of his divine form that bestows liberation. || 111 ||
Holding all weapons in his four hands and attended by the multitude of Ramās,
he granted a direct vision of himself in the form of Nārāyaṇa to the men.
Thus, O Rādhikā, the glorious Lord Bālakṛṣṇa Hari made known the nature of the inner self within the hearts of embodied beings. 113.
For that sovereign lord of the city named Maṇḍapa was indeed recognized;
he arrived at the front of the gateway and then attained stability for a moment.
And the entire army also stood for a moment, duly honored, by the eminent Kṛṣṇa, Bṛhaspati, and the twice-born who had arrived nearby. (115)

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-first chapter, titled "The Description of the Bewilderment of Men and Women through the Attraction of Every Limb of the Resplendent Bālakṛṣṇa, His Divine Appearance, and Their Arrival at the Gateway," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, Śrī Bṛhaspati stood before Hari together with millions of sages, holding vessels for the worship of unbroken grains and other offerings.
The beautiful city known as Maṇḍapa, extending for fifty yojanas, was filled with subjects who had gathered to behold the King, the Lord. || 2 ||
There Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself bowed down to Śrī Hari,
and the brāhmaṇas also prostrated themselves while chanting Vedic mantras at that time.
Then they also gave barley sprouts into the hand of Bālakṛṣṇa;
Kṛṣṇa placed a cluster of flowers in his hand and a garland around his neck.
Bṛhaspati placed a garland of *kādamba* flowers around his neck;
likewise, the Guru applied sandalwood paste mixed with unbroken grains of rice and saffron upon his forehead.
The women on the side of the bride's maternal kin increased [the fire] with parched grain;
and there, Bṛhaspati offered a drink of water to Īśvara.
He caused Bālakṛṣṇa’s army to enter the city;
and the subjects beheld it entirely as possessing a divine form in every respect. || 7 ||
Daughter-gods, daughter-nāgas, and princesses,
as well as daughters of sages and daughters of Īśa, were all gazing upon the Lord Hari.
All the women watched with unblinking eyes as Śivasvāmī arrived before the city gate for the purpose of performing worship.
Having honored him and inquired after his welfare, he made him joyful,
as well as his father Vasu and the other great lords of the earth.
The women of Mahimāna bowed down, beholding the Supreme Lord—whose face was gracious, who was lovely, enchanting, and possessed of a beautiful form. || 11 ||
Having worshipped the Lord— who is endowed with every splendor, who grants all desires, who is heart-pleasing,
who resides upon a celestial chariot (vimāna) on earth enriched by the brilliance of the finest jewels,
who is the Supreme Self of all, and who is accessible through grace to his devotees— [he attained his goal]. 12.
White as the new moon and adorned with rows of necklaces.
With all his limbs anointed with sandalwood paste and adorned with many garlands,
he was radiant with jeweled armlets, bracelets, and necklaces of gems.
Adorned with jewel-earrings that illuminated his cheeks,
and made radiant by the tinkling of anklets fashioned from the finest essence of precious gems.
Smiling, with a cluster of flowers in his hand, he gazes at a jeweled mirror; he is attended by white chowries and a parasol made of pearls. || 16 ||
At his side, he was graced by the self-luminous Primordial Lord;
endowed with fresh youth, his eyes were like autumn lotuses. (17)
His face is like the full moon of autumn; he bestows grace upon all; his beauty equals ten million gods of love; he is beyond the imperishable and is infallible.
Purified by sacred fords, purified by fame, worshipped by the lords of the gods and others,
the supreme delight of the Lord of Devas, a treasure-trove of beauty.
He bore a silk thread with *dūrvā* grass and a blossoming cluster from a plantain tree upon his crest, wearing a garland made of various flowers.
Seeing Hari with such a supreme, fragrant cluster of flowers offered by the woman, the women then fell into a swoon. 2.11.
"Lakṣmī’s life is blessed and praiseworthy"—thus they spoke their desire;
and Śrī, born of the Himavat, gazed upon Tāraka again and again.
Śiveśvara, separated from his beloved, arrived together with his ministers and his priest and bowed down before Hari, the Lord of gods.
In the long pavilion at the front,
he had a dance performed by dancers and an exceedingly delightful singing by musicians.
He indeed caused the songs of the female singers, the dances of the dancers,
and the various sounds of musical instruments to be performed before him.
The bursting of clapping hands, the play of lightning, the bursting sounds of mechanical devices, and the deep rumbling of kettledrums; 26.
Then Śiva went ahead at the head of the army;
moreover, the subjects also increased the prosperity of the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa.
Thus, at that time, the pilgrimage procession arrived at the rest-house;
Kṛṣṇa, descending from his celestial chariot, took his place at the city gate.
Pārvatī increased his joy by repeatedly offering her joined palms as a gesture of reverence;
indeed, she washed the feet of Hari with the water from sacred bathing sites.
He was worshipped with sandalwood, unbroken rice, flowers, and other auspicious liquids;
he was honored with barley sprouts, dūrvā grass, and fragrant substances.
Then, having been honored with parched grain and the rite of waving lights (nīrājana),
he was further strengthened by the benedictory words of the brahmins and his preceptor.
Then, having been sprinkled with water, he was led for a moment to the side into a rest-house,
onto an auspicious golden throne that bestows all peace.
He seated Hari, as well as all those most worthy of worship,
and honored his parents and Śiva, the Lord of Gods, with a welcome.
Then Śivasvāmin gave him a meal known as madhuparka, accompanied by a drink of water, for the sake of worldly peace and tranquility.
Then even millions of maidens put on their own finery; eager for the occasion, they donned garments and ornaments suitable for yoga. (35)
With bodies fragrant with perfumes and likewise adorned with colorful dyes, they stood ready, joined by pairs of dots and bindus. (36)
When Hari shall accept the gift of Lakṣmī, then Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa will take taxes from us. (37)
Thus, at that time, her friends performed an auspicious adornment for Lakṣmī;
they indeed dyed her beautiful nails, which resembled land-lotuses. (38)
They likewise dyed the palms of their hands and the soles of their feet with lac,
and they stained their lips with red pigment.
They indeed adorned both their cheeks and ears with saffron paste, and they likewise anointed their eyes with collyrium.
They adorned his forehead with saffron and sandalwood paste,
and they made his body fragrant by anointing it with sandalwood.
Likewise, they made her body richly fragrant with essences of sandalwood,
and they adorned her hair with scented, high-quality oil.
They fashioned their hair-crests (kabarī) to be beautiful, radiant, and auspicious;
they bound their braided locks (dhammilla), adorned with garlands of land-lotuses. 43.
It was likewise surrounded by a necklace of jasmine buds, joined with *mālatī* flowers and woven together with variegated threads. (44)
At its edge was a beautiful piece of silk cloth, adorned with variegated patterns and resplendent with a crest of *pārijāta* flowers. ||45||
They placed a moonstone (*candrakānta-maṇi*) there for the sake of illumination, upon that auspicious site which was made to resemble a cowherd’s ball by golden garlands of jewels. (46)
They placed a sun-gem, radiant with light, at the site of the *brahmarandhra*;
and they placed upon their heads beautiful crowns suitable for women. (47)
Rich with jeweled necklaces and precious gems, the golden [palace] was variegated with colors;
there, crests made of flowers of jewels and pearls hung down. (48)
They wore on their foreheads strings of gold beads interwoven with many jewels and other ornaments, and they likewise caused them to be made.
In the center, he drew the *sucandrikā* and the *bindu* with saffron paste;
likewise, on his broad forehead, he drew the *kesarī* marks along with *akṣata* grains.
They drew curved lines, vertical ones, and auspicious diagonal curves;
and at intervals within the fourfold squares, they made saffron-colored dots.
They scattered a small amount of glittering powder and placed flower garlands suitable for offering during the auspicious ceremony.
They also wore very small, exquisite necklaces made of gold, enriched with pearls, and fashioned from beautiful gems,
as well as excellent strands of beads.
They likewise gave him a chin rich with gold and adorned with gold;
they placed a bindu on his cheek and gave him earrings for his ears.
And they placed upon their ears golden earrings adorned with diamonds and other gems, as well as five-stringed ear-ornaments.
They gave two leaf-shaped earrings set with fine diamonds;
then they gave a golden neck-ornament encrusted with gems.
She wore a silk garment that bound her breasts and a silk bodice,
richly adorned with rows of golden buttons and filled with lines of golden stars;
it was interwoven with divine diamonds, gems, and the like, and patterned with diamond knots.
They placed a *keśācalī* adorned with *cipikās* upon their shoulders;
they gave them a binding rod (*bandhikā*) made of gold and silver,
as well as a woolen garment (*orṇī*) enriched with golden stars, which the *kārpaṭikas* likewise presented.
They applied saffron to her breasts, which were dyed and rich with the beauty of red;
they wore a beautiful golden garment studded with fine diamonds, and,
full of longing, they put on a soft, delicate necklace made of fine silver.
They bound the garment with leather thongs,
cords, and other such means; likewise, they filled the spaces between with flattened, fine-textured sticks— between the arms, between the chest, and between the hips.
They indeed bound [him] and placed within him a small *ghargharī* and also a large *ghargharī* set with gold and pearls,
auspicious and inlaid with tiny mirrors and gems.
It is red in color, adorned with various patterns, and likewise has reddish-yellow edges.
They placed upon her hips a girdle enriched with a silk sash and set with channels of diamonds,
and upon her feet two anklets made of gold and gems, fashioned like lotus petals, soft and resembling land-lotuses.
Then they gave him a golden ring, complete with chains for each finger, sufficient for all five fingers;
and above the two *pañcajaya* [conch shells], they gave him a golden tortoise-shell.
They also placed rings set with diamonds and other gems upon her hands, as well as lotus-shaped ornaments on her wrists and anklets upon her forearms—
anklets made of gold, richly adorned with lions and resounding with a network of tiny bells.
They placed golden *kāmbika* and *kaṭakika* bracelets set with rubies upon the two forearms of Śrī;
they also placed a golden girdle adorned with pearls around her waist. || 69-70 ||
Upon the wrist-bracelets set with diamonds and gold filigree,
as well as upon the armlets adorned with gems and diamonds,
they likewise placed bracelets and bangles enriched with lotus designs.
And they gave golden armlets and auspicious earrings upon the petals. ||72||
They gave golden auspicious bracelets and even chains;
they also placed a golden svastika and a crescent moon upon their two arms.
They likewise gave necklaces made of gold, adorned with jewels and diamonds,
as well as garlands of mung beans, garlands of barley, and garlands of rose-apple flowers.
They placed upon her a leaf of the Plakṣa tree, a golden ornament, a necklace of pearls, a chain of seven links, and a beautiful, delicate leaf-patterned garment. (75)
A four-tiered garland of *dalī* flowers, a garland of *badarī* fruits, and a *māṣika* garland;
a supreme golden necklace set with diamonds, worth ten million coins;
and a bodice-like garment (*paṭṭikakañcukī*) that creates all-encompassing beauty and steals the very eyes.
They indeed held it fast and placed their hands upon the leather strap. ||77||
Thus the maiden Lakṣmī was adorned by her companions,
and at that time all the maidens, even by the millions, were likewise adorned.
"Kṛṣṇa will carry us both in the great union," they said;
then all the musical instruments of those traveling for wealth were sounded. (79)
On an auspicious and favorable moment, under an excellent constellation that brings about well-being,
in a conjunction that bestows all good fortune, and during the Māhendra yoga which grants prosperity.
In a most excellent ascendant that bestows great bliss, endowed with success, and auspiciously suited for marriage, accompanied by its own lord; ||81||

When the six planets are pure in aspect, when they are non-existent [in malefic positions] and free from adverse aspects, when the Moon and stars are pure, and when it is free from the defects of planetary conjunctions (*vedha*) and the like; ||82||
And at a moment free from [the presence of] the divining sticks and other such things, always providing happiness, and at a time suitable for the pleasure of the couple, Bālakṛṣṇaka [appeared]. (83)
At night, Hari, having been entreated by Bṛhaspati, the brahmins, and the sages, arrived at the courtyard of Śivadeva’s palace on Kailāsa. || 84 ||
Accompanied by Lomaśa and others, together with his kinsmen and relatives, along with his father and mother, as well as kings, relations, and friends. ||85||
Together with the gods and the ancestors, along with virtuous ascetics,
as well as with the attendants, the lords, the liberated ones, the bhaṭṭas, and the family priests.
Accompanied by all the guardians of creation, he went to the sacrificial altar-pavilion,
which was adorned with thousands of plantain pillars decorated with golden bands.
It was beautifully adorned with archways made of campaka, aśoka, mango, and sandalwood trees,
and with garlands of flowers possessing every excellent form.
With auspicious golden jars adorned with fruits and sprouts,
honored with musk, unbroken rice, parched grain, dūrvā grass, and saffron,
and provided with flowers, leaves, sandalwood, gems, and garments; ||89||
It was adorned on all sides with radiant [jewels], most enchanting to the mind.
It was indeed surrounded by all the attendants of Śambhu who move through the sky, as well as by those of great majesty, and by his pārṣadas and incarnations headed by Saṃkarṣaṇa.
By the lords, the deities, the seers, the kings, the guardians of the quarters,
and also by those dwelling on Kailāsa and those inhabiting the three worlds.
By domestic priests, Brahmins, ascetics, and mendicants;
by groups [of attendants], yoginīs, and even by the fathers of the maidens. || 93 ||
The auspicious abode was provided with a pedestal fashioned from the finest essence of jewels,
and it was adorned with colors, sandalwood powder, musk, saffron, and other such substances.
It was made fragrant and beautifully colored with scented heartwoods, pervaded by the luster of various jewels, and perfumed with the sweet scent of incense. ||95||

It was endowed with wonderful beauty, delightful, accompanied by the songs of Gandharva maidens, resonant with the sounds of musical performance, and beautifully adorned by the dances of Vidyadhara women. ||96||
The auspicious vessel, a source of well-being, was gazed upon from all sides by young women,
while the preceptor and the family priest held it.
The gift-pavilion was adorned with wish-fulfilling creepers and other ornaments, while the king stood nearby with kusha grass in hand, prepared to bestow gifts.
The sacrificial pavilion was adorned with Dānavas and their consorts,
and on all sides and in the upper parts by ten million lotus-maidens and others.
Bālakṛṣṇa entered that beautiful pavilion, which had been consecrated with perfumes and adorned with offerings for the ancestors and other deities.
Honored and celebrated by the twice-born, he arrived at the main gate;
there, Śiveśvara came forward to offer him worship.
Then the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, having reached the appointed time, quickly commanded all those beloved women who were his own.
Wearing all the garments, ornaments, and finery offered by me, which are suitable for the wedding, let them come to the beautiful pavilion. (103)
"Your marriage must indeed be performed by me along with Śrī.
Having heard this, they all prepared themselves and arrived at the pavilion for the auspicious ceremony.
Accompanied by their respective fathers and others, they then assembled for the purpose of giving,
according to the rite for the sake of Śivasvāmin’s own daughter.
In this ritual, the same procedure applied to all of them;
hear now, O Rādhikā, the wonder regarding the wives of those who possess millions, billions, and hundreds of billions of intellects.
In the Kṛta age, Kṛṣṇa displayed wonders and such;
indeed, Śiveśvara set the ritual section (Karmakāṇḍa) in motion everywhere.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-second chapter, titled "The Description of Bālakṛṣṇa’s Worship and Vision at the City Gate, His Dancing and Clapping before it, His Resting in the Resting Hall and the Offering of Madhuparka, the Adornment of All the Maidens and Lakṣmī, and the Lord’s Return to the Main Door of the Dāna-maṇḍapa," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Śiveśvara was a great devotee who, knowing the majesty of Hari, then considered himself blessed and fortunate while reciting this. (1)
Today my birth has become fruitful; today my religious rites have become fruitful;
today everything of mine has become fruitful, since Puruṣottama is in my home.
Today my life has truly come to be; everything has been well-lived, since that which arose through ten million births has now reached the dissolution of its root in karma.
Today, indeed, Śrī Hari— the bestower of all fruits, whose lotus feet sages constantly meditate upon within their hearts— has appeared in my courtyard.
And today, O best of holy places, the three worlds have come into my courtyard;
oh, until the end of the kalpa, my courtyard has become a sacred site! (5)
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Supreme Lord,
Hari— who was invisible to the eyes— is today visible to me in my courtyard.
I bow to you, the giver of the fruits of actions, the eternal one whose form is light, the Supreme Self abiding within, who is my very self. || 7 ||
Having thus offered praise, and remembering Hari who is praised by Śiva, Rādhikā joyfully offered water for the feet at his lotus-like feet, which are worshipped by Padmā. || 8 ||
There he offered the *arghya* water accompanied by *dūrvā* grass, flowers, and fruits;
he also presented a small *madhuparka* and applied a beautiful crescent mark (*candraka*) upon his forehead.
She applied a tilaka made of saffron, unbroken rice grains, and musk;
she also applied fragrant sandalwood paste and camphor to her body.
And he placed a garland of *pārijāta* flowers, which was dear to her, around her neck;
likewise, a necklace of jewels upon her neck and a gem-ornament on her wrist.
He gave him divine garments purified by fire, a radiant crown,
earrings, bracelets, and also anklets, rings, and so forth.
A pair of jeweled chowries, a golden umbrella,
his own diamond necklaces, the Kaustubha gem, garlands, and ornaments.
He placed crores upon crores of gold at the feet of Kṛṣṇa;
likewise, he offered incense, jewel-lamps, and the ritual waving of lights (nīrājana).
He indeed gave a beautiful golden lion-throne as a gift for Hari,
as well as water from seven sacred fords and likewise the honey-mixture (madhuparka).
Then he gave him water for sipping, betel, drinking water, and fragrant substances; as well as an excellent bed and ornaments. (16)
She offered a handful of flowers and likewise bowed at his feet;
Girijā also honored her daughter’s beloved with great respect.
She washed his feet, honored him with parched grain,
worshipped him with sandalwood paste and other offerings, and gave him gold coins and other gifts.
He took down from his head the household utensils,
as well as the key to the treasury, the pen, and the sword.
A pestle, a wooden scraper, a broom,
as well as a winnowing fan, a ladle, a chain, a wedge, and likewise a staff.
A trident, a conch, a discus, a mace, and a shield;
a rope, a small bell, a mirror, and likewise a water-pot. ||21||
A cooking vessel, auspicious pills, durvā grass, a bamboo stalk,
fruit, food, water, vegetables, an ornament, and likewise sacrificial fuel.
He removed all these [ornaments] from the head of Kṛṣṇa; then, having performed the lustration ceremony (*nīrājana*) over his head, he [removed them].
With palms joined in reverence, he meditated five or six times on the destruction of suffering;
then he caused [the deity] to enter through the gateway upon that ground.
And seeing that the shell of the universe, constructed from two skull-halves and bound together by the threads of *māyā*, was firmly established, Mādhava [reflected]. (25)
Then Hari placed his own foot upon it and broke it,
having thereby completely destroyed the obstacle and [revealed] the excellent golden lion-throne.
He took that seat which had been placed near the sacrificial pit;
he sat down right there and also bowed to the sacrificial post.
He bowed down in every direction to the water-pot, the Mātṛkās, Gaṇeśa, and likewise the deities, as well as the pavilion, the sacrificial pit, and the preceptor.
The Śiveśvara brahmins honored him with unbroken grains of rice;
thus, having received the formal invitation, the Blessed Lord Hari shone resplendently.
In the meantime, Lakṣmī, the daughter of Śiva who bestows happiness,
arrived at the edge of the altar in the pavilion along with her female companions.
Excellent musical instruments were played and songs were sung;
and the sounds of Vedic mantras arose from those who know the Vedas.
The beautiful Lakṣmī arrived there, accompanied by her mother and her friends;
adorned with ornaments of excellent jewels, she came on foot out of devotion.
Wearing garments purified by fire, adorned with her heavy braid of hair,
that virtuous woman, fragrant with sandalwood and other perfumes, gazed into a mirror.
Adorned with drops of musk and a dot of vermilion upon her forehead, she possesses the luster of molten gold and is beautiful with a halo of radiance. ||34||
Wearing ornaments and accompanied by offerings such as garlands, she arrived in the presence of the bridegroom together with her brothers and other relatives. (31)
Millions of great souls beheld her, who was like the moon;
indeed, Rādhā is the most radiant and supreme among all women in every creation. (36)
Seeing that [splendor] even more radiant than before, they praised it again and again;
and Lakṣmī, devoted to her husband, likewise bowed down to the pavilion.
Having prostrated before her husband, she performed seven circumambulations of the gods;
she sprinkled them with cool water and moistened them with tender sandalwood leaves.
Bālakṛṣṇa sprinkled that beloved Lakṣmī, who was smiling beautifully;
at that auspicious moment, the lover beheld his beloved, and the beloved beheld her lover.
O Rādhikā, listen in every way to that supreme wonder which occurred:
when the Lord consecrated Lakṣmī, at that very moment there was a consecration [of himself]. (2.293.40)
It fell from all sides upon the heads of all the maidens who had been brought outside; indeed, they all became filled with joy at that time. ||41||
Then Lakṣmī, having bowed to Kṛṣṇa, sat down upon the seat;
standing to his left, accompanied by her lord, she performed the worship of the deity. 42.
Bṛhaspati and Lomaśa both performed [the rites], proclaiming the place and time for the successful accomplishment of the gift of the maiden. (43)
On the fourth day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, they performed the worship of Gaṇeśa as well as the worship of Śrī Viṣṇu. (44)
There is also the worship of Rudra and likewise the worship of the Mātṛkās;
as well as the worship of the deities of the pavilion and of the Yoginīs. ||45||
The worship of the planets, the guardians of the directions, the Vasus, as well as the two Aśvins, the Ādityas, the sages, the ancestors, and the inhabitants of heaven; 46.
The worship of Brahmā and likewise the worship of the Īśvaras, the worship of all the lords, and likewise the worship of the Vighnas; ||47||
Likewise, there was the worship of the Rākṣasas who protect maidens,
as well as of the fires, the deities of the sacrificial pits, and those residing in the branches and archways.
They also caused the worship of Lakṣmī to be performed for those stationed at the gate, those within the pavilion, and those residing upon the ruby pillars. 49.
They likewise performed the worship of Pārvatī, the worship of Hanumān,
the worship of Durgā, and the Śrāddha ceremony.
In whatever manner the worship was performed, all the maidens, indeed all the daughters of Kṛṣṇa, observed it and performed it in that very same way. ||51||
Having thus performed the worship, he then worshipped the Āhavanīya fire situated within the sacrificial pit; then the maiden, having arisen, [offered] that which was born of flowers.
She placed her husband’s wide necklace around her own neck,
and she also prostrated at his feet, marking her forehead with saffron and unbroken grains of rice.
She applied a tilaka mark and a crescent moon ornament, offered a handful of flowers,
declared, "I am yours," and sat down upon her own seat.
And Kṛṣṇa placed a garland with unbroken grains and saffron around her neck;
and having applied moist [sandalwood paste], he drew a crescent moon upon her forehead.
And he gave her a lock of hair and auspicious vermilion;
he also offered a handful of flowers and a handful of gulāl. ||56||
She too gave a handful of auspicious clay to Kṛṣṇa;
then the two priests joyfully recited the mantras for the gift.
And all the maidens to be given away likewise performed the same;
then, upon the two wrists of the two [brides], they placed heavy ornaments that yielded the fruit of their desires.
Likewise, they tied knots at the ends of their garments;
they placed a garland around the necks of both, making it one long strand. (59)
And then, O Rādhikā, when all those maidens— numbering in the millions and billions—
found themselves for a moment without their beloved before them, they fell into deep anxiety.
Then that glorious Bālakṛṣṇa displayed a miracle;
he became possessed of ten million forms, wearing ten million times ten million garlands.
Regarding as many maidens as had been previously acquired, for each maiden there was a husband who possessed a form like that of a lotus.
Whichever [goddesses] were situated wherever, they remained there according to the prescribed rule;
just as Lakṣmī was on the right side, so too did all [the others] occupy their respective sides.
He took a garland for the neck and gave him vermilion and other such items,
as well as a bracelet made of *kāma-phala* fruit to be bound upon his forearm.
Indeed, everyone there who beheld it obtained everything;
and another wonder arose there—listen to this, O Rādhikā! (65)
Then, by the will of Bālakṛṣṇa, Bṛhaspati and Lomaśa became the pillars, the lotus-base, and the sacrificial pit of the pavilion.
Then the deities, beginning with the lotus-born Brahmā, were struck with awe;
even the fathers of the maidens experienced great wonder.
Śiva’s consort Pārvatī, beholding the supreme lordship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, as well as the majesty and sovereignty of the glorious Supreme Soul, [was filled with wonder]. (68)
Satisfied and serene, they were filled with joy and bowed down again and again;
and being captivated, they then beheld the entire ritual for the giving away of the maiden.
The fathers of those maidens remain there for the purpose of giving them away;
however, for those whose fathers no longer exist because they have passed away, [the gods stand in their stead].
Remembered by Bālakṛṣṇa, they arrived there quickly in their beautiful forms;
at the time of the gift, all those auspicious ones were seen filled with joy. ||71||
Lomaśa also attained great wonder, as did Bṛhaspati: "No such marvel has ever occurred before, nor will there ever be one again. (72)
Then, as all the people watched in the open light, this indeed occurred during the union of the maidens with their beloveds. (73)
Their own daughters, who were radiant with splendor, auspicious, and possessed of faces bowed down by modesty, were given away by their fathers according to the rite of giving. (74)
Then all of them gave their respective daughters to the Most Perfect One;
indeed, they placed the hands of the girls into the right hand of Bālakṛṣṇa.
All the fathers gave [their consent], and Śiva also gave her away;
they bestowed her through the formal gift-rite with Vedic mantras, O Rādhikā. (76)
This maiden is given by me to the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Self, to Bālakṛṣṇa, the seer. (77)
Having thus recited this and then holding water in their hands,
they poured it out upon the ground in the presence of Gaṇeśa, with fire as witness.
Then, by his father's command, Bālakṛṣṇa said, "May it be well," and Śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇa indeed accepted the maidens as Lakṣmīs.
Then, in a single moment, he assumed the form of as many Arbuda lotuses;
having seen such immense sovereignty, the most excellent Śiva offered praise.
Having attained the state of Śiva and assumed a divine form, he took his own ḍamaru drum in his hand, sounded it, and danced. ||81||
For you alone are that Supreme Lord, the witness of the entire world, the setter in motion of the wheel of creation, shining resplendent in the imperishable abode. 82.
He has come to my house for the sake of attaining ten million maidens;
today my home is blessed, and likewise my sacrifice here is eternal.
Since tens of millions of maidens with divine knots are offered in his house to the Supreme Lord, this most excellent Śiva is truly blessed. (84)
I bow to you alone—the Lord of lords, the Protector of protectors, known as the Supreme Lord, the Ancient Person;
the Beloved of my daughter, and likewise the Beloved of the daughters of Arbuda.
You are subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, golden-hued, the Inner Soul of the universe.
I bow to you, who are seated in the hearts of all beautiful women and who possess infinite forms. ||86||
You are the syllable named Oṃ, the seed of liberation; you are self-luminous, you are the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama).
You are the Lord of all, with ten thousand heads; you are eternal, you are the Supreme Person. 87.
Today I know you alone as that Ancient One, radiant as the sun, beyond the darkness;
you have come for the sake of my liberation, for she is indeed your own ancient beloved. (88)
I am indeed your ancient devotee; by gathering all beings together, you have surely delivered them.
I take refuge in You, who possess infinite forms, who grant birth in excellent forms, and who are worthy of supreme worship. ||89||
Having spoken thus to Śrīmat Bālakṛṣṇa, O Rādhikā, Śaṅkara gave him a dowry,
and then all the kings likewise presented gifts.
A celestial mansion made of ten million pieces of gold, radiant as the sun;
a wish-fulfilling creeper, a parasol for the head, and fly-whisks with handles of jewels.
A golden vessel for betel-leaf, as well as an inexhaustible vessel, a kalpa-vessel, and likewise golden sandals adorned with jewels and gems. (92)
A thousand cows that yield milk at will along with their calves, a thousand elephants, and a hundred thousand horses. ||93||
Śambhu offered everything within his reach—household utensils, beds, and so forth—to Hari, Bālakṛṣṇa. 94.
The kings there also gave auspicious beds that provide pleasure,
as well as various treasuries, gold, diamonds, and pearls.
Then the partisans of Hari also gave to Kṛṣṇa everything:
hand-clasps, wealth, gold, silver, thrones, and so forth. (96)
Vāsudeva gave him a divine crown and the elephant-throne;
Mahāviṣṇu gave him there a celestial vehicle, a flying chariot.
Vairāja gave two golden earrings and a golden parasol;
Brahmā gave a kalpa-vessel, and Viṣṇu then gave him his discus.
The ancestors presented various golden vessels, and the gods gave him caskets of nectar as well as divine garments. (99)
Then the guardians of the quarters gave divine golden coins;
the oceans likewise gave pearl necklaces and strings of pearls.
There the trees gave forth juices, and the kings joyfully presented jewels and gems, as well as cows, horses, elephants, and bulls in infinite numbers.
They then gave ten million female and male servants,
as well as whatever was most excellent within the three worlds, belonging to whomever it might have been at that time.
They all took each other's hands; indeed, they gave gifts of excellent articles, and those belonging to the bride's side also then gave her dowry.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa gave him a thousand gopīs adorned with jewels,
as well as diamond necklaces, strings of gems and jewels, and ornaments.
And Saṃkarṣaṇa likewise gave a crown worthy of a virtuous woman;
Sadāśiva gave jeweled necklaces, and Kāla gave garments.
He also gave him a divine garment free from decay, a bodice for one in the prime of youth, and an eternal [ornament]; likewise, the Rudras gave him garlands.
The Rudras gave him divine golden garlands and countless ornaments of adornment; Śaṅkara gave him a parasol.
The goddess gave a lion-throne, Kubera gave a *koṭikānaka* [drum], and Lakṣmī was then given wealth; the world-protectors likewise gave riches.
The celestial dwellers of heaven and Śeṣa and the others gave jewels; all the hosts of spirits and ghosts then gave garments and ornaments.
According to worldly custom and the custom of the gods as was appropriate, the men and women gave abundant gifts to the maidens and to their husbands.
The Supreme Brahman himself, whose very form is the universe, has today accepted this gift; indeed, it could not be contained within the pavilion.
Thus, after the gift, the fathers of the maidens then took water in their hands and spoke, declaring their lineage, names, and so forth.
Salutations to the great-souled Bālakṛṣṇa, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, the foremost among the Nārāyaṇas consisting of the syllable Kṛṣṇa, who has the Supreme Brahman as his lineage. 113.
To the eminent Brahmin who was a master of the Sāmaveda and a follower of the Patnīvratīya branch,
Śiva himself acted as witness in the presence of the fire for the illustrious Gopālabāla.
I belong to the lineage of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and am a descendant of Sadāśiva; my three *pravara* ancestors are named Rudra, Kāla, and Yama, and I am a follower of the Ṛgveda.
He gave me his daughter Śrī Lakṣmī, who is the very embodiment of Lakṣmī;
by that gift, may the Blessed One, Puruṣottama, be pleased. (1.16)
Having spoken thus, he again released the water upon the ground;
and there Hari spoke once more, saying, "I have taken it."
In this manner, all the fathers spoke likewise and shed tears;
thereafter, the two priests tied a divine knot upon his garment.
There, the two gurus caused the Lord and the maiden to circumambulate the fire four times, while garlands were placed around their necks.
Having bowed to the fire, the couples indeed sat upon their respective seats;
there, at that auspicious Gārhapatya fire, they performed the oblation.
They performed the oblation with ghee, sesame seeds, sugar, excellent fruits, rice, and various other sacrificial materials. 121.
Then, with mutual courtesy, they both accepted the honey-mixture (madhuparka) and the morsel of food placed into their mouths by Kṛṣṇa’s beloved.
Then, having touched each other’s hands with palms joined in reverence, they both bowed;
at that moment, perspiration quickly appeared on the forearms of Śrī.
At that time, even Kṛṣṇa experienced the bristling of his body hairs;
all the maidens, adorned with garlands on their necks, performed the circumambulation of the fire.
The monkeys also made their offerings and took mouthfuls of food;
likewise, they performed the oblations and other rites all at the same time.
Rādhikā, Rādhikā, Lakṣmī, Śrī, Ramā, Māṇikī,
and Padmāvatī— these six true maidens performed circumambulation.
Together with Vahni and Kṛṣṇa,
both Ramā and Padmāvatī performed the rites here in the pavilion provided by Hemanta.
Those other women, who had been given by Nārāyaṇa to Hari,
together with Vahni, performed the circumambulation of the fire along with their husband.
All the other beautiful women performed the circumambulation of the fire;
seeing the rite which bestowed supreme joy, they rejoiced together with their beloveds.
One hundred and forty maidens residing in the temple performed circumambulations together and offered morsels of food to Hari.
Likewise, all the daughters of Brahmā, as well as other daughters of Īśa, princesses, daughters of the world, and miscellaneous maidens, circumambulated [him]. (131)
And they made morsels for one another, giving their own excellent portions to the bridegroom and the brides following upon the taking of those morsels.
The ring slipped into the water of the stage;
hear from me here, O Rādhā, how Kṛṣṇa’s wives were attached to it. (133)

Thus, in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the second section, the *Tretā-santāna*, [is described] the worship of Kṛṣṇa performed by Śiveśvara; the removal of household utensils performed by Goddess Pārvatī; Kṛṣṇa’s sitting upon the seat in the pavilion; the arrival of the bride and the maidens; the worship of Kṛṣṇa and the worship of the gods; the binding with the fruit that grants desires; the giving away of the bride; the gifts given during the taking of the hand; Kṛṣṇa assuming as many forms as there were crores, billions, and hundreds of millions of brides; the taking of the hands of all the brides; and the wearing of garlands of necklaces by all of them.
The two hundred and ninety-third chapter, titled "The Description of Circumambulating All Fires and the Offering According to the Rules of Lineage and so forth. || 293 ||
Śrī Rādhikā said: Tell me here of all those beloved ones who have attained perfection, by the mere remembrance of whom a person is liberated from Māyā. || 1 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā, to how at that time you were with Bālakṛṣṇa—
how Lakṣmī was, how Ṣaṭkaṃ was, and how Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and Māṇikī were.
Ramā, Padmāvatī, and Śrī— these one hundred and forty principal daughters, beginning with Aśanā, who are beloved by Brahmā, were offered as gifts.
Adorned with garlands of flowers, they circumambulated the fire;
fourteen thousand Meghanādas were thus consecrated.
Likewise, on the sixth day, with his mind, he offered ten million lamps and young maidens after circumambulating the fire.
Talājā alone is known as the wish-fulfilling cow (Kāmadhenu), numbering ten million;
and Vasumatī and others, also numbering ten million, were acquired and offered. (6)
Śāmbhavī, Krodhanā, Kanyā, Dharāputrī, and Gahvarā—
ten million in number— were joyfully presented there by Dharā.
The daughter of Vedhas, Sucī, and a hundred thousand daughters of forest deities were present;
they were adorned with the bridegroom’s garland offered by the forest deity and were filled with joy.
A hundred thousand Rākṣasa maidens, adorned with flower garlands, were offered by Damana; having circumambulated the fire, they then took their places beside him.
Six young maidens and ten thousand *kaṅkatālikā* girls,
having placed fire upon the *kaṅkatāla* trees, performed a circumambulation of it.
Adorned with flower garlands, they were brought into union with Bālakṛṣṇa;
and the hundred thousand daughters of the Pitṛs, bestowed by Aryaman, were likewise taken as his own.
Twenty daughters of the people were made his own,
and ten thousand paternal slave-girls were also acquired there as his own.
Then five thousand maidens born of Daityas from Rāsātala,
having circumambulated the fire while holding flowers and sacrificial ladles, [approached].
Then Vāsanta gave him sixteen maidens who were as beautiful as spring;
having circumambulated the fire, they were indeed bestowed upon him.
Five hundred maidens of the Daitya Sālamālī, along with a hundred Mothers (Mātṛs), were surrendered there by the Daityas and brought under his own control. || 15 ||
Twenty thousand Svastika nāga maidens,
carrying flowers and incense, circumambulated the fire.
A thousand daughters of King Śāvadīna, adorned with beautiful garlands,
circumambulated the fire and were bestowed by the king upon him as his own.
And a thousand daughters of the illusionist, born of Śambhu and bestowed by Śambhu himself, were taken as his own wives in the presence of fire, adorned with flower garlands.
Sarasvatī and the fourteen branches of knowledge— these sixty maidens were offered by Brahmā with fire as witness and adorned with garlands.
And two thousand maidens from the subterranean regions of Lākṣmaṇya were indeed presented there by Lakṣmaṇa and taken as his own in the presence of the sacred fire as witnesses.
The seventy-two thousand channels (nāḍikās) were bestowed by Brahmā upon the daughter of Vedha,
and they were made his own in the presence of Agni as witness.
Three hundred maidens of the Gandharvas, presented by Viśvāvasu, circumambulated the fire while holding flowers and incense. ||22||
A thousand princesses of King Jummalā were offered by Jummalā;
having circumambulated the fire, they were made to enter it along with flowers and garments. ||23||
And five thousand Sāntapanī Rākṣasa maidens were offered by Sāntapana as witnesses before the fire, having been adorned with garlands.
Having performed a circumambulation of the fire a hundred times with gentleness, he presented the maidens, who were adorned with flower garlands and offered by the gods and sages.
The three maidens, having made the fire their witness, were offered by Mahābāla to Baleśvara; adorned with flower garlands, they were rendered his own. ||26||
Then the sole daughter of Ailavila was offered by Ilavila;
there, in the presence of the fire, she was presented along with a garland of flowers.
He took as his own one hundred daughters of the kings of Dakṣa’s lineage, who were adorned with beautiful garlands, as well as a thousand daughters of the Uṣṇālaya dynasty. ||28||
Having circumambulated the fire from left to right, those adorned with flower garlands—
the maidens from the eastern regions, the daughters of kings, and those born of common folk— [proceeded].
In the presence of the fire as witness, they were presented by their fathers in numbers reaching ten million;
they were adorned with saffron-colored garments and consecrated with excellent garlands.
The two daughters of the Brāhmaṇa Santāraṇa, adorned with flower garlands,
were presented there by Santāraṇa as his own daughters, with fire as witness.
Then, one hundred daughters of King Śibi-deva,
offered by Śibi and adorned with flower garlands, were made his own in the presence of the fire as witness.
The fifty daughters of King Tharkūṭastha were given with fire as witness;
they were presented by Tharkūṭastha, adorned with garlands of flowers, and made his own wives.
A hundred daughters of King Vīrajāra were indeed given away with fire as witness;
presented by Vīrajāra, they were adorned with flower garlands and made his own.
Śaktākṣī gave sixty princesses with fire as witness;
furthermore, a hundred Piśācinī maidens were offered by Śaktākṣī. (35)
Having circumambulated the fire, two hundred princesses of King Kāliṃśa, adorned with flower garlands and made ready, were presented by the king.
In the presence of Agni as witness,
thirty maidens of King Uralaketu, adorned with garlands of yoga, were offered there by the king himself.
In that place, accompanied by the *Yogamālā*, they were made to swear by fire;
indeed, the five daughters of King Kratha swore by fire as their witness.
There, twenty daughters of King Pṛthu, who had been offered by their father and were joined with the garland of yoga, were made his own and given to Agnika.
Having performed a circumambulation, they were made their own garlands of union.
And the daughters of Uṣṭrāla, the king, were presented by Daśoṣṭrāla.
In the presence of fire as witness, they were made naked there, adorned with flower garlands—
five for King Haṃkāra and five for Jayakāṣṭha.
There were six [elephants] belonging to King Tīrāṇa, five to King Alvīnara, and seven to King Jīnavardhin; likewise, there was one without a master. 42.
Having circumambulated the fire offered by various kings, they were united with Bālakṛṣṇa through the yoga-mālā. ||43||
Two hundred and one thousand auspicious maidens,
who had been seized by Rākṣasas, were made his own wives with fire as witness, having adorned themselves with beautiful garlands.
Alpaketu had seven daughters; Jayakṛṣṇa had one daughter, Ekalā; and likewise, King Parīkṣit had twenty-one daughters. ||45||
At that time, King Indurāya also had two beautiful daughters, and King Mudrāṇḍa had fifteen daughters adorned with ornaments. (46)
Gaṇḍabhūpa had nine [wives],
and Bṛhaccharanṛpa likewise had four daughters-in-law and eleven maidens.
There were forty daughters of King Balalin, five of Varasiṃha, and eight born of Rāyagāma. (48)
For the king Phenatantu there are two, for Stokahoma one;
for the king Kāṣṭhāyāna there is one, and for Kolaka also one. 49.
Two daughters of King Dinamāna, together with Yogamālikā,
circumambulated the fire and were offered by their respective fathers.
Those fifty-one daughters of Rāya Kinnara-rāja, who had been offered by kings, were taken into his own service by Bālakṛṣṇa. ||51||
Likewise, there were twenty-one daughters of Rāyakoṭīśvara,
and twenty daughters of Rāyaraṇajit;
and at that time, there were three daughters of King Rāyavākakṣa.
And King Rāyamārīśa had three beautiful daughters. ||53||
Rāyabaleśvara also had three other daughters;
furthermore, King Rāyalambāra had six daughters endowed with youth.
King Rāyanavārka had seven very beautiful daughters;
King Rāyahūṇḍeśa had nine very delicate daughters. (55)
There was one virtuous and auspicious daughter of King Rāyakūpeśa,
as well as four daughters of King Kālīmaṇḍa.
The five daughters of King Vanajeleśa were very pale,
while even the three daughters of Pārāvārapiba were deeply red.
King Koṭīśvara had two daughters, King Satīśa had three, and King Tretākarkaśa had seven beautiful daughters. (58)
King Āṇḍajara also had four auspicious daughters,
and King Bālyarajas had one daughter who was endowed with righteousness.
King Rāyasomanabha had three very beautiful daughters,
and King Ūrugavākṣa likewise had two beautiful daughters.
The daughter of King Rājārāya, sister of the king who turned his back [in battle], was alone;
the forty-one beautiful daughters of the lord of Īśānapāna were likewise alone. (6.1)
The thirty-three daughters of kings, lords of men, and sovereigns of the earth—
all of them were there at that time, adorned with garlands of yoga.
Adorned with royal ornaments bestowed by their respective fathers,
they circumambulated the fire and were taken into the care of Bālakṛṣṇa.
Thirty maidens, beginning with Maṅgalā, were presented by the great sages;
they were taken as his own wives by Bālakṛṣṇa for those various sages.
Ten thousand radiant maidens from the regions of Ājanābha, belonging to various kings, were presented by their respective fathers and other relatives.
Ten thousand daughters of subjects were presented by the people—richly adorned with every ornament and graced with garlands of yoga. ||66||
Having circumambulated the fire, those who had been made their own by Bālakṛṣṇa [performed the rites] individually in separate sacrificial pits, each in the presence of a separate fire.
At that time, the taking of their hands in marriage took place for all of them—
Rādhikā, as well as the others, and thousands of daughters of Kubera.
And by the thousands were the daughters of Mahendra, and by the thousands the daughters of Yama;
those of Vāyu, Vaiśvakarman, the trees, Rudra, and those born of Fire.
There were also the Śrāvaṇyas, Khānijyas, Sāṃvatsaryas, Gopikās,
Prācīnyas, Piśaṅginīs, and Rāśiyānyas by the millions;
as well as the Raumāyanīs, Pāraśvas, and Dhaivaryas by the thousands.
There were also millions of Kinnarīs, Apsarases, Gaurīs, and Pārṣadās. || 71 ||
There were also those from Ābhīra, Hārita, Pātāla, and Svarga;
and even crores of Apsaras from the Brahma-lake and the Gandharvas.
Vidyunmaṇiśca, the skillful Yoginī, and two others; likewise, there were Bhaumyas and Dānavīs numbering in the hundreds of millions, billions, and trillions.
Who among men with limited vision could possibly calculate their number?
All of them, having remembered their fathers and ancestors, stood in close proximity near their father. (74)
Adorned, having secured the ends of their garments, and being in the full bloom of youth,
they then performed circumambulations of the fire while wearing garlands of yoga.
Then, each of them was indeed accepted individually by the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa through the grasping of their hands, which had been offered by their respective fathers and others.
While everyone was looking on, the Supreme Soul Bālakṛṣṇa married them all in the presence of the fire, having entrusted them to the witness of all.
O Rādhikā, at the beginning of creation, these were made known to you by the Supreme Soul;
indeed, all these beloveds of Brahmā were wedded by Brahmā himself.
Those [goddesses] have arisen from the form of Hari; they are indeed the powers (śaktis) of Hari, who have come to the earth for the sake of Hari throughout the entire creation.
Abiding as they please at all times, those who are entirely devoted to Kṛṣṇa have taken refuge in the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa in Kāśī.
They were given in the courtyard of Śiveśvara, where Time does not exert its power;
for Śiva is indeed the very nature of Time, and therefore they have transcended it by being offered to him. 8.1
All those [images] that have passed the prescribed time and are composed of the form of Kṛṣṇa indeed bestow liberation;
Saurāṣṭra is born from my jewel, and Bālakṛṣṇa shines here. (82)
Having entered into marriage with Kāśī, he shines throughout the three worlds;
and all those [goddesses], waiting for him, have indeed today attained that marriage.
They became fulfilled and filled with eternal bliss;
Lakṣmī, the daughter of Śiva and Īśvara, attained her own beloved on earth. 84.
Padmavatī, daughter of the quarters; Subhāsvarā, daughter of the Sun;
Śrī, daughter of the Kalpa-tree; and Lakṣmī, daughter of the Ocean of Milk. (81)
And Māṇikyā, the daughter of Divyavibhūti, the virtuous Akṣarī,
Kamalā, and others likewise, having obtained the auspicious Hari as their beloved— 86.
They became fulfilled and were provided with every luxury;
all were married there during that auspicious conjunction of the two Kṛṣṇas.
Listen, O Rādhā, what then happened regarding King Śivachattra of Kāśī.
Likewise, Dhenupāla was also a supreme king among the devotees of Śiveśvara.
Beholding the infinite, supreme lordly power within Bālakṛṣṇa,
the King of Kāśī immediately gave him all ten of his daughters.
In the meantime, Dhenu-pāla gave him three daughters with Agni as witness.
And those women, accompanied by their retinues of female attendants, were brought here into the pavilion.
Then the king bestowed upon them a dowry of one hundred thousand gold pieces,
as well as a palanquin, a hundred female slaves, and various ornaments.
Then the subjects also gave various kinds of gifts to Bālakṛṣṇa in the pavilion; afterwards, there was an oblation into that sacrificial pit. || 92 ||
Having offered into the fire the excellent household duties as instructed by his guru, the bridegroom,
together with his wife, heard there the duties to be protected on all sides:
"O Mādhava, protect the indivisible dharma of the couple."
And these women here are your consorts; protect them all.
O Supreme Lord, perceive happiness in happiness and likewise sorrow in sorrow;
the beloved and the lover are indeed not distinct, for they bring about the unity of two bodies. 95.
Perceive all beloved ones as being like yourself and gladden them;
for within the midst of those beloved ones, your own body shines forth.
Head to head, face to face, heart to heart; belly to belly, middle to middle, and feet to feet. || 97 ||
Considering her body and your own body as one, protect them both;
perform together here those religious duties that serve to increase the lineage. (98)
One's own beloved should indeed be regarded as one's very life;
one should always serve that life-force in every way, as if it were the Lord himself. 99.
Chastity must always be maintained by wives for the sake of happiness;
the command of the husband must always be obeyed even at the cost of one's life and all other actions. (2.294.100)
"The Lord himself should be contemplated and worshipped with a sense of oneness.
Having perceived this, couples should conduct themselves constantly in this manner. 101.
Rivalry should never be displayed toward one another;
co-wives should always behave toward each other as if they were sisters.
O daughters, you must always take pleasure in providing happiness to your fellow wives.
The portions of the Lord must indeed be understood as his own parts; it is never otherwise. 103.
"Thus one should remain firm in the bull [of dharma]; may there be well-being for you, happiness, and peace.
Having spoken thus, the two gurus performed a sprinkling with water from the vessel of sprouts. || 10.4 ||
Kṛṣṇa gave a profuse sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), as well as many young maidens,
ten million jewels, gems, and ten million measures of gold.
Then the two gurus performed the concluding rites of the sacrificial ritual,
as well as the dismissal of the deities and the dismissal of all [the participants].
Then Hari swiftly brought about the dissolution of his many forms.
In the meantime, the goddess Girijā arrived quickly,
preceded by virtuous women who possessed sons and husbands.
Then all the Mothers, who dwell within every creation, arrived there as well; having performed all auspicious rites, they performed the ritual sprinkling and other ceremonies.
They caused the couple to dwell in a palace fashioned of jewels, which was illuminated as if it were fit for the residence of ten million, a hundred billion, and a hundred trillion celestial maidens.
It was created by Viśvakarman as if it were a second Goloka, newly renovated with the assistance of the liberated one named Kailāsa. || 2.294.110 ||
They caused the maidens to dwell upon very precious lion-thrones, and they also had them fed together with their lord.
They offered camphor, betel-leaf, and scented water;
then Sarasvatī and all the Mothers of Creation spoke.
May the goddesses who are truthful, virtuous, devoted to Nārāyaṇa, faithful to their husbands,
and auspicious maidens bestow supreme blessing.
Just as the master, so too has the maiden been united by the Supreme Self;
may the unions of the wise with the wise be auspicious.
Then the Lord of Śivā honored all the great men and women according to the prescribed rites and fed them with due respect.
"Let it be eaten! Let it be enjoyed! Let what is desired be sucked and licked again and again! Let it be given, let it be given, and let it be taken; may you be satisfied! || 1.16 ||
"Drink! Taste!"—such was the incessant sound that arose;
within the halls, there was a clamor accompanied by the auspicious sounds of musical instruments and song.
Thus, at the end of the meal at night, when even the betel-leaf has been discarded,
the lords of the earth attained supreme peace, rest, and auspicious sleep.
Both sides took up residence in the vast, well-constructed city;
even the infinite Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa stayed in the home of the royal couple.
In whatever number the beloved women were, the Lord assumed that many forms;
served by them upon soft beds, he became the bestower of happiness.
O Rādhikā, even hundreds of millions of billions of consorts are never able to conquer this yogin, who possesses infinite being and infinite vigor.
At night, there were dances, sports, and other excellent arts of wrestling,
the sounding of musical instruments, and performances of dramatic arts.
In that city, the festivities for the wedding were suspended;
thereafter, from the middle of the night onwards, the entire circle of Satyamandala became truly peaceful.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of Those Married with Fire as Witness in the Second Tretā Cycle of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā; Instruction on Domestic Duties; Renunciation of Marriage Rituals; Feeding of the Couple; Feeding of All; Renunciation of the Forms of Koṭi, Arbuda, and Abja; and the Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in the Form of All with All in the House of the Couple, as well as Their Sleeping Together. || 294 ||
Śrī Rādhikā said:
How many beloved maidens were enumerated at that time in the chamber of amorous play—
those who were previously obtained, and how many indeed were obtained thereafter?
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhikā, those maidens who were offered by their own fathers and others—those beloved ones numbered four crores, that is, four hundred thousand.
Furthermore, fifty-five thousand, six hundred, and twenty-two new maidens were brought under his control. (3)
Then other maidens, starting with Kauberī, who had come from the three worlds, arrived;
they were indeed Arbudā, Svāgatā, Tathābjā, and Sūkṣmavartikā.
O Rādhikā, these very friends were in the palace of Bālakṛṣṇa on the bed of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
All those beloved women, numbering in the hundreds of billions of trillions, were indeed in the pleasure-chamber;
they remained there for that long upon beds of hundreds of billions of trillions, endowed with excellent boons.
Then, when morning had dawned on the fifth day, Śrī Hari was [awakened] at that time by auspicious songs and the sounding of beautiful musical instruments.

[He was honored] by the singing of the fame of hired bards and panegyrists, by the recitations of the twice-born, by the sounds of Vedic hymns and chants, and by the praises offered by the cane-bearers.
The Lord also woke up, and all the mistresses woke as well;
having performed their baths and daily rites, and adorned with ornaments, they were like young Kṛṣṇas.

Accompanied by beloved women adorned with the splendor of their finery, he rose early in the morning and honored the elders, the venerable, the gurus, the most excellent, and the virtuous, faithful wives.
Having received the blessings of the elders and accompanied by ten million women and men,
he, prepared for the festival procession, set out to wander through the city.
Then, according to the instructions of the elders, the yogayātrī was properly prepared,
made beautiful, filled with blossoming purpose, and most splendid.
Then, with a virtuous heart, he ascended his own celestial chariot, which possessed the splendor of an elephant,
was vast, exceedingly beautiful, and had been fashioned by the Creator of the Universe.
It is also broad enough for the path and many yojanas in length;
it is well-served by rivers carrying their own waters, numbering in the millions, billions, and trillions.
The Supreme Lord shone upon that celestial chariot, Bhūsparśa,
which had been sent by Śiva— the one known as Kailāsa— and was newly established there.
Adorned with the fragrance of saffron paste, Kashmiri saffron, and musk, it shone with rows of flower offerings and was beautiful in its entirely circular form. 16.
It was a sight of countless golden lion-thrones, enchanting to behold,
arranged like a trough for scattering flowers, resembling a vessel of saffron paste.
It was preceded by men who were foremost among those honored by the earth,
and followed behind by women who were foremost among those honored by the earth, resounding with the noise of song.
Likewise, it was accompanied by the parents and other relatives of the couple;
it was honored with the foremost of all musical instruments and filled with resounding music.
The celestial chariot of Śrī Śaṅkara was worshipped in the courtyard of the house; it was attended by a couple who offered handfuls of full-blown gulāla flowers.
Advancing slowly at first, revealing great bliss,
that army proceeded forward from the temple of Śiva.
Then the people of the community honored the couples with fruits and other offerings,
with gifts of wealth, necklaces, hand-gifts, flowers, and auspicious blessings.
Having wandered through the entire city of Girijā, the goddess Phullayātrikā accepted all the worship offered by the subjects and increased their prosperity.
Then, having wandered through the entire city of Kāśīpattana, including its outskirts, he likewise beheld the sight of Durgā, the family deity.
The sight of Hanumān and the sight of Viśveśvara;
the sight of Annapūrṇā and also the sight of Gaṇeśa. (25)
On the banks of the five Gaṅgās, he also beheld Dharmadeva and worshipped him with wealth, gifts, flowers, leaves, fruits, and other offerings. ||26||
Having performed [these rites] everywhere, he then went to Bindumādhava;
there, having worshipped the illustrious Mādhava and given gifts and sacrificial fees, [he stayed].
The celestial chariot, indeed, moved away over the purifying waters of the Gaṅgā;
the beloved women were bound by the knots of yoga, and the lover likewise [was bound] by the river water.

Having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) and worshipped that most excellent sacred ford (tīrtha), and having asked forgiveness from the glorious Gaṅgā and offered a gift of lamps; ||29||
They offered a gift of much gold into his mouth accompanied by mantras;
there, the true guru Lomaśa untied the knots of yoga.
Then, by means of a celestial chariot, the Lord once again departed through the middle of the city along the royal highway, accompanied by the sounding of musical instruments.
Men and women stood everywhere, eager to see him;
having seen him again and again—so beloved, so handsome, so worthy, and so beautiful.
Indeed, they praised in many ways the supreme happiness of the divine couple;
there, being enchanted by Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, they spoke thus to one another. (33)
And this very one is the Blessed One, the treasury of compassion; O friend, when will that Lord meet us?
For here, the Lord has been found by many young maidens.
It is through compassion alone, and certainly not from the accumulation of one's own merit. ||34||
O friend, having obtained here this human body which is so difficult to attain, if the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa is not served,
then the bonds of worldly existence will never come to an end.
Let this Lord be beheld with your own eyes. ||35||
He is worshipped by the infinite retinues who gaze upon the supreme syllable, and by the bliss-bestowing wives of the Lord;
he is also worshipped by maidens within the various worlds.
The Giver of Happiness has arrived here; let him be sprinkled [with water]. ||36||
For he possesses the power to assume many millions of forms; for he is the fulfiller of the essence of all desired pleasures.
Though abiding within the heart, he is yet visible to one's own eyes.
Let it be accepted here by her as she falls. ||37||

In former times, the Vedas served him with songs of his glories; moreover, maidens in human form, as well as the wives of the gods and princesses, attended upon him together—behold those who travel in celestial chariots like the goddess Harivati.
Surely it is easily accessible through the wealth of merit and knowledge;
