yet we are bereft of such wealth here. Indeed, we have not obtained that which exists in the other, imperishable state.
It is also desired in terms of the vessel and the dissolution. ||39||
O friend, just as the tip of the beloved’s tongue is enjoyed here,
yet Hari is not obtained even through one's own karma;
and even if He were obtained, He is certainly not enjoyed here.
Even then, one's own birth is seen to be fruitless. ||2.295.40||
May they, adorned with beautiful garlands, remain victorious for many years, immersed in an ocean of happiness;
may they possess the splendor of the most excellent form of a hundred crores of Kamadevas.
And may they also find happiness and attain true bliss. ||41||
O friend, a longing for his lotus-face arises within me; what means is there here to attain it?
This very prayer is present within my heart—you yourself.
May he indeed grant us a new union there. ||42||
O bride, you who have been saluted by the Lord, please look upon us, for we are indeed your handmaidens;
at some time, in the place of delight, [look upon] your own husband.
For this is indeed our request: "May you grant us remembrance. ||43||
Having praised them with the words "O Rādhikā! and so forth, and having bowed down and placed Lord Hari within their hearts, they honored the Lord Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa with flowers and other offerings. 44.
Listen, O Rādhā; having beheld the Supreme Brahman, thousands of celestial women worshipped Him and, full of longing, offered Him their praises.
Then, by their mother’s command, those three hundred and four maidens, remaining unhurt, fainted along the way as they beheld the Lord, the bridegroom.
Having worshipped him, they indeed placed flower garlands around the neck of the Lord; once offered by the mothers, those garlands caused him to ascend into the middle of the celestial chariot.
And those wives of Kṛṣṇa were born as Gāndharva maidservants forever;
thus, O Rādhā, they are the wives of the beginningless Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. 48.
There were four crores, four lakhs, and even more than that—fifty-six thousand added to the previous total. (49)
Those numbering in the millions, billions, and trillions, as well as others, have been rendered soulless;
they all rejoice together with those who possess equal forms and are entirely identical.
By the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇas and the Śrī Bāla Kṛṣṇas, [the lineage was established]; thereafter, in the Tretā age, there arose the Vāhinī of Phullayātrī.
Having gone to the unsurpassed residence of Śivasvāmin, the city, the Phulla festival procession was then canceled, which brought auspiciousness. (52)
Śiveśvara and the others, filled with eagerness, departed for their own abodes;
thereafter, Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the others proceeded to the auspicious city of Pārvatī.
Then Śaṅkara caused all the great lords to partake of food according to the prescribed rite, providing indeed many kinds of delicious dishes.
Various kinds of milk-rice, even the most excellent boiled rice, as well as leafy vegetables, pulses, and all manner of foods to be chewed or swallowed; ||55||
Śaṅkara fed him all kinds of foods to be licked and sucked, whatever sweet drinks there were, and even all the nectars.
Then Śaṅkara fed all the dignitaries, the parties of the bride and groom, the villagers, the subjects, and the poor mendicants. (57)
And likewise all the groups of attendants, the groups of dancers and the like, all the groups of panegyrists, and indeed all the musicians; ||58||
He [honored] the carriers, all the guards, as well as the singers, the laborers, the ascetics, the virtuous, and the guests who had arrived. ||59||
To all the Brahmins, to all the gurus, to those dear to Brahmā, as well as to the Lord, to Kṛṣṇa’s father, his brothers, and his entire family; || 2.295.60 ||
Śivarāja fed them all and gave them drinks;
he provided for everyone dwelling in the netherworld as well as all those dwelling on earth.
He fed all those dwelling in heaven and elsewhere, all those dwelling in the abodes of the lords, and all those dwelling in the imperishable realm in many ways.
She fed the sages, the virtuous men, and the chaste women who were observant of celibacy; likewise, she fed the groups of renunciants, the groups of yogis, and the lords.
She also fed even the insects, moths, and the like, as well as the beasts and flocks of birds.
Those born from sweat, those born from water, and those born from the earth—both the stationary and the moving.
He [beheld] sacred fords, mountains, rivers, streams, and oceans;
all the wish-fulfilling creepers and the like, as well as all the gods and shrines.
Śaṅkara fed the bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and others, as well as the gandharvas, kinnaras, cāraṇas, and those dwelling in Kāśī.
He also provided drinks, betel leaves,
and abundant sacrificial fees consisting of gold, silver, and fine pearls.
Then Śiva gave there golden seals, ornaments, garments, and garlands, numbering in the millions, tens of millions, and hundreds of millions.
Afterwards, he gave her a dowry consisting of ten million gold rings,
a casket of recipes, a vessel of recipes, and likewise an inexhaustible cooking pot.
Also the inexhaustible treasury, the unimpeded parasol,
the vessel containing all flavors, and the beautiful creeper possessing every fragrance.
A doll possessing all forms, a pill of perpetual youth, a fly-whisk that grants movement through the sky, armor that wards off the power of time; ||71||
At that time, he indeed gave to Bālakṛṣṇa a bed called Ānandanidhi, as well as the Pāraśa jewel and the Cintāmaṇi.
The King of Kāśī also gave a celestial chariot with the splendor of the sun,
a hundred elephants, a thousand horses, and a thousand wish-fulfilling cows (kāmadhenu).
A hundred thousand bulls, a hundred thousand horses with black ears, a thousand female slaves, and likewise a lion-throne of jewels.
The kings, as far as those born from the navel [of Viṣṇu], also gave as wedding gifts the "Death-eater" great staff and the "Disease-destroyer" cane-stick.
From their very navels, they produced offspring and likewise gave dowries;
so too did the fathers, brothers, and mothers of the maidens bestow them.
They also gave the maiden’s dowry, consisting of beautiful ornaments, garments, and the like,
as well as gems, diamonds, garlands, necklaces, and those fashioned with jewels.
Golden, silver, and jewel-encrusted vessels, pearls,
celestial chariots, excellent vehicles, and beds adorned with couches.
Likewise, the liberated ones and the lords, as well as the incarnations and the hosts of goddesses, the gods, the ancestors, the great seers, and human beings. ||79||
Everyone gave wedding gifts in every way according to their respective fitness;
then, when the distribution of the wedding gifts was completed, Hari himself [bestowed his own].
He bestowed golden rewards upon those worthy recipients according to their merit,
giving ten thousand to each among the servants, the attendants, and the dependents.
He also gave gold to the laborers, as well as to the singers, the barbers, and the carriers. (82)
He gave wealth to the body-massagers, as well as to the female attendants, the scrubbers, the washers, and the decorators. (83)
He gave wealth to the female dancers, the instrumentalists, and the singers; he gave wealth to the hired actors, the bards, the captive women, and the Vidyādharas. ||84||
Likewise, he gave wealth to the musicians and to the artists and painters;
he bestowed wealth upon those who showed him the way and those who were victorious.
He gave wealth to those who manage waterworks, to those who manage wind, and to those who manage fire;
he bestowed wealth upon those who drive carts, those who travel in celestial chariots, and those who ride in chariots.
He gave wealth to the banner-bearers, the musicians, and the charioteers;
he gave wealth to the guards, the companions, and the mendicants. ||87||
He bestowed wealth upon the maidens, the youths, and the virtuous women;
he gave wealth to the *nālinīs*, the *śodhinīs*, and the *tālinīs*.
He gave wealth to the Vaṃśins, to the twice-born, and to the followers of various religious orders;
he also gave wealth to the Darśakas and to the Lambahastakas. ||89||
Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa gave even to those who merely desired it in their minds;
and the kings likewise gave gold, silver, and rings.
They gave alms-bowls, garments, and wealth by way of rewards to the weavers, the garland-makers, and the dyers. ||9.1||
Hari himself gave wealth even to the Gandharvas, the Sārīs, and the birds, as well as to Kailāsa, the pavilion, and the embodied form [of the deity]. 92.
He gave golden crowns, each worth ten million billion lotuses,
and he also bestowed golden rewards upon all the Gaṇas.
The beginningless Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa also gave rewards to others, as well as to his sisters' sons and daughters. 94.
There, Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa gave excellent golden ornaments, garments, and other items to the God who accomplishes all tasks;
he also gave a golden neck-ornament set with ten million diamonds.
Then the Blessed One, possessing the nature of the Supreme Lord, gave to Śiveśvara a beautiful crown made of gold and jewels,
as well as a divine throne that is unassailable throughout the three worlds.
Śiveśvara also gave his entire possession to the Supreme Self,
and then Hari likewise bestowed his entire possession upon Bṛhaspati.
Thus they bestowed there appropriate rewards according to merit;
then, at midday, they obtained a brief rest.
Then the Blessed One, desiring once again to bathe at a sacred ford,
went back to the Gaṅgā together with all the women and the great sages.
Then he performed the rites at sacred fords and indeed gave various gifts;
having performed penances, he bathed again and again.
All the beautiful women bathed and gave abundant gifts;
then Śambhu, disguised as a brahmin, arrived there as a mendicant.
The Blessed One begged for alms; he gave a hundred thousand gold pieces.
He begged again, and then he gave him a garland of tulasī.
Then he requested again, and Hari gave him his own form, a golden image endowed with all beautiful features; Śaṅkara said, "May it be well."
Hari again requested him to speak; Śambhu replied, "Tell me here:
for the sake of the holy ford, he indeed requested a dwelling in the Gaṅgā."
At Varaṇā, Hari likewise requested a dwelling from the Supreme Soul; "So be it," the Lord replied on the bank of the waters of the five Gaṅgās.
Having established Bālakṛṣṇa as a great sacred site (tīrtha), Hari then dwelt there;
he remains forever invisible, existing in another divine form.
On the fourth and fifth days of the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa,
he arrives every year accompanied by the beloved of Brahmā.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra;
from bathing and giving gifts to Him at that time, the fruit of liberation is certain.
Then, having bathed together with his beloved, Śrī Hari went to the city of Śiva;
after drinking milk and other refreshments, Acyuta attained rest.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Number of Wives, the Morning Procession and Wandering for the *Phullaka* Festival on the Fifth Day, the Untying of Knots at the Gaṅgā, the Midday Meal, Resting upon arriving at Śivapura, the Presentation of Rewards and Gifts, the Repeated Holy Bath in the Gaṅgā, the Bālakṛṣṇa Tīrtha, the Granthi Tīrtha at Pañcagaṅgā, and the Giving of Alms to Śaṅkara," in the second section (Tretā-santāna) of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhikā, wherever the Lord performed his wedding ceremony in a pavilion,
that place is indeed eternally known as the sacred site (tīrtha) called Udvāha.
Likewise, at Varaṇā, there is the auspicious Koṭitīrtha which bestows liberation;
there the Blessed One accepted those [waters] in the form of ten million, a hundred million, and a billion [streams]. || 2 ||
Then there is the sacred site of Śivapura, as well as Pārvatīpattana;
the sacrificial site known as Maṇḍapa is called the essence of the earth.
On the fifth day, at the end of the third watch, Śaṅkara granted leave;
he bestowed many riches upon all those belonging to the dark fortnight.
He performed the worship of Kṛṣṇa and also asked his father for forgiveness; he likewise asked for forgiveness from the groups of deities beginning with Mahīmāna for any deficiency in his service.
With a faltering throat, Śiva himself, the sovereign lord, made his request;
even that king Śivachatra then repeatedly begged for forgiveness.
She also gave him excellent food and drink, including well-cooked meals smeared with ghee, as well as provisions for his journey, intended for his protection and sustenance.
And Hara deposited all his personal property in that most excellent celestial chariot;
he also gave him a host of attendants to serve as the bearers of the chariot.
Then musical instruments were played that indicated the dawn; the sounds of mechanical devices arose, and at that time, auspicious sounds of song emerged.
Śiveśvara also mentally embraced Gopāla Kṛṣṇaka; having asked for forgiveness regarding any deficiency in his service, he spoke as follows.
O giver of honor, you must come here considering this home as your own, and regarding me and my family—especially this daughter of yours—as your own kin; indeed, we must be protected by you.
Having obtained auspicious writing materials and saffron from Lakṣmaṇa, as well as from his brothers and his kinsmen; || 12 ||
Likewise, the Lord Hari, who consists of all the gods, begged for forgiveness from all his brothers and sons who were possessed of divine nature.
From Akṣara she obtained the multitude of liberated beings, and likewise Kṣamā from Vāsudeva;
from Pradyumna and Aniruddha she obtained Bhūmi, and also Virāj from Manu.
[He is superior] to all incarnations, as well as to Nārāyaṇa, Nara,
Viṣṇu, Mahāviṣṇu, Brahmā, and likewise Śaṅkara.
He likewise begged for forgiveness from Aryaman, Sanatkumāra, and the others who were present, as well as from the sages, the virtuous, the gods, the goddesses, and the women.
It went to the abodes of kings, world-protectors, guardians of the directions, and gods,
as well as to human beings and to the women related to Bālakṛṣṇa.
Although he begged for forgiveness, he nevertheless gave a fitting parting gift to all embodied beings dwelling on earth who had come from the world of the Nagas.
The Lord begged forgiveness from the men and women of Saurāṣṭra, as well as leave-taking,
water for drinking, sweet and desired food, and beautiful flower garlands.
Śivasvāmī gave these [gifts] to them and met them with his chest;
Hara, with palms joined in reverence, begged for forgiveness from the venerable Āryās. (2.296.20)
Then Śiva, the goddess Pārvatī, and all the Mothers quickly paid homage to the illustrious Kaṃbharā and begged her for forgiveness.
Having honored and bowed to the other noble ladies, she, being of a humble nature,
begged for forgiveness from them regarding the verbal offense committed during her service.
He requested forgiveness for any deficiency in the giving of material gifts, in protection, in honoring, in welcoming, as well as in feeding, putting to sleep, and providing drink. (23)
"My daughter is your daughter, O Mother; you must protect her.
And occasionally, O most affectionate one, send some pleasant news. (24)
He asked forgiveness from his young daughters-in-law, saying, "Protect your domestic prosperity," and having spoken thus,
he gave them the appropriate leave-taking.
He also gave flower garlands and offered water for drinking and other refreshments;
and Śivachattra then begged for forgiveness and a boon.
Then Śiveśvara also begged for forgiveness;
the king, a devotee of Śiva, begged for forgiveness from Kambharā. (27)
All the beloved ones, their eyes streaming with tears, bowed to their parents;
Jayā and the others, as well as Candrapālā and the rest, also implored them for forgiveness.
Then Jyeṣṭhāśokā, Lakṣmī’s sister-in-law, quickly [approached].
For the sake of his sister Santoṣā’s welfare, he even begged for forgiveness.
Then other women requested forgiveness from their brothers' wives;
in this way, the women [inquired after] one another's welfare, and the men [inquired after] each other's well-being.

After inquiring after one another and bestowing leave-taking gifts, the members of the bridegroom’s party and the honored guests, headed by Śrī Kṛṣṇa, then presented garlands of flowers to each other. ||3 1||
Likewise Saṃkarṣaṇa, Rudra, Śaṃkara, and Śeṣa;
also Mahākāla, Yama, the Lord of Yakṣas, and the Bhairavas of the spirits. ||32||
Skanda, Gaṇeśa, Nandin, Vīrabhadra, and the others—all numbering more than millions upon millions—as well as Caṇḍī and the other Śaktis. ||33||
From Bālakṛṣṇa, from Kāṃbhareya, and likewise from Gopālakṛṣṇa;
from Vāsudeva, from Vyāsadeva, and from Kapila Nārāyaṇa. ||34||
Then they entreated Viṣṇu, Dharma, and Virāja for patience;
they entreated them for well-being, happiness, security, and a spirit of affection.
Rādhā, Lakṣmī, Satī, Durgā, Sarasvatī, Nārāyaṇī, Kamalā, the wives of the sages, the goddesses, and likewise the courtesans. ||36||
Then the hosts and the attendants likewise [honored] Kambharāmātā,
as well as Mahālakṣmī, Lakṣmī, Sāvitrī, and Vaiṣṇavī.
Having bowed to Sūrya, Candra, the Vasus, the Sādhyas, as well as Saṃjñā and Rohiṇī,
he begged these goddesses for forgiveness, happiness, and peace.
They also gave him a parting gift of flower garlands, unbroken grains, and other offerings;
thus did all the honored ones dwelling in the three worlds [act]. (39)
Men and women gathered together and begged for forgiveness from one another;
they then offered blessings to Śrī Hari and to their beloved wives.
All the men and women of their respective parties became ready indeed when Kṛṣṇa and his beloveds arrived at the celestial chariot to sit within it. ||41||
Placing their heads at the feet of their parents, the young maidens then wept for a moment, born of the pain of separation from their loved ones.
Placing Jānakī and the other mothers and daughters upon their chests,
they shed tears and drenched them with the water from their eyes.
"And how can we live without you daughters, who are as dear as life itself? O little ones, do not go from our home to the house of Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa. (44)
Having spoken thus, the daughters seated themselves upon the celestial chariot;
the parents also then summoned their fortitude and seated their sons there.
Lord Bālakṛṣṇa also shed tears through his divine power (māyā),
and Śrīgopālakṛṣṇa caused him to ascend the celestial chariot.
Then Śiva and the others, being deeply moved, indeed presented their beloved son and family as a distinguished dowry. ||47||
Elephants and horses, female slaves and servants, gold, priceless jewels and ornaments, vessels, and likewise fragrant cows. ||48||
Their garments and auspicious furnishings were prepared; all those on their own side were ready, honored with flower garlands and other offerings.
They ascended their celestial chariots; not a single one remained behind there, and the supreme sound of kettledrums was heard as they departed.
Then, mingled with the sounds of musical instruments and the resonance of conchs,
and augmented by shouts of victory, it pervaded everywhere.
Then all one thousand celestial chariots, which move at will, swiftly traveled happily through the sky toward the western direction.
Then the sounds of the arrival of the Śiva-yogins arose there;
at that time, Śivasvāmī [received them] from Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord.
He quickly prayed for his own final liberation from birth:
"O Lord, ocean of mercy, when will you liberate us?
O Lord of gods, I remember my past lives; by you, Lakṣmī has been obtained for you. (54)
Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa said: "I shall grant liberation after one year; remember me daily in your heart.
I bid farewell to all of you, but you must come to me on the day of my birth."
Then, on the day of the eighth lunar day of the dark fortnight in the month of Kārttika, at the sacred site of Kuṅkumavāpikā,
O Śambhu, I shall fulfill the desire requested by you.
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One then directed his own celestial chariot;
and Śiveśvara likewise proceeded toward Prayāga by means of his own celestial chariot.
The King of Kāśī, as well as Kṛṣṇa, Saṃkarṣaṇa, and the others,
having drunk the water of the Triveṇikā, set out to dispatch [the messenger].
Then they all turned back and proceeded ahead through the sky;
having seen the forest of Indraprastha from the air and beheld the Sarasvatī river, [they continued on].
They went to the sacred field of Ānarta, the site of the Kuṅkumavāpikā;
in the evening, they reached the vast bank of the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake.
Then musical instruments were played and shouts of victory arose in the sky;
on the surface of the earth, the sounds of the multitude then became expressions of victory. (61)
Śāvadīnā Mahākālī and the Kṣetrapālas likewise rejoiced;
Vārinara Kṣetrapāla also rejoiced and roared.
The gods, the sacred fords, the trees, the one known as Maṇḍapa, and the assembled kings likewise raised shouts of victory. ||63||
The subjects, exceedingly joyful, raised shouts of victory;
and the travelers, beholding the sky at that time, likewise raised shouts of victory.
All the creatures, their eyes fixed upon the sky, ran forth to see;
they remembered Hari, and the female deer likewise remembered him.
A thousand celestial chariots descended from the path of the sky onto the earth according to available space, and the chariot of Hari likewise alighted.
In the beautiful western region,
the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa, accompanied by all his followers, descended into that most splendid place.
Having entered his beautiful city, he caused auspicious rites to be performed and had enchanting musical instruments played swiftly.
Then Kambharā, the goddess Cāmarī, and other women, having beheld all her companions, Lakṣmī, quickly [approached] at that time. (69)
There, by means of the imperishable Brahman, he fashioned from himself nine new [worlds],
each containing billions of crores of lotus-like maidens who were his beloveds, each with a distinct attire.
And [he saw] the city of Brahmapriyā, and the Lord, the Sovereign Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
[there were] forty million, four hundred thousand, and fifty-six thousand [deities]. (71)
The beloved women caused Lakṣmī to enter at that moment of auspiciousness;
they performed the auspicious rites according to the prescribed ritual for entry.
The worship of Gaṇeśa and others, the thorough worship of the pavilion, the worship of the Guru, the worship of the sacrificial post (yūpa), and the worship of the deities. ||73||
The Brahmins and others caused the drinking water to be prepared and then gave it;
the honored guests then departed from that most excellent great pavilion.
Then, at the arrival of night, Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa indeed caused all the great lords and the subjects as well to take their meals.
Kambharā fed all the male and female servants, the field-protectors, the laborers,
the does, and Bālakṛṣṇa.
Having fed the four classes—those liberated ones and the lords, the gods and others, the honored men and women, the sages, the kings, and his kinsmen—[he attained success]. ||77||
And having offered betel leaves and other gifts to the Brahmins residing in the three worlds— both his own and those of others— he indeed granted them leave to depart.
Then he caused wealth to be given to the Brahmins as sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā),
including various excellent jewels and many riches.
The cowherd performed auspicious rites for the delight of Kṛṣṇa;
having eaten, they attained rest and thereafter fell into sleep.
The young women, filled with fresh joy, performed service for Bālakṛṣṇa—who had assumed the form of a female counterpart for each—house by house. ||8 1||
The Supreme Lord, possessing unswerving great being and great heroism, bestowed upon them an infinite joy that is the innate bliss of the Supreme Brahman. 82.
Fainting for a moment in the samādhi of great bliss, the passionate women perceived the night, made by their beloveds to seem like an eon, as being equal to it.
O Rādhikā, before that night of the rāsa dance, even my own power seems like a mere fraction; indeed, the capacity of the Supreme Lord cannot be overcome by anyone at all. (84)
Then Śrī Śivadeva and the others departed from Prayāga for their home, recounting the virtues of their lordly kinsmen. 85.
Even Kṛṣṇa and the other Mādhavas considered themselves blessed with great fortune;
having gone to Pārvatīpattana, they all then partook of food.
Having received betel and areca nut, they slept in a pleasant slumber;
on the morning of the sixth day, they were awakened from sleep by auspicious musical instruments.
Having all performed their baths and offerings, they then partook of milk;
they also prepared meals consisting of sweet foods and milk-rice (pāyasa).
They took up water for drinking as well as betel leaves;
then, at midday, they obtained rest thereafter.
Men and women gathered together, along with kinsmen and friends,
Gopīs and Īśānīs, truthful Sādhvīs, goddesses, and likewise the wives of sages.
The Mānavyas, the Surāṇyas, the Gaṇyas, and likewise the Phaṇikas;
the Bhūtyas and other such groups, as well as the attendants (pārṣadas). ||91||
The cowherds, having requested one another's welfare, security, and forgiveness for their shortcomings, [departed]; so too did Śiveśvara and Pārvatī. (92)
Then, having requested forgiveness from those who honored the earth and having asked for a means of livelihood,
they both spoke accordingly as was appropriate.
By your scriptures, every rite has become most auspicious;
I am a benefactor to all, and my offense should be forgiven. (94)
Girijā, being virtuous herself, also requested forgiveness from the other chaste women:
"You must come here again; you should always show me your compassion. (95)
Having spoken thus, Śivasvāmī then gave the departing man wealth and other gifts; he honored the men with necklaces. 96.
The daughter of the Snowy Mountain (Pārvatī) and the maiden Aśokakumārikā likewise honored the groups of women and granted them leave to depart. 97.
Then he set aside his ornaments, garments, vessels, and even his excellent ritual implements;
and thereafter, the great lords indeed departed.
Having prepared themselves, they all then swiftly ascended their celestial chariots upon hearing the sounds of the departure-music echoing through the sky. 99.
He suddenly caused the celestial chariots to proceed on all sides;
then indeed, Śivarāja and all of them went along their respective paths.
He commanded his attendants, and they constructed a protective enclosure,
as well as a pavilion for Śiva’s city and a city for Pārvatī.
Suddenly vanishing from Kailāsa with extreme speed,
Śiveśvara, whose umbrella is auspiciousness, bestowed this supreme reward.
They gave to the laborers what was appropriate and granted them rest, while remembering Kṛṣṇa, the Lord.
They always worshipped the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa; even the lords of the worlds conducted themselves in the world according to worldly custom, O Rādhikā.
And having provided excellent provisions for the journey for the next day,
they went home praising those very guests.
Having received their leave, great honor, and supreme renown,
they departed for their own abodes, impelled by the power of Śiva.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Prodvāha-tīrtha, Koṭi-tīrtha, and Yajña-tīrtha; the Departure of the Great Beings, Mutual Petitions for Forgiveness, Grief at Separation, the Ascension of the Celestial Chariots, Arrival at the Kuṅkumavāpikā Field, Giving of Gifts, Auspiciousness, Entry into the Home, Feasts, and the Joyful Amusements and Sleep of the City Women," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhikā, at dawn on the sixth day, all the great Mānaka deities, together with Kṛṣṇa, remained awake through most auspicious sounds of musical instruments.
Having performed their baths, twilight prayers, and worship in the house of Kṛṣṇa, all those beautiful women, wearing sacred threads, eagerly engaged in the study of the Vedas.
The Pauruṣa Sūkta, the Nārāyaṇa Sūkta, as well as another, the Viṣṇu Sūkta, the Śrī Sūkta, and likewise the Lakṣmī Sūkta. (3)
They caused the Devīsūkta and the Bṛhatsāman to be recited,
performed oblations in the fire, and duly carried out the five great sacrifices.
They likewise performed the worship of the elders and carried out the worship of their husbands;
and Lakṣmī recited the Śatarudrīya as her daily practice.
They likewise performed the recitation with a rosary: "Oṃ Śrī Kṛṣṇa Narāyaṇa!
O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Śrī, Master, Master, Son of Gopāla! (6)
In this manner, O Rādhikā, they constantly performed the worship of Lord Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa according to the prescribed rites.
Performing priceless services, they drank the water from their husband’s feet;
the husband himself gave them the mantra of self-surrender:
"Oṃ, may Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa be my refuge forever. (8)
Thus Hari then gave the refuge-mantra separately:
"Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā. (9)
The Lord himself gave this mantra of surrender to them,
out of fear of Time, Māyā, sinful karma, the god of death, and the wicked-hearted.
The Lord himself gave them this protective mantra, which bears the signs of the trident, fish, banner, bow, discus, and the svastika.
I am a Brāhmaṇī, an eternal devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is my lord and husband.
The Lord Bālakṛṣṇa, the Supreme Brahman and my eternal husband, himself bestowed this Brahma-mantra upon them. || 13 ||
"May he be my father, kinsman, well-wisher, friend, protector, and guardian.
The Lord himself then gave him this mantra of self-surrender: || 14 ||
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the illustrious Puruṣottama, the son of Śrī Kambharā and Nanda, the divine child Gopāla Kṛṣṇa. || 15 ||
The Blessed One, the cause of all, who transcends the supreme Brahman and the imperishable, who assumes the essential forms of the incarnations, is eternally the inner controller within us. 16.
The inner self of all, the Lord of all, untainted and the bestower of liberation—he who is purifying when served, and the giver of both worldly enjoyment and liberation—may he protect us always. 17.
Thus the Lord himself gave this mantra of knowledge to them:
"I am a devotee of the beloved of Kṛṣṇa; Śrī Hari is my refuge. (18)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Hari, Śrī Svāmī, is my manifest refuge;
Śrī Kṛṣṇa-deva is my master—Śrī Hari is my refuge. 19.
And He gave these refuge-mantras, which bring about realization of identity with Him,
to all the beloveds of Brahmā and to the women such as Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and others.

They are the very nature of the Supreme Brahman, half-manifestations of the Supreme Brahman, the entire essence of the Supreme Brahman's purpose; they are divine, bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation. ||21||
"Furthermore, even the actions associated with them are always devoid of qualities and grant liberation.
Thus the Lord himself gave this mantra consisting of knowledge to them. (22)
Whosoever and whatsoever truly worship Bālakṛṣṇa and His beloved consorts, each and every one of them becomes identical in nature to Him; they are divine and eternally bestow liberation.
Thus she also bestowed the knowledge that grants the state of being devoid of qualities (nirguṇatva);
in this way, all the Vidyadhara women were enriched with such knowledge and mantras. ||24||
O Rādhā, they always served the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Sovereign.
Then, Queen Śrī Kambharā, having performed her morning rites, [arose]. 25.
The daughter, having come to see the highly honored women,
honored them with food, drink, and other offerings, as well as the respectful gift of betel leaves.
Likewise, all the women praised her beauty, and other lovely wives, beholding her exquisite form, repeatedly bestowed blessings upon her. (27)
May the wives of Kṛṣṇa be happy and eternal;
may they possess sons, daughters, and other kin, and be forever endowed with good fortune. (28)
Having thus bestowed their blessings and received worship, the women went to their homes;
and Śrīmad Gopālakṛṣṇa [dismissed] all the great men of honor.
And he fed those who had performed their baths and worship with milk-rice,
various kinds of sweet foods, and diverse vegetables.
There were cooked foods and boiled rice seasoned with the taste of nectar, as well as soups, savory broths, and delightful curds and milks. (3.1)
Likewise, pills combined with saffron and sugar, as well as sweet, fragrant, and auspicious drinks that are sour and bitter. (32)
He gave divine betel leaves to everyone—
the people residing in Kuṅkumavāpikā as well as those dwelling in Saurāṣṭra.
On the sixth lunar day, indeed for the occasion of the festival of Kṛṣṇa, he fed millions of people at the abode of Śrī Kambharā. (34)
All the daughters there eagerly performed the serving;
that festival, consisting of a feast, continued until midday. ||35||
After midday on the shore of the Aśvapaṭṭa lake, those excellent women,
accompanied by their husbands, went forth from there to behold the forests.
Then all those who were honored rested happily in that abode of bliss;
and for the beloved ones, there was a celestial chariot belonging to Hari originating from the northern direction.
Having clearly identified the region, she then proceeded through the air;
and having seen the grove of *śāla* trees and the grove of *bilva* trees to the north, she moved on from there.
Having gazed repeatedly upon the forest of *pālāśa* trees, as well as the sandalwood grove,
having beheld the forest of *devadāru* trees, and the most excellent forest of *tulasī*, [he departed].
Having beheld the grove of Campaka trees in the eastern direction, as well as Vṛndāvana, the grove of sandalwood trees, and likewise the grove of Kaṇikā trees; ||2.297.40||
Having beheld a grove of mango trees, as well as a grove of kunda flowers, land-lotuses, aśoka trees, and likewise a grove of ketaka flowers; ||41||
To the south, he beheld hermitages established by sages such as Lomaśa, surrounded by lotuses, pārijāta trees, and clusters of kadamba trees.
They beheld gardens containing jambīra, coconut trees, and others, as well as groves of amṛtā and plantain trees in the west. (43)
Having beheld the delightful ground adorned by the Badarī forest, and having gazed upon the grove of Bakula trees and the grove of Jambū trees; ||44||
Having likewise beheld the Gundravana forest and the Sītāphala forest,
they arrived joyfully at the Aśvapaṭṭa lake at the onset of night.
Having descended from their celestial chariots, they performed their evening prayers;
then, accompanied by Bālakṛṣṇa, they went to their own dwellings.
Then they all took their meal and performed their adornments;
thereafter, Bālakṛṣṇa went forth for the purpose of serving the great men of honor. 47.
Together with his father, brothers, and others, he fed everyone in the great pavilion, preceded by great honor. 48.
She offered betel leaves and other items, as well as whatever else was required there;
indeed, everything was fully provided—what could possibly be lacking in the house of Mādhavī?
Filled with great honor and serene through their discernment of the boon,
the men and women found supreme rest during the night.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa came to the palace;
then those newly-wed brides awaited their beloved to bring him joy. (51)
To fulfill the desires of all his nine wives, the Lord, the Consort of Śrī, assumed ten million, a hundred billion, and a trillion forms.
In every single house, he bestows delight;
that Lord of the Great Lords of Yoga manifests during the night. (53)
Listen, O Rādhā; at that time, a single divine maiden arrived to behold the pavilion praised by the gods in the form of swans. (54)
She had come to behold both the very small and the great;
indeed, she first beheld the great pavilion in its form as ten million [parts].
Having become [thus], she then beheld everything as a great wonder;
then, with a steady gaze, she again beheld the small pavilion.
Having beheld this great wonder of the threefold creation, she returned once more;
having uttered "Salutation to the Pavilion," she remained silent for a moment. ||57||
Śrī Rādhikā said: Who was that girl? How did she come there and then go away again?
O Blessed One, tell me everything, if it is something fit to be heard. (58)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhikā, having seen the pavilion, the deities indeed took the form of swans and,
ascending to heaven, praised that most beautiful pavilion.
Having heard that, Dyaus immediately made up her mind to see him for herself;
Dyaus herself, having become a young maiden, came to Kuṅkumavāpikā.
Adorned with earrings, a crown, and chains, and graced with all ornaments;
she possesses every splendor and is filled with the fullness of the nectar of immortality.
With limbs corresponding to her form, like another enchanting woman—
whether she be Rādhā or Kamalā— another [goddess] has arrived there.
Whatever she had never before seen or even heard of anywhere,
having beheld all that within the pavilion, the virtuous woman was struck with great wonder.
In a very small pavilion, the Goddess stood by the side of the sacrificial post;
accompanied by her salutation, the pavilion offered a welcome to the Goddess. (64)
"Come, O Goddess of Heaven; let me offer you a welcome.
Accept water for the feet, the guest-offering, the honey-mixture, food, and water. (65)
Having spoken thus, he gave her a throne, water for washing, and so forth;
he also offered her the honey-mixture (madhuparka) and provided auspicious food.
Having obtained the pavilion, she said: "O King Muktarāja, listen to this pavilion;
for such a pavilion as this belongs to Bālakṛṣṇa. (67)
What would that palace be like, and what would its splendors be? And what would those most divine women be like who enjoy it and are its beloveds? (68)
What would their beloved be like, and what would his splendors be? What indeed would they be like? I wish to see this heaven.
"He alone is the lord of crores, billions, and hundreds of millions of beautiful goddesses;
this I have heard today from the mouth of Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods."
"How may he be one to be served by all? I wish to see the heavens;
for the gods dwell within me, yet what power does this [being] possess compared to them? (7.1)
What is his sovereignty, what is his heroism, or what is the power of his yoga?
Of what form does he exist today, he who is indeed the sole Lord of all? (72)
"I have heard that even Indra, my husband, is not capable of such a thing;
therefore, I have come here, urged on by Urvaśī, to see him. (73)
And it was said by the preceptor of the gods: "Unable to endure [the situation], she has arrived;
I have been insulted by the gods, who said, 'You are not like Maṇḍapā. (74)
"You do not possess even a ten-millionth part of the majesty of Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa;
therefore, I have come here today after seeing this pavilion."
"Even though this jewel, unseen and unheard of, is situated right here on the threshold, I have become free from pride; indeed, I wish to behold its splendor. (76)
I, the sky, desire to behold his prosperity, that divine beauty, and those millions of lotus-born women, and especially that new Lakṣmī. (77)
Thus addressed, Maṇḍapa quickly went to the palace of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and,
having arrived at the door of Lakṣmī’s residence, informed the staff-bearer.
The cane-bearer, endowed with jewels, having gone and received the command,
led that maiden into the celestial palace of Lakṣmī.
Having assumed the form of ten million billion lotuses, she became coextensive with the sky and then entered all the houses to observe them.
She saw Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, possessing a divine form, staying with a Pratyekabuddha in every house, engaged in various activities.
In the house of Lakṣmī, Dyaus beheld Acyuta swaying upon a swing together with Lakṣmī; he worshipped him and bowed down.
In the house of Māṇikī, she saw Kṛṣṇa eating;
in the house of Padmāvatī, she saw her beloved reclining on a couch;
and in the house of Ramā, she saw him drinking milk.
She saw Kṛṣṇa lying on his bed in the house of Rādhā;
in the abode of Śrī, she saw him sporting with Śrī at a game of dice;
and in the palace of Kuśalā, she indeed saw him chewing betel-leaf.
And she saw him staying in the house of Sarasvatī, singing with a lute,
and in the house of Gaṅgā, having his feet massaged by Gaṅgā herself.
She saw him wandering here and there in the house of Virajā;
she saw him laughing with playful words in the temple of Durgā;
and indeed, she saw him chanting his rosary in the abode of Śāradā.
[He saw] Him in the form of Kṛṣṇa in the houses of the daughters of the King of Kāśī. ||88||
She saw him bringing delight to women, causing them joy;
she saw him in various forms within the houses of people from the navel of the earth up to the heavens.
He was depicted in a historical narrative, engaged in artistic skill,
and residing in the house of his one hundred and thirty wives, beginning with Aśanā.
She indeed beheld him taking delight in the state of being well-joined with his bed;
and then Dyaus beheld the Lord Bālakṛṣṇa performing the dressing of hair in the houses of auspicious women and others.
Then he saw the Lord, who had been massaged by women in the houses of the southern region and bathed with oils,
essences, and the like, and adorned with ornaments,
in the palace of the beautiful women of the eastern quarter. (92–93)
The celestial maiden Subhāgyagā beheld him being colored and adorned with lac-dye and other pigments by those women, and saw him sporting and making them laugh. (94)

In the houses of the beautiful women of Rāśiyānīya, he saw his lord Hari, radiant and absorbed in the local customs of those various regions. In the houses of the wives of the Kiṃpuruṣas, he saw the son of Kambharā.
Then she saw him absorbed in music together with all of them;
in the palaces of the beautiful women of Ketumāla, she saw him wearing royal ornaments and following the customs of kings. 96–97.
And heaven beheld him dancing in the houses of the immortals, accompanied by those women and filled with joy. (98)
In the dwellings of the Hārītīs, she saw him seated upon a throne, surrounded by women and attended by his kinsmen.
In the dwellings where the Brāhmīs resided, the sky-goddess beheld at night that Lord, devoted to the worship of the gods and endowed with a divine form.
In the temples of the Ābrikīs, she beheld Kṛṣṇa, who was immersed in his own state, filled with the essence of the *rajaḥ* quality, singing along with instrumental music and rhythmic beats. 101.
In the house of her paternal ancestors, she saw Kṛṣṇa engaged in the performance of Śrāddha;
she saw Mādhava endowed with the amorous sentiments and other states of the goddesses.
In one place she saw him watching a theatrical performance together with a woman; in another, she saw him touching her with an expression of love.
In one place she then saw him immersed in meditation like a yogi;
in another place she saw him fast asleep in slumber.
In some places he was instructing women in the knowledge of Brahman,
and in other places he was then filling the hearts of women with joy.
Somewhere he saw one weaving a garland from various kinds of flowers;
Dyaus then beheld him standing alone in the courtyard of the house.
In some places he was coming from one side-room to another room;
in other places, he was burning with fire in the middle of the house.
He saw the Lord right outside, perhaps at the gate, or somewhere else;
in another place, he saw him going along with his wife, adorned with ornaments.
In one place, she saw her own wife showing her face with a mole in a mirror, while simultaneously making a mole appear on it. || 109 ||
In one place he was applying collyrium to the eyes of a woman,
and in another place he was then drawing decorative patterns on the forehead of his beloved.
In some places he was even anointing their feet with lac-dye; in others, out of extreme identification [with them], he was embracing them as well. || 11.1 ||
In one place he was feeding his own dependents with morsels from his own mouth, and in another place he was offering them the juice of betel from his own mouth.
The sky beheld Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa accompanied by a fan;
in another place, she saw that king of kings seated upon his throne.
In some places he was being massaged and rubbed by many women, and in others he seemed to be calling his own beloved by means of even the pretext of a glance.

In some places he saw the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa writing on a leaf with his secret movements concealed; thus, the Sky beheld the all-pervading Lord in all ten thousand mansions, engaged in various different activities.
With supreme affection, she worshipped the divine couple in every house.
And Lakṣmī and the others, recognizing her as their own honored guest from heaven and earth, joyfully welcomed her and offered her food.
And the women gave them excellent rewards such as garlands of flowers, and they bestowed upon them the remembrance of the Lord’s charming pastimes, which grants liberation.
Dyau beheld a prosperity, the most excellent of all,
which exists neither in heaven, nor in Satyaloka, nor even among the lords.
Those various riches, garments, ornaments, and seats;
couches fit for reclining, vessels, and gems and diamonds.
Even after beholding treasuries, four-pillared pavilions, excellent mechanical devices, golden caskets, and celestial mansions, she was filled with great wonder.

In the palace of Indra, in the mansion of Brahmā, in the abode of the Sun, in the dwelling of the Moon, in the home of Dhruva, and in the residence of Kubera—there is no prosperity that does not exist there. (122)
Beholding it in a single house, the sky became divested of its pride;
then, having received blessings and forgiveness, it returned to the pavilion.
She departed for heaven by way of the sky, illuminating the ten directions;
thus, O Rādhikā, was the glorious deed of Bālakṛṣṇa. 124.
Endowed with the sovereignty of ten million, with ten million times a hundred billion lotuses as his consorts,
he is eternally filled with the sentiment of erotic love together with that many [consorts].
Indeed, it should be understood as divine alone—devoid of qualities, auspicious, and bestowing liberation;
for the Blessed Lord is eternally the giver of happiness to those who serve him with devotion.
The Lord, the fulfiller of all desires and the object of good fortune, fell into a most pleasant sleep as the companion of the newlywed brides during the night.
Then, O Rādhikā, although she had gone to heaven, Dyau was enchanted by Hari;
from that time on, she constantly strove day and night to become his wife.
Once, out of a desire for sensual enjoyment, she approached Śrī Hari in private;
having eaten and being satisfied, Hari made her content, and she departed joyfully for heaven.

Thus, in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the second section, the *Tretā-santāna*, the sixty [wives] performed their morning rites at dawn and received the mantras; there was a feast for the great sages (*mahīmānas*); the young women traveled through the sky in celestial chariots (*vimānas*) to view the forests; they took their evening meal; the maiden Dyau arrived to witness the divine play (*līlā*); having beheld Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa displaying various pastimes within the palaces of millions, billions, and hundreds of millions of women, the enchanted Dyau returned to heaven; and then came the sleep of Hari.
The two hundred and ninety-seventh chapter, titled "The Definition of Cetya and Other Terms."
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhikā, at dawn, Hari— who had simultaneously granted pleasure to his own wives during the night— awoke to auspicious musical instruments and hymns of praise.
Then, at the hour of Brahmā, they remained awake with their senses under control;
and Hari said to them all, "Stay for a moment in meditation upon me."
"By my yoga, you women have today become divine;
you are liberated, freed from illusion, and devoid of all veils."
Thus addressed by Rādhikā, all those wives of Kṛṣṇa and Mādhava—
women devoted to their husbands— having received the command of their beloved, remained for a moment in meditation.
Then, under the power of the Lord, all the channels and vital breaths,
having withdrawn the breaths from the channels, entered into the heart in meditative absorption.
Having forgotten their perception of the body in the presence of their beloved, they beheld him in their hearts, radiant with the splendor of Brahman, abiding within his own form.
There, masses of splendor appeared like great oceans;
from there, they beheld heaven and all the abodes of the gods.
Then, from that point onward, they proceeded in their own celestial chariot together with their lord,
beholding the regions of the ancestors, which were radiant with merit.
Then, accompanied by Kṛṣṇa, their beloved, they indeed proceeded further ahead;
they all went to Satyaloka and were honored by its inhabitants.
Having attained a divine state, they all shattered the firm covering of the earth and then proceeded toward the covering of water.
Then, at the boundary of the enclosure near the splendor of Vaikuṇṭha, those female servants of Śrī Rāma beheld him.
Sītā, Rāmā, and the others joyfully offered them a welcome;
Rāmāditya also extended a welcome to the Supreme Soul.
Then they proceeded further ahead, leaving behind the cloth of the winds there,
as well as the cloth of the sky and the wall of the ego, ascending upwards.
Leaving behind the veil consisting of the principle of Mahat,
they went upward together with their beloved to the auspicious palace of Vairāja.
There, the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa was honored by him,
and all the royal women of the Vairāja realm were also worshipped.
Then they all proceeded further toward the realm of Hiraṇyagarbha,
the great kingdom of Mahāviṣṇu, where Gopālakṛṣṇa resides.
His own lord shines there together with his consort, the illustrious goddess known as Mahālakṣmī, as well as with the goddess Śrī Kambharā.
And by them the god was worshipped; then indeed the beloved father was honored, and the beloved mother was also worshipped, and by those two the Śrīs were likewise treated with respect.
Having been fed, embraced, and properly honored with blessings, the husband was also worshipped; then, having received his permission, [they went] to the upper story.
Accompanied by their husbands, they went from their celestial chariots to the vast Mahāsthala;
there they were honored by the goddess Bhūmi, and Hari was honored by Bhūmi with great abundance.
Having beheld those manifestations before them, they went to the abode of Vāsudeva;
there, Vāsudevī, filled with great devotion, offered them hospitable reception.
Vāsudeva-Nārāyaṇa performed a grand reception for Hari,
providing him with drinks of nectar, food of ambrosia, and other such offerings.
The descendants of Vāsudeva caused [the festival] to be performed and likewise offered worship;
then the Blessed One, having revealed the abodes of his incarnations, departed from there.
Having bathed him in the lake of Brahman and drawn him out into the imperishable splendor, Hari indeed went to his own supreme, immutable abode.
Then, having dissolved all of them into his own form and having made them divine and liberated, endowed with the same form as himself, he did so indeed at that time. (25)
Established in their own nature, they are free from all obscurations;
they possess the state of the Supreme Person and are of the essence of the Supreme Brahman. //26//
O Rādhā, Hari then manifested here with his entire being through the essential natures of material forms and qualities, just as he does for himself; what indeed can I say to you?
In the sacred field of Kuṅkumavāpikā, the bodies of his own wives became fit for absorption into the Divine Effulgence; their illusory nature dissolved away.
They are always of the nature of bliss whose sole essence is consciousness;
indeed, they are rich with the expansion of the mass of self-knowledge consisting of omniscience. 29.
"Truly, they have become perfected and fully accomplished, having reached their destined state; they were born from that, and even from bathing in the Brahma-lake. (2.298.30)
They possess the very nature of the body of Brahmā, they are liberated souls,
and they are indeed composed of light, having the form of the imperishable Brahman.
Then, having been born and having attained their formal existence as distinct entities,
they indeed became the Bhāgavatas, having acquired the very form of the Blessed Lord.
Indeed, those born [of this] are portions of Brahman consisting of consciousness; they are indeed designated as "knowledge," "splendor," and "perfect similarity. (33)
There, the glorious Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is attended by these innumerable female attendants (muktānīs) and served by the liberated souls (muktas). ||34||
He indeed showed them the imperishable sovereign empire,
the universal sovereignty of a great king, situated above the three worlds.
Mādhava revealed all his own sovereign powers, as well as every manifestation, which are eternal bliss and objects of enjoyment.
Kāntaka displayed millions of circles of pearls all around—divine and magnificent mandalas of pearls. (37)
Kṛṣṇa showed them all the wonderful gardens, the auspicious palaces, and their own respective dwellings.
He displayed all divine prosperities, all sources of good fortune, and the Kaustubha jewels that fulfill every desired wish.
The rays of his own form bestow nourishment on all sides;
they grant satisfaction, provide the attainment of happiness, and bestow bliss.
The Lord indeed showed them things that bestow pleasure, love, and joy, that grant the fulfillment of desires, and which are filled with eternal bliss.
Likewise, there were all kinds of halls, ever-new and fit for service, as well as auspicious grounds for pleasure-gardens, desirable and unobstructed. (42)
Indeed, pervaded by the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, he manifested divine appearances, ornaments, garments, and finery. ||43||
And she showed them delightful beds for their secret dwelling;
having shown them everything located there, she did so thereafter.
He gave them food consisting of the bliss of the Supreme Brahman, excellent drink, betel-leaf, and he granted them the pleasure of divine sport. ||45||
The Lord also granted them absolute bliss born of the secret [teachings],
as well as the auspicious worship appropriate for those who have attained great liberation from that abode.
The Blessed One accepted their worship, which was performed by both the liberated women and the liberated men, in the presence of those who were still bound. ||47||
Those of divine form received him with a warm welcome and great honor;
thus, Lord Hari showed them his entire home.
From that imperishable state, he departed for the glorious abode of Goloka;
there, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul, extended a warm welcome to him. (49)
At that time, Rādhā and the others gave the wives of Hari the honor they had received there, as well as the drinking of the milk from the wish-fulfilling cow, Kāmadhenu.
They likewise offered foods such as milk-rice and various delicacies;
then the Lord quickly departed for Vaikuṇṭha along with them.
There, a welcome was offered by Lakṣmī, Kamalā,
Bhārgavī, Śrī, Vikuṇṭhā, and others as well.
Having received the honor bestowed by Nārāyaṇa, as well as the worship and praise of Śrī Hari at that time, those who desire prosperity displayed their joy.
The Lord himself went to the divine Kailāsa, the abode of Sadāśiva;
and there, the Blessed One beheld all his beloved manifestations.
He manifested the forms of Śiva and Durgā and others, whom they worshipped;
all the Gaṇas there also performed the worship of Hari.
Then Śrī Hari indeed went together with them to that auspicious abode of Mahāmāyā, which is composed of illusion, for the sake of curiosity. 56.
Beholding millions of beautiful women who were like the beloved of Hari, all of whom were dear to Brahmā, they received great honor there. 57.
They were honored there by various illusory maidens and served in many ways with the most excellent illusory objects.
With excellent foods, drinks, and enjoyments, with garments, ornaments, and decorations, and with all stimulating powders that increase the erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra-rasa). || 99 ||
The women were served and honored with all kinds of attire and utensils, with all objects of good fortune, and with states that bestow every joy.
Mahāmāyā herself performed the massaging of Hari’s feet there; seeing this, all the wives of Hari were struck with great wonder. || 61 ||
She is indeed the Queen of the Queens of Kings, the Sovereign of All, and the Mistress of Queens;
while serving her own husband, she was beheld by everyone.
Having displayed his abode of *māyā*, Hari then quickly departed from there and went to the abode of Viṣṇu; there, the attendants of Viṣṇu paid him honor.
They offered a welcome to all of them, as well as the ritual waving of lights (*nīrājana*) and worship.

They gave him desired food and drink, as well as garments and fine clothes. Then the illustrious Bālakṛṣṇa, adorned by his beloveds, departed for the abode of Viṣṇu with a hundred heads and the wielder of the Śārṅga bow with a thousand faces.

Hari indeed [created] the cosmic eggs of the Creator, who shines with a face as vast as a parārdha, [and those] of Viṣṇu with a hundred thousand faces, of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow with ten million faces,
of Śambhu with lotus-eyes,
and of Brahmā with a lotus-face.
He indeed showed them all the infinite manifestations of creation.
Worshipped by each of them, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, his own beloved son,
revealed to them the divine glories (vibhūtis) dedicated to himself.
All these manifestations, offered to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa,
were enjoyed by all of them together with the beloveds of Brahmā;
for at that time, O Rādhikā, they were indeed perceived directly in Samādhi.
Then, having indeed taken up those planets, beginning with the sun and the moon, [he departed].
He showed them those beings dwelling in the worlds who were situated within the nature of hell;
yet, upon seeing them, their minds did not indeed become attached to that place.
He quickly brought them to his own auspicious pavilion and residence called Divyākṣara, located at Kuṅkumavāpikā.
There, their minds attained steadiness through the syllable *oṃ*;
and from that meditative absorption (*samādhi*), they all then awakened to their own [true] selves.
They beheld those supreme, non-human beings who had attained divine bodies residing in their abodes— bodies that were free from the state of being veiled, non-material,
devoid of illusion, eternally uniform in form, and exempt from hunger and thirst.
And those who are devoid of the qualities of illusion (māyā), yet endowed with splendor and sovereignty.
They possess the nature of all abodes, consist of bliss equal to the Imperishable (Akṣara),
are filled with the joy of Brahman, and are adorned with divine attire.
Possessing sovereignty no less than that of their husbands and established in divine treasuries,
they became filled with the weight of great bliss and capable like Bālakṛṣṇa himself.
Having thus attained divinity and obtained their husband at that time,
those wives— whether they were young brides or even elderly matrons— attained omniscience.
In this way, Hari granted them his own eternal equality;
for just as you, O Rādhikā, were made by me beautiful through identity with myself.
Thus Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa indeed made his own wives the covering of the earth,
the covering of the walls, and the enclosure of the house.
For those [women] who experience no obstruction when closing a door, nor in the midst of water such as the ocean, nor in the flow of a river, nor in snow; (8.1)
In their bodies, there is no affliction from rain and the like, nor indeed is there any burning by fire, nor any scorching by the heat of the sun. (82)
Even the submarine fire or lightning does not burn these;
the sun, the moon, and other planets have no independent power to go toward them. //82//
These [energies] are not dependent on breath, nor does the wind dry them up;
existing above the practice of prāṇāyāma, they are the consorts of Brahman.
Drowsiness, lethargy, and heaviness do not exist in them at all;
nor indeed can they ever be overcome by poison. ||85||
Not even a blow from a weapon ever causes a wound to their bodies;
nor are diseases able to remain within them, for they are illusory. (86)

The accomplishment of hearing from afar, the accomplishment of direct perception from afar, the accomplishment of grasping objects from afar, and the accomplishments of conversing from afar and so forth. || 87 ||
Their state of being subtle is indeed their possession of the speed of mind;
their state of being great is also their power to resolve all desires.
There is mastery over all things, as well as the assumption of forms such as ten million;
there is the ability to travel within the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) and immunity to cold and heat. (8–9)
The power to create by mere volition and whatever perfections and sovereign powers there may be— these manifest for them through the grace of Bālakṛṣṇa.
The wish-fulfilling creepers, the wish-fulfilling cows, the wish-fulfilling vessels,
and even the wish-fulfilling jewels exist for them by the power of their mere thought.
O Rādhā, such incomparable sovereignty as this occurred for them moment by moment;
they then beheld it when they had emerged from their state of absorption.
Observing that their bodies were liberated from their abodes and rendered bodiless,
they all became serene, freed from the pride of illusion.
Then they all arose and served Bālakṛṣṇa, their own Lord, in a divine manner with baths, worship, and meals. || 94 ||
Śrīmad Gopālakṛṣṇa, Bālakṛṣṇa, and the others likewise offered [the gifts] to the honored guests who had performed their ritual bathing and daily rites.
Having received worship, food, honors, wealth, and even betel-leaves to their satisfaction, they all prepared to depart for their respective homes. (96)
The lords of the lands and the worlds petitioned Acyuta—the illustrious Gopāla Kṛṣṇa—and likewise the virtuous Śrī Kambharā. 97.
Hare’s father begged them for forgiveness regarding his inferior service;
"By your arrival, this festival has become truly magnificent. (98)
When will there be the yoga or the vision of the Blessed Ones?
Having recognized that one's own [mind] is subject to its own control, one must necessarily come here. 99.
Having spoken thus, he bowed down and gave him many gifts of leave-taking;
he performed worship in many ways and likewise bestowed various articles upon him.
The father bestowed gold, silver, and diamonds during the worship;
he gave these very items as rewards to his employees.
He gave as much as they desired to the groups of the poor, the helpless, and guests;
and he bestowed wealth for their satisfaction upon his servants, employees, and those skilled in the arts.
The Lord indeed gave beautiful crowns to all the kings,
and he bestowed diadems upon the gods and the lords.
He also bestowed garments, ornaments, and the like upon the queens and the women;
he gave to everyone their own desired gifts as rewards for their pleasure.

The incarnations, as well as the manifestations, the stages [of yoga] beginning with the earth, and the Virājas; the Viṣṇus, the unborn ones, the ancestors, the gods, the Siddhas, and the great seers.
The Mānavas, the inhabitants of Aṣṭala, and all the sacred fords, mountains, rivers, and so forth, being entirely satisfied, said: "We are always well-pleased with you."
O Gopālakṛṣṇa, we shall depart; may there be well-being for your son, and likewise well-being for the maidens; may you all always be in good health.
Having spoken thus, they, being in a state of readiness and having prepared their equipment and other necessities,
readied their celestial chariots and became ready to depart at that very moment.
Those who were honored by one another, kinsmen, and friends met with one another;
even the women did likewise, pressing chest against chest.

Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Threefold Creation, the Abode of the Imperishable, and so forth, within the Samādhi of All at Dawn on the Seventh [Day] in the Second Tretā Cycle of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā; as well as the Transformation of Them into the Nature of Eternal Divine Liberation, along with the Greatness, Feeding, Worship, Giving, Tolerance, Knowledge, and so forth, and the Rewards for the Deities of the Sacred Field."
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā; at the time of departure, all the maidens were embraced by their mothers and fathers, their hearts filled with affection.
Having shed tears of separation, they remained silent like those deprived of sense;
they were divine, possessed of celestial bodies, and previously arisen from the qualities of the lotus.
Beholding the affection of her relatives, which had increased even further,
she then became unable to bear even the slightest thought of separation from them.
Then, seeing their daughters, their mothers were pained by the sorrow of separation;
those simple women entreated Bālakṛṣṇa.
He took his own daughters with him for only a short time,
in order to visit his kingdom, his family members, and his friends.
The sisters and co-born ones repeatedly gazed upon the noble Śrī Hari, saying:
"O Lord, send us, your daughters, for the sake of our happiness."
Furthermore, we shall quickly send Tārā here at the end of the month;
O compassionate Kṛṣṇa, fulfill our request for service unto you.
Hari said, "Let it be so," for the sake of their affection;
he then commanded them all to go together with their mothers and others.
Then, having heard of the Lord’s magnanimity, they all became filled with serene joy;
suddenly approaching Hari, they bowed to the Lord and embraced him.
Having said, "We shall return quickly," they remained in close attendance for a moment,
providing satisfaction as they awaited their return.
Having repeatedly attended upon their own beloveds, they became ready, adorned, and beautifully decorated;
thus prepared, they worshipped the Supreme Lord.
Having honored the father, the mother, and the sister of Viṣṇu,
as well as all the elderly women of the household, he bowed to them and addressed them with a welcome.
Having spoken words of comfort that were appropriate and fitting, and being provided with suitable garments and ornaments, they ascended their celestial chariots as directed by their Lord.
"You must all return," said the Blessed One at that time;
the Soul of the Universe, though himself free from illusion, shed tears through his illusory power.
Then musical instruments were played, worship was performed with flowers and unbroken grains of rice, and the celestial chariots were adorned with auspicious ornaments and other decorations.
The seasons, Dharma-deva, Nara, and Devī are the pedestal;
the earth is the pavilion, and the ruby pillar is also liberated. (16)
Likewise, Sudarśana, the discus, and Hara, the leader of the Gaṇas—
these nine indeed approached for the sake of beholding the Mothers.
"Field-protectors who have acted like criminals must be forgiven";
having said this, Hari then stood before them.
All the beloveds of Hari, as well as Vāsudeva and the others,
bestowed their blessings and gave them rewards.
Various kinds of jewels, as well as garlands of diamonds and other gems, beautiful crowns, vessels, ornaments, and garments.
Likewise, name-plates inscribed with golden letters, as well as wealth and excellent, auspicious implements. || 21 ||
Having gathered them together, they became happy and were born as the children of the field;
then the sounds of the two-fingered ones arose like the sounds of mechanical devices.
The sounds of kettledrums and shouts of victory arose everywhere in the sky;
at that time, the joyful maidens stood within their fathers' celestial chariots.
Even while gazing upon the lovely Aśvapaṭṭasaraḥ field,
they honored Lomaśa with showers of flowers and prostrations.
Then, in the sky, crores, billions, and hundreds of millions of celestial chariots became mobile; all those daughters, together with their fathers and other kinsmen, ascended them.
Except for Kāśīśvarī, they went to other lands along with their mothers;
likewise, the Brāhmī vowels were liberated there without the Lord.
Thinking, "I must not go," Rādhikā remained dwelling in her own beloved’s palace; Bālakṛṣṇa, as her inner self, also stayed there with her.
Accompanied by women who offered themselves to him, he went forth invisible;
those beloveds of the three worlds then departed for their respective realms. (28)
In the field known as Kuṅkumavāpī, everything became as if empty in an instant;
then, by the command of Hari, even the pavilion vanished from sight.
Even that very small pavilion quickly vanished there;
thus was the obstacle swiftly resolved by the will of Bālakṛṣṇa.
As long as those friends, the daughters of the King of Kāśī, remained in the service of their husband,
they joyfully served Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa day and night.
Divine and of celestial form, they were indeed devoted to their husbands;
they performed service through action, mind, speech, and body. (32)
Lakṣmī serves the Supreme Lord with special affection,
even though she has thousands of female attendants who are equally virtuous.
Bathing, the offering of garments, anointing with oil, the grooming of the hair, dressing, the washing of clothes, and likewise the cleansing of the teeth; ||34||
Applying collyrium to the forehead, massaging the body with oil, rubbing the feet, providing water for drinking, and giving food—[these are the services]. (35)
The offering of betel-leaf, the fanning with a fan, the gift of a garment, the gift of fruit, as well as the bed, the bedding, and the presentation of the water-jar. ||36||
Whatever may belong to one's own body, all that one should perform oneself;
such is the complete service and ultimate refuge for one's own Lord. (37)
Lakṣmī alone is Lakṣmī; indeed, there is no other equal to her anywhere.
While such Lakṣmī was present with Kṛṣṇa at any time, [he remained indifferent]. ||38||
No harm is seen resulting from service; indeed, that is what makes it superior.
Nevertheless, Kṛṣṇa looks upon all with an equal eye, endowed with equanimity toward everyone. (39)
It proceeds as one that bestows happiness and is full of great affection, yet it is not partisan;
that very same nobility always exists in the Supreme Beloved.
She fulfills all desires and grants satisfaction according to one's wish;
indeed, her service surpasses that of Padmāvatī and Ramā.
Because of these two who are ever devoted to their master’s interests, even Lakṣmī herself was made to feel envious. 41.
Then, in the spring season, Kṛṣṇa celebrated the festival of Rādhā;
he also performed the delightful festival of the flower-swing,
and he further conducted the Cāturmāsya festival consisting of religious vows.
"The month of Kārttika has arrived, and the eighth lunar day that awakens [the memory of] his birth is at hand; furthermore, Kṛṣṇa himself is nearby"—having reflected thus, the women [prepared]. (43)
All of them, accompanied by their fathers and others, quickly ascended a magnificent celestial chariot from their father’s house and arrived at the abode of Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa. 44.
Having reached their master’s house, they were indeed happy at that time;
it was a source of joy and honor for all those who were most highly esteemed. ||45||
Then the illustrious Gopālakṛṣṇa indeed acted according to what was right;
the kings likewise did so out of devotion to their lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
In the fifteenth year, upon the full completion of the sixteenth year, on the birth festival of their sons, all the fathers dwelling in every creation [assembled]. 47.
They arrived at the sacred field known as Akshara to honor Hari;
having performed their ablutions early in the morning on the eighth lunar day, they observed the auspicious rites.
Having adorned himself with elegant attire, Hari entered the assembly hall;
he was honored by Lomaśa and others, and further gladdened by their auspicious blessings.
Purified by offerings and gifts, delighted by praises of his glory,
and enriched by the splendor of a king of kings, the Supreme Lord shone resplendent.
And thus, when the great festival of his birth was taking place in the morning,
gifts such as elephants, horses, cows, and so forth were distributed there.
And [the theft of] cows, buffaloes, bulls, camels, vehicles, and mounts;
as well as houses, fields, gardens, groves, wealth, and gold. (52)
There musical instruments are played and his glories are sung; then, when the ritual circumambulation is completed, the midday meal and other rites take place. (53)
It became most excellent indeed for all the lovely people of the world;
hospitality toward guests was performed with food, clothing, and other such things. (54)
At night, there was a captivating performance of dance to be seen, as well as the wrestling of athletes and the sounds of musical ensembles. (55)
The poetic compositions of the best of poets, the dances of courtesans, and the instructions of the virtuous occurred during the festival of his birth. (56)
O Rādhā, during this festival, Nārāyaṇa, the father of Ramā and Padmāvatī, and his son Cārudeva, are present at the divine Akṣara-kṣetra.
He who was proclaimed as a divine incarnation himself, a portion of the Sun,
came from Kāśī there, recollecting the words of Hari.
For Śiva himself, being one who remembers his former births, acts for the sake of liberation;
having cast off the human state, he strives for the state of Śiva. (59)
The cowherd also, having given his own kingdom to his son,
the yogi Dharmapāla, then departed together with him.
Having all formed their resolve for the sake of liberation, they then became eager;
and having celebrated the auspicious birth-festival,
they prayed to the Supreme Self for the purpose of release from the body.
Hari, beholding the sun situated in its northern course, said:
"I must go to my own abode; you all should remain here in this house for now.
Thus he placed the hope of the entire family of Śrī upon their heads.
Śiva himself remained constantly in the vast inner chamber of Lakṣmī’s house; there he asked Hari, the husband of his daughter, about the means of accomplishment.
Then Kṛṣṇa spoke to his beloved regarding liberation itself:
"Listen, O Śambhu, I shall tell you the supreme means for attaining liberation. (64)
Indeed, for those who are established in liberation and are free from the state of illusion,
liberation is attained through their company and service.
I, who dwell in liberation, dwell eternally within all selves;
by constantly worshipping me, a human being attains liberation.
Time, action, dharma, knowledge, and these powers are mine;
realizing that I am thus possessed of power, whoever takes refuge in me is liberated.
He who has offered himself to me entirely— with body, action, speech, mind, and his own possessions— is swiftly liberated.
May he behold me and may he relish me; may he always proclaim my name;
may he smell me, touch me, hear me, and contemplate me. (69)
May he take hold of me, serve me, and always massage me;
may he approach me in secret and gladden me within his heart.
One should establish me, reflect upon me, and determine me within the heart;
one should desire me always, and one should dwell forever in my yoga.
One should meditate upon me, embrace me with a heart full of affection, and even merge with me;
having unified oneself with me, one should take up all objects of enjoyment and cast them into me.
Having made me manifest before him, he should perform actions for my sake;
having thus attained Śivarāja, he shall reach liberation through union with me. 73.
Delighting, wandering, roaming, dancing, and fighting; waking, sleeping, proceeding, and returning. (74)
Whether walking, wandering, performing virtuous conduct, or moving about, one should indeed do everything for my sake; thus, one shall certainly attain liberation. ||75||
Thus addressed, O Rādhikā, this Śivarāja, as well as Śītajā, Jaya, Candra, Dhenupāla, Aśokā, and Haristhirā [remained there]. (76)
They became steadfast in meditation and devoted to steady service;
having attained a divine state, they served by offering their very selves.
Then, while the sun was in its northern course, they became intensely eager;
desiring liberation, they closely embraced their own daughter, Lakṣmī.
Having bathed in the Aśvapaṭṭasara lake and performed the worship of Hari,
the cowherd then addressed his three daughters.
Having withdrawn all their mental functions, they then became absorbed in meditation;
the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the giver of knowledge and the sovereign of all, was seated within their hearts.

Thus, having perceived those whose minds were set on nirvāṇa standing right before him, he quickly ascended his divine celestial chariot for the sake of those who were attached to their own [worlds]. (8.1)
Then Hari, the Lord of Lakṣmī, arrived in his own divine form to grant liberation to them by means of those very bodies. 82.
He caused him to ascend a divine celestial chariot while the virtuous looked on;
then, the drums of the gods resounded in every direction.
Sadāśiva attains supreme liberation, eternally free from all exertion;
all [the beings], augmented by the gods and others, went to the most excellent Kailāsa.
The attendants departed for Vaikuṇṭha eternally, as did Kṛṣṇikā, Lakṣmī, and the Supreme Lord, the noble Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa. ||85||
Indeed, they were capable of doing everything with that very same body;
O Rādhā, they have led those [souls] to liberation—this was truly a great wonder. ||86||
Thereafter, together with her lord, the daughter performed the subsequent rites there, including worldly gifts, ancestral offerings (śrāddha), festivals, and so forth. ||87||
Then Śrī Bālakṛṣṇa also performed the worship of the cows during their northern course (uttarāyaṇa) there, for the sake of initiating meritorious deeds.
At that time, he gave fresh fodder and grain to the cows,
and he had secret stores of grain and food distributed everywhere.
Then, from all the worlds, cows with divine forms,
residing on the earth, quickly arrived, longing for his grace.
Having eaten, bowed to Hari, and received worship, they departed for their respective hermitages;
then the Blessed One bestowed abundant gifts upon the twice-born.
He gave garments and excellent foods to the virtuous,
and he gave in every way to the poor, the helpless, and even to the mendicants.
At that time, having performed the rite of giving in this manner— consisting of sweet foods, garments, silver, gold, vessels, and a new vessel filled with the seven types of grain— (93)
Hari ate it together with curd and sour gruel, along with parpaṭa cakes that were tender, cooked,
and mixed with ghee.
He caused all his beloved wives to eat the excellent dish known as *kṛsara*, which was prepared with boiled pulses, delicious, fragrant, and flavorful. 95.
Thus, O Rādhikā, the noble beloved of Kṛṣṇa, born of Gopāla and Kṛṣṇa, indeed celebrated a great festival for the conjunction of the northern solstice.
In his sixteenth year, accompanied by Brahmapriyā, he who brings about all auspiciousness enjoyed manifold pleasures. || 97 ||
