Sacrifice, ancestral rites, worship, hospitality, the offering of honey-mixture (madhuparka), sacrificial fees, and oblations to the gods and ancestors—all these consist of me; they are my very forms.
The mortar, the grinding stone, the hearth, the water-jar, and the broom—when employed for my sake, these are my purifying forms. (3.2.110)
Whether it be a bed, a vehicle, a mount, cattle and wealth, or a house and so forth—if these are used for my sake, they are all of the very form of my own body. (111)
O Nārāyaṇī-Śrī, just as you are ever united with me, so too shall everything done for my sake grant me the state of union (sāyujya). || 1.12 ||
Thus has this food been described to you here; I am its form in the shape of silver. Ask me anything else that you may desire to know.
O beloved, by reciting this and likewise hearing it, one shall attain my own state;
one shall obtain liberation after liberation, and obtain the fruit of sacred pilgrimage sites as well as the fruit of yoga.

Thus ends the second chapter, titled "The Description of the Names of the Fifty-two Years of Brahmā, the Names of the Fourteen Manus of the Current Kalpa, the Names of the Final Forty Kalpas of the Fiftieth Year, and the Manifestation of the Glory of the Threefold Creation Nourished by the Rays of Puruṣottama," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the third section, the Dvāpara-santāna.
The illustrious Śrī Nārāyaṇī said:
"O Blessed One, ocean of mercy, please tell me this which I desire to know:
during which year of Brahmā’s fifty-two-year cycle [does this occur]? (1)
You have been born as the primary incarnation, endowed with name, action, and qualities;
I desire to hear all of that, since your divine play bestows liberation.
There is no end to your incarnations; I shall not place that burden upon you.
The manifestation of the nature of the Incarnator occurred in the past.
O Blessed One, I desire to hear that which may become a source of remembrance for me;
O affectionate one, tell me merely of the manifestation of Puruṣottama.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī; I shall tell you, understand it from me—O beautiful lady, that very account of mine which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
In the eighth kalpa of the lotus-born Creator, during the eighth Manvantara,
from the Nāla-khaṇḍa of the Creator, there arose the asura Rohiṇāṇḍodara.
He was indeed born equal to the cosmic egg in both body and strength;
by his fiery power, and even by his dark power, he became a devourer of the three worlds.
Struck by Rudra with both a mace and a trident, he fled into the midst of the water; then Rudra pursued him.
Having pierced through the covering of the earth, he entered the sphere of the cosmic egg;
leaving behind the worlds of Satya, Tapas, and Jana, he proceeded to Maharloka.
Then, having become minute and remaining hidden in a cave of Mount Meru,
Rudra indeed went to the abode of Mahendra to behold heaven.
The gods, the ancestors, and the great seers also arrived;
at that time, Indra’s assembly hall was filled with the sun, the moon, and others.
Then Rohiṇāṇḍodara, perceiving the opportunity, grew until his belly became equal to Mount Meru; having opened his mouth wide, he swallowed that entire assembly.
He suddenly swallowed all of heaven, including its celestial realms together with the sun, moon, Indra, Rudra, and the constellations; all of heaven came to be within his belly.
A great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose, and the worlds were agitated;
the realms of Mahar, Jana, and the others trembled all at once.
Then, in the world of truth (Satyaloka), a great and most terrible trembling arose;
even the Lokāloka mountain shook repeatedly at that time.
Knowing that the destruction of the heavenly world was imminent, the deities,
together with Rudra, Indra, the Sun, and the Moon, took their place within the interior of the cosmic egg of Rohiṇī.
Overcome with fear, they then praised me, the Supreme Person:
"O Supreme Brahman, ocean of mercy, protector of all, Mādhava! (17)
Salutations to you, O Blessed One, the inner witness of all, the Supreme Lord!
Apart from you, there is no other protector here against sudden dissolution and the like.
"O Lord of Life, you exist; protect me, protect me from this great abyss!
Where have Kevala and those dwelling in heaven gone now, into this cavernous pit? (19)
O Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Teacher of the World, we do not know how the divine heaven, consisting of all splendor, came to be in this vast abyss. (3.3.20)
Or perhaps some being has swallowed one of us who had fallen; untimely destruction has arrived, therefore protect us, protect us! 2.11.
"O God, we have come to you for refuge, having surrendered ourselves;
we offer our very selves here, so act as you wish for our sake. (22)
Thus was I praised, and I was also praised by Brahmā;
then, O Śrī, consort of Nārāyaṇa, you were together with me within the belly of Rohitā.
I quickly became the mind-born son of Indra, possessing his discus;
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. ||24||
At that time, O beloved, you also became the mind-born daughter of Rudra;
then the gods beheld me, Puruṣottama, who had become manifest before their eyes.
Beholding him, their hearts were submerged [in devotion] and they worshipped him with the offering of their hearts.
At that time, I swiftly fashioned the great Sudarśana discus.
A discus, ten million times more effective than a sword, was swiftly released by me from my hand; it then cut through the body of that asura, Rohitāṇḍodara.
Having gone in many directions all around and having wandered about again and again,
the great fire produced by the discus [consumed] the fragments of the Asura's body.
He reduced those pieces cut into ten million fragments to ashes;
and that ash then became gold known as Rohita.
When the destruction of Rohita’s egg and its interior had occurred, the gods and others became at ease,
having recognized me as the Lord of the Imperishable, the illustrious Mahendra-Bālaka, the Sovereign.
Having performed a supreme great festival for the Protector, the Supreme Lord, in the abode of Indra, the abode of the gods, Rudra indeed [did so] with the gods as witnesses.
Then, in the pavilion, he gave you his own mind-born daughter to me;
at that time, I too obtained you as my wife through the decree of fate.
At that time, my perception was that Anādijyotirāyaṇa was [the source];
then heaven and likewise the gods were established by me in their proper places. ||33||
By the power of my yoga alone, this transformation was well-performed;
I am that very one who descended, and he who was here has become me.
O dear Raudrī, remember my pastimes there with you, the Yoginīs;
in that region, many of my incarnations occurred there every single day. (35)
Thus has my first mental birth been described;
now hear also of my second birth, which occurred in the second year.
In the year called Nālaka, on the first day of Brahmā, at the end of the third Manvantara, there was indeed a mountain named Meru. (37)
Then, indeed, by the great weight of the fourteen worlds, he was overwhelmed and sank slightly into the depths of Pātāla.
Endowed with fourteen tiers and containing the abodes of both gods and asuras, the fourteen worlds remained even when Mount Meru sank into a low state. (39)
They were indeed shattered along with Meru and cast down;
they were bent against the flanks of Meru and dragged away in every direction.
Then, truly, heaven, earth, and the netherworld (rasātala)—all indeed reached a state of bottomlessness on every side. ||41||
The Lokāloka mountain, which forms the wall of the cosmic egg on all sides,
was drawn inward toward the center and assumed the form of a short ring.
Nevertheless, by his power, even though they were bent, the worlds remained firm; there, for a moment, they even became contracted.
Seeing the destruction of the pillar and perceiving it to be the destruction of the universe, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the others [sought] the Supreme Lord for the sake of its protection. ||44||
They praised me, the Supreme Brahman, Lord Hari Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, with supreme fear for the sake of protecting Mount Meru. ||45||
O Supreme Lord, for the protection of this universe and for the preservation of the worlds, you are the support of all cosmic eggs. 46.
O Lord, the power of stability for the entire creation resides in you alone; because everything exists within you, all things are established as stable. (47)
O Blessed One, that which has arisen from you and rests entirely upon you would go to destruction if deprived of you; save me from the proximity of ruin! (48)
Without a pillar, a house would not stand; likewise, this [universe] depends on him.
Without Mount Meru, the worlds would not remain in the sky. (49)
"Mount Meru, burdened by weight and covered with layers, sinks indeed at its base;
we shall come to destruction. Therefore, let us protect Meru, which is our refuge. (3.3.50)
Having thus praised me, the lords of the gods meditated for a moment;
and I, O Lakṣmī, together with you, quickly [departed] from the imperishable abode.
He quickly arrived in Satyaloka in the presence of the Creator;
while the gods were looking on there, he became a child in the lap of the Creator.
Resplendent with the brilliance of ten million suns, wearing matted locks and adorned with all ornaments, I laughed and spoke to the Creator on my lap, saying, "I am your father."
Addressing me as "son," he accepted me as his son through his illusory power (māyā).
The gods, having bowed to Hari and recognizing him as the Supreme Lord, [worshipped] the Supreme Controller with flowers and other offerings.
They honored me, offered hymns of praise, and said again and again, "Protect us!";
even I am the son named Anādi-Śrī-Meru-Nārāyaṇa.
Having quickly made you my supreme power, the sustainer of Mount Meru, and having very swiftly merged you—who are perfectly endowed with my own form—into myself, [I shall depart]. (56)
Having led the gods, beginning with Brahmā, he went together to Pātāla;
there I worshipped that which is situated at the base of Meru on the earth.
Having worshipped you, Mahānārāyaṇī then commanded Śrī:
"Enter here immediately as the very embodiment of Śakti. (58)
You, the Great Power (Mahāśakti), were created by me and entered [into me] accompanied by me;
then Meru was uprooted at its base by me together with the gods. ||59||
Lifted up by Brahmā and others of exceeding strength together with him,
Mount Meru then attained its height according to their respective requirements.
All the worlds became level with the surface of a taut thread, suitable for habitation; the gods and others became happy. (61)
O Lakṣmī, from that time forth, you— being of the nature of your own shadow and known by the name Dhṛti (Fortitude)— have always supported this Meru at its base for a long duration.
And I entered there upon Meru in the form of the sustaining power; as the inner self in the form of the attractor of space, I dwelt within the interior of Meru.
Thus, having established supreme stability on Meru by the gods and others,
and having observed that the roots of the worlds were attached to Meru, [he acted].
Then, having firmly established themselves and remaining steady in due order,
they [arose] from Rasātala, as well as from Mahātala and Talātala.
From Sutala, Vitala, and likewise from Talātala, he came toward the earth;
together with you, he traversed Bhuvarloka, Svarloka, Maharloka, and Janarloka.
Having attained the supreme truth through austerity, I, the son of Ajā, became steadfast;
I am the beginningless Śrī Meru-Nārāyaṇa, the son of Brahmā.
I was married by you and the gods and others to Meruputrī;
and from then until the end of the kalpa, I remained for the sake of protecting all beings.
The supreme Lord Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa himself is the original source of the incarnations;
thus, my incarnations have occurred in every age and in every kalpa.
O Śrī Mahānārāyaṇī, you who are subject to manifold duties and whose further shore is not found— then remember that from which you were born.
O Lakṣmī, in the third year after that of Brahmā, there was also my auspicious manifestation as Meru-Nārāyaṇa.
I shall tell you my birth here; listen, O Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇī! It was in the first year of the Nāla era, during the third Manvantara of the Kalpa.
O Nārāyaṇī, at that time in heaven and on the earth, the solar orb became unrestrained and indeed reduced the worlds to ashes.
It was endowed with a hundred thousand rays, burning in every direction—
the cardinal points, the intermediate directions, the worlds, the planets, and all embodied beings.
It was the burner of all the terrestrial realms and the oceans;
indeed, it became the consumer of all wind-born creations situated upon the earth.
It was the burner of Meru, the divider of light and darkness for those dwelling in the forest;
it was the burner of the lunar mansions and stars for those dwelling among men.
For those dwelling in the Mahārāja heaven, as well as for those living in the realms above,
there arose on all sides a consuming fire that reduced them to ashes.
Encountering the pain of that burning, the Manus, the deities,
and all the inhabitants of the worlds then praised the Creator.
Having heard the hymn of praise, Brahmā went for the sake of pacifying the Sun;
he too, being scorched, turned back and then departed for Satyaloka. (79)
Śaṅkara indeed went toward the Sun to perform a great propitiation; he too, being consumed by the heat, bowed down and, turning back, became motionless.
Then Viṣṇu and the gods, having assembled together, praised me, the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. ||81||
To pacify the splendor of the sun, they paid homage again and again, saying:
"O Blessed One, O Supreme Lord, you are the leader of ten million suns! (82)
O Eye of the World, O Bestower of Light upon the World, protect us from the Sun—us who dwell in the three worlds, as well as others who dwell above. (83)
We would have been scorched by the sun’s rays spreading across a hundred thousand leagues;
it was by you that the entire world was made luminous for the sake of happiness. (84)
If it were already burnt to ashes, what need would there be for the sun?
Therefore, O Lord of Gods, protect us and grant peace to those who are tormented. (85)
Having spoken thus, they offered abundant worship in the form of an offering unto Me,
the Supreme Soul, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Then, O Kamalā, I, as Nārāyaṇa, quickly came from the imperishable [realm] along with you to the true abode of Brahman, which is beyond that. (87)
Worshipped by the gods, I became the son on the lap of Viṣṇu;
gentle and possessing a thousand arms, I was adorned with a crown, earrings, and other ornaments.
Equipped with whetstones, weapons, and the like, as well as jars of nectar and ambrosia,
I instantly fashioned the Sudarśana [discus] there from the essence of the whetstone.
"O Lakṣmī, that nectar of immortality which extinguishes all fire possesses the power of consumption; therefore, commanded by me, you, O Goddess, become the Consumer. (3.3.90)
Having entered the sun, O Śātani, hold the nectar there;
act quickly so that its heat may be diminished. (9.1)
And you, having received my command, quickly assuming the form of fire,
becoming composed of great splendor and being truly the causer of heat for Arbuda— 92.
Having taken up the nectar, she entered the solar orb;
then, she slowly deposited that ambrosia within its interior.
Gradually, the rays of the sun indeed attained tranquility;
and you, too, gradually withdrew your own splendor there.
Then, having placed the sun upon a whetstone wheel in the form of your own body,
I sharpened its exceedingly fierce rays even down to their subtlest points.
Having pierced through all those regions, he then gave them to the gods and others;
and they, in turn, fashioned weapons that were indeed unimpeded at that time.
There, I created the thousand-rayed Sun who bestows happiness;
O Lakṣmī, the other rays were absorbed by you into your own body. (97)
From that time forward, that Sun became the bringer of prosperity to the world;
and you, therefore, are his daughter, the daughter of the Sun, known by the name Śātanikā.
I, the son of Viṣṇu, the destroyer of the Sun, have married that Abhavā, who is also wedded to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. 99.
And remember how you dwelt there with me until the end of the kalpa; O Śrī, you were Nārāyaṇī, and I was the Lord Sūryakarmā.
O beloved, I myself, the Supreme Brahman, became Sūryakarma;
likewise, even there in that year, my incarnations were by the millions.
He has appeared for the sake of protecting the Dharma and likewise for the protection of embodied beings;
He Himself is declared to be the primordial Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa, the Incarnate One.
O Lakṣmī, my third manifestation indeed took place there in that year;
and I know all of that, O beloved, as clearly as an amala fruit in the palm of one's hand.
Indeed, by worshipping me, countless embodied beings have then attained liberation;
likewise, through reciting or even hearing this, both worldly enjoyment and liberation shall come to pass.

Thus ends the third chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestations," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the second section on the Dvāpara age, concerning the first year of the Creator [Brahmā]: the manifestation of the beginningless Śrī Dyunārāyaṇa for the purpose of protecting heaven from being swallowed by the demon Rohiṇāṇḍodara; concerning the second year: the manifestation of the beginningless Meru-Nārāyaṇa for the purpose of supporting Mount Meru as it was sinking under its own weight; and concerning the third year: the manifestation of the beginningless Viṣṇu-Nārāyaṇa for the purpose of cooling the sun as it was burning. || 3 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, to my fourth mode of conduct,
which protects the moon in heaven and bestows supreme liberation upon those who sing it.
Then, in the fourth Kalpa of Ajita,
during the twelfth Manvantara, there was an exceedingly terrible Asura.
Named Dhūmra, he was fierce; born from the back of Śambhu’s head, he possessed a body of sky, moved through the atmosphere, and was terrifying.
Seeing that beautiful jewel shining on the forehead of Śambhu,
the moon entered into a rivalry with it and rose into the sky to seize that "jewel of the night."
He then made a great effort to seize the moon,
even though he was resisted by the moon with sharp weapons and missiles.
Then he descended from the sky onto the mountain named Śvetaśṛṅga;
thereafter, the son of Śambhu performed penance directed toward Śambhu.
Then Śaṅkara remained without food for one yuga;
being pleased, he spoke to that son Dhūmra, who was born from the back of his head.
"Tell me, what pleases you today? Why do you persist in asceticism? Speak your desire; I shall surely grant it. Do not perform such fierce penance."
Thus addressed, the Asura said: "Grant me a boon that brings victory;
I desire nothing other than this, that I may conquer Candra without effort. (9)
"So be it," Hara said, and he gave a trident to Dhūmra—
a weapon invincible, indestructible, and superior in power even to the discus.
Having taken that, Dhūmra first went to Mount Meru,
impelled by the thread of craving to achieve universal sovereignty.
Having conquered the gods dwelling on Meru, he went forth to conquer the kings upon the earth;
and having conquered the rulers of the earth, he then proceeded to the netherworlds (pātāla).
Having conquered the Daityas, Nāgas, tortoises, crocodiles, fish,
as well as sharks and hooded serpents, he proceeded toward the forest.
Having conquered the Vidyādharas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras,
and having defeated the Guhyakas and Cāraṇas, he then went to the city of Saṃyamanī.
Having then defeated the messengers of Yama, he fought with Yama himself;
the Asura fought with Kāla’s staff and with Yama’s trident, each against the other.
They fought, yet there was no defeat for either;
Rudra was summoned by Yama, and Hara was summoned by the Asura.
Hara and Rudra arrived and stood between them;
they both tried to stop them, but being praised [by the sages], they went home.
Then the Asura, filled with pride, went toward Indra, the lord of heaven;
and Indra, knowing that the invincible spear had been granted by Mahādeva, [prepared for battle].
Rising with a gentle disposition, he performed auspicious hospitality for the Asura and gave him a beautiful necklace fashioned from jewels.
And the Asura, having beheld that, became gentle and, free from anger, worshipped the trident of Śambhu in many ways.
He went forth to conquer the Sun, and the Sun quickly went to its setting;
then that Asura went forth to conquer the Unborn One, the Supreme Lord.
Brahmā, having recognized that trident as belonging to Śambhu, worshipped it;
he offered the honey-mixture (madhuparka) and paid honor to the Asura.
Having taken his seat upon a highly beautiful golden throne, Dhūmra became humble, rejoiced, bowed to the Unborn One (Aja), and departed for heaven.
Seeing the moon with its full radiance, she went toward it with haste;
there, the moon was always healthy and complete at all times.
He is of a single form, devoid of decay or growth, eternal, and blissful;
free from being eclipsed by planets and the like, he is full in all his digits on every side.
Having approached that terrifying Dhūmra who possessed such full nectar,
he assumed a form extended with a hundred moons and seized him with his hand.
Through the touch of those rays which were like nectar and ambrosia, the great asura indeed attained an unprecedented, supreme happiness filled with great bliss. (27)
Therefore, having conceived greed for the moon, he seized the moon in his mouth; a great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose everywhere in heaven and on earth. (28)
Indeed, that jewel was a repository of nectar, bearing a cool radiance;
yet even without attaining its moonlight, the medicinal herbs possessed extraordinary vitality.
The gods became as if dead, deprived of the nectar of immortality;
and all living beings, who are sustained by the rays [of the sun], were possessed of death.
Then the gods who had been born went for refuge to their own preceptor;
Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods, praised me, the Supreme Lord.
For the sake of protecting the moon and for the purpose of protecting the world, homage to the God of gods, whose eyes are the sun and the moon. (32)
To the inner controller of all, the protector, the Supreme Self, known as Puruṣottama, the bestower of nectar, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow; ||33||

Salutations to the Great-Souled Bhāskara, the lord of the planets, lunar mansions, and stars; salutations to the one who dwells within the inner altar and who brings about the destruction of those lacking devotion.
"Come quickly, O Hari; you must provide protection for the Moon.
Mahādeva, absorbed in meditation, remains there for a long time. (35)
"O Lord of Muktā, O Śrī Parameśvara, protect me quickly from Dhūmra! Thus praised, I, Nārāyaṇī, then spoke to Śrī immediately.
Together with you, he came to the celestial abode of the Preceptor of the Gods;
though his form was instantly invisible, his mental son remained within his body.
I, Subāla, became equal [to him], adorned with all ornaments, bearing the conch, discus, mace, lotus, trident, spear, and arrows as my weapons. (38)
Adorned with a vajra, a bow, a staff, a noose, a sword, and a shield,
you were then commanded by me and entered the belly of the asura.
O Lakṣmī, by your power, the lunar digit that protects the moon became steadfast; thus, at that time, the moon did not fall into a swoon.
Nor was he devoid of splendor, nor was he bereft of nectar;
nor was he fully cooked in the womb by the smoke-colored fire of the Asura Dhūmra. ||41||
In this very way, it was as it had been before in the womb;
then, honored by the gods and graced by the preceptor of the gods, he spoke.
Requested for the sake of destroying the asuras, I went to that great asura and,
accompanied by the divine army, fought with Candraghātī.
Then, O Lakṣmī, at my command, you became a maiden for a moment;
and even the asura named Dhūmra, upon beholding you, was infatuated.
Having cast aside the trident for a moment, he made an effort to seize you;
however, that trident was then swallowed by you at my command, O Śāṅkara. (45)
By me, with my discus, that asura Dhūmra was swiftly slain into a thousand pieces;
he met his destruction and was then reduced to ashes. 46.
There, the moon with its full digits emerged from his belly;
and you, O wielder of the trident, became the lunar maiden known by the name Kaumudī.
The Supreme Goddess has been nourished and worshipped by all the gods and others;
likewise, I too have been worshipped, nourished, and saluted by everyone. (48)
"I am the son of the preceptor of the gods, the Blessed One, Puruṣottama;
having recognized me as Hari, Candramas likewise saluted and worshipped me. (49)
"O beloved, you were then a maiden named Kaumudī, given to me;
and you were wedded by me while I was living in the house of the preceptor of the gods."
O Narayani, I then remembered Śambhu by the name Anādiśrīdevanārāyaṇa even while in the house of the preceptor of the gods.
Śambhu arrived quickly upon learning that I am the Supreme Lord,
and Hara rejoiced indeed upon knowing that Dhūmrāsura had been destroyed.
Śambhu indeed gave the eternal trident to Candra;
your father gave you this eternal, auspicious trident as a wedding gift.
And that which was given to me by you has been made into a beautiful line on my hand;
behold it, always held, upon my right hand. (54)
The trident remains inscribed there, and it manifests according to one's will;
remember, Lakṣmī, that your manifestation and mine likewise occurred then.
At that time, I myself was Devanārāyaṇa;
likewise, my incarnations at that time were also in the thousands of millions.
And until the end of the kalpa, I indeed remained with you in the house of my preceptor;
then, in the fifth year of Ajā, I was he who I have become. (57)
In the first kalpa, during the first Manu, you were also present;
hear the account of that first Manu in the aeon named Vyomabāṇa.
While the sons of Brahmā, great ṛṣis who proclaim the Vedas, were assembled in an unceasing assembly, they indeed engaged in deliberation.

Within the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), the terrestrial realm is the land of action that yields fruit; whatever is performed there by embodied beings—whether it be charity, the dedication of a bull, or other such acts—is indeed fruitful. (3.4.60)
Everything given on the surface of the earth—food, water, clothing, and ornaments—is obtained by all those who have gone to other worlds. (61)
Fields, gardens, silver, maidens, gold, houses, and means of subsistence; offerings to the gods, offerings to the ancestors, ritual oblations, merit, vows, ancestral rites, and assistants. ||62||
In every other world, the giver obtains ten thousand times more than the doer;
just as those who have renounced, forest-dwellers, and lifelong celibates continue to live.
Having undertaken the life of a householder and likewise having performed [their duties] upon this earth,
the gods of heaven, the ancestors, and the great seers all live [sustained by it].
That sacrificial rite is well-performed, and that is the true livelihood for all embodied beings, wherein the feeding of Brahmins constitutes the oblation to the gods. (65)

The ancestral rite (śrāddha) for the ancestors and gods, as well as the merit of the sages—all this, including the nectar of immortality and the essence of Soma, is indeed obtained at the sacrifice. ||66||
Therefore, sacrifice must be performed and taught as a ritual act for the sake of humanity and the gods upon earth, so that the continuity of ritual action may be maintained.
When the thread of the sacrifice has been commenced, woven together, joined,
and completed through the proper performance of sacrifices, one's life shall be free from affliction.
Therefore, O great sages, let us indeed go today to the surface of the earth;
having taken the gods and the ancestors with us, we shall perform the supreme sacrifice.
Having thus deliberated, O Lakṣmī, the sages, the ancestors, and the lords of the gods came to the earth near Mount Meru for the sake of the sacrifice.
All those belonging to the Pālāśa forest-dwellers, stationed on the banks of the celestial Gaṅgā,
strove for the sake of sacrifice, each engaged in his specific ritual duty.
Since this was the first sacrifice, they did not know the proper sequence;
there was no one within the sphere of ritual action who had practiced all the sacrifices. (72)
When the father was a god, a brahmin, or a great seer, the manifestation of the sequence of karma occurred there accordingly. (73)
Then, having fallen into delusion and being ignorant of the ritualistic section (karmakāṇḍa), they became obstinate, saying, "This is primary; this is primary. ||74||
When the sequence of the sacrifice and the sequence of its constituent parts were not yet determined,
there was the son of Vedhas, named Brahmakumāra, who possessed the character of a perpetual student (naiṣṭhika).
And there he spoke to the sacrificer, the Manu named Jyotiṣmat:
"Indeed, we are all within the sphere of the unprecedented (apūrva) in the ritual section (karmakāṇḍa). (76)
But if the sacrifice is deficient in its qualities, the result will be the opposite;
there is no one other than Nārāyaṇa who can witness a sacrifice or explain it. (77)
Let us worship here, having united for the sake of following the proper sequence, that very Śrī Hari, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), who is the supreme Brahman beyond the imperishable.
And he, the performer of sacrifice, having arrived, will teach the entire ritual;
he is the deity of sacrifice, the soul of sacrifice, the knower of sacrifice, and the maker of sacrifice.
Having been addressed thus, Manu and the others accepted those words;
then, filled with eagerness, they approached the Supreme Lord and worshipped him.
The great sages, the ancestors, the deities, the brahmins, and others—[we offer this]:
Om, salutation to the Supreme Lord, the embodiment of sacrifice, who is the performer of action. 8.1.
To Yajñadeva, to Sacrifice, to the Knower of Sacrifice, to the Performer of Rites, to the Teacher of Sacrifice, to the Executor of Ritual Duties, to the Supreme Self. ||82||
"Salutations to the Inner Controller, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, who grants us assistance"—thus did the gods and others praise me, the Supreme Person, for the sake of the sacrifice. (83)
Then, having heard even a single syllable and its meaning from you,
I indeed went with you to the bank of the Ganges, to the forest of Palāśa wood on Mount Meru.
In the presence of Brahmakumāra, I was a child wearing the guise of a sage, possessed of all branches of knowledge, a seer of all mantras, and acting under his command. (85)

"As long as I am proficient in the ritual procedures, as long as I am a twice-born who carries the sacred vessel, as long as I am a knower of all sequences and possessed of knowledge regarding all substances and so forth. (86)
Indeed, I manifested myself as a second Brahmā;
and all, O Brāhmaṇa, beheld me shining with the brilliance of ten million suns.
Rising suddenly, they bowed to me and asked eagerly, "Who are you?
"I am the sacrifice, O Blessed One; I am the fruit of your worship. (88)
Having spoken thus, I, in the form of a child, entered the lap of the young Brahmin;
he too meditated upon me in that way, as his own son.
At that time, you entered the radiant Manu as his wife, being more powerful than all others;
then I, having comforted everyone, [established them] in the ritual acts for the sake of sacrifice.
Having appointed them in successive order, I then commenced the sacrifice;
I am the Supreme Lord, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (91)

Having become the illustrious Yajñanārāyaṇa from time immemorial, I caused that Vaiṣṇava sacrifice, which was fit for a universal monarch, to be performed until its conclusion with the avabhṛtha bath.
At that time, on the sacrificial ground, within the pavilion near the altar, I, Adhvara, requested from Manu a more abundant sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Then, O auspicious one, you appeared as a maiden named Bhūyasī, also called Dakṣiṇā; indeed, as a maiden, you were a seeker of me. (94)
Indeed, Manorjyotiṣmat’s daughter was Nārāyaṇī, who was exceedingly abundant;
at the sacrifice, she was richly adorned with celestial ornaments and possessed a wealth of ten million gold pieces. (95)
"Indeed, she was bestowed upon me by Manu as one suitable for me when I made my request;
from that time on, throughout that year consisting of a thousand kalpas. (96)
All sacrifices were performed by me according to the manner I had instructed;
and there, along with you, I lived for an entire kalpa during that great sacrifice.
I am that very Yajñanārāyaṇa, the beginningless Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), the incarnator himself, the Lord, the Supreme Brahman, and the Highest Sovereign. ||98||
At that time, you became my wife, Bhūyasī by name;
O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, remember that kalpa and that year. (99)
Furthermore, O Lakṣmī, there were indeed tens of millions of other incarnations of mine therein;
I know them all, but others do not even remember them.
I am the very nature of all sacrifices; all sacrifices abide in me.
All sacrifices are my forms, and I am the instigator of all sacrifices.
I am the enjoyer in all sacrifices, the bestower of the fruits of all rituals,
and I am the knower of the entire collection of rites within the sacrifice.
Without you, O Lakṣmī, I do not remain at all— whether in rites for the gods, the ancestors, or the sages, nor in human rituals, in giving, honoring, or worship.
O Goddess of gods, O Sovereign Śivā, I attend upon you in recitation, in vows, in ritual sequence, in knowledge, and likewise in the practice of virtue; it shall not be otherwise.
Thus has the birth of Adhvara been narrated by you;
by reading or even hearing this, the fruit of a great sacrifice shall be obtained.
O Lakṣmī, by remembering you as well, there shall be abundant fruit from sacrificial fees;
success in all prosperity shall be attained here, and liberation shall occur in the hereafter.

Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Primeval Lord Nārāyaṇa for the sake of destroying the demon Dhūmra and protecting Candra in the fourth year of the Creator [Brahmā], and the Manifestation of the Primeval Sacrificial Nārāyaṇa for the purpose of completing the sacrificial thread in the fifth year," in the *Śrī Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*.
Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, during the sixth year of my asceticism,
in the second Kalpa of this Creator (Brahmā) and in the first Manvantara.
Your manifestation arose from Rudra, and mine from Brahmā;
therein, at every kalpa, the creation of the three worlds takes place.
In this context, Brahmā is indeed the creator, Hara is the destroyer at the end,
and Viṣṇu is always considered there to be the performer of nourishment.
But having set aside that rule, the god Rudra, the Great Lord (Maheśvara), said to Brahmā: "Do not perform creation; I shall do it."
"Perform the evening duty, which is the withdrawal of the world;
for that action known as destruction does not please me, O Brahmā. (5)
For yogis like me who possess discernment, that is a great suffering;
for me, a withdrawal consisting of violence and extreme cruelty is not appropriate.
The dharma of the virtuous is certainly not violence, which brings suffering to others;
since I cannot endure the suffering of another, violence does not please me. (7)
I do not desire to harm others, even by body or mind;
how then could I, through my actions, perform a terrifying deed of evil? (8)
For the killing of footless creatures by those possessing feet is accompanied by greater sin;
even among those with feet, the killing of lice and flies is more [sinful] than that.
It is greater than that of sparrows, vultures, and Garuḍas;
then [greater] than that of dogs and the like, cows, buffaloes, camels, and elephants. (3.5.10)
The violence of the nāgas, piśācas, and bhūtas is greater than that;
the violence of the daityas and rākṣasas is indeed even greater than that, and the violence of the dānavas is greater still. (11)
The [power] of charioteers, bards, panegyrists, servants, and even outcastes, as well as of men, brahmins, and women, is greater than that. (12)
Likewise for maidens, boys, and children who are virtuous;
and also for yogis, devotees, holy men, and those practicing celibacy. || 13 ||
It is even greater for those who are pregnant, for women in childbirth, and for virtuous wives;
it is also greater for sacred fords (tīrtha), for shrines (caitya), and for images (pratimā). (14)
Furthermore, violence against temples, sages, and gods is more [sinful]; likewise, violence against those seeking liberation and ascetics is even greater in its sinfulness. (15)
The injury of those worthy of sacrifice, of kings, and of gurus is greater than that;
indeed, the injury of the Vedas and the scriptures is the greatest of all. (16)
Furthermore, the harming of the manifestations of Hari and Īśa is even more [grave] than that;
thus, this expansion of sin, being violent in nature, does not please me. (17)
"I shall indeed perform the creation; you, however, must perform the dissolution. For a long time I have performed the dissolution, while you have performed the creation."
"In the future, you alone must perform the act of withdrawal and not the act of creation;
I, for my part, shall always perform the act of creation and never the act of withdrawal. (19)
O Lakṣmī, having been addressed thus, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, then said to Śaṅkara: "Do not speak so; for I am no such injurer as you."
Abandoning the most excellent task, what person would enter into a lesser one?
Being a Brāhmaṇa, I am never able to do such a thing here.
That task was yours, O Rudra, cruel and pitiless;
for Brāhmaṇas are endowed with compassion, whereas Niṣādas never are.
I do not consider, even in my mind, the work of a hunter—namely, the casting of nets, snares, and traps, as well as killing, cutting, and piercing. (23)
For that which pertains to the Niṣādas consists of tearing apart, obstructing,
burning, splitting, grinding, and the extraction of the life-force.
"O Śambhu, this act of killing is an evil deed; it does not please me.
Since I am one whose wisdom is established, I ought not to do that. (25)
Thus addressed, O Lakṣmī, Śaṅkara fell into a state of wrath;
unable to endure those words, he seized the Creator by the throat.
There, Hara cast him face-upward upon the ground before the Creator;
placing his foot forcefully upon his chest, he drove the trident into his throat.
Then a great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose among the inhabitants of the three worlds;
they thought, "Today, the destruction of Brahmā will surely come to pass. (28)
The sages, the ancestors, the gods, and even the insentient as well as the sentient beings trembled at the wrath of Rudra; not a single person remained neutral. (29)
Even Viṣṇu fell into fear there; what then can be said of others?
Thereupon Brahmā remembered me, the Supreme Lord, as his protector.
O Lakṣmī, he quickly arrived there from my abode, Akṣara; then, together with you, he grasped the trident in his hand.
O beloved Hari, you were commanded to enter as the virtuous Śāntikarī;
at that time, by your penetration, the wrath of Hara became pacified.
"Seeing me, who bear the conch, discus, mace, and lotus—the glorious Puruṣottama—he was ashamed and, bowing down, thought this to be an improper act. (33)
He who possesses a radiance equal to ten million suns, adorned with every ornament,
the Lord of all, holding a trident, the Master who provides protection for Brahmā.
To the one who has arrived unexpectedly, the peaceful one dwelling within all, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Supreme Lord. ||35||
O beloved, at that time the foot of Śambhu was placed upon the chest of Brahmā by me,
and the trident was effortlessly uprooted from my two hands.
Then Śambhu fell forcefully on his back by my power;
as Śambhu was falling onto his side, the gods provided him support. ||37||
Protect, protect us, O Hare-Kṛṣṇa, Bāla-Kṛṣṇa, Supreme Lord!
Protect Aja, protect Hara, and protect us who have come to you for refuge! ||38||
"We are all your children; we must always be nourished and protected by you.
Having said this, they then fell at my feet like a prostrate staff. (39)
With flowers and other mental dispositions, they worshipped me, Hari, the bearer of compassion,
who is the Supreme Brahman beyond the imperishable, residing within the heart of Brahmā.
Śaṅkara, who was also my devotee, begged for forgiveness;
and I, having been enlightened by Śambhu, told him: "There is no fault in you regarding this destruction."
"You are the very nature of my power, and I am the agent possessing your form;
all this has been created by me, who am of the nature of the Knower, the Creator, and Consciousness. (42)
Everything is nourished by me, who am Viṣṇu in the form of the Giver;
everything is withdrawn by me, who am Hara in the form of the Destroyer. ||43||
I who am I—Hara, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā, endowed with distinct names;
there is no separate existence for you from me, yet my Māyā is difficult to overcome.
And having been led to differentiation by that very Māyā through my own will,
I make everything appear as if possessed of difference, just like another who is distinct.
"I act like one who is ignorant; that is my eternal play.
In that regard, O Śambhu, there is indeed no fault in you consisting of the defect of violence. (46)
That which has arisen must indeed perish; this is the inherent nature of things.
In that regard, you, O Rudra, are my witness according to reason concerning my destruction.
The signs are the dissolution and so forth; time consists of the ages and likewise the nights.
Indeed, the limit of time as a sign has been established by me according to the prescribed boundary.
"Therefore, O Śambhu, there is no possibility of harm to you in any way during the dissolution.
Thus addressed by me, O Lakṣmī, Śaṅkara attained composure.
Having abandoned that quarrel and always possessing a mind intent on withdrawal, he indeed serves my command and carries it out at the end, as has been declared.
Then, having indeed disciplined Śambhu, I became the son of Brahmā—
the beginningless, illustrious Brahmā-Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama.
And you, Lakṣmī, emerged from the body of Hara as a maiden;
you are indeed the daughter of Rudra and the consort of Viṣṇu, bestowed upon me by Hara.
In this very manner, my manifestation occurred there for you as well;
from then until the end of the kalpa, O Brahman, I remained as Nārāyaṇa. (53)
"Indeed, along with you, I remember that Vaiṣṇavī, Nārāyaṇī Śrī;
likewise, millions of other incarnations of mine occurred there. (54)
O beloved, no others besides me are able to enumerate them;
now hear about my manifestation in another year as well.
In the first year called Yamya, and likewise in the first Kalpa and the first Manvantara,
a dispute arose among the deities dwelling in heaven regarding their celestial abodes.
One said, "I alone shall enjoy the station of Mahendra," and another then said, "I am the Sun; there shall be no other. (57)
The third said, "I am the Moon," and the fourth said, "I am Kubera. One said, "I am Varuṇa," and another said, "I am Vāyu. (58)
I am Vasu, I am the preceptor of the gods, and I am the deity Īśāna;
I am Agni, I am Gaṇeśa, I am Senānī, and I am Dhruva as well.
Meru is mine, heaven is mine, and I am indeed the wind;
I am Yama, I am Viṣṇu, and I am also Śaṅkara.

I am the guardian of the quarters, the guardian of the worlds; I am indeed the Sādhya, and I manifest as such. I shall enjoy the station of the Viśvedevas, and I shall likewise enjoy the station of the Pitṛs.
As the gods were speaking thus, a great quarrel arose among them,
which could not be pacified by any ruler whatsoever.
Then, O Lakṣmī, those most excellent of gods, being powerful, completely brought each other's desired positions under their own control by force.
Then they remained powerless and without support;
the heaven won by strength there became like a kingdom of the blind.
Then the sattvic deities, such as Indra, Vasu, Candra, and others, gathered at the house of the Guru indeed for the purpose of warding off blindness. (65)
They deliberated thus: "How might this blindness be removed? Is it indeed by the words of Brahmā, or of Śambhu, or of Viṣṇu? (66)
Driven by arrogance, the gods do not recognize the bounds of propriety;
therefore, a rule must be established here for the benefit of everyone.
"Just as the Preceptor of the Gods might show the path, we alone shall follow it.
Having heard this, the Preceptor of the Gods himself then spoke to the gods.
The sky is indeed the eternal mother of the gods; she protects the gods within her womb.
She exists here in embodied form, and we shall do whatever she commands.
Likewise, the Sun-god named Viṣṇu shines here even in this assembly;
we shall all carry out his beneficial word exactly as he speaks it.

Having been addressed thus, the two of them, after bowing to all the gods who were present, said: "We are indeed capable of making a decision regarding the blindness; nevertheless, [we act] for your sake."
Let us both indicate Hari Kṛṣṇa, the eternal Supreme Brahman;
and let us worship the Lord right here, who bestows the station of authority.
He alone, the Lord of the Imperishable, who has sustained everything and by whom this was indeed set in motion, will surely grant us the final decision. (73)
He by whom it was set in motion shall give us the decision;
he by whom prosperity was bestowed according to one's karma and according to one's merit. (74)
Having arrived according to his proper place, according to his sovereignty, and according to his station,
he, being propitiated, will grant us a definitive decision regarding our positions.
Thus addressed by those who spoke with force, all the gods,
for the sake of instruction, called to mind the eternal Supreme Brahman.
I, the great lord, have quickly arrived from the abode of the Imperishable before the Blessed One, the Lord of the Imperishable, the Supreme Lord of all lords.
Then, O Nārāyaṇīśrī, the Supreme Lord was with you in the assembly of the Preceptor of the Gods, in the presence of the Sun-god named Viṣṇu.
Divine, adorned with celestial garments and ornaments, and endowed with divine sovereignty,
he stood in the midst of the assembly, possessing the splendor of ten million moons and suns.
O Lakṣmī, you were then commanded to abide within the body of Dyu;
invisible, you are the ruler of all and the bringer of benefit to everyone.
Upon seeing me, the Lord of the lords of all lords, Surā bowed down and then offered me a seat as well as the honey-mixture (madhuparka). ||81||
I asked them about their welfare, but they did not inform me; for the sake of my own station in heaven, I even requested the alleviation of their blindness. (82)
O Nārāyaṇīśrī, at that time my Sudarśanas were capable, possessing their released forms, and acting as rulers on all sides. 83.
O beloved, those cruel weapons, fully armed, were launched into the sky wherever the gods were stationed in their celestial abodes at that time.
Having summoned all those who were devoted and auspicious to me,
they repeatedly held the door of the preceptor and brought them into my presence.
When I questioned those who were the instigators of the blindness, they, being ashamed, said nothing at all; instead, they begged for my forgiveness. (86)
Indeed, all those gods dwelling in heaven have been punished by me and restrained in their own places, and established in their appropriate positions according to their merit.
Indeed, I have established the authority and the formal arrangement for all;
at that time, you were appointed by me as the sovereign ruler over everything.
O Lakṣmī, at that time you became one who obstructed those worthy of the supreme abode and improper recipients;
and sovereignty was then bestowed upon you by me. (89)
"O beloved, you must always remain present at every single sacrificial hearth (dhiṣṇya).
If anyone unworthy should forcibly approach that supreme station," [so it was said].
O Lakṣmī, from that time forward, another [person] must be cast far away by you from any other deity; for among the gods, no one else at any time shall occupy another’s place. 9.1.
One who is seated indeed becomes capable and is swiftly cast down;
thus, O beloved, you were established in all those very positions at that time.
At that time, I became the beloved son of Viṣṇu Āditya;
you, moreover, were born as a maiden from the womb of Dyau, Śrī Nārāyaṇī. (93)
Then Heaven and Earth were entrusted to me; then you, O Narayana, were the Sun; and then, in that kalpa, I was the primordial Aditya-Narayana.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, the infallible Acyuta, always remained as my son in that Sun-god’s abode until the end of the kalpa. 95.
"You are the daughter of the Day, my wife; you were Devavīthī at that time.
I remember all of that; you too, remember Devavīthī. (96)
I myself, as the Supreme Brahman, was indeed always present there;
and in that year, my innumerable incarnations also took place there.
Thus, having indeed abandoned their dispute over the sacrificial hearths (dhiṣṇya) as prescribed, all the gods went to their respective seats, freed from the grounds of contention. 98.
From that time onwards, there was never again any conflict over the meaning of words anywhere in that year,
nor even in another kalpa.
Everything has been regulated by me and established according to my will;
thus it proceeds with ease, and never indeed does it go contrary to that.
Thus, O Daughter of Śiva, my manifestation has been proclaimed to you;
by reading or even hearing this, one obtains the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation," in the third section (the Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, concerning the appearance of the beginningless Brahma-Nārāyaṇa in the sixth year of the Creator for the purpose of instructing Rudra, and the appearance of the beginningless Āditya-Nārāyaṇa in the seventh year for the purpose of regulating the stations of the gods. || 5 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, and furthermore, in the eighth year known as Ajaniyama, during the fifth Kalpa.
Furthermore, while the seventh Manu was reigning there at that time, I myself was the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama.
Indeed, I manifested at that time for the sake of the happiness of those possessed by pride.
Once, O beloved, in Pātāla, there were Nāgas capable of assuming forms at will.
They performed the Mahārudra sacrifice to propitiate Saṃkarṣaṇa;
at that Mahārudra sacrifice, indeed, the families of the serpent-bearers were present.
Then there were fifty-two thousand gathered together—
black, red, variegated, white, spotted, and brindled.
Blue, yellow, and green svastikas and moon-marks,
as well as double-edged spears with two hoods, three hoods, and four hoods.
Likewise, there were snakes with a hundred faces, others with a thousand hoods,
as well as the serpent-kings Karkaṭaka, Śītala, and Ḍiṇḍima.
The Bhūpiṇḍas and others, the Koḍiphas, the pale Paṇḍakas, as well as the Śūlakas, Daṇḍakas, the Dvimukhas, and those with divine vision; || 8 ||
The Oṃkāras, Tilavarṇas, Pāraḍaṅkas, and Kaṇāśanas; the Tiryagdhāras, Sūtradhāras, Mudrapṛṣṭhas, and Dvipṛṣṭhakas. || 9 ||
The Dvijihvas, Bahujihvas, Bahudaṃṣṭras, Viṣālayas,
Kālakūṭas, Samaṇayas, Kārdamikas, and Vārśayas.
The Ānalikas, Anilakas, Mārucchryas, and Sapakṣakas; the Ugrakas, Śāntadāsas, Māhālasyas, and Viḍambins. (11)
Thus, at that time, many kinds of Kaṇādhras gathered together [to worship] Saṃkarṣaṇa,
Yajñadeva, and their own chosen deity, Analānana.
Eagerly, they performed sacrifices to please [the gods] with sweet oblations;
they conducted their own sacrifice for a thousand days according to the prescribed rules.
Svastika was their preceptor, and Śeṣa was then the king;
he was the foremost patron, while others were the meritorious officiating priests.
Delicious foods from the netherworld, savory juices from the ocean,
fruits grown in the forest, and various kinds of royal edibles.
He also gathered grains produced from crops, as well as tubers, medicinal herbs, and shrubs; various kinds of sacrificial fuel and diverse types of *gundra* grasses.
In that sacrifice, they offered all kinds of foodstuffs produced from the earth, as well as oblations fit for vows and meals.
Saṃkarṣaṇa, the Great God, adorned with his own mandala, along with the wealthy gods of Pātāla and tens of millions of Garuḍas, [departed]. || 18 ||
Accompanied by the Surāṇīs, he attained supreme satisfaction at the sacrifice;
on the final day, he appeared there in person, assuming the form of Rudra.
During the *pūrṇāhuti*, while it was being performed with milk-rice and other offerings, ghee, sesame seeds, flour-cakes, sweet juices, and pungent herbs, [the following occurred].
"I am pleased," he said to the serpents; "I am satisfied," he said again and again. "Choose a boon; may you be happy," he said to them once more. (21)
Then those serpents, including Prajādi, made this request to the king:
"In the world of men, we indeed wish to become sharers in the kingdom. (22)
"Having performed our duties, we shall go to liberation, heaven, or the supreme dissolution;
grant us this boon, O excellent Karṣaṇa, if you are pleased. (23)
"O Viṣṇu, O Saṃkarṣaṇa, O granter of our own desires, we are worthy of choosing [a boon].
Having reflected thus for a moment, Saṃkarṣaṇa spoke to them.
May those who constantly dwell in the great forest, living as forest-dwellers, become enjoyers of sovereignty on earth, partaking in the pleasures of the gods. ||25||
"O twice-born ones, let them never at any time cause distress to human beings dwelling on the earth; having made this rule, I grant you this boon. (26)
While you conduct yourselves in this manner, there will be supreme happiness;
O twice-born ones, may you always attain prosperity and well-being.
Having spoken thus, the god Saṃkarṣaṇa, together with the gods, received the sacrificial food (haviṣyānna) which was the very form of the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti), and then vanished from sight.
Then indeed those hooded serpents were no longer thirsty for the boon of power over Nārāyaṇī’s splendor, nor even for human excellence.
Greedily attached to human enjoyments and slain by delusion, they indeed arrived from all sides at the world of mortals through the openings of the winds.
All the men, women, and human beings who have come to this earth possess the power to assume any form at will; indeed, they do not have the appearance of serpents. (31)
Concealed among men, they move about and dwell there as servants acting with deceit, in order to seize kingdoms and enjoyments. (32)
Throughout the entire surface of the earth, they were indeed endowed with beauty of form;
both the Nāgas and the Nāginīs became intent on performing service.
They dwelt among kings, merchants, groups of brahmins, and those who served ministers; they also stayed with virtuous and eminent householders.
Having become servants, male slaves, and female slaves, they imitated the social orders;
indeed, daughters were married among one another by those of human birth. (35)
The daughters of Mānava and the Nāgas in human form gathered together;
having thus established this relationship, they took their opportunity.
In various places, they bit men at night while they were under the power of sleep;
and kings and queens, having been bitten, died in every way. (37)
The merchants and the wealthy, the best among all the castes, then made that empty place their own property. (38)
The serpents, who could assume any form at will and were lords of the earth, feasted;
for the words of Saṃkarṣaṇa had not been carried out by those dominated by darkness (tamas).
By those intent on their own interests, who assume deceptive guises and are devoted to secret indulgence,
the human creation has thus been almost entirely destroyed.
And by those of the serpent race, who were devoted to their own self-interest and concealed the faults of biting, their own creation was further increased. (41)
Even all the ritual acts of human beings were considered as worship of the gods;
yet the sacrificial rites were repeatedly neglected, the twilight prayers were omitted, and likewise the fire-oblations were abandoned.
The ancestral rites (śrāddha) were thus neglected, as were charity and self-restraint among men;
likewise, the lineage-designations of the sages were lost on all sides.
The ritual procedures have been lost to men, as have the activities of the serpents;
the vows have also been lost, and the invocation and other rites have vanished.
The water offering (argha) for the Sun has been omitted, and the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice has come to an end;
likewise, the rites for the deceased have been neglected, and the temples of the gods are devoid of worship.
The fragments of the narrative have reached dissolution; indeed, the Brahmins and kings have passed away.
The dwellings of the celibate students and the residences of the teachers have likewise gone to destruction. (46)
The truthful and the virtuous have died, even those killed by millions of serpents;
the holy men have also died, as have their dwellings, villages, and cities. (47)
But they became non-human on all sides due to the wrath of the Nāgas;
and the names of the most eminent ones vanished from their dwellings. (48)
People did not understand how this had come to pass; consequently, the gods were deprived of their sacrifices and the ancestors were denied their satisfaction. (49)
When a hundred years had passed, they remained composed without investigating: "Whence has this come about, and how was this inauspicious atheism born upon the earth? (3.6.50)
"A hundred years of human life have passed even on our earthly plane;
why indeed does there not occur any invitation, invocation, or other such rites? (51)
But having seen with their divine vision that men had died, they understood that snakes were ruling the kingdoms, even though the subjects themselves were of serpent nature. (52)
Snakes capable of assuming any form at will, as well as female nāgas who likewise take on whatever forms they desire,
enjoy the riches of the earth.
This birth was indeed undesirable, devoid of righteous action;
they were serpents of the nature of darkness (tāmasa), concealing their true nature while acting with deceit. ||54||
They enjoy human pleasures, destroying the exaltation of the divine sages;
indeed, the destruction of humans has occurred in manifold ways since ancient times.
In places such as dwellings, humans do not exist, nor are serpents found within them;
in forests and the like, humans are found, though they are sparse in some locations. (56)
However, they must be made aware by us that death awaits them from the nāgas, and they must also be informed of the means for slaying those nāgas. (57)
Having thus consecrated them with mantras, they descended from the sky to the surface of the earth,
to Ilāvṛta, the central region, which was filled with vast forests.
There dwell pure brahmins in the forest, free from serpents—
those who know the Gāruḍa and Atharva Vedas, and who are devoted to the performance of fire-offerings.
Beholding the sages and the gods, the twice-born offered them a welcome,
presented the honey-mixture (madhuparka), and inquired as well about the purpose of their arrival.
Those desiring to know questioned the gods, who then spoke to them:
"Let all the twice-born and men, along with millions of nāgas, come to understand. (61)
All those who have died perish day after day from the effects of poison;
they were serpents in human form on earth due to the boon granted by Saṃkarṣaṇa.
For having assembled, they exist after having slain human beings;
enjoying human pleasures, they rejoice while remaining in disguise.

The rites pertaining to the gods, the ancestors, and the sun— such as the worship, invocation, honoring, and offering of dharma and ritual action— as well as the astrological calculations of one's birth, have all been fully explained.
"O sirs, that you live as forest-dwellers is the grace of Hari;
for it is by good fortune that you live where there are neither snakes nor predatory beasts. (65)
Having recited the mantras found in the Atharvaveda which are means for slaying nāgas, let them bring about the destruction of the nāga hosts upon the earth.
Let the twice-born kings here perform the Nāga-sacrifice,
and likewise worship the Supreme Lord, the Ruler of the World, during the ritual.
May the Lord of Śrī, Puruṣottama, who is the Supreme Brahman transcending the imperishable, grant protection to us and drive away the serpents from here. 68.
Having spoken thus, the Pitṛs and the gods departed for their own abodes;
the Brahmins, remaining in the region of Āvṛtakhanda, performed the sacrifice.
There, one known as Gāruḍa, who was indeed proficient in the rites of the Atharvaveda, became the Hotṛ priest at that sacrifice; the other Brahmins performed the invocation.
Then the serpents fell down, not being drawn into the sacrifice;
those mantras, being powerless, spoke to the composed brahmins: ||71||
"Propitiate the Lord of the lords of gods, the Lord of the lords of lords;
for he, O Brahmins, the Supreme Lord, will surely act for your welfare. (72)
Thus addressed, O Lakṣmī, those thousand Brahmins quickly performed the Brahma-sacrifice in the hermitage of the twice-born one named Gāruḍa.
There, Hari, the Lord and Master of the syllables, arrived swiftly;
he who is "I am He" is the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person, together with you.
In the midst of the house of Gāruḍa, while the twice-born yogins were looking on,
he appeared bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, and was attended by mantras.
There, I stood before him accompanied by the Vedas in embodied form;
seeing me, the twice-born rose up and bowed to me, offering words of welcome. (76)
They offered him a seat, the honey-mixture, water for his feet, and respectful honors;
all of them reported the calamity that was destroying the human race. ||77||
"I say 'svasti' to you; your fear has now departed. Indeed, perform the snake-sacrifice and employ these mantras. (78)
Thus addressed and impelled by my words, the Garuḍas, O Brahmins, quickly performed the sacrifice against the serpents; the slayers of the hooded snakes recited the mantras.

O you who dwell among mortals, O you who dwell in heaven, O you who have departed, and also those who have not yet departed; O you who enjoy the essence of the earth, O you who are immortal, O you who possess sin, O you who dwell in the waters, O you who do not experience [the fruits of action], may you descend here and partake of the oblations offered! Om! 3.6.80.

Oṃ! May those who are treacherous, who bite their lips, who are murderous, who act crookedly, and who destroy the Dharma, fall here; Oṃ! May those who drink the hundred-fold nectar and those who drink the ocean’s nectar also fall here, streaming with blood into the fierce flames. 81.
Oṃ! May those who enjoy immortality, those who enjoy extreme immortality, those who enjoy the hooded serpents, and those who enjoy abundant flowers come here;
Oṃ! May those who enjoy prosperity, those who enjoy extreme humility, those who enjoy guilelessness, and those who enjoy supreme sovereignty come here as lords of the world. (82)
Then the Garuḍa-brāhmaṇas there recited these mantras and,
having invoked the nāgas with mantras beginning with cruel seed-syllables, they performed oblations.
Then, coming again and again from the sky over the entire expanse of land reaching to the edge of the ocean,
the nāgas fell indeed into that pit, which was fierce with the fire of poison.
Thousands have died and been burned; those who remain are bound with ropes.
Bound by mantras, they are truly not able to liberate themselves at all. 85.
Then the bound Ananta-Śeṣa praised me, the Supreme Lord:
"Protect us, O Lord, ocean of mercy; release us from this great fire! (86)
O Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Supreme Lord, we shall not remain upon the earth;
protect us who have fallen at Your shelter and grant us the gift of life. (87)
"O Janārdana, I am Ananta-Śeṣa and I am always your devotee.
When I had spoken thus, he then said to Ananta, "Go to the serpent-bearers who dwell upon the earth. (88)
"Taking all the various classes of nāgas, go indeed to the lower realm;
do not establish your own abode here again in this world of men. (89)
Thus addressed, he accepted everything as released by me;
indeed, all the serpents were liberated from the jaws of death by means of the Gāruḍa [mantra].
Ananta, my devotee, worshipped me, the Supreme Lord;
at that time, O daughter of Śeṣa, you were born as Jānakī. 91.
And you, Ānantī, were indeed offered by Śeṣa as a sacrificial fee to me, the son of a Brahmin, Śārṅgin, who belongs to the Atharvaṇa-Gāruḍa lineage. ||92||
To the protector of the nagas and serpents, the glorious Lord, the Supreme Self—to Him, the sacrifice was then ordained and performed by me. 93.
Then Śeṣa, having taken all the serpent lineages dwelling upon the surface of the earth, went indeed to the subterranean holes known as Pātāla. 94.
Therefore, this world of men was made by me subject to reproach;
then [I established] men dwelling in the region of Ilāvṛta-khaṇḍa throughout all lands.
And I made them dwell there, along with many lineages;
then, as a man, I gathered the human realm once again.
Through my yoga, all those gods who were devoted to the rites for the ancestors and the gods became highly learned and prosperous. 97.
At that time, I became the beginningless Śrī Garuḍa Nārāyaṇa;
you, Ānantī, the daughter of Śeṣa, became my wife. (98)
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, the incarnator himself, has manifested there before me. 99.
Then, many incarnations of Brahmā occurred in that year;
I know all of this, for I remember my former existence.
At that time, I indeed provided protection for human beings on the earthly realm;
thereafter, I remained steadfast with you until the end of the kalpa.
From reciting, hearing, chanting, and even remembering this, no fear of serpents arises; likewise, there shall be both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "The Manifestation on Earth of the Boundless Garuḍa-Nārāyaṇa for the Purpose of Subduing the Serpents in the Eighth Year of the Creator," in the Third Section (Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Now, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, listen to my story,
which is beautiful and purifying for the Daityas who dwell in Sutala.
Formerly, in the ninth year known as the *āsana* of Brahmā, during the first of the fourteen kalpas, in the world-system of Sutala within the lower regions; || 2 ||
There was a king named Calavarman, a universal monarch of great strength,
the lord of Atala, Vitala, and Sutala.
At that time, his vehicle indeed became one that travels through the sky throughout the three worlds;
so too did the subjects and people of Atala, Vitala, and Sutala.
They indeed worshipped King Caladeva as their manifest protector;
the king too was righteous and devoted to the protection of his subjects.
O Daughter of Śiva, my devotee is devoted to the worship of the gods;
he is a refuge for the helpless, for guests, and for women, and is radiant with virtuous conduct.
Half of that day he always spends in the worship of the God,
and half of that [remaining] time he spends in observing the kingdom.
The remaining half always goes to his own worlds during his sojourn;
as he was acting in this manner, a desire for asceticism arose within him. (8)
"Since austerity bears fruit ten-thousandfold more swiftly on the land of action (karmabhūmi),
I shall go to the earth and perform penance," he reflected, and traveling by celestial chariot, he departed.
Having consulted with his royal sages regarding a true guru, the king then entrusted the entire kingdom to him;
and, having honored his teacher, he set out for Mānavīkṣita.
Having reached Mount Kumuda, he performed austerities for a thousand years without food in a forest perpetually pervaded by cold.
There, during his ascetic penance, that king beheld with divine vision Nārāyaṇa, the supreme lord, the god Śrī Puruṣottama.
Having bowed down to me alone, the Supreme Self, he spoke what was in his mind:
"Salutations to you, the Supreme Lord, the bestower of the fruits of austerity."
Having said, "To Hari, the Supreme Soul, who fills the minds of His devotees," he prostrated himself like a staff and drank the nectar of my feet.
Then, urged by me, King Cala begged:
"Grant me immovability here; for that which is mobile surely goes to destruction."
Kingdom is transient, wealth is transient, and likewise the family is transient;
even life itself is transient, O Kṛṣṇa, and consequently even the netherworlds and other realms are transient.
Therefore, I choose from you that which is immovable; I am your devotee, grant me this boon.
The illustrious Supreme Lord said:
Listen, O King, everything is moving; even this cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) is moving.
Time is moving, Māyā is moving, and both the mind and the individual soul (jīva) are moving.
"Tell me, you consider everything that moves to be moving and everything that does not move to be unmoving.
Śrī Caladeva said:
The mind is moving, fortune is moving, and even the royal command is moving. (18)
"Indeed, your devotion is unshakable; I choose that [devotion], so grant it to me, O Lord!
Then, O Keśava, may I become an unwavering vessel for that which is unshakable."
The illustrious Supreme Lord said:
"My loving devotion is unshakable, and service preceded by love is that [true] service.
If you truly desire to become such an unshakable vessel for it," || 3.7.20 ||
Then I shall grant you eternal and unshakable liberation in my world;
quickly take my mantra and go to my imperishable abode.
Śrī Caladeva said: "I was fickle, yet by your grace I have now become steadfast;
O Ordainer, ensure that my lineage likewise becomes unshakable. (22)
The illustrious Supreme Lord said:
"O King, just as you have become immovable through a portion of my grace, so too shall your lineage attain immovability through union with me."
"You remain childless, O King; become one who has offspring!
Without me, all that is transient belongs to you as your offspring—I myself shall become your child. (24)
"Behold, O Lakṣmī, I am your offspring here, immovable";
having spoken thus, I then became his mind-born son.
But the king named Abhavat, known as Ārṣadeva, attained supreme satisfaction;
having completed his ascetic penance, he took the king along with me [to the world of Brahmā].
There, the noble sage, my guru, did not recognize me as the Lord;
yet by my command, O Lakṣmī, you became the daughter of that great sage.
The king, according to the prescribed rites, consecrated his own mind-born son, Ārṣadeva, in the kingdom;
and that sage-like king also gave his daughter to me.
You, named Ārṣapadmā, have served both me, the Lord of Śrī,
and the divine seer, the incarnate Lord Śrī Puruṣottama.
For the sake of preserving my word, even Viṣṇu himself has been manifested by me as a mental son in the form of a son.
Named Dṛḍhadhruva, bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus as his excellent weapons, Viṣṇu was born as a youth, resplendent with sovereign power and other attributes. (31)
He was indeed established in the immovable, supreme station at the end of heaven;
he is the foundation for the worlds, as well as for the planets and the luminaries.
The circles of the constellations, the stars, and the sages revolved because of the stability of the Pole Star, which was made firm by the name "Dhruva."
Caladeva, sent by me to Nārāyaṇīśrī, has reached the imperishable, immovable, and undecaying abode; my word has been fulfilled by me.
I am the immovable one, likewise the son of the beginningless Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa; I am myself the Supreme Brahman, known as the beginningless Ārṣanārāyaṇa.
My son, named Dṛḍhadhruva, is Viṣṇu himself;
by the power of my words, he has been rendered immovable until the end of the kalpa.
Thus indeed, O Lakṣmī, my manifestation occurred of old upon the surface of the earth, and my son’s sovereignty was in the world of Sutala, above heaven. 37.
Then you must remember your own Ṛṣipadmā, the daughter of a sage;
O Ṛṣinārāyaṇī, the manifestation of my Lord has been described. 38.
Thereafter, O beloved, I shall declare my manifestation; listen to me.
Now, Lakṣmī, in my lineage, there was a son of Dṛḍhadhruva. (35)
And there was a king of devotees, a sage and ascetic named Thurānanda;
he, a Vaiṣṇava, performed extensive penance for the duration of a Manvantara. (3.7.40)
Then the blessed Lord Brahmā, being pleased, granted a boon:
"O Indra among kings, do not perform penance; choose a boon as you desire. (41)
Thus addressed by Brahmā, he said: "My lifespan is only two years;
make me live for a long time, for two thousand kalpas. (42)
"So be it," said the Creator, granting a boon to Thurā;
and Thurānanda, too, enjoyed himself in Satyaloka according to his desire.
Indeed, his life span of two years was thus divided between day and night;
in the ninth year, that two-year lifespan had passed away in two parts.
A thousand kalpas constitute their days, and a thousand kalpas their nights;
thus, when the tenth year of the restraint of breath had arrived.
And at that time, O beloved, on the fourteenth day of the Kalpa of Vedhas, during the first Manvantara, [this occurred] for Thurānanda.
A period of two Brahma-years passed there by means of days and nights;
remembering his former births, he once again began his ascetic penance.
Indeed, for the sake of sovereignty over the three worlds, he was restrained by the gods,
by the sages from Satyaloka, and by the ancestors beginning with Jana.
Prevented from the heavens by the gods and from the surface of the earth by humans,
he then went to the netherworld (atala) for the sake of asceticism, being honored by the Dānavas.
Honored by the Daityas and also honored by the Asuras,
he performed fierce ascetic penance at the sacrifice, propitiating Rudra.
He offered his head, together with the eyes, into the fire within the sacrificial pit;
at that moment, Rudra himself appeared there, resplendent with divine luster.
"Tell me what pleases you here; choose, and I shall give you everything.
Then Thurānanda said, "O Lord, grant me immunity from death."
Hara said: "Except for Kṛṣṇa, the eternal Supreme Brahman, your invincibility has been granted; let your head be joined [to your body]. (5.3)
Thus addressed, Dhruvānanda, the son of Dhruva, was exceedingly delighted;
he then brought to an end both his ascetic penance and his own sacrifice.
Then the king also, accompanied by the Dānavas, set out to seize the earth; together with the Daityas and Asuras, he made both the earth and the heavens his own.
Wherever there existed that supreme status, consecrated for sovereignty, belonging to kings, gods, and those of other worlds, [he attained it]. (56)

Having conquered all those various powerful beings, that warrior intoxicated by battle brought the Dānavas who had taken refuge with him under his control and installed them in their respective positions.
He consecrated the Daityas, Asuras,
and kings under his own authority as rulers over all regions on the surface of the earth— both kings and Daityas and Dānavas.
The lords of beings and the asuras became oppressors of the subjects;
they were devoid of righteous action and conduct, and were possessed of fallen behavior.
Lacking virtue and acting according to their own whims, filled with violence and wickedness, and devoid of the practice of sacrifice, they became consumers of the wealth of their subjects. (3.7.60)
Deprived of sacred fords, gifts, and worship, strayed from the right path, and abandoned by the Veda,
even the gods, the ancestors, and the great seers [fled] out of fear of him.
All the humans became distressed, tormented by the Rākṣasas;
even Thurananda was accompanied by the Asuras throughout all the worlds.
He indeed travels by means of a celestial chariot and proclaims in every way:
"Let the people worship, honor, and propitiate the lord of men! (63)
Considering me directly as the Supreme Lord, let them offer gifts;
let them worship me in sacrifices and even in the temples of the gods. 64.
"May people always worship me in the place of Gaṇeśa;
may they pay tribute to me and proclaim my virtues. (65)
"Let them behold my image and offer me ritual services;
let them take my name in the morning. I am Viṣṇu, and not another. (66)
"Thurānanda! Thurānanda! Thurānanda!"—let them cry out thus.
In Thurānanda, great bliss (mahānanda) and the bliss of Brahman (brahmānanda) shall meet. || 67 ||
I am the one known as Brahman, the Support; in the Support, illusion does not exist.
Having attained and served the Support, suffering shall be eternally destroyed.
Having obtained me as their protector, may the people of Mathurā be happy forever;
for I am the king of yogins, as well as of the ancestors and the celestial dwellers. (69)
Among men, sages, Daityas, and likewise Rakshasas,
as well as among the Vasus, the treasures, and the guardians of the quarters, I am the king.
"I am the king of the oceans, the forests, and the Gandharvas"—
thus [he spoke] in the tenth region, known as Prāṇarodha, belonging to Ajavyuha.
In that fourteenth kalpa, during the first Manvantara, O King,
there was a powerful monarch who was honored by the Daityas and Dānavas.
Then, O Sovereign Goddess, the subjects, gods, ancestors, sages, women, the truthful, and the virtuous all propitiated me. (73)
Remaining concealed within their own homes and concentrated within their own hearts, humans and others offered praise to me, Śrī Hari, for the sake of protection. 74.
O Lord Hara, ocean of mercy, friend of the distressed, Janārdana! O crusher of unrighteousness, destroyer of the Daityas, Supreme Lord! (79)
Protect, protect us, O Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Ādinārāyaṇa, Lord!
You are the Supreme Brahman, the inner self; protect us who are tormented by the dānavas.
In this manner, all embodied beings offered their prayers in many ways;
then, having reflected upon that deed of Thurānanda, I spoke.
Even until the end of the granting of boons, may there be a reunion with you on the surface of the earth, in the world of humans, in the western region of Mount Meru.
Then, by the sight [of him] in the presence of his wife Viśokā, in the district of Bhāmantaka known by that name, which was the dwelling place of wise brahmins.
I appeared in the form of a child, bearing the conch, the discus, and the mace;
the Lord bearing the wheel, the thunderbolt, the spear, the trident, the staff, and the noose.
I am that Hari, the eight-armed one, the Supreme Brahman Nārāyaṇa; I am radiant with the power of ten million Cupids, and skilled in battle.
Then you, O Lakṣmī, an expert conversant with all weapons and mantras, devoted to the state of Brahman, were commanded by me and departed swiftly. 8.2.
In order to manifest her own presence in the abode of Thurananda, the Goddess became the mind-born daughter of Thurananda immediately upon birth. || 83 ||
