Named Jyotsnākumārikā and endowed with all auspicious marks,
you were then at the king’s palace, fit for a svayaṃvara.
The king held a great assembly on earth known as a *svayaṃvara*, and in the vast region of Bhāmantaka, he performed an invitation to the three worlds. (85)
Right there, the king then had a pavilion for the *svayaṃvara* constructed; it was a celestial pavilion, equal in splendor to the city of Indra.
When the day had been determined, the Daityas and Dānavas arrived there,
as did the kings, the lords of the earth, the rulers of Pātāla, and the lords of heaven.
The guardians of the directions and protectors of the worlds from the fourteen realms arrived at that pavilion, desiring to see Jyotsnākumārikā. (88)
A gathering of hundreds of kings took place there in the royal palace;
at that most excellent moment, adorned by the moonlight, [the bride] cast the garland upon the groom.
Having been led away by her kinsmen, who were skilled in the use of superior weapons,
the maiden Jyotsnikā— truly so named— was one who drew all beings toward herself.
Accompanied by an excellent attendant, a woman of known noble lineage, and a venerable Brahmin, she entered the pavilion.
You are of a supramundane nature, bringing an end to the dullness of the assembly;
everyone is enchanted upon beholding you, who dwell within the imperishable. 92.
"Never before seen, nor heard of anywhere—may she be mine!"—thus did the hearts of the kings momentarily become at that place. (93)
Indeed, the minds of those whose yoga was incomplete were shattered;
even the minds of those who were complete became objects of doubt. 94.
O Lakṣmī, at that moment, by your splendor, the assembly of hundreds of millions of kings became,
in an instant, as if devoid of luster in your presence.
Even the kings of heaven then became despondent in their hopes:
"She will certainly not choose us, for we are unworthy and devoid of beauty. (96)
Thus, even those devoid of desire [are liberated]; what then need be said of others?
Then, having gone to the gate and bowed to the deity of the gate— (97)
Having entered the divine pavilion by way of the golden path,
she beheld the king and heard [the account] from the old woman.
Having failed to find the one who dwells in her heart, she whose mind remained unattached there wandered again and again;
after circling the pavilion three times, she gazed at it from every side.
Not seeing me, she approached the city gate accompanied by her bridegroom’s garland;
there I became a Brahmin who was indeed unable to enter.
The Brahmin was poor, wearing a yellow washed garment and a yellow tunic; his head was wrapped, and he appeared like a youth of sixteen years. 101.
Endowed with physical beauty and equipped with all subtle weapons,
he arrived after concealing his subtle form, intent upon the destruction of the Daityas.
Having applied sandalwood paste upon my forehead and holding a rosary in my hand,
while wearing sandals upon my feet, I became one who was extraordinary to the world.

Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Manifestation of the Beginningless Wise Nārāyaṇa for the Purpose of Overcoming Thurānanda—the Son of Dhruva-deva, who was Nourished by the Dānavas—and the Svayaṃvara of Jyotsnākumārikā Lakṣmī," in the ninth year of the Creator’s [incarnation] within the lineage of Caladeva during the third period, the Dvāpara-yuga, as described in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. || 7 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Then, O Lakṣmī, having beheld your own ancient beloved,
you placed the garland of choice upon my neck while the kings looked on.
The entire assembly was struck with wonder and filled with great amazement;
an exclamation arose: "Oh, how the Brahmin has won the princess!"
A daughter given to a poor man, to one devoid of fortune,
or to a beggar who is unequal to her— such a daughter has indeed gone unto death.
Oh, what a misfortune was my birth in Rājagṛha, which brings the suffering of poverty! The wish-fulfilling creeper, radiant as gold, has fallen into the hands of a bear.
A beautiful golden lotus fell into dry mud,
and a garland consisting of land-lotuses came to rest upon the monkey's neck.
Like lightning from the clouds of Svāti falling upon a dry mountain,
divine Fortune, worthy of a king, has now fallen upon a pauper.
The moonlight, having abandoned the moon, has resorted to a tiny star;
the radiance, having forsaken the sun, has resorted to the empty sky.
Having abandoned the virtuous man, learning has taken refuge with the caviler;
like the sky, which, having deserted Mahendra, has sought shelter with Nairṛta.
Beauty has abandoned the beloved and, like a delusion, resorted to the deluded; the virtuous woman, having utterly forsaken the truth, has gone through illusion to the illusory one.
The matted locks have abandoned Śambhu and leaped toward a clump of banyan trees;
the Gaṅgā has left the foot of Viṣṇu and come to the salt ocean.
Having abandoned the path of devotion, she has fallen into immoral conduct; having forsaken her husband, she has followed after another man. (11)
Siṃhikā, having abandoned the lion, has approached a boar;
the female elephant, having left her mate, has taken refuge with a wild buffalo.
Having abandoned Śeṣa, the serpent-queen indeed entered the state of a reptile;
and Kālī, having cast off her crown, went to Cirpaṭaveṭana.
Oh, the power of destiny! The Queen has resorted to the speech of Hari;
such a thing was never seen anywhere before, nor is it ever seen by people anywhere. 14.
People consider this divine garland of wish-fulfilling gems placed around the neck of a dog to have surely been brought about by fate. (15)
Or rather, since the maiden was overwhelmed by beholding the assembly,
she rendered this [assembly] lusterless by means of her own splendors.
For that which has been produced is indeed undesirable, as it will surely not be accepted by the maiden;
or rather, the maiden does not know that this is a garland for the bridegroom.
Having observed that it was common property, the garland of choice was bestowed upon a poor man; it may even become a second [garland] for the cuckoos.
Or perhaps this girl is intended for the purpose of honoring the Brahmins;
therefore, while there are virtuous kings, a daughter should not be given to a poor man. (19)
Or else, if the king gives her to him, we shall take her away;
for even when a *svayaṃvara* has taken place, a maiden remains subject to war.
"Having fought, we shall obtain the jewel; there is no doubt about this"—thus did the king and the others speak there in many ways. (21)
The father of the maiden also fell into grief for a moment;
seeing that his daughter had gone away to a poor man, he was seized with fever.
Then, considering that some fortune had arrived for the sake of his daughter,
the king indeed desired to bestow her upon the bridegroom according to the prescribed rites.
Then the queen and the elderly preceptor also restrained the king, saying:
"O King, do not act so hastily; let it be so in the pavilion."
And this has turned out to be improper, since the girl is indeed deluded;
or rather, she is devoid of mental stability and lacks a steady state of mind. (25)
"Therefore, the garland must be given once again for the sake of the svayaṃvara itself. Having heeded these words, the king said to them, "So be it. (26)
Then the group of princes also considered that to be appropriate;
and the maiden was repeatedly questioned by Janaka and the others regarding this matter.
Then she, perceiving the hint from Rameśa, said something;
meanwhile, the king had gone and placed the maiden at a distance from the brahmin. (28)
Having led her to the pavilion and again given him a supreme garland,
the maiden, having wandered everywhere within the pavilion, placed the marriage-thread upon his hand.
In this very way she remains composed; she offers herself to no one at all;
she speaks not, nor does she look at another, nor does she desire anything. (3.8.30)
As if contemplating the pretext for the destruction of the Asuras,
O Lakṣmī, she then spoke to you as you approached the city gate.
Thinking her to be Māmakī, he seized Samālā by force;
and as I was leading you away alone, having taken hold of the garden fence, [he appeared]. (32)
Meanwhile, messengers, groups of servants, and warriors approached me;
they indeed struck me and seized you, who had been separated from me.
Then a great clamor arose and the assembly became agitated:
"This virtuous maiden, who is surely to be won by strength, is being carried away by servants! (34)
"Kill them, fight them, and seize the maiden!"—in this way, the very foundation of battle was indeed commenced in an instant. (35)
While they were looking on, I quickly placed you upon my shoulder, took hold of you, and fled; at that time, a rain of arrows fell.
I remembered my own celestial chariot, called Akṣara, which was exceedingly brilliant, shining on all sides with supreme and great splendors. ||37||
O Lakṣmī, it was resplendent with attendants and hosts of liberated ones, adorned with white elephants, bearing all kinds of weapons, and accompanied by divine female pearl-ornaments. 38.
Having placed you in their midst for the sake of battle with the Dānavas,
I alone became armored, a Brahmin assuming the form of a Kṣatriya.
Taking up his own great bow,
which brings all things into existence, he indeed cut down all those arrows with his own feathered shafts.
He shattered the golden armor of the warriors;
and all the kings, those preeminent Daityas, surrounded him on every side.
The Asuras and Dānavas also struck me from all sides;
at that time, I thought, "I must bring about their destruction. ||42||
Some were slain there by his power, others were struck down by the *bhūśuṇḍī* weapon, and still others were felled by *toma* arrows and lunar shafts. 43.
Some were broken by maces, others pierced by swords;
some were killed with clubs, and others split apart by battle-axes.
Some were mangled by thunderbolt-like speeds, others were pierced by spears, and still others were rendered lifeless there on the field of battle by pikes. (45)
Others were struck down by swords, while some were mangled by iron balls;
at that time, the bodies of the warriors were pulverized by the Mudgalas.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, there I alone deprived crores of asuras of their lives, sending them either to heaven or to the abode of Yama.
Indeed, the powerful ones were led to the imperishable station of Vaikuṇṭha, as well as to the immortal realm, the uncreated Goloka. 48.
Then King Sahasrahasta, motivated by the skull, came to fight with me at that time in Sutala. ||49||
All his arms were severed by the Sudarśana discus;
having bowed down and become my devotee, he departed from the battlefield.
I gave him exactly two hands, no more; having forgiven him as his hands rose up against my shoulder, I went home.
Then King Śatamūrdhan, whose vehicle was a deer and who bore the name Sāraṅgavāhana, fought with the son of Vitala and me using crescent-shaped arrows.
He too was indeed cut in the throat by me with arrows radiant as the sun;
his headless trunk fell upon the earth, and he died.
Then the king of Atala, named Sāmarāyodhana,
approached me with a thousand foot-soldiers for the purpose of battle.
Then my feet were indeed severed by his discus;
his headless trunk fell down and he died. (55)
Then the great king Mahendrabhīṣaṇa by name, the sovereign of that nine-province region of the earth, came there to fight against me.
He indeed hurled many spears to cut my throat;
with my own spear, I lacerated his right arm from the shoulder.
Then that hero, with one hand, took up an excellent sword and rushed toward me; at that moment, I struck off his head with my blade.
Then those Daityas who were appointed to positions of authority in heaven arrived by way of the sky to fight with me in the atmosphere. ||59||
I have fought with thousands of forms using various weapons; they have been torn asunder by my Sudarśana discus and by many other wheels.
Thus, in that place, the brave Arbudas were sent by my hands and weapons to the state of departed spirits, even though they had been released from their bonds.
There in the battle, Thurānanda, the sovereign emperor, was captured alive by me, bound with nooses and reins, and brought under my control.
At that time, O Lakṣmī, you were overcome by affection for your father and said, "Do not do this to me! and so the king was released by me.
Having sought refuge, the king bowed at my feet;
through my granting of fearlessness, he was established as a sovereign of unwavering devotion.
Then other armies of the Dānavas fled,
leaving behind those who had gone from the surface of the earth to the sky, and from the sky back to the earth.
Having thus rid the surface of the earth of its thorns, even making it like heaven itself, he then desisted from battle, thinking, "I am now in my father-in-law's house. (66)
The king led me to his own residence in the midst of the wedding pavilion;
there, according to the prescribed rites, he then gave his daughter Jyotsnāśrī and you to me.
The king indeed bestowed as a dowry countless gold and jewels,
as well as celestial chariots, vehicles, elephants, horses, bulls, and so forth.
Having taken male and female servants, cities, wish-fulfilling creepers, pools of nectar,
golden chariots, and human vehicles, I shall then lead you away from there as well.
Having performed the funeral rites for the deceased, he then returned to his own home together with you to the dwelling of the wise Brahmin.
Then, indeed, I made the kings and the Brahmins upon the earth;
the earth became dependent on the Brahmins, performing the rites for the gods and the ancestors. (71)
He restored Bhuvaḥ, Svarga, and Janādya, each to its respective abode exactly as it was before; he gave them back to them again according to the sacred ordinance.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, at that time the world was deceived by the wicked, even though it belongs to the Supreme Self, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (73)
By Puruṣottama Kṛṣṇa, the source of all incarnations,
I indeed then became the beginningless Śrī Prājña Nārāyaṇa.
Then, until the end of the kalpa, your father Thurananda remained in the Bhāmaṇṭaka region; he was my devotee and a knower of the Self. (75)
At the end of his life, that man of pure devotion went to my imperishable abode.
Remember your own splendor, which is like moonlight; all that is beneficial is within my reach.
In this way, other innumerable incarnations of mine also occurred thereafter;
now listen, O beloved, as I describe another manifestation of mine.
In the year of the Creator known as Pratyāhāra, consisting of one hundred and ten thousand years,
and also during the ninth Kalpa and the second Manvantara.
Due to the power of past times, atheism indeed arose everywhere in the world; through the influence of the Tiṣya age, my worship has been destroyed. (79)
The temples have been destroyed and the sanctuaries have vanished;
the images have gone to dissolution and the holy fords have been ruined.
At that time, the beastly bull was indeed pervasive among human beings;
then those people were of little knowledge, short-lived, and forgot me. 8.1.
Living in pits, naked, and subsisting on crops, grains, and the like;
they will be small in stature, short-lived, and filled with atheism during the Tiṣya age.
The Vedas have reached dissolution for me; the ritual section has gone to its end. Even my worship, my chanting, and my recitation of praises and so forth have reached dissolution.
At that time, as if something unprecedented had occurred, I was entreated by Brahmā;
for the sake of establishing devotion to Dharma, I became accessible through my compassion. (84)
In the house of King Vīraśarabha, the four-armed Lord appeared, endowed with great virtue and vows, accompanied by the bull of the righteous. ||85||
At the time of my manifestation, the gods rained down flowers and other offerings, and the celestial drums of the gods resounded then as well. (86)
The queen Saurabheyī beheld me upon the bed—born not from a womb, endowed with all divine qualities, and most desirable. (87)
She indeed announced to the king: "Look, O King, at this boy here beside me.
The king said: "O Queen, this child has been intended by me [for you]. (88)
"A son born without a womb exists for you; protect him.
Then, as soon as he was born, the son appeared there as a youth. (89)
Endowed with all the qualities of knowledge, a treasure-trove of all specialized sciences,
perfectly accomplished in the attainments of yoga, he has reached the further shore of all languages.
He is complete in all arts and sciences, an awakener to the path of devotion;
he is endowed with the sacred thread and accompanied by a bull and a celibate student.
Out of great joy, he taught the true doctrines to human beings:
celibacy, non-violence, truthfulness, and conduct free from theft. (92)
Purity, contentment, and constant devotion to the Supreme Lord;
likewise, the vow of contentment, as well as forbearance and detachment. (93)
Service to the elders, service to the virtuous, abiding in the bliss of the Supreme Self, charity, compassion, fire-offerings, hospitality, and the worship of Hari. 94.
Austerity is the restraint of the impulses of the senses, the avoidance of delusion, the vision of the Self in all things, and devotion to the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Self. (95)
Hearing, chanting, remembering Kṛṣṇa, and likewise bowing down, as well as self-surrender to Kṛṣṇa—this is the supreme relationship with Hari. (96)
Thus he indeed taught the dharmas of liberation at that time,
and he adopted the life-long vow of the paramahaṃsa.
And you, Lakṣmī, commanded by me, were born as the mind-born daughter of the sage Śārdūla; as soon as she was born, she was eloquent in speech. (98)
She was a young woman in the form of Brahman, endowed with all sovereign powers; she was a virtuous lady devoted to celibacy, who awakened others to the dharma of faithful wives. 99.
She is virtuous, established in dharma, and devoted to my vows;
she is constantly intent on worship, full of devotion, and likewise a bringer of liberation.
"She was indeed entrusted to me by her father and mother for the very purpose of initiation;
initiation has been conferred upon you by me, and you shall always remain a celibate student. (10.1)
O beloved, you became the most venerable among all virtuous women and the giver of instruction; indeed, at that time, your scripture was characterized by the dharma of the righteous.
Then, that [text] consisting of the Śārdūlikāśrīsaṃhitā, which endures until the end of the eon,
was indeed brought down by us both from all the worlds onto the surface of the earth.
The duties of those committed to lifelong celibacy (naiṣṭhika) as well as devotion to Hari were taught;
countless living beings were delivered and established in the Imperishable (akṣara). 104.
Remember this, O Lakṣmī: that at that time you were your own Śārdūlikā-Śrī, and likewise, I was the beginningless Lord Hari, Vīra-Nārāyaṇa.
In this way, my other incarnations were then innumerable;
I know them all through recollection, for they indeed bestow liberation upon remembrance.

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Bestowal of the Garland of Boons upon the Primordial Wise Nārāyaṇa by Jyotsnā Śrī; the Battle of the Kings; the Destruction of the Daityas, Dānavas, and Asuras by Hari with the Sudarśana and other weapons; the Liberation of Thurānanda; the Entrustment of the Earth, Heaven, and other realms to humans and gods respectively; and the Manifestation of the Primordial Heroic Nārāyaṇa in the eleventh year of Brahmā for the purpose of establishing the dharma of perpetual asceticism. In the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, within the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, [this is the eighth chapter].
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, during the twelfth period of concentration (pradhāraṇa),
in that sixth year of Brahmā’s life, within the eighth Manvantara of that Kalpa.
Śoṇabhadra was a Vaiśya devoted to me, one who had conquered his senses;
he was intent on all sacrifices, a giver of all gifts, and fond of guests. || 2 ||
Possessing a hundred thousand cattle and thriving through agricultural enterprise,
he was skilled in buying and selling and honored like a king by the king himself.
Even though his wealth was infinite and his honor preeminent among the people, even though his undertakings were innumerable and his followers numbered in the thousands; (4)
That Blessed One never forgets me at any time;
rising early in the morning during the Brāhma-muhūrta, he [remembers] me, his devotee.
He constantly practices meditation again and again on all the limbs [of yoga];
then, satisfied by meditation, my words are accompanied by the sounding of cymbals.
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, O Lord Nārāyaṇa, Hare!
O Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, O Śrī Puruṣottama! || 7 ||
While he was thus reciting, he then bathed in the river water,
offered libations of water to his ancestors, performed the twilight prayers (saṃdhyā), and completed my worship.
He performs the invocation, the offering of a seat, water for the feet, the respectful oblation (arghya), and likewise water for sipping, using all materials upon my golden image.
Then follows the cleansing of the teeth, gargles for purifying the mouth,
purification with earth, as well as cleansing, and thereafter the purification with water.
Anointing the limbs with fragrant oils and massaging the body, as well as [baths] with milk, curd, clarified butter, and likewise honey. || 11 ||
Likewise, bathing by means of an ablution with sugar and water from sacred fords,
as well as cleansing with a cloth and wearing garments of priceless value.
The gift of fragrant substances by the virtuous, as well as the offering of beautiful articles, and also collyrium for the eyes and an excellent tilaka upon the forehead. (1.3)
A crescent moon on his head, oil for coloring the palms of his hands,
all manner of ornaments, sandals, and flower garlands.
Saffron, *abīra*, *gulāla*, auspicious sandalwood paste, unbroken grains of rice, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings. || 15 ||
Various kinds of foods, betel leaves, water,
sprouts and leaves of Tulasī, and garlands of gold and diamonds.
The nightly lamp-offering, prostration like a staff, hymn-singing, circumambulation, the offering of a gift, salutation, and the seeking of forgiveness for transgressions. || 17 ||
Then, having performed the offering of a handful of flowers and the ritual dismissal of the worship,
he also pays homage to virtuous people, guests, and brahmins.
She always honors and worships cows, children, the distressed, the helpless, and beggars whenever they arrive.
Having caused food and other provisions to be prepared, he gives them as required;
every year, upon the arrival of the new grain, he maintains a most magnificent sacrificial session (*satra*).
The gods and humans indeed partook of the Vaiṣṇava offering;
thus was that auspicious sacrifice of new grain performed by him in nine ways.
Hundreds of thousands of virtuous people, including Brahmins and others,
have constantly gathered there for the seven-day sacrifice of my devotee.
Having come in an invisible form, I accept the offering presented;
and having partaken of the essence of Śiva’s existence, O Goddess, I depart for my own abode. (23)
Thus, when the sacrifice had commenced for those Brahmins who were learned in many scriptures, who had come from various countries, and who were conversant with diverse ritual practices. ||24||

When there was disagreement regarding the auxiliary rites in the ritual section (karmakāṇḍa), when the rite of Rudra was deficient, and when defects arose in the subsidiary acts of the sacrifice due to the provocation of the fire; ||25||
Suddenly, a circle of fire, rising from the sacrificial pit, leaped up and instantly attached itself to the canopy above the pavilion, causing a burning sensation.
The stretching out was swift and ablaze;
the pavilion suddenly burst into flames, and fire spread rapidly on all sides. ||27||
Blazing with flames, fanned by the wind, and greatly increased,
he spread everywhere among the oblations, in dwellings, and in houses.
Then, among the garments, in the sacrificial halls, and even among the men,
the fierce fire— cruel and of cruel deeds— increased with great intensity.
Kālī, Karālī, Vikarālī, Nīlā, and Lohitā [also increased].
The flames are tawny, white, and greenish-yellow, and they are variegated.
There, fifty thousand men were reduced to ashes by the flames, and from that a cry of "Alas! Alas! arose.
Śoṇabhadra, my devotee and king among devotees, fell into great sorrow;
he performed all the funeral rites for the deceased there.
Then, on account of their many murders and sins,
this Vaiśya who was the sacrificer was afflicted with great sorrow.
For a long time indeed, he found neither peace nor sleep;
desiring to raise the dead, he performed worship unto me. (34)
Having renounced food and water, he observed the vow of fasting;
with his mind fixed on me, he devoted himself to my worship day and night. (35)
O Lord Janārdana, having yourself become our son, effect our deliverance; and remove the stain of the destruction of the sacrifice.
Thus, as I have been entreating him, a year has passed in lamentation;
for one whose purpose is death, a year has passed without water. (37)
Then I granted him a boon: "I shall become your son, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. (38)
Having spoken thus, his mind-born son appeared before him;
his wife, a virtuous woman devoted to her vows, was Satī, known by the name Bhadreśvarī. (39)
Having seen me, the lovely child, increased by all splendors,
bestowing all perfections, gentle, and adorned with all ornaments.
The lady, considering it a great festival, accepted that [garment] endowed with divine qualities;
at that moment, a rain of celestial flowers fell from the sky. ||41||
The liberated gods and lords honored me with flowers, shouts of victory, the sounds of musical instruments, and offerings of sandalwood paste and unbroken grains of rice. ||42||
My father performed my birth festival with unparalleled grandeur;
abandoning his own fast, he fed [guests] by the millions. (43)
Then, on that day, Śoṇabhadra [honored] the virtuous, his devotees, the wretched, the helpless, the best of the twice-born, as well as maidens and boys. (44)
The father bestowed gifts of all kinds of objects as the most excellent;
at that time, there were indeed festivals in every house on account of Kṛṣṇa’s birth.
O Śivakanyā, you were not present then; therefore, support me.
O Lord, if I am to take birth, then grant me your command. (46)
Then, having been told by me, "So be it," you were born as the daughter of a Vaiśya woman named Sarayūkāsati, possessing a beautiful countenance. 47.
Indeed, you were born from the mind as the auspicious goddess named Śrī;
endowed with all auspicious marks, you dwell in the heart accompanied by Hari as your calf.
Within the heart is the sign of the golden line, equal to the light of a lamp;
and above that is the sign of Hari, four-armed and of beautiful form.
And seeing you there, golden-hued, your mother spoke to your father, who was indeed named Sāravat.
Indeed, Kamalā, rich in every splendor, exists as his daughter;
and within her heart dwells Hari, whose form is adorned with golden lines. (51)
"Therefore, it must be given to the Blessed One, the Supreme Soul Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and to no one else"—this the Vaiśya also considered to be the truth. (52)
As soon as she was born, that young woman, endowed with excellent virtues, heard from her mother and father that the son of the merchant Śoṇabhadra was the Supreme Lord.
At that time, you were given by me through my resolve to the Lord of Śrī;
thereafter, I performed a sacrifice for the sake of rescuing the deceased.
O Padmaja, having arrived there at the commencement of the rite, you were offered to me by your parents according to the sacred law, and you were accepted by me in the marriage pavilion.
Then, according to the very ritual prescribed for a sacrifice, I caused the rite to be performed;
O auspicious lady, the sacrifice was carried out by me together with you. (56)

Then those classes of departed spirits were duly summoned according to the prescribed rite by means of ancestral śrāddha offerings, the presentation of funeral cakes (piṇḍas), oblations, and rites dedicated to the gods.
All of these were indeed delivered by means of the food consisting of the grace of the sacrificial offerings;
at that time, they all became five hundred thousand beings, each possessing four arms.
Then those hungry ghosts, having turned back and become four-armed gods,
stood as attendants in that pavilion, seated upon excellent celestial chariots.
And all of them were sent by me to Vaikuṇṭha, the supreme abode;
they were liberated from there, and I remained forever in the service of my parents.
The beginningless Śrī Bhadranārāyaṇa, Śrī Puruṣottama,
and many other incarnations of mine appear there during that kalpa.
"O beloved, I know them all thoroughly because they were born to me through the power of my purpose;
remember that Sairabhadrā, who was dear to Śrībhadra and to me."
Now, O daughter of Śiva, hear of another manifest state of mine:
in the thirteenth year of Brahmā, known as Pradhyāna.
In the fourth Manu of the third Kalpa, on the southern side of Mount Meru,
in the region of Aghamarṣaṇa upon the earth, she was indeed a female celibate student (brahmacāriṇī).
But through the power of yoga, that yoginī, who was devoted to me and possessed great capacity, became known by the name Tuṅgabhadrāsana. || 61 ||
He spends half the day in my worship in a secluded place;
at midday, he brings back fruits, roots, and other produce grown from the wild trees of the forest.
Having offered [the food] to me, he eats; thereafter he performs the ancestral rites (paitrya).
He constantly worships me in the evening, the Supreme Lord, the Teacher of the World.
Having meditated at night, he indeed sleeps; in the morning, he also performs meditation.
[He does so] during bathing, meditation, recitation, fire-offerings, libations, and worship.
Whether in water, in the sky, by day, or by night, this Yoginī indeed remembers me;
through the power of long practice, she is a treasury of all accomplishments.
Just as you were Lakṣmī, so too have you become endowed with sovereignty;
devoted to the knowledge of the Self, you are Vāṇī, perfected in speech and perfected in the fulfillment of your will.

The great virtuous woman, whose body was perfected, who was free from the touch of dualities, and who was superior in every respect, was born with the power to act, to refrain from acting, or to do otherwise. (71)
She is capable of traveling through the sky and entering the bodies of others;
she possesses the power to obstruct the movement of the planets, lunar mansions, and stars. (72)
This beautiful woman was always devoted to Hari and remained ever faithful to her husband Kṛṣṇa;
she was a constant protector of her devotees and a guardian of the poor and the helpless. (73)
Devoted to serving the virtuous and dedicated to righteous deeds,
she lived thus in the great forest, always during the night;
and likewise, she encountered Rākṣasas who had gone out into the darkness for the sake of food.
For he beholds harmful beings such as bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and others. || 75 ||
Those evildoers who devour flocks of sleeping birds and beasts become like frightened animals themselves, even while awake, in the midst of darkness. (76)
Falling under the power of the unseen, they are unable to run;
and as they run, the Bali-rākṣasas seize them by force.
And every night, that virtuous woman, for the sake of warding off the suffering of others, repeatedly reflected upon those embodied beings who were crying out. (78)
Having reflected at length upon how the perpetual great suffering of embodied beings might truly perish, [he devised] that which brings about the destruction of the Rākṣasas.
He called to mind Mahālakṣmī, the fierce one who removes suffering;
commanded by me, you have become manifest before her.
The sixteen-armed maiden, bearing all weapons, with a gracious countenance, entreated you for her own daughter. 8.1.
Then you, Mānasī, having become his daughter and remaining in that hermitage, became the destroyer of all rākṣasas and spirits, and the protector of cattle and other animals. ||82||
By name, Śobhanā was known as Sarvabhadrāśrī due to her activities;
she was a female ascetic devoted to the Dharma and possessed of all powers. (83)
She was a virtuous, auspicious young woman and a yoginī who performed good deeds; while she was living in this manner, she reached a forest region. (84)
Abandoning that place, all the rākṣasas went to another forest;
and there, living beings were likewise being harmed by the rākṣasas and others. 85.
Helpless indeed, having heard that your mother—the protector of embodied beings—had come seeking you for the sake of protection, they have approached you and made their request. (86)
Your mother gave you to them for the sake of protection, and you then went there;
out of fear of you, those rākṣasas fled from that forest.
In that very forest, such violence indeed occurred;
those Rākṣasas even sought after the sacrificial animals for their own well-being. (88)
Thus, in all respects, this very invocation known as Sarvabhadrikā came into being among the worlds, for it is renowned as a performer of protection. ||89||
The mother reflected: "In this way there will be no end; my daughter does not remain at home, but dwells as a virtuous woman in the forest. (3.9.90)
"Even though I have no desire for the acquisition of wealth, it is for the sake of destroying the Rākṣasas that I shall do such a thing, so that my daughter may dwell in my house. (91)
I shall act in every way so that the strength of the Rākṣasas, by its very nature, comes to destruction, and so that night itself may never come to be.
"The strength of the Piśācas, Bhūtas, and likewise the Rākṣasas is at night;
therefore, may there be no night for you. Thus did your mother pray then. (93)
Taking water in her hand and reflecting upon it, she consecrated that water with mantras and repeatedly sprinkled it into the sky. 94.
May the movement of the luminaries and the planets, beginning with the sun, become fixed, and may there be a state of non-movement so that it may indeed be day forever. (95)
"May we not reach night, nor may the setting of the sun occur!"—saying this, they ascended to heaven, having cast down drops of water. (96)
The obstructing deities, possessing rays of all-encompassing power, then blocked the course of the sun, and the circle of constellations was obstructed. (97)
Indeed, everything attained a state of permanence; it was day forever, and that which had set never returned to the setting place again. 98.
Consequently, the evening twilight vanished and the day became exceedingly long;
everyone waited for the evening, wondering when it would finally arrive. (99)
The entire assembly of gods and men became agitated and distraught;
therefore, they then praised me, Śrīpati, the Supreme Person.
All the morning and midday rites have indeed passed away;
the gods and other beings, as well as human beings, are hungry and deprived of their seasonal offerings. (101)

The entire world, heated by the rays of the sun and sprinkled with water during the ascetic practice, has become inclined toward a state of being burnt; thus, the cool luster of the moon is no longer obtained.
Nectar is not obtained even by medicinal herbs in the forest;
the trees and other plants merely wither away when drenched by the heat of the sun.
Thus, when there was gain for one, a great loss befell the others;
through that heat, humans and the rest then fell into a state of madness. (104)
The waters of the lakes there became parched and then vanished entirely;
thus, a fierce suffering prevailed on all sides.
The strength of the Rākṣasas was destroyed and they entered Pātāla;
the Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, and others entered the caves.
For them there is no suffering at all, but rather a burning with heat;
O Supreme Lord, protect them from that unbearable suffering they have encountered. 107.
Protect, protect, O Ocean of Compassion! The three worlds have become paralyzed;
the planets and stars have ceased their movements, and the measure of the day has come to an end.
O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the night has come to an end as the world sleeps;
likewise, there is no rising of the moon, for the month has reached its dissolution. (109)
The seasons do not arise at all, and the multitudes of medicinal herbs do not bear fruit;
all coldness has vanished, and fire breaks out even in the forest.
"Protect, protect us, O ocean of compassion, O friend of the day, from the heat!"—
thus, O beloved, did all embodied beings in the three worlds praise me at that time.

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Prayer to the Supreme Lord when the Yoginī Tumagabhadrāsana obstructed the movements of the Sun and other celestial bodies during the thirteenth year of profound meditation, for the sake of liberation of those who had been consumed in the Śoṇabhadrā sacrifice in the twelfth year of the Creator [Brahmā] during the third period, the Dvāpara-santāna, in the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*."
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Then, O Śivasatyeśri, O beloved Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇi,
I ascended a celestial chariot and arrived from the abode of Akṣara.
In the assembly of the deities, the gods, filled with eagerness, performed acts of purification;
likewise, they all reported the obstruction of his path.
The great suffering born of that, which causes torment even for human beings,
and its cause have been declared by me there in that assembly.
The power of the *rākṣasas* in this world always manifests at night;
likewise, the power of the *bhūtas*, *pretas*, and *piśācas* also manifests at night.
At night, they indeed devour the sleeping creatures in the forests;
the local beings [worship] the Yoginī who resides on the Tuṅgabhadrā.
Seeking indeed for the sake of protection, she prayed to Lakṣmī;
Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa now exist as her two daughters.
Indeed, although all embodied beings were thus protected by the Rākṣasas,
nevertheless, there were many Rākṣasas in all the regions.
But when Lakṣmī departs from them, the mother remains alone;
the daughter wanders through the worlds, and no happiness is obtained by the daughter.
Therefore, it would not be night; having reflected thus on what must be done, Tuṅgabhadrikā obstructed the circle of the planets by her own power.
My devotee is a great and virtuous woman, a yoginī who is a treasure-trove of sovereignty; this indeed is the supreme cause for the obstruction of my movement.
"Therefore, O Narayani, let us go to that very place where the path by which I came has been blocked"— having reflected thus, I, along with the gods, [proceeded].
She arrived where her mother sat upon the Tuṅgabhadrā;
having observed the celestial chariots with her yogic vision, that great chaste woman [perceived them].
In his heart, he created another heaven within the midst of that forest for the purpose of welcoming [the sage],
along with various gardens containing wish-fulfilling trees that grant one's own desires.
He built rivers filled with water for his friends who were like nectar,
as well as excellent halls for bathing and other activities, and palaces worthy of the gods.
The sacrificial halls, cooking halls, and sleeping quarters were exceedingly beautiful, white like the moon and enriched with the splendor of golden pitchers. || 15 ||
There were assembly halls, suitable women’s quarters, and central pavilions;
there were well-fitted doors for garments and chests for ornaments. ||16||
There were excellent treasuries of jewels, diamonds, and gold;
and well-provided channels of clarified butter, channels of curd, and channels of milk.
Of nectars, juices, and sweet foods; of kitchens, swings, and mirrors; and of the hollows of walls containing objects of enjoyment. (18)
She likewise created beautiful houses for those well-established perfumes, as well as lamps for the streams of lightning.
Then she fashioned garlands of sandalwood, beautiful flowers, and diamonds, with ripples naturally arising from the breezes.
The Yoginī indeed caused millions of maidens to stand there holding vessels for the madhuparka offering and other items.
There were also players of musical instruments, performers of dance and song, and maidens bearing banners who resembled milk and gold in complexion. (22)
There, the virtuous lady, by means of her resolve, prepared seats for the Tuṅgabhadrā,
as well as vessels for inexhaustible offerings and bowls of saffron and unbroken grains of rice.
That young maiden performed fresh massages of his feet and other services;
there was no such new city where anything remained inferior to heaven. (24)
By the power of her own sovereignty, she indeed fashioned that which is called heaven;
and she quickly appeared at the front of the city gate for the sake of his welcome.
Seeing those manifestations, all the gods were struck with supreme wonder;
indeed, we quickly descended from the path of the sky into the forest.
At the top of the gateway, countless maidens arrived to offer a welcome;
they paid honor to all the gods by presenting them with garlands. (27)

They celebrated with shouts of victory using saffron, unbroken rice, flowers, and other offerings; they then led all the gods to their respective dwellings that had been prepared according to their requirements.
They gave them the honey-mixture (madhuparka) and other foods such as ambrosia and nectar;
they provided water for drinking, services, and massages to relieve their bodies.
All the gods were satisfied; we were all gratified by the maidens for a moment.
That [bliss] was heaven and yet another heaven; it was not lacking in anything at all.
The gods, momentarily deluded, forgot their own enjoyments;
then, at the end of that moment, the virtuous Satī, seated upon the lofty Bhadrāsana, [arose].
Indeed, she had desired to know the reason for the arrival of the gods;
and that virtuous woman, having quickly come to the assembly hall, [beheld] the deities.
Having summoned him, he indeed announced his own fortune in the presence of the gods:
"Oh! My entire lineage has been purified, and the forest has been sanctified. (33)
This surface of the earth has been sanctified, and my hermitage has been sanctified by your holy selves having come together to my home. (34)
Indeed, another heaven has been created for me today; I am blessed in every way, since there shall be heaps of ten million merits earned from former times within my home. (35)
There the gods arrive in person, accompanied by Nārāyaṇa; I stand ready for service and at the command of those who dwell in heaven. (36)
"Indeed, I am your servant; please command me.
Having spoken thus and prostrated herself before the gods seated upon their golden thrones, she [continued]: 37.
The Sun, the Moon, Venus, the planets, the best of the seven sages, the lunar mansions, Mahendra, Bṛhaspati, and also Agastya—[he saw them all]. (38)
Beholding Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa again and again, she repeatedly offered salutations;
then, looking at me once more with eyes filled with tears, she stood there in his presence.
She quickly fell at his feet and said,
"I am surrendered," to me, Hari, the Supreme Person.
Then, having been swiftly commanded by me there, Bṛhaspati informed your mother, Satī; listen to that, my dear. (41)
We are all gods who follow our devotees and have taken refuge in Nārāyaṇa; yet, due to the offense of our devotees, we flee far away in fear. ||42||
You are endowed with devotion, worthy of worship, honorable, and virtuous to us;
we bow down to these deities—be gracious, O Yoginī! (43)
O beautiful lady, you have indeed obstructed the course of the moon and the sun for the sake of destroying the night, in order to diminish the strength of the Rākṣasas. (44)
But this destruction of the world has arrived through heat;
religious rites have been obstructed, and even the seasons have gone to their dissolution. (45)
Indeed, the entire world rejoices in dependence upon the movement of the planets;
therefore, O Goddess, we beg you before your presence for the cessation of that movement. (46)
This is the divine Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person;
accompanied by tens of millions of gods, he has come here for the sake of alms. (47)
We are your guests; indeed, we desire no other object whatsoever before you.
O performer of auspicious deeds, grant us alms here. (48)
O Nārāyaṇī Lakṣmī, having heard that, your mother Satī then said to the gods and to me as well: "I too shall beg for a place of auspiciousness. (49)
I am a Yoginī for the sake of the Supreme Lord, the Lord of the Imperishable, the Lord of Śrī, Puruṣottama— the best of men— whom I worship.
If the gods surrender this eternal Supreme Lord, the Brahman, the Master, to me, I shall grant him unimpeded progress. (51)
"May there be supreme welfare for me, and likewise welfare for you;
may there also be welfare for all people, so that everything may become a source of auspiciousness. (52)
Then the gods said: "Puruṣottama is independent;
he cannot be commanded by us, for the Lord himself is the one who listens. (53)
"Janārdana will act for the sake of all happiness according to his will.
Having heard these words of the gods, O Śivaśaṃjikā, I then spoke.
I asked your mother, "O great yoginī, what do you desire?
She replied, "O Blessed One, Lakṣmī here is your maidservant; she is my daughter. (55)
She remains waiting for you; accept her as your own beloved.
This entire new heaven has been prepared as a dowry for your sake.
And these tens of millions of maidens have been prepared for your sake;
accept them all through the rite of marriage, O Supreme Person. (57)
"Having become my son-in-law, dwell in my house for eternal years.
Thus he requested; consequently, night became day, and everything was as he wished. (58)
"I am your devotee, O Lord, and you are renowned as one who is affectionate toward his devotees;
you act for the welfare of the gods, of the worlds, and of me as well. (59)
"You are capable of doing so, yet no effort is seen from you.
Accept everything, O Blessed One, and grant me your auspicious word."
"Take water in your hand and say to me here, 'I have taken it';
then indeed I shall create an obstruction to the path of all the gods."
And I, Hari, smiling at her, replied "Om";
she took the water in her hand, and the gods proclaimed victory.
Then musical instruments were played, and the deities were pleased;
at that time, showers of flowers fell upon the assembly of goddesses.
At that moment of the Abhijit muhūrta, all the maidens became joyful;
in an instant, they adorned the daughter, who was seated upon the Tuṅgabhadrā throne, with ornaments.
And he presented a decorated young woman before the onlookers;
you then placed the bridegarland around my neck there. (65)
Then your hand was placed in my hand by my mother;
and you were seated right there upon half of my throne.
Then other maidens, arriving quickly according to their instructions before me,
offered the bridegroom’s garland to me, who had assumed ten million forms.
Then, at that moment, the preceptor Bṛhaspati himself quickly recited Vedic mantras suitable for the wedding ceremony there at the prepared sacrificial pit.
And by his mere resolve, that yogi quickly caused it to be made;
and by means of Viśvakarman as the craftsman, he established the sacrificial fire.
He caused the marriage ceremony to be performed and gave the maidens in marriage, saying:
"You are the principal one, and the other ten million maidens are my wives."
All of them were obtained there by me, a yogi devoted to the Supreme Person;
those women who are here have been bestowed upon you by your mother. (71)
Those various groups of your co-wives were formerly my own wives;
they are the ones whom I married in Kāśī at the house of Śivasvāmin. (72)
There, those women at the edge were indeed virgins;
O Lakṣmī, remember all that divine history of former events.
Then, having quickly performed the circumambulation of the fire in this manner, I sat down there upon my seat; at that time, the couple was made to prosper.
All the couples were blessed with auspicious benedictions; thereafter, there was a playful exchange of saffron, unbroken rice grains, flowers, and other offerings.
Then your mother provided various kinds of foods and diverse drinks, as well as all manner of enjoyable delicacies. (76)
Then everyone became satisfied, yet midday had not passed;
this very moment was that one known by the name Abhijit.
O Lakṣmī, at that time, everything proceeded there even without the movement of the sun;
then all the gods were honored and commanded by her.
Having asked for forgiveness for her offense, the virtuous lady bowed down to the millions of gods, presented them with offerings, and then dismissed them to heaven.
I always dwelt together with you and others in that city known as Puruṣottamapura, which is called heaven itself.
At that time, O beloved, it became renowned as lasting until the end of the kalpa;
then, the destinies of the gods quickly came into being.
And at that time, the period following midday gradually proceeds;
thus am I, the Lord of Śrī Sarvabhadrā, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). 82.
Then I became the husband of the daughter of Tuṅgabhadrā, a supreme lord;
there, I had hundreds upon hundreds of beautiful sons. (83)
There were twenty very beautiful daughters and twenty [sons];
they all possess the lifespan of a kalpa, and even now they abide in the Imperishable.
"O Subhadrā, remember and behold all my liberated souls in this abode!
[There is] Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. (85)
O virtuous lady, for the sake of accomplishing the purpose of Satī, I likewise dwelt in her house; O faithful one, my devotee’s home is my own home because of my imperishable nature. (86)
"O beloved, wherever you are, there my dwelling shall always be;
and through your yoga, the yoga of others shall likewise become mine. (87)
Then, the remover of suffering and the creator of happiness for all, the Lord known as the beginningless Śrī Hari Nārāyaṇa came into being. 88.
And you, O queen, shall be known by the name Sarvabhadrāśrī;
all the others at that time shall indeed become renowned as Śrīharipriyās.
And in that very place, O beloved, there was likewise the manifestation of Me, the Supreme who have descended; and at that time, My incarnations there became innumerable.
I know all this as clearly as a precious jewel held in my hand;
remember those divine forms and the wonders created at that time. 91.
Then, when she had given birth during the night and darkness had set in,
there occurred a calamity for those Rākṣasas who were anywhere about.
I am that beginningless Śrī Harinārāyaṇa;
having gone again and again to that place, I have slain those Rākṣasas from every part of the earth.
And they, having been exiled by me, went to the worlds beginning with Atala;
indeed, protection for human beings was established by Hari in various places.
At that time, I granted forest retreats, woods, and mountain caves to the sages and ascetics for the purpose of their dwelling. 95.
The duties of householders, which bestow heaven and other rewards, have been established by me;
and devotion and the path to liberation have been established by the Supreme Self. (96)
There, I initiated crores of virtuous men and women; thus, on Mount Sarvabhadra, the path to liberation was set in motion. (97)
The state of liberation has been granted by me to you, my mother Tuṅgabhadrā;
likewise, the state of release has been granted to countless human beings.
These attendants of mine, who belong to a previous kalpa, are present here;
at that time, the sacred fords on the surface of the earth were indeed established by me there. 99.
Likewise, the paths of sacrifice that grant liberation were then set forth;
thus, O Sarvabhadra, has my manifestation been described to you.
From reading this, from hearing it, from remembering it, and from chanting my praises,
there shall be enjoyment and liberation, and the attainment of my own abode is certain.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Establishment of Dharma and Other Deeds by the Beginningless Śrī Hari Nārāyaṇa," in the third section (the Dvāpara-santāna) of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. It describes the arrival of Puruṣottama from the Imperishable Abode (*akṣara*) along with the gods at the house of Tuṅgabhadrāsana; the worship performed; the request for the planets to depart; the petition to Hari to remain as the son-in-law of Tuṅgabhadrāsana in order to accept his daughter; Hari’s acceptance; the marriage festival; the departure of the planets and others; and the establishment of dharma and other acts performed in the form of the beginningless Śrī Hari Nārāyaṇa.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, during the fourteenth year, in the seventh Kalpa of Brahmā known as Mānasa. || 1 ||
But as for how I attained manifestation in the fifth Manu-period,
that occurred from the region between the head and the hips of the Creator (Brahmā).
From that [seed], a bull among Rākṣasas named Abhidha was born;
as soon as he was born, he rushed toward the Creator to devour him.
Brahmā said: "O fool! You wish to eat in vain.
Tell me what I shall give you to ward off your hunger; choose it without delay."
Thus enlightened, consoled, and steadied for a moment,
the thief of the treasure reflected and spoke to the Grandfather (Brahmā).
"If this is so, then grant me indeed seeds to be eaten for the sake of my strength,
as well as [the power of] pervading all things and assuming subtle, innumerable forms."
Brahmā said: "Waste not the seed of embodied beings in vain;
let everything you desire be fulfilled therein, and be satisfied."
Thus addressed, that Rākṣasa, the son of Brahmā, departed from the house of Brahmā and went there, entering among the religious students (brahmacārins).
Having entered their storehouses and consumed the accumulated seeds,
those Vairājas, who were practitioners of celibacy, then ate them.
They all became weak without any apparent cause; then they came to understand the reason for their weakness. (3.11.10)
Through the power of samādhi, they indeed entered [the body] by virtue of a boon from the Unborn One; then, with the nooses of yoga, they bound that rākṣasa.
Even the Rākṣasa, filled with fear, remained within the cavities of their bodies;
rendered dependent on others and exceedingly wretched, he entreated for his release.
I shall not dwell here among those practicing celibacy anywhere,
having likewise abandoned Satyaloka and the worlds of the Vairājas.
"I shall go to the lower worlds; let them deliver me, who am wretched, from this place"—thus were the Vairāja Brahma-cārins entreated by Śīladharma.
They were released from their bonds, and he too then quickly departed from Satyaloka, leaving the sages on all sides.
Having likewise abandoned the world of the ancestors, he reached the heavenly realm;
as a thief of the treasury, he pervaded the bodies of the gods everywhere.
For the seed of the gods is indeed in vain, since they have no offspring;
there embryos are not conceived, nor does virtuous conduct prevail. (17)
"For a seed that ends merely in enjoyment is considered useless.
Having reflected thus, he entered among the gods and became a treasury-guardian.
Fearless, he ate the seed right there;
yet those gods did not even realize it was the eating of the seed.
The Rākṣasa eats seeds constantly from all the treasuries;
Indra has become a eunuch, and Bṛhaspati is a eunuch.
The Sun was born as a neuter; the Moon and Venus were neuters; and Mercury, Mars, and Saturn also became neuters. (21)
The Vasus, as well as the Rudras, the Ādityas, and the Maruts;
and Īśāna, Anala, Varuṇa, Kubera, Yama, and Nirṛti. ||22||
Vāyu, Aśvinīkumāra, and the neuter beings were born;
so too were the treasures (nidhis), the sages (ṛṣis), Dhruva, Kāma, and Manu. ||23||
The Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the hosts of world-protectors, as well as other excellent deities, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras; || 24 ||
The Kiṃpuruṣas, the messengers, and the gods became neuter;
indeed, Kośabīja, Dararākṣasa, and Kṛtavān made them neuter.
Then the entire heaven became devoid of potency, for it was like a eunuch;
the householder's life, stripped of splendor and empty of desire, went to its destruction. ||26||
The gods fell into supreme grief, rendered powerless and despondent;
they sought the cause of their plight and went to Brahmā for refuge. || 27 ||
Then they all reported their own lack of vitality;
for even this physician of the gods became devoid of vitality. (28)
"Where shall we go now for the sake of herbs and to regain our strength?
For even he who was the bestower of power has fallen into a state of weakness. (29)
The wish-fulfilling trees, the wish-fulfilling creepers, as well as the wish-fulfilling cintāmaṇi gem, all the wish-fulfilling vessels, and likewise the wish-granting cows.
Even if the daughters of the eon, the gods of the eon, and the rain of jewels at will were produced for the sake of obtaining the relics, they would nonetheless be fruitless. (3.1)
When the great dissolution has occurred and the elements have been exhausted, no one at all continues to act here;
indeed, all those who perform improper deeds become known as Kalpas.
Therefore, O Grandfather, we have come to you for refuge here. What is the cause, and how indeed have we become eunuchs? (33)
The nectar must be consumed by us in every way, even though it has become like death for us.
What shall we do? Where shall we go? We shall die, O Grandfather! (34)
Thus all the gods, being non-existent [in essence], fell at the feet of Brahmā;
Brahmā then reflected upon that deed of the thief of the seed. ||35||
Since the seed of the gods always exists in heaven according to its nature,
he who consumes that very seed of the gods shall now bear fruit.
By the granting of a boon, the thief of the seed attained victory;
he created an obstacle in heaven, and thus heaven itself turned into no-heaven. (37)
"Even though they have living husbands, these goddesses have been rendered like widows by him;
therefore, I shall seek a means by which the Rākṣasa may meet his destruction. (38)
At that moment, Brahmā, seated within the heart, became absorbed in meditation;
then, a reflection arose in his heart [that there was nothing] without Śrī Puruṣottama.
"No one shall be his destroyer, for the gods have been rendered neuter;
moreover, a boon has been granted to him by me, and thus I am not able to slay him. (3.11.40)
Therefore, together with the gods, I myself must never forget Hari—the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. 41.
The King of Kings, the soul of all, the inner self, the Supreme Lord—he alone shall lead this seed-soul to the further shore. 42.
The Grandfather quickly informed the gods:
"We shall perform a sacrificial session for Hari; he will provide us with assistance. (43)
Thus addressed, the hosts of deities gathered together in Satyaloka and performed the Brahma-sacrifice there, intent upon my ritual practice.
All of them were devoted to me, intent upon my glorification, and dedicated to my worship, hymns, recitation, and meditation. ||45||
Some then performed the preliminary rites of hymns to me,
while others, led by Bṛhaspati, performed oblations.
Some performed the recitation of garlands, while others carried out worship; likewise, some practiced meditation, and others maintained mindfulness.
Others, however, performed the worship of my form at that time;
thus all the hosts of gods performed my propitiation. 48.
There, in the uncreated abode within Satyaloka, those [gods] offered salutations to the beginningless Śrī Hari; they said, "O best of men, please come here. 49.
You are the very nature of all seeds, for you are the cause of causes;
you are the embodiment of all powers, resplendent with every capacity.
You are the root of all creation, you are the bestower of all bliss;
you are indeed composed of all beings—O Inner Self, please enter within.
Everything known as the Yuga has been created by you, the Supreme Soul; indeed, everything known as the Yuga must be protected by you, the compassionate wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
No one other than you is capable of protecting the Incarnate One;
come, save your own people, protect them, nourish them, and serve them. (53)
O you who are compassionate toward those who seek refuge, you fill the gods with bliss;
you are food, you are life, you are the womb, and you are likewise the vital breath.
You alone are the mother, the father, the protector, the nourisher, and the lord;
you are Brahmā, you are Virāṭ, Viṣṇu, Great Time, and the Supreme Puruṣa. ||55||
You are the god, you are the beloved husband and supreme lord of women;
you are happiness, you are great bliss—come hither and protect us! 56.
Thus the gods praised me, and then Hari himself, along with you,
quickly arrived at the true abode of Brahma.
When I was present there in person before the gods, I beheld the gods as being black-complexioned and devoid of strength. (58)
Just like those who are dead, or those who are diseased, or those suffering from consumption, so too have I seen all the gods, including the Sun and the others. (59)
When questioned by me, they told me the cause was the deficiency of living beings; "We do not know by whom this was done, O Blessed One, but you surely know it. (3.11.60)
O Hare, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Lord!
O Janārdana, grant protection here to those who have passed from immortality into death.
Then I said there: "Indeed, although I am endowed with power, I shall enter among you yourselves and put the rākṣasa to flight."
"Kill that most cruel thief, the son born from the thigh of the Creator!
When I had spoken thus, the gods there stood with palms joined in reverence.
O daughter of Śiva, while they were intent on meditation for a moment, I quickly entered among all the gods along with you in every way.
Having assumed the form of her husband and paralyzed the Rākṣasa,
I seized him by the throat as he took on an exceedingly subtle form.
At that time, the various forms of the Rākṣasa were destroyed by me;
even Mahendra, remaining in his original form, was held back by me.
Seeking a means of livelihood, he requested to go from heaven to the forest,
where he might dwell among plants that are devoid of fruits, flowers, and the like.
Thus commanded by me, he then went to fetch grass and other materials;
at that time, the men there became possessed of great strength.
Possessing splendor and power, these embodied beings have become as they were before;
all of them have become filled with joy and accompanied by great festivities.
Having assembled together in Indra’s abode in heaven, they then held a great festival,
having fashioned an image of me made of gold.
Together with Lakṣmī, the inhabitants of heaven honored Praśṛṅgārya and offered them milk-rice and nectar as food offerings.
Then they all performed the *ārārtrika* rite; at that time, O Lakṣmī, I, the Lord Hari, became manifest before you by my own will.
Bearing the conch, discus, mace, lotus, svastika, banner, and trident,
I became auspicious just as I abide in the imperishable abode.
The Blessed Lord, the illustrious Śrīśa, the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person, became independent,
born of neither father nor mother, and possessed of a fixed form.
The primordial Śrībīja-Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of all lords,
the Supreme Lord, was constantly entreated by the gods to remain in heaven.
The Supreme Person has always shone in the abode of Mahendra,
remaining with you until the end of the kalpa for the sake of his incarnations, together with Śrī.
In that same way, there were many other incarnations of mine;
I know them all, so remember your own self then, O Lakṣmī! (77)
O beloved, that Rākṣasa who had the form of grass became, in another kalpa,
the seeds from which plants destructive to living beings arose.
Those grasses, commands, cattle, and even humans, as well as whatever birds there were on the earth that fed upon the ground—[all these were consumed]. (79)
Then all those people indeed became devoid of seed;
thus, once again, there was suffering in the world of men.
And when that state called "seedlessness" had arisen in all ways among embodied beings, I, being entreated by men, indeed came down to the earth. (81)
He seized that Rākṣasa Bījasta with a binding noose;
trembling with fear of death, he too praised me like a wretched man. (82)
Then, as the one who granted him his domain, I established this boundary for him:
"Those men on earth who forcibly go to the wives of others," 83.
I have granted you residence among them; there, bring about your state of impotence.
You are givers of suffering to your own wives and violators of religious vows.
Bring about impotence for those who forcibly seize enjoyments;
bring about impotence for those who do not give satisfaction to their own wives and are devoted to adultery;
bring about impotence for those who perform the excision of testicles. (85)
Those who kill for the sake of women, those who destroy the efficacy of mantras, those who cause the arrest of conception, and those who cause the suppression of the fertile period; ||86||
Those who employ mantras to cause barrenness, those who bring about miscarriages,
those who destroy breast milk, those who cause the suppression of urine,
those who cause the falling away of the penis, and those who bind the vulva— ||87||
Bring about impotence in those who cause constipation, who bring about misfortune,
who practice with eunuchs, who prevent the manifestation of virility, and who create aversion toward sexual pleasure. 88–89.
For those who are attached to sensual desires, who are like cattle, and who destroy desire;
for those who are harmful, self-seeking, and wicked, and who cause the ruin of the householder's life—
for such as these, you should practice impotence.
For that reason, you remain as the seed; indeed, the Rākṣasa is the son of Brahmā. ||9 1 ||
If you abide by my command, then your [merits] shall be imperishable;
otherwise, your destruction will occur—do not indeed proceed upon a wrong path! 92.
"Devour the exhausted element of those unrighteous evildoers!"—thus have you been [commanded] by me in the world, among mankind, and in the nether regions (atala) and so forth. 93.
"Even in the worlds, places have been assigned; enter into them.
Thus indeed, O Lakṣmī, was the boundary for the Rākṣasa established by me.
From that time forth, men and women in the worlds [behave] in every way...
Possessing righteousness and observing vows, they refrained from committing the aforementioned faults;
all those householders became exceedingly happy.
And I too was honored by men, as well as by yakṣas and rākṣasas.
I indeed dwelt in many ways upon the earth as Puruṣottama himself—
the beginningless Śrībīja Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Supreme Lord.
O Lakṣmī, you indeed dwell with me as my independent consort;
thus, in the world of humans, my incarnations are truly infinite.
At that time, by the force of necessity, all of them were born as my incarnations [of] the glorious Nārāyaṇa, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow and the sovereign of the Imperishable. (99)
Those on earth who shall worship me, the glorious Nārāyaṇa, will attain both worldly enjoyment and liberation; of this there is no doubt.
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person; for those worldly beings by whom I have been worshipped here, not even a trace of suffering remains.
Those by whom the rites for the marriage of Lakṣmī have been performed in this world, even though they themselves are married,
shall attain the fulfillment of the four aims of life and a flood of bliss.

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Bījanārāyaṇa for the Protection of Heaven—Whose Seeds had been Stolen by the Rākṣasa named Kośastena during the Fourteenth Year of Brahmā in the Third Cycle of the Dvāpara Age—and the Establishment of the Boundaries of the Thief’s Dwelling," in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to my manifestation thereafter;
it occurred during the fifteenth year of Brahmā, known as Samādhi.
In the sixth Manu of the tenth Kalpa, he was born in the house of a Brāhmaṇa on the surface of the earth,
to the east of Mount Meru, in a most righteous land.
In the great section known as the Vārtika, I became the fulfiller of the hopes of my devotees;
listen, O Lakṣmī, in the Vārtakhaṇḍa there was a twice-born man named Dharmavrata.
He was a Brāhmaṇa who knew Brahman directly, an incarnation of Dharma and the gods,
constantly devoted to the six duties, and likewise possessed of the thirty-two qualities.
Endowed with ninefold devotion and worshipping the sixteen articles,
he bathed daily at the three periods of the day, and at times practiced the penance of the five fires.
He was devoted to moral conduct and vows, dedicated to ascetic observances and religious duties, intent upon the five great sacrifices, and graced by every means of spiritual accomplishment.
He was constantly devoted to the dharma of the virtuous, dedicated to his vow of fidelity to his wife,
intent on serving the good, and devoted to the goals of human endeavor.
He was devoted to self-surrender, adorned by the excellence of his virtuous nature,
learned in the scriptures, endowed with sacred knowledge, and intent upon the performance of sacrificial rites and dharma.
Thus, always endowed with such virtues, he was a supreme worshiper of the Lord;
then his wife became a virtuous woman named Bhaktivratā.
She was constantly devoted to her husband, eternally dedicated to the Blessed Lord,
intent upon her household duties, and well-versed in the laws of domestic life.
She was a virtuous woman, radiant with moral conduct and vows, free from passion and hatred,
always devoted to Kṛṣṇa Hari, and surrendered in spirit to Him.
She was a performer of religious vows, a worshiper of Hari, and a host to guests;
she was constantly immersed in the chanting of His glories and entirely devoted to her duties.
Deprived of any other speech, she was devoted solely to the chanting of the Name;
that virtuous woman was intent on the purity of ritual bathing and dedicated to the service of the holy.
In every action—whether eating, giving, or performing vows—she is dedicated to Kṛṣṇa;
she is free from the perception of faults and perceives only virtues.
At dawn, he indeed performs meditation upon Hari,
as well as worship, recitation, hymns of praise, the chanting of the rosary, and the offering of oblations.

At midday, she was devoted to the performance of the *ārārtrika* rite, the offering of food (*naivedya*), the presentation of water, and betel-leaf; likewise in the evening, she remained intent upon those various services.
In this manner, she indeed performs all the vows during the month of Kārttika;
likewise, she performs the ritual bath in Māgha and also gives gifts in Vaiśākha.
When her supreme Lord and husband was thus somehow stained by the violation of his wife's devotion, Bhaktisundarī immediately performed an act of expiation. 18.
Indeed, that Goddess Bhakti herself exists in such a manner;
she always remains radiant with devotion, her life being my very devotion.
Thus, while in the bloom of youth, she gradually obtained here in this world a son from her husband, who was like a god, marked with the signs of the conch, the discus, and other emblems.
He bore upon his forehead a naturally produced mark like the moon—brilliant, a quencher of heat, and bringing peace to the sight. 21.
Having obtained a son, the father celebrated a great festival for the birth of his son;
even the Brahmin, filled with the wealth of sovereignty through devotion to the Lord, [was filled with joy]. ||22||
He celebrated a great festival for his son's birth with the ritual gifting of gold and cows,
as well as the distribution of diamonds and other gems, along with gifts of food and precious stones.
During the great festival celebrating the birth of his son, he gave gifts of fields and groves, as well as houses, and bestowed wealth in charity.
During the course of the year, he performed all the purificatory rites according to the prescribed rules;
when the year was complete, the father celebrated the birthday festival.
When the thirteenth month was complete, a celestial chariot then arrived from the sky,
descending from Vaikuṇṭha and adorned with divine attendants.
The attendants quickly took that boy, who was afflicted by fever and attended to and protected by his mother and father, and carried him away. (27)
Possessing a divine body, divine luster, and four divine hands, and resplendent with a necklace and a crown, he appeared in the presence of the corpse. (28)
For a moment, out of affection, both the mother and the father wept; likewise, the kinsmen, friends, and neighbors wept because of his death. (29)
The attendants, having turned back for a moment, said to the son and the father:
"One who is devoted to piety should not weep on account of him."
The fruitfulness of human birth is attained by him who has reached the feet of Hari;
for that which was to be attained has indeed been attained by him—the imperishable state.
Therefore, a festival for him should be celebrated; grief should never be felt. Only at the end of many births does devotion to Hari arise. (32)
By the power of your great merit and through your devotion to your parents,
you two parents have become such givers of liberation to your son here on this earth.
Having attained birth through those two, he indeed proceeds toward liberation;
there is sorrow in falling into *māyā*, but certainly no sorrow in liberation.
If, having become a son, one should attain the supreme state of the Blessed One, there is no gain like this; for he indeed grants liberation to his parents. (35)
He who, having attained birth, goes to the abode of Janārdana, has thereby delivered his parents as he crosses the ocean of worldly existence. ||36||
That son is truly a son who saves himself and causes others to cross over;
he is not considered a son who sinks down and causes others to sink. 37.
Therefore, taking him with us, we shall go to the abode of the Blessed One;
for by the grace of the Blessed One, the state of the Blessed One is attainable by everyone. (38)
Thus addressed by the attendants, the virtuous woman, devoted to the vow of bhakti, said to them:
"Tell me, how does he depart after casting off his body in childhood? (39)
Having heard this, the attendants said: "Listen, O beautiful lady of good fortune!
Indeed, yogis who have fallen from yoga are born in the house of a devotee. (3.12.40)
At the time of abandoning the previous body, by the power of latent impressions (vāsanā), one indeed takes on a new birth in the house of a devotee. 41.
Whether it be for wealth or the earth, for a field or the sky, for food or drink, for a vehicle or livelihood, for a woman, a son, or a home—(there is no desire). ||42||
In one's daughter, husband, people, kinsmen, servant, slave, or circle of friends; in learning or in art, in fame, in an enemy, in happiness, or in one's family— (43)
Whether they are dispassionate or deeply attached, whether in desire or in destructive greed, in quarrel or even in enmity, or in regard to form, taste, and pleasure; 44.
In a country, a village, heavenly bliss, fragrance, touch, or even sound; in enjoyment, disease, as well as in sovereignty or in preeminent prosperity—(45)
Whether in a sacred seat (dhiṣṇya), in authority, in measurement, in weight, or in honor—whatever kind of latent impression (vāsanā) a being possesses, in that very state it is born. (46)

In the vessel [of the guru], in the propitiation of Śrī Hari, in services and other ritual acts, toward one's mother or father, and likewise toward the deity, the spiritual preceptor, and the saintly; ||47||
Whatever kind of contemplation one has, that very thing arises for them in that regard:
"This son of yours was a devotee of Hari and a servant in his previous birth. (48)
Devoted to serving the virtuous and dedicated to the service of the gods,
he was a Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇa and a disciple of Dharmavrata.
"O beautiful one, listen to the grief that arose when his death arrived:
'Having abandoned my teacher, the giver of knowledge, I am departing, having met my end. (3.12.50)
Having abandoned my vow of righteousness, where shall I go now? My life-breaths have departed while I was still residing within your belly. (51)
"This son born to you is the great ṛṣi Prājāpatya;
having taken birth, he indeed possesses the memory of his former lives. (52)
Everything dissolves right here and proceeds to the imperishable abode;
your birth, held within your home, is purifying and bestows the Lord. (53)
This purifying prasāda has been consumed by him;
it flows forth within him, and even his resolve consisting of passion and hatred has here been exhausted.
This devotee is purifying and attains the abode of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow;
for those who fall from yoga are born as short-lived children.
For the devotees and the liberated women who have fulfilled their resolve, you shall become their offspring, either within a year or even within two years. (56)
Having completed everything except for the remainder, they go to the supreme state;
in this manner, O Prājñāyana, your son was born as a brahmin.
Having fulfilled his own nature, he indeed proceeds to Vaikuṇṭha;
marked with the conch, discus, and other signs, he goes to the auspicious abode of Hari.
One attains that state of fearlessness; do not grieve, O Bhaktivṛttikā!
All other gifts do not equal even a sixteenth part of the gift of fearlessness. (59)
Having spoken thus, the attendants, whose very nature was devotion, bowed to their mother and,
having bowed to their father Dharmavrata, departed for Vaikuṇṭha.
The parents, devoted to righteousness and piety, were freed from grief;
they became joyful through the attainment of liberation for their son. (61)
Then, in the course of time, a second son was born to them;
he too met his death in the same manner when two years had passed.
The attendants arrived, seated upon their celestial chariots, to lead him away;
likewise, they once again dispelled the grief of his parents.
Then, in the course of time, a third son was born to them;
he too, when two years had passed, met his death in the same manner.
The fourth and the fifth also died within three years;
in this way, their hundred and ten younger brothers passed away.
Within three hundred years, all those boys indeed died; they were all led away by the attendants to the abode of Hari.
The ignorant people, possessed of latent tendencies, proclaim it to be the fruit of sin;
but the wise devotees proclaim it as the merit of Hari, for that is indeed His grace.
That from whose womb beings take birth and thereafter attain the supreme abode;
that which is equal to the state of being virtuous toward one's parents; and that which indeed bestows liberation upon embodied souls—[this is the greatness of the Mother]. 68.
That house in which birth was attained and the door to liberation opened, that house and those two parents are divine—Śrī Nārāyaṇa himself. (69)
Seeing the liberation of their sons, the parents attained great joy; yet, for this reason, a sense of degradation was observed in worldly conduct. (3.12.70)
