She was adorned with a crown resplendent with shimmering golden stars, and wore golden earrings in the shape of makaras encrusted with jewels. 43.
Her auspicious face shines with a gentle smile as radiant as the light of ten million moons;
her well-developed chest is adorned by a row of golden necklaces. 44.
Abounding in the splendor of arms like serpents, adorned with the Kaustubha gem and necklaces, marked with the Śrīvatsa sign, and beautifully graced by armlets. 45.
Adorned with golden bracelets and graced by the conch, discus, and other [emblems],
she wears yellow garments and a tunic enriched with yellow and red coverings.
She was endowed with a golden girdle, beautified by golden anklets, joined with a golden chain, and resplendent with golden armlets. ||47||
Her fingertips are adorned with finger-rings set with golden bands;
she is resplendent with the fish, trident, banner, bow, arrow, and svastika [mudrās]. 48.
Adorned with a pair of lips resembling ripe bimba fruits, she is auspicious;
she is endowed with eyes as restless as fish and long eyes like lotus petals. 49.
Her nose was like a sesame flower; her cheeks had the luster of two moons;
and the drawing of her two eyebrows was worthy of being the abode of ten million Cupids. (3.17.50)
Less than sixteen years of age, yet adorned with a line of beard;
with well-developed shoulders and palms as soft as land-lotuses. (51)
Richly colored like waves of lac, beautiful with thighs like the trunks of elephants, soft as a *śirīṣa* flower, and radiant with moon-like nails. (52)
Adorned with three folds on her abdomen and a beautiful navel, she is overflowing with all-encompassing bliss;
she has lotus-like eyes, is tranquil, and is radiant with wrists as lovely as lotus buds.
Her knees are well-rounded and full, her shanks are perfectly cylindrical and straight, and her hips are exceedingly beautiful, abounding as they do with the dwelling place of all desires. (54)
She is filled with all fragrance, beauty, and sweetness;
she is replete with all affection, gentleness, magnanimity, and friendship. (55)
You are the treasury of the wonders of all sovereignty, qualities, and powers,
resplendent with Lakṣmī, who is enriched by every kind of ornament.
Accompanied by many attendants, served by circles of liberated ones, and saluted by female liberated ones, my form was seen. (57)
She was fanned with a most divine fan by Lakṣmī, who stood to her left, adorned with every ornament and beauty, possessing a single head.
She was beheld with eyes that were beautiful, endowed with the lovely splendor of excellent garlands of lotuses, and capable of discerning the innermost depths of the eyes [of others]. (59)
Beheld with wonder by all the gods and others, for she is indeed unprecedented—the eternal form of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (3.17.60)
Then they all praised me, having bowed to me as such a Lord;
seeing me with only one head, they reached a supreme conclusion.
The gods and others indeed offered praise and then performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana);
and I instructed them directly so that they might become like me.
O gods and others, may you here hear me in my true form:
I am eternally two-armed within the imperishable abode that is higher than the highest.
He has a single face and a divine form, yet he can assume many bodies at will;
he may have four arms, or a hundred arms, or even a thousand hands.
I also possess such a face as that which obstructs my purpose;
yet, by my own will, various forms come into being. (65)
Having accomplished the appropriate task, I shall withdraw that form;
for you have propitiated me, O Supreme Lord, for the sake of reaching a final decision. (66)
Thus, I am exactly as my true nature is, and I am the object of experience here;
this is my true nature, and it should be meditated upon without interruption.
That which indeed does not undergo dissolution even during the destruction of infinite creations,
nor does it attain invisibility— that is truly my own form.
Let them hold this in their hearts and worship it incessantly; let them honor and praise this my eternal and auspicious form. (69)
Now I shall indeed become invisible to you who look here;
having completely abandoned your dispute, worship me always in this manner. (3.17.70)
When the gods, humans, and great sages had spoken thus,
mental resolves arose within them to establish me upon the earth.
They said to me, "O Supreme Lord, for the sake of liberating embodied beings, please always establish your residence in the world of men, O Blessed One. (72)
Likewise, the path of Dharma and liberation shall come to embodied beings through service;
therefore, O Śrī Puruṣottama, show this compassion. (73)
Then, out of compassion for embodied beings, I reflected that through association with me, there might come ultimate welfare and supreme well-being. (74)
Through my yoga, they shall become my devotees in age after age; and they shall also be virtuous ones, effecting the attainment of dharma and liberation. ||75||
Through their union, the liberation of living beings will come to pass;
therefore, I must remain upon the earth together with these purifying men. (76)
And having assumed a human form with four faces according to the species of beings,
you must likewise remain together with Lakṣmī, who also possesses four faces.
Having thus resolved, O Lakṣmī, I then said "So be it" to the people and the sages; at that time, all became wicked.
They worshipped with supreme devotion using flowers, unbroken grains of rice, and excellent sandalwood paste.
Then, I, the four-faced one, reflected upon my parents who were on the ground.
Then, O Lakṣmī, she became invisible along with you;
and all the gods and humans likewise departed for their respective worlds. (3.17.80)
Then I appointed the auspicious and righteous Brahmin Kṛṣṇayaśas as my father, and I became his mind-born son.
And when my wife Prabhāvatī had occupied the four-faced one, I appeared right there as a son seated upon Prabhāvatī’s lap. (82)
With eight arms, the form of his father, four faces, and exceedingly beautiful, divine drums resounded and a rain of flowers fell at that time. (83)
Then shouts of "Victory! arose from the sages, and there were their blessings:
"Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, Śrī-Puruṣottama! (84)
Immediately upon birth, I myself became the four-faced Narayana, from youth onwards, for the sake of fulfilling all desires.
Therefore, commanded by me, you shall indeed become the daughter born from the mind of Mākṣikī, the wife of the brahmin Madhuvidya. 86.
And you yourself were born as Ramā, four-faced and eight-armed, endowed with all auspicious marks and radiant with every excellent quality. 87.
Born as soon as you were conceived, you are a young woman by virtue of the law of the age;
O Supreme Goddess, you have been fashioned by your parents for my sake.
And according to the rites of marriage, I wedded you, an excellent maiden, who possessed the sovereignty over all the Smaras of former times. (89)
Then the creation, possessing four faces, having approached me, Hari,
and having approached you as well, being of equal nature, served us both equally.
Then, O lady of auspicious countenance, she remained with you until the end of the kalpa for the sake of undertaking service to the creations of the Four-faced One.
O beloved, there have been innumerable incarnations of mine together with yours;
throughout various ages and kalpas, such [manifestations] have existed.
They are the performers of all that is auspicious and the fulfillers of all intentions;
I know all of this entirely, whereas others do not know it in its totality.
Remember your own birth as the four-faced Śivadevi-Śrī; at that time, you indeed attained the names Pramā, Akṣikī, and Ramā. 94.
In that kalpa, your form and my four-faced form existed here in these temples, and likewise in the heavens and other realms. (95)
Indeed, such forms existed in every house upon the earth;
those two-armed people who worshipped me went to the divine abode. (96)
Then, having assumed a divine form and abandoned the four-faced corpse, and having quickly cast off the eight-armed body, she became once again single-faced. 97.
Led by my attendants, they attained the abode that is beyond the unmanifest and supreme;
and at that time, the names of their mouths became the names of the directions. 98.
The faces of the Brahmins were indeed renowned for possessing the knowledge of dharma, dispassion, and devotion; they were truly the bestowers of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. 99.
For Kṣatriyas, it contains [teachings on] conciliation, gifts, sowing dissension, and punishment;
for Vaiśyas, however, it contains [teachings on] dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
And for all of them, there were well-known pleasures consisting of truth, compassion, sacrifice, and austerity, which indeed yielded their respective fruits.
For the slaves, there was satisfaction in their resolve and service, as well as the desire for your favor; thus did those very faces become the givers of fruit when they were created at that time.
Thus, my manifestation together with you occurred at that time, O son of the illustrious Śivasvāmin; this has been declared as a source of happiness. 103.
From reading, hearing, and remembering this, there is the destruction of sins;
the attainment of desired supernatural powers occurs, and the acquisition of liberation arises.
Indeed, the fruits of all sacred fords, the fruits of all sacrifices, and the fruits of all vows are produced here; of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Beginningless Four-faced Nārāyaṇa, who is like the Creator himself and accompanied by Pramā, Kṣikī, and Ramā, during the twentieth year of the Creator in the third period, the Dvāpara-santāna," in the glorious Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, to my supreme and virtuous narrative;
it took place during the twenty-first year of the Creator, the year of the Vedas.
Furthermore, in the eightieth kalpa, long ago during the twelfth Manu-period,
there was a twice-born man named Puṇyarāta, who was devoted and solely intent upon devotion.
His wife was named Rādhanikā, and she was devoted to her husband;
the couple daily performed ritual bathing, meditation, and my worship.
They also performed devotional service and the sacrifice of recitation (japayajña) in groups,
and they occasionally engaged in the drinking of unbroken wine.
They performed my worship with one hundred thousand tulasī leaves during the month of Kārtika, and for my sake, they observed vows and their concluding ceremonies.
They prepared offerings of various kinds of most delicious new grains,
and likewise they celebrated the spring festival during the month of Māgha.
Filled with devotion, they also performed the festival of the flower-swing and the religious observances of the month of Vaiśākha, as well as the restrictive vows during the Cāturmāsya period.
Eagerly, they both constantly performed service to virtuous men and women; from those virtuous ones, they heard [the teachings] during the course of their conversations.

The gift of food is proclaimed to be the highest gift; the gift of clothing is proclaimed to be superior to the gift of food; and the gift of wealth is proclaimed to be superior to the gift of clothing. (9)
The gift of cows is proclaimed to be the supreme gift after the gift of wealth;
and the gift of a maiden is proclaimed to be the supreme gift after the gift of cows.
The gift of a daughter is a supreme gift, and the gift of a son creates a noble lineage;
the gift of land is proclaimed as a gift superior even to the gift of a son. (1.1)
The gift of health is superior to the gift of land;
the gift of a house together with a means of livelihood is more excellent than the gift of health. (12)
The gift of merit is considered superior to the gift of a house with its virtuous inhabitants;
and the gift of righteous action is considered supreme over the gift of merit. (13)
The gift of knowledge is always superior to the bestowal of Dharma and ritual acts;
and the gift of devotion surpasses all gifts, including the gift of knowledge. (14)
The gift of devotion is superior even to the gift of heaven, for it bestows eternal bliss;
if that gift is further endowed with devotion, it then grants the gift of fearlessness.
All gifts are delightful and bestow rewards in the next world;
indeed, whatever gifts there may be, they are all equal to the gift of the Cosmic Egg (Brahmāṇḍa). || 16 ||
They do not equal even a sixteenth part of the gift of fearlessness to living beings;
[this gift] which is fearless regarding time, illusion, and likewise regarding karma. (17)
Liberation from evil, from the messengers of Yama, from deceitful people, from enemies, as well as from latent impressions and from bonds, is the granting of fearlessness. (18)
Liberation, which consists of non-return, is superior to that; among those, liberation in the same world (sālokya) is indeed excellent, while that called equality of power (sārṣṭi) is more weighty.
Then, that which is called Sārūpya (having the same form) is declared to be even more excellent and endowed with bliss;
and then, indeed, that which is called Sāmīpya (proximity) is the most excellent of all. (3.18.20)

And that which is called *sāyujya* (union) is the most excellent of all, for there exists no other state higher than it, which is characterized by the granting of fearlessness and is preeminent as the crowning glory. ||21||
Therefore, among all gifts, the gift of fearlessness is superior;
it is such as has never been offered or performed by others in former times.
"Such a gift alone should be given here, and it must consist of fearlessness"—having thus heard this nectar-like discourse from the mouths of the virtuous, [he then acted]. ||23||
Puṇyarāta and his wife deliberated repeatedly:
"In this world, those who are wealthy give gifts such as wealth and other things. (24)
We must give that which has not been given by anyone before;
we must indeed give such as has never been given by others. (25)
Then, having deliberated thus, those two perform the act of bestowing devotion;
and they themselves always grant knowledge and devotion to those who give them.
Thus, as those months and even years passed by,
they became devoted to the practice of breath control (prāṇāyāma) and dedicated to the performance of yoga.
Then those two ascetics, capable of restraining their vital breaths, established in meditative absorption, devoted to Brahman, and having renounced the pleasures of the body, [remained there]. (28)
The two Videhas were liberated while living, free from attachment to Māyā, having exhausted their binding karma, and having burnt away all desires; they were true yogins. ||29||
Devoted solely to the dharma of granting fearlessness to others,
they constantly deliberated upon how liberation might be attained by embodied beings.
In this matter, there must be absolute [renunciation], and that which should be performed is giving alone;
for there is indeed no gift equal to the gift of fearlessness (abhaya-dāna).
And the gift of fearlessness must be bestowed upon all living beings.
In this world, the granting of liberation to each individual may arise from instruction;
likewise, through the bestowal of mantras, it may arise for hundreds and thousands.
Furthermore, there is great effort required therein for those who rely upon the means of accomplishment.
Therefore, regarding Hari, who is indeed the goal for us both,
an effort must be properly made to attain that Supreme Lord by humans dwelling on the earth as well as those connected to them. (33–34)

In this way, even for animals, liberation would be possible; thus the Supreme Lord is worthy of being sought after, whether in a single age, or in ten ages, or while Manu remains, or when another Manu is established.
Śrī Hari himself is directly present here; he shall grant eternal liberation to all human beings, according to their respective efforts. 36.
"Whether great or small, this must be accomplished with this very body"—having thus resolved, O Lotus-born One, those two were filled with devotion. (37)
Standing near my image, they both took a firm vow:
"From this day forward, the auspicious sacrifice of recitation (japayajña) to Śrī Hari must be performed. (38)
Having made one's dwelling in the open air day and night, eating only once a day, one should consume only a single kind of fruit and drink water only once a day. (39)
Indeed, until Hari himself appears, one must always maintain virtuous conduct and observe vows, and one must dwell in the forest. (3.18.40)
Having thus undertaken these vows and observances, the couple indeed performed supreme penance, beginning from the day of the start of the Yuga.
Capable of sustaining the body and likewise abandoning it at will,
and capable of obstructing time itself, they both became conquerors of death.
Constantly worshipping me and devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa,
they became dear to me as well, being entirely intent on devotion to me.
For the sake of its protection, I have stationed Sudarśana there in that forest by its side in an invisible form, to dispel the fear of Time and other such dangers. (44)
Forest fires, excessive rain, violent storms, extreme cold, snowfall, or constant obstacles such as cruel animals [are encountered]. (45)
For the four yugas, filled with lack of fortitude, are warded off by my discus, which provides protection for my devotees. (46)
When that time had passed, I, in the form of a brahmin, went before them and said at midday, "Give me alms," in their presence. (47)
Rising quickly, one should offer water, fruit, and a seat to the Brahmin, as well as water for the feet, the honey-mixture (madhuparka), prostrations, and an apology for any offenses. ||48||
Having said, "May Nārāyaṇa be gracious," it was indeed offered by me;
and having received it, I said to those two devotees, "May prosperity be yours always. (49)
Having said "Om," they both spoke to me: "Grant us the most excellent blessings so that the highest good may come to all embodied beings here. (3.18.50)
I have said that sinful souls are composed of latent impressions;
their welfare may also be achieved through austerity, yoga, and meditative absorption. (51)
"Indeed, this cannot be accomplished in a short time, but through practices performed over a long period.
Then the two of them said to Hari, "When indeed will you meet with us here? (52)
For the sake of liberating all human beings, when will he appear in person? For the sake of releasing all embodied beings, when will Kṛṣṇa appear? (53)
Having heard that, I said to you both: "Hari has indeed appeared for the sake of liberating all humanity, now that half of the Manvantara has passed. (54)
When this manvantara has fully elapsed, Hari will appear here in person through the power of austerity and devotion, for the sake of the liberation even of those born as animals.
"The Lord will be found here; I speak according to my understanding.
Having heard these words of Sīma, both of them were filled with joy.
They fell at my feet and worshipped me again and again;
they bowed repeatedly, even then licking the dust of my feet.
Having recognized that "this is Nārāyaṇa," they became eager and said to me, "Grant us a vision of your own true form. (58)
Then, being pleased, I granted him my divine vision,
appearing with a serene countenance and bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
They massaged his feet and performed various acts of worship to him, whose face possessed the luster of many millions of moons and who was adorned with ornaments.
Those two were described for the sake of obtaining boons, and they then made their request for the benefit of human beings dwelling on earth as well as those connected to them.
O Lord, we both desire at once the supreme liberation for all living beings—this best of boons, which grants fearlessness to all. (62)
"O Lord, ocean of mercy, grant [us] this; O Keśava, be gracious!
Thus did Nārāyaṇa and Śrī pray for the supreme boon. (63)
I have said this for the sake of bringing about your liberation;
I have indeed come here quickly, so come along with me.
"O Lord, there is no doubt that our liberation will come from your yoga;
indeed, the deliverance of living beings and human beings is already known. (65)
"Without our lute we shall not go; do as you wish, O affectionate one.
Hari said, "So be it; even such a desire will indeed be fulfilled by time at some point. (66)
"Through your asceticism and devotion, all will come to pass; I shall go, and may it be well with you both.
Having spoken thus, O lotus-born one, I quickly vanished from sight.
Those two, being pleased, their desires fulfilled, and their joy increasing,
remembered me in the form of a brahmin and showed me devotion.
Constantly possessing fresh enthusiasm until the end of forty yugas, they performed penance and devotion; then I returned once more.
The Blessed Lord himself, bearing the conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
spoke to the two ascetics who were my devotees and whose bodies were emaciated.
"Having led all humans dwelling upon the earth, go to my imperishable realm;
I have come here to bestow such a fruit of your asceticism. (71)
"Accept the perfection of your asceticism, which grants liberation to human beings.
Then, having worshipped me and served me with the highest devotion, those two [spoke]. (72)
They both said, "O Blessed One, here in every house of men there are cows, horses, elephants, camels, goats, mules, and deer. (73)
The uraṇas, wild beasts, lions, gavayas and the like—whatever animals there are, as well as the parrots and other birds; ||74||
"Furthermore, let all those such as reptiles and others who are useful to human beings attain liberation together with mankind; act accordingly. (75)
"Abandoning them, we two do not desire liberation for human beings at all.
Having heard this, I said to the two of them, "It shall indeed come to pass after a long time. (76)
Then, having reached the appointed time, the two of them became filled with joy;
and after receiving their worship, I quickly vanished from sight.
Then, likewise devoted to austerity and devotion, the two of them were born as those affectionate toward me, devoid of water and food. (78)
The penance of those two became complete, and their devotion then reached perfection;
though formerly known as Tṛṇa and Mṛttika, they now possessed physical forms born of their asceticism.
When the period of a Manvantara had passed, those two came into being for my sake,
for the benefit of embodied beings and for the liberation of those with animal bodies.
For the sake of bestowing fearlessness, they both renounced their own happiness;
indeed, for the sake of bestowing yoga upon all living beings, they did so in every way. (8.1)
The two of them, devoted to austerity, became like stone and clay;
then I suddenly arrived there along with Lakṣmī and my attendants.
Endowed with all the requisites for worship and the like,
the lords, sages, gods, and seers indeed approached;
then all the sacred fords (tīrthas) came to that place where I was at that time.
And then the drums of the gods were sounded in the sky. ||84||
Then there was a fine rain of sandalwood and a rain of nectar; and the cries of "Victory! from the spirits arose on every side, all around. (85)
Then, by my will, countless celestial chariots belonging to the inhabitants of heaven arrived, and millions of liberated souls also came together.

There were tens of millions upon tens of millions of celestial palaces, as well as tens of millions upon tens of millions of lords, tens of millions upon tens of millions of gods, and tens of millions upon tens of millions of great sages. ||87||
The sky was entirely pervaded by those celestial chariots.
"I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). 88.
Descending from their celestial chariot onto the ground at the waters of the Brahma-lake,
they indeed stayed upon the earth in a small grove of clay within that land of asceticism.
As I cast it there with my joined palms, a great fire,
composed of divine splendor and surpassing even the brilliance of heaven, burst forth from the earth.
Then, from the midst of that splendor, there arose the divine body of the twice-born;
a most beautiful form bearing the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus. 91.
His wife was likewise like one liberated from the syllable (akṣara), possessing a form like that of Muktānikā and resembling Ramā herself. ||92||
Both of them, whom I addressed regarding security, liberation, and happiness, replied out of compassion alone: "We have reached the further shore by relying on you. (93)
If those two who are fit for liberation are born together with humans, or with beings related to them such as animals, birds, and so forth, [they are still liberated]. (94)
Then, O Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa, Supreme Lord, higher than the highest:
grant me liberation; the time for my mantra has passed because of your word. ||95||
O Supreme Lord Mādhava, grant the gift of [these] celestial chariots;
for indeed, innumerable vimānas have arrived. (96)
Salutations to you who are present here even in tens of millions of forms;
salutations to you, the self of all beings, O Supreme Lord—let there be salutation to you! (97)
O Lord of syllables, inner controller, fulfiller of the aims of devotees! Grant liberation to embodied beings, and indeed, quickly grant what I have requested. 98.
O Blessed One, forgive my offense; indeed, by me, through asceticism and devotion, you were restrained for a period of Manu for the sake of the liberation of all beings. (99)
O Keśava, hundreds of millions of offenses have been committed by me;
having forgiven them all, O Mādhava, lead all embodied beings to their respective abodes.
"Lead me to whatever abodes are appropriate, for you are independent;
O Lord, I have no attachment here to heaven, nor to truth, nor to the imperishable."
O Supreme Lord, fulfill all that I have requested;
my desire for the gift of fearlessness from countless beings has been fulfilled by you, O Master.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Arrival of Śrī Puruṣottama Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by all the lords, gods, and others, for the fulfillment of the desires of the two brahmins Rādhanika and Puṇyarāta—who were performing penance for the sake of the liberation of all beings on earth during the twenty-first year of the Creator in the third cycle of the Dvāpara Age, once the Manvantara period had passed. || 18 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī; therefore I am Puruṣottama. Having observed the merit, devotion, and austerity of the two devotees born of Manu and Kālā, [I have come]. || 1 ||
In order to fulfill the heart's desire previously requested by the two yogis, who have become divine vessels of my grace and have attained lordship. || 2 ||
On the earthly realm, whatever men, women, and eunuchs there may be—
children, the elderly, and the young, as well as the widowed and the householders— (3)
Having simultaneously endowed all those renunciants dwelling in the forest with divine bodies on every side, he established them within celestial chariots.
I dispatched some to Śvetadvīpa, some to the Ocean of Milk,
some to various heavens, and some to Janaloka, Maharloka, and Tapoloka.
Some indeed [they sent] to Satyaloka, some to Vaikuṇṭha;
some to the realms of Virāja, and some to the abode of Viṣṇu.
To some he granted eternal Kailāsa; to some, the unmanifest state (Avyākṛta-pada);
to some, the immortal abode (Amṛta-dhāma); and to others, the supreme Vaikuṇṭha.
Some [he sent] to Goloka itself, some to the supreme imperishable realm (akṣara),
and some to various abodes, whichever were appropriate for each.
I, the illustrious Puruṣottama, led them all to those [abodes];
and then as for the beasts, birds, wild animals, and so forth— || 9 ||
Reptiles and other creatures as well, which depend on humans for their livelihood—all those dwelling in villages or forests—are dependent upon human beings. (3.19.10)
Immediately, tens of millions of gods were made to possess divine bodies with two arms;
having placed them all within celestial chariots, [he departed].
Heaven, the world of men, the great realm, truth, the solar, the lunar, the domain of Varuṇa, the fiery, the ascetic, that of the Ṛṣis, and even the abode of Virāj.
I sent forth the appropriate souls according to the desires of my devotees;
having burnt away their worldly karmas, I liberated those souls dwelling on earth.
Without causing them to reach the divine worlds, according to their expectations and through my grace,
O Lakṣmī, this compassion has been exercised by me in accordance with the devotion of my followers.
The world of mortals was sent away for the most part to the worlds of the blessed;
the earth became empty, devoid of those in human form.
Likewise, by the power of the devotion and asceticism of those engaged in that yoga, as well as of the cattle and other beings, the entire earth became empty through their symbolic forms.
Long ago, living beings were liberated by my devotee, a brahmin rich in merit and a yogi, through the giving of fearlessness.
When another woman, a devotee of mine and a wife of a brahmin, likewise performed worship,
I, who am compassionate toward all creation, then attained renown.
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, being subservient to His devotees, has indeed brought about the highest welfare through His sovereignty. (19)
Then I indeed became the Lord Nārāyaṇa, Anādiśrīkṛpā.
Listen, Lakṣmī, to that devotee Puṇyarāta and likewise to Satī. (3.19.20)
Having granted Rādhanikā a divine body, both of them having become the very form of Viṣṇu,
I placed them in my own celestial chariot and sent them to my own imperishable abode.
Then Brahmā and the other gods, seeing that the surface of the earth was devoid of people,
prayed most earnestly for the creation of humans once again.
And for the sake of creating cattle and other beings, as well as for my own abiding until the end of the kalpa, I then dwelt upon the earth in this world, possessing a divine form. (23)
Together with you, Lakṣmī, who possess a divine form, that best of men performed the mental creation once again, exactly as it was before.
By the will of the Creator, I dwelt until the end of the kalpa among humans, animals, birds, and indeed all embodied beings.
In this way, liberation was brought about, and again creation was brought about;
remember all this, O Queen Śivā, for others do not know it at all.
Indeed, my incarnations are innumerable, occurring according to my purpose;
O beloved, I know them all within those years and kalpas.
"And you, O Lakṣmī, became compassionate toward me at that time.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, has my manifestation been described to you at that time.
Now, listen as I also describe another year:
during the two-hundred-kalpa period known as Rudra’s year of Brahmā. (29)
There was a devoted Cāraṇa named Rakṣālaya,
and his wife was a Cāraṇī named Santayoginī.
Having fallen from yoga, they were born with the memory of their former lives;
and with devotion, they worshipped me, Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord. (31)
Devoted to bathing and devotion, and dedicated to the service of holy men and women,
they lived in Mahiṣī-govraja, which was thick with trees.
In a village near a small town, beautiful with grass, fodder, and the like, illuminated by the open sky, on the bank of the river Kāmakalpā; || 33 ||
Constantly tending cattle for their livelihood through curd, ghee, and other products, they wore woolen garments and remembered Hare Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (34)
And without first offering to me a plate filled with *polikā* cakes and curd,
they do not eat in the morning, nor at midday, nor likewise at night.
Having gathered water, leaves, fruits, and flowers—beautiful, excellent, and pleasing—from the wild trees themselves, I offer them to you. (36)
To those virtuous guests who come to his own hut,
he offers milk-rice, ghee, curd, and cakes.
Being contented, they perform the chanting of the names of Hari;
day and night they either go about as they please or remain where they are.
Virtuous yoginīs who are deities of truth also arrive there; even those who are celibate students come to that famous abode of the Cāraṇas. (39)
Just as a temple is, so was that village consisting of cow-pastures; through the residence of virtuous, chaste, and noble women, it became equal to a temple of the gods. (3.19.40)
Where there is constant devotion to me, where there is perpetual worship of me, and where there is constant glorification of me—there is my temple. 41.
Thus, O lotus-born one, although I am beyond the reach of the senses, I dwell eternally there in the hearts of the devoted, as well as in their homes and in the sacred mandala.
I dwell even in sacred fords (tīrtha) for the sake of the welfare of my devotees;
every day I eat, sleep, dance, drink, and rejoice.
I dwell, I laugh, I endure, and I enter; whatever you say, sing, show favor toward, or worship, [I do likewise]. 44.
I bathe, I purify myself, I perform rituals, I reflect, and I even sing;
having gathered together with my devotees, I perform various activities.
I also experience all divine pastimes that grant liberation,
even through the state of being a donkey, along with the cowherds and cowherd-maidens, and even in my wanderings.
I always dwell in the abodes of my devotees;
thus, I resided in the settlement of the Cāraṇas within that circle of devotees.
In every way and at all times invisible, and not knowing them as they were, I dwelt in that hut in the cow-pen in the form of a physical body. 48.
Then, on one occasion, on the bank of the river Kāmakalpā,
there occurred an auspicious assembly of holy men and a great festival consisting of a free distribution of food.
There, at that festival consisting of a sacrificial feast of food, the *cāraṇas* and virtuous men also went in order to feed the people. (3.19.50)
The gift of food, the gift of milk, the gift of clothing, and the offering of ghee are given according to one's ability to the mendicants on the riverbank. (51)
Consequently, this sacrificial session (sattra) became renowned as the "Festival of Giving" (dānotsava).
Thereupon, all the male Cāraṇas and the female Cāraṇī went there.
She remained alone in the house for the purpose of guarding it, as well as for the sake of tending the calves and performing other household duties. (53)
Then the gods arrive from the path of the sky upon the earth at that great sacred site of charity, filled with great wonder.
And the Brahmins, repeatedly assuming the forms of mendicants and the appearances of holy men, accept some gift that grants desires like the wish-fulfilling tree. (55)
In that case, the fruit arises equally for both the giver and the receiver;
therefore, the gods accept gifts out of a desire for merit.
Since the variety [of results] in this sacrificial feast of giving yields fruit on both sides,
then at that time a god of little merit belonging to a celestial mansion appeared from the sky.
He set out by way of the sky, looking toward the river and the village;
with that deluded vision, he beheld a beautiful and virtuous Cāraṇī woman. 58.
Radiant, with a well-nourished body, she was a young woman wearing a very small cloth;
in that secluded place, she was pervaded by splendor, her limbs beautifully adorned and well-knit.
With her mind absorbed in chanting, she opened her voice in a sweet tone;
with her entire body wet from bathing, she was sprinkling water upon her own limbs.
Having seen her, who possessed the luster of a golden campaka flower and was like another embodiment of Rati,
that bewildered celestial being indeed stood there in solitude.
He desired that virtuous goddess and descended to her side;
though he was a god, he became a handsome youth, the best of celestial singers (cāraṇas).
Adorned with all ornaments, well-nourished, and in the bloom of youth,
he shone there with exceeding splendor like the very embodiment of desire.
He came into her presence, smiling, wishing to touch her as he pleased;
she too, seeing that new person was quickly filled with desire, was devoted [to him].
Rising quickly, she went indeed to the hut for the sake of the forest of virtuous conduct:
"O Lord, do not look upon me, who am endowed with virtue, with a wicked gaze. (65)
I worship you; I bow down to you. Go forth, go forth, O powerful one!
For the violation of an unwilling woman yields only a lowly fruit.
The gods are always to be honored and worshipped; they must certainly not be struck by me even slightly.
Depart happily from this sacrifice, abandoning your hope like a celestial chariot that has met its end.
"I offer this handful of milk to you as an act of worship;
honoring my words well, please depart by the way you came. (68)
O virtuous one, the rod of Yama is irresistible toward those devoted to their husbands, ascetics, cows, and likewise toward those practicing celibacy.
Whether he be a god, a sovereign, a brahmin, or even a lord—if he treads a wrong path, he is to be punished; if he stands upon the right path, he is to be honored. (3.19.70)
Although addressed thus, he approached the hall to touch and violate that chaste woman; being distressed, she spoke to him.
Having been a god and enjoyed divine pleasures, you have nonetheless fallen into delusion here in a human body; O lustful one, be reduced to ashes!
O gods, do not come from now on to this earth traveling in celestial chariots;
for those who shall enter this region of the earth will surely be reduced to ashes.
As soon as these words were spoken, he was instantly reduced to ashes;
and those gods who were present on earth at that time during the sacrificial session for gifts (dānasatra), [were likewise affected].
O beloved, they too were instantly reduced to ashes by the mere curse;
then a great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose on earth due to the curse of Āraṇī.
Having understood through their divine intellect that this was the cause of their own destruction,
the gods quickly fled through the sky, abandoning the gift and returning to their own abodes.
The arrival of the gods was obstructed; Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, as well as Indra, Candra, and the others, did not come to the earth out of fear.
The deities did not assemble; the gods of the sacred fords departed for heaven.
Stricken with fear by the curse of the devoted wife, they went to the celestial realm.
Now, those men in the world who are sinful go to sacred fords;
indeed, they wash away their sin at those sacred fords situated upon the earth. (79)
O deities, those sins do not come to burn the holy fords (tīrthas),
even at the Kumbha festival, during the solstice (saṃkrānti), or at the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), out of fear.
Then all the holy fords (tīrthas), overwhelmed by the sins of the wicked, became distressed and propitiated Acyuta. ||8 1 ||
Due to Satī’s curse, the gods do not come to the surface of the earth out of fear;
otherwise, our destruction would surely occur before long through the accumulation of their sins. (82)
Therefore, O Blessed One, come and grant us deliverance upon this earth;
for I am myself the Supreme Brahman, [attained] through the hymns of praise of the gods. (83)
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa; having come to the earth, I entered the house of Cāraṇī and became her son upon her lap. 84.
Worshipped by the holy fords and the gods, and bearing the marks of the conch, discus, and other symbols, you then became the daughter of the Cāraṇa named Ratnadhana. (85)
Having recognized you by these signs, O Ramā, you are Ratnanārāyaṇī;
you, the glory of Ratnanārāyaṇī, have been offered to me by Brahmā.
I am the Supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa, the primordial and venerable Tīrtha; I, the Highest Lord, have been proclaimed by all the holy fords and the celestial bards.
Then, together with you and accompanied by my parents,
I visited all the sacred fords (tīrthas), going to them again and again.
I committed a sin against them, yet I also brought about their release from the curse; indeed, by the command of my mother, I did this on earth for the sake of the arrival of the gods. (89)
Then the gods arrived after the withdrawal of the curse;
thereafter, until the end of the kalpa, I became Tīrthanārāyaṇa.
Having established himself in dharma and having brought his parents along with him,
he took their food offerings and then departed for his own ancient abode.
Thus, O Kamalā, I have told you how my manifestation occurred long ago on this portion of the earth for the sake of removing the curse of Cāraṇī.
I know all of that, whereas others, being forgetful, do not know it;
O beloved, remember her who was born as Cāraṇī, the jewel-like Nārāyaṇī.
O Queen Śivā, many other incarnations of mine have been born upon the earth in your company; I know them all. (94)
Then I made a survey of the world regarding the classes of gods:
all of them were exactly as they are, just like the Brahmins who are honored by the earth. (95)
Through reading this, through hearing it, through causing others to hear it, as well as through remembering and reflecting upon it, a person shall partake in liberation even by my manifestation. (96)
He shall be wealthy, righteous, possessed of sons, and endowed with all powers;
even a woman shall become possessed of good fortune, happiness, sovereignty, and other such blessings.

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Manifestation of the Beginningless Tīrtha-Nārāyaṇa in the Lap of Cāraṇyā for the Purpose of Purifying the Holy Places," in the twenty-second year of the Creator during the Dvāpara Age, within the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. || 19 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, to my manifestation thereafter—
that of the Supreme Self, the controller of all lords of lords.
In the twenty-third year of the eternal Creator (Brahmā), known as Sanātana,
and in the first Manvantara of the fifty-second Kalpa, long ago.
On the earth, on the bank of the celestial river, in the Kālādāna forest,
and on the side of Mount Madhumañcchṛṅgavān, the gods indeed resided.
The ascetics were devoted to meditation, dedicated to sacrifices and offerings,
intent upon the duties of Brahman, and focused on the supreme truth.
Established in the duties of householders, primarily devoted to ritual action and formal distinctions,
they did not consider manifold devotion to be the means for liberation.
For those who are devoted to their own duty and possess discrimination between the inert and the conscious, they hold that consciousness joined with the Dharma is truly great discernment.
Even those enriched with all enjoyments cross over bondage through knowledge;
for the self is a non-doer and a non-enjoyer, eternally pure within the bodies.
Free from the sense of "I" and "mine," devoid of attachment and aversion, and liberated from pleasure and pain, he is indeed liberated; of this there is no doubt.
Devoid of the latent impressions of past tendencies, free from effort toward action,
and lacking external perception— one is certainly liberated, without a doubt.
One who is free from the state of passion, devoid of desire, anger, and the like, and free from futile exertion, is indeed liberated; of this there is no doubt.
Even if he is joined with wife, son, and home, or possessed of forest groves,
buffaloes, cows, and bulls, one who is free from attachment is indeed liberated.
One who is always endowed with worldly conduct, devoted to the conduct prescribed by the scriptures, and abiding within the bounds of propriety is indeed liberated; of this there is no doubt.
Thus, those foremost of bulls among the earth-dwellers (brahmins), performers of sacrificial rites,
lived upon the riverbank together with their virtuous wives, daughters, and sons.
Subsisting on fruits, roots, and leaves, as well as eating food ripened by the sun and even food ripened by the seasons, they lived free from worldly desires.
They were devoted to the conduct of Brahman, wearing garments of rags and bark; they bore matted hair and smeared themselves with ashes, dwelling in leaf-huts and similar dwellings. || 15 ||
They observed the vow of celibacy as was appropriate and maintained their religious observances;
they performed sacrifices and festivals, even those celebrated by the wise.
Thus indeed, as they lived among the people on the earth and other realms,
they established that knowledge which, together with action, is the means to liberation.
They do not remember devotion, nor do they take refuge in dharma;
then once, by means of his very emaciated wife's devotion, the husband [was moved].

Dharmadeva was entreated for the nourishment of his own life, as you are the protector of your own life; O beloved, you are the protector of the worlds and truly one who observes the vow of devotion to his wife.
In this current Kalpa, the lords of the earth provide nourishment for you;
my place is not there, and therefore I shall indeed meet my death.
"O Lord, you must never depart, leaving me behind;
your nourishment and my loss—this is never appropriate. (21)
Just as my own prosperity should be ensured, so too must your beloved be protected;
for if I am displeasing to you, then indeed I, being a mere woman, should always be abandoned.
"By what means would death be better for me than life?
Having been addressed thus, Dharmadeva indeed grieved for a moment.
Keeping the nourishment of devotion in his heart, he reached a definitive conclusion regarding that work;
he went to Nārāyaṇa Viṣṇu, the eternal Supreme Brahman.
Having come to me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), in the supreme abode known as Akṣara, she worshipped me.
O Supreme Brahman, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Supreme Lord, the Bull [Dharma] prayed for the purpose of establishing the Goddess of Devotion upon the earth. 26.
In this present age, the people on earth are devoted solely to ritual duty;
they are intent upon the section of the Veda concerning action, devoid of devotion, yet possessed of discernment.
Those who know the distinction between the insentient and the sentient indeed become intent on the goal of liberation;
for them, O Lord, there is no longer any need for the worship of Nārāyaṇa.
Not even the scent of an image of you, Hari, exists anywhere upon the earth; therefore, how could there be worship, service, and so forth, toward one who has no form of an image? (29)
O Bhagavān, O Mādhava, exert yourself to promote devotion, to nourish it likewise, and to give life to the various forms of devotion. (3.20.30)
O Lakṣmī, having heard this prayer of Dharmadeva which nourishes devotion, [he approached] Sadāśiva, who is indeed ever-yoked in yoga. || 31 ||
He indeed impelled [them] upon the earth to go forth and likewise to refute both the doctrine of action alone and the doctrine of knowledge alone.
"Without devotion, action is indeed fruitless, and knowledge does not grant liberation.
For the purpose of this instruction, he sent Śaṅkara. (33)
Having gone swiftly to the earth and seeing the people engaged in ritual acts, yet devoid of devotion toward the gods and other deities, he performed a marvel.
Having become a radiant youth clad in the directions alone, with his body appearing as if composed of delusion,
Hara, nourished and joined by the Goddess, went to the village of the earth-dwellers (brahmins).
Where all those diligent gods of the earth and others dwell, as well as their wives, their daughters, and the sons born of the twice-born. (36)
All these people, though diligent in ritual action and devoted to the knowledge of duality, are devoid of devotion, lacking divine vision, and conceited in their identification with the body. (37)
Furthermore, those who are devoted to lust and anger, devoid of the greatness of the Divine, and likewise devoid of the greatness of yogis, holy men, and the like; ||38||
Devoid of hospitality and lacking the state of Brahman, they are possessed of the vision of saṃsāra and endowed with hearts full of faults. ||39||
Wherever such gods of the earth dwell together—whether they be men or women living in villages or residing in leaf-huts and the like—[they are all protected]. (3.20.40)
There, this Śaṅkara went about naked, imitating the gestures of a lover;
he went from house to house, [surrounded] by girls as well as boys. ||41||
And likewise, young women and wives, seeing that intoxicated embodied being—heedless, handsome, robust, and deluding—ran after him. (42)
They spoke playful words, looked at the Lord, and laughing like lovers, they threw dust and other things at him. (43)
Some of the wives of the Asuras, being deluded, followed [him] without clothes, striking him on the hips with sticks.
Out of greed for pleasure, they touched her and led her to a secluded bower;
the brahmins, devoted to the ritualistic portion of the Vedas, saw this and heard of it. (45)
Those who bore the banner of false discernment pursued him in order to kill him;
having caught up with him, they struck him excessively with clubs and staffs.
Śaṅkara, as if truly disciplined and fit, did not feel pain at all;
having received a powerful blow, he fell to the ground and died. ||47||
He became like a corpse there and did not breathe at all;
he remained as if in meditative absorption (samādhi), just as one who is dead. ||48||
Having abandoned the fallen one, those brahmins went to their respective dwellings;
then the virtuous goddess Satī, becoming enraged, cursed those Prātadakas.

For those twice-born ones who possess the banner of discrimination are the authors of false knowledge; they are devoid of the existence of the Self and merely imagine themselves to be non-doers. (3.20.50)
Those who merely know the grandiosity of words do not consider that the self’s lack of agency, its lack of being an enjoyer, and its eternal purity are but partial aspects [of its nature]. (5.1)
They were devoted to ritual action, embodied in their physical forms, and intent upon desire and anger;
likewise, they were ignorant of the divine majesty of the true yogis.
Devoted to sensual pleasures, intent on your own interests, and full of suspicion, you are merciless and like killers of Brahmins; may you go to death just as Hara did. ||53||
Thus, when Satya had spoken, those classes of men belonging to the earth—whether in the hamlet, the small town, or the forest—swiftly met their death in due course. (54)
Corpse-like calamities have arisen in every house and even within the dwellings of men; a great cry of lamentation has broken out on all sides, even in the abodes of the Brahmins.
The Brahmins will surely meet their death due to the curse of the naked women;
what should be done, and where should one go, for the sake of protection here today? (56)
Women wept all around, and young girls wept as well;
even men, having heard [the news], wept at every place. (57)
Deprived of their own true nature and lacking the knowledge born of discernment, they are merely performers of verbal knowledge, devoid of the wisdom that perceives reality as it is. ||58||

At that time, throughout the entire world of men and in all regions upon the earth, there were those devoted to ritual action who were possessed by the defects of anger, lust, and the like, and filled with grief.
Then the gods upon the earth lost their luster and became as if lifeless;
at that time, throughout the entire day and across the whole earth, O Kamala, [all things were thus].
At that time, there were indeed cemeteries of hundreds of billions of corpses;
in every house there, a corpse was produced at every single moment.
Other people, including women and those other than Brahmins, considered this anger to be something extraordinary, even the greatest of all, and one that would bring about universal destruction.
Wherever there were Brahmins who were ritualists yet held divergent doctrines and were devoid of devotion, they all then attained the state of being corpses.
When such a cry of "Alas! Alas! arose, the men and women who remained performed the propitiation of the Supreme Lord, my own Self.
You are the vital breath, you are life itself, and you are the protector, O Mādhava;
you are the refuge of women, O Lord—bring our husbands back to life!
Having heard this praise and perceiving the omen regarding my arrival,
O Lakṣmī, Puruṣottama came together with you.
May he quickly descend to earth, adorned with the conch, discus, mace, lotus, and other emblems;
resplendent in golden ornaments and garments, and blazing with divine luster. (67)
Where the corpse of Haraśava lay, and likewise where the corpses of the twice-born were,
there I manifested my form and comforted the women.

Likewise, I granted supreme fortitude to those men who were distinct from the twice-born—those who were merely performers of ritual acts, makers of knowledge, yet devoid of discernment and right conduct. (69)

Devoid of devotion and possessing only dry intellectual knowledge, these offenders against the virtuous have immediately reaped the fruit of their actions, remaining unaware that they were wrongdoers.
Great is the sin in dry knowledge for one who possesses it but lacks right conduct;
for that which is known is neither proclaimed, nor practiced, nor retained.
There is no other sin for embodied beings equal to that sin;
these people, though devoted to the ritual section of the Vedas, carry the banner of discernment [only in name]. (72)
They do not at all maintain freedom from passion and hatred;
yet they have killed this yogi, who is beyond reproach and possessed of discernment. (73)
When the death of the virtuous one was announced by those devoid of devotion,
the people, the men, and the women then questioned the Supreme Lord.
"Tell us how this great downfall may be dissolved; instruct us.
Then, O Lakṣmī, I said to them: "Indeed, for the sake of worshipping Him... (75)
Having gone to that corpse which has been slain, let them worship it once it has been installed;
let them perform the consecration of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) and worship that image. (76)
Let them worship Him with the sixteen primary offerings and other services, by presenting food offerings, by performing the waving of lights (nīrājana), and by means of hymns of praise.
Then this calamity of death will go to destruction;
having heard this, both women and men will likewise be devoid of the discernment to distinguish falsehood from truth.
Having brought all the excellent requisites—sandalwood, unbroken rice, garlands, incense, lamps, fine food offerings, garments, ornaments, and sandals—[they arrived]. (779)
Having performed the invocation and other rites, and having worshipped with all manner of offerings,
my ancestors— the women, men, and others— performed the consecration of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhā).
They performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), and at that moment Śambhu,
regaining consciousness, opened his eyes and rose up in an instant.
They offered him food offerings and then gave him water to drink;
at that time, Hara became pleased and spoke to them for the sake of granting a boon.
Then everyone requested the restoration of the dead to life;
Hara, having worshipped this goddess and received her auspicious blessings, spoke.
They shall possess life; it shall never be otherwise. Then, O Lakṣmī, those women and men worshipped the Goddess. 84.
They even requested the restoration to life of those who had died;
and Śivā spoke here regarding how she was worshipped together with Śaṅkara.
Likewise, let everyone worship this Lakṣmī together with the glorious Nārāyaṇa; then, having died, they shall attain life. (86)
Thus addressed, the men and women worshipped me together with you;
then they all rose up, freed from their offenses and from death.
Having regained their lives, they indeed sang of me as "Jīvan-Nārāyaṇa";
thus I too attained the renown of being the primordial Jīvan-Nārāyaṇa.
Together with you, my form consists of Nārāyaṇa through devotion;
therefore, people [should always worship it] with the devotion shown by me. (89)
They served [Him] exceedingly, having abandoned dry intellectual analysis;
they indeed performed the ritual section (karmakāṇḍa) consisting entirely of self-surrender. ||3.20.90||
Then Śaṅkara instructed them all in the entire ritual section (karmakāṇḍa) dedicated to me, which consists of devotion to me. ||9.1||
My knowledge, which is endowed with righteousness and devotion, is indeed realization;
therefore, in that kalpa, it was set forth as auspicious and bestowing liberation.
The revival of devotion has occurred and the path of devotion has been set in motion;
my own forms and those of Śambhu, together with their Śaktis, have appeared upon the earth. (93)
Then, having been restored to life by them, they were established and revealed just as before;
and being worshipped everywhere, their devotion indeed attained full growth.
Thus Śambhu, joined by Satī, having performed the supreme rite of auspiciousness (kautuka), established on earth the worship of the image as well as the highest devotion. 95.
And I, the Lord Jīvanārāyaṇa, was seen by you on earth for a duration of time equal to the end of a kalpa, dwelling together with you.
Thus, O Śivarājñī-Śrī, the manifestation of the beginningless Supreme Soul, Śrī Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, has been proclaimed by me. 97.
For the nourishment of devotion to the Dharma, for the cultivation of spiritual practice, and for the worship of my own form as well as the form of Śaṅkara; (98)
In that kalpa, there was indeed no liṅga nor any image of Hara;
at that time, my own form existed, but the Viṣṇu-stone did not exist.
"In this way, I know all that previously occurred;
remember my worship and so forth, as well as my manifestation at that time."
O Lakṣmī, by reading, hearing, remembering, or even reflecting upon this, one shall certainly obtain the fruit of my worship; of this there is no doubt. (10.1)

Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of the Primeval Śrī Jīvanārāyaṇa at the Request of a Devotee in the Twenty-third Year of the Creator during the Dvāpara Age, and the Propagation of the Path of Devotion through Śaṅkara," in the third section, the Dvāpara-santāna, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Queen of Śiva, to another manifestation of mine;
it occurred in the twenty-fourth year of Brahmā, known as Ārṣa.
Just as it occurred formerly in the sixth Manu of the hundredth Kalpa,
at that time there were Brahmins learned in the Vedas as well as ascetics.
The deities, the sages, and the ancestors also gathered at the bank of the Mokṣadā river for the sacrifice consisting of all things, which was performed by Aja.
There, the deliberations of everyone were directed toward me:
"What kind of Hari is this to be served—is he alone, or is he a pair? (4)
Whether devoid of qualities or possessed of qualities, whether embodied or indeed formless, whether having the form of fire or the nature of the sun, or even being formless; || 5 ||
Then Brahmā himself, existing in the form of a couple, spoke there;
and the other great sages said: "He alone is the one who is higher than the highest."

The gods said, "He is possessed of attributes (saguṇa)," while the ascetics declared him to be himself without attributes (nirguṇa). Others sang that he should be served according to his fitness, being manifest in embodied form (mūrtimān).
Those devoted to ritual action say that this formless one is indeed to be served;
others say that Hari is directly the fire itself, while the supreme ones say he is the sun.
While they were thus engaged in debate, asserting that he was both to be served and the very embodiment of Brahman, the conclusion reached was not uniform; then Viṣṇu spoke.
"And whatever this Śambhu may say to us shall indeed be the final decision.
Having heard the words of Hari, Śambhu addressed the members of the assembly: [3.21.10]
"Let them meditate for a moment; he himself will provide the decision.
These were the words of Śaṅkara spoken then at the Sarvamedha sacrifice.
While the gods, sages, ancestors, and humans were absorbed in meditation,
a mountain composed of divine splendor emerged from the sky.
It pervaded the entire sky, heaven, earth, and the quarters of space; in their midst was my beloved, the excellent celestial palace named Akṣara.
O Lakṣmī, at that time I was seen there by you along with Him—
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, whose body is half that of Kamalā.
Then, he became directly manifest before them within the range of their meditation;
half of his crest remained upon his head, while the other half was the glorious mass of hair coiled in a topknot.
On one half of her forehead was a fine topknot, and on the other half was a beautiful crescent moon;
in her right ear was an earring, and in her left was a small, trembling earring.
On the right [hand] is stainless powder, while on the left eye is collyrium;
on the right [side] is a beard, and the nose is empty on the right but possesses a nasal septum on the left.
The right breast is elevated, while the left is accompanied by a nipple;
the two right hands, adorned with beautiful bracelets, hold a conch and a discus.
My two left hands are provided with a lotus garland, a chain, and a fan;
on the right is the half [image] marked with the Śrīvatsa, and on the left is the half-form of myself.
On the right side of the abdomen there are three-and-a-half folds; on the left, the nature of a flat abdomen.
On the right is half a human linga, and on the left is half a yoni.
On the right there is indeed one male organ, while on the left there is a concealed knot;
the right foot is hairy, while the left is hairless and brilliantly radiant; the phallus is long like that of a man, while the vulva is short and excellent like that of a woman. ||21||
The right half [of his body] possesses a dark beauty, while the left half is radiant with gold;
the right half is adorned with a crown of yellow and white jewels and other golden ornaments.
The left half [of the body] is endowed with a bodice, a lower garment, and a golden crown; the right half is richly adorned with male ornaments, while the left is adorned with female ornaments. (23)
The right side was endowed with masculine strength, while the left was exceedingly soft like a woman;
thus, though being one alone, he possessed two forms.
Before them stood the Lord Nārāyaṇa, possessing half of his splendor;
and they meditated within their hearts upon me as well, in that same form of two-in-one.
Human beings, gods, sages, and even the ancestors worshipped me;
Brahmā and the others entreated me: "Dwell here on this earth forever. (26)
In this very same form, you exist for the sake of the welfare of the world;
therefore, I am on the bank of the river Mokṣadā, to the west of Mount Meru.
I, the Supreme Lord, whose range is universal, have dwelt eternally upon the sacrificial ground until the end of the kalpa, instructing [the world] in the worship of the image.
The Lord Nārāyaṇa, the beginningless and glorious Lord of Half-Śrī (Ardhaśrīśvara),
is present in every way within temples and the like, as well as in every single house.
My form became of one kind: half that of Śrī and half that of Nārāyaṇa;
likewise, my worship, meditation, ritual service, and the wearing of attire were of that same nature.
O Lakṣmī, in that kalpa, my entire body was indeed of such a nature, served by devotees; it was made so by me through my own will.
Indeed, I have assumed whatever form is desired, distinguished according to each syllable;
then the gods and others likewise perceive me as that supreme being.
They worshiped and served [me], and they attained liberation;
thus was my manifestation in that kalpa described to you.
"O Goddess, remember in this way the unity of the Couple and Your own manifestation;
O Lakṣmī, I know all of them, as well as those of many incarnations. (34)
Now, I shall proclaim to you the manifestation of both me and the other [Viṣṇu] at the beginning, during the twenty-fifth year of the Creator known as Dharma. (35)
In the first of the five-hundred eons, long ago, the hosts of ancestors descended upon the earth from their lineages and proclaimed the ritual feeding of the śrāddha.
The learned people born of those various lineages performed that [rite],
and with faith, they offered the funeral cakes (piṇḍa) and other offerings intended for the assembly of ancestors.
All those ancestors also emerged with half their bodies visible;
with both arms outstretched, they joyfully received the rice-balls (piṇḍas).
With serene faces and likewise with hands raised aloft, they stood still after receiving the funeral cakes, their bodies visible only from the navel upward. 39.
At that time, all remained thus steadfast, with their food already held in their hands;
they did not eat, remaining silent, peaceful, and free from desire.
Then, they were observed by the brahmins and others born of their lineage while they were not eating;
and all the fathers were asked: "Why do you not eat, even though [the food] has been offered? (41)
They said: "There is nothing so pleasing to Hari as this very thing;
it is always inedible for us, because we are indeed Vaiṣṇavas. (42)
Then the members of the lineage asked: "How could it be so pleasing, since Narayana is neither seen here nor does he exist? (43)
Then those ancestors said: "Let them recite the *Harisūkta* here;
Hari himself will come and accept the rice-balls (*piṇḍa*), the milk-rice (*pāyasa*), and other offerings. (44)
Then, at that moment, they worshipped me— the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama— with the Harisūkta.
O Lakṣmī, because of my devotion to the ancestors, I was present there together with you before the members of the lineage, yet I did not ascend the funeral pyre. (46)
Sitting right there with his ancestors, he partook of milk,
milk-rice, sweet food, fruit, leaves, and radish.
And you, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, whose form was visible above my navel, were adorned by me and partook of the milk-rice together with me. (48)
Then all those ancestors, eager for happiness, ate the water, food, and other offerings which were pleasing and provided by me. (49)
Having eaten and being satisfied, all of them went from the world of the ancestors to their own abodes;
meanwhile, I remained ready on the earth along with the brahmins and others.

The two of them, possessing divine forms, beautiful and of gentle appearance, were requested to dwell there eternally; they were not [ordinary] beings bearing superior bodies, yet they remained partially visible.
Thinking, "So be it," they remained forever on the earth;
until the end of the kalpa, they always bore the form of the half-body above the navel.

And likewise, such forms as these appeared in the home, the forest, and the temple; they were present in meditation, in worship, and in festivals, both in their entirety and as partial manifestations.
I became renowned as the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, and as the one known as the beginningless Ardha-pitṛ Nārāyaṇa. 54.
Remember, Lakṣmī, that my form was then half-completed by you;
furthermore, even then, there were millions of other incarnations of mine as well. (55)
I know all of them who have departed, whereas others do not indeed know them;
they are auspicious, bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation through mere remembrance and salutation. (56)
The portion below the navel is illusory and bestows rebirth in hell;
the portion above the navel is purifying and has been shown by me to bestow liberation.
Then, knowledge arose in the form of a half-ascending image;
having realized this and performed worship in such a manner, people went to the imperishable abode.
Now I shall speak: in the twenty-sixth year of the Age of the Creator (Vedhas), in the seventh Manvantara of the seventh Kalpa, I am the Supreme Lord.
I appeared in the midst of the Plakṣa tree as the beginningless Nārāyaṇa of the Plakṣa;
in that kalpa, there were indeed great-souled beings devoted to the knowledge of the Self.
Indeed, there were virtuous and steadfast men devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa;
they wore matted hair and garments of bark, and subsisted on food obtained without asking.
Content with whatever they obtain by chance, they bring about the welfare of the world;
they are endowed with the sacred thread and their bodies are marked with the sectarian tilaka.
Adorned with necklaces, garlands, and other ornaments, those who were devoted to meditation and worship once gathered together on the auspicious bank of the Viṣṇu river.
In the forest of devotion, for the sake of austerity and for the sake of devotion to the Supreme Self, they,
being well-united, held a conversation with one another.
O twice-born ones, does austerity bestow the highest good, or does devotion bestow the highest good?
Or is it that both are considered to bestow the highest good; if so, which indeed is the most excellent? (65)
When such a core question had arisen among the practitioners of auspicious yoga, some said that austerity is supreme, while others said it is not so. (66)
Through austerity, sin is destroyed and auspicious merit is produced;
by that, one attains enjoyments and heaven, and upon its exhaustion, death occurs.
Therefore, worldly austerity at the end does not yield such spiritual excellence;
consequently, supreme devotion is the most excellent, for it is the eternal bestower of the highest good.
Others say: "She who possesses desire does not bestow ultimate welfare;
she who is free from desire is superior and more excellent, for she indeed bestows the highest good. (69)
Others, however, say: "If devotion is desireless—that is, devoid of longing—it is fruitless;
for, lacking a result, it is merely a form of exertion. (3.21.70)
"Therefore, she should be made to have desires, for she bestows the excellent fruits of one's own wishes.
While the great sages were speaking thus, Vṛṣa [spoke].
Dharmadeva, in the form of a brahmin, standing in the assembly, spoke this:
"He who is the inner self of all, the witness of all, shines forth. (72)
That deity shines here upon this righteous Plakṣa tree;
having performed worship to him, the burden of questions lies here with the Pippala tree.
"And Kṛṣṇa, abiding therein, will bestow that which is to be deposited as the subsequent [portion].
Having thus made this single resolve, the great seers then [proceeded].
Having worshipped the Pippala tree there and caused the Supreme Lord to hear [his words], he asked:
"O Lord, what is the ultimate supreme good—is it austerity or is it devotion? (75)
Having thus proclaimed this, those whose wealth was their asceticism remained for a hundred years engaged in penance;
nevertheless, they did not obtain an answer from the Plakṣa tree.
Then, from a voice in the sky, the Lord, the Supreme Ruler, said to them:
"O you whose wealth is penance, ultimate welfare cannot be attained through austerity alone. (77)
"May you propitiate me, the Supreme Brahman, the witness of all;
for when pleased by desireless devotion, O twice-born ones, I am ever satisfied. (78)
"Through devotion, you shall attain ultimate welfare and the ultimate goal.
Having been addressed thus, they said: "How [can there be] devotion without Hari? (79)
Without directly perceiving Hari, how can there be devotion or loving service?
O Mādhava, if we have been purified by austerity, we have become worthy recipients. (3.21.80)
O Abode of Mercy, come among us and stay forever;
for you are eternally dear to your devotees, and it is for their sake that you remain in the sky.
Though invisible, you, who are affectionate toward your devotees, issue commands—even through a voice from the sky—considering them to be for the welfare of your own people. 82.
Just as you have taught us through words, so too instruct us through your own essential nature;
O Mādhava, delight us, your own people, with direct perception. 83.
Thus addressed, I said to them: "Let them cultivate [this] with concentrated minds;
for when the fruit of their worship is attained, I shall indeed become their object of perception. (84)
Then, considering themselves to possess the supreme good fortune of Nārāyaṇīśrī,
the twice-born remained there for a hundred years.
Worshipping the Lord of gods, the Lord of lords, the Lord of lords, those holy men were free from desire and devoted solely to the hope of attaining Brahman. 86.
Having the form of Brahman and having become one with Brahman, they took refuge in the shade of a Plakṣa tree;
they chanted my name, Nārāyaṇa, and worshipped me through the recitation of my names.
They worshipped me with offerings such as *tulasī* and held me within the temple of their minds;
and when a hundred years had passed for those virtuous ones who were devoted to my practice, [they beheld me].
I myself was present there in person, seated at the foot of a Plakṣa tree, together with you, Lakṣmī, as Śrīplakṣanārāyaṇa. (89)
He is established in the Plakṣa-Brahman, within the womb-like portion of the Plakṣa-stambha, which is infused with divine splendor and situated in the spacious ether of consciousness (cidākāśa).
On my left, upon a lotus together with you, is the four-armed Nārāyaṇa;
I am Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). ||9 1||
Manifested by his own will alone for the fulfillment of the desires of the virtuous,
he bears the conch, discus, mace, lotus, svastika, banner, and trident.
Adorned with all divine ornaments, wearing a golden crown and earrings,
he possessed the radiant complexion of a divine campaka flower and was likewise clothed in celestial garments.
Pervaded by divine splendor, the Supreme Lord, whose nature is that of a couple, is present there to fulfill the desires of the virtuous and bestow all blessings. (94)
Then, with their divine eyes, they beheld me within the trees— there,
in the midst of the celestial dwellings, that most excellent of men, concealed by the trees.
They prostrated like a staff, offered praises to the Supreme Lord,
and then honored Him there with gathered offerings and services.
"Out of affection and devotion, they always served me while protecting me within the maṇḍala;
in this way, O beloved, I became the bestower of welfare upon all the worlds. (97)
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the eternal one; by my own will, I am indeed Puruṣottama within the circle of the virtuous. 98.
"I exist as the primordial Śrī Plakṣa Nārāyaṇa;
I know everything—remember me, O dweller of the Plakṣa tree. (99)
Your auspicious form is the eternal embodiment of Lakṣmī;
moreover, hundreds of thousands of other incarnations of mine have also come into being.
Even the lords do not know [it], much less the gods and humans;
[this is known] by reading, hearing, causing others to hear, and even by remembering this.
From serving her who dwells in the Plakṣa tree, and from my service as well, there shall be both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
indeed, the highest liberation shall come to pass.
He who worships Pippala-Śrī and Śrī-Nārāyaṇa at the Pippala tree shall never be separated from Lakṣmī, and the attainment of liberation will be certain for him. || 103 ||

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Beginningless, Illustrious Ardha-Śrīśa Nārāyaṇa in the twenty-fourth year of the Creator [Brahmā] during the Dvāpara cycle of the third book; the manifestation of the Beginningless, Illustrious Ardha-Pitṛ Nārāyaṇa in the twenty-fifth year; and the manifestation of the Beginningless, Illustrious Plakṣa Nārāyaṇa in the twenty-sixth year," in the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. || 21 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to my other manifestation,
which occurred in the twenty-seventh year of the Creator [Brahmā] known as Avṛṣa.
In the third Manvantara, during the fourth cycle of time (kalpa), there were gods on the surface of the earth;
those protectors of the world performed many sacrifices. || 2 ||
The Agnihotra, the Darśahoma, the Paurṇamāsa, the Prayāja offerings, the Sviṣṭakṛt sacrifice, the Pitṛyajña, and the Vaiśvadeva; || 3 ||
The Cāturmāsya, the Sākamedha, the Soma sacrifice, the Āgrayaṇeṣṭi, the Avabhṛtheṣṭi, as well as the Atirātra and the Vājapeya; || 4 ||
The Agniṣṭoma, as well as the Sautrāmaṇī, the Rājasūya,
the Aśvamedha, the Sarvamedha, the Puṃmedha, and many other Soma sacrifices.
The Bṛhaspatisava, the Vaiśyasava, the Somasava, as well as the Gosava, the Brāhmaṇasava, and the auspicious Audanasava. || 6 ||
Once, they performed the Pṛthisava, the Marutstoma, the Putreṣṭi, and other sacrifices; then they commenced the Nṛmedhaka.
Then, during that sacrifice, for five days, he duly offered one hundred and ninety-eight men to the deities. || 8 ||
The twice-born, deluded though they were knowers of reality, began to slaughter men for the sake of the omentum and for the purpose of oblation. 9.
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, as to who those beast-like kings were: they were less than twelve years of age, yet they wore the sacred thread.
Brahmins and others, both devotees and non-devotees, were assembled there for the purpose of the sacrifice;
among them, however, there was one yogi who was solely devoted to me.
Unattached to time, illusion, and the like, the man is free from desire for the body and its possessions;
he is of a bright complexion, named Sundara, tender, and his face bears an expression of joy.
Purified by the Brahmins, consecrated, and brought forward,
he was worshipped according to the rules within the slaughter-hall.
With his mind fixed on Nārāyaṇa, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, the Inner Self,
he should constantly offer himself and perform all his activities solely for my sake.
Knowing that my devotee was of such a nature and intended for slaughter, I quickly arrived at the lotus in the house of slaughter. (15)
At that time, I was indeed invisible to those devoted to ritual action, yet visible to my devotee;
having rendered my devotee invisible, I remained clearly manifest in that very place.
He possesses that very form and remains silent for the sake of protecting his devotees, for the purpose of destroying delusion, and indeed for the cessation of violence. (17)
It is for the sake of protecting the Dharma, for the cessation of false actions, for the purpose of bestowing awakening upon the Brahmins, and for the practice of truthfulness. || 18 ||
O Lakṣmī, for the sake of destroying the sinful deeds of those characterized by tamas, my own protector then appeared visibly in the temple. 19.
Then those twice-born ones, having received initiation for the sacrifice, chanted the mantras;
having sprinkled everything according to the proper rite, they seized me, the Puruṣa.
The merciless ones bound their mouths by stuffing them with barley;
eager for the kill, they crushed their testicles and cut them off.
While I was still alive, wicked men, possessed by delusion, carried out my slaughter through a rite based on error; therefore, I am the destroyer of sinners. (22)
With my two testicles, which had been castrated and were as hard as thunderbolts, I swiftly struck the skulls and cranial apertures of those ritualists.
Struck by those two [beings] who resembled vajra-jewels and were accompanied by fire, the twice-born ones blazed up and perished,
their heads and skulls shattered.
Arising by the thousands, they were massive and circular;
they had the form of great boulders and resembled the fire of universal destruction.
These indeed caused the earth and the stars in the sky to burn;
these, consisting mostly of mountains, then shattered everything.
They destroyed the sacrifice on all sides, as well as the sacrificial implements;
