Furthermore, O Lakṣmī, after that I shall also briefly describe another auspicious manifestation of mine, which bestows great merit. (46)
Formerly, in the thirty-ninth age of Brahmā,
during the sixth Manu of the sixth Kalpa, there was a great Asura named Ilodara.
The consumer of the essence of all principles, the devourer of the essence, the formidable one;
the son of Rāhu, of demonic deeds, the devourer of the essence of heaven and earth. (48)
Having arrived upon the earth, he performed most severe penance for a thousand years on Mount Meru;
Śaṅkara himself was pleased.
He came into his presence and said, "Choose a boon. Thereupon, the asura requested the power to consume all flavors.
Having said, "So be it," Hara quickly vanished;
that Asura [then consumed] the juices of the earth always present in the waters.
He eats as much as he desires and constantly attains nourishment from all sides;
then, being fully satisfied, for more than a thousand years thereafter, he performs supreme austerity.
He performed [austerities] directed toward Brahmā for the very purpose of becoming invulnerable;
seeing him withered of limb and subsisting only on air, Brahmā indeed approached him.
Having sprinkled him with water and restored him to life, he then said:
"Choose a boon as you desire; I am pleased with you, O great Asura. (54)
Opening his eyes, he too spoke of his supreme invincibility:
"Indeed, I am not to be conquered by those who dwell upon the fourteen worlds."
"Let it be so," the great asura received these words from Brahmā;
and Brahmā, having vanished from sight, the great asura then departed.
Fearless, he enjoyed divine and human pleasures many times over;
nevertheless, he reflected: "May death not come to me. (57)
Then, having reflected thus, he performed penance once more on Mount Meru for a thousand years,
indeed directing his penance toward Viṣṇu.
At the end of a thousand years, Viṣṇu, impelled by the gods, arrived;
he said to him, "What indeed do you desire? Choose! I am Viṣṇu here. (59)
"I have come for the purpose of granting a boon; do not delay. The Asura said, "If it is so, then let death not befall me. (3.32.60)
"In this manner, I choose from you, O Viṣṇu, the boon desired by me.
Viṣṇu said: "O Dhruva, for whom there is birth, for him death is certain."
The death of your father, known as Rāhu, is indeed certain;
likewise, the death of his father Kaśyapa, and even of his father, is certainly fixed.
No one is free from death except for the illustrious Puruṣottama;
the self is eternal, the enjoyer of karma, and dwells within the cage of the body. (63)
And when that [consciousness] has departed from the body, the body is designated as "dead.
The body consists of six sheaths, and these sheaths arise from the elements and so forth. (64)
The transformations of the elements indeed arise constantly;
since transformations are always impermanent, the body is therefore impermanent.
There is no permanence in that which is impermanent; choose instead another, a stable state—be it sovereignty, heaven, the netherworld, or even eternal life. (66)
"O Asura, I give to you wealth—gold, silver, and the earth;
as well as the status of Surya, Candra, Mahendra, and even Kubera. (67)
"Choose another superior state; I shall grant it to you without delay.
Having heard this, he said: "O All-eater, let there be no death for me here. (68)
"I choose [the boon] from those created by the three deities; grant it to me.
"So be it," said Hari, and he quickly vanished from sight. (69)
Then that Asura, having abandoned his asceticism and being likewise freed from the fear of death,
forcibly enjoyed the pleasures of gods, Daityas, and humans.
Having forcibly seized all the divine powers of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva as well, he enjoys them, strengthened by the power of his boons.
Once, having conquered the gods, he went to Kailāsa;
there he said to Śaṅkara, "Give me battle, or else give me Kailāsa. (72)
Śambhu said, "This half of Kailāsa belongs to you in every respect;
take it. Having received that half, he too rejoiced.
Then he went to Satyaloka and said to Brahmā:
"O Brahman, give me your entire being or else give me battle. (74)
Brahmā said, "Accept this half-portion of my supreme station.
Having received it, he too became delighted and went to Viṣṇu, who was like a mass of milk.
He spoke to me with anger: "O Viṣṇu, give me the White Island (Śvetadvīpa), or else grant me battle; do whatever you deem best. (76)
Viṣṇu said, "I have always granted you half of the Milk Ocean as your portion.
Having received it, the Asura was delighted and went to Meru, his own abode.
Then, while that great asura was entreating Śivā, Śrī, and the goddess Brāhmī,
the gods were engaged in his destruction.
They formed a plan for the Asura and quickly devised a stratagem;
Hara himself assumed the forms of those three Piśācinīs.
Then Ilodara sent him away, and the fool rejoiced;
the Piśācinīs undertook a vow consisting of consuming all kinds of flavorful juices.
"Having observed for one month the vow named 'Consumption of All Tastes,' then, when the vow is completed, we shall proceed to the service. (81)
Having heard that they had arrived and having understood this, the asura rejoiced, for he was capable of gathering all the essences. (82)
He quickly brought all the terrestrial juices and all the aquatic ones as well, in their entirety, whether they were prepared by cooking or not. 83.
He gave [these things] to those women of the three classes and even to the female Piśācas;
he fed them in many ways and caused them to drink in every respect.
The earth was indeed bereft of its essence, and the water was bereft of its essence; those elements which were flavorful became flavorless. (85)
Food devoid of flavor, even ghee, is considered nectar; likewise, all offerings to gods and ancestors, as well as meat and other such things, are [deemed so] when they are lacking in flavor. (86)
Because of that, everything born became unfit to be eaten or drunk;
all living beings—including gods, asuras, sages, and humans—fell into suffering. (87)
Furthermore, because the food offering was devoid of flavor even when dedicated to the Supreme Lord,
all the gods consequently refused to eat their meal, which had become as bitter as a donkey's fodder.
Then they all gathered together and, being deeply distressed, propitiated me; for the sake of destroying Ilodara, they praised me in many ways.
Having heard this, I, the Supreme Brahman, the Lord of Śrī, the Puruṣottama,
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Supreme Lord, [spoke].
O Lakṣmī, from that very imperishable abode, Hari himself came along with you and appeared visibly before millions of gods.
Having been honored, requested, and informed regarding the destruction of the asuras,
I went to the region of Mount Meru where the asura rejoices.
There I became the form of nectar, remaining as a lake—
sweet, cool, fragrant, bestowing bliss, granting happiness, and auspicious.
Radiant, in the form of white nectar, intoxicating, and gentle, I became a full lake in the form of a flowing stream near him. 94.
The three Piśācinīs, having beheld that lake of supreme nectar, spoke of it;
he too arrived there with great speed.
Thus, with great joy, he drank the nectar and made them drink it as well;
there was no satiety in drinking, no belching arose, and indeed, he drank again and again.
Abandoning his pride, he drank excessively; indeed, he drank until his throat was full.
"I am the essence," [he thought], yet it did not remain in his mouth; rather, it increased within his belly. (97)
Having drunk and drunk all that inexhaustible essence, he became Mahodara;
as great as the perfection of his magnitude was, so great did he become.
Having overcome pride, he drank the nectar again and again;
indeed, his belly abandoned its power of retention.
Torn from the region of the navel down to the heart,
and the hips likewise torn apart, I emerged in the form of vital essence.
It fell outside his very belly and he died;
I am Anādiśrīrasanārāyaṇa, together with you.
I remained there together with Anādiśrīrasalakṣmī;
and the Piśācinīs, being pleased, worshipped me after having worshipped Hari.
These [beings], beginning with the gods, went to Kailāsa itself, and having arrived there,
they rained down flowers and praised me, whose nature is rasa.
The lords always entreated Śrī Puruṣottama, the primordial Nārāyaṇa whose essence is Śrī, for the purpose of making his residence [there].
I always dwell upon the earth for the sake of increasing its nourishment and growth; at that time, I existed in embodied form for the duration of a single Manvantara.
Then, O beloved Lakṣmī, having become composed of rasa, I remained for a kalpa;
remember that manifestation of mine which was of the nature of rasa.
Then all the gods went to their own abodes in heaven and other realms;
at that time, thousands of other incarnations of mine also came into being.
I became the incarnation Rasanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Brahman;
by reading or hearing this, both worldly enjoyment and liberation shall be attained.

Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Vahninārāyaṇa together with the Earthly Śrī for the sake of destroying the great Asura Analāda in the thirty-eighth year of the Creator [Brahmā] during the third Dvāpara cycle in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, as well as the manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Rasanārāyaṇa together with Śrī Rasalakṣmī for the sake of destroying the great Asura Ilodara-Rasāda in the thirty-ninth year. || 32 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, and I shall tell you of my manifestation thereafter;
it occurred in the fortieth year of the Creator, during the eighth kalpa.
And when the tenth Manu is present, throughout the world during the final Dvāpara age,
when the power of dharma has been weakened by the force of time among embodied beings who are prone to sin.
When the power of unrighteousness had spread, increasing the strength of the asuras,
the subjects were indeed oppressed and sacrifices were obstructed on all sides.
Charity, compassion, self-restraint, and the like have entirely vanished;
non-violence, truthfulness, and non-stealing are no longer seen upon the earth. (58)
Purity, austerity, and religious observances have indeed perished among living beings;
neither beneficence nor even good conduct is seen at all.
All oppress the weak, and the powerful enjoy their possessions; they even seize their wealth by force from every side.
Tens of millions of Daityas, Dānavas, and Asuras on earth are seen everywhere, having gone to their dissolution through pilgrimage.
The boundaries of conduct for men and women have indeed been destroyed by the Rākṣasas; all castes have become independent and devoid of righteousness and justice.
All worship of the gods has completely ceased;
the protection of children, the helpless, and guests has come to an end.
There arose atheism regarding all undertakings and all religious duties,
as well as the disparagement of elders and the oppression of the righteous.

In this world, all manner of things have been done by the Asuras— those who eat what is unfit to be eaten, those who drink what is unfit to be drunk, and those who perform actions that are improper and loathsome.
When all the kings on earth were of the Daitya lineage, the teachers were of the Daitya lineage, and even the preceptors were of the Daitya lineage.
Then all that pertains to the gods, the ancestors, and likewise that which leads to heaven, quickly went to dissolution;
at that time, by the gods, the sages, and men whose minds were fixed on dharma.
Indeed, he has personally propitiated the glorious Supreme Lord himself—the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the illustrious Puruṣottama. (14)
Then, in the abode of Jñānaviṣṇu, I became his son in form;
together with Sudarśana, I was the Lord Cakranārāyaṇa. || 15 ||
My mother was indeed aware [of my presence], and I became manifest from her womb;
at that time, by my command, you became an auspicious princess.
Then Sudhākṣiṇī was born from the womb of Queen Śobhālikā, the consort of King Brahmacitradhara, the sovereign of the whole earth.
Your father, the sovereign Sudhākṣi, personally arranged your svayaṃvara;
then, the kings who were the foremost among the Asuras held a great festival there.
At your command, all the sovereigns of your own realm as well as those of other realms arrived,
even the Vaimānika gods who dwell in celestial chariots and are formidable in their power.
"I am indeed a Vaiśya, the son of Jñānaviṣṇu, endowed with the discus; possessed of beauty, sovereignty, and virtue, I went there to the svayaṃvara. (3.33.20)
O Supreme Goddess, upon beholding me, you set aside them all and placed this most beautiful garland around my neck in the midst of the assembly.
Then those groups of kṣatriyas, enraged, rose up for battle;
by me, with the Sudarśana alone, ten thousand kings were struck down.
There is no counting those common to all; all the Daityas have been slain by me, and the Dānavas have been struck down, as well as all the Asuras brought low. (23)
Then your father, being my sole devotee, was protected by me;
consequently, being childless, he bestowed his own kingdom upon Sudhākṣiṇī.
Then, for a thousand years, I ruled the entire kingdom;
I established in the world and among the subjects the duties toward the gods and the ancestors.
Furthermore, the rules for gifts and sacrifices have been established by me,
the beginningless Śrī Cakranārāyaṇa, the conqueror of all.
"O Nārāyaṇīśrī, remember that sovereignty was indeed yours at that time;
for I know all of that, whereas no others know it. (27)
Through both recitation and hearing, enjoyment and liberation shall certainly be attained.
My other incarnations, numbering in the hundreds, are likewise protectors of the Dharma. (28)
At that time, many beings were born—gods, humans, and perfected siddhas—who protected the Dharma and bestow liberation; remember them, O Lotus-born One. (29)
Furthermore, in the forty-first year of the Creator, during the fifty-third kalpa called Adhvara, in the seventh Manvantara; (3.33.30)
O Śrī, listen to how my manifestation occurred during the sixty-seventh Kali age, which belongs indeed to the Supreme Brahman itself:
when the power of Kali had completely pervaded the world and people were likewise filled with barbarians (mlecchas). || 31 ||
In a world of uniform appearance, devoid of castes and stages of life;
in a body only a span high, with its dwelling in a cavity of the earth;
in a world subsisting on grass and roots, and free from rites for the gods and ancestors. (32–33)

In this world, where family ties have been severed everywhere, where there is only the pursuit of one's own self-interest, where people act according to their whims in pairs, and which is devoid of my light— 34—
a place of excessive affliction, meager happiness, and lacking any refuge.

And once [the world] had arisen, Hari himself appeared on earth for the sake of establishing the true dharma, having become the son of a devotee; the Lord himself, four-armed, was born as the son of the brahmin Drāvaṇa by name. || 35–36 ||
At that time, you, Śrī known as Vijayā, who abide eternally within my body as the seat of Brahmanic luster, became invisible in form along with me. Then,
for the sake of destroying the Asuras, Garuḍa was summoned by me.
There was a divine chariot and elephants with four tusks, white in luster;
all manner of weapons were present—maces, swords, arrows, and scimitars; bows, spears, thunderbolts, discs, javelins, barbed missiles, and lances. (38–39)
Bearing missiles and weapons, together with you, Vijayā,
I mounted the victorious, upward-soaring chariot that bore the Garuda banner;
traveling through the sky and capable of being borne by elephants, I fought against millions of asuras.
In the past, kings, barbarians, and powerful lords of the Daityas were destroyed. || 41 ||
The lords of the Dānavas, the lords of the Asuras, and then the Mleccha populations and others who had come for refuge were protected by me there in battle;
having made them drink water, those Brāhmaṇas were then honored at my feet. ||42||
And all of them were cast out from the interior of the fire of my manifestation;
ten million twice-born ones were purified and made into the body [of my teaching], and within all of them were established my dharmas born of truth. || 43-44 ||
By the power of my existence, all beings indeed became endowed with the quality of sattva; men and women became exceedingly pure,
and by my influence, everyone became devoted to truth and righteousness.
Wind, fire, water, earth, space, and the rest have attained the state of being sentient beings. ||46||
At that time, the trees, creepers, grasses, and other plants became filled with sap;
the Brahmins were indeed made into kings, and Yaśas was also set in motion.
Faith in the afterlife, the duty of giving, and the institution of marriage were established;
furthermore, virtuous men and women, as well as holy and auspicious perfected beings, were brought into existence.
Tiṣya was destroyed and Satya was established by me;
all the gods were protected and the sages were restored once more.
Temples were caused to be built and fire-chambers were established;
at that time, I dwelt upon the earth during the era of the Satya and Tretā Yugas.
Remember, O Lakṣmī, that ancient miracle of mine:
the beginningless Śrī Satyanārāyaṇa accompanied by Śrī Vijayā. 51.
The Supreme Brahman, who is himself the establisher of truth and the one who descends in incarnations—Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. ||22||
In this way, thousands of other incarnations of mine have also appeared here and there;
I alone know them all, and no one else.
By reading or hearing this, one shall become established in truth and righteousness; there shall be both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and one shall obtain whatever fruits are desired. ||54||
Now I shall tell you of another divine manifestation of mine:
in the forty-second year of Brahmā, during the epoch named Hiraṇya.
In the ninety-eon period at the commencement of the first Manu,
there were mountains on the earth that divided the twelve regions.
The co-parties, the independent ones, and likewise other islands and mountains—sentient, powerful, and embodied—engaged in debate for the sake of their respective positions. (57)
"I shall dwell in the vicinity of Meru, not far away," he said;
"I too [shall do so]," they replied—thus was their mutual discussion. (58)
Among them, those who were strong by virtue of their power remained there,
while others, having dwelt in their desired places, departed toward Manu.
They were summoned and exhorted by Manu to report their respective hardships;
nevertheless, being powerful, they did not heed Manu’s words at all.
Then he gave the command to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt,
to instruct Parvateśvara and to punish other mountains otherwise.
Indra, having arrived at the region of Mount Meru near the peak of Meru,
summoned the mountains in their embodied forms and spoke for their benefit.
"You were created by Brahmā for the sake of stabilizing the earth, for the purpose of dividing it into regions, and for the sake of [ensuring] treasures of jewels. (63)
For the sake of the task of protecting the subjects and for the purpose of repairing the broken walls,
those who were appointed to various places must remain in those very places by all means.
Dwell [here], for this is indeed for your benefit; my word must not be treated otherwise.
Otherwise, having forcibly stripped away your wings, I shall strike you all down to the ground with my thunderbolt in every way.
Having thus heard Indra’s words full of pride,
those formidable mountains immediately leapt into the sky;
all were powerful, exceedingly arrogant, and at that time capable of assuming any form at will.
Equal to the planets, they indeed fell upon Mahendra;
Indra, being crushed there, became as if dead.
Even the vajra of the Vajradhara was destroyed and turned to powder;
Indrabala was slain and then crushed by long mountains.
The Kaccaritas, the Suras, and others fled;
even the mountain-dwellers and those who move through the sky engaged in battle with the gods.
Deprived of its weight and having lost its level balance, the earth sank at its sides and began to descend toward the great depths of the waters.
Then portents occurred from all sides, even among the planets;
there was instability of the winds, and indeed, the mountains were shaken.
The entire sky, together with its mandalas, trembles as if at the time of dissolution;
yet the protection and stability of the earth is supported by the stability of the mountains. (72)
From the stability of the earth comes the stability of Meru and also of Dhruva;
this being so, there will be stability and happiness for the heavenly worlds. (73)
Having reflected, Brahmā, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and the other deities—great beings who were humble in disposition and possessed of minds intent on conciliation—suddenly [approached]. (74)
Then they awakened those mountains in many ways for the purpose of making them dwell in their assigned places; nevertheless, they did not heed it.
Hiraṇyaka, Kānaka, Rājata, Rātnaka, Māṇeya, Vaiṣṇava, Haimeya, and Digīśaka; ||76||
Bhairava, Mahendra, as well as Udayana-parvata, Āruṇa, Mahābha, Lokāloka, and Meruka. ||77||
In this way, other gods who were exceedingly fierce did not then perceive Nārāyaṇa as the one capable of pacifying the great affliction of the mountains. //78//
I, bearing the conch, the discus, and the mace, quickly remembered the Supreme Lord, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa Hari. 79.
The Supreme Brahman himself arrived there with great speed;
he held the Sudarśana discus, while I held the mace upon the earth.
Where the earth rose upward, there it became levelled by him as required; and she was protected by the weight of his held weapons. (81)
Then, O Lakṣmī, having summoned the mountains by means of a boon, they were joined together by me and made into my dwelling place. 82.
In whichever places on earth those mountains shall remain that I have mentioned,
there I myself, Śrī Puruṣottama, shall also abide.
Then those mountains, quickly following my word, were arranged all around Meru, including the Lokāloka mountain. ||84||
At the four corners, four rivers flowing to the ocean were created:
Hiraṇyakā at the southeast corner, and Kānakā at the southwest and northwest corners. 85.
The silver [mandala] is in the northwest corner (marutkoṇa), and the jewel [mandala] is in the northeast corner (īśakoṇa).
To the east, the Māṇeya and Vaiṣṇava [mandalas] extend toward the north and south.
In the south, there are Prāka and Paścalaṃba, as well as Haimeya and Digīśaka;
in the west, there are Uttara and Dakṣa, as well as Mairava and Mahendraka.
In the north, the two great mountains, Mahābhra and Cāyatu, were established; and in the eastern ocean was placed Udayana, accompanied by all the suns.
In this way, other mountains were also placed at intervals between them.
Then they made this request: "Indeed, let there be no destruction of our wings. (89)
And I have said, "Let those who are on your side indeed remain steadfast;
for if you possess the power of movement in the sky, then this [will come to pass]. (3.33.90)
Mahendra will have his wings clipped by Vajradhara;
thereafter, they shall attain stability and dwell happily in their respective places. (9.1)
Then all the gods and others, having worshipped me,
departed for their own worlds and for their dwellings upon the mountains together with you.
Assuming many forms, the Lord who provides protection caused [all things] to be fashioned;
indeed, I dwelt together with you, Hiraṇyā, until the end of the kalpa.
Anādiśrī, Hiraṇyaśrī, and Nārāyaṇa, the supreme among men—I, bound by my word, dwelt upon the mountains, awakening the gods. 94.
He [delighted] men, the ancestors, and the great sages who travel through the sky;
then the earth became stable and the mountains became happy.
By my dwelling here, the subjects have become fearless and likewise happy;
[I am] the beginningless, glorious, golden Nārāyaṇa, the supreme Lord. (96)
Remember Nārāyaṇīśrī; likewise, remember you as Hiraṇyā.
In this same way, there are other incarnations among gods, humans, and living beings.
I know all those who have existed in dependence upon their actions;
through reciting and hearing [this], auspicious enjoyment and liberation shall come to pass. 98.
Dwelling in the home of my rememberer occurs for me eternally;
and wherever my devotees, endowed with devotion, reside, there too [I dwell]. (99)
I dwell indeed, there is no doubt, upon mountains and in forests as well;
in houses and palaces, in great abodes and even in water.
For the sake of protecting my devotee, for the sake of his nourishment and protection as well, and also for the sake of the creation and protection of the gods and the worlds. || 101 ||
Making that very place my abode, I dwell there even though I am non-human;
for wherever I reside, right there is my imperishable realm.
All the liberated ones come to that very place and attain it there;
those who are subject to illusion do not see it, but those with divine vision do see it.

"O beloved, the Siddhas, the liberated ones, the virtuous, the holy, the stainless renunciants, the noble women, the truthful ones, and my devotees behold My birth. Thus, in the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*, in the third section concerning the lineage of the Dvāpara age, during the fortieth year of Brahmā, for the purpose of destroying the Daityas, there was the manifestation of the beginningless Śrī Cakranārāyaṇa together with Sudhākṣiṇī-Śrī; in the forty-first year, for the purpose of establishing the dharma of the Satya Yuga, there was the manifestation of the beginningless Śrī Satyanārāyaṇa together with Vijayā-Śrī; and in the forty-second year, for the sake of the mountains... [text continues].
The thirty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Hiraṇyanārāyaṇa, together with Hiraṇyāśrī, for the Purpose of Stability. || 33 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to my manifestation and that of others;
it occurred long ago in the forty-third year of Brahmā’s reign.
In the seventy-second kalpa, during the thirteenth Manvantara,
there was a lifelong devotee of Viṣṇu named Nirañjana.
That brahmin lived among the trees, subsisting on roots, leaves, and fruits;
he was eternally devoted to truth and righteousness, and constantly intent upon the chanting of the name of Hari.

He was devoted to breath control (prāṇāyāma) and intent upon the perfected posture (siddhāsana); he was dedicated to sensory withdrawal (pratyāhāra) and absorbed in concentration (dhāraṇā) and meditation (dhyāna). || 4 ||
Devoted solely to Viṣṇu in body, mind, speech, and soul,
he is self-controlled, a knower of Brahman, and free from passion, hatred, and other such afflictions.
Radiant like pure crystal, with an interior as stainless as the sky, full of affection for the company of the virtuous, and devoted to the service of the good. || 6 ||
My vision is that of Brahman, my effort is for Brahman, and my treasury of accomplishments is like that of Brahman;
for I am indeed as Brahmā, as Viṣṇu, and as Śambhu.
By the power of his worship, he became an ocean of all sovereign powers;
he assumed many forms and possessed the ability to enter the bodies of others.
Likewise, he possesses unimpeded movement through the worlds of the lords of gods and others;
he is perfected in meditative absorption, my devotee, and one who is solely devoted to me.
Once, while standing at the foot of a tree, he reflected:
"Today I shall ask Viṣṇu, who dwells within my heart, about his four arms. (3.34.10)
Reflecting thus, "What indeed is the divine vision of Nārāyaṇa like?",
he bathed at dawn and sat down for worship.
Having projected the four-armed Viṣṇu and worshipped him with all ritual offerings,
he then entered meditative absorption and summoned Viṣṇu, who stood before him.
And filled with humility, he questioned Viṣṇu of divine form as to what the divine vision of Nārāyaṇa is truly like.
Viṣṇu said: "I am indeed Nārāyaṇa; behold me!
I am the four-armed Śrīnivāsa, bearing the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus. (14)
Nirañjana said to him: "You are another Nārāyaṇa;
there is no Paranārāyaṇa. Show me the Supreme here."
Upon hearing this, Viṣṇu then became there one with a thousand arms,
equal to a thousand Viṣṇus in splendor, age, and qualities.
He said: "Behold Nārāyaṇa, the stainless one who is indeed higher than me;
from him, Viṣṇus like myself are produced day after day. (17)
Year after year, thousands dissolve again and again;
having heard, seen, worshipped, and bowed down, Nirañjana spoke.
Although this Lord is thousand-eyed, possesses a thousand arms,
and is the Supreme Nārāyaṇa, even so, there is another who is superior to him.
Nārāyaṇa indeed becomes [manifest] to him for whom my sight is dear;
having perceived and understood the desire of his devotee, Viṣṇu then acts accordingly.
He quickly transformed his form into that of Mahāviṣṇu,
which was served by Mahālakṣmī and resembled ten million Vairājas.
By means of his splendor, age, sovereignty, virtues, and the majesty of his divine powers, he revealed that form and said to the devotee, "Behold me! (22)
With arms reaching ten million yojanas and eyes casting ten million lotuses—
this is my supreme form, the cause of ten million heroic kings.
Having heard, understood, seen, bowed down to, and worshipped him, the stainless one said to Viṣṇu: "This is not even the supreme form of the Lord."
Beyond this, there exists yet another form which is the cause even of this form;
show me indeed that form which is supreme and higher than even this.
Having heard the devotee’s state of mind and understood it, Viṣṇu thereafter transformed his form into one even greater than that.
Equal to ten million Great Viṣṇus, surpassing ten million sovereign powers, and preeminent through beauty, charm, sweetness, splendor, and other such qualities. (27)
He has millions of billions of eyes and arms, and millions of billions of lotus-feet; he possesses more than millions upon millions of virtues—behold him, who is even greater than that! 28.
But Nirañjana, beholding him, bowed down and worshipped him with devotion;
having prostrated like a staff and offered a handful of flowers, he spoke.
O true Guru, by your grace I have seen this form, which possesses all sovereignty and is the controller even of all lords. (3.34.30)
I am satisfied, O Supreme Lord, having beheld this supreme form of yours, which is the creator of the lords of creation and the ruler of them as well. 3.1.
But I am not yet fully satisfied, for my mind runs forward to behold your supreme form, and beyond that, the transcendent form of the Supreme Lord.
Having heard and seen his state of devotion, Viṣṇu, whose form is the earth itself,
quickly transformed him into one with eyes like the petals of a lotus bud.
Then follows the stage of the lotus-born [Brahmā] beginning with the Arbuda, which possesses the good qualities of ten million times a hundred billion;
it produces ten million worlds and performs the deeds of ten million Saṃkarṣaṇas and others.
It is divine, having Vāsudeva as its essence, served by ten million Pradyumnas, and endowed with ten million Nārāyaṇas (Tejas) of great sovereignty, along with Aniruddha and others. ||35||
Beholding the Lord Vāsudeva, his mind became exceedingly joyful;
that king of devotees quickly prostrated himself before Him like a staff in great delight. (36)
Afterwards, he praised Viṣṇu with his heart, and He spoke to him again:
"The mind finds no satisfaction here; therefore, show me something superior to this. (37)
As long as there is a quartet, so long that supreme form cannot exist;
He alone is the non-dual Supreme Lord, higher than the highest. (38)
Having heard and understood his state of devotion, Viṣṇu then once again revealed his own beautiful form as Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
The devotee, having bowed to him and worshipped him, prostrated himself like a staff;
then Viṣṇu spoke to him again regarding that form.
Then he indeed revealed his own true form as Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa;
having bowed down, worshipped, and offered praise, the devotee spoke again in this manner. (41)
Beyond even this is the Supreme Brahman, Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of lords, the inner controller of all, the glorious Supreme Lord, Puruṣottama. (42)
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is the glorious Supreme Lord, the sovereign of Akṣara, the Protector served by millions of liberated souls and others. ||43||
O Viṣṇu, I truly desire to see Him who is stainless and even the one who descends through all incarnations; if You have compassion for me, show Yourself.
Viṣṇu said to me, "I have no authority over that stainless state; indeed, no one is capable of assuming the form of that Incarnate One. (45)
The incarnations, the lords, those with attributes and even those without attributes, as well as the portions, the manifestations, the parts, the infusions, and the great lords. ||46||
Furthermore, even the various manifestations (vibhavas) and their arrays (vyūhas) are never able to sustain those forms;
indeed, only the Incarnate Lord himself is capable of sustaining them.
Therefore, I am not capable of showing it to you;
yet, O stainless one, if you desire to behold it, [I shall show it]. 48.
Worship that Supreme Lord within you as your inner controller—Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. (49)
That which is your self is indeed my self, abiding in my heart;
in the imperishable, supreme abode, that very self is eternally situated.
The Supreme Brahman himself was pleased by your meditation, service,
intense worship, and your exceedingly great affectionate devotion.
Driven by compassion, He Himself will come here within the range of your vision;
therefore, worship Him, the Lord of Śrī, the Lord of all, the one Supreme Lord. ||5 2||
Worship Him, the Lord of all who are liberated, the Lord of all powers, the Lord of Ramā, who is borne by Māṇikī; you shall behold Keśava.
"Having two arms, enriched with all splendor, and the inner controller of all"—
having spoken thus, Viṣṇu suddenly vanished thereafter.
The Stainless One performed meditation upon me, who am present in all forms;
he also performed concentration (dhāraṇā), and likewise performed meditation once again. ||55||
Then he attained samādhi upon me, the glorious Puruṣottama;
through that samādhi, he entered into the imperishable, supreme abode.
And he beheld my supreme form together with you—divine, characterized by liberation, and distinct from all other incarnations and the like. (57)
That is indeed one without a second, supreme over all, and of the nature of the Absolute;
wherein exist all incarnations and all abodes whatsoever. (58)
Nirañjana beheld all the lords, their worlds, and all the emanations; he beheld the very root-form itself.
The devotee prayed to me: "Go with me to my own world;
become accessible to living beings for the sake of their ultimate liberation."
"Though I am subject to the devotion [of my devotees], I said to him at that time: 'So be it;
together with you and Śrī, I shall dwell upon the earth along with that devotee.'"
Then, O Lakṣmī, Śrī Puruṣottama himself appeared;
fulfilling the desires of my devotees, I became a human being in the world of mortals. (62)
Indeed, my manifestation occurred in the house of Nirañjana;
at that time, you were the attendant of that ascetic brahmin. (63)
O beloved, though I was named Niṣkiñcana (the Possessionless), you were born as my daughter;
and in time, knowing that I had descended [to earth], he offered her to me.
To the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, the Supreme Brahman beyond the imperishable, the eternal Supreme Lord. ||65||
And so, O beloved, I, the beginningless Śrī Nairañjanī-Nārāyaṇa, have attained renown together with you, who possess the fortune of absolute poverty.
I dwelt for a manvantara, liberating the human beings who took refuge in me;
remember that time, O Lakṣmī, and remember your own beautiful manifestation.
O my beloved, there were other incarnations of mine even in that kalpa;
I know them all, O Nārāyaṇī, but others do not know them.
"Innumerable living beings were indeed sent by me to liberation at that time;
and by you as well, innumerable living beings and virtuous women have been liberated. (69)
From reciting, hearing, remembering, and even retaining this,
there shall be both enjoyment and liberation, and one shall become possessed of bliss according to one's desire.
Your mother was named Agrahā, and my mother was Śutoṣiṇī;
she obtained as her daughter Śrī, and as her son, the Supreme Lord Hari, the Master. (71)
Those two [wives] were always liberated from their husbands;
those two, however, became the teachers' wives and both became mothers of the worlds. (72)
O beloved, those two lineages, glorious, bestowers of liberation, worthy of worship by all, and supreme abodes, then became eternally venerable. 73.
Furthermore, O Lakṣmī, listen to this other manifestation of mine:
in the forty-fourth year of Brahmā, at Kapālaka.
In the ninety-ninth kalpa above the nine hundred, during the Manu period called Advaya,
there was a virtuous woman named Puṇyavatī who was devoted to me and faithful to her husband.
The daughter of Vipra, Devapuṣpā, became the wedded wife of a Brahmin;
she was devoted to virtuous conduct, dedicated to dharma, and intent upon the worship of the gods.
Devoted to the service of her husband and dedicated to truth and righteousness, she was a performer of pilgrimages, an observer of vows, and intent upon the yoga of meditation. ||77||
The Brahmin was also righteous and devoted to the service of the virtuous;
however, the couple were indeed childless and overcome by old age.
A son was not born, nor did she give birth to a daughter;
being distressed by her longing for a son, Satī lamented her ill fortune again and again. (79)
Once, she cursed the Creator, the ordainer of destiny:
"Become dull-witted and bereft of progeny; become just as we two are! (3.34.80)
Then, in that very moment, the rod of creation fell from the hand of the Creator in Satyaloka,
just as a potter’s staff falls from his hand.
The wheel of saṃsāra fell from the stake onto the ground at its side;
and the globular jar of the cosmic egg shattered, blown apart by the force.
The thread was cast so far away, and the auxiliary tools were likewise flung;
Brahmā, however, fell into a state of stupor and became as if unconscious, like a corpse. ||83||
The potter’s workshop trembled from the crushing impact;
other vessels that had been made were shattered by the wheel. (84)
Then a great cry of "Alas! Alas! arose from all around the potter's workshop:
"Brahmā, the Creator, is dead!"—for he was indeed nearly dead, being in a state of unconsciousness. (85)
"We do not indeed know the cause," said those who perform rituals;
then Sāvitrī and the others arrived and wept upon seeing him unconscious.
The perfected ones, the great seers, and the lords of creatures also refreshed themselves there;
the sons of Brahmā, who carry out his tasks, arrived at the hall. (87)
All the guardians of the quarters and other Brahmās also arrived;
they looked again and again at him who was rendered inert by the curse and thus deprived of his power to create.
All of them, gathered there together, wailed in many ways;
likewise, those who were the sons of Brahmā and those who were the daughters of Brahmā.
Furthermore, being overcome by the curse of Brahmā regarding their childlessness,
they quickly became afflicted with disease and fell into a swoon, as if facing death.
Just as those two were bereft of sons and likewise bereft of daughters, so too was Brahmā bereft of his daughter and the rest, and Sāvitrī was likewise bereft. ||9 1 ||
Destined by fate to be deprived of sons, daughters, and the like, she saw her own sons and daughters afflicted with idiocy and disease. (92)
Because the curse was terrifying, he suddenly brought about the death of those who were about to die there;
the curse was thus set in motion by Satī for the purpose of leaving only two remaining.
Then Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Virāṭ, and Narāyaṇa were remembered by all;
and in an instant, they all arrived for the purpose of obstructing the curse.
Having consulted together and sought the cause, they went quickly toward the virtuous and meritorious woman on the earth, and there they indeed consoled her.
Having worshipped all the Blessed Ones, she spoke what was in her heart:
"How is it that my fortune has been made devoid of sons and daughters? (96)
"O lords of the gods, I shall not revoke the curse that has been given;
go home as you have come, otherwise you shall be cursed. (97)
Having understood and heard those powerful words of the devotee,
they were all struck with fear and remembered Śrīpati, the Supreme Person.
O lotus-born one, remembered by them, I, the Blessed Lord Hari—the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa—have indeed come there along with you. 99.
Upon seeing her Lord, the meritorious woman became bowed with shame;
beholding her chosen deity, the Supreme Lord, she went for refuge to me.
She quickly fell at the feet of both my husband and me;
having been addressed and consoled by me, she then begged for that pair.
Then, through the ascent of good fortune, there shall be an end to the curse of the Creator for my son, for me, as well as for your son’s wife and yourself.
When I said, "So be it," she spoke to the Creator: "Let him become dull-witted, and let there be no equality between him and us. (103)
"May she possess offspring and have many sons and daughters!"—
as soon as this was said, that Sucetanā quickly went to the pottery workshop.
Brahmā and the conscious offspring of Brahmā were indeed born desiring to live, impelled by the words of Satī.
I was born as her son right there, O Supreme Lord;
I am the beginningless Śrī Puṇyanārāyaṇa, the illustrious Puruṣottama.
And you, named Kalyāṇikā, became my daughter, a devoted one,
born as the offspring of the twice-born Agnihotra.
By him you were bestowed upon me according to the sacred rites and wedded to me; at that time, O Lakṣmī, you became known as Kalyāṇīśrī.
Remember my entire birth, which brings about all good fortune;
by reciting it, hearing it, or even remembering it, one obtains both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
O beloved, there were thousands of other such incarnations of mine at that time, which bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation, and protect the world.

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Nairañjanī-Nārāyaṇa together with Naiṣkiñcanī-Śrī for the sake of His devotees in the forty-third year of the Creator’s Dvāpara cycle within the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, and the Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Puṇya-Nārāyaṇa together with Kalyāṇikā-Śrī for the purpose of removing Brahmā’s affliction in the forty-fourth year. || 34 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, thereafter my manifestation occurred in the ocean of Apsarās during the forty-fifth year of the Kalpa of the Creator, in the thousandth cycle.
And in the second Manvantara, I, the primordial Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the bestower of liberation, was drawn [to her] by the devotional sentiments of all the Apsarases.
Listen, O Lotus-born one, to how I indeed became manifest upon the earth,
while in heaven, in the assembly of Mahendra at Satyaloka, amidst millions of gods.
Likewise, praise for me arises everywhere else as well—regarding my form, qualities, nature, sovereignty, happiness, and splendor. (4)
In touch, in sound, and in movement; in conduct, in satiety, in taste, and in strength; in bliss, in companionship, in yoga, in laughter, and in jest. || 5 ||
In lying down, in service, in delusion, in gesture, in emotion,
in attraction, in joy, in delight, in dalliance, in festival, in eating, and in remaining [in these states].
In sitting, riding, traveling, dwelling, drinking, and dancing;
in amorous adornment, fragrance, valor, prowess, and in action— (7)
In matters of passion, in action, in clarity, and in enjoyment, there is no other equal to the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (8)
Upon hearing such praise, millions of apsarases in heaven conceived a longing for union with me, for my company, and for delight in amorous play.
But those women, having abandoned all enjoyments and being eager for the sake of attaining me, performed many vows like human beings. (3.35.10)
May the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, become our husband, by which we may indeed be satisfied in every way. 1.1.111.
Having thus resolved, they all performed my worship;
then, by means of a voice from the sky, it was indeed announced to them by me.
May all human women become auspicious maidens through their own portions—whether they be daughters of kings, daughters of Brahmins, or daughters of devotees—in every way. (13)
"From this day forward, may they indeed take birth as they desire upon the surface of the earth,
in the region to the west of Meru, in the realm known as Hemaratha."
There, indeed, I shall be born as a human being, a preeminent Kṣatriya, the foremost of a radiant lineage—the Supreme Brahman, Hari himself. (1.5)
Thus addressed, those Apsarases took up births in every way;
O Lakṣmī, I was born together with you in the region named Hemaratha.
Then, in the radiant royal palace of King Bṛhadindra, within the illustrious lineage of Kṣatriyas,
I indeed manifested swiftly from Queen Prabhāvatī.
Adorned with the conch, discus, mace, lotus, kaustubha gem, and other [emblems], my parents are devoted to me; therefore, my fortune and good luck are blessed. 1.8.
The celestial drums resounded, and even the great sages performed auspicious rites;
they offered prayers and worship, and the lords increased their blessings.
A rain of flowers fell from the path of the sky, foreboding auspiciousness;
the king, the subjects, the gods, and the great seers all celebrated the festival.
Then, you were manifested from the womb of Queen Rukmacampā, the consort of King Gavendra, as the most beautiful woman endowed with all auspicious fortune.
With a body possessing the luster of refined gold and endowed with every auspicious mark,
she was offered to me when the time suitable for marriage had arrived.
This beautiful woman was given to me by your father and likewise by your mother;
there, that most lovely lady was wedded to me according to the prescribed rites. (23)
At the wedding festival of that sovereign king, by my command, the royal lineages as well as other merchant lineages [were present]. (24)
Lineages of Brahmins, lineages of Kṣatriyas, and lineages of Vaiśyas arrived;
as did those Apsarases who had seen me in a dream at night. (25)
My marriage was performed with Hari, the Supreme Soul.
On the night of your wedding, they saw me as their husband and lord.
Then they reached a decision: "At our own choice-marriage (svayaṃvara), we ourselves shall choose a husband by offering him the bridegroom's garland. || 27 ||
Then the Supreme Self, endowed with great sovereignty,
granted those maidens— who were for his sake— a vision of their parents.
"In a dream, during that festival, my two parents gave their own daughter to me";
then, upon waking, the parents [beheld] all [the girls] according to their true nature.
They both gave various daughters to me, the glorious Supreme Soul;
indeed, crores of celestial nymphs, having obtained me as their desired beloved, [remained with me].
They attained supreme bliss and reached unsurpassed happiness;
at that time, the king became a universal monarch (cakravartin) for the duration of one Manvantara. || 31 ||
By name he was Samrāṭ Bṛhadbrahmanārāyaṇa, the lord of kings; at that time I had sons numbering ten million, a hundred million, and a billion, as well as daughters.
Likewise, they became innumerable and were established in royal lineages; my grandsons and granddaughters' sons consisted of the essence of the Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas.
Likewise, kings born on earth were of the nature of progeny;
then, at the end of the Manvantara, he liberated those wives thereafter.
O Nārāyaṇī, I too went to the forest together with you;
in the forest, I became invisible along with you. (35)
In this way, worship of me also has been set in motion among the worlds, forever for the beginningless Śrī Bṛhadbrahmanārāyaṇa. 36.
O Lotus-born One, together with you and Rukmavatī, remember everything until the end of the kalpa— both your manifestation and mine, O Queen of Śiva.
In this way, many other incarnations also occurred during that kalpa;
by reading or even hearing [of them], supreme enjoyment and liberation shall be attained. (38)
There shall be the fruit of all sacred fords (tīrthas), as well as the fruit of vows, the fruit of gifts, and whatever fruit may arise from the study of the Vedas. ||39||
There shall be the destruction of all sins and the attainment of all bliss;
one shall partake of all joy, and likewise, there shall be the attainment of me.
Now I shall further declare my manifestation; listen to that:
in the forty-sixth year of the Creator, during the Brahma-sārasa [era]. (41)
Formerly, in the first Kṛta age, during the sixth of the nine Manvantaras, wise great sages were created by Brahmā, O Brahmins. (42)
They dwelt upon the surface of the earth in the land of action (karmabhūmi), residing in the region of Tura;
they were all perceivers of direct reality and devoted solely to all the dharmas. ||43||
The knowledge of Brahman became inherent and spontaneously operative for them;
then, when the Tretā Yuga arrived, it underwent a partial decline.
The great seers engaged in debates with one another through logic, and they became forgetful, struck down by ignorance over the course of time. (45)
Then they worshipped me, the glorious Lord, the Supreme Person, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the illustrious Supreme Controller.
I appeared in their midst as the bestower of knowledge. (46)
He taught him the supreme Vedic knowledge as well as other sciences, the knowledge of the Vedas, the knowledge of the Self, and those consisting of religious rites. (47)
At that time, he also taught other sciences to the great sages—those auspicious sciences which destroy false reasoning and bring about the realization of worship and devotion. 48.
I, the preceptor of the great sages, became the bestower of Vedic knowledge, teaching that lore which grants liberation, bestows heaven, and confers welfare.
Having become a Brahmin with a voice like that of Brahmā, the son of a ṛṣi, established in a state of dignity, he indeed caused the scriptures to be recited while attended by hosts of great sages.
With you, Suvidyā, who are like a daughter of the Ṛṣis dwelling within my heart, I shall live until the end of the Dvāpara age, together with you, the goddess Śrī named Suvidyā.
"O beloved, at that time, remember the beginningless Śrī Guru Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, and you yourself as the presiding deity of all knowledge. (52)
In this way, many other incarnations also occurred at that time;
I know all of them, O Supreme Goddess—remember them! (53)
From reciting and hearing this, darkness shall dissolve from its very root;
the light of Brahman shall arise, and one shall attain the vision of the Self. (54)
Thus, my manifestation within the lotus has been described to you;
now I shall tell you something else concerning my very nature as the Supreme Brahman.
In the forty-seventh year of the Svardhūnī [cycle], during the eighteenth kalpa, in the eighth Manvantara, one hundred and thirty-eight years [elapsed]. (56)
There was a king named Bṛhaddharmā, a lord of men who was devoted to me;
he commenced the magnificent Rājasūya sacrifice. (57)
In the renowned capital city of Ojasvatī, the king himself caused various sacrifices,
animal sacrifices, and Soma sacrifices to be performed.
He caused one hundred and thirty-nine iṣṭis to be performed;
he caused six soma sacrifices and seven darvīhomas to be performed.
On the first day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna,
he should commence that sacrifice, and it shall last for one year.
The king caused the Cāturmāsya rites to be performed according to the prescribed rules,
and he also caused the sacrifices to Vaiśvānara and Parjanya to be performed.
The [oblation] for Agni, for Soma, for Savitṛ, and thereafter for Sarasvatī;
then for Pūṣan, for the Maruts, for the Viśvedevas, and for Heaven and Earth.
In that parvan known as Vaiśvadeva, the king himself performed these eight sacrifices, and there he worshipped the deities in their proper order.
He offered a cake on eight potsherds to Agni,
a caru-oblation to Soma, and one on twelve potsherds to Savitṛ.
He offered a sacrificial pap (caru) to Sarasvatī and likewise gave a pap to Pūṣan;
to Marut, however, he gave a pap made of flour on seven potsherds.
He gave the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) to the Viśvedevas and gave the curd-mixture (āmikṣā) [to them];
he gave the auspicious single-pot-sherd offering (ekakapālaka) to Heaven and Earth.
Then, O King, the king himself gratified Puroḍāśa, as well as Madhu, Mādhava,
Śukra, and Śuci there with offerings of ghee.
Having thus performed the Vaiśvadeva-parvan, the king then duly performed the second [parvan], the Varuṇapraghāsa-parvan. (68)
The [offerings] dedicated to Agni, Soma, Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, and Pūṣan;
as well as those for Indra-Agni, the Maruts, Varuṇa, and Ka.
There he performed the Avayāja offerings, as well as those for Agni Stoma,
Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, and Pūṣan.
The king duly performed the worship of Indra, Agni, the Maruts, and Varuṇa in their proper order, using the respective materials such as oblations and other offerings.
Having offered oblations with the mantras "nabham," "nabhasyam," "iṣam," and "ūrjam," he satisfied the deities;
he performed the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) and also undertook the prescribed observances.
And thereafter, he also caused the third festival, the Sākamedha, to be performed,
as well as the Anīkavatī and other sacrifices, and the Mahāhavis offerings.
He also caused the ancestral sacrifice (pitṛyajña) and the Tryambaka oblations to be performed;
he summoned Ṛṣabha and indeed had the Krīḍaneṣṭi sacrifice conducted.
He gratified Saha, Sahasya, Tapasa, and Tapasya;
thereafter, he performed the great Pitṛyajña according to the prescribed rites.
He gratified the Agniṣvātta ancestors who sit upon the sacrificial grass;
he offered funeral cakes according to the prescribed rite and presented the oblations for Tryambaka.
He offered an oblation to Rudra and established Āditi as the presiding deity;
thereafter, he performed the Śunāsīrīya sacrifice with sacrificial porridge (caru).
The king caused the rites dedicated to Agni and the others to be performed according to the rules;
likewise, he caused the rites for Indra-Agni and those for the Viśvedevas to be performed.
He likewise caused the Śunāsīrīya, Vāyavya, and Saurya sacrifices to be performed,
and he also gratified the respective deities of those rites.
He likewise offered a cake on a single potsherd (ekakapāla) under the name of Adhikamāsa;
thus, he performed all the sacrifices pertaining to the full moon within the course of a year.
Then the king also caused the six types of Soma sacrifices, beginning with the Pavitra,
to be performed in succession, each accompanied by the gift of a thousand cows as a sacrificial fee.
He also gave [offerings] to Anumati and others, and caused the eight sacrifices to be performed;
he offered a cake on eight potsherds (*aṣṭākapāla*) to Anumati.
The king likewise offered a sacrificial pap (caru) dedicated to Āditya,
and he also presented an oblation on eleven potsherds (ekādaśakapālaka) dedicated to Agni and Viṣṇu.
He gave an offering of eleven potsherds dedicated to Agni and Soma,
and then one of eleven potsherds dedicated to Indra, and thereafter one dedicated to Agni.
With that [offering], the king gave an oblation of curd for Indra on eight potsherds, as well as a caru-oblation for Indra and Agni on twelve potsherds, and one for the Viśvedevas. ||85||
He offered a gentle oblation of śyāmāka grain, a sacrificial pap (caru) for Sarasvatī,
a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, and a caru of gāvīdhuka grain for Rudra.
He offered curd for Indra and a sacrificial pap made of barley for Varuṇa;
thereafter, the king caused oblations to be performed with Apāmārga plants.
The king gave a sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) on twelve potsherds to Dhātṛ; he gave an oblation of boiled rice (caru) to Anumati and an oblation of boiled rice to Rākā. ||88||
He gave an oblation of cooked rice to Sinīvālī and an oblation of cooked rice to Kuhū, and he also gave sacrificial fees;
furthermore, he gave a cow and a bull, and then other offerings as well.
The king offered a cake on eleven potsherds dedicated to Agni and Viṣṇu,
and likewise he offered a similar sacrificial cake dedicated to Indra and Viṣṇu.
The king likewise offered a cake on three potsherds dedicated to Viṣṇu,
and then one on eleven potsherds dedicated to Agni-Soma.
He gave a sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) for Indra and Soma, and likewise another such one;
he also gave a pap (caru) for Soma, and he gave a pap for Soma and Pūṣan. ||92||
The king likewise gave a caru-offering dedicated to Indra and Pūṣan, as well as one to Pūṣan alone,
and then an auspicious cake on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara.
He performed a sacrifice and offered a *caru* oblation to Varuṇa; then he offered a *caru* to Bṛhaspati and an eleven-potherd cake (*ekādaśakapāla*) to Indra.
Then he offered a sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa), and thereafter he offered a caru-oblation to Āditya;
and [he offered] a caru-oblation to Nirṛti and an eight-potsherd cake (aṣṭākapāla) dedicated to Agni.
He offered a sacrificial cake on ten potsherds dedicated to Varuṇa,
and likewise he offered a sacrificial cake on seven potsherds dedicated to the Maruts.
He offered a cake on twelve potsherds dedicated to Savitṛ;
likewise, he offered a cake on two potsherds dedicated to the Aśvins.
Then the king offered an oblation of cooked rice (caru) to Pūṣan and also one to Rudra;
thereafter, the king had twelve sacrifices performed by the brahmins.
He performed the Dīkṣaṇīyā sacrifice to Mitra and Bṛhaspati;
thereafter, he offered eight oblations in the Agniṣomīya rite.
Then the king himself offered a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds to Agni, and he gave an oblation of śyāmāka grain to Soma.
Then the king gave a cake on twelve potsherds to Savitṛ,
and he gave a caru-oblation of gāvīdhuka grain to Rudra.
He also gave an oblation of wild rice to Bṛhaspati,
and he offered a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra.
Having offered a *caru* oblation to Mitra and a barley-based *caru* to Varuṇa,
and having thus performed all the sacrifices, the king remained there.
Brahmā, having touched the hand of the king, announced him to the subjects:
"This man is your king. The subjects accepted the monarch. || 1.07 ||
They performed the consecration with waters and he celebrated the Rājaṣaṭhoma sacrifice,
which was endowed with all ritual materials and the like, and which brought delight to the deities.
After the *pārtha-homa*, the two kings ascended the chariot;
having performed the *ratha-mocana-homas*, the king remained seated upon it.
After listening to the discourse from the Brahmins and giving them gold,
he thereafter performed the Vaiśvadeva rite as well as the Māhendra sacrifice.
Having performed the Avabhṛtha sacrifice, he prepared ten oblations;
then he offered a cake on eight potsherds dedicated to Agni.
After that, the king also offered a *caru* oblation to Sarasvatī,
and he gave a twelve-potherd sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) dedicated to Savitṛ.
Then the king also gave an oblation of cooked rice (caru) for Pūṣan and an oblation of cooked rice for Bṛhaspati;
thereafter, he offered an oblation on eleven potsherds for Indra.
He offered an oblation on ten potsherds to Varuṇa, a sacrificial pap (caru) to Soma,
an oblation on eight potsherds to Tvaṣṭṛ, and an oblation on three potsherds to Viṣṇu.
He offered the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) and likewise performed the Saṃsṛp rites;
the king himself bestowed excellent sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās) within the pavilion.
To the Adhvaryu, two golden mirrors adorned with jewels;
to the Udgātṛ, a golden garland; and to the Hotṛ, a circular one.
The king gave a horse adorned with ornaments to the Prastotṛ and the Pratihartṛ;
to the Brahman priest, he gave ten cows pregnant with young calves.
Then the king gave a barren cow to the Maitrāvaruṇa priest;
at that time, the king also gave a bull to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest. (11.5)
Then he gave two clean, beautiful garments to the Neṣṭṛ and the Potṛ;
and he then gave a cart filled with barley to the Acchāvāka.
The king likewise gave a bull to the Agnīdhra priest according to the prescribed rule;
then, having performed the Daśapeya sacrifice, he indeed undertook a vow.
The king performed the rite known as the shaving of the hair for a period of one year,
and thereafter he undertook the Soma sacrifice consisting of the Atirātra ritual.
He also caused the Vyuṣṭidvirātra and the Kṣatradhṛti sacrifices to be performed; thereafter, the king likewise performed the Sautrāmaṇī according to the prescribed rites.
The king indeed performed the final purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), consisting of oblations of milk-offerings dedicated to Indra, the Aśvins, Sarasvatī, and Indra-Vāyu. 3.35.1–20.
Thus the king performed various acts of charity and gave away many gifts;
he desired to bestow his kingdom and then take up the auspicious and virtuous initiation.
Having indeed sought [permission] from his chosen deity, he announced it to the Brahmins;
for the sake of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), he gave the entire earth to the Brahmins as a gift.
For my sake, he who is the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, undertook a vow of fasting together with his consort.
Having come in person and initiated me, he caused me to become a virtuous man;
he then offered the fruit of sacrifices such as the Rājasūya to Lord Hari.
Having understood that resolve and even the request of the brahmins,
O Lotus-born One, I indeed went with you for the sake of fulfilling the desire of your devotee.
He suddenly appeared, resembling ten million suns;
they offered him a welcome and performed worship for him, and then I too did so.
The brahmin great sages bestowed upon the king the auspicious, virtuous, and liberating great initiation (mahādīkṣā), and they also conferred initiation upon the queen after observing them.
Those one hundred thousand received the great initiation from me alone;
appearing in the form of an ācārya, I instructed them in the duties of the virtuous.
O beloved, all those subjects born from her became followers of Viṣṇu and attained liberation; at that time, you were born as Satī, the great preceptor of women.
From that, I became the beginningless Śrī Mahācārya Nārāyaṇa;
then Hari himself, joined by his consort, the beginningless Śrī Mahācāryāṇī.
Requested by the virtuous, I indeed wandered upon the surface of the earth for the duration of a Manvantara in divine form,
devoted solely to the dharma of liberation.
Remember both you and me, O Lakṣmī, in our forms as the Great Teacher;
likewise, there have been thousands of other incarnations of mine.
The king was named Rājasūyāyana, for he had been initiated for the Rājasūya sacrifice;
and at that time, his virtuous queen became the very embodiment of the glory of the Rājasūya.
O beloved, from reciting or hearing this, there shall be enjoyment and liberation;
even heaven and final release shall occur, and passion shall turn into dispassion. (134)
Ignorance shall dissolve, and all bonds shall go to destruction;
one shall become possessed of a divine form and shall be worthy of being served by those who share in merit in this very world. || 135 ||

Thus, in the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā, within the third section, the Dvāpara-santāna: in the forty-fifth year of the Creator (Brahmā), for the purpose of fulfilling the desires of the Apsarases who had become human, there appeared the beginningless Śrī Bṛhadbrahma-Nārāyaṇa accompanied by Rukmavatī-Śrī; in the forty-sixth year, for the purpose of bestowing the knowledge of Brahman and other sciences upon the great sages, there appeared the beginningless Śrī Guru-Nārāyaṇa accompanied by Suvidyā-Śrī; and in the forty-seventh year, [there appeared] the devotee of Hari...

The thirty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Mahācārya Nārāyaṇa and the Venerable Ācāryāṇī, who were requested for the purpose of the Great Initiation of the virtuous queen after King Bṛhaddharma had given away all his possessions in the Rājasūya sacrifice. || 35 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to my manifestation thereafter,
during the kalpa known as Vedhasa, in the year named Arcirmārga.
Now, during the fifth Manu-period, in the eight hundred and sixty-seventh [year],
the Rākṣasa Vidyutsrāva was indeed born from the womb of Rudrakukṣi.
He performed severe penance for the purpose of pleasing Śambhu and to obtain a splendor that surpassed the brilliance of the sun, the moon, and fire.
When five hundred years had passed, Śaṅkara himself was pleased with supreme affection and urged her to choose a boon.
He too chose a boon: "May I possess a supreme splendor, like that of the sun, the moon, and fire, which may be as great as I desire and indeed indestructible even by the gods."
"So be it," Hara said, having received the boon and being filled with great joy;
abandoning his asceticism and becoming radiant, he went to heaven and returned.
The Apsarases were bewildered, and even the goddesses fell into a state of infatuation; seeing him, those fickle women pursued him, though they were restrained by the gods.
Indeed, this new affliction has arisen for the gods in the heavenly realm;
even a Daitya, resplendent like a god, has assumed the form of a Rākṣasa.
Richly adorned with divine ornaments, he travels from heaven to heaven;
he utterly deludes even the goddesses and instigates strife as well.
Having become superior to the sun, beautiful of form, possessed of great splendor, and bearing a radiant luster,
he approaches the sun and eclipses the maker of light.
It approaches the moon and eclipses it with its brilliance;
it likewise approaches the submarine fire and even approaches the planets.
In the netherworld and other realms, he approaches and even surpasses the holders of jewels;
likewise, in the great waters at the bottom of the ocean, he outshines the gems of the sea-monsters.
Having indeed eclipsed the lights,
that Daitya, who can assume any form at will, displayed his own pride, realizing his own great strength.
Desiring to become king, he went to the city of Kubera;
he fought intensely with Kubera and brought that city under his own control.
Then he went to Vahni in battle, conquered him, and brought him under his own control;
he also went to conquer Candra, and he too became subject to his power.
Desiring to conquer the sun, that great asura Vidyutsravas set out for Ravi for the sake of battle; he fought for four months.
He suffers no defeat and undergoes not even the slightest exhaustion;
yet, manifesting flashes of lightning, he causes the worlds to be consumed by fire.
With a splendor exceeding that of the sun, it scorched these three worlds;
then a cry of "Alas! Alas! arose, and the sun, distressed, lamented.
He remembered the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Lord, the Eternal One—
me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Puruṣottama.
"I have arrived, glorious and endowed with splendor, the Lord who provides protection from the sun; I am indeed the golden Supreme Ruler, possessing all radiant energy, missiles, and weapons."
O Lakṣmī! Together with you, who are known as Īśānī and possess all powers, he performs the hospitable rites such as the worship due to him which was performed by the Sun.
Indeed, with my Sudarśana discus, I struck down that asura;
Vidyunmālin met his destruction and fell into the ocean.
At that time, I extinguished the fires unleashed by him upon the worlds,
along with tens of millions of gods, sages, gandharvas, grahas, and humans.
Praised by all beings, I indeed performed a journey;
in the sun I am Hiraṇmaya, and as Hari, I possess golden hair.
In the moon, I am one with a silver body and curly hair, being Hari himself;
in fire, O Lord, I become one with a blazing body and radiant whiskers.
Then, on the surface of the earth, entreated by human beings along with you,
I became the beginningless Śrī Mahāvidyunārāyaṇa.
Endowed with the splendor of lightning, I dwelt here in this world of men for the duration of a Manvantara, indeed for the sake of the liberation of human beings. (27)
Remember Lakṣmī and me, for our manifestation has indeed arisen in that manner;
likewise, many other incarnations of mine have appeared upon the earth.
From reciting and hearing this, there shall be the destruction of suffering in this world;
there shall be enjoyment here, and in the end, liberation in the eternal state. (29)
Now I shall tell you something else; listen, O beautiful one, to this manifestation:
in the year of the Creator known as Abdimathana, increased by nine [months]. (3.36.30)
O Lakṣmī, in the third Manvantara, during the one hundred and fifty-second kalpa, I came into this world together with you.
The son of the Daitya Rasātala, who subsisted on liquids,
was the powerful Daitya Madhubhakṣa, who in former times became so through his ascetic penance.
He then performed intense penance on the mountain named Sundara;
having propitiated Śaṅkara through his austerity, he indeed chose a boon from Śaṅkara.
May my power be vast to enjoy savory juices and to enjoy honey;
and as I consume them, may there be digestion accordingly. (34)
May there never be indigestion for me at any time;
may I have no loss of appetite, and may there be great nourishment and strength. (35)
Having heard this, Śaṅkara said: "Without killing the medicinal herbs and trees, eat the juices and honey; otherwise, what else but death awaits you? (36)
Having thus granted the boon, Hara became invisible;
meanwhile, the Asura Madhubhakṣa remained on Mount Sundara among the trees and other vegetation.
Having entered them all through his illusory power, he sucks the honey within;
he sucks the honey from every source, including that which resides in leaves, flowers, and so forth.
Fruits do not form at all, even the leaves wither, and from that point on, no new sprouts grow whatsoever. (39)
Then he enjoys the sap of the roots, the sap of the stalks, the sap of the trunks, and thereafter the sap of the branches— he partakes of all these essences.
He also sucks the juices from the twigs and the juices from the leaves;
he indeed sucks all the juices of the flowers and the juices of the fruits.
From trees, from creepers, from shrubs, from the roots of grass, from bulbous roots, and from stalks—he enjoys all kinds of juices. (42)
Through his illusory power, Śatarūpa assumes a thousand, ten thousand, ten million, a hundred million, and a billion forms, and having manifested them again and again, he devours [them] excessively.
In whatever manner they consume flavors, all of these are digested;
thus he becomes nourished, strong, and capable of eating even more.
And by means of his illusory power (māyā), he assumed a vast body upon the mountains and in the forests,
in the wilds and even in great gardens, as well as among the trees of palatial mansions.
In the gardens, in all cultivated crops, in all trees,
in sprouts, in fruits— whether ripe or unripe— in every way.
He always consumes the juices of honey and makes the trees wither;
indeed, the forests, the fields, and the groves all become parched.
Neither by offspring, nor by cattle, nor by birds, nor by creatures,
nor even by living beings are the flavors and the spring seasons ever exhausted.
Afflicted by hunger, everyone dies untimely deaths;
a famine destructive to life has arisen even without drought. (49)
And from the netherworlds (pātāla) among the worlds of men,
the great asura arrived, sucking up the earth-dwelling creepers and trees.
He suddenly rendered all kings, emperors, and even plants such as creepers, grasses, and trees sapless and withered in form. (51)
The foods of human beings and the foods of the gods—all those which have their essence in taste—have completely perished in every way. (52)
All kinds of honey were drunk by that Rākṣasa;
thus strengthened, he became powerful and pervasive like the wind. ||53||
By virtue of the boon, he became all-pervading among the plants through his great power;
and by means of his illusory energy (māyā), that Daitya became a devourer of all living beings.
Since the clouds were useless and likewise the cultivation was fruitless, the earth’s provision of its essence was then rendered purposeless. (55)
The sapid potency of all seeds was rendered useless by that very asura for the sake of the subjects, and the world was tormented by hunger. (56)
By that act, he then propitiated both Hari and me—the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama. (57)
Having heard their prayer and perceiving the oppression by the asuras,
as well as the loss of vitality in the medicinal herbs, he came toward the earth.
Bearing the conch, discus, mace, lotus, Śārṅga bow, and other weapons myself,
I, Hari, in my divine form, indeed fought with him at that time.
Madhubhakṣa was slain by me with the Sudarśana discus;
you, Mādhavī Lakṣmī, having been made by me, were placed within the trees.
O Lakṣmī, you then became the essence of sweetness, consisting of nectar, among all species of trees; you were the exalted glory of the Mādhavī creeper. 6.1
I, the beginningless and glorious Nārāyaṇa, dwelt as a visible presence among all creatures for the duration of a Manvantara together with you.
Through that entry, the trees then became filled with sap;
indeed, in all worlds and everywhere, the trees began to flow with honey.
Then the rivers flowed with honey, the cows yielded milk sweet as honey, and the herbs were filled with honey, fragrant with the scent of spring.
They became sprouted, fruit-bearing, and yielding honey;
at that time, O Lakṣmī, I was Mādhava, consisting of nectar, together with you.
And even when the Supreme Lord stayed among the trees and other places with Mādhavī,
the people there worshipped us two, Mādhavī and Mādhava.
"Remember me in the form of Mādhavī and yourself as the essence of Madhurasā;
and at that time, O beloved, the other gods and great sages [will remember me as well]. (67)
They worshipped the Supreme Lord, the giver of life, with supreme affection.
O Nārāyaṇī, I have thus described to you my very manifestation. 68.
They too are the protectors of the world and of all embodied beings;
furthermore, I shall now declare another [teaching] concerning the manifestation of both you and me.
In the fiftieth year of the Creator, named Nārada, during the eighty-eighth [year] of the fourth century, in the eighth Manvantara; (3.36.70)
During the Tiṣya and Saptarṣi ages on this earth, the Daityas, Dānavas,
and Asuras became entirely atheistic destroyers of dharma.
The laws and human virtues were lost, and great cruelty prevailed;
all men and women became eaters of flesh and took on the appearance of barbarians (mlecchas).
Evil-natured, performers of evil deeds, devoted solely to wickedness, snatchers of everything, eaters of everything, consumers of all things, they have strayed onto the wrong path. ||73||
For humans indeed devour animals, flocks of birds, and living beings;
what need is there to mention that humans also devour other humans? (74)
O Lakṣmī, other living beings on earth raised cries of "Alas! Alas!
for indeed, the wild animals had been devoured by humans. (75)
Even when birds have been devoured, they do not necessarily meet again;
indeed, forests and wildernesses became places of destruction for beasts and birds.
Then, being deprived of wild animals and birds, those humans indeed began to eat domestic animals and birds. (77)
Female buffaloes, ewes, and all female sheep were devoured; horses, camels, donkeys, and even bulls were likewise eaten. (78)
There were also elephants, gavayas, deer, and monkeys;
bears, lions, beasts of prey, dogs, boars, and so forth. ||79||
All were devoured by cruel Rākṣasas, Daityas, and Dānavas;
likewise, all the cows and calves were eaten by such humans.
And when cows are being devoured by meat-eaters on earth, then I come for their protection, even though I am not impelled [by anyone]. (8.1)
All the gods reside within cows; by virtue of propitiating them, I am the lord who destroys the suffering of the gods and provides protection for the cows. (82)
O beloved, Hari himself, the protector of the Dharma on earth, has also swiftly arrived along with you, bearing all his weapons. (83)
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the glorious Puruṣottama, the Supreme Lord, indeed assumed this form for the purpose of protecting the cows. (84)
The creator of all protection, the protector of Dharma, the Lord of Śrī, and the Master—I, the destroyer of the defects of the Kali age, indeed quickly became visible. 85.
Standing upon the chariot called Akṣara, where the bull was being slain upon the earth,
he went swiftly through the path of the sky to that spot and indeed struck him down.
The slayer of the cow, the killer, and even other killers—though he did not kill them there and then, they became enraged at him as they stood before him. (87)
Having gathered together, those Dānavas, Daityas, and crores of Asuras—mostly Mlecchas—came from various places to strike me down. (88)
Having roamed across the entire earth in battle, I slew those cruel ones by the hundreds of millions and billions; indeed, the subjects were liberated through my virtuous nature.
Through my connection with Vāyu, the virtuous beings became disciplined;
protection was afforded to the cows, to the Brahmins, and likewise to the righteous.
The protection of the Dharma has been accomplished, and the gods have been gratified by me;
those who abide in truth and righteousness have been established, and the barbarian kings have been struck down. (91)
Non-violence has been established, as well as my own worship;
furthermore, everything for the purpose of worshipping the gods has been re-established. (92)
The duty of service and the duty of compassion have been established by me once again;
thus, I, the beginningless Śrī Nātha Nārāyaṇa, have become firmly established upon the earth.
As the protector of the helpless cows, you bore the name Nātha;
and then, O Lakṣmī, you became Śrī by name, the mistress of the cows. (94)
Having remained on earth for half a yuga as the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), I went with you to the imperishable abode; remember that birth. 95.
Thus, for the sake of instructing the people of the Tiṣya age, I indeed manifest again and again as incarnations such as Aṃśa, Āveśa, Kalā, and Bhūti. (96)
Indeed, there is no counting them; they arise according to the requirements of their tasks.
Having accomplished their task, they dissolve into me alone, who am Śiva-Śambhu.
In age after age, whether by my own will or under the influence of my devotees,
I, the Lord who acts for the welfare of all, indeed descend upon the earth out of compassion.
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), the incarnator, the Supreme Brahman, and the Lord Śrī Parameśvara himself. 99.
