From reciting and hearing this, there shall be both enjoyment and liberation;
furthermore, the attainment of all desired fruits shall occur here in every way.

Thus, in the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*, within the third section, the *Dvāpara-Santāna*, during the forty-eighth year of the Creator (Brahmā), for the sake of destroying the Rākṣasa Vidyut-srāva—who had conquered the sun, the moon, and other luminaries—the beginningless *Śrī-Mahā-vidyut-Nārāyaṇa* appeared together with his consort *Īśanī-Śrī*. Furthermore, in the forty-ninth year, for the sake of destroying the Daityas such as Madhu-bhakṣa and others, the beginningless *Śrī-Madhu-Nārāyaṇa* appeared together with his consort *Mādhavī-Śrī*. And in the fiftieth year, during the *Tiṣya* age, for the sake of [destroying] those who slaughter cows and those who destroy righteousness...
The thirty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrīnātha Nārāyaṇa, together with Dhenumatī and Śrī, for the purpose of destroying the Daityas. || 36 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Śrī Nārāyaṇī, to the manifestation of me as an incarnate being,
during the fifty-first year of the Vaikuṇṭha-kalpa of Brahmā.
In the first Kalpa, during the first fire at the beginning of the Kṛta Yuga,
the gods and others celebrated a festival for half of the Creator’s lifespan, which was a festival of gold.
There, in Satyaloka, there was an assembly of the inhabitants of the celestial realms:
those dwelling on the earth, those dwelling in heaven, and those who dwell in the world of ascetic penance.
Those dwelling on Meru, those residing on Mānasa, those living on Lokāloka,
and others dwelling in Vairāja, all arrived at Satyaloka.
The Siddhas, the Sādhyas, those of Brahmanic conduct, and the Brahmachārins arrived; the great seers, the seers, and the ancestors also assembled there. || 5 ||
The world-protectors, the guardians of the gods, and the lords of the world arrived,
as did the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Manus, and the two sons of the Aśvins.
Indra, the grahas, the tāras, and the nakṣatras arrived;
the yakṣas, the cāraṇas, the followers of Yama, and the gandharvas also arrived.
What men, Kinnaras, serpents, Nāgas, and Rākṣasas came there?
Those dwelling on Kailāsa and those dwelling in the Ocean of Milk also arrived. (8)
Men, rivers, streams, trees, and creepers arrived;
sacred fords, seasons, times, and the fortnights and so forth also arrived.
The Yugas and the years, as well as the elements and principles, arrived;
likewise, the lineages of Dharma, virtuous and chaste women, and yoginīs also arrived.
Even egg-born creatures and animals that remembered their former births arrived;
and the sons of the Magadhas, as well as bards and learned men, went forth. || 11 ||
The Vedas, the Rudras, the kings, and the aquatic creatures assembled; the oceans, rivers, lakes, mountains, and other such features arrived.
The Apsarases from the Brahma-lake, as well as male and female servants, all came together.
Various vehicles, weapons, and missiles arrived. || 13 ||

The vowels, the scriptures, the sciences, and the daughters of the sciences arrived; the regions and the provinces, having taken embodied forms, as well as the sweat-born beings, also came forth. (14)
Those born of the mind, those born of the body, those produced by touch, and those born of sight departed; both the insentient and the sentient, assuming forms at will, arrived as well. (15)
The hosts of Kāma and others, as well as those beginning with Vasanta, and the attendants departed;
the devotees, the liberated ones, the lords, and the goddesses also arrived. (16)
A gathering of all [the gods] took place, overflowing with immeasurable joy;
in the morning, they performed the consecration of Brahmā there.
Then those gods of the earth, the gods of heaven, the gods of truth, and the forest deities adorned a goat according to the prescribed ritual and purified it.
All the kinsmen and the gods worshipped the Supreme Lord;
they offered blessings and presented auspicious gifts. || 19 ||
In the assembly hall, there were also auspicious expositions praising Brahmā, delivered by the reciters who were deities such as Bṛhaspati.
Then dancing and singing also occurred in many ways; there were various musical performances as well as feasts. (21)
At that time, the gifts of reward were also most excellent;
moreover, there was the drinking of nectar and the eating of ambrosial food and other delicacies.
Having done so, they all performed a great festival of devotion to me, the worship of me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (23)
O Supreme Brahman, beyond the imperishable, O Supreme Lord, O Puruṣottama!
Victory to You, O Brahmā and Śiva, O Lord of All, O Śrī Hari, O Supreme Sovereign! 24.
Victory to you, the sustainer of the incarnations; victory to you, the manifester of the cosmic array!
Victory, O Lord of lords, Lord of gods; victory, O Lord who dwells within as the inner controller! 25.
Thus all embodied beings, including the gods, performed worship;
thereafter, Brahmā and all others, with concentrated minds, offered praise to me.
Come, O Blessed One, O Lord, O Creator of all creation;
O Supreme Lord, having shown us mercy, purify our homes today.
O Lord of incarnations, Lord of abodes, Lord of liberation, O Sovereign as far as you extend!
O Lord of the attributeless, Lord of the qualified! Purify our homes this very day.
You are life, you are supreme existence, you are the intellect, and you are sovereign splendor; you are light and consciousness, you are will, and you are volitional effort. || 29 ||
You are the action, you are the application, you are the fruit, and you are the bestower of the fruit;
you are the enjoyer, you are the object of enjoyment, and you are the presiding deity of the experience.
You are the self and you are the supreme self; you are everything, and all actions reside in you.
You are in all things, O Great King; purify our homes this very day.
O Lakṣmī, having been thus entreated by you at that time, Hari himself reflected and immediately came to Satyaloka along with me. (32)
Indeed, his domain is within the assembly hall at the moment of the devotees' worship;
endowed with all splendor, he is the Great Lord of divine form. ||33||
I shone resplendently upon a beautiful golden throne offered by all the gods and others;
then Brahmā bowed to me, and Viṣṇu and Śambhu also bowed to me.
Surā and the others honored me and prostrated like a staff;
likewise, virtuous women such as Sāvitrī and others paid you the same respect.
By us two, Brahmā was honored with blessings and sprinkled with water;
thereafter, Brahmā and the other deities [received] from us the auspicious food consisting of the offering (naivedya).
They offered betel and other items, as well as water which they regarded as nectar;
they massaged his feet and, filled with longing, made their requests.
O Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, Supreme Lord, we have been purified by your grace;
indeed, O Lord of all, we have obtained the sight of you. 38.
Through your grace, this universe has attained sanctity;
today the assembly, the day, and even we ourselves have become purified.
Just as you have shown favor by granting a vision in the realm of truth (Satyaloka),
so too, having shown favor, grant a vision to all the worlds.
Dwell within truth and austerity among the people on this great earth;
O Śīśa, dwell within the non-ultimate and the rest, and grant your grace, O Supreme Brahman. 41.
"O Lotus-born One, when I was thus entreated by you along with all [the others], I then gave my promise there, saying: 'So be it. (42)
I am the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), the Supreme Brahman myself, dwelling in Satyaloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka, and on the surface of the earth. 43.
Then, at the conclusion of Brahmā’s festival, having received their leave, those men set their minds upon going to Maharloka and likewise to Svarga. (44)
The Suras, the lords of the gods, the Pitṛs, and the great ṛṣis led me—the omnipresent Lord who assumes various forms—to their respective worlds. 45.
I then dwelt upon the surface of the earth and other realms before Nārāyaṇa, the beginningless Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), who is accompanied by the all-pervading Śrī. 46.
For one manvantara, out of compassion for this and that [place],
remember, O Lakṣmī, my manifestation as the Supreme Lord.
And at the conclusion of fifty years, during the festival of Svarṇaka, he went to Śvetadvīpa together with you; thereafter, [he remained there].
And at the conclusion of fifty years, during the festival of Śambhu’s golden age,
O Supreme Goddess, she went to Kailāsa together with you.
Brahmā was the eldest, Viṣṇu the middle, and Śambhu the youngest; these three brothers were born from Vairāja on the same day. (3.37.50)
Then, on the first day of the fifty-first year, I indeed attended those great festivals there. (51)
In the fourteen worlds, through my yoga, there are mental offspring,
as well as offspring that are tactile, visual, and likewise those that are associated with contact.
O Lakṣmī, all those [goddesses] became Nārāyaṇīs, taking refuge in me;
likewise, throughout the various Manvantaras, they were born as Vaiṣṇavīs in every way. (53)
Then, by my yoga, all those virtuous subjects became devoted to me;
and until the end of the kalpa, all those subjects became Nārāyaṇīs.
My incarnations are innumerable, and those incarnations are indeed countless;
remember them along with Śrī, for I know them exactly as they are.
Thus has been told to you that which is the most supreme manifestation;
now I shall tell you another thing regarding the year of Soma, the Creator.
In the fifty-second cycle of sixty kalpas, during the fourth Manvantara,
Brahmā once addressed his sons, the sages, and the gods in the assembly hall.
He also instructed the Pitṛs in the ritual sections that bestow happiness:
"Perform meditation in the morning, and then indeed perform your ablutions;
perform worship of the gods, especially those who are portions of Brahmā. (58)
Perform the Vaiśvadeva offering and also present the food offering; perform the sacrifices for guests and other rites, as well as your worldly affairs.
Perform the twilight prayers, salutation, devotion, listening, chanting, and so forth;
and also take rest, sleep, purification, and eat. (3.37.60)
Perform rites for the gods and ancestors, meritorious deeds, charity, and service;
practice the service of the virtuous, keep the company of the good, and perform righteous actions with sincerity. (6.1)
Support your wives, sons, and daughters; support your husband, kinsmen, and relatives; support your livestock, cattle, birds, and all living beings.
Render assistance to others; likewise, maintain your homes, gardens, fields, and various crops, and support those who depend upon you. (63)
Acquire virtue, wealth, and pleasure as is appropriate, and may you attain happiness and heaven again and again, day after day. (64)
"O sons, maintain the flow of creation without interruption;
at the end of the kalpa, you shall indeed return to Satyaloka, and from there once again."
At the beginning of the kalpa, the great ṛṣis, the gods,
the ancestors, and the guardians of the worlds were born again for the purpose of setting the creation in motion.
As soon as they heard this, the sons of Brahmā who were perfected yogis— possessing the character of Brahman and observing the vows of Brahman— questioned the Grandfather.
O Grandfather, for those who have no interest in that matter, explain to them whatever other appropriate action there may be, having distinguished it from this. 68.
Having heard this, the Creator said to them: "In this world, action is twofold—pravṛtta (engaged) and nivṛtta (withdrawn); indeed, the fruit of both is likewise twofold."
All that has been described has proceeded from wife, son, wealth, and so forth;
it is joined with passion, hatred, and the like, and produced by desire, anger, and the rest. (3.37.70)

And where there is no renunciation of the attachment born of greed for the home, which is joined with the delusion of latent impressions (vāsanā), nor of that [attachment] produced by the desire for worldly objects through one's wife; //71//
There is indeed no abandoning of the pairs of opposites— pleasure and pain, as well as birth and death— and there is no end to saṃsāra where these whirlpools persist.
Where there is returning again, accompanied by old age and death; where there is the attainment of desires for sense objects, and likewise a nature consisting of thirst for enjoyment. (73)

It is thoroughly joined with cold, heat, and so forth; it is yoked with sorrow, agitation, and the like; it is overcome by festivals and non-festivals; and it is extended through the expansion of one's lineage. (74)
All this that has proceeded, concerning the cause of creation, has been told by me;
as have the former seven ṛṣis and likewise the ten great ṛṣis.
The Lords of Creatures (Prajāpatis) and the Manus, having performed that karma of worldly activity,
indeed resorted to cremation grounds characterized by rebirth.
That which is filled with passion and hatred, accumulated with grief, agitation, suffering, and the like, and where the pair of impure actions resides—that home is a cremation ground. (77)
That house where the threefold suffering arises, where merit and demerit emerge, and which is connected to the three desires—that indeed is a cremation ground. (78)
Where hungry ghosts die and are born again in suffering, and where those dwelling in the womb are brought forth—that house is indeed a cremation ground. (79)
Where union with those of impure bodies is indeed desired,
that cremation ground is the birthplace for the dead, serving only for their further death.
The entire cycle of existence is indeed a cremation ground;
however, that karma which is distinct from it is cessation, and that bestows liberation. (81)
Where there is no taking of a wife, nor any latent tendency toward sensual desire; where there is neither passion nor hatred, neither lust nor anger, and no greed for a home.
Where there is no delusion, no longing, and no dualities—that state is the hall of Brahman, the bestower of the knowledge of Brahman. ||83||

Wherein there is celibacy (brahmacarya) and wherein indeed there is the offering to Brahman (brahmārpaṇa), as well as the abode of desire for sense-objects and likewise the abode of thirst for enjoyment; ||84||
Therein indeed exists self-contentment, delight in the Self, and absorption in the Supreme Brahman;
there is truly no experience of sorrow, agitation, heat, cold, or other such sensations. (85)

Where there is always a festival of Brahman, as well as belonging to the lineage of Acyuta; where there is indeed the company of the virtuous for the good, and a state of being intent on offering everything to Brahman. (86)
Indeed, that action which consists of loving devotion to Hari is ceased [from worldly motives];
by performing all such acts, the virtuous truly attain liberation. (87)
Likewise, renunciants, perfected ones, ascetics with sublimated vital energy, those whose character is Brahman, those devoted to Brahman, the truthful, and virtuous women of that same kind; ||88||
Those of old, relying on the path of renunciation, attained the eternal heavens;
yet that [state] was neither unmixed with suffering and the like, nor was it free from being eventually consumed by them in the end. (89)
The bliss of non-return and the unsurpassed, inviolable heaven—indeed, the ancient devotees of the Blessed Bhāgavata attained that very heaven. (3.37.90)
Having worshipped the Blessed Lord Hari, Nārāyaṇa, the Sovereign, the Supreme Person who is the Transcendent Brahman beyond the Imperishable; ||91 ||
Having worshipped the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of all incarnations,
the Lord of Śrī and the Lord of the liberated, they attained His abode.
Service to Him, devotion to Him, beholding Him, being His servant, worshiping Him, friendship with Him, and the offering of one's very self to Him. ||93||
Having surrendered their entire being to that yoga there, they attained the imperishable, supreme abode—the eternal realm of ultimate liberation. (94)
Having desisted from worldly activity, they attained that mass of eternal bliss;
through union with the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), they reached the highest abode. ||95||
O noble ones, you who are perfected beings devoted to the dharma of Brahman, having completed the rites of renunciation, proceed to the supreme imperishable state. 96.
Thus addressed, those ascetics were indeed satisfied with their return;
having performed total surrender and devotion, they attained the state of having fulfilled their purpose.
Then Brahmā spoke again to both the sages and the ascetics:
"Whether it be the path of worldly engagement or the path of renunciation, the offering to Brahman is the cessation [of all action]."

Whether an action is performed by the body or arises from the body, if both types of karma are indeed offered to the Supreme Lord, the Sovereign of All, who is directly perceptible, [then they are purified]. (99)
That which has ceased [to flow] would arise again, granting liberation through union with Hari; just as everything is reduced to ashes by the excessive force of fire.
"By the direct application of *suyoga* to Hari, everything likewise becomes reduced to ashes.
Having heard this, the sages who were devoted to ritual action (*karmaṭha*) were indeed exceedingly delighted.
Having returned, they were all filled with joy; bowing down to the Grandfather (Brahmā) and remembering Śrī Puruṣottama, they questioned him indeed. (102)
"How indeed may we have direct union with Hari in this world?
Show us that method by which we may perform service consisting of self-surrender. (103)
Even after performing active duties within the sphere of sensory experience,
by offering them up to Hari, we shall attain the supreme, imperishable abode from which there is no return to higher states.
Brahmā said: Then, O Lakṣmī, he spoke these words quickly to them all:
"Let them perform a sacrificial session right here, consisting solely of worship."
Drawn by that, Hari will quickly become subject to devotion;
he will appear before you in person and accept your service.
Having heard this, all the gods and others, both groups together,
performed with concentrated minds the sacrificial session of chanting the names in Satyaloka.
O Lakṣmī, having heard the devoted praise of those ascetics,
I indeed came along with you from the realm of the Imperishable (Akṣara).
In the midst of that assembly, the Gocaras bowed to me, the Supreme Lord; they worshipped me and made a request for permanent residence.
Among the ṛṣis in Satyaloka, and likewise among the Siddhas;
among the Pitṛs in Janaloka, and likewise among humans on earth.
"So be it," I said, "I shall remain forever with you—Anādi-Śrī-Mokṣa-Nārāyaṇa, Śrī-Puruṣottama. (11.1)
Known by the name Muktiśrī, you are the illustrious Puruṣottamī;
assuming many forms, you both dwell throughout all the worlds. || 112 ||
Then, having completed the sacrificial session, they went to their own homes;
those engaged in worldly activity attained worldly success, and even those withdrawn from it attained liberation.
By surrendering to me, they attained freedom from the qualities of nature (nirguṇya) and reached my abode;
other great sages were also born as meritorious souls in that place.
Thus, together with you, I have manifested that which bestows liberation;
remember the duration of the Manvantara, for I myself was present upon the earth.
In this way, thousands of other incarnations of mine have also occurred;
I know all of them by the hundreds of thousands, but others do not.
By reading and by hearing this, one shall certainly obtain enjoyment and liberation,
as well as divine and worldly prosperity pertaining to both this life and the next.

Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa together with Vibhvī Śrī during the Golden Festival in the fifty-first year of the Creator [Brahmā] in the third period, the Dvāpara-santāna, and the Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Mokṣa Nārāyaṇa together with Mukti Śrī in the fifty-second year," in the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said: Listen, O Lakṣmī, then, regarding the unborn one (Aja) again during the Gāyatrī year,
in the first Vārāha Kalpa and in my first Manvantara.
Of the beginningless Supreme Soul, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, who exists at present together with you, Śrī Śivarājñī. || 2 ||
Indeed, my manifestation is here in this field known as Akṣara,
on the bank of the Aśvapaṭṭa lake, in the vicinity of Kuṅkumavāpikā.
In the city of Surāṣṭra, in the house of Mahālakṣmī Kambharāśrī which was filled with all prosperity,
[he was born] from his father known as Śrīmad Gopālakṛṣṇa.
For the sake of fulfilling the desires of crores, billions, and trillions of maidens, and for the purpose of protecting the Dharma, I have come here out of compassion. (5)
Drawn here by the fierce austerities of Pitr̥ and Tr̥ṣu, I, who dwell in the Imperishable, have manifested myself in this place; you have been made my own by me here.
O Nārāyaṇī, my beloved, even though you are accompanied by crores, billions, and hundreds of millions of maidens,
I shall nevertheless be born again and again in kalpa after kalpa.
O Kamalā, together with you alone in the field inhabited by Lomaśa, my many incarnations— such as the Fish, the Boar, and the Tortoise— took place.
Kapila, Siṃha, Turaga, Haṃsa, Vāmana, Nārada, Vāsudeva, Haridatta, Ātreya, Parśudhara, and Ṛṣabha. (9)
Pṛthuyajña, Kumāra, and others, Vyāsa, Rāma, and Adhirāja;
likewise Dhanvantari, Buddha, Kṛṣṇa, Kalki, and Mohanika.
Harikṛṣṇa, Naranārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanarāyaṇa,
and others will appear by the thousands on earth and in heaven, according to the requirements of their tasks.
In age after age there shall be my incarnations, and also Vyāsas in age after age, who will establish righteousness and awaken people to the Dharma according to the requirements of each time.
There will be a sage named Śvetakṛṣṇāyana, possessed of a topknot;
he will be Śvetavyāsa, the narrator of the story and the compiler of the Saṃhitā.
Today my incarnation must be accomplished; the Lord Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa shall be the proclaimer of Dharma, worthy of homage even in the world of Brahmā.
Likewise, there are other Vyāsas as well, who are my portions and revealers of dharma:
Satya, Bhārgava, Savitṛ, Vasiṣṭha, Aruṇi, and Sṛñjaya. (15)
Ṛtañjaya, Bharadvāja, Tṛṇabindu, Dvaipāyana, Prabhū, Vallabha, Saureya, Devānīka, and Ṛtaṃbhara. (16)
They were like the fire of the great Vāreya spell, free from all taints;
they maintained the vows of the Dhārīṇaka, Sukaukṣeya, Vārṣadhāra, and Vanavrata ascetics. || 17 ||
They shall become my portions, manifesting the sciences;
it is not possible for anyone else to enumerate them due to the length of time. 18.
There have indeed been ten million times a thousand past self-born ones;
again and again, there will be ten million times a thousand more.
In substance, all those creators of the universe are countless, devouring time;
yet the Nārāyaṇas, who do not devour untimely [death], are of the nature of Śrī and myself.
Those who are eternally liberated, as well as those being liberated— the millions of liberated ones—
all of them, eating at no fixed time, are residents of the abode of the Abode.
Thus, O Lakṣmī, everything you asked has been told to you exactly as it is;
I, the Incarnate One, have revealed myself and have been described by me.
"O Lakṣmī, always obtain your own happiness from me, who am ever-incarnate; furthermore, O Nārāyaṇī, ask whatever else you most desire. (23)
The illustrious Queen Śrīśivarājñī said: "I am satisfied, having learned of my former forms from the mouth of my beloved.
Salutations to you, O Lord of my life, who possess manifold forms and bear the Śārṅga bow. (24)
Obeisance to you, the Lord of Raudrī and Ramaṇī, the glorious Dyunnārāyaṇa;
obeisance to you, the Merunārāyaṇa united with Mairavī and Dhṛti. ||25||
Salutations to you, Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa, the son of Sūrya, the destroyer of Śatru; salutations to you, Candra Nārāyaṇa, the son of Candra, the moonlight-like lord of gods. ||26||
Obedience to you, the Lord of Śrī, who possesses abundant sacrificial fees;
O Brahman Nārāyaṇa, the Consort of Vaiṣṇavī-Śrī, let there be salutation to you. ||27||
Obeisance to you, Ādityanārāyaṇa, the glorious Lord of the celestial path;
obeisance to you, Garuḍanārāyaṇa, the glorious Lord of Ananta. ||28||
O Lord of the Ṛṣi-lotus, salutations to you; O Ṛṣi-Nārāyaṇa, salutations to you!
O Lord of the splendor of moonlight, O Prājña-Nārāyaṇa, let there be salutations to you! ||29||
Obeisance to you, Śārdūlikāśrīśa Vīranārāyaṇa;
obeisance to you, Sarobhadrāśrīśa Bhadranārāyaṇa. ||3.38.30||
O Lord of auspicious glory, O Hari Nārāyaṇa, salutations be unto you!
O independent Lord of Śrī, O Bīja Nārāyaṇa, salutations be unto you! ||3 1||

This hymn to the beloved of the glory of the Couple, consisting of one thousand and twelve names, is supreme and bestows the four goals of human existence. 28.1.

It bestows good fortune and perpetuates the lineage; it grants prosperity and confers all forms of wealth; it bestows sovereignty and heaven; it grants all objects of enjoyment and is the supreme giver of one's heart's desires.

It bestows success, bestows merit, and through its form it bestows meditative absorption; it is purifying, it destroys sin, it overcomes death, it dispels obstacles, and it eliminates suffering. ||283||
It bestows a divine nature, leads to the ground of supreme liberation, is auspicious, grants what is otherwise unattainable, and always bestows health and prosperity. (284)
For all men and women who read it, listen to it, or likewise remember its meaning, it fulfills every desire. (285)
O Hari, this [stotra] has been produced directly from my own mouth; it is born of Lakṣmī and bestows prosperity.
I am Lakṣmī in the form of the hymn, and you, my Lord, are the recipient of the hymn. (286)
"May there be equality between us two and those who praise us.
O Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, obeisance to You, the Inner Self! (287)
"Salutations again and again, salutations, salutations to all your female forms!
Tell me other deeds of yours that truly create affection for you."
And those auspicious incarnations that exist on earth, such as Nara, Nārāyaṇa, and others, are the manifestors of the state of Puruṣottama. (289)
O Ocean of Compassion, tell me how those who have descended [to earth] bring about awakening; if it is for the benefit of the world, please explain that to me. (3.38.290)
Without the consciousness that descends [into the body], supreme worship cannot take place;
therefore, O Beloved Lord, please tell it to me, your beloved, out of compassion. (29.1)

Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of the Beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa together with Queen Śrī Śivarājñī in the fifty-third year of the Creator [Brahmā] during the Dvāpara Age within the Third Section of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā," and the description of the hymn of one thousand one hundred and twelve names for the Divine Couple. || 38 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Lakṣmī, I shall narrate the story of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, which is rich with the realization of Puruṣottama and brings about direct intuitive knowledge of Me. 1.
Once, however, those great seers went to Viśālā in order to behold my own form as Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
There, the illustrious Śaṅkara also arrived accompanied by Satī;
Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, and Sanandana also came there.
The most excellent great sages, such as Aṅgiras and others, who were self-luminous;
the twice-born Patnīvrata and other ancient ones, such as Lomaśa and the rest.
Desiring to perform a sacrificial session of austerity (tapaḥsatra), they beheld the pure son of Dharma,
as well as Nārāyaṇa and Nara, and a beautiful female ascetic who was my own body.
Having worshipped according to the rules and praised him with Vedic hymns, all those foremost among the knowers of Yoga, filled with devotion, prostrated themselves like a staff.
With joyful hearts, they spoke to Nārāyaṇa, their supreme teacher:
"We have approached You alone, the Supreme Person, for refuge. (7)
Nārāyaṇa himself is the manifest, ancient Supreme Lord;
austerity becomes supreme through you, yoga becomes [supreme] through you, and knowledge is the highest austerity.
That penance is supreme and bestows liberation wherein you are worshipped;
tell us that, O Hari: from what does this world proceed?
What is the self and what indeed is liberation? What is this transmigratory existence that has been created?
What is that supreme Brahman? You ought to tell us all of this.
Thus questioning, the sages beheld that Nārāyaṇa,
who had cast off his ascetic garb and was the eternal Supreme Brahman.
He was radiant with splendors, attended by the liberated circles [of sages],
abiding in the abode of the imperishable Brahman, marked with the Śrīvatsa, and encompassed by Śrī.
[Behold] me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama),
laughing together with you and endowed with all my own weapons.
O Lakṣmī, upon seeing [this], Śambhu and all the others were momentarily stunned; immersed in extreme bliss, they attained the state of the Supreme Lord.
Then, having concealed my divine nature,
Nārāyaṇa became an ascetic, just as he had been under the banyan tree.
Then, Narayana spoke there to all the sages who were established in their own states:
"That form of mine which is invisible is designated as the Supreme Lord."
Because Narayana, whom even the gods do not recognize despite their efforts without [divine] grace, shines forth here revealed within me. (17)
Having obtained a vision [of the Lord] through grace, those most exalted ones have become one with Brahman;
established in Brahman and proclaimers of Brahman, they do not enter into the cycle of worldly existence again. 18.
Today I shall declare that knowledge of the knowers of Brahman who possess devotion:
this Self of embodied beings is translucent, pure, subtle, and eternal. (19)
Therein dwells the Lord Śrīmad-Brahma-Nārāyaṇa, who is the innermost of all;
he exists in the form of the vital breath (prāṇa), that supreme person who is the inner controller (antaryāmī). || 3.39.20 ||
Indeed, from this abode of the Imperishable (akṣara), all things come into being;
by means of his own māyā, he creates various bodies for the sake of emanation. ||21||
For living beings and others, bound by karma, transmigrate again and again;
but those freed from the bonds of karma proceed to that supreme state. 22.
Just as a connection between light and darkness is not possible, so too a connection between saṃsāra and nirvāṇa is not possible. ||23||
Just as shadow and sunlight are distinct, so too are the world and the Supreme Being;
likewise, the Self of embodied beings is distinct from the form of worldly existence. 24.
The notion that "I am the agent," "I am happy," "I am miserable," or "I am thin and fat"—this is superimposed upon the Self by people due to the agency of the ego (ahaṃkāra). (25)
Therefore, this cycle of existence, bound by karma, has its root in ignorance;
through the lack of discrimination regarding the ego-sense, one performs the bondage of karma. (26)
Devoted sages and supreme worshippers behold the Lord, the Consort of Śrī, the Supreme Sovereign, within their own pure self. 27.
Having understood primordial nature (prakṛti), the person (puruṣa), time (kāla), and likewise his own self (ātman), he who is united with Hari indeed partakes in eternal bliss. ||28||
If one does not realize one's own self as the imperishable Brahman, then the cognition of the self in that which is not the self bestows suffering and saṃsāra. (29)
All defects such as passion and hatred are rooted in ignorance;
indeed, they cause embodied beings to perform meritorious and non-meritorious actions. (3.39.30)
By the power of that alone, the manifestation of all bodies occurs for everyone;
therefore, the virtuous should indeed contemplate Brahman as their own self. 3.1
The wise should realize their own identity as being pervaded by the Supreme Lord;
for just as space does not become defiled through contact with the earth, [so too the self remains untainted]. ||3.2||
In the same way, the Self is not tainted by the states arising from the internal organ, just as the sun shines everywhere by its own radiance. //33//
Likewise, the Self consists of knowledge and shines forth when joined with it;
therefore, this [Self] is of the nature of knowledge, of the nature of consciousness, and free from worldly existence. ||34||
Just as a crystal is perceived by people as colored when in proximity to a dye, so too is this [Self] perceived as possessing the qualities of objects due to their proximity. (35)
Therefore, I must constantly worship, contemplate, and listen to that Supreme Lord—the imperishable, pure, and eternal Self who is devoted to me. (36)
When Mādhava thus shines forth everywhere within his knowledge, then Hari becomes fully realized by that faithful devotee. (37)
When the supreme Brahman, which is the self of all, truly shines within him,
then he beholds that [Brahman] in its perceptible form within his own very self.
When one perceives that Supreme Lord within all beings, then the Supreme Brahman reveals itself everywhere to the devotee. (39)
When, abiding in the Self, one perceives nothing else whatsoever by oneself, then, united with the Supreme, one beholds the Supreme Lord. ||3.39.40||
When the desires of the heart indeed dissolve and no longer exist, then, having become immortal, he beholds the Supreme Lord. ||41||
When one perceives Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa as abiding in all things, then, having attained union with Him, one becomes fit for His own nature. ||42||
When he beholds the Lord of Gods, the Supreme Person, the Sovereign, as being nothing more than Māyā, then for him there is no transcendence of Brahman. 43.
When one's own knowledge—the realization of Brahman—exists as the sole remedy for birth, old age, suffering, and disease, then that person is Śiva. 44.
Just as all rivers and streams flow into the vast ocean, so too do devotees enter the imperishable Brahman through their acts of worship. 45.
As long as those deluded by ignorance do not acquire true knowledge, they—drawn away by the darkness of ignorance—do not reach the supreme state. (46)
Self-knowledge must be cultivated, as well as yoga directed toward Nārāyaṇa;
through both of these, Śrī Hari, his Supreme Self, is revealed. (47)
Through union with Hari, all his sovereign powers manifest;
either in this very body or at the end of the body, by virtue of Hari’s own grace.
One shall attain that divine sovereignty which is esteemed by all;
he who bestows that sovereignty is the Supreme Lord of all. (49)
He is the Self of all beings, dwelling in all, facing every direction;
he is the form of all, the taste of all, the scent of all—undecaying and immortal.
He whose hands and feet are everywhere is the Inner Controller, the eternal Śrī Sanātana;
though without hands or feet, He is swift and a grasper, residing within the heart. ||51||
Though eyeless, he is a seer; though earless, he hears as well.
He knows all this, yet no one knows him. (52)
Those of pure intention call him the Supreme Lord, the Great Master;
the sages behold him as the cause of unsurpassed sovereignty. (53)
Having realized this, those who have transcended his illusion—which exists in the form of bondage—attain union with Him once they have entered therein. (54)
They attain the supreme abode, Nirvāṇa, together with Hari;
by his grace, they never again undergo rebirth.
O best among the knowers of Brahman, this supreme knowledge, which bestows liberation and grants peace, must indeed be given to sons, disciples, and yogis. (56)
Listen further to what else arose from the Supreme Lord:
the Puruṣa known as Kāla, and likewise the Prakṛti of Puruṣa.
From those two [Prakṛti and Puruṣa] comes Pradhāna; from those two comes the golden Ajā; and from those two come both the golden Virāṭ and the Vairājikī.
From those two [the male and female principles] arose the three deities, and from them this world consisting of men and women;
thus, all this belongs to Hari, and therefore the world is composed of Brahman.
Hari is the self of all beings, the knowing self, the Supreme Lord;
O twice-born ones, listen further, for in ancient times there was indeed the will of Hari.
That Māyā, though possessing a divine form, is endowed with the karma of living beings;
she is of the nature of the activity of Sattva when she is Sāttvikī, but Rājasī when her activity is Rajas.
And she, joined with darkness, is of the nature of tamas and consists of action;
she appears to people in whatever form the actions of living beings take.
It is said that its light is red, as if rich with red glass;
yet in reality, it is pure in form, though entered by the individual soul (jīva). //63//
That illusion, which yields fruits according to karma, is of three kinds:
the root, the pure, and the uneven; it follows the course of karma. (64)
From that, the principle of Mahat, known as the intellect (buddhi), indeed manifests;
from the principle of Mahat arises the ego-sense (ahaṃ-buddhi), which consists of self-conceit (abhimāna). ||65||
From that arises the group of sixteen, consisting of the subtle elements (tanmātras), the sense organs, and the mind;
and from the subtle elements arise the gross elements, which possess qualities.
From the gross elements, indeed, that world is born;
for although it is insentient in nature, being pervaded by sentient beings, it performs actions. ||67||
Saṃsāra, consisting of latent impressions (*vāsanā*), is a refuge [for beings] according to their karma;
that too is subject to time and arises from a lack of discernment (*aviveka*). (68)
Relying on the assistance of the mind, [the latent impression] sets embodied beings in motion;
therefore, the wise person should first restrain the mind and then destroy the latent impression. 69.
Having assumed the form of Kālamāyātīta, one should worship Mādhava;
there is nothing superior to that, and by worshipping Him, one is liberated. (3.39.70)
Indeed, this [Lord] cannot be known by men through various austerities, nor by charity, nor by sacrifice, except through unsurpassed devotion. (7.1)
He indeed dwells within all beings on every side;
by knowing Him as the witness of all, one is liberated from all bondage. //72//
Within him all this exists, yet he is the supreme ender of all;
the scriptures proclaim him alone as the one true Supreme Lord.
Brāhmaṇas worship Him with various sacrifices and millions of sacrificial sessions;
practitioners of yoga meditate upon Him, and stainless holy men devote themselves to Him.
He is the embodiment of all the gods; the righteous worship him, and to them he grants that state, the blissful supreme goal. (75)
Men and women as well, established in their duties, devoted and free from sin, worship him with devotion; they attain the supreme goal. ||76||
Thus, having understood Him as the Supreme Lord, Hari, the inner controller of all, let the sages meditate upon Him and proceed to the supreme abode.
Having spoken thus to the eminent sages, Śivarāja, the Lord of Badarī,
again revealed the Lord within the body of the ascetic.
Abounding in the splendor of ten million Cupids, endowed with glory, higher than the highest, possessed of manifold sovereign powers, and graced with the majesty of a king of kings. ||79||
He is the primordial Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, most beautiful, the beloved of all, and endowed with the honey-sweetness of every divine loveliness. (3.39.80)
The supreme state of the Lord is served by infinite liberated souls,
and it is likewise honored and praised by the various manifestations and emanations.
The divine abode consisting of the Supreme Brahman, served by the Lord of All and others, filled with every splendor—the Lord of the Abode, Śrī Puruṣottama. ||82||
Having beheld that form of Hari, those sages were satisfied and filled with happiness;
having attained the fruit of their penance, they rejoiced and praised him once more. (83)
You are the Lord, you are the Supreme Brahman, you are Kṛṣṇa, you are Nārāyaṇa;
you are Nārāyaṇa, the supreme light, the possessor of the imperishable abode.
You possess a golden form and you are Viṣṇu; you are the all-pervading one, you consist of all the gods, and you are the ascetic, O Supreme Lord. (85)
Having seen you, the Supreme Person, we have accomplished our purpose; having attained you, we have today crossed to the further shore of illusion. Your compassion bestows infinite liberation. (86)
Since you have arrived here by your own will, your heart's desire is fulfilled;
no other task remains to be done beyond this sight of you.
"May your supreme, supramundane form always shine before us; we desire only this—grant us this boon, for it is our boon. (88)
Having thus praised the glorious Śivārājñī, they remained in silence;
then that divine form of the Supreme Brahman vanished from that place. (89)
I indeed became an ascetic instantly, possessing the nature of Nārāyaṇa;
and while I was situated beneath the Badarī tree, they worshipped me in that manner.
Having received my command, they departed for their own abodes while honoring me;
you should recognize that form of mine as being of the nature of Nārāyaṇa. 91.
Know me as the ascetic who always acts for the protection of the world and the preservation of Dharma,
who is the very self of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, and who is the inner controller (antaryāmin).
And know him who is named Puruṣottama as your husband;
having fully grasped this knowledge, Śaṅkara and the others [attained it] thereafter on earth. (93)
The sages taught liberation and bestowed it everywhere upon embodied beings who practice my worship, through the very essence of Brahman. 94.
O Lakṣmī, it should be known that this bestows liberation through recitation, hearing, or even mere remembrance; it grants all bliss, for there is nothing superior to it. 95.

Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Instruction Given by Nara and Nārāyaṇa to Mānava and Others, Following the Great Sages Who Had Arrived at Badarī for the Purpose of Austerity and Were Satisfied by the Vision of Nara and Nārāyaṇa as the Form of the Supreme Brahman," in the Third Section, the Dvāpara Cycle, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said: "Tell us the duties and religious practices of those who are beloved by Puruṣottama,
so that the faults of household life may not arise here."
You abide as the Supreme Brahman, and we are your wives of the Brahmanic order;
in you, there exists no trace of defect whatsoever, for your divinity is absolute.
Nevertheless, for embodied beings—both men and women—who abide by the duties of the household, there may be the attainment of dharma; therefore, please tell us those duties of the household.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, and may all those dear to me listen as well;
I shall declare the duties of householders which remove faults and bestow prosperity.
The house is to be known as the abode, the Imperishable (Akṣara); the Lord is Śrī Puruṣottama; the sons are to be understood as the five deities; and the ritual acts are my worship. || 5 ||
Thus, for those women established in the householder’s life who proceed in this manner with a disposition of total surrender unto me, their dharma is entirely Vaiṣṇava.

A man should constantly meditate on Hari as his husband, and upon me, the Supreme Person, as his wife; a woman should always meditate on Lakṣmī as her husband, and on Śrī, the virtuous Supreme Woman, as herself.
One should meditate upon the attendants (pārṣadas) in one's sons, Śrī, Ramā, and others in one's daughters,
Garuḍa and others in one's vehicles, and the liberated souls (muktas) in one's kinsmen and so forth.
One should thus meditate upon Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person, within one's own body,
and offer everything to Him who dwells within one's inner self.
Thus indeed has this yoga of action been described for you;
when joined with the realization of actionlessness and endowed with devotion to me, it bestows liberation.
Among all forms of the application of action, this yoga is distinguished as superior:
the yoga consisting of service to Hari through deed, mind, and speech.
Hari alone is to be constantly worshipped through the chanting of His names and other such means;
one should also perform circumambulation and worship my image.
One should eat the food offered with devotion to me, fix one's mind upon my feet,
dance before Hari with loud sounds, and likewise converse with him.

One should perform singing with beautiful tones through the coordination of hand-claps and other instruments; one should constantly listen to the sacred narrative and wear the remains of the offerings upon one's head.
I am the Lord who bestows liberation, always worthy of worship and salutation;
therefore, [one should worship] Anādikṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the beloved of Śrī, the infallible Acyuta.
Worship me as Śrī Hari and behold me moment by moment;
O beloveds, always remain devoted to your husband Hari. 16.
Constantly worship me, Hari, through the yoga of action;
sacrifice to me, Hari, along with Lakṣmī, by means of bathing, feeding, and service.
O beloveds of Brahmā, rising before me every morning, always perform the massaging of my limbs and the rubbing of my feet while I am asleep.
"Gladden me, your husband, and the god as you desire through your service;
go from here indeed with the hope that it may purify your own bodies and so forth."
Remembering me, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, they shall bathe with the waters from my feet,
chant my name, and perform libations with water.
Having recollected the gods and the ancestors, offer salutations with joined palms;
bow down to the elders, the Brahmins, the virtuous, the chaste women, and the cows.
Always bow down to the celestial trees, the sacred fords, and the gods;
having bathed, offer appropriate gifts only to worthy recipients.
Bestow upon them whatever they require— wealth, food, clothing, ornaments, and so forth—
and after arranging for their audiences with the gods, send them home.
"Having arrived, perform for me properly that auspicious service consisting of the preliminary rites of bathing and so forth; indeed, bathe me with warm waters."
Having massaged me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama), as is appropriate with fragrant oils, ointments, and so forth; ||25||
Clothe them in garments of gold, silver, and silk; likewise, adorn them with ornaments and embellish them with excellent unguents. ||26||
With fragrant flowers, garlands, and the like, as well as with sandalwood paste and other perfumes, with incense, lamps, and so forth, and with the grooming of my hair and other such services; ||27||
Worship me and feed me with meals of milk and rice-pudding;
always offer me water and betel-leaf with love. (28)
"Cleanse the courtyards of the houses, gather up the beds as well, fetch water, and likewise proceed with the milking of the cows. (29)
Prepare curd, yogurt, and other such items; honor the elders as well. Perform the cooking and other tasks, and feed the deities.
He fed the sages, guests, brahmins, and holy men,
and he also gave mouthfuls of food and other offerings to the cows and performed oblations for the sacred fires.
Feed the destitute, the wretched, the children, and others with excellent food;
perform acts of service for others, and bow to the sun at all times. (32)
Feed those who have arrived and offer them a welcome and so forth;
always adorn your own bodies with ornaments and the like. (33)
May all you ladies, who are dear to me, whose very selves are mine, and who exist for my sake, attain my grace and become laden with meditative cultivation. (34)
May they eat their most desired sweet foods and remain joyful;
may they honor the commands of the elders and the well-spoken words of their superiors. (35)
May they protect the family traditions and likewise other kinship duties;
may they adopt the local customs and my own dharmas as their primary and most excellent obligation. (36)

May they always effect the perfect purification of garments and other items through washing with earth and other cleansing agents; may they ever follow after the most excellent forms of Lakṣmī, as well as sacred narratives, knowledge, the arts, and various forms of skill. (37)
May they always study the arts such as cooking and the like, as well as the service of mothers, sisters, and mothers-in-law;
and may they increase their abundant affection for their co-wives day by day. (38)
May they protect their greatness, honor them with food,
and likewise show respect to the monks by providing all kinds of gifts.
Let them honor the virtuous men and women, and especially the Vaiṣṇavas;
and let them enjoy pleasures with favor, offered even unto Me.
Let them recite the Sandhyā goddess and the Gāyatrī joined with me;
let them perform the recitation in my name, remembering me, the Supreme Lord. 41.
May they perform their household duties clearly and auspiciously;
may they protect all kinds of household goods effectively. (42)
Let them cause dancing, singing, fine attire, and so forth to be performed for my sake;
let them serve cows and the like, as well as calves and the like, with their meditative visualizations.
May they protect the parrots, swans, peacocks, garuḍas, and so forth;
may they likewise protect the elephants, horses, bulls, and the female buffaloes.

May they effect the purification of food and other such things, the cleansing of garments and so forth; may they observe the rules regarding birth-impurity and the like, and transform the various modifications [of matter]. (45)
May they perform the purification of their homes, may the members of the household provide nourishment, may they increase fame and renown, and may they be endowed with fortitude. (46)
May they be endowed with the virtues of compassion, forbearance, mercy, and service;
may they always be dear to others and characterized by altruism. (47)
May they be free from desire, distinguishing between their own interests and those of others; and may they act for the sake of others while being devoted to the ultimate truth. 48.
May they always possess faith in the performance of divine rites, be devoted to the service of the world, and remain intent upon the service of their disciples. (49)
May they also be devoted to the service of their subjects, intent upon offering blessings and the like, always possessed of auspicious intentions, and bestowers of excellence upon others. (3.40.50)
May they rejoice in the prosperity of others, cultivate the dedication of their own prosperity, observe the virtue of non-possessiveness, and be dedicated to me. (5.1)
They were free from injustice, immersed in righteousness, endowed with virtuous vows, devoid of greed for craving, and liberated from passion and hatred. ||52||
May the wives of Brahmā be endowed with the lineage of Dharma, be free from the succession of unrighteousness, and possess the very nature of Nārāyaṇī. (53)
May they be as illusory as a magical illusion toward their own relatives, kinsmen, and so forth, yet may they always remain full of affection for their own family members. (54)
Those who practice the dharma of the untouchable have resorted to the conduct of a daughter-in-law;
those who practice the dharma of the touchable have resorted to the conduct of a mother.
And may the goddesses always remain positioned at the front and lower than the elders, seated on low seats and with their hands joined in the añjali gesture. ||56||
Let them be sweet-spoken, with their necks and minds bowed down, upon seeing that the work of their own homes remains unfinished even as it stands before them. (57)
Let my inner beloveds act without pride and without internal stiffness;
let them generate mutual joy that bestows assistance. (58)
Let them also provide mutual assistance to one another along with their wives, and let them serve each other with the arranging of hair and other such services. (59)
When unwell, let them attend to one another with devotion;
and for the sake of purifying vessels and such, let them always look after the female servants.
Let them provide for the protection of the female servants by means of food, clothing, and wages,
as is appropriate, through considerations such as honor and gifts.
May they observe their menstrual purity, maintain physical cleanliness, and indeed avoid those faults born of anger and the like which cause suffering. (62)
Let them abandon in every way greed and other vices that destroy happiness;
let them not kill even lice and the like, nor those born from sweat or from eggs.
Let them not kill any living beings born from a womb, even the most minute ones, anywhere;
having strained water and milk, let them drink them only when purified.
May they not consume those things that cause disease, nor those that produce dullness and laziness, nor even those that cause the mind to wander and are filled with foul odors and the like. (61)
Let them never indulge in liquor, meat, sexual intercourse, or theft;
let them certainly not practice falsehood, untruth, or deceit.
Let my dear ones never speak words of reproach for the sake of some other's loss;
nor let them ever speak what is unpleasant, distressing, or cruel. (67)
Let them never indeed display their own faces with anger;
let them never perform any action suddenly or without reflection. (68)
Let them not go to my domain, that supreme abode, which is unfit for them;
let them abandon their state of doubt and establish themselves in firm resolve. 69.
May they not practice fruitless deeds, nor engage in vain speech or futile actions; may they not indulge in idle sleep, nor likewise in aimless wandering.
May they never cause futile obstacles for anyone;
may they not practice the conduct of beasts, and may they abandon folly from afar. (7.1)
May they grasp discernment and discrimination, and may they receive instruction with ease;
may they abide in accordance with what is excellent, venerable, and virtuous. (72)
By constant practice, they should always restrain the mind in every way; and they should abandon from all sides those desires which bring about suffering. (73)
May these women, who grant happiness, fulfill their righteous desires;
let them not place their trust in those who are objects of distrust. //74//
May they never have unobstructed bodies nor be naked; may they never be devoid of good fortune and ornaments. (75)
May they not indulge excessively in even beloved pleasures that cause disease and suffering;
may they not practice the violation of their vows, nor ever abandon the gains [of their spiritual practice]. (76)
Let women abandon unfitness for action and negligence far away, and let them practice gentleness, skill, and perseverance. (77)
May they cultivate mutual affection and abandon stubborn insistence;
may they renounce futile obstinacy, which brings loss as well as suffering. (78)
Thinking, "This is yours, not mine," and "This is mine, not yours," let them never do anything harmful, whether toward themselves or toward others. (79)
May all the female servants of Nārāyaṇa look upon me as their own; whatever belongs to me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, let that be theirs. (3.40.80)
And may they all see that very thing as their own individual self,
just as it truly is— belonging only to themselves and not belonging to another.
May they never show partiality toward any objects of enjoyment;
may they well protect their abundant prosperity, making it ever new and divine. 82.
Let them make appropriate expenditures as they desire for their own happiness; and on the occasion of their birthdays and other such events, let them give gifts in abundance. (83)
May they always protect their devotion to their husbands, nourished by the vows of a wife;
may they perform offerings to the gods, such as the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice and other rites of charity.
Let virtuous women never look upon naked men anywhere, and let them pacify disputes and quarrels arising from others. (86)
Let them never place their trust in water, fire, or floods;
let them certainly not place their trust in those who are like beasts.
Let them not dwell with deceivers, nor with rogues or women; let them avoid association with atheistic and hostile women. (87)
When their principles are violated, let them not commit suicide, nor cause division, nor inflict beating, cutting, or even the destruction of limbs. (88)
May all such daughters-in-law as my mother be for the welfare of everyone;
may they always act for their own benefit as well as for the benefit of their husbands. (89)
May they not allow any impurity to remain in their vessels, their garments, or their bodies;
may they administer medicinal herbs that are wholesome and bestow well-being.
Let them proceed to the assemblies as is appropriate, accompanied by their circles;
and even in the assembly of women, let them strive for a position of preeminence. (91)
May they be enriched with qualities that are foremost among women and others;
may they not indulge in the playful behaviors characteristic of childhood. (92)
May they take up pleasant tasks and not indulge in gambling;
may they avoid excessive sleep and overeating, which cause disease. (93)
May they enjoy all kinds of objects of enjoyment for the sake of satisfaction—all those that are obtained through righteous means and consist of the five sense-objects. (94)
Having mounted auspicious vehicles, carriages, palanquins, and celestial chariots,
let them behold the forest regions with eyes directed toward the sky.
May they indeed enjoy all flavors offered to me with devotion,
and may they experience all objects of touch with longing directed toward me.
May all my actions be entrusted to me, Mādhava; and may they accept from me whatever is deficient, as well as everything that is required.
"May all [these women], though dependent on me, always remain independent;
may they never at any time become outward-looking according to their respective dispositions. (98)
May they not even tolerate the scent of others, yet may they be dear to me;
may they always be auspicious, possessed of modesty and happiness. (99)
May they become visible to Brahmā and visible to the divine, liberated from the ten million bonds; may they perceive the seasonal purity within earth, water, fire, air, and the rest.
May beloved wives perform such auspicious vows, accompanied by the giving of *śrāddha* and other rites, performed with devotion, which bestow a favorable rebirth. (10.1)
They bestow wealth and grain, as well as sons and daughters for the continuation of one's lineage;
they grant longevity and fame, and also increase good fortune.
May the oceans of joy become for me the bestowers of splendor, the bestowers of cheerfulness, the bestowers of bliss, and the bringers of serenity.
May my virtuous wives, who are dearer to me than life itself, always be victorious— endowed with every happiness and possessed of the fulfillment of all their desires.
Whatever other women shall exist in the world as described, they are considered by you to be like delightful women from sacred lands, O Devikā.
Heaven shall be in their very homes, liberation in the palms of their hands, and eternal good fortune shall belong to them; of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the fortieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Duties of the Housewife as Taught by the Beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. || 40 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
A man and a woman, with a concentrated mind, should preserve their sacred thread;
likewise, a wife should always perform the twilight devotions and bow to her elders.
One's preceptor, father, and elder brother, as well as the king, maternal uncle, father-in-law, and one's maternal and paternal grandfathers. (2)
One's paternal uncle who is superior by caste, one's maternal grandmother and mother, one's father's sister, one's elder teacher, one's mother-in-law, and likewise one's paternal grandmother; || 3 ||
The daughter-in-law should bow to her nurse, her elder co-wife, and her sister;
she must follow their will through the actions of her mind, speech, and body. (4)
Upon seeing them, he should protect them, rise up, and offer his salutations;
he should not sit together with them, nor should he dispute with them for his own sake.
One should never insult one's gurus out of hatred, even for the sake of one's own life;
for a daughter-in-law who harbors excessive hatred toward her gurus falls into a low state.
The husband, the brother, the giver of knowledge, the mother, and the father—
these five are especially worthy of worship as the foremost gurus.
One should always act for the welfare of one's mother-in-law and father-in-law with every effort, even at the cost of one's own life.
Having urinated, one should perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) three times; likewise after eating.
Having discharged excrement, one should indeed perform a bath for the sake of comfort.
Upon touching one's hair or the private parts of the body, the nose must be washed; likewise, upon touching the ears, the navel, and so forth, both feet must be touched with water.
Nor in fire, in a cremation ground, on wood, on a grassy plot, or on cow dung; nor in water, in a dilapidated temple, on an anthill, or in a hole inhabited by creatures. || 11 ||
One should not void excrement, urine, and so forth on the royal highway, nor on husks and the like, nor in a field, nor in a hole, nor at a sacred ford, nor in a garden, nor in a city dwelling. (12)
A virtuous wife should always be absorbed in diligent effort and devoted to righteous conduct; she should never place her feet upon the lap of her elders. 1.3.
Wherever there is censure of the guru or even slander of the guru’s wife,
one should cover one's ears there, just as one would elsewhere.
One should go there and perform service endowed with meditative cultivation;
one should always employ speech that is sweet and beneficial. 15.
Whether it be worldly, Vedic, or even spiritual knowledge—from whomever one acquires it, the womenfolk should not bear him ill will. (16)
And the wives of one's gurus who are of the same caste should be honored like a guru,
by means of anointing, bathing, and the like, as well as by massaging their limbs and so forth.
The heavy tasks, such as dressing the hair and other services, should be attended to by the women of the household;
the wife of the guru should be saluted, and thereafter one should study the Vedas.
Established in Brahman and composed in mind, she should daily study and practice the Sāvitrī, the name of Śrī Hari, and the Vedāntas that have been refined by her own self-realization.
Having first uttered the syllable *oṃ*, and thereafter the *vyāhṛtis*, one should then recite my name, the glorious Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. (3.41.20)
The young bride should never appear with worn-out or dirty clothes;
she should maintain friendship with her female companions and act for her own welfare.
She should live in the house, conforming to the likeness of her husband's age, occupation, wealth, learning, and lineage, as well as to the customs of the country, speech, and intellect.
She should practice only that which is excellent and practiced by the elders, both male and female;
by doing so, she does not incur any fault at any time.
She who serves the three aims of life and is distinguished by her sense of proportion is always called a true housewife; she is the bearer of heaven and the other realms of truth. 24.
One should diligently protect the body, for it is the abode of Dharma;
indeed, without the body, I, Nārāyaṇa, am not within the range of attainment. (25)
One should not harm any living beings, nor should one ever perform an act harmful to another;
one should not be a stealer of the property of the gods, for the wealth of the deity is indeed poison.
One should not commit treachery against the gods, nor likewise against one's guru;
one should not commit treachery against one's master, nor should one practice treachery against one's mother-in-law.
Indeed, through falsehood, excessive indulgence in pleasures, causing pain to others,
and by means of curses and diseases, one's long life comes to an end.
A daughter-in-law should never dwell anywhere with those who are very foolish or sinful, because sin is transmitted through living together, association, and the like. (29)
She should not engage in groundless enmities, nor should she utter words that pierce the vital organs;
and a daughter-in-law should never, under any circumstances, enter into conflict with many people at once. (3.41.30)
One should not prevent what is being given to the gods, gurus, or Brahmins;
one should not praise oneself, and one should also avoid censure [of others]. ||3.1||
One should not speak of the evil of the wicked, nor should one attribute false faults to them;
one should never eat together with one's master from the same vessel.
One should not cause pain to anyone; rather, one should instruct one's daughter or disciple.
One should not despise oneself and should always avoid dejection.
One should not scratch one's own head with both hands joined together;
nor should one ever utter insults, nor likewise speak vulgar words. (34)
One should never sleep in an empty house, in a deserted place, or on another's seat;
one should not cut down a sacred tree (caityavṛkṣa), nor should one ever deceive one's gurus.
She should not go to a temple after having committed an improper act;
nor should the bride maintain contact with those afflicted by disease. (36)

One should not revile yogis, those who have attained perfection, or ascetics observing vows; nor should one revile the gods, the dwellings of the gods, virtuous women, faithful wives, or female gurus. (37)
At night, one should neither discard nor eat curd mixed with sesame;
one should not consume buttermilk with milk, and one should avoid that which is infested with worms. ||38||
One should indeed give gifts of wealth for one's own prosperity to a worthy recipient;
one should always give water, food, and so forth, and on certain occasions, such as during vows, one should give [other specific items]. (39)
One should give what is auspicious for the sake of offspring, victory, and sovereignty;
indeed, one should give to those who discourse on Brahman out of great devotion to me, Hari.
A worthy recipient honored with a gift certainly delivers one in every way;
it should be given with devotion, bringing joy to both the giver and the recipient. (41)
One should give land endowed with sugarcane, barley, wheat, and rice;
likewise, one should give knowledge, as well as gold, silver, and jewels.
One should give diamonds, jewel ornaments, and the like, as well as garments and woolen blankets;
one should also bestow food, vegetables, vessels, honey, and clarified butter. (43)
"One should offer sesame seeds, saying: 'May the Lord Hṛṣīkeśa, my master and lord, be pleased with me.
Having spoken thus, one should honor and present them to ascetics, virtuous men, and virtuous women. (44)
One should give fruits, roots, drinks, vegetables, and likewise medicinal herbs; one should also give an umbrella and sandals, or whatever else may be desired, one should offer it.
A virtuous woman should perform the gift of her daughter’s hand in marriage to a man who is well-born, endowed with beauty and excellent qualities, prosperous, wealthy, and steadfast. (46)
One's own daughter, adorned with all ornaments, should be given away in marriage;
the sale of a daughter must never be performed by those seeking their own welfare. (47)
By giving land, a cow, gold, wealth, clothing,
and grain as a dowry to one's daughter's husband, everything becomes inexhaustible.
A girl given away without a dowry enters into a state of slavery;
likewise when [the husband] is excessively gluttonous, living far away, beset by calamities, or exceedingly wicked. (49)

It should never be given to one of low birth, nor to a fool, nor to one who is excessively old, nor to one who is extremely wretched, nor to a sick person, nor to one who brings about total ruin. (3.41.50)
A daughter must certainly not be given to one who is excessively angry or dissatisfied;
the giver of a daughter attains heaven and a husband who is a supreme lord. ||51||
The giver of a daughter shall obtain a wife of excellent complexion in the next world;
[the five household burdens are] the mortar, the grinding stone, the hearth, the water-jar, and the broom.
The five slaughterhouses of householders are destroyed by the five true sacrifices; one should give to living beings and likewise offer to the ancestors. (53)
One should likewise give to aquatic creatures, and one should give among cows, trees, and plants;
one should also present offerings to the deities and to guests according to one's wealth.
In this way, through giving, faults are indeed destroyed; there is no doubt about this.
Giving, as well as purity and a pure recipient, certainly brings one across.
Fire is pure in every way, and women are always pure; moreover, virtuous men and the gods are considered to be exceedingly pure—these three are so regarded. (56)
A woman who drinks liquor, is diseased, or is hateful should never be made a bride;
there should never be any conflict between a wife and her husband or others.
Where there is harmony between husband and wife, the three goals of life flourish;
she who does not go to another man, whether her husband is dead or alive, [is a virtuous wife]. (58)
She attains fame in this world and rejoices in her own home as a virtuous woman;
women must carry out their husband's word—this fault does not exist [in such a case]. (59)
Commanded by her husband, brothers, father, kinsmen, mother-in-law, father-in-law, or brother-in-law, she should undoubtedly carry out what is auspicious as well as what is inauspicious. (3.41.60)
Women should be honored by their kinsmen with ornaments, clothing, and food;
they should keep the household utensils in order, be skillful, cheerful, and averse to wasteful expenditure.
She should always perform prostration at the feet of her mother-in-law and father-in-law;
being devoted to her husband’s welfare, she shall attain heaven after gaining fame in this world.
A woman whose husband is away from home should avoid playing, grooming her body, attending social gatherings or festivals, laughing, and visiting the houses of others. (63)
She should not remain apart from her husband by day, at twilight, or at night;
she should honor her beloved according to the prescribed rule, and likewise delight and gladden him.
One should not have a desire for food prepared by others, except when invited by those who are blameless;
indeed, women should avoid restlessness of speech, hands, and feet.
One should practice a conduct that is appropriate, straightforward, and free from deceit; likewise, one should avoid hypocrisy, heretical sects, and the behavior of a heron.
One should not warm one's feet over a fire, nor should one step over it;
one should avoid forbidden actions and shun the smoke from a funeral pyre.
One should not step over a teacher, a scripture, a preceptor, a king, a woman, or a husband; likewise, one should avoid stepping over one's mother or mother-in-law, as well as their shadows.
She should avoid the beds and other belongings of others, and she should refrain from the property of others;
having become one who relishes the taste of flavors, she should not resort to another man. (69)
It would never be without oil, nor would it ever be hidden;
[it would be made] of gold, silver, lotuses, conch shells, ropes, skins, and so forth. (3.41.70)
Indeed, the purification of vessels and seats should be performed with water;
that of the *sruk* and *sruva* ladles with hot [water], and that of grains by sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*).
By carving wooden items such as sacrificial ladles and horns, by scrubbing [vessels], and by using alkaline substances, acids, and water for cleansing tin, lead, and copper; ||72||

Iron and bronze vessels are purified by ashes and water; the ground is purified by sweeping and similar means; and that which has been smeared with impurities is purified by earth and water, through the removal of odor and stain.
One should not eat food while sitting on one's haunches, nor should one ever sleep naked;
one should not bite off one's nails or hair with the teeth, nor should one awaken a sleeping person. (74)
One should not enter through a side door, nor cross a river by swimming with one's arms;
one should never step upon charcoal, ashes, hair, or similar refuse.
She should be skilled in lighting the mechanical stove, the hearth, the lamp, and so forth;
she should always be attentive when fetching water and on the road. (76)
She should be absorbed in meditation on the banks of wells, rivers, tanks, and the like;
she should be skillful even in placing her feet, in agriculture, and in [the handling of] grass and such. ||77||
She should be skilled even in gathering dried cow dung, wood, and the like;
she should also be skilled in [preparing] a corner that is worn out, infested with insects, and situated on bare ground. ||78||
On the road or even while traveling in a vehicle, the bride should follow her own beloved husband;
she should remain vigilant behind him so that no confusion with another may arise. (79)

She should be skilled in protecting children, such as sons and daughters; she should be skilled in discerning what is wholesome and unwholesome, and in determining what is to be accepted and so forth. ||3.41.80||
A virtuous woman should properly discipline her sons and refine them with auspicious virtues;
she should instruct them in pleasant duties and always maintain a spirit of faith.
A young woman should always bathe with water, excluding the head;
however, she should indeed perform an oil bath on the head every single day.
One should perform auspicious body-massage, bathing, and likewise the bath of knowledge;
one should always practice the bath of contemplating Brahman and the purification of the self.
A bride, established in tranquility, should constantly recite a rosary of Hari’s names consisting of a thousand at most, a hundred in the middle, or ten as the minimum. (84)
One should constantly worship the ancestors; they are remembered as being threefold:
those who are manifest as human beings here, and likewise the gods who have gone to heaven. (85)
Other pretas obtain birth as these three types of ancestors:
the mother, the father, the teacher, the mother-in-law, and the husband, who are all within the range of direct perception. ||86||
The moon, the sun, and fire—these deities indeed reside in heaven; yet others, who were previously deceased ancestors, have entered the state of hungry ghosts (preta) in another birth. ||87||
These three must be awakened; the householder should bow to them:
the Moon is the father, the Sun is the grandfather, and Fire is the great-grandfather.
The Somapas, the Barhiṣads, and the Agniṣvāttas—these, in that order, are the sacrificial Brahmins who drink the clarified butter; one should feed those virtuous ones, O Lord. (89)

The lunar deities are the mother, father, and so forth; the solar deities are the twice-born and others who are auspicious; the fire-deities are guests and the virtuous; and the ancestors are those who come within the range of one's vision. (3.41.90)
One should always feed those [brahmins] according to one's capacity and wealth;
and desiring prosperity, abundance, and good fortune, one should serve cows and other such beings. 91.
The bride should offer salutations to the deities and always bow to her elders; she should pay homage to her guru and recite my mantra ten million times using a rosary.
During the time of recitation, one should not speak; one should remember the Lord of Śrī, the Infallible Acyuta.
The worship of Hari is meritorious; one should constantly worship Hari.
The bride should offer herself to the glorious Supreme Self;
she should daily worship Lord Hari at the twilight hours, her husband who bestows all peace. 94.

One should offer food to the gods; that indeed constitutes the sacrifice to the gods (devayajña). One may also offer it to the [deity’s] image, or into water, or upon the ground, as part of the Vaiśvadeva rite.
One should offer the remainder to cows, to those who cook for dogs (outcastes), to dogs, and to all beings;
that is called the sacrifice to beings (bhūtayajña) for the sake of the wretched and the fallen, as well as for birds.
One performing the ancestral sacrifice should feed virtuous Brahmins, chaste women, and children;
he should always satisfy the guest with food, treating them as one would his own ancestors.
A virtuous woman should honor guests who have arrived according to her ability,
and she should give alms to a mendicant and to a virtuous student of sacred knowledge.
Free from greed, one should indeed give daughters even to those who request them;
this is called the human sacrifice, which is a means for attaining great blessings. (99)
One should always give food to me, who am Śrīmat Paramātman;
and one should also give it to the knower of Brahman—that indeed is considered the Brahma-yajña.
In every way, a virtuous woman should wash her hands during the act of eating;
indeed, she should offer [the food] preceded by purification, for by that the deities are satisfied. 101.
For the purpose of eating, one should sit down after having washed both feet and hands;
then, having performed the *āpośāna* rite, one should indeed offer [the food] to the vital breaths (*prāṇas*).
One should eat food preceded by praise and offer it as an oblation within oneself;
one should not eat before a solar eclipse, nor after an evening lunar eclipse.
One should not eat during an eclipse; having bathed, one should eat and offer [the food].
For her, eating is for the sake of her own purpose, and sexual union is for the sake of enjoyment.
And for one whose livelihood depends on her artistic skill, life ends in emptiness;
she should not sleep facing south, nor should she sleep facing west.
Neither in the open air, nor naked, nor while seated on another's seat,
should a virtuous woman ever remember me, Śrī Hari, in all her daily activities.
Day and night, one should indeed remember me, the Supreme Person who grants liberation;
one may serve me as desired, without any constraint, like a wife.
Constantly observing these duties and right conduct, she dwells in happiness;
she shall always rejoice in her home and possess an abundance of bliss. || 108 ||
From reciting and hearing this, one obtains the fruit of practicing the Dharma;
through its observance, there shall be the destruction of evil, and one will proceed upon the path to liberation.
A virtuous daughter-in-law shall obtain the fruit of visiting sacred fords, giving gifts, and observing vows;
likewise, she shall attain dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, as well as sons and daughters.

Thus ends the forty-first chapter, titled "Description of the Duties and Eternal Conduct of a Young Wife," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*. || 41 ||
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O auspicious Nārāyaṇī-Śrī, to the glory of Śiva’s queen; thereafter, I shall describe to you various other modes of conduct.
