One should meditate upon Acyuta, who is perfectly peaceful, seated in the svastika posture, holding the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, and intent on bestowing blessings. 3.46.50.
Accompanied by Brahmapriyā, attended by noble ladies, beautiful in every limb, delightful, and adorned with all ornaments. (51)
Having thus meditated upon me as a youth of white form, encircled by a halo of radiance, one should then depart elsewhere for the sake of purifying the body. (52)

Therefore, O beloved, all ritual acts performed during a period of impurity become fruitless; hence, one should always practice the purification of the body through water and other means, such as ritual bathing.
Devotion devoid of purity of being does not flourish at all;
mantras chanted by one devoid of purity of mouth are meaningless. (54)
Longevity, strength, fame, luster, progeny, cattle, and wealth, as well as sacred knowledge, wisdom, and intelligence—supreme purity bestows all these. (55)
One should bow to the sun, one should bow to elders, and likewise, being an elder, one should bow to virtuous women; one should bow to chaste women, serve them, and also serve virtuous people.
One should lead devotees of Hari to temples and other such places;
one should also utter their names and likewise remember those things that purify.
Sāketa, Madhupurī, Māyā, Kāśī, Avantī, Kāñcī, Suvarṇanagarī, and the city Puruṣottamī. (58)
One should likewise bow down to these [deities] at Kuṅkumavāpikā, which grant liberation;
as well as to Śālagrāma from the Gaṇḍakī river, to Śambhala, and to Harimandira.
One should likewise remember Nandigrāma situated in Kosala, as well as Akṣaragrāma,
Daṇḍaka, Saindhava forest, Jambūbhāga, and Puṣkara.
One should likewise remember the forest of Utpalāvarta, Naimiṣa, Kurujāṅgala, Arbuda, Hemavanta, and the tiger-forest (Vyāghrāraṇya).
She should apply a tilaka mark on her forehead, adorned with red saffron;
likewise, O virtuous woman, she should place a saffron crescent moon in the center of her forehead.
Having gone toward the temple, she should ring the bell;
she should perform kīrtana and bhajana while remembering the Supreme Lord.
Uttering cries of victory and clapping her hands,
she should bow to the Lord and light a lamp scented with fragrant ghee.
"Arise, arise, O Blessed One! Abandon your yogic sleep, O Lord!
I have come to serve you"—in this way, one should awaken Hari. (65)
One should perform the massaging of the feet and attend to the service of the body;
having offered a tooth-stick for cleansing the teeth, one should bathe [the deity] with fragrant waters.
One should offer me the essence of fragrance and other such items, and then offer garments;
one should worship me with sandalwood paste and the like, and perform the auspicious waving of lights (ārati).
One should cause it to be whirled nine times over my face;
having whirled the five-wick lamp, the water, and the cloth, one should proclaim victory.
Having offered various cooked foods and milk mixed with sugar, and having performed the rite of adornment with devotion through garments, ornaments, and auspicious items; ||69||
One should perform the waving of lights (ārārtika) with lamps, necklaces, and other such items, as well as with erotic ornaments;
one should also offer sweetmeat balls, *laḍḍu*s, fresh butter, curd, and milk.
Then, having offered the five enjoyments, one should offer betel and water; thereafter, being eager, one may attend to one's own worldly affairs. (71)
And at midday, one should offer great enjoyments and various flavors;
having prepared whatever is fit for a king's enjoyment, one should cause my bed to be made.
The virtuous woman should always eat prasāda accompanied by tulasī;
and when four ghaṭikās remain of the day, she should awaken me.
With the sound of musical instruments and with devotion, one should offer the enjoyment of the fruit;
thereafter, one should perform service to me and carry out one's own ritual duties and so forth.
Then one should perform the waving of lights (ārārtika) and offer milk and other substances;
at nightfall (pradoṣa), one should again perform the ārārtika and give my desired offerings.
She should cause a beautiful bed to be prepared and perform service to the King;
by making a total surrender of herself, the virtuous woman shall obtain great bliss.
Thus, that virtuous woman was devoted to Kṛṣṇa, her mind absorbed in service, and dedicated to the servitude of the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (77)
Having delivered a hundred generations of his lineage, he goes to my imperishable abode.
Thus, my Janmāṣṭamī and the auspicious Rādhāṣṭamī should be observed.
The Lakṣmī-navamī should be observed with vows, festivals, and worship;
likewise the Rāmāditya-navamī and the Vāmana-dvādaśī. (79)
There is also the festival of the heap of food (annakūṭotsava), as well as Ananta-caturdaśī,
the fourteenth day of Nṛsiṃha, and likewise my own birthdays.
The Śukla-ramā-saptamī in Kārtika is the embodiment of the vow;
likewise, the meritorious Pūrṇimā of Caitra should be observed with great festivity.
On a sacrificial ground (sthaṇḍila) endowed with five colors, one should cause a beautiful mandala called Sarvatobhadra to be made, auspicious and consisting of seven kinds of grain;
it is joined with thirty-two petals and radiant with a pericarp and filaments. ||82||
One should place me, the virtuous one, upon a golden lion-throne in the pericarp;
and [therein] Ramā, Rādhā, Śrī, Bhū, Virajā, Māṇikī, and Rati.
Padmāvatī, Lakṣmī, Amṛtā, and likewise Maṅgalā;
Durgā, Sarasvatī, Haṃsī, Mañjulā, Sadguṇā, and Jayā; Campā, Kastūrikā, Haimī, Śāntā, Muktā, and Devikā. ||84||
He should place me, the beloved of my devotees, himself among those virtuous women;
he should also place Rādhā, the companions of the month, and my other attendants.
The conch, the discus, the mace, the lotus, the Śārṅga bow, the arrows, and the sword Nandaka;
likewise the pestle, the plough, the staff, the Kaustubha gem, and the svastika. ||86||
One should install the forest-garland, the Śrīvatsa mark, the yellow garment, and the staff; and also Garuḍa, as well as the palm-tree that adorns the chariot.
Also Sumati, Dāruka, Kumuda, Kumudākṣaka,
Nanda, Sunanda, Caṇḍa, Pracaṇḍa, and likewise Bala.
[He worshipped] Prabala, Vallabha, Śuka, Bhāgavata, Svaprakāśa, Hemanta, and the Lord who is the master of the directions. (89)
Viśvaksena, the Imperishable (Akṣara), Śiva, Viṣṇu, Vināyaka,
the planets, the gods, the Mothers, and the mandala beginning with Brahmapriyā.
Likewise, one should assign Vītihotra and all the avatāras;
then, being virtuous, one should worship them with devotion through the rites of invocation and so forth. 91.
Invocation, the seat, water for the feet, the arghya offering, and fragrance;
the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), bathing with water, ornaments, garments, and sandalwood paste. (92)
The honey-mixture (madhuparka), incense and lamps, fragrance, a sacred thread, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), delightful liquids, saffron, and excellent water. ||93||
One should likewise offer water for sipping (ācamana), the food offering (naivedya), betel leaf (tāmbūla), and a priestly fee (dakṣiṇā);
then perform circumambulation (pradakṣiṇa), prayer (prārthanā), prostration like a staff (daṇḍavat), and the request for forgiveness (kṣamāpana). ||94||
Then one should offer the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), prostrations, and a handful of flowers;
thereafter, one should indeed offer [worship] to all the presiding deities, the goddesses, and the attendants (pārṣada) and so forth.
A devoted woman, firm in her vow of chastity, should worship with supreme devotion while the bells,
cymbals, bronze lutes, flutes, and other instruments resound.
One should perform kīrtana and dancing accompanied by cymbals, mṛdaṅga drums, and other instruments;
those devotees who, overwhelmed with love, dance before Śrī Hari [attain the highest state]. 97.
Accompanied by shouts of "Victory!", they should all be intent on reciting virtuous stories and narrations; thereafter, they should perform dances and playful jests.
And those who are truthful and devoted to me with devotion should prepare my bed;
likewise for the daughter-in-law, the wife, and the woman whose primary concern is service. 99.
I always dwell in the *sadāṅka* (the seat of the six) and likewise reside in the heart;
she too, having established herself in the *nāka*, indeed proceeds to my abode.
Whoever in the three worlds shall offer me any kind of worship at all, they shall go to my imperishable abode, which bestows the four goals of human existence.
May he worship me with devotion, remember me, or serve me; may he feed me, delight me, adorn me, and gladden me.
Having become my companion in dwelling, she should lay me down upon the bed;
she should massage me, carry me, make me laugh, and even cause me to sing.
One should practice and also cause others to practice every form of devotion consisting of love;
she indeed shall be dear to Me, ever-attendant, and become beloved by Brahman.
Whether a man be liberated through Brahman or one who knows the Self, he is indeed a divine attendant forever; he is equal to Me—of this there is no doubt.

Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Yoga of Śrī Puruṣottama," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the glorious *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, to my supreme and transcendent yoga directed toward Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the World, who bestows the fruits of all desires. (1)
She who would place her love in me, Kṛṣṇa, shall attain the supreme state;
O Lakṣmī, even a Cāṇḍālī woman intent on meditation upon me is indeed a deity.
This courtesan of mine is established in yoga, free from worldly qualities, and follows a divine path;
she is perfected in the knowledge of the inner self and is solely devoted to the worship of Hari. || 3 ||
And he attains the imperishable abode from which there is no return, from which this entire universe is born, and by which consciousness is experienced. || 4 ||
In whom all things dissolve, and by whom they are pervaded so that they live;
who, though devoid of qualities, appears as if possessed of qualities—He is the Supreme, the Infinite. || 5 ||
I, who am eternally situated within, am the destroyer of the fear of saṃsāra;
by worshipping me, the beloved Lord, one is completely liberated from saṃsāra.
Through action the embodied soul obtains a body, and by desire it is bound;
having surrendered that desire to me, let him attain the state which has me as its supreme goal.
Deprived of me, she becomes possessed by desire and overcome by anger;
greed indeed enters her and brings about the destruction of her virtue. (8)
It produces delusion of the mind and leads a person to sin;
thus, O beloved, the body would be the root of sin without me.
Therefore, having attained union with Me, one should go beyond all defects that are devoid of qualities;
having withdrawn every perception, he rests in the abode of the Imperishable.
Knowing him to be the bestower of liberation, one who abides in the dharma of truth should serve him;
he is worshipped with various sacrifices by those who know the meaning of the Vedas and understand ritual action.

He alone is the bestower of the fruits of action for those who observe vows, for ascetics, for practitioners of yoga, and for those who perform the sacrifice of knowledge; and he is the giver of liberation to those whose actions are free from desire.
The sages know that Lord who, assuming the forms of deities and ancestors during the offerings of *havya* and *kavya*, partakes of me—that Lord is the bestower of liberation. 1.3.
Whether meditated upon, saluted, or worshipped with devotion, I grant the eternal abode; one should worship me, that Hari.
I alone am the supreme lord, the support of all beings;
free from old age and death, I am the imperishable Hari, the bestower of liberation.
O Nārāyaṇī, even embodied beings who worship my lotus feet quickly attain immortality; know me to be Puruṣottama.
Blissful, undecaying Brahman, the supreme light, eternal, higher than the highest—that am I; that is the supreme state of Viṣṇu.
Non-dual, devoid of qualities, eternal, without a second, incomparable, the most perfect, consisting of pure knowledge—this is the means to liberation. || 18 ||
O Lakṣmī, that Yoginī who worships me in such a manner with service characterized by every disposition attains my supreme state.
Free from qualities, devoid of attachment, adorned with virtues such as tranquility, and liberated from latent impressions—this Brahmic beloved attains the imperishable state. (3.47.20)
My incarnate forms indeed appear as pairs;
they all honor me, Hari, the bestower of the eternal abode.
Having meditated upon that which is undecaying and supreme, wherein all this— both that which moves and that which does not move— is non-different, the virtuous woman is liberated from saṃsāra.
Having conquered her vital breaths and mastered her diet, she is devoted to my service;
she beholds me, her beloved who bestows all bliss and happiness, within her heart. (23)
Though devoid of qualities, I assume the form of one who bestows grace upon the worlds and accept all service rendered with sincerity, becoming the very foundation of those virtues.
The overseer of all actions, residing in the hearts of embodied beings, incomparable and the support of all—let him indeed take refuge in Me. (25)
Know me to be that Hari, Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, the stainless one, by whose will the principles beginning with Mahat and ending with the Viśeṣas were produced through his creative act. 26.
By whose command Aniruddha creates the world with its forms,
Pradyumna remains as its protector, and Saṃkarṣaṇa withdraws it.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa are His portions, devoted to His activities;
one should know Me as the sustainer of all those portions, and from that, one shall attain liberation.
That knowledge which is rooted in devotion is indeed the knowledge that bestows liberation;
such devotion consists of service characterized by affection and is the most auspicious and supreme. (29)
May there be devotion toward me, Hari, for her by whom various gifts, sacrifices, vows, pilgrimages, and acts of worship were performed in former times.
The eternal, supreme Dharma shines even through a mere fragment of devotion;
endowed with supreme faith, one becomes a true devotee of Me. 3.1.
When the defects are dissolved, the intellect always becomes clear;
those defects, such as passion and the rest, have been cast into me by the wise. (32)
Since it is from me alone that the qualities arise and evolve, the intellect endowed with them becomes excellent, serene, and confident. (3.3)
And when that stream consisting of knowledge is attained, I myself become accessible;
for that intellect, being of the nature of knowledge, indeed bestows liberation and grants my abode.
Having performed *kriyāyoga* toward me, one should acquire the purity of the intellect;
then, through the yoga of service, one should constantly serve me as a maidservant.
Saints, the earth, water, fire, the sun, Brahmins, the heart, and those born of various minerals;
virtuous women, cows, yogis, the intellect, and so forth—these are my images and my forms. (36)
Deities, shrines, sacred fords, and the like, as well as images and manifestations—
among these, I alone am to be worshipped, just as Janārdana is worshipped in his consort.
She who, endowed with devotion, worships me—the omnipresent one—with action, mind, speech, and devotion, shall become one with Brahman. (38)

Even when the husband possesses human nature rather than divine nature, the bride likewise does not possess divinity; for the defects of passion, anger, and so forth are indeed observed [in him]. (39)
But if a wife always maintains a divine disposition toward her husband with her mind,
serving him with the vision of Nārāyaṇa, that service shall grant liberation.
If divine vision is directed toward the form of a woman or an image, it will indeed grant liberation, just as the mind [fixed] upon the Śiva-linga does. ||41||
The virtuous men and women are my very forms and images;
having fixed one's auspicious and divine gaze upon them, one should perform service to them. (42)
These images composed of the five elements are indeed conscious and belong to me alone;
for by pleasing them, I truly become well-pleased. (43)
There, the offering of action has been performed; I accept that which consists of service.
And I bestow upon the female servant the supreme state, the imperishable abode. 44.
Non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, celibacy, non-possessiveness, absence of envy, compassion, tranquility, and service—these are the virtues of the good. 45.
Having placed all [the deities] within me, one should practice my yoga;
for the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Puruṣottama is the soul of all that moves and is immobile. 46.
Realizing this, the beloved should make Śrī Hari her own husband and worship Him;
this yoga is indeed of the nature of the goal, supreme, and manifest as My very self. 47.
That [state] is of the nature of attainment for me; the wise know this, having abandoned faults and indeed made them into forms of virtues within Hari and myself. 48.

A virtuous woman, devoted to the yoga of ritual action, should worship me, her beloved, who am the Lord of all, with full conformity; she should worship daily for the sake of liberation, being ever dear to me. 49.
Devoted both to the welfare of the world and likewise to her own welfare,
that virtuous woman, performing divine rites, indeed honors me.
In the morning, he praises me, Hari, the source of the universe, the inner controller of all, with hymns and other forms of praise; he sings of the Lord through recitations. (51)

Furthermore, through fasting and other observances, by listening to and reflecting upon the teachings, and even by worship with flowers and other offerings—that indeed is considered the divine practice. (52)
For those who thus engage in the practice of devotion, faults are destroyed at their very root;
even desire, anger, and the like surely attain a divine state.
One's intellect shall also become divine, bestowing liberation and filled with knowledge;
for everything other than me, the one Nārāyaṇa, is impermanent. (54)
All objects are indeed impermanent, while Lord Hari alone is eternal;
therefore, one should take refuge in that single, eternal One by means of impermanent instruments. (55)
One should always be dispassionate toward enjoyments both here and hereafter;
for one who is not dispassionate never turns back from saṃsāra at all. //56//
Endowed with virtues such as tranquility, she should practice the awakening to liberation;
intent upon meditation on Hari, she shall become one of purified intellect. (57)
One should meditate upon me everywhere as the Lord of Śrī, the Supreme Person;
I, Kṛṣṇa, abide pervading the entire universe consisting of the perishable and the imperishable.
Knowing this, one who has taken refuge in devotion should worship me everywhere;
for by its very nature, the Self is twofold: both the supreme (para) and the non-supreme (apara). ||59||
I am the Supreme Soul, the Transcendent, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Puruṣottama; my many incarnations are considered to be Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa, and others.
The auspicious splendor of my form is declared to be the imperishable Self;
there are many who are liberated, and they all become the Supreme.
The lords, the powers, the gods, the goddesses, humans and others—all these, as well as all other living beings, become embodied in existence. ||62||
Thus, having established her conscious awareness upon both the individual soul and the Supreme Soul, the virtuous woman should always worship the supreme Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. (63)
He is the one, the pure, the supreme among the imperishable, the Lord of souls;
the Lord of Māyā, Kāla, and the Imperishable, and the Sovereign Lord of incarnations.
Hari is the Lord of the virtuous, the Lord of the liberated, the Lord of those dear to Brahman,
the Lord of the chaste women, the Lord of devotees, the Lord of the devotees' consorts, and the Lord of his beloved.
One should contemplate Him as the Lord of Brahmā, the Lord of all, the Self-lord, the Supreme Sovereign, and the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa. ||66||
Having known Me as that very one—without a second, the supreme, eternal Brahman, and the object of knowledge for the Vedāntas—one shall attain the Imperishable. 67.
I alone am supreme bliss, devoid of qualities, higher than the highest;
I am Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord, filled with divine attributes.
To the wise, I am the Supreme Self, shining eternally within their hearts;
having ascended the eight steps of perfection, one attains my supreme state.
Purity of food is the first; purity of the body is the second;
purity of the senses is the third; and the fourth is internal purity.
Purity of the self is indeed the fifth, and the sixth is the concentration upon the Supreme Self.
The seventh is the functioning of meditation, and the eighth is being fixed upon that very [object]. || 7.1 ||
Thinking thus, the virtuous woman should briefly take refuge in this octad;
for by my grace she shall become a consumer of my food, and that indeed is the purity of her sustenance.
Indeed, that which is considered bodily purification is for me to be accompanied by initiation;
the third purification is truly that wherein the senses are dedicated to my sake.
All actions are for my sake, and purification occurs in the interval;
this is indeed considered the state of being endowed with divine, excellent qualities through self-surrender to me, Kṛṣṇa. (74)
For here, the excellence of being itself is considered to be the purification of the self;
the virtuous woman should always contemplate her own self as having the nature of Brahman. (75)
She is liberated, eternal, the great liberation, the form of Lakṣmī, and the everlasting;
she is indeed declared to be the purity of the Self, devoid of illusion and its products. (76)
Having made his own throne, he should cause me, the Supreme Lord, to be mounted upon it;
he should bear me, establish me, and practice my yoga.
I dwell within the consciousness of her form, which is fit to be sustained by me;
that indeed is my abode in her, and this is considered the supreme meditation upon the Self.
But that which is the very continuity of my state of being the object of trust, and that which is the very continuity of the flow of all bliss; || 79 ||
That which is the singular continuity of the flood of all light, and that which is the singular continuity of the flood of all consciousness; || 3.47.80 ||
Furthermore, that which is the very one-pointedness of the flow of wisdom, and that which is the state of being fixed upon me in an uninterrupted stream; ||| 81 ||

That is declared to be the excellent Sopānikā-vṛtti, the seventh stage of meditation; it occurs when the dissolution of the self into the circle [of the heart] has become superior to all other states of consciousness directed toward Śrī Hari. ||8.2||
The offering of the attracted consciousness is non-dual yoga;
that is the supreme samādhi here, which milks out eternal bliss. ||83||
Where there exists the manifestation of the nature of the Supreme Lord, yet no manifestation of itself exists—that is the eighth state, the supreme condition. ||84||
When one's own form, consisting of the bliss of Brahman and identical with the Supreme Lord,
shines forth, then one enjoys all desires together with me.
Happiness, satisfaction, contentment, fulfillment, bliss, celebration, delight, serenity, joy, great joy, and mental rapture; ||86||
The wave, expansion, enjoyment, goodness, and supreme sovereignty;
blossoming, horripilation, affection, love, and boundless delight. (87)
It is known by many names such as attraction (ākarṣaṇa), rest (viśrānti), the great deep sleep (mahāsuṣupti), the fourth state (turyāvasthā), and innate bliss (nijānanda). ||88||
The fruit is described by those who know it, and that very state is the eighth station;
having attained it, there is no returning again—indeed, none at all.
O Nārāyaṇī, by means of this eightfold yoga described by me,
one should indeed marry Me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
For her whose devotion to Hari is firm and whose worship of Hari is likewise supreme,
for that yoginī of pure discipline, liberation is indeed within her grasp.
May [the breath] be firm within me and may it rest upon me, the Lord;
for that should be understood as the supreme posture, wherein one takes refuge in both the vital breath and myself. 92.
One should also perform the withdrawal [of the senses] into me alone;
thus one shall go forth to the Supreme Brahman, from which there is no return. 93.
One should cause the Supreme Lord, the Consort of Śrī, to enter one's own self;
the virtuous woman should establish me, the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, within herself. 94.
He is the self of all, his own self, the sole cause of all the worlds;
he is of beautiful form, most lovely with splendor, and resplendent with an aura of light.
Accessible to the mind, youthful, and the fulfiller of all desires;
with eyes like the petals of a blooming lotus, adorned with beautiful earrings. ||96||
Long-armed, with noble limbs, adorned with every ornament,
wearing yellow garments, lovely, a worthy husband, and a good companion.
Wearing a golden sacred thread and a garland of excellent *tulasī* leaves,
with the *śrīvatsa* mark upon his chest, he was adorned by necklaces and the Kaustubha jewel.
One should meditate upon me as the Supreme Self; from that, one shall attain supreme liberation.
Through meditation, sins are destroyed, and through meditation, even liberation comes to pass. (99)

Hari is pleased through meditation; I am firmly established in meditation. When the triad of meditation, the object of meditation, and the state of the meditator becomes one, [then Hari is pleased]. (3.47.100)
Then immortality comes to pass as one partakes of the nectar of knowledge;
one enjoys great bliss and constantly partakes of the nectar of Brahman. || 10.1 ||
The Brahman of sound, the Brahman of the syllable, and the Brahman of the instrument,
as well as the Brahman of the self and the supreme Brahman— these indeed become one.
Indeed, liberation is born from samādhi within the great ocean of bliss;
bliss is indeed the supreme Brahman, and the Lord Hari is the supreme Brahman. (103)
"Om"—this indeed is the Supreme Brahman; it is existence, consciousness, and bliss (saccidānanda).
One who is joined with the practice of this very [syllable] attains even supreme liberation. 104.
But she who, with a concentrated mind, should either hear or even read this, having attained oneness with me, will certainly become beloved of Hari. 105.

Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Yoga of the Supreme Brahman in Person," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Śrī Nārāyaṇī Śrī said:
O omniscient one, O beloved, O ocean of compassion, tell me that by which the Blessed Lord, the Supreme Ruler, who is higher than the highest, may be pleased. (1)
Śrī Puruṣottama said: O beloved, if you desire bliss, worship with your whole being me, Nārāyaṇa, the supreme lover, whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss.
Enemies do not harm or oppress her, nor do malevolent planets and the like;
even Rākṣasas do not look upon a woman who is devoted to Viṣṇu.
For one whose devotion to the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Self, becomes firm, their spiritual perfections are accomplished; therefore, they become even more endowed with devotion.
Those two feet of hers are fruitful which go to the abode of Viṣṇu;
those two hands of hers are fruitful which are intent upon my worship.
Those eyes of hers are fruitful which behold the Lord of Śrī;
that tongue alone is auspicious which is devoted to the name of Hari.
Those two ears of hers have become fruitful by grasping the essence of the sacred narratives of Śrī;
indeed, that skin of hers is truly purifying, which perceives the touch of Hari.
That tongue is truly flavorful by which the nectar of Hari is attained;
for its sense of smell is indeed meritorious, since it perceives the fragrance of the glorious [Lord].
That waist which was for the sake of Hari, and likewise for the sake of Hari alone;
the chest also for the sake of Hari, and those two cheeks for the sake of Hari alone.
He even offered his cheek for the sake of the lions, likewise his hips for the sake of the lions,
his thighs for the sake of the lions, and his shanks for the sake of the lions alone.
Even my lips are for the sake of Hari, my hair is likewise for the sake of Hari;
my bed is for the sake of Hari, and my wakefulness is for the sake of Hari.

Her dalliance was for the sake of Hari; even her playful gestures were for the sake of Hari; her coquettish expressions and emotional states were for the sake of Hari, and her dance as well was for the sake of Hari.
Singing and laughter, as well as whatever gaze is directed toward Hari; whatever mental reflection and whatever intellect is directed toward Hari alone. (1.3)
Even the sense of ego is for the sake of Hari, and action is likewise for the sake of Hari;
her erotic sentiment is for the sake of Hari, and her form is indeed for the sake of Hari.
Ornaments are for the sake of Hari, and decorations likewise are for the sake of Hari;
collyrium, sandalwood paste, oil, and the braided hair are all for the sake of Hari. (15)
Dharma is for the sake of Hari, prosperity is for the sake of Hari alone;
likewise, vows, good conduct, purity, and ritual bathing are for the sake of Hari alone. (16)
The formative activities (saṃskāras) are also for the sake of Hari, and their expansion is likewise for the sake of Hari;
manifestation, modesty, joy, and affection are also solely for the sake of Hari. (17)
Delicacy, sweetness, and luster—all directed solely toward Hari;
adornment for the sake of Hari, and even exertion for the sake of Hari. (18)
Festivals are for the sake of Hari, and splendor is likewise for the sake of Hari;
acquisition and expenditure, as well as effort, are also solely for the sake of Hari. (19)
Happiness, delight, and great bliss—all are for the sake of Hari alone;
home, field, and prosperity—all are for the sake of Hari alone.
Sons, daughters, cows, and likewise horses for the sake of the Lord;
elephants, vehicles, and celestial chariots—all these were for the sake of the Lord alone. (21)
The garden, the abundance of crops, and the household utensils are for the sake of Hari;
even a moment, the protection from breath, and consciousness itself are for the sake of Hari.
Their qualities exist for the sake of Hari, and their cultivation is also for the sake of Hari;
their exertion, their rise, and even their cessation are for the sake of Hari. (23)
Her state is one of non-obstruction, and she is the very heart of Hari;
she is the secret mantra and the mystery for the sake of Hari, everything belonging to him.

The arts, the study of the sciences, and practice—all for the sake of Hari; passion and tranquility—for the sake of Hari; undertakings and their completion—and even maturation—for the sake of Hari. (25)
Wandering, worldly activity, and mental manifestation are for the sake of Hari;
greed, desire, volition, and celebration are for the sake of Hari. (26)
Sacrifice, charity, devotion, and religious duty are for the sake of Hari;
a bed of flowers, a bed upon the chest, and a bed in the upright posture are for the sake of Hari. (27)
The pavilion, the canopy, the rāsa dance, the play, and the longing were all for the sake of Hari;
even the wandering, the seizing, and the very livelihood were for the sake of Hari. (28)
Writing and playing, as well as skill for the sake of Hari; cleverness and even fickleness, as well as divinity for the sake of Hari. (29)
Even the bending of limbs, perspiration, and likewise stimulation—all such Rajasic impulses are for the sake of Hari alone. (3.48.30)
Food, drink, belching, and the attainment of the elements are for the sake of Hari;
even the convention and the secret sign are for the sake of Hari. (31)
Seeking, searching, and waiting for the sake of Hari;
the desire for the bliss of Hari alone; and a secluded place for the sake of Hari—[these are the characteristics]. (32)
She whose very form is love for Hari is indeed Hari himself, both within and without;
all this has truth as its essence, and there is no beloved other than Keśava.
In this truly essence-less cycle of existence, the beloved Hari alone is the great essence;
for those who are not devotees, the snares of worldly existence become exceedingly firm. (34)
Indeed, for you who are devoted, these [waters] shall surely bestow virtues and become free from bonds (vipāśā);
having brought incomparable bliss under my control, one should acquire [merit]. (35)
That state, its form, and likewise its bliss cannot be described;
it can neither be pointed out nor seen by those whose selves are unrefined.
The bliss of Hari is free from all limiting adjuncts and is unsurpassed;
having experienced that bliss which consists of the Supreme Brahman, the virtuous woman becomes one with Brahman.
O Lotus-born One, I am always pleased with her who delights in discourse on that [Truth] and engages in excellent conversation; she is indeed in constant association with the virtuous. (38)
I am indeed pleased with her who constantly performs the chanting of my names even during hunger, thirst, stumbling, and other such circumstances. (39)
But that bride who holds her husband as her very life and is devoted solely to the worship of her husband—for her I am always pleased, and I grant my own beloved abode. (3.48.40)
But that virtuous woman who is free from envy, likewise devoid of egoism, and devoted to the state of a servant—in her I am pleased in every way. (41)
Therefore, all you who are dear to Brahmā, dear to Hari, and whose very selves are me—worship here Hari, my beloved, the lover of Kṛṣṇa. 42.
The body is indeed the abode of death and the abode of decay for those engaged in ritual action;
life is flickering, and riches are as unstable as a flash of lightning. (43)
Wealth is subject to seizure by kings and others; prosperity is fragile and momentary;
half of one's life is consumed by sleep, and likewise, half is spent for the sake of acquisition. (44)
Having reflected that half of that [life] is for enjoyment and the other half is childhood and deep sleep, a virtuous woman should perform my worship as if she were in her youth. (45)
Since the body is the abode of destruction and the supreme seat of calamities, and its path is suddenly severed, one should therefore accomplish devotion to it. (46)
A woman, knowing that liberation is possible, should indeed offer herself with her whole being to me—the essence—within this essenceless saṃsāra. 47.
For the sake of ceasing the union with the body, O virtuous woman, you should worship me, Nārāyaṇa—the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa—this very moment. 48.
After wandering through thousands of millions of births among stationary beings and others, human birth has somehow been attained by this bewildered woman. (49)
In that regard, giving gifts and performing worship are the fruit of austerity in previous births;
devotion is the fruit of receiving blessings, and service likewise results in good fortune.
Having attained this human birth which is so difficult to find, that virtuous woman who does not worship Hari is indeed a fool of dull intellect; such a woman shall be born again and again.
What can discernment avail that exceedingly foolish woman?
When Hari-Kṛṣṇa is propitiated, he bestows the desired fruit.
Whether it be an outcaste, one who is base, impure, or even a sinner; or whether it be a courtesan, devoid of virtue and devoted to sexual intercourse and the like. (53)
Whether she be impure or recently delivered, a devotee of Viṣṇu is superior to a twice-born;
whereas one devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu, even if a twice-born, is like a dog-eater.
Therefore, by serving Hari alone, one should satisfy the Supreme Lord;
for when I am satisfied, everything is satisfied, since I am the Self of all.
Just as all footprints are contained within the footprint of an elephant, and all elemental beings are contained within space,
so too is everything established in me, the beginningless Śrī Hari.
Birth and death are its two boundaries; their destruction comes through service to me.
Whether meditated upon, remembered, worshipped, or saluted, I shall deliver [the devotee]. 57.
Out of compassion, I always effect the severing of the bonds of saṃsāra;
merely by the utterance of my name, there is the destruction of great sins. (58)
O beloved, by the mere remembrance of my embodied form, even the state of Brahman may be attained;
and through service to my chaste wife, one shall swiftly attain liberation.
Even one who is devoid of merit, being led away by the messengers of Yama and powerless to liberate herself, shall remember me; I rescue her from that suffering.
Having put to flight the messengers of Yama, I lead my beloved to my own abode—
she who remembers me, a weak woman who has sought refuge with a distressed mind.
I shall uplift her who is protectorless, under the power of others, devoid of a mass of merit, lacking a support, and without refuge. (62)
As long as there is no impairment of the senses and as long as disease does not afflict you, so long, O virtuous lady, you should serve me and prepare the path to liberation. (63)
Kṛṣṇa, Mādhava, and Hari are always to be worshipped with one's whole being, meditated upon, served, and propitiated by a virtuous woman. 64.
Without propitiating the Lord of the World who dwells within the heart of the beloved of Brahmā, one cannot attain supreme bliss; by serving him, one shall proceed to happiness.
O Acyuta, Ananta, Govinda, Kṛṣṇa, Mādhava, Keśava; O beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, O Lord Dāmodara! ||66||
O Hare Kṛṣṇa, O All-pervading Rāma, Nārāyaṇa, Narāyaṇa! O Lord of the senses, O Supreme Brahman beyond the imperishable, O Supreme Sovereign! (67)
"Puruṣottama, Mukteśa, Brahmeśa, and Janārdana;
O Blessed One, Pervasive Lord," thus a virtuous woman should always utter [these names]. (68)
For her who worships me in this way, I do not dwell far away;
O beloved, she abides in me and I abide in her at all times.
O Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the World, son of Kambharā, granter of desires!
O Vāsudeva, son of Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa, Janārdana! || 3.48.70 ||
"O Beloved, O Self-controlled One, O Bestower of Great Bliss, O Śrī Parameśvara!
O Lord of Satī, O Lord of the virtuous!"—thus indeed do they call out repeatedly. (71)
Even the deities beginning with Brahmā perform worship to them;
they are indeed venerated everywhere, just like Kamalā.
For those whose minds are shrouded by illusion and who do not know His power, and who do not know Him residing within the lotus of the heart—their loss is the greatest. (73)
Hari is pleased with those who possess faith, but not by wealth nor by kinsmen;
Janārdana is pleased by devotion, and not by personal virtues nor by austerity.
He is pleased by service, by worship, and by remembrance;
He is pleased by the surrender of the self. Therefore, let those dear to Him bring Him satisfaction. (75)
Sons, friends, prosperity, and many riches—these abundant accomplishments are indeed not difficult to obtain for those who are devoted to the worship of Hari. (76)
Desiring happiness in this world and the next, one should worship me, Hari—the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). (77)
The body of that woman whose head does not bow to Viṣṇu— the bestower of liberation and the destroyer of karmas— should be understood as a treasure-trove of sins.
A body endowed with devotion to Hari is to be understood as divine, even in the case of a woman;
through devotion they indeed become superior, while those devoid of devotion are the lowest. (79)
Therefore, O Lakṣmī, those women who are filled with devotion and who delight in serving me through acts such as sweeping and cleaning are worthy of worship. (3.48.80)
Those who bring about the assembly of the virtuous attain the supreme state—those who are devoted to the dharma of Hari, who are peaceful, and who serve the lotus feet of Hari. 8.1.
Devoted to the deeds of Hari, they were intent on incessantly crying out "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa";
every single pore of their bodies was radiant with the overflowing of love for Kṛṣṇa.
"I am Kṛṣṇā, and I too am Kṛṣṇā"—thus they acted, having taken refuge in this [deception].
They were called out with the words, "Take the flute and come to the grove. (83)
Take me aside here; grant me your secret.
O dweller of the grove, make me drink the nectar of love and the great bliss. (84)
O Kṛṣṇa, make her drink the essence of internal absorption arising from union with You;
cause her to attain the love of identity and make her clearly Your servant. 85.
O Mādhava, make me a handmaid to Rājanasī and her friend;
O Lord, make me a lotus in a secluded lake. (86)
O All-pervading Lord, create for the autumn night a moon resembling the foam of milk;
O Hari, create a female cuckoo among the creepers of spring.
Out of compassion for me, who am afflicted by the cold, please provide me with a woolen garment;
and here, please fashion me into the sacrificial altar for the performance of every sacrifice.
O ocean of compassion, please make me your pillow for the sake of my rest;
manifest yourself as a cool beloved to one who is heated by the fire of longing. (89)
Make the bliss of Brahman your beloved through the supportless samādhi;
worship me as Muktānikā, the consort of Kṛṣṇa who is united with Māyā.
Make the mind that has been drawn toward everything find its place of immersion;
behold the oceanic expanse of the rivers of the flow of love. ||91||
Make your own form distinct from that of one whose joy has arisen from the absence of a lover;
make me your army for you who are joined with the god of love in battle. 92.
Make your heart the seat for the Kaustubha gem that has been separated from it,
and well-join it here as the supporting vine for the bimba-fruit lip of love.
Make the bimbas of my eyes like lotus petals; O Lord of the Moonlight, become mine here, equal to the full moon of the new moon day.
O virtuous one, be my lord here; for Cakorā you are the moon, for Kṛṣṇā you are Kṛṣṇa, for Śalabhā you are fire, and for Timi you become the nectar of the throat. 95.
O best of husbands, be as the rain from the *svāti* constellation is to the *cātaka* bird; be as the cloud is to the peahen; and be as Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa is to the new bride. (96)
Be a provider of water for the yogis scorched by the forest fire of separation;
be a Hari who takes her hand as she is submerged in the pit of the ocean of worldly existence. 97.
Be established in the eyes, the heart, the mind, and consciousness;
be the giver of bliss in all the senses and remain steadfast within the inner self. 98.
"O Śivārājñī, O Śrī, dwell within me to whatever extent you may, reaching from my nails to the crown of my head"—thus is the unification through identity with me. (99)
She who goes forth shall become beloved of Brahmā and beloved of Hari in this world;
by reading or hearing this, one becomes equal to Rādhā and Lakṣmī. (3.48.10)
Indeed, through metaphorical devotion, this union of identity with me may come to be; having realized himself as being of my very nature, a man or a woman shall attain me.
Indeed, this [fire] does not cook for one who is unworthy or devoid of devotion;
having heard the *Vadhūgītā* in the past, one should always be devoted to right conduct.
Having become established in being, one should then practice the yoga of devotion which is devoid of qualities;
and by descending into the yoga of Puruṣottama, one should become absorbed in Him. || 103 ||
Then she becomes firmly united with the Supreme Brahman in person;
through her, this state of identity is attained by virtue of my grace. (104)
When I am thus most perfectly complete, all women become brides; likewise, having become so, the noble ladies of the world will become my very self.

Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Yoga of Identity with that which Transcends the Imperishable," in the third section, the Dvāpara Age, of the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīyasaṃhitā*.

The illustrious Śrī Nārāyaṇī said: O Lord of Mercy, O Lord of Ramā, O Lord of All, O Master of the virtuous! [Tell me of] her who, though devoid of a mass of merit, becomes a seeker of enjoyment among millions. (1)
O Hari, tell me: what should be done here at the very beginning to establish the seed-force for the state of desiring liberation?
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
Listen, O Nārāyaṇī Śrī, for the purification even of a sinner;
I shall describe the sequential state by which one may attain the final goal.
"In times of distress and times of calamity, my strength must be proclaimed to her;
for even when remembered in the mind, Kṛṣṇa truly brings an end to misfortune."
She should then remember me; thereafter, for her who is filled with longing, one should instruct her to perform the auspicious vow known as Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, and she shall indeed do so.
Thereafter, one should perform the purification of the body with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya);
then, one should drink the water from my temple as the water for sipping (ācamanīya).
One should observe a fast and perform my worship;
one should indeed listen to the Vadhūgītā and then hear my mantras.
May Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa be my refuge at all times.
Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the Lord; svāhā! || 8 ||
Out of fear of Time, Illusion, evil karma, enemies, Yama, and treacherous friends,
one should bear the signs of the trident, fish, banner, bow, wheel, and the svastika.
I am Brāhmī, an eternal devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa;
the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa is my lord and husband. (10)
Bālakṛṣṇa is the Supreme Brahman; he is indeed my eternal Lord. May he be my father, kinsman, well-wisher, friend, protector, and nourisher. (11)
The beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, the beloved of His devotees, is the Supreme Brahman beyond the Imperishable (Akṣara), who assumes the essential forms of all incarnations. 12.
The Lord, the inner controller, the cause of all, the indwelling Self of all, the sovereign of all, untainted, and the bestower of liberation, is ever present within us. 13.
May the Purifier, who grants both worldly enjoyment and liberation when served, protect us always;
and may all the beloved consorts of Brahmā, such as Rādhā, Lakṣmī, and others, likewise protect us. (14)

They are the very nature of the Supreme Brahman, the half-bodies of the Supreme Brahman, the entire essence of the Supreme Brahman’s purpose; they are divine, bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Even the actions associated with them are always devoid of qualities and grant liberation; whoever, in whatever manner, worships Bālakṛṣṇa and his beloveds— || 16 ||
She is *sa sa sā sā*, whose nature is that very reality; she is divine, the eternal bestower of liberation. *Oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇanārāyaṇāya svāmine svāhā* ||17||
I am a devotee of Śrī Kṛṣṇasvāmī; Śrī Hari is my refuge.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrīvallabha, and Śrīsvāmī are my refuge. (18)
"Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Beloved, the Lord, Śrī Hari, is my refuge"—
the Guru should cause [the disciple] to recite all these mantras along with their meanings,
and he should perform my worship within the Sarvatobhadra maṇḍala.
I shall proclaim the procedure for worship, which is an integral part of the vow; listen to it in its entirety.
The full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa should be taken as the day of fasting.
Having performed the morning bath, one should offer water at a sacred ford or similar site. (20)
Having gone to the house of her father, a woman should remember Nārāyaṇa;

having washed her feet and sipped water (ācamana), being virtuous and wearing clean garments, she should perform the daily worship of the deity, followed by the formal ritual resolve (saṃkalpa). ||21||
One should worship the deity Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa with a spirit of devotion, holding a water-pitcher filled with fragrant water. (22)
Having taken the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and placed the golden image of Śrī Narāyaṇa in a pure vessel, [he should bathe it] with the five nectars and other waters.
One should bathe [the deity] and also offer garments and ornaments;
one should worship with perfumes, flowers, and the like, as well as with sandalwood, oils, and saffron.
With incense, lamps, excellent food offerings, roots, fruits, water, and so forth;
with betel, the ārārtika offering, hymns of praise, prostrations, supplications, and the like. ||25||
The observer of the vow, being composed in mind, should indeed perform congregational chanting (saṃkīrtana) with songs, instrumental music, dances, and the recitation of the Saṃhitās. 26.
Having prepared a square sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) one cubit (aratni) in size before the deity, and having established the fire there with ghee and other offerings... [27]
One should personally perform the oblation with devotion using ghee, sesame seeds, and other materials;
then one should offer it, saying: "Svāhā to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa. (28)
Thereafter, for the sake of removing all sins, the Guru should cause her to perform one hundred and eight oblations and other such expiatory rites. (29)
Having performed the worship once more, one should arrange for the dismissal;
indeed, endowed with devotion, one should offer the services and other honors to the deity. (30)
O Lord, I offer unto You the vow performed on the full moon day;
one should also present an *arghya* offering to the Moon and pay obeisance with beautiful flowers.
Then, with unbroken grains and other offerings, one should perform a vigil until the end of the night;
one should listen to the Saṃhitās and engage in dancing, chanting, and other such devotions.
Having bathed in the morning, she should feed virtuous and holy men, and then she herself,
having worshipped her husband and Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, should take her meal.
One should perform the breaking of the fast and also feed Brahmins;
in this manner, one should observe the vow for one year, beginning with the month of Pauṣa.
And on the full-moon day of the month of Kārttika, one should perform the concluding rite (udyāpana);
one should have a beautiful, auspicious, and quadrangular pavilion constructed.
Abounding in the beauty of plantain trunks, with archways of fresh sprouts, adorned with water-pots and other ornaments, and resplendent with rows of lamps. ||36||
Adorned with flower garlands and the like, and decorated with canopies and banners,
in its center is a five-colored *maṇḍala* called the *sarvatobhadra*.
In the center of that, the virtuous woman should place a new pitcher enriched with precious gems;
and its top should be adorned with the five types of sprouts, cloth, and other ornaments. (38)
One should place me, Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa Hari, in a vessel of sesame seeds;
having bathed me with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), one should worship me in due order with perfumes and other offerings.
Furthermore, with garments, ornaments, and the like, as well as various kinds of food and drink, one should place me upon a lion-throne; thereafter, the ārātrika ceremony follows.
One should pass the day with storytelling, recitation, and devotional worship;
at midday and at night, one should perform worship and keep a vigil.
On the following day, in the very morning, she should worship me, the Lord of Śrī;
she should also feed virtuous women and then partake of her own meal. 42.
One should present a statue, sesame seeds, and other offerings to the venerable goddesses;
one should perform a fire sacrifice with sesame seeds and pray to Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
O Lord of Gods, by your grace this annual vow has been performed;
may Lakṣmī be pleased and may Nārāyaṇa be gracious. (44)
O Mādhava, having made me, your devotee, entirely your own, accept me;
O Beloved Śrī Puruṣottama, grant me both worldly enjoyment and liberation. 45.
"O Lord, I offer all the fruit [of my actions] unto you. Having spoken thus, one should offer a handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali) and then bow down. ||46||
Having thus provided this remedy, one should perform the ritual dismissal;
one should constantly listen to the sacred discourse and cultivate the company of the virtuous. ||47||
Having become the repository of a mass of merit, may she go to my imperishable state after enjoying great pleasures here in this world, accompanied by sons and grandsons. (48)
Completely liberated from all sins and accompanied by ten thousand members of her family, she goes to my abode, which is difficult even for yogis to attain. (49)
Through my yoga, O beautiful woman, you shall become a divine Muktā here;
thereafter you shall become Brāhmī, the beloved of Brahmā, and then the beloved of Hari.
Endowed with all perfections and possessing all forms of sovereignty and other qualities, may she then become my beloved, just like Lakṣmī and just like Rādhā. (51)

The illustrious Śrī Nārāyaṇī said: "Tell me of a simple and easily accessible means for the destruction of the sins of a sinful woman who is unable to perform religious vows, which requires no effort. (52)
Śrī Puruṣottama said:
For a woman who is weak, sinful, or incapable of performing vows,
the offering to the Guru— relying upon the Guru as a boat— is the destroyer of sin.
She who bathes at the sacred ford of the Guru shall indeed become pure very quickly;
she immediately becomes an inhabitant of heaven and attains her desired liberation. ||54||
In the sacred ford of the Guru lies supreme accomplishment, for that is indeed the highest of all sacred fords;
meditation is a sacred ford, Hari is a sacred ford, and the eternal Brahman is a sacred ford. (55)
In that state where the functions of the senses indeed cease, and where the supreme cessation of the activity of the mind and intellect arises; 56.
Peace of the self shall also arise through the power of the true guru;

The letter *ga* is darkness, while the letter *ra* is its obstructer;

One should bestow knowledge upon oneself, as well as meditation upon Hari; one should also bestow discernment regarding sins and merits, and [the distinction] between the insentient and consciousness.

It bestows the perception of what is auspicious and inauspicious and wards off faults; one should cultivate the desire for liberation—that indeed is the heavy [burden], for it is the savior. (3.49.60)
One should grant peace through discernment, purity through grace, blessings with great affection, and fortune through strength. ||6 1 ||

She who grants prosperity through austerities and grants Hari through devotion, she who grants liberation through her own departure—she is always the great one because of her taking refuge [in the Lord]. (62)

The water from whose feet certainly serves to wash away all sins.
And whose food, born of her grace, becomes a cleanser of latent impressions. ||65||
The flowers, fruits, and garments of her which come into contact with the body—though insentient—are divine, pure, meritorious, auspicious, and bestow liberation. (66)
She whose body exists is indeed the body of the Lord, there is no doubt;

The divine Mahābhāgavatī, who has offered her entire self at all times—even the dust of her feet purifies those who are sinful. 68.
When washed from its very root, it likewise becomes a bestower of liberation;

The Lord’s hair is woven within her hair; the aperture of Hari is in her *brahmarandhra*, and Hari’s head is upon her head. (7.1)
On his forehead is the forehead of Hari; on his brow is the frown of Hari;

The wisdom of Śrī Hari is in Medhā; the cheeks of Hari are in [the goddess] Gaṇḍā; the temples of Hari are in the temples [of the devotee]; and the nose of the Lord is in the nose.
In her mouth, tongue, teeth, and lips are the face, tongue, teeth, and lips of Hari; indeed, her jaws and chin are the jaws and chin of Hari. (74)
Hari’s neck was upon her neck; Hari’s chest was upon her chest;
and [his presence was] in her two arms, hands, forearms, fingers, and nails. (75)
Hari’s arms, hands, forearms, fingers, and likewise his nails;
her belly is Hari’s belly, and within that belly is Hari’s stomach. (76)
Her navel was the navel of Hari; on her hips was the hip of Hari;

The feet of Hari are in his own feet, and his two hoods are also in his hoods;

The hairs of Śrī Hari are present in her hairs; his mind is in her mind;
his senses are in her senses; and the qualities of Hari are in her qualities.
The reality of this [individual soul] exists within Hari, as does its internal difference;
likewise, knowledge, will, and effort exist in Hari, and knowledge and the other qualities exist in the individual soul. (81)
In this ritual of Śrī Hari, the actions and movements of Hari are likewise performed:
laughing, walking, traveling, chanting, and sleeping. (82)

Everything belongs to the Guru and to Hari; therefore, the Guru is indeed the savior, the bestower of liberation, standing on the far shore of worldly existence, divine, and the giver of the divine goal. (83)
The sacred fords (tīrthas) of the feet of the Guru always abide upon the earth;

All the medicinal herbs reside in his body hair, and hosts of deities dwell on his two sides;

The sun and moon shine in her two eyes, and Brahmā shines upon her head;

In her heart was the lineage of Dharma, and in her mind were the beloveds of Hari;

Indeed, when the guru is pleased, worldly enjoyment and liberation shine forth;

The Vasus are in her palms, the Rudras are in her smile, and likewise the Bhāskaras are in her eyebrows and her cheeks. (93)
O Blessed One, the divine Māyā shines upon your lips; the imperishable Brahman resides on your venerable seat, and likewise, the Gaṅgā is present in your sandals.
Mahālakṣmī resides in her heavy sari, Rādhikā in her bodice, the celestial nymphs in her waistcloth, and Śrī, Ramā, and others in her ornaments. (95)

The three worlds reside in her sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), the eight supernatural powers (*aṣṭasiddhi*) in her meditation-band (*yogapaṭṭa*), and all forms of prosperity dwell within the heaps of auspicious substances.

Whether she be a meat-eater, an eater of all things, a killer, or even a dog-cooker, she is purified by taking refuge in the company of the virtuous and by serving them; thus she becomes stainless, shines forth, and even transcends [suffering]. (10.1)
"Released from the bonds of illusion, time, and action, one attains liberation through me;

Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Holy Places of Śrī Hari, the Guru, and the Guru’s Consort, and of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa Vrata which Liberates from Sin," within the *Vadhūgītā* of the third section, the *Dvāpara-santāna*, of the *Śrī-Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.

by day the sun, by night the moon, and the Guru is always the lamp within the house. || 9 ||
The Guru, who brings about the manifestation of Brahman, shines forth in the heart of the disciple;

Having understood this, she, being heavy with devotion, should propitiate the Guru with all her states of being—

On this matter, I shall relate to you a divine and captivating story:
Bhrigu was the son of Brahmā, and in his lineage was born the sage Cyavana.
Thinking repeatedly, "When shall I be endowed with knowledge?", he went on a pilgrimage for that purpose, in order to attain knowledge. (13)
From Badarī, he undertook a pilgrimage to the Gaṅgā and Kapilāśrama;
likewise, he performed pilgrimages to the Godāvarī, the Sarasvatī, and the Narmadā.
His body became stainless, possessing a radiance equal to the splendor of the sun;
having reached Oṃkāreśvara, he took his stand in the shade of a banyan tree.
Having drunk the water of the Narmadā, he became absorbed in meditation for a moment;
there he heard the speech of the birds, which was filled with profound wisdom.
For Śuka had four sons who delighted their father:
Ujjvala, Samujjvala, Vijvala, and Kapiñjala. || 17 ||
These parrots born in the grove are devoted to their father and mother;
having gathered fruits, they give them to their parents and also eat them themselves. (18)
Eager to be near their mother, they play in the presence of their father;
and they sleep constantly even as Cyavana watches them.
Having returned in the evening, they all perform their daily service;
and having performed it, they come to their father’s nest which brings them happiness.
They both bowed down to their father and mother, and being honored by them, they offered fruits to their parents while feeling a sense of weariness.
They were addressed and attended to by them, and they too served their parents with fanning and other such acts; at that time, the parents bestowed [their blessings] upon them.
Then the father asked them only auspicious blessings:
"O Ujjvala, in which direction have you gone today? (23)
"In that regard, tell me anything you have seen or heard that is unprecedented.
Having heard this, Ujjvala bowed to his father and related that story.
Today the king went to Gaṅgādvīpa, where indeed the righteous Divodāsa dwells, devoted solely to truth and dharma.
His wife was the goddess Brāhmī, devoted to her husband;
she gave birth to Suśīlā, who was rich in virtues and beauty, and possessed of lovely auspiciousness. (26)
And having beheld the maiden known as Divyādevī—a treasury of loveliness, divine, in the prime of her youth, and worthy of a husband—[he spoke]. (27)
The father, having summoned Citraprasenaka, the king of the Kāmarūpa region, gave his daughter to the wise Citrasena.
During the marriage sacrifice, that King Citrasena died;
the maiden, having failed to circumambulate the fire, was deprived of good fortune. (29)
At that time, the king indeed became anxious and questioned the brahmins regarding the cause:
"At the time of her marriage, Citrasena has gone to heaven. (3.50.30)
"Tell me truly, what kind of karma does she possess?
Having heard this, the brahmins replied, 'The time for the auspicious union (lagna) is indeed such.'"
The husband died, or else the wife became a wandering ascetic or fell ill;
then, in due course, the king went to the city of Indraprastha.
Rūpasena delivered her to the army of King Indraprastha;
Rūpasena, however, met his death at the very moment of the wedding.
Thus, whenever and to whomever the king gives a maiden in marriage, her husband indeed meets his death swiftly in the presence of the fire as witness. (34)
Twenty-one excellent men likewise met their death, while the maiden remained indeed unharmed; thus Divodāsa grieved.
Then, taking the minister’s words to heart, he caused a svayaṃvara to be held;
many kings were summoned there from all directions. (36)
When the young maiden entered the midst of the assembly for the svayaṃvara,
the kings then gazed upon her, who was like Rādhā and possessed a moon-like face.
But upon beholding the form of Adattavaramālā, the kings, overcome by darkness (tamas), fell into delusion and prepared themselves to seize her. ||38||
Others, however, fought at that very moment for her protection;
thus, a great slaughter of kṣatriyas occurred there during that svayaṃvara. (39)
Divyādevī, afflicted by extreme suffering and having attained a state of world-weariness, went to the Vindhya mountain to perform penance; there she wept.
I indeed heard her weeping and saw it near her;
O father, how could such ill fortune, which leads to the destruction of royalty, befall her? (41)
"His childhood, his dwelling in the forest, and likewise half of his life spent as a householder—such is the doubt that exists within me regarding this matter; please dispel it. (42)
Having heard his son's words there, Śuka Kuñjalaka spoke:
"O son, listen indeed to everything done in a previous birth, even that which was done in Kānyakubja."
That maiden had previously been the wife of a Vaiśya named Suvīra;
in Vārāṇasī, she was indeed known by the name Citrā and was one who acted according to her own will. ||44||
Devoted to improper conduct, sinful, wanton, and unfaithful, that wicked woman, devoid of merit, does not respect her husband at all. (45)
Causing distress and devoid of the true Dharma, she reviles her husband;
she dwells in another's house and wanders from home to home. (46)
She quickly perceives the faults of others and is intent on censuring the virtuous;
she is wicked, making others laugh, and devoid of good conduct. (47)
Indeed, having been cast out from the house by the Vaiśya Suvīra,
she fell into the company of the wicked and performed the work of a procuress.
An unchaste woman causes others to engage in acts of infidelity;
she brings about the ruin of the homes of virtuous people who abide on the path of dharma. 49.
Having summoned a virtuous woman, he entices her with gifts of wealth;
he causes her mind to break and even joins her in sexual union.
That woman, having violated virtuous men, would even give herself to another;
thus, in the past, a hundred houses were ruined by the wicked Citrā.
That greatly wicked woman waged war against her husband and sons;
thus devoted to sin, she died and went to the city of Yama.
Having experienced torments after the ripening of her karma had arrived,
that passionate woman now experiences the fruit of her own actions and weeps.
Since there were a hundred houses, therefore she had a hundred suitors—
along with twenty-one more— for her marriage and for the svayaṃvara.
If at an auspicious time there are as many deaths of excellent persons as the number [of syllables] in a Pāpā [yoga], the destruction of anyone's house must not be carried out. //55//
"When another is defeated, one's own defeat inevitably follows; of this there is no doubt.
Having heard this, Ujjvala said: "O father, she is from a great family. (56)
"Tell me also how the birth of that sinful woman came about.
Having heard his son's words, Kuñjala spoke to his son.

Where that messenger was, there once lived a certain Brahmin—a practitioner of virtuous dharma, one who had attained the state of the Siddhas, though poorly clad, yet carrying his staff as an ascetic. ||58||
Clad in a garment consisting merely of a loincloth, he stood at the gateway of Citra;
silent, with his senses conquered, wise, and devoted to the worship of Brahman. ||59||
Seeing the one who perceives reality—though overcome by hunger and thirst, exhausted, and weary from the long journey—he was beheld by Citrā as if he were happy. (3.50.60)
Having seen Citrā, she called him of the Kṛṣṇāyana lineage to her home;
she gave him a seat, water, food, and the honey-mixture (madhuparka).
Considering him a virtuous person worthy of excellent service, she massaged his body;
being pleased, she bestowed upon him auspicious blessings. (62)
"Let it be so, O princess," having said this, he indeed departed.
Then, after some time, Citrā met her death here.
Through the fruit of serving that holy man and likewise through his blessing,
a divine daughter, Divyādevī, was born in the house of Divodāsa.
For she has indeed provided food, water, service, and likewise a seat;
therefore, by the greatness of that merit, she truly lives as a princess. (65)
Indeed, due to sins such as the ruin of one's home, one repeatedly experiences widowhood;
therefore, service to the virtuous must be performed constantly.
Service to the guru must be performed, as well as service to the virtuous one who observes the vows of dharma;
for service to a virtuous woman must also be performed, as it indeed bestows all prosperity. (67)
Those princes who died were, in their previous lives, types of burglars;
they were stealers of women's necklaces, and because of that sin, they have died.
In the past, we were devoted to the service of cows, Brahmins, gurus, and holy men;
it is because of that indeed that we have attained the status of princes.
Therefore, virtuous people and spiritual teachers should indeed always be served;
one must never cause the ruin of others nor the ruin of one's own home.
Having heard this, Ujjvala again questioned his father there:
"Tell me, how may she be released from this grief and great suffering? (71)
"How does she attain liberation? Tell me that means as well.
Having heard this, the father Kuñjala spoke to his radiant son. (72)
Listen, my son, I shall explain the means for destroying her suffering and for her liberation, by which she will become purified. (73)
Through meditation on Hari, as well as through recitation, observance of vows, and service to the guru, the destruction of sin and liberation will surely occur; of this there is no doubt. (74)
The divine Nārāyaṇa, who is higher than the highest, dwells in the imperishable abode;
he is omniscient, omnipotent, and endowed with all sovereign powers.
The youth, enriched with all splendors, the beloved of Śrī, the Supreme Lord—free from any illusory form, he is endowed with a divine form. ||76||
With a divine crown upon his head, adorned with divine wheels and other ornaments,
his face possesses the luster of ten million moons, and his eyes resemble the petals of a lotus.
Abundant with the splendor of all ornaments, he shone with the Kaustubha gem;
he was served by Lakṣmī and graced by the Śrīvatsa mark. ||78||
And Satī should constantly meditate upon Him whose form is captivating, who is beloved, and whose youth is worthy of a beloved woman—this meditation which purifies all sins. (79)
O Hare, Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Śrī, Lord of Kamalā!
O Anādi-Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa, O Śrī-Kṛṣṇa, the bestower of liberation! ||3.50.80||
One should indeed perform worship in this manner and perform the recitation (japa), saying "O Hari!
On the full moon day, one should observe the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa vow.

she indeed performed service there for the preceptor Cyavana.
"By means of action, mind, and speech, one shall then abandon suffering. Having spoken all this, he bowed down to the offspring of the bird. (83)
Having received her father’s command, she went indeed to where she was;

"Who are you? To whom do you belong? For what reason have you come here? (85)
"O sinless one, explain to me the reason for your asceticism.
Having beheld the offspring of the bird, that divine lady spoke thus.
"O bird, listen to the truth as it is: we have fallen into great wonder.
Tell us who you are here, so that confidence may arise. (87)
The bird said: "O illustrious lady, I am a bird who shall remove your sorrow;
seeing you weeping, I have asked this—tell me the cause. (88)
"I shall strive according to my power for the destruction of your suffering.
Having heard this, Divyādevikā spoke to the bird: [89]
I experience the fruit of my past actions; I am the daughter of Divodāsa, and more than a hundred husbands have died during the celebration of my wedding.

I shall employ such means as will bring about the destruction of my sins.
Having heard what was said by his father, Ujjvala spoke to the woman;
she too considered that to be the truth and desired it as her penance.
He asked the bird about the atonement for previously committed sins;

Perform the recitation of the names: "Hare Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Supreme Lord!
Observe the auspicious vow, the supreme Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa vow. (94)
On the full moon day, observe a fast accompanied by a night vigil;
perform the concluding rite and serve the preceptor. (95)
And here, on the auspicious bank of the Narmadā, there is the preceptor Cyavana;
worship that great-souled one, and you shall become a mass of merit. (96)
Thus addressed, that lady of auspicious fortune accepted everything from the bird;
she observed the vow, performed the recitation of mantras, and likewise practiced meditation upon Hari. ||97||
Having gone to the banyan tree of Cyavana, that maiden indeed performed service for her guru through her body, mind, and speech, by means of total self-surrender. 98.
By the grace of her guru, that virtuous woman beheld within the span of a year the divine Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa, the Supreme Lord.
Having beheld him who was dark as a rain-cloud, beautiful, bearing the conch, discus, and mace,

"Through the attainment of my guru's grace, I have gained the vision of you.

I shall worship your feet; grant me devotion to you as my beloved. (103)
"O Lord, if you are pleased with me, grant me the status of a maidservant in liberation. Hari said, "Let it be so; come indeed to my abode."
Then she too became a divine goddess, possessing the very form of Lakṣmī;
having ascended an excellent celestial chariot, she departed for Vaikuṇṭha itself.
Ujjvala related the entire account to his father,

Cyavana was the fulfiller of all desires and a Vaiṣṇava preceptor;

"Tell me, what unprecedentedly radiant thing have you seen or heard?

Betrayal of a friend, breach of trust, causing schism among the gods, the destruction of one's livelihood, the ruin of one's pasture, and setting fire to dwellings.
The destruction of virtuous men and women, the giving of poison which causes terror, the killing of mother and father, and even the sexual enjoyment of young girls. (21)
Indeed, men wash away the twenty great sins—such as the slaughter of animals and sexual union with one's mother—as well as other sinful acts. ||22||

Having reached the bank of the Narmadā, the swans were deeply distressed;

She indeed took up the flowers that had been carried along by the flow of tears arising from her longing and weeping, and out of her sincerity, she worshipped Śaṅkara with them. (86)
That which was born from him was indeed undesirable; therefore Śaṅkara became enraged and uttered the sound "huṃ," by which the Dānava truly died.
Thus was the work of the gods accomplished by the powerful Viṣṇu;
then Viṣṇu, having assumed the form of a woman, vanished from sight.
The deities became exceedingly pleased due to the destruction of Huṇḍa.
Then, in ancient times, during the churning of the ocean, four maidens were born. (89)
Alakṣmī, Vāruṇī, Kāmodā, and Lakṣmī as the fourth—
these were then given by the Ocean to Uddālaka.
And the goddess Vāruṇī was indeed offered by the Ocean to Varuṇa; and Kāmodā, who will become Tulasī, was given to Viṣṇu. ||9.1||
And Lakṣmī, who dwells with Viṣṇu in Vaikuṇṭha, was given to him;
she is indeed Kāmodā, the daughter of the ocean, born from the churning of the waters through Nārada. (92)
She heard again and again that Viṣṇu’s birth would take place among humans;
and Kāmodā, unable to endure even the thought of separation from Viṣṇu, [was filled with longing].
Having gone to the bank of the Gaṅgā alone at that time, she wept indeed many times;
from those very tears, those red flowers were surely produced.
The fruit arising from that worship became the death of the Daitya;
now listen as I tell you the cause of Kāmodā’s laughter. (95)
When she takes the form of Tulasī, she shall become useful for the worship of Viṣṇu by offering her own leaves. || 96 ||
"The Lord of the World shall indeed always sport with her.
Remembering this, the maiden Kāmodā laughed here and there. (97)
And it should be understood that when *tulasī* is used, the cluster of blossoms (*mañjarī*) is produced by laughter.
One should offer either a single leaf or a cluster of blossoms of *tulasī* to Viṣṇu. (98)
One shall likewise become a partaker of the desired fruits for Brahmā and Śaṅkara as well;
thus, the auspicious fruit arising from worship with flowers should be understood in this manner. 99.
O Kapiñjala, likewise the woman is shown to be kāmodā (arousing desire), accompanied by weeping, accompanied by laughter, and the producer of flowers. || 3.52.100 ||
Vihuṇḍa, the stealer of merit, has also been shown to you by me;
thus, through the conjunction with the holy site of the Guru in the form of Viṣṇu, the tulasī [is attained].
Kāmodā is always to be worshipped, and her merit is also worshipped;
O son, the circle of deities is always worshipped with flowers.
The great Gurutīrtha is proclaimed as always bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
Vihuṇḍa met his destruction and went indeed to Kailāsa.
Even Huṇḍa went to heaven through the power of Śambhu-tīrtha and by means of royal yoga; therefore, the Guru-tīrtha is indeed preeminent.
Having spoken thus to his own sons, Kuñjala fell silent;
but then, O Lakṣmī, Cyavana, having heard this, questioned the bird.
"Who are you that remain here, O divine-knower of birds?
The bird replied: "Formerly, I indeed belonged to the lineage of Kaśyapa."
The son of that Vidyadhara was indeed named Dharmaśarman;
once, when he had become a complete fool, he came to my house.
The great sage Siddhāyana, a holy man, also arrived there;
he too was served by me and bestowed auspicious knowledge upon me.
That sage Siddhāyana, having become free from attachment and desire, and taking refuge in a solitary place, bestowed a blessing upon me. (109)
You shall become a knower who illuminates all things and a seer of all;
even while remaining in a single place, you will know that which is born within the three worlds.
Thus, by the grace of my guru, I know everything born within the three worlds;
I know you, Cyavana, to be the supreme true guru who bestows liberation.
And I shall tell you the cause of my state as a parrot;
listen: "Sin is born from association, and merit likewise is born from association. (1.12)
I bought a young parrot, and I was always infatuated with it;
it would speak thus to me: "Father, come here and sit down. (113)
"Go to bathe, O illustrious one, and worship the gods"—
by means of such diversion through his words, my religious duty was forgotten.
Then, having gone to the garden for the sake of vegetables and such from that house, I saw a bird that had been killed by a cat upon my arrival. || 15 ||
After that, due to extreme suffering, I died and became a parrot;
at the time of death, while possessing the nature of a parrot, I entered into birth as a parrot.
Through the power of Siddhāyana, I attain the memory of my past births here;
for there is no holy place equal to the Guru in regard to knowledge and liberation in every respect.
Just as external impurity is removed by water but not internal impurity,
so too, the impurity created in previous births is destroyed by visiting a great sacred ford (gurutīrtha).
O preceptor Cyavana, this moving supreme holy ford exists solely for the sake of crossing over saṃsāra; now I desire to cross, so please ferry me across.
Having spoken thus, the king of birds, accompanied by his son and joined by his wife,
came before the feet of the high-souled Cyavana.
The venerable Cyavana indeed gave the name-mantra to Śuka and caused him to drink water consecrated with the name of Kṛṣṇa.
Having bowed to their guru and remembered me, Nārāyaṇa,
those birds cast off their bodies and, becoming my attendants (pārṣadas), went to Vaikuṇṭha.
Having obtained that divine true guru as their sacred ford (tīrtha), they attained liberation;
for the sacred ford of the guru is indeed the supreme ford among all sacred fords.
Whether a man or a woman, she is the bestower of liberation; she is venerable and the very embodiment of sacred pilgrimage sites.
Whether she be a wife or even one who is not yet married, if she is truly devoted, she indeed grants liberation.
Resorting to her, eternal liberation must indeed be attained;
that virtuous goddess, the destroyer of sins, is to be served by wives. 125.
Brāhmī, Brahmapriyā, Haripriyā, and Pativratā;
Sādhu, Satpuruṣa, and Sadguru, who is dear to Hari. (1.26)
Bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation, it should always be cultivated by people;
O Lakṣmī, through its recitation and hearing, liberation shall certainly be attained.
